about: FIN-906 names pack: every researched name, with its evidence and disposition, today's reading ('before', the app without the pack) and the pack's ('after'); 'shipped' says whether it is in Lexicons/names.json, 'drop_reason' why not. decisions.about: How the names pack's clashes with the tech list were settled (FIN-906). A capitalised name reads as the name: pronunciation-only tech entries spelled exactly like a researched name were removed from Lexicons/tech-lexicon.json and tech-lexicon-10k.source.json (below, with the removed source entry); the rest are in lexicon-src/decisions/conflicts.json (Pir and Gui split by casing). Sui is held back from the pack by the owner's decision (2026-10-09): it reads as the blockchain, SWEE, from the tech list's entry.

entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi नारायण: /nɑː.ɾɑː.jəɳ/
entries.notes: US today's reading kept (only the unstressed final vowel differs). GB-only fix: today's GB nɑɹˈɒjɒn uses the 'lot' vowel for long ā. Stress on the second long syllable as usually said; Hindi doesn't mark it.

entries.name: Jack
entries.notes: Ordinary word 'jack' (car jack, playing card). Name and word sound the same.

entries.name: Mehdi
entries.source: Wiktionary, Persian مهدی: Iran formal [mæɦ.d̪íː], Tehrani [meɦ.d̪íː]; stress on the last syllable
entries.notes: The spelling Mehdi follows Persian (IR 318), Turkish and Maghrebi French usage, all final-stressed; today's 'MED-ee' drops the h and the stress.

entries.name: Fatima
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic فاطمة (fāṭima): /faː.tˤi.ma/, stress on the long first syllable

alternatives.context: a common English and South Asian rendering: fuh-TEE-muh

entries.notes: Arabic, Moroccan, Algerian and Nigerian (Hausa) bearers stress the long first syllable; today's US stresses the second and GB uses the 'a' of 'cat'.

entries.name: Eva
entries.source: Wiktionary Eva: German /ˈeːfa/ (also /ˈeːva/), Spanish /ˈeba/, Czech [ˈɛva]; today's AY-vuh is the shared reading
entries.notes: usage other (0.08): the continental AY-vuh is the majority and is already today's reading (also an English variant).

entries.name: Zhen
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 真 (zhēn): /ʈ͡ʂən⁵⁵/
entries.notes: zh [ʈʂ] → ʤ; -en is [ən] ('un'), not 'en'. Today's zˈɛn is a spelling reading.

entries.name: Jimmy
entries.notes: Ordinary word 'jimmy' (to force a lock). Name and word sound the same.

entries.name: Gang
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 剛 (gāng): /kɑŋ⁵⁵/
entries.notes: Ordinary word 'gang'. The name (Chinese 刚/鋼 gāng, Korean 강) is said GAHNG; that reading is given here.

entries.name: Sam
entries.notes: Collides with the acronym SAM (surface-to-air missile) and 'Uncle Sam' usage; the name sounds the same.

entries.name: Bo
entries.notes: Word 'bo' (bo staff); the English name sounds the same (BOH). Bearers are split: US and Danish BOH, Swedish and Norwegian BOO, Chinese 博/波 (bó) BWAW; no group clearly outnumbers the others, so no name reading is given.

entries.name: Mamadou
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Mamadou: /ma.ma.du/; French names take final stress in English (guide)
entries.notes: West African (Senegal, Guinea, Mali) form of Muhammad, written in French spelling. Today's mˈæmədˌu has the 'a' of 'cat'.

entries.name: Yūsuf
entries.source: Arabic يوسف (yūsuf): /juː.suf/, stress on the long first syllable; Indonesian Yusuf /ˈjusuf/ [ˈju.sʊf] (Wiktionary)

alternatives.context: Turkish Yusuf (usually without the macron): yoo-SOOF

entries.notes: The macron spelling is the Arabic transliteration. Today's jˈusˌʌf says 'YOO-suff'.

entries.name: Ismail
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic إسماعيل: /ʔis.maː.ʕiːl/; Turkish İsmail [ismaˈil]; stress on the final long syllable
entries.notes: US already right; GB-only fix (today GB ˈɪsmIl, 'IZ-mile').

entries.name: Wēi
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 威 (wēi): /weɪ̯⁵⁵/

entries.name: Oliver
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Oliver: /ˈɒlɪvə(ɹ)/; matches today's reading

entries.name: Lin
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 林 (lín): /lin³⁵/
entries.notes: Norwegian/Danish Lin (NO 494) is said the same.

entries.name: Abbas
entries.source: Wiktionary, Persian عباس: Iran formal [ʔæb.bɒ́ːs]; Arabic /ʕab.baːs/
entries.notes: Stress on the long final syllable; Persian â → 'ah' (as in Payam); geminate bb single. Today's 'AH-buhz' stresses the first.

entries.name: Farida
entries.source: Arabic فريدة (farīda): /fa.riː.da/; Indonesian Farida [faˈrida]; matches today's reading

entries.name: Tara

entries.notes: Irish origin (the Hill of Tara) and Indian bearers say TAH-ruh, as do UK and Irish bearers; US bearers are split between TAIR-uh, TARR-uh and TAH-ruh. GB is already right; US-only change.

entries.name: Hasan
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Hasan: /həˈsɑn/; Turkish Hasan [haˈsan]

alternatives.context: Arabic Ḥasan, often spelled Hassan: HAH-sun

entries.notes: Turkish bearers (wd TR 675) are the largest group; today's 'HAY-zun' is a spelling reading.

entries.name: Yong

entries.notes: Pinyin -iong is [jʊŋ] ('yoong'); today's jˈɔŋ ('yawng') is a spelling reading.

entries.name: Robin
entries.notes: Ordinary word 'robin' (the bird). Name and word sound the same in English; French Robin (FR 60k) is roh-BAN.

entries.name: Bruno
entries.source: Wiktionary Bruno: Italian /ˈbru.no/, German /ˈbʁuːno/, Spanish /ˈbɾuno/; matches today's reading

entries.name: Guang
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 光 (guāng): /ku̯ɑŋ⁵⁵/
entries.notes: Pinyin -ang is a back 'ah' [ɑŋ], not the 'a' of 'bang'; unaspirated g [k] → English g.

entries.name: Michel

entries.name: Arvind

entries.name: Diego

entries.name: Alfredo

entries.notes: Stressed e in an open syllable → A (guide table); today's 'al-FRED-oh' uses the closed 'eh'.

entries.name: Alice

entries.notes: usage english.

entries.name: Dennis

entries.name: Pablo

entries.notes: Stressed Spanish a → GB ɑː (guide table); US already right, GB-only fix (today GB pˈablQ, 'PAB-loh').

entries.name: Linda

Croatian, Serbian, Slovene, Czech and Slovak bearers: EE-vahn

entries.name: Nancy
entries.notes: Ordinary word 'nancy' (slang) and the French city Nancy. The English name sounds like the word.

entries.name: Susan
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Susan: /ˈsuːzən/; matches today's reading

entries.name: Felix
entries.source: Wiktionary Felix: German /ˈfeːlɪks/, Finnish /ˈfe(ː)liks/; English /ˈfiːlɪks/
entries.notes: usage other (anglo_share 0.05): German, Austrian, Swiss, Dutch and Scandinavian Felix (a top-10 German name for two decades), plus US Hispanic Félix entered without the accent, outnumber English FEE-liks. Close call on the register counts alone (US 71k, GB 15k, CA 26k); review.

entries.source: Wiktionary, English Nicholas: /ˈnɪkələs/; matches today's reading

entries.name: Nan
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 楠 (nán): /nan³⁵/

alternatives.context: English-speaking bearers (short for Nancy, Ann): NAN

entries.notes: Everyday British word 'nan' (grandmother: 'my Nan'), also how English bearers say the name. The Chinese name 楠/男 (nán), the largest bearer group, is said NAHN; that reading is given here.

entries.name: Amar
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi अमर: /ə.məɾ/, [ɐ.mɐɾ] (stress unmarked)
entries.notes: Three bearer groups: Indian (Hindi अमर, both vowels [ɐ], stress unmarked: uh-MUR or uh-MAR), Algerian (ʿAmmār, a-MAHR, matches today) and Bosnian (AH-mar). Missing: a source for the Indian-English stress and vowel, and which group is largest. Candidate is today's reading.

entries.name: Barbara
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Barbara: /ˈbɑːb(ə)ɹə/; matches today's reading

entries.name: Ben
entries.notes: Ordinary word 'ben' (Scottish mountain, Ben Nevis). Name and word sound the same.

entries.name: Helen
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Helen: /ˈhɛlən/; matches today's reading

entries.name: Herman
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Herman: /ˈhɜːmən/; matches today's reading

alternatives.context: Dutch, Swedish and Norwegian bearers: HAIR-mahn

entries.notes: Judgement call (anglo_share 0.02 is driven by Wikidata scaling): US bearers (86k) are about as many as the Dutch and Scandinavian ones together; German spells it Hermann. Kept the English reading; review if the pack prefers the continental one.

entries.name: Nadia

entries.notes: Every bearer group, and the English dictionary reading, has 'ah'; today's US nˈædjə and GB nˈadjə use the 'a' of 'cat'.

entries.name: Karim
entries.source: Arabic كريم (karīm): /ka.riːm/; today's differs only in the unstressed first vowel

entries.name: Sandeep
entries.source: Hindi संदीप (sandīp) by Hindi orthography: short a [ə], long ī; Hindi stress is weak and not written; stress here is the usual Indian-English one, on the heavy final syllable.
entries.notes: Today's 'SAN-deep' has the 'a' of 'cat' and first-syllable stress.

entries.notes: Spanish j [x] → h; today's ʤˈuliO says 'JOO-lee-oh'.

entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi किरण: /kɪ.ɾəɳ/; today's kˈɪɹən has the same sounds
entries.notes: Hindi doesn't mark stress; first-syllable stress is the common Indian-English reading.

entries.notes: Pinyin yun is [yn]: ü → 'oo' (guide table), as in Korean 윤. Today's jˈʌn rhymes with 'fun'.

entries.name: Hugo
entries.source: Wiktionary Hugo: Spanish /ˈuɡo/, Portuguese /ˈu.ɡu/, French /y.ɡo/, German /ˈhuːɡo/, English /ˈhjuː.ɡəʊ/

alternatives.context: English-speaking bearers (and the Hugo site generator on the tech list): HYOO-go
German, Swedish and Czech bearers: HOO-go

entries.notes: Readings split by language; Spanish and Portuguese OO-go (ES 102k + Latin America + Brazil) is the largest group, and French oo-GO shares its sounds. Today's HYOO-go comes from the tech list (Hugo the static site generator): that clash is for the merge. Review.

entries.name: Pankaj
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi पंकज: /pəŋ.kəd͡ʒ/, [pɐ̃ŋ.kɐd͡ʒ]
entries.notes: Today's pˈæŋkˌI ('PANK-eye') misreads the final -aj. Hindi short a → 'uh'.

entries.name: Narendra
entries.source: Wikipedia, Narendra Modi: Gujarati [ˈnəɾendɾə]; e in the closed syllable 'ren' → ɛ (guide table) gives today's reading
entries.notes: Today's nɑɹˈɛndɹə differs only in the unstressed first vowel.

entries.name: Qí
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 琪 (qí): /t͡ɕʰi³⁵/
entries.notes: q [tɕʰ] → ʧ (guide table). US is already right; GB-only fix (today GB kˈiː 'kee').

entries.name: Gopal
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi गोपाल: /ɡoː.pɑːl/
entries.notes: US already right; GB-only fix (today GB ɡˌQpˈɒl uses the 'lot' vowel for long ā).

alternatives.context: Italian and Romanian bearers, and Spanish Mónica: MOH-nee-ka

entries.name: Abhishek

entries.notes: Aspirated bh → b (guide table); today's əbhˈɪʃɛk splits b and h ('ub-HISH-ek'). Closed final eː → ɛ (guide table).

entries.name: Andy
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Andy: /ˈændi/; matches today's reading

entries.name: Hamid

alternatives.context: Arabic Ḥāmid (حامد), a different name romanised the same way: HAH-mid

entries.notes: Iranian bearers (wd IR 152) dominate; their name is حمید.

entries.name: Karan

entries.notes: Hindi short a is 'uh'; today's kˈɛɹən says 'Karen'. First-syllable stress as commonly said in Indian English.

entries.notes: Word 'Raj' (the British Raj). The Hindi name राज (rāj) sounds the same: RAHJ.

entries.notes: Pinyin -en is [ən] ('wun', not 'wen'). Tones dropped; primary stress on the last syllable and secondary on the first (the guide's convention for two-syllable Chinese given names, no English source gives it).

entries.name: Harry
entries.notes: Ordinary word 'harry' (to harass). Name and word sound the same.

entries.name: Edwin
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Edwin: /ˈɛdwɪn/; matches today's reading

entries.notes: Today's kəɹˈɛn is the ethnic group's reading, not the given name's (US 990k). Note: the entry would also change 'the Karen people' in text.

entries.notes: ħ → h (guide table); today drops the h, and GB uses the 'lot' vowel (ˈɒmɒd).

entries.name: Shankar

entries.notes: Today's 'MAN-ish' reads it as an English word.

entries.name: Mahesh
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi महेश: /mə.ɦeːʃ/; e in a closed syllable → ɛ (guide table) gives today's reading

entries.name: Bin

entries.name: Betty
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Betty /ˈbɛti/

entries.name: Gilbert
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Gilbert /ˈɡɪlbət/, US /ˈɡɪlbɚt/; French /ʒil.bɛʁ/

alternatives.context: French and Belgian bearers (FR register 150k): zheel-BEHR

entries.notes: Bearer choice (review): the FR register (150k) beats the US one (107k), but the Philippines (Forebears 149k) and anglophone Africa also say GIL-bert, making English the largest reading group; the capitalised spelling is also a common English surname (W. S. Gilbert, the Gilbert Islands).

entries.name: Dinesh
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi दिनेश /d̪ɪ.neːʃ/
entries.notes: Long [eː] -> 'ay' and takes the stress; today's DIN-esh reads it as English.

entries.name: Sachin
entries.source: Wikipedia, Sachin Tendulkar: Marathi [sətɕin]; Hindi सचिन [sə.t͡ʃɪn]
entries.notes: Hindi/Marathi a is schwa ('such'), not today's TRAP vowel.

entries.name: Vicente
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Vicente /biˈθente/, /biˈsente/; Wikipedia, Vicente Fox: [biˈsente]

alternatives.context: English speakers' usual v; Portuguese and Tagalog bearers say v

entries.notes: Today's vee-CHEN-tee is Italian-style. Spanish word-initial v is [b], an English sound, so the reading keeps b; English speakers often say v, listed as an alternative.

entries.name: Johan
entries.source: Wiktionary, Swedish Johan [²juːan]; Norwegian Bokmål /jʊˈhan/; Dutch [ˈjoːɦɑn]
entries.notes: Swedish bearers are the largest group (wd SE 3661); Swedish drops the h and stresses the first syllable. Today's final stress matches only Norwegian.

entries.name: Héctor
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Héctor /ˈeɡtoɾ/ [ˈeɣ̞.t̪oɾ]
entries.notes: Spanish h is silent; final o is a full vowel. The c before t is a soft [ɣ] English lacks; English speakers keep the spelling's k. Today's HEK-ter is the English Hector.

entries.name: Moses
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Moses /ˈməʊzɪz/, US /ˈmoʊzɪz/
entries.notes: Bearers (Uganda, Nigeria, US) use the English form.

entries.name: Qin
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 秦 qín /t͡ɕʰin³⁵/; Wikipedia, Qin dynasty: English /tʃɪn/
entries.notes: Pinyin q [tɕʰ] -> ch; today's ʧˈɪn is right. Tone dropped.

entries.name: Habib
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic حبيب /ħa.biːb/
entries.notes: ḥ -> h. Today's həbˈib differs only in the unstressed first vowel.

entries.name: Raúl
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Raúl /raˈul/; Wikipedia, Raúl Castro: [raˈul]
entries.notes: The accent splits a-u into two syllables with the stress on u; today's RAWL makes one syllable.

entries.name: Francesco
entries.source: Wiktionary, Italian Francesco /franˈt͡ʃe.sko/
entries.notes: Today's fɹænʧˈɛskO differs only in the unstressed first vowel.

entries.name: Jiahao
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 家 jiā /t͡ɕi̯ä⁵⁵/; hao [xɑʊ̯] (浩然 hàorán /xɑʊ̯⁵¹ ɻän³⁵/)
entries.notes: jia is one syllable 'jyah'; h [x] -> h. Mandarin tones dropped; with no English source for this given name, primary stress on the last syllable and secondary on the first (guide convention).

entries.name: Zhiming
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 志明 zhìmíng /ʈ͡ʂɻ̩⁵¹ miŋ³⁵/
entries.notes: Retroflex syllabic zhi -> English 'jr' (ʤɜɹ/ʤɜː); today's guess reads 'zy-ming'. Mandarin tones dropped; with no English source for this given name, primary stress on the last syllable and secondary on the first (guide convention).

entries.name: Han
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 漢 hàn /xän⁵¹/; Dutch Han [ɦɑn] and Korean 한 [han] the same 'hahn'

alternatives.context: the Star Wars character Han Solo: HAN

entries.notes: Mandarin, Dutch and Korean bearers all say 'hahn', as English does for the Han dynasty; today's TRAP vowel is a spelling reading (and Han Solo's).

entries.name: Anne
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Anne /æn/; French /an/

alternatives.context: German, Dutch, Danish, Norwegian, Finnish: AH-nuh

entries.notes: English and French bearers (US 258k, FR 279k) share the one-syllable 'an'; the two-syllable Germanic AH-nuh group is smaller.

entries.name: Nathan
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Nathan /ˈneɪθən/

entries.name: Carl
entries.notes: Ordinary word 'carl' (archaic: a churl). The name is said like the word, KARL (Swedish and German Carl too); today's kˈɑɹl / kˈɑːl is right.

entries.name: Leonardo
entries.source: Wiktionary, Italian Leonardo /le.oˈnar.do/; Spanish /leoˈnaɾdo/
entries.notes: Today's lˌiənˈɑɹdO differs from the Italian only in unstressed vowels.

entries.name: Allan
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Alan /ˈæl.ən/ (Allan is a spelling of the same name)

entries.name: Ajit
entries.source: Hindi अजित [ə.d͡ʒɪt] (regular Devanagari spelling: short a and i; Wiktionary has no entry)
entries.notes: Today's əʤˈɪt matches. The spelling अजीत (Ajeet) has a long ī, but this spelling is short.

entries.name: Xuan
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 宣 xuān /ɕy̯ɛn⁵⁵/; Vietnamese Xuân [swən˧˧]

alternatives.context: Vietnamese Xuân (many US, Canadian and French bearers): swun

entries.notes: x [ɕ] -> sh; the ü-glide -> w, the usual English approximation; vowel [ɛ]. Today's 'zhwahn' is a spelling reading. Tone dropped.

entries.name: Reza
entries.source: Wiktionary, Persian رضا: Iran [ɹe.ˈzɒː]; Wikipedia, Reza Pahlavi: Persian [ɾeˈzɒː], English /ˈreɪzə/

alternatives.context: English rendering (Wikipedia for Reza Pahlavi), and Indonesian Reza: RAY-zuh

entries.notes: Persian stresses the last syllable; â [ɒː] -> English 'ah' as in the guide's Payam. Today's REZ-uh is a spelling reading.

entries.name: Mona
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Mona /ˈmoʊ̯nə/; German [ˈmoːnaː]; Swedish /²moːna/
entries.notes: English, German, Swedish and French bearers agree on MOH-na.

entries.name: Manoj
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi मनोज /mə.noːd͡ʒ/
entries.notes: Long [oː] takes the stress; today's guess MAN-uj reads it as English.

entries.name: Arturo
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Arturo /aɾˈtuɾo/; Italian /arˈtu.ro/
entries.notes: Stressed Spanish/Italian u is 'oo'; today's ʊ (as in 'tour') shortens it, most audibly in British.

entries.name: Marc
entries.notes: Ordinary word 'marc' (grape pomace; the brandy). The name is said like it, MARK (French and Catalan Marc too); today's mˈɑɹk is right.

entries.name: Leon
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Leon /ˈliː.ɒn/, US /ˈli.ɑn/

entries.name: Uma
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi उमा /ʊ.mɑː/
entries.notes: Today's YOO-muh adds a y the name never has. Short [ʊ] in an open stressed syllable -> English 'oo'; Hindi stress is weak and does not fall on a plain long final vowel.

entries.name: René
entries.source: Wiktionary, French René /ʁə.ne/

entries.name: Stephanie
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Stephanie /ˈstɛf.ə.ni/

entries.name: Geeta
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi गीता /ɡiː.t̪ɑː/
entries.notes: Hindi g is always hard; today's JEE-tuh softens it.

entries.name: Hong
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 宏 hóng /xʊŋ³⁵/; Wikipedia, Mao Zedong: English /ˈmaʊ (t)səˈtʊŋ/ renders pinyin ong as ʊŋ

alternatives.context: Korean 홍 and Vietnamese Hồng bearers: HOHNG

entries.notes: Protect-word (review): capitalised 'Hong' in English text is mostly Hong Kong, read HONG (today's hˈɔŋ); the app reads 'Hong Kong' word by word (Hong=cmudict, Kong=lexicon), so a general name entry would make it 'hoong kong'. The given-name reading, Mandarin hóng [xʊŋ] -> HOONG (pinyin ong as English ʊŋ, as in Zedong), is in us/gb for a name-only context. Tone dropped.

entries.name: Vanessa
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Vanessa /vəˈnɛsə/

entries.name: Dōng
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 東 dōng /tʊŋ⁵⁵/; Wikipedia, Mao Zedong: English /ˈmaʊ (t)səˈtʊŋ/
entries.notes: Pinyin ong is [ʊŋ] ('oong'); today's 'dawng'/'dong' is a spelling reading. Tone mark dropped.

entries.name: Sheila
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Sheila /ˈʃiːlə/

entries.name: Joyce
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Joyce /d͡ʒɔɪs/

entries.name: Leslie
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Leslie /ˈlɛzli/, /ˈlɛsli/

entries.name: Jasmine
entries.source: Wiktionary, English jasmine /ˈd͡ʒæzmɪn/, /ˈd͡ʒæzmən/
entries.notes: Covered by the tech lexicon on purpose; the reading is right for the name.

entries.name: Dina
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Dina /ˈdiːnə/; Spanish /ˈdina/; Italian /ˈdi.na/

entries.name: Seema
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi सीमा /siː.mɑː/
entries.notes: GB-only fix: today's British final ɒ ('SEE-mo') should be the 'ah' of long ā. US already right.

entries.name: Isabel
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Isabel /isaˈbel/; Portuguese /i.zɐˈbɛl/; German [izaˈbɛl]; English /ˈɪzəbɛl/
entries.notes: Bearer choice (review): ES register 237k plus Latin America and Portugal, all stressing the last syllable, against about 140k English bearers.

entries.name: Frederick
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Frederick /ˈfɹɛd(ə)ɹɪk/

entries.name: Jacqueline
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Jacqueline /ˈdʒækəlɪn/; French /ʒa.klin/; German /ʒaˈkliːn/; Dutch /ʒɑkəˈlin/

alternatives.context: French, Belgian, Swiss, German and Dutch bearers: zhak-LEEN

entries.notes: Close call (review): US 419k plus the UK, Ireland and the Philippines against FR 329k plus French-speaking Belgium and Switzerland and the German/Dutch use of the French form; Forebears' DR Congo and Cameroon estimates (~357k) would tip it to French zhak-LEEN. Today's JAK-wuh-lin (CMUdict) is the common American variant of Wiktionary's JAK-uh-lin; stress and stressed vowel match.

entries.name: Carmen
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Carmen /ˈkaɾmen/
entries.notes: Today's kˈɑɹmən differs only in the unstressed final vowel.

entries.name: Shahid
entries.source: Wiktionary, Persian/Arabic شاهد šāhid (Levantine [ˈʃæː.hɪd]); Urdu شاہد [ʃɑː.ɦɪd] with the stress on long ā

alternatives.context: the different name Shaheed (شهيد, 'martyr'), sometimes spelled Shahid: shuh-HEED

entries.notes: Shahid (Shahid Afridi, Shahid Kapoor) is شاہد 'witness', SHAH-hid; today's shah-HEED is Shaheed.
entries.word_check: gold has 'shahid'; kept: gold lists the name in lower case; no ordinary word

entries.name: Martha
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Martha /ˈmɑː.θə/

entries.name: Mathew
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Matthew /ˈmæθjuː/ (Mathew is a spelling variant)

entries.name: Alfonso
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Alfonso /alˈfonso/; Italian /alˈfɔn.so/
entries.notes: Stressed Spanish o is 'oh'; today's al-FAHN-soh (GB al-FON-so) is an English spelling reading.

entries.name: Sophia
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Sophia /soʊˈfiː.ə/, UK also /səˈfaɪ.ə/

entries.name: Indira
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi इन्दिरा /ɪn.d̪ɪ.ɾɑː/; Wikipedia, Indira Gandhi: Hindi [ˈɪndɪɾaː]

alternatives.context: the common English rendering (Wikipedia for Indira Gandhi): in-DEER-uh

entries.notes: Hindi stresses the first syllable; today's in-DIH-ruh is the English rendering.

entries.name: Serge
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Serge /sɛʁʒ/
entries.notes: Collision with 'serge' (a fabric; word_freq uncommon). The name's bearers are overwhelmingly French (FR register 212k) and say SAIRZH, in us/gb. The capitalised spelling in running text is almost always the name, so this could ship as a name entry if the merge allows uncommon words.

entries.name: Maryam
entries.source: Wiktionary, Persian مریم /mar.ˈjam/, Iran [mæɹ.jǽm]
entries.notes: Iran has the most bearers; Persian stresses the last syllable with the TRAP-like æ, as in the guide's Payam. Today's 'mehr-YAHM' has the wrong vowels.

entries.name: Guy
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Guy /ɡi/; English Guy /ɡaɪ/

alternatives.context: English (Guy Fawkes, Guy Ritchie) and Hebrew גיא bearers: GUY

entries.notes: Ordinary word 'guy'. The most bearers are French (FR register 245k), who say GHEE (in us/gb); English and Israeli bearers say it like the word.

entries.name: Edgar
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Edgar /ˈɛdɡɚ/; German /ˈɛt.ɡaːɐ̯/; Dutch /ˈɛt.ɡɑr/
entries.notes: German, Dutch, Spanish and Polish bearers differ only in the unstressed second vowel (ED-gar).

entries.name: Uday
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi उदय /ʊ.d̪əj/ [ʊ.d̪ɐj]

alternatives.context: Arabic ʿUday (Iraq) and some Indian speakers: oo-DAY

entries.notes: Short [ʊ] in an open syllable -> English 'oo'; final -ay as in Akshay. Hindi stress is weak and falls on the first syllable here (the final is not superheavy), as in today's ˈudA.

entries.name: Víctor
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Víctor /ˈbiɡtoɾ/ [ˈbiɣ̞.t̪oɾ]; Catalan [ˈbik.tur]

alternatives.context: English speakers' usual v; also Portuguese Víctor

entries.notes: Accented spelling: Spanish and Catalan bearers. Stressed i is 'ee' and final o a full vowel; today's VIK-ter is the English Victor. Spanish word-initial v is [b], an English sound, so the reading keeps b; English speakers often say v, listed as an alternative.

entries.name: Marcel
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Marcel: /maʁ.sɛl/
entries.notes: Also the word 'marcel' (a hair wave), said the same way. Today's mɑɹsˈɛl / mɑːsˈɛl is already the French (and English) name reading, so the word and the name agree; nothing to change.

entries.name: Lal
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi लाल (lāl): /lɑːl/
entries.notes: Long ā is 'ah', not the 'a' of 'pal'.

entries.name: Anton
entries.source: Wiktionary, German Anton: /ˈantoːn/; Swedish, Norwegian, Czech and Slovene bearers also stress the first syllable with an 'ah' vowel

alternatives.context: English-speaking bearers; the usual English reading of Anton Chekhov

entries.notes: Covered by the tech list (ˈæntɑn). anglo_share 0.02: most Latin-script bearers are German, Austrian, Slovene, Scandinavian and Czech, who say AHN-ton. US fix only: the British 'a' already matches German short a, so GB stays as today.

entries.name: Xiaoyan
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 小 xiǎo [ɕi̯ɑʊ̯], 燕 yàn [jɛn]; guide convention for two-syllable Chinese names: primary on the last syllable
entries.notes: Pinyin x [ɕ] → sh (guide). Pinyin -yan is 'yen'. Tones dropped.

entries.name: Xiaodong
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 東 dōng [tʊŋ]; Wikipedia, Mao Zedong: Mandarin [... tʊ́ŋ]; guide stress convention
entries.notes: Pinyin x → sh; unaspirated d [t] → d; -ong [ʊŋ] uses the 'book' vowel.

entries.name: Qun
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 群 qún [t͡ɕʰyn]
entries.notes: Pinyin q [tɕʰ] → ch; the ü vowel [y] has no English match, 'oo' is the guide's approximation.

entries.name: Salim
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic سَلِيم (salīm): /sa.liːm/; Arabic stress falls on the long final syllable
entries.notes: Today's SAL-im stresses the wrong syllable.

entries.name: Ricky
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Ricky: /ˈɹɪki/

entries.name: Chao
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 超 chāo [ʈ͡ʂʰɑʊ̯]: 'chow', as today

entries.name: Hua
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 華 huá [xu̯ä]: one syllable
entries.notes: One syllable; today's HOO-uh splits it in two. Pinyin h [x] → English h.

entries.name: Xiangdong
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 向 xiàng [ɕi̯ɑŋ], 東 dōng [tʊŋ]; guide stress convention
entries.notes: Pinyin x → sh, not zh as today.

entries.name: Maurice
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Maurice: /mɔ.ʁis/; US English also /mɔˈɹis/
entries.notes: French bearers are the largest group; today's mo-REES is their reading and the usual US one.

entries.name: Julius
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Julius: /ˈdʒuːli.əs/

alternatives.context: German, Dutch, Scandinavian and Lithuanian bearers (YOO-lee-oos)

entries.notes: anglo_share 0.03, but the other bearers split over several readings; English is the largest single group and is how English text reads Julius Caesar.

entries.name: Baba
entries.notes: Also the word 'baba' (rum baba; 'father' in several languages), said BAH-bah like the name. Today's reading already matches; nothing to change.

entries.name: Sharon
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Sharon: /ˈʃæɹən/ (UK), /ˈʃɛɹən/ (US)
entries.notes: GB-only fix: the British voice says SHAIR-un (ʃˈɛːɹən); British English says SHARR-un. US is right.

entries.name: Julia
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Julia: /ˈdʒuːli.ə/

alternatives.context: German, Polish, Scandinavian and Dutch bearers (YOO-lee-a)

entries.notes: Covered by the tech list (the Julia language), which gives the English name reading. English is the largest single group; Spanish HOO-lya and German/Polish YOO-lee-a split the rest.

entries.name: Tina
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Tina: /ˈtiːnə/

entries.name: Shyam
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi श्याम (śyām): /ʃjɑːm/
entries.notes: One syllable with a long 'ah'; today's SHY-um is a spelling guess.

entries.name: Claude
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Claude: /klod/

alternatives.context: English-speaking bearers (Claude Rains) and Anthropic's Claude

entries.notes: Covered by the tech list on purpose: in English text 'Claude' is now very often Anthropic's AI assistant, said 'klawd'. Most bearers of the given name are French (KLOHD), but a name entry would change every mention of the assistant, so it's protected; the French name reading is recorded in us/gb for review.

entries.name: Priyanka
entries.source: Wikipedia, Priyanka Chopra: Hindi [prɪˈjəŋka]
entries.notes: Hindi short a [ə] is English 'uh', not 'ah' (and not the British 'lot' vowel).

entries.name: Radha
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi राधा (rādhā): /ɾɑː.d̪ʱɑː/
entries.notes: Aspirated dh → d. Today differs only in the unstressed final vowel.

entries.name: Dominic
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Dominic: /ˈdɒmɪnɪk/

entries.name: Thị
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese thị: (Hà Nội) [tʰi˧˨ʔ]
entries.notes: Vietnamese th is an aspirated t, not English th; tone dropped. Usually a women's middle name.

entries.name: Guohua
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 國 guó [ku̯ɔ], 華 huá [xu̯ä]; guide stress convention
entries.notes: Two syllables, gwaw + hwah; primary on the last by the guide's convention.

entries.name: Paula
entries.region: Spain, Latin America, Germany, Brazil, Poland
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Paula: /ˈpaula/; German /ˈpaʊ̯la/; Portuguese, Polish, Romanian and Finnish also POW-la
entries.notes: anglo_share 0.12: the Spanish, German, Portuguese, Polish, Romanian and Finnish bearers all say POW-la, together far more than the English group (the guide's Andrea case). Review: this changes the reading for English-speaking Paulas.

entries.name: Federico
entries.source: Wiktionary, Italian Federico: /fe.deˈri.ko/
entries.notes: Today differs only in unstressed vowels.

entries.name: Luiz
entries.source: Wiktionary, Portuguese Luís/Luiz: (Brazil) /luˈis/, (Portugal) /luˈiʃ/
entries.notes: Two syllables, stress on the second; today's LOOZ drops one.

entries.name: Abdoulaye
entries.source: Wikipedia, Abdoulaye Wade: French [abdulaj wad]
entries.notes: French -aye here is [aj] 'eye', not 'ay'. Last-syllable stress as for French-spelled names in English.

entries.name: yenni
entries.notes: Lowercase spelling: a register/Wikidata artefact. Its Wikidata labels point to Naser/Nasser (ناصر), which don't match the spelling, and an entry would only touch lowercase 'yenni'. The capitalised given name Yenni (Indonesian, Hispanic) would be a separate row.

entries.name: Gaurav
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi गौरव (gaurav): /ɡɔː.ɾəʋ/
entries.notes: Hindi au is [ɔː]; stress on the heavy first syllable (Hindi stress is weak). Today's go-RAV is a guess.

entries.name: Yogesh
entries.source: Hindi योगेश (yogeś, yoga + īśa): long o and long e; stress on the superheavy last syllable by the Hindi weight rule
entries.notes: Hindi e is a long 'ay'. Stress is weak in Hindi; the final syllable is the heaviest.

entries.name: Roman
entries.source: Wiktionary, Polish Roman: /ˈrɔ.man/; English /ˈɹəʊmən/
entries.notes: Polish, Czech, German and English bearers all stress ROH; only the unstressed vowel differs.

entries.name: Ramón
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Ramón: /raˈmon/
entries.notes: Today differs only in the unstressed vowel.

entries.name: Fang
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 芳 fāng [fɑŋ]
entries.notes: Also the English word 'fang' (fˈæŋ). The Chinese name is FAHNG; recorded here for review, protected so the word keeps its reading.

entries.name: Fēng
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 峰/風 fēng [fɤŋ]; Merriam-Webster feng shui: \ˈfəŋ-ˈshwā\ (English 'fung')
entries.notes: Pinyin -eng [ɤŋ] is 'ung' in English, not 'eng'.

entries.name: Ashley
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Ashley: /ˈæʃli/

entries.name: Ken
entries.notes: Also the word 'ken' (range of knowledge; Scots 'know'). The name (English Ken, Japanese ケン) is said like the word; today's reading is right.

entries.name: Qian
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 倩 qiàn [t͡ɕʰi̯ɛn]
entries.notes: One syllable; pinyin q is 'ch', -ian is 'yen'. Today's KEE-ahn is a spelling guess.

entries.name: Rong
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 榮 róng [ʐʊŋ]
entries.notes: Pinyin r [ʐ] → English r; -ong [ʊŋ] with the 'book' vowel (as in Mao Zedong's -dong).

entries.name: Xiǎopíng
entries.source: Wikipedia, Deng Xiaoping: Mandarin [ɕjàʊ.pʰǐŋ]; the guide's worked Xiaoping reading
entries.notes: Pinyin x → sh, not zh as today.

entries.name: Ann
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Ann: /æn/
entries.notes: English is by far the largest group; Swedish/Norwegian Ann [anː] is close.

entries.name: Florence
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Florence: /ˈflɒɹəns/; French /flɔ.ʁɑ̃s/
entries.notes: English-reading bearers (US, UK, English-speaking Africa, Australia) outnumber the French, and 'Florence' is also the Italian city in English text, read the same way.

entries.name: Antoine
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Antoine: /ɑ̃.twan/
entries.notes: GB-only fix: the British voice ends in the 'lot' vowel (-TWON). US is right.

entries.name: Sean
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Sean: /ʃɔːn/

entries.name: Xing
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 星 xīng [ɕiŋ]: 'shing', as today

entries.name: Hóng
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 紅 hóng [xʊŋ]
entries.notes: Pinyin -ong [ʊŋ] uses the 'book' vowel. Hong Kong's 'hong' is Cantonese-based; this accented spelling is pinyin.

entries.name: Johann
entries.source: Wiktionary, German Johann: /ˈjoːhan/
entries.notes: Today differs only in the unstressed vowel.

entries.name: Cynthia
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Cynthia: /ˈsɪnθi.ə/

entries.name: Elias
entries.source: Wiktionary, German Elias: /eˈliːas/; Swedish, Norwegian, Dutch and Portuguese bearers also stress -LI-
entries.notes: Today's EE-lee-uz is neither the English (ih-LYE-us) nor the continental reading; the continental eh-LEE-us is the largest group (Elias is a top name in Germany, Austria, Sweden and Norway).

entries.name: Regina
entries.source: Wiktionary, German Regina: /ʁeˈɡiːna/; English Regina: /ɹɪˈdʒiːnə/, (UK, Canada) /ɹɪˈdʒaɪnə/
entries.notes: Today's ri-JY-nuh is the reading of Regina, Saskatchewan, and of Latin 'Regina' in British case names (Regina v Smith), both frequent in English text. Bearers mostly say reh-GEE-na (German, Polish, Czech) or ri-JEE-na (US). Protected so the city keeps its reading; review whether a name entry should ship.

entries.name: Salman
entries.source: Wikipedia, Salman Rushdie: English /sælˈmɑːn/; Arabic سلمان salmān
entries.notes: Today's SAM-un drops the l and stresses the wrong syllable.

entries.name: Wilson
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Wilson: /ˈwɪlsən/
entries.notes: Many bearers are Brazilian and Colombian, named after the English name; their WEEL-son is an adaptation of the English reading. Wilson is also a common English surname.

entries.name: Abdulhamid
entries.source: Arabic عبد الحميد ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd: stress on the long last syllable (-mīd); Wiktionary, English Abdul: /ˈæbdʊl/
entries.notes: Arabic ḥ → h, ʿayn dropped (guide). Today's ab-DUL-uh-mid stresses the wrong syllable.

entries.name: Anh
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese anh: (Saigon) [ʔan˧˧], (Hà Nội) [ʔajŋ̟˧˧], (Huế) [ʔɛɲ˧˧]
entries.notes: Southern and overseas bearers say 'ahn'; today's reading is English 'Ann'. Tone dropped.

entries.name: Rodolfo
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Rodolfo: /roˈdolfo/
entries.notes: Spanish o is 'oh', not 'ah' (today ro-DAHL-fo).

entries.name: Giuseppe
entries.source: Wiktionary, Italian Giuseppe: /d͡ʒuˈzɛp.pe/
entries.notes: Italian s between vowels is z here; final -e is 'ay' (guide). Today's ji-SEP-ee is an English mangling.

entries.name: Praveen
entries.source: Hindi प्रवीण (pravīṇ): /pɾə.ʋiːɳ/; today's pruh-VEEN matches

entries.name: Nitin
entries.source: Hindi नितिन: short i in both syllables; pronounce.tv: NI-tin, stress on the first syllable
entries.notes: Short i, not 'eye' (today NY-tin). Hindi stress is weak; first-syllable stress follows the name site.

entries.name: Prashant
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi प्रशांत (praśānt): /pɾə.ʃɑːnt̪/
entries.notes: Mainly a GB fix: the British voice uses the 'lot' vowel (-SHONT) for long ā. US only loses a secondary stress on the unstressed first syllable.

entries.name: Madhu
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi मधु: /mə.d̪ʱuː/ (stress not marked); Vedic Sanskrit /mɐ́.dʱu/ (first syllable); pronounce.tv: first-syllable stress
entries.notes: Sounds are as today; only the stress moves. Hindi stress is weak and analyses differ (a weight-based account would stress the long final ū, as today does); first-syllable stress follows the Vedic accent, the two-syllable rule (Mehrotra) and the name site.

entries.name: Abel
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Abel: /aˈbel/; French /a.bɛl/ and Portuguese /aˈbɛw/ also stress the last syllable

alternatives.context: English-speaking bearers; the biblical Abel in English text
Dutch and Scandinavian bearers (Niels Henrik Abel)

entries.notes: anglo_share 0.04: Spanish, French and Portuguese bearers (ah-BEL) far outnumber English ones. Review: English text about Cain and Abel would also get ah-BEL.

entries.name: Antony
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Antony: /ˈæntəni/
entries.notes: The largest groups, Indian (Kerala) Christians and English speakers, both say AN-tuh-nee; it is also Mark Antony in English text.

entries.name: Jordan
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Jordan: /ˈdʒɔːdən/

entries.name: Pascal
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Pascal: /pas.kal/; Merriam-Webster, Blaise Pascal: \pa-ˈskal\
entries.notes: The tech-list term reading (the language, the unit) is the usual English reading of the French name: final stress, front 'a'. GB 'a' matches French [a] closely.

entries.name: Shuzhen
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 淑 shū [ʂu], 珍 zhēn [ʈ͡ʂən]; guide stress convention
entries.notes: Pinyin zh [ʈʂ] → j (guide), not zh; -en [ən] is 'un'.

entries.name: Josephine
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Josephine: /ˈdʒəʊzəfiːn/

entries.name: Umar
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic عُمَر (ʿumar): /ʕu.mar/, stress on the first syllable
entries.notes: No y-sound: the Arabic ʿayn is dropped (guide), so today's YOO-mar is wrong. Hausa Umar is the same.

entries.name: Amadou
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Amadou: /a.ma.du/
entries.notes: Only source: French /a.ma.du/ (French names take final stress in English). Bearers speak Wolof, Fula and Bambara; I found no source for their stress. Today's AM-uh-doo may be fine; candidate in us/gb.

entries.name: Georges
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Georges: /ʒɔʁʒ/
entries.notes: One syllable; today reads it as English 'George's'.

entries.name: Lucy
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Lucy: /ˈluːsi/

entries.name: Ahmet
entries.source: Turkish Wiktionary, Ahmet: /ah.ˈmet/
entries.notes: Final stress; today's AH-mət is a guess.

entries.name: Ruby
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Ruby: /ˈɹuːbi/
entries.notes: The tech-list term (Ruby language) and the word 'ruby' are said the same as the name.

entries.name: Zhi
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 志 zhì [ʈ͡ʂʐ̩]: the -i after zh is a buzzed r-like vowel
entries.notes: Pinyin zh → j (guide); the syllabic [ʐ̩] has no English match, and 'jr/jur' is the usual pinyin-teaching approximation. Not 'zhee' as today.

entries.name: Divya
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi दिव्या (divyā): /d̪ɪʋ.jɑː/
entries.notes: Short i (DIV), not 'ee' as today.

entries.name: Zheng
entries.source: Wikipedia, Zheng He: Mandarin [ʈʂə̂ŋ]
entries.notes: Pinyin zh → j (guide), -eng → 'ung' (as in feng shui). Today's 'zeng' is a guess.

entries.name: Ravindra
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi रवींद्र (ravīndra): /ɾə.ʋiːn.d̪ɾᵊ/
entries.notes: Long ī (VEEN), not short i as today.

entries.name: Vinay
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi विनय (vinay): /ʋɪ.nəj/; pronounce.tv: first-syllable stress
entries.notes: Short i, not 'eye' (today VY-nay). Stress kept on the first syllable as today; Hindi stress is weak.

entries.name: Augusto
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Augusto: /awˈɡusto/ (Italian and Portuguese also au-GOO-)
entries.notes: Today's aw-GUST-oh is an English spelling reading.

entries.name: Anjali
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi अंजलि (añjali): /ən.d͡ʒə.liː/
entries.notes: Hindi short a [ə] → 'uh'; stress on the heavy first syllable. Today's ahn-YAH-lee is a guess.

entries.name: Kim
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Kim: /kɪm/
entries.notes: English and Scandinavian Kim are both 'kim'.

entries.name: Biao
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 彪 biāo [pi̯ɑʊ̯]: one syllable
entries.notes: One syllable; today's bee-OW splits it in two.

entries.name: Amrita
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi अमृता (amṛtā): /əm.ɾɪ.t̪ɑː/
entries.notes: Sounds are solid (short a 'uh', ṛ = 'ri' with short i). Stress on the heavy first syllable follows the Hindi weight rule (rightmost non-final heavy); no source marks it, and English speakers often say am-REE-ta.

entries.name: Óscar
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Óscar: /ˈoskaɾ/
entries.notes: The accented spelling is only Spanish; today reads it as English Oscar (AHS-kər).

entries.name: Samantha
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Samantha: /səˈmænθə/

entries.name: Julian
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Julian: /ˈdʒuːli.ən/

entries.name: Laila
entries.source: Wiktionary, Finnish Laila: /ˈlɑi̯lɑ/; Arabic لَيْلَى (laylā) [ˈlaj.laː]
entries.notes: Every bearer group says LYE-la; today's LAY-luh is a guess.

entries.name: Yvonne
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Yvonne: /ɪˈvɒn/; French /i.vɔn/
entries.notes: French and English agree except for unstressed vowels.

entries.name: Salvador
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Salvador: /salbaˈdoɾ/
entries.notes: Capitalised 'Salvador' in English text is very often part of 'El Salvador', said SAL-vuh-dor. A name entry would change the country, so it's protected; the Spanish name reading is recorded for review.

entries.name: Ángel
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Ángel: /ˈanxel/
entries.notes: Spanish g before e is [x] → h; the accented spelling is only Spanish. Today reads it as English 'angel'.

entries.name: Luís
entries.source: Wiktionary, Portuguese Luís: (Brazil) /luˈis/, (Portugal) /luˈiʃ/
entries.notes: Brazilian bearers are the larger group; today's loo-EES is theirs.

entries.name: Gabriela
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Gabriela: /ɡaˈbɾjela/
entries.notes: Stress and stressed vowel match; only unstressed vowels differ.

entries.name: Xavier
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Xavier: /ˈzeɪvi.ə(ɹ)/, /ɪɡˈzeɪvi.ə(ɹ)/; French /ɡza.vje/
entries.notes: The English reading is the largest single group (Catalan, French and Portuguese readings all differ), and it's the reading of Francis Xavier and Xavier University in English text.

entries.name: Khaled
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic خَالِد (ḵālid): /xaː.lid/; the -ed spelling reflects Egyptian/Levantine [ˈxaːled]
entries.notes: Arabic kh → k (guide, as in Khalid). Today's HUL-ed is a spelling guess.

entries.name: Fred
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Fred: /fɹɛd/

entries.name: Ibrahima
entries.source: familyeducation.com: Ib-rah-hee-mah; no dictionary source found
entries.notes: Today's ib-rah-HEE-muh matches the one name-site respelling and how English commentators say it (Ibrahima Konaté). Bearers' own stress is not documented.

entries.name: Rosa
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Rosa: /ˈrosa/

alternatives.context: English (Rosa Parks), Italian [ˈrɔːza] and German [ˈʁoːza] bearers

entries.notes: anglo_share 0.07; Spanish-speaking bearers are the largest group and say s, not z. Review: English text about Rosa Parks would get ROH-suh.

entries.name: Joan
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Joan: /dʒəʊn/

entries.name: Solomon
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Solomon: /ˈsɒləmən/
entries.notes: Most bearers are in English-speaking Africa and use the English reading.

entries.name: Gregory
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Gregory: /ˈɡɹɛɡəɹi/

entries.name: Archana
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi अर्चना (arcanā): /əɾ.t͡ʃə.nɑː/
entries.notes: ch, not k; stress on the heavy first syllable (Hindi weight rule). Today's ar-KAN-uh is a guess.

entries.name: Agnes
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Agnes: /ˈæɡnɪs/; German /ˈaɡnɛs/
entries.notes: Close call: English and the continental readings share the stress; the continental groups split (German AHG-nes, Swedish ANG-nes), so English is the largest single group.

entries.name: Devi
entries.source: Hindi देवी (devī): /d̪eː.ʋiː/; today's DAY-vee matches

entries.name: Jay
entries.notes: Also the word 'jay' (the bird) and the letter J. The name is said the same; today's reading is right.

entries.name: Hannah
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Hannah: /ˈhænə/

entries.name: Jenny
entries.notes: Also the word 'jenny' (female donkey, spinning jenny). The English name is said the same; today's reading is right. Swedish bearers may say YEN-ny.

entries.name: Douglas
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Douglas: /ˈdʌɡləs/

entries.name: Santiago
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Santiago: /sanˈtjaɡo/
entries.notes: Stress and stressed vowel match; tee-AH vs TYAH is unstressed. Same reading as the city.

entries.name: Billy
entries.notes: Also the word 'billy' (billycan, club). The name is said the same; today's reading is right.

entries.name: Vasant
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi वसंत (vasant): /ʋə.sənt̪/
entries.notes: Short a [ə] in both syllables; stress on the superheavy last syllable. Today's VAZ-ənt is a guess.

entries.name: Abd al-Karīm
entries.source: Arabic عبد الكريم ʿAbd al-Karīm: stress on the long -rīm; Wiktionary, English Karim: /kəˈɹiːm/
entries.notes: ʿAbd as in the guide (ʿayn dropped). Today's AL-kuh-rim stresses the wrong syllable.

entries.name: Adel
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic عَادِل (ʿādil): /ʕaː.dil/; the -el spelling reflects Egyptian/Maghrebi [ˈʕaːdel]
entries.notes: Stress on the long first syllable; today's uh-DEL is a guess.

entries.name: Evelyn
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Evelyn: /ˈɛvəlɪn/

entries.name: Adil
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic عَادِل (ʿādil): /ʕaː.dil/
entries.notes: Arabic and Urdu stress the long first syllable.

entries.name: António
entries.source: Wiktionary, Portuguese António: /ɐ̃ˈtɔ.nju/
entries.notes: This accented spelling is European Portuguese: open ó [ɔ], final -io [ju].

entries.name: Vishal
entries.source: Hindi विशाल (viśāl): long ā in the last syllable (Wiktionary, Sanskrit /ʋi.ɕɑː.lɐ/)
entries.notes: Stress on the superheavy last syllable; today's VISH-əl is a guess.

entries.name: Kailash
entries.source: Hindi कैलाश (kailāś): ai [ɛː], long ā; stress on the superheavy last syllable
entries.notes: Hindi ai is [ɛː]. Today's KAY-ləsh stresses the wrong syllable.

entries.name: Da
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 大 dà [tä]
entries.notes: Also the common short form 'da' (dad; 'the' in dialect) and capitalised in names like Da Vinci and Da Nang. The Chinese name is DAH; protected, name reading recorded.

entries.name: Zémín
entries.source: Wikipedia, Jiang Zemin: Mandarin [tɕjáŋ tsɤ̌.mǐn]; guide stress convention
entries.notes: Pinyin z [ts] → dz (guide), e [ɤ] → 'uh'. Today's ZEE-min is a guess.

entries.name: Joaquim
entries.source: Wiktionary, Portuguese Joaquim: (Brazil) /ʒo.aˈkĩ/, (Portugal) /ʒwɐˈkĩ/
entries.notes: Portuguese j is zh; final -im is a nasal 'ee' (English adds n). Today's wah-KEEM is the Spanish Joaquín.

entries.name: Tommy
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Tommy: /ˈtɒmi/
entries.notes: Swedish and Norwegian Tommy [ˈtɔmːy] is close.

entries.name: Irfan
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic عِرْفَان (ʿirfān): /ʕir.faːn/, stress on the long last syllable
entries.notes: Urdu, Turkish (İrfan) and Arabic all stress -FAHN; today's UR-fən is a guess.

entries.name: Sofia
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Sofía/Italian Sofia: /soˈfia/

alternatives.context: some British bearers; Sofia, Bulgaria, in British English

entries.notes: GB-only fix: the British voice says SOH-fee-uh; bearers (Spanish, Italian, Swedish, Finnish and most English speakers) say so-FEE-a. US is right. Note it also changes the British reading of the Bulgarian capital.

entries.name: Xī
entries.source: Wikipedia, Xi Jinping: Mandarin [ɕǐ]
entries.notes: Pinyin x → sh (guide); today's 'zye' is a spelling guess.

entries.name: Charlie
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Charlie: /ˈtʃɑːli/

entries.name: Henri
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Henri: /ɑ̃.ʁi/
entries.notes: French h is silent; final stress. English text about Henri Matisse uses this reading too.

entries.name: Ved
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi वेद (ved): /ʋeːd̪/
entries.notes: Long e 'ay' (as in Veda), not 'ved'.

entries.name: Stella
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Stella: /ˈstɛlə/; Italian /ˈstɛl.la/
entries.notes: English, Italian, Greek and French agree.

entries.name: Vikas
entries.source: Hindi विकास (vikās): short i, long ā; stress on the superheavy last syllable
entries.notes: Today's VY-kəz is a spelling guess.

entries.name: Eddie
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Eddie: /ˈɛdi/

entries.name: Judith
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Judith: /ˈdʒuːdɪθ/

entries.name: Akbar
entries.notes: Readings conflict and none is clearly the largest: Persian اکبر [ʔækˈbæɾ] (final stress; Iran has the most notable bearers), Urdu/Hindi अकबर /ək.bəɾ/ (UK-bər), Arabic and Indonesian [ˈakbar] (AHK-bar). Today's AK-bər (ˈækbəɹ) is the English reading of Akbar the Great. Needs a decision on which population to follow.

entries.name: Samson
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Samson: /ˈsæmsən/
entries.notes: Bearers are mostly in English-speaking Africa; English reading.

entries.name: Leonard
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Leonard: /ˈlɛnəd/

entries.name: Herbert
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Herbert: /ˈhɜːbət/

entries.name: Emilio
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Emilio: /eˈmiljo/
entries.notes: Stress and stressed vowel match; only unstressed vowels differ.

entries.name: Amina
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic أَمِينَة (ʔamīna): /ʔa.miː.na/

alternatives.context: Āmina (آمنة), e.g. Hausa Queen Amina; Bosnian bearers

entries.notes: Today's uh-MEE-nuh matches; only the unstressed first vowel differs.

entries.name: Sophie
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Sophie: /ˈsəʊfi/; French /sɔ.fi/; German /zoˈfiː/
entries.notes: Close call: register counts give US+UK+IE+CA about 259k against France 241k, and the UK counts start late; German bearers say zo-FEE, a third reading. English kept as the largest single group; worth a second look.

entries.name: Mariano
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Mariano: /maˈɾjano/
entries.notes: Mainly a GB fix: the British voice uses the 'lot' vowel in the stressed syllable (-ON-). US first syllable 'mah', not 'mare'.

entries.name: Melissa
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Melissa: /məˈlɪsə/

entries.name: Josef
entries.source: Wiktionary, German Josef: /ˈjoːzɛf/; Czech /ˈjozɛf/
entries.notes: J is a y-sound; today's JOH-səf is an English reading of a German/Czech spelling.

entries.name: Monika
entries.source: Wiktionary, German Monika: /ˈmoːnika/; Czech, Slovak and Lithuanian also stress MO-
entries.notes: Today's MAH-ni-kuh is English Monica. Initial-stress groups (German, Austrian, Czech, Slovak, Lithuanian) together outnumber Polish.

entries.name: Stefan
entries.source: Wiktionary, Polish Stefan: /ˈstɛ.fan/
entries.notes: Close call: German/Austrian SHTEF-ahn is the largest single country group, but Polish, Swedish, Dutch, Balkan and English bearers all say STEF-ahn, together more. Today's reading kept.

entries.name: Félix
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Félix: /ˈfeliks/
entries.notes: The accented spelling is Spanish and French; Spanish-speaking bearers are the larger group. Both say 'fay', not today's English 'fee'.

entries.name: Nabil
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic نَبِيل (nabīl): /na.biːl/, stress on the long last syllable
entries.notes: Today's nah-BEE drops the final l.

entries.name: Sunny
entries.notes: Also the word 'sunny'. The name (English, and Indian Sunny as in Sunny Deol) is said the same; today's reading is right.

entries.name: Hari
entries.source: Hindi हरि (hari): short a [ə], short i (Wiktionary हरि)
entries.notes: Hindi short a is 'uh', not 'ah'.

entries.name: Naveen
entries.source: Hindi नवीन (navīn): /nə.ʋiːn/; today's nuh-VEEN matches

entries.name: Sharad
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi शरद (śarad): /ʃə.ɾəd̪/ (stress not marked); pronounce.tv: first-syllable stress
entries.notes: Both vowels are short a [ə] ('uh'), not 'a' as in 'sad'. Stress is weak in Hindi and analyses differ; first-syllable stress follows the two-syllable rule and the name site.

entries.name: Derek
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Derek: /ˈdɛɹɪk/

entries.name: Angel
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Ángel: /ˈanxel/

alternatives.context: English-speaking bearers, mostly women; the word 'angel'

entries.notes: Also the common word 'angel'. Most bearers are Spanish speakers (AHN-hel), recorded here; protected so the word keeps its reading.

entries.name: Cristina
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Cristina: /kɾisˈtina/; Italian /kriˈsti.na/
entries.notes: Today's kris-TEE-nuh matches; only the unstressed first vowel is reduced.

entries.name: Philippe
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Philippe: /fi.lip/
entries.notes: Today adds a final 'ay' (fi-LEE-pay); the French final e is silent. French names take final stress in English.

entries.name: Mauricio
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Mauricio: /mauˈɾiθjo/, Latin America /mauˈɾisjo/
entries.notes: Today's mow-REE-see-oh matches; it only splits the final -io into two syllables (as accepted for Antonio and Mario).

entries.name: Daniela
entries.region: Spain, Italy, Germany, Latin America, Brazil
entries.source: Wiktionary, Italian Daniela: /daˈnjɛ.la/; Spanish /daˈnjela/

alternatives.context: Spanish, German and Romanian bearers (close e): dahn-YAY-luh

entries.notes: Bearers split between an open e (Italian, Portuguese, Polish, English) and a close e (Spanish, German, Romanian); today's dan-YEL-uh matches the first group, and the unstressed first vowel is only reduced.

entries.name: Vera
entries.language: Russian (also German, Spanish, Italian, Czech, Portuguese)
entries.region: Russia, Germany, Spain, Brazil, Czechia, Norway
entries.source: Wiktionary, Russian Вера: [ˈvʲerə]; Macedonian [ˈvɛɾa]; English /ˈvɪəɹə/

alternatives.context: English-speaking bearers (US 84k, UK): VEER-uh; the tech list's reading (Vera Rubin)

entries.notes: Covered by the tech list, which reads VEER-uh on purpose for English bearers. anglo_share 0.05: Russian, German, Spanish, Italian, Czech, Hungarian and Brazilian bearers all have an e vowel (VEH-ra, VAY-ra) and far outnumber English VEER-uh; English 'air' is the nearest sound before r. Review: a visible change for English bearers (Vera Wang, Vera Lynn).

entries.name: Pamela
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Pamela: /ˈpæmələ/

entries.name: Julie
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Julie: /ˈd͡ʒuːli/; French /ʒy.li/
entries.notes: English bearers (US 509k, UK, Ireland, Canada) outnumber French ones.

entries.name: Steve
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Steve: /stiːv/

entries.name: Aishwarya
entries.source: Wikipedia, Aishwarya Rai Bachchan: Hindi [ɛːʃʋəɾjᵊ]
entries.notes: Hindi ai is [ɛː] (the 'e' of bed), not 'eye'; ʋ → w; three syllables, stress on the heavy first syllable (Hindi weight rule; no English source marks stress). GB keeps the r because it starts the last syllable (-rya). Today's EYE-shwair-ee-uh adds a syllable.

entries.name: Pramod

entries.name: Jinlong

entries.notes: -ong is 'oong' (as Long). Today's guess says JIN-lawng. Tones dropped; primary stress on the last syllable and secondary on the first (the guide's convention for two-syllable Chinese given names; no English source gives it).

entries.name: Silvia
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Silvia: /ˈsilbja/; Italian /ˈsil.vja/
entries.notes: anglo_share 0.01: Spanish (ES 120k) and Italian bearers say the stressed i as 'ee'. v is kept as English speakers say it.

entries.name: Fatoumata
entries.region: Senegal, Mali, Guinea, Côte d'Ivoire, France
entries.source: Name sites disagree on stress: NameDrop fah-too-mah-TAH, FamilyEducation fah-TOO-mah-tah, Ask-Oracle fah-too-MAH-tah; no dictionary or IPA source
entries.notes: West African form of Fatima in French spelling. All sources give four full vowels (fah-too-mah-tah), so today's fuh-TOO-muh-tuh reduces them; the stress is unsourced (the Mande and Fula languages use tone, not stress). The candidate follows the French final stress used for Mamadou. Needs bearer audio or a pronunciation dictionary.

entries.name: Kapil
entries.source: Hindi कपिल (kapil) /kə.pɪl/; short a is 'uh' (as Karan)
entries.notes: Today's KAP-ul has the 'a' of 'cat'. First-syllable stress follows the Karan precedent; Hindi stress is weak. Reviewer: the stress is unsourced and contested. Wikipedia's Hindustani stress rule puts it on a final heavy syllable when no other syllable is heavy (its example kidhar kɪ.ˈdʱər), which gives kuh-PIL, as do the Vijay and Ajay precedents; the Karan precedent and the NameDrop respelling (KA-il) stress the first syllable. The vowel fix (uh, not the 'cat' vowel) stands either way.

entries.name: Humberto
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Humberto: /umˈbeɾto/
entries.notes: Spanish h is silent; today's hum-BUR-toh reads the English spelling. e in a closed syllable → ɛ (as Alberto).

entries.name: Katherine

entries.notes: West African form of Sulayman (Solomon). Today's SOO-lee-mayn stresses the first syllable and reads -mane as English 'mane'.

entries.notes: English bearers (US 374k, Ireland, UK) outnumber French ones.

entries.notes: Today's guess says ab-yoo-BAK-er; the u is 'oo' with no y, and the a's are 'ah'. Nigerian bearers (wd NG 85) dominate; Hausa uses tone, so the stress is the usual Nigerian English one.

Tones dropped; primary stress on the last syllable and secondary on the first (the guide's convention for two-syllable Chinese given names; no English source gives it).
