entries.name: Oussama
entries.region: Egypt, Tunisia, Algeria, Morocco, France, Spain
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic أسامة (usāma) /ʔu.saː.ma/, stress on the long ā; today's usˈɑmə matches

entries.name: Farid
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic فريد (farīd) /fa.riːd/; Persian [fæ.ɾíːd]; stress on the long ī
entries.notes: Today's guessed FAIR-ud stresses the wrong syllable.

entries.name: Mário
entries.source: Wiktionary, Portuguese Mário: Brazil /ˈma.ɾi.u/, Portugal /ˈma.ɾju/; unstressed final o is [u]
entries.notes: Today's MAH-ree-oh is the Spanish/Italian Mario; Portuguese final o is 'oo' (as for Paulo).

entries.name: Zhicheng
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 志 zhì [ʈ͡ʂʐ̩], 成 chéng [ʈ͡ʂʰɤŋ]; zhi as in the earlier Zhi entry; guide convention for two-syllable Chinese given names: primary on the last syllable, secondary on the first
entries.notes: Pinyin zh → j, ch → ch; -eng [əŋ] is 'ung' (as for Zheng). The syllabic vowel of zhi has no English match; 'jr' follows the Zhi entry.

entries.name: Ronghua
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 榮 róng [ʐʊŋ], 華 huá [xu̯a]; as for the earlier Rong and Hua entries; guide convention for two-syllable Chinese given names: primary on the last syllable, secondary on the first
entries.notes: Pinyin r → English r; h [x] → h; -ong uses the 'book' vowel. Tones dropped.

entries.name: Gerardo
entries.region: Mexico, US Hispanic, Spain, Argentina, Peru
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Gerardo /xeˈɾaɾdo/
entries.notes: Spanish g before e is [x] → English h. Bearers are overwhelmingly Spanish-speaking (US=54624 largely Mexican-American, ES, MX, AR, PE).

entries.name: Ellen
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Ellen /ˈɛlən/; Swedish/Norwegian and Dutch bearers also say EL-en

entries.name: Faha
entries.notes: Not an attested given-name spelling: Wikidata has no given-name item 'Faha' (only places in Ireland and Germany). The row's native field and its Saudi/Pakistani bearers point to Fahad (فهد, Q23049786); 'Faha' looks like a truncated label of that item.

entries.name: Aminata
entries.region: Senegal, Mali, Guinea, Côte d'Ivoire, France
entries.source: No dictionary IPA found; today's ah-mee-NAH-ta (penultimate stress, all vowels 'ah'/'ee') is the usual English rendering and matches the spelling's vowels
entries.notes: Wolof/Mandinka/Fula name from Amina. French speakers stress the last syllable (a-mi-na-TA); no source settles a preferred English stress, so today's reading is kept (like Ibrahima).

entries.name: Bernardo
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Bernardo /beɾˈnaɾdo/; today's bəɹnˈɑɹdO differs only in the unstressed first vowel

entries.name: Kelvin
entries.region: US, UK, Nigeria, Australia, New Zealand
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Kelvin /ˈkɛlvɪn/
entries.notes: Also the unit 'kelvin' and Lord Kelvin; the name and the word are said the same. Nothing to change.

entries.name: Zhe
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 哲 zhé [ʈ͡ʂɤ]; pinyin e [ɤ] is English 'uh' (as in the earlier Zheng and Zémín entries)
entries.notes: Today's ZHAY reads zh as the 'measure' sound and e as 'ay'. Pinyin zh is unaspirated [ʈʂ] → j.

entries.name: Guowei
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 國 guó [ku̯ɔ], 偉 wěi [u̯eɪ]; as for the earlier Guohua and Wei entries; guide convention for two-syllable Chinese given names: primary on the last syllable, secondary on the first
entries.notes: Today's GOH-way drops the w of guo and stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Ambrose
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Ambrose /ˈæmbɹəʊz/

entries.name: Friedrich
entries.source: Wiktionary, German Friedrich [ˈfʁiːdʁɪç]; German ch → k (guide); today's fɹˈidɹɪk matches

entries.name: Nikola
entries.region: Serbia, Croatia, Bosnia, Montenegro, Czechia, North Macedonia
entries.source: Wiktionary, Nikola: Serbo-Croatian /nǐkola/, Czech [ˈnɪkola], German /ˈnɪkola/ (first-syllable stress)
entries.notes: Serbian, Croatian, Czech and Slovak bearers stress the first syllable (Nikola Tesla [nǐkola]); Bulgarians stress the last; nobody in the main groups says nih-KOH-la.

entries.name: Roland
entries.region: US, Germany, Switzerland, Sweden, Austria; France
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Roland /ˈɹəʊlənd/; German [ˈʁoːlant]; today's ɹˈOlənd (tech list) matches
entries.notes: Covered by the tech list (Roland, the instrument maker) with the same reading. English, German, Swedish, Dutch, Polish and Hungarian bearers stress the first syllable and together outnumber the French.

entries.name: Sami
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic سامي (sāmī) /saː.miː/; Finnish Sami /ˈsɑmi/; today's sˈɑmi matches

entries.name: Heinrich
entries.source: Wiktionary, German Heinrich [ˈhaɪ̯nʁɪç]; German ch → k (guide); today's hˈInɹɪk matches

entries.name: Jiayi
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 佳 jiā [t͡ɕi̯a], 怡 yí [i]; guide convention for two-syllable Chinese given names: primary on the last syllable, secondary on the first
entries.notes: Today's jee-EYE-ee reads yi as 'eye'. The y glide is written so the two syllables stay apart.

entries.name: Xinyu
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 新 xīn [ɕin], 宇 yǔ [y]; ü → 'yoo' (guide); guide convention for two-syllable Chinese given names: primary on the last syllable, secondary on the first
entries.notes: Pinyin x → sh; the front rounded [y] has no English match. Today's ZIN-yoo reads x as z.

entries.name: Liu
entries.source: Wikipedia, Liu Cixin: Mandarin Liú [ljǒʊ]; Wiktionary 劉 liú /li̯oʊ̯³⁵/
entries.notes: Pinyin -iu is short for -iou [joʊ]: 'lyoh', not 'lyoo'.

entries.name: He
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 何 hé / 和 hé [xɤ]
entries.notes: Also the English pronoun 'He', which starts countless sentences: the name reading must not replace it. Name reading in us/gb: pinyin h [x] → h, e [ɤ] → 'uh'.

entries.name: Siyuan
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 思 sī [sz̩], 遠 yuǎn [ɥɛn]; guide convention for two-syllable Chinese given names: primary on the last syllable, secondary on the first
entries.notes: Pinyin si has an apical vowel, close to 'suh'; yuan is one syllable [ɥɛn] ('ywen'). Today's see-oo-AHN gives three syllables and the wrong vowels.

entries.name: Chunhua
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 春 chūn [ʈ͡ʂʰu̯ən], 華 huá [xu̯a]; guide convention for two-syllable Chinese given names: primary on the last syllable, secondary on the first
entries.notes: Pinyin -un after ch is -uen [wən], 'wun' (as for Wenbin). Today's CHUN-hwuh drops the w and stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Chu
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 楚 chǔ [ʈ͡ʂʰu]; Korean 추 [tɕʰu]; today's ʧˈu matches

entries.name: Jiàn
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 建 jiàn [t͡ɕi̯ɛn]; as in the earlier Jiànpíng and Jianguo entries
entries.notes: Pinyin -ian is [jɛn] ('yen'); today's JEE-un splits it into two syllables.

entries.name: Kē
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 科 kē [kʰɤ]; pinyin e [ɤ] is English 'uh'
entries.notes: Today the app says only a k sound (no vowel).

entries.name: Veronica
entries.region: US, UK, Canada, Ireland; Italy, Romania
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Veronica /vəˈɹɒnɪkə/; today's vəɹˈɑnəkə / vɪɹˈɒnɪkə matches
entries.notes: The English reading is the largest single group (US=207203; Spanish speakers mostly write Verónica). Italian and Romanian differ mainly in the full unstressed vowels.

entries.name: Aamir
entries.source: Wikipedia, Aamir Khan: [ˈaːmɪr xaːn]
entries.notes: The doubled aa marks a long first vowel that carries the stress; today's ah-MEER stresses the second syllable.

entries.name: Joey
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Joey /ˈdʒəʊi/
entries.notes: Also the word 'joey' (a young kangaroo), said the same. Nothing to change.

entries.name: Nandita
entries.source: Hindi नंदिता (nanditā) [nən̪d̪ɪt̪aː]: short a and short i; stress on the heavy closed first syllable (as for Anjali); Bengali নন্দিতা also stresses the first syllable
entries.notes: Today's nahn-DEE-tuh uses 'ah' for the schwa and a long ee for the short i.

entries.name: Doris
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Doris: UK /ˈdɒɹɪs/, US /ˈdɔɹɪs/; today's dˈɔɹəs / dˈɒɹɪs (tech list) matches
entries.notes: Covered by the tech list (Apache Doris) with the same reading; usage english.

entries.name: Said
entries.source: Wikipedia, Edward Said: /sɑːˈiːd/; Arabic سعيد (saʿīd) [saˈʕiːd]
entries.notes: Also the very common word 'said' (sentence-initial 'Said the...'). Name reading in us/gb: two syllables, sah-EED; the ʿayn is dropped.

entries.name: Priscilla
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Priscilla /pɹɪˈsɪlə/

entries.name: Ruben
entries.source: Wiktionary, Dutch Ruben /ˈry.bə(n)/, Swedish /ˈrʉːbɛn/, English Reuben /ˈɹuːbən/: first-syllable stress; today's ɹˈubən matches

alternatives.context: Spanish speakers (usually spelled Rubén), US Hispanic bearers who drop the accent, Armenian Ruben

entries.notes: Hard call. The registers fold Rubén into this row (ES=131134), but Spanish speakers have their own row (Rubén); bearers who write it without the accent are mostly Dutch, Scandinavian, German, Portuguese (Rúben) and English, all first-syllable stress. US Hispanic bearers who drop the accent say roo-BEN. Worth a review.

entries.name: Raphael
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Raphaël /ʁa.fa.ɛl/; Brazilian Raphael [ʁafaˈɛw]; same final stress as the earlier Rafael entry

alternatives.context: English: the painter, the archangel, English-speaking bearers (RAF-ee-el)

entries.notes: In English text 'Raphael' is mostly the painter or the archangel, always RAF-ee-el (today's reading). Like Jesus, the name reading shouldn't replace it; French, Quebec and Brazilian bearers say ra-fa-EL. Decision worth a review.

entries.name: Mohammed
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Mohammed: /məˈhæməd/ (also /mʊəˈhɑːməd/); today's reading differs only in unstressed vowels

alternatives.context: closer to Arabic Muḥammad; many Arabic-speaking bearers

entries.notes: Control: the app's CMUdict reading (mOhˈæmɪd) is an accepted English reading of this spelling.

entries.name: Tim
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Tim /tɪm/; German and Dutch Tim the same

entries.name: Huiling
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 慧 huì [xu̯eɪ], 玲 líng [liŋ]; as for the earlier Hui entry; guide convention for two-syllable Chinese given names: primary on the last syllable, secondary on the first
entries.notes: Pinyin -ui is short for -uei [weɪ] ('hway'); today's HY-ling reads it as 'eye'.

entries.name: Ida
entries.region: Norway, Sweden, Denmark, Germany, Italy, France
entries.source: Wiktionary, Ida: Italian /ˈi.da/, Dutch /ˈi.daː/, Polish /ˈi.da/; Norwegian, Swedish, Danish and German bearers also say EE-da
entries.notes: anglo_share 0.06 (NO=20093; SE, DK, DE, IT, FR): EE-da is the main reading; the English EYE-duh goes in alternatives.

entries.name: Sultan
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic سلطان (sulṭān) /sul.tˤaːn/; Turkish Sultan, final stress
entries.notes: Also the word 'sultan' (a ruler), read SUL-tun. The name reading (stress on the long final syllable) is in us/gb.

entries.name: Luciano
entries.source: Wiktionary, Italian Luciano /luˈt͡ʃa.no/; Wikipedia, Luciano Pavarotti [luˈtʃaːno]
entries.notes: Italian ci before a vowel is just 'ch'; today's loo-chee-AH-noh adds a syllable.

entries.name: Chloe
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Chloe /ˈkləʊi/

entries.name: Denny
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Denny /ˈdɛni/; Indonesian bearers say it the same way

entries.name: Avinash
entries.source: Hindi अविनाश (avināś) [əʋɪnaːʃ]: stress on the long ā (as for Prakash and Vikas)
entries.notes: Today's AV-in-ash stresses the first syllable and uses 'cat' vowels.

entries.name: Aparna
entries.source: Hindi अपर्णा (aparṇā) [əpəɾɳaː]: short a [ə] before r, as in the earlier Archana entry
entries.notes: Retroflex ṇ is English n. The vowel before r is a schwa, not today's 'ah'.

entries.name: Nakul
entries.source: Hindi नकुल (nakul) [nəkʊl]; today's nɑkˈul differs only in the unstressed first vowel (final stress as for Arun)

entries.name: Manohar
entries.source: Hindi मनोहर (manohar) [mənoːɦəɾ]: stress on the long o
entries.notes: Today's MAN-uh-har stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Subodh
entries.source: Hindi सुबोध (subodh) [sʊboːdʱ]: stress on the long o; aspirated dh as plain d
entries.notes: Today's SUB-ud loses the long o.

entries.name: Sunanda
entries.source: Hindi सुनंदा (sunandā) [sʊnən̪d̪aː]: stress on the heavy closed syllable 'nan'; short a is a schwa
entries.notes: Today's suh-NAN-duh uses the 'cat' vowel for the schwa.

entries.name: Zhihao
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 志 zhì [ʈ͡ʂʐ̩], 豪 háo [xɑʊ̯]; zhi as in the earlier Zhi entry, hao as in Hao; guide convention for two-syllable Chinese given names: primary on the last syllable, secondary on the first
entries.notes: Today's ZHEE-how reads zh as the 'measure' sound and zhi as 'zhee'.

entries.name: Harold
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Harold /ˈhæɹəld/; today's hˈɛɹəld / hˈaɹəld matches (US merged vowel)

entries.name: Usman
entries.source: Urdu عثمان (usmān), from Arabic ʿUthmān [ʕuθˈmaːn]: stress on the long final ā (as for Salman and İmran)
entries.notes: Today's US-mun reads it as an English word. Hausa bearers (NG:41) and Pakistani bearers both keep the long 'ah'.

entries.name: Simone
entries.region: Italy (men); also Germany, Switzerland, Netherlands, Brazil (women)
entries.source: Wiktionary, Simone: Italian /siˈmo.ne/, Brazilian Portuguese /siˈmõ.ni/, French /si.mɔn/, English /səˈməʊn/

alternatives.context: German, Swiss, Austrian and Dutch women (zee-MOH-nuh)
English-speaking bearers (Simone Biles, Nina Simone): today's reading

entries.notes: Hard call, worth a review. Italian (men, IT:622 on Wikidata), German, Dutch and Brazilian bearers all say see-MOH-neh / -nuh / -nee with three syllables, outnumbering the French (see-MON) and English (sih-MOHN) two-syllable readings; Italian is the largest single group.

entries.name: Lakshmi
entries.source: Merriam-Webster, Lakshmi: \ˈlək-shmē\; Hindi लक्ष्मी [ləkʃmiː], short a
entries.notes: Today's LAHK-shmee uses 'ah' for the Hindi schwa.

entries.name: Rekha
entries.source: Wikipedia, Rekha (actress): [ˈreːkʰa]; Hindi रेखा (rekhā)
entries.notes: Hindi e is long [eː] ('ay'); aspirated kh is plain k. Today's REK-uh uses the 'bed' vowel.

entries.name: Anup
entries.source: Hindi अनूप (anūp) [ənuːp]: long ū, stressed
entries.notes: Today's uh-NUP reads the u as in 'up'.

entries.name: Juliana
entries.source: Wiktionary, Juliana: Portuguese (Brazil) /ʒu.liˈɐ̃.nɐ/; Spanish /xuˈljana/; Polish /juˈlja.na/; Dutch /ˌjy.liˈaː.naː/
entries.notes: Brazilian bearers (BR:155 on Wikidata; a very common Brazilian name) are the largest single group. Their stressed vowel is a nasal [ɐ̃], closest to English 'uh'. Worth a review.

entries.name: Marko
entries.source: Wiktionary, Serbo-Croatian Marko /mâːrko/, Finnish /ˈmɑrko/; today's mˈɑɹkO / mˈɑːkQ matches

entries.name: Colin
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Colin: UK /ˈkɒlɪn/ (also /ˈkəʊlɪn/), US /ˈkɑlɪn/ (also /ˈkoʊlɪn/)
entries.notes: Today's KOH-lin is the second reading; British, Irish, Scottish and most American bearers say KOL-in.

entries.name: Noor
entries.region: Pakistan, Malaysia, Arab world, UK; Netherlands
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic نور (nūr) /nuːr/; English has no separate 'oor', so today's nˈʊɹ / nˈʊə (as in 'poor') matches

alternatives.context: Dutch bearers (Noor, a popular Dutch girls' name)

entries.name: Carla
entries.source: Wiktionary, Italian Carla /ˈkar.la/, Spanish /ˈkaɾla/; today's kˈɑɹlə / kˈɑːlə matches

entries.name: Alessandro
entries.source: Wiktionary, Italian Alessandro /a.lesˈsan.dro/
entries.notes: The double s is a voiceless s, not today's z; British today says the stressed a as the 'lot' vowel.

entries.name: Georg
entries.source: Wiktionary, German Georg /ˈɡeː.ɔrk/ (final g devoiced); Norwegian /ˈɡeː.ɔrɡ/; Swedish /ˈjeːɔrj/
entries.notes: German final devoicing: the last sound is k. German-speaking bearers dominate (DE:3735).

entries.name: Rachid
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic رشيد (rašīd) /ra.ʃiːd/; the French spelling ch = sh
entries.notes: Today's RATCH-id reads the French ch as English ch and stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Gita
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi गीता (gītā) [ɡiː.t̪ɑː]; today's ɡˈiTə / ɡˈiːtə matches (the US flap is the app's rendering of t)

entries.name: Farah
entries.region: Arab world, France, UK, Pakistan, India
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic فرح (faraḥ) /ˈfa.raħ/

alternatives.context: English (Farrah Fawcett), some US and UK bearers

entries.notes: Final ḥ is dropped as English speakers do. Today's FAIR-uh is the English Farrah.

entries.name: Hoàng
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese hoàng: Hà Nội [hwaːŋ˨˩], Saigon [waːŋ˨˩]
entries.notes: oa is [wa]; tones dropped. Today's HOHNG reads the o as a vowel.

entries.name: Alina
entries.source: Wiktionary, Polish Alina /aˈli.na/; today's əlˈinə differs only in the unstressed first vowel

entries.name: Ferdinand
entries.region: Germany, Austria, Belgium, Netherlands, Czechia; France
entries.source: Wiktionary, German Ferdinand [ˈfɛʁdinant]; Dutch /ˈfɛr.di.nɑnt/

alternatives.context: English: historical figures (Franz Ferdinand, King Ferdinand) and English-speaking bearers

entries.notes: anglo_share 0.01: German, Austrian, Dutch, Belgian and Czech bearers say FAIR-dee-nahnt (first-syllable stress, final t). Today's FUR-di-nand is the English form of historical names.

entries.name: Clement
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Clement /ˈklɛmənt/
entries.notes: Also the adjective 'clement' (mild); the name and the word are said the same. The French Clément is a separate spelling.

entries.name: Lihua
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 麗 lì [li], 華 huá [xu̯a]; as for the earlier Hua entry; guide convention for two-syllable Chinese given names: primary on the last syllable, secondary on the first
entries.notes: Today's LEE-hwah stresses the first syllable; otherwise the sounds match.

entries.name: Indra
entries.source: Merriam-Webster, Indra: \ˈin-drə\; Indonesian /ˈindra/; today's ˈɪndɹə matches

entries.name: Bruce
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Bruce /bɹuːs/

entries.name: Ernst
entries.source: Wiktionary, German Ernst /ɛʁnst/; Norwegian /ærnst/
entries.notes: German short e is the 'bed' vowel; today's URNST is the English 'earnest' vowel.

entries.name: Nilesh
entries.source: Hindi/Marathi नीलेश (nīleś) [niːleːʃ]; today's nˌɪlˈɛʃ matches in the stressed syllable (e in a closed syllable → ɛ, as for Ramesh and Mahesh) and differs only in the unstressed first vowel

entries.name: Jitendra
entries.source: Hindi जितेंद्र (jitendra) [dʒɪt̪eːnd̪ɾə]; today's ʤɪtˈɛndɹə matches (closed-syllable e → ɛ)

entries.name: Diane
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Diane /daɪˈæn/; today's dIˈæn matches

entries.name: Natalie
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Natalie /ˈnætəli/

entries.name: Akash
entries.source: Hindi आकाश (ākāś) [aːkaːʃ]: both vowels long ā, stress on the second (as for Prakash)
entries.notes: Today's uh-KASH uses the 'cat' vowel for a long ā.

entries.name: Iris
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Iris /ˈaɪɹɪs/

alternatives.context: Continental bearers (France, Spain, Germany, Netherlands, Norway): EE-ris

entries.notes: Also the words 'iris' (eye, flower). usage english: the English name reading equals the word's, so nothing to change.

entries.name: Geoffrey
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Geoffrey /ˈd͡ʒɛfɹi/

entries.name: Jackson
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Jackson /ˈd͡ʒæksən/

entries.name: Edith
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Edith /ˈiːdɪθ/
entries.notes: usage english: the English reading.

entries.name: Franco
entries.source: Wiktionary, Italian Franco /ˈfraŋ.ko/, Spanish /ˈfɾanko/
entries.notes: Italian and Spanish stressed a is 'ah', not today's 'cat' vowel.

entries.name: Nicolás
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Nicolás /nikoˈlas/
entries.notes: The accent marks final stress; today's NIK-uh-lus is the English Nicholas.

entries.name: Paulus
entries.source: Wiktionary, Dutch Paulus /ˈpɑu̯.lʏs/; Czech [ˈpau̯lus], Finnish /ˈpɑu̯lus/
entries.notes: au is the 'ow' diphthong for Dutch, German, Indonesian and Scandinavian bearers.

entries.name: Zihao
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 子 zǐ [t͡sz̩], 豪 háo [xɑʊ̯]; z as dz (as in the earlier Zémín entry); guide convention for two-syllable Chinese given names: primary on the last syllable, secondary on the first
entries.notes: Pinyin z is unaspirated [ts] → dz; the apical vowel of zi is close to 'uh'. Today's ZEE-how reads zi as 'zee'.

entries.name: Gordon
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Gordon /ˈɡɔːdən/

entries.name: Hermann
entries.source: Wiktionary, German Hermann /ˈhɛʁ.man/
entries.notes: The double-n spelling is German; German short e is 'air' before r and the a stays full.

entries.name: Manu
entries.source: Wiktionary, Finnish Manu /ˈmɑnu/; today's mˈɑnu / mˈɑːnuː matches

entries.name: Crystal
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Crystal /ˈkɹɪstəl/
entries.notes: Also the word 'crystal', said the same. Nothing to change.

entries.name: Fu
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 福 fú [fu]; today's fˈu matches

entries.name: Mohamad
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic مُحَمَّد (muḥammad) /mu.ħam.mad/; Malay Mohamad [moˈhamad]
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today uses the 'lot' vowel (muh-HOM-ud); the stressed a is 'ah'. US unchanged.

entries.name: Thierry
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Thierry /tjɛ.ʁi/; Wikipedia, Thierry Henry: French [tjɛʁi]
entries.notes: French th is t; today's thih-REE reads it as English th.

entries.name: Youssef
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic يوسف (yūsuf), Egyptian/Maghrebi [ˈjuːsef]; today's jˈusɛf matches

entries.name: Si
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 思 sī [sz̩]
entries.notes: Also the words 'si' (Spanish/Italian 'yes', the musical note) and the British nickname Si for Simon (SIGH). The Chinese name reading in us/gb is approximate: the apical vowel of si has no English match ('suh').

entries.name: Di
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 迪 dí [ti]; unaspirated d → d; today's dˈi matches

alternatives.context: English short form of Diana/Diane (Princess Di; Australian and British bearers)

entries.notes: In British and Australian text 'Di' is often the short form of Diana (DYE), a different reading. Chinese bearers lead the counts, so today's reading stays; worth a review.

entries.name: Xi
entries.source: Wikipedia, Xi Jinping: /ˈʃiː dʒɪnˈpɪŋ/; Wiktionary 習 xí [ɕi]
entries.notes: Collision with the Greek letter xi is technical and rare in capitalised form (XI in caps is untouched); the name, mostly Xi Jinping, is what readers meet. Treated as a name, as the guide allows.
entries.word_check: gold has 'xi'; kept: the Greek letter is written 'xi' or ξ; capitalised Xi is the name (Xi Jinping)

entries.name: Brenda

entries.name: Cong

entries.notes: Pinyin c is [tsʰ], not k; today's KONG reads it as English c.

entries.name: Zhang
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 張 zhāng [ʈ͡ʂɑŋ]; English rendering /dʒɑːŋ/
entries.notes: Pinyin zh is unaspirated [ʈʂ] → j; a is 'ah'. Today's ZHANG uses the 'measure' sound and the 'cat' vowel.

entries.name: Hashim
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic هاشم (hāšim) /ˈhaː.ʃim/
entries.notes: Long ā is 'ah', not the 'cat' vowel of today's HASH-im.

entries.name: Shuai
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 帥 shuài [ʂu̯aɪ]; as for the earlier Shuang entry
entries.notes: One syllable: today's SHOO-eye splits it in two.

entries.name: Franck
entries.region: France, Cameroon, Côte d'Ivoire, DR Congo
entries.source: Wikipedia, César Franck: French [fʁɑ̃k]; Wiktionary French Franck
entries.notes: French nasal ɑ̃ → 'ahn' (guide). Today's FRANK is the English Frank.

entries.name: Boris
entries.region: Slovenia, Germany, Croatia, Serbia, Czechia, UK
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Boris: UK /ˈbɒɹɪs/, US /ˈbɔɹɪs/; Serbo-Croatian and Slovene Boris, first-syllable stress
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today says BAW-ris; British and South Slavic bearers use the short 'lot' vowel. US unchanged.

entries.name: Tania
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Tania /ˈtanja/; English UK /ˈtɑːnjə/
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today says TON-ya (lot vowel). US unchanged.

entries.name: Laurent
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Laurent /lɔ.ʁɑ̃/
entries.notes: French names are stressed on the last syllable in English; nasal ɑ̃ → 'ahn' and the t is silent. Today's LOR-unt is a spelling pronunciation.

entries.name: Kazi
entries.source: Urdu قاضی (qāzī) [ˈqaːziː]; Wikipedia, Kazi Nazrul Islam: Bengali [kad͡ʒi]

alternatives.context: Bengali pronunciation (KAH-jee), Bangladeshi and West Bengal bearers

entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today says KOZ-ee (lot vowel); both Urdu and Bengali have a long 'ah'. US unchanged. Bengali speakers say the z as j in their own language; the z of the spelling is kept here.

entries.name: Pradip
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi प्रदीप: /pɾə.d̪iːp/ [pɾɐ.d̪iːp]; stress on the heavy final syllable
entries.notes: Hindi short a is schwa and ī is a long 'ee'; today's PRAD-ip reads it as an English word.

entries.name: Murtuza
entries.source: Azerbaijani spelling of Arabic murtaḍā (Wikipedia, Murtuza Mukhtarov: Azerbaijani 'Murtuza Muxtarov'); Azerbaijani orthography is phonemic and names take final stress, as Persian Morteza does
entries.notes: Today's mur-TOO-zuh stresses the middle syllable. No IPA source for this exact spelling; the reading follows the regular Azerbaijani spelling and stress. South Asian bearers' stress (Urdu Murtaza) is not sourced.

entries.name: Tenzin

entries.notes: Standard Tibetan བསྟན་འཛིན་ is also TEN-zin; today's reading matches.

entries.name: Ray

entries.name: Abigail
entries.notes: Also the word 'abigail' (archaic: a lady's maid). The name is said the same, AB-ih-gayl; today's ˈæbəɡˌAl / ˈabɪɡAl is the English reading of the main bearers (US, UK), so nothing needs to ship.

entries.name: Bob
entries.notes: Ordinary word 'bob'. The name is said like the word, BOB; today's bˈɑb / bˈɒb is right.

entries.name: Luigi
entries.source: Wiktionary, Luigi: Italian /luˈi.d͡ʒi/; English /luˈiːd͡ʒi/

entries.name: Gilberto
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Gilberto: /xilˈbeɾto/ [xilˈβ̞eɾ.t̪o]; Brazilian Portuguese /ʒiwˈbɛʁ.tu/; Italian /d͡ʒilˈbɛr.to/
entries.notes: Spanish g before i is [x] → h (guide). The US 27.8k births are mostly Hispanic; with Spain and Mexico the Spanish reading is the largest group. Today's hard g matches only Tagalog.

entries.name: Elvis

entries.name: Gladys
entries.source: Light verification: the app's dictionary reading is the established English one (/ˈɡlædɪs/)
entries.notes: US 115k English-speaking bearers are the largest single group.

entries.notes: Today's BEE-triz reads it as English Beatrice. Spain (ES 122k), Latin America and Brazil all stress the last syllable.

entries.name: Kimberly
entries.source: Light verification: the app's dictionary reading is the established English one (/ˈkɪmbəli/)

entries.name: Terry
entries.notes: Also the word 'terry' (terry cloth). The name is said like the word, TERR-ee; today's tˈɛɹi is right.

entries.name: Jules

alternatives.context: English nickname (Julian, Julia) and the tech list's reading (today's)

Decision to review: English text about Jules Verne often says JOOLZ, and the tech-list product reading would change too.

entries.name: Wilfred
entries.source: Light verification: the app's dictionary reading is the established English one (/ˈwɪlfɹɪd/)
entries.notes: Dutch and African bearers keep the same stress and vowels.

entries.notes: Ordinary word 'prince'. The name (Ghana, Nigeria, US) is said like the word, PRINS; today's pɹˈɪns is right.

entries.name: Kyle
entries.source: Light verification: the app's dictionary reading is the established English one (/kaɪl/)

entries.notes: US 171k English-speaking bearers outnumber French ones.

entries.name: Atul

entries.name: Leandro
entries.source: Wiktionary, Leandro: Spanish /leˈandɾo/, Italian /leˈan.dro/; Portuguese (Brazil) /leˈɐ̃.dɾu/, (Portugal) /ˈljɐ̃.dɾu/

entries.notes: GB-only fix: the British voice says the 'lot' vowel (ɒ) for the stressed 'ah'; bearers say ɑː. US already right. entries.name: Valentina

entries.name: Tamara

entries.name: Elisabeth

entries.name: Martín

entries.name: Axel
entries.drop_detail: the skating jump is written 'Axel' in capitals ('a triple Axel')
entries.source: Wiktionary Axel: Swedish /¹aksɛl/, German /ˈaksl̩/, Dutch /ˈɑk.səl/, French /ak.sɛl/, English /ˈæk.səl/
entries.notes: Swedish, German, Danish and Dutch bearers share AHK-sul; British today already says it with the short a (as for Hans). US-only fix. Review.

entries.name: Valerie
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Valerie /ˈvæləɹi/

entries.name: Richa
entries.source: Hindi ऋचा (ṛcā): ṛ is [ɾɪ] in Hindi; today's ɹˈɪʧə matches

entries.name: Namrata
entries.source: Hindi नम्रता (namratā) by Devanagari spelling: short a [ə]; stress on the heavy closed first syllable
entries.notes: Today's nam-RAT-uh uses the 'cat' vowel and stresses the light middle syllable.

entries.name: Lalitha
entries.source: South Indian spelling of Sanskrit ललिता (lalitā): th is the dental t [t̪]; Dravidian languages stress the first syllable (as for Kamala, /ˈkɑːmələ/)
entries.notes: Today's luh-LITH-uh reads th as in 'thin'; in Indian spelling th is a dental t.

entries.name: Austin
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Austin /ˈɒstɪn/, /ˈɔstɪn/

entries.name: Salma
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic سلمى (salmā) /sal.maː/; Spanish Salma /ˈsalma/
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today uses the 'lot' vowel (SOL-muh). US already right.

entries.name: Iván
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Iván: /iˈban/ [iˈβan]; the accent marks the final stress
entries.notes: Spanish bearers (Spain, Argentina, Peru, Colombia, Mexico) far outnumber the Hungarian ones. Spanish v [β] is said v by English speakers, as the Ivan precedent (ivˈɑn). Today's EYE-vun is the English Ivan.

entries.name: Lola
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Lola: /ˈlola/; English /ˈloʊlə/
entries.notes: Spanish, English and German bearers all say LOH-luh, together more than the French register.

entries.name: Esteban
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Esteban: /esˈteban/
entries.notes: Today's ES-tuh-bahn stresses the first syllable; Spanish stresses -te- (penultimate rule for a word ending in n). Stressed e in an open syllable is 'ay' (guide table); the soft [β] is said b.

entries.name: Nadine
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Nadine: /na.din/; English /neɪˈdiːn/
entries.notes: Today's nuh-DEEN keeps the stressed DEEN; only the unstressed first vowel differs. German bearers also stress -dee-.

entries.name: Cheryl
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Cheryl: /ˈʃɛɹəl/

entries.name: Luisa
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Luisa: /ˈlwisa/

alternatives.context: Italian (/luˈi.za/) and German bearers, voiced z; today's reading

entries.notes: Spanish bearers (ES register 39k, plus Mexico, Colombia, Peru and US Hispanic) are the largest group, and Spanish has no z sound (as the José precedent). The u is kept as its own 'oo', as the Luis precedent. Today's loo-EE-zuh is the Italian and German reading; the population call is a judgment.

entries.name: Gideon
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Gideon: /ˈɡɪdi.ən/

alternatives.context: Israeli bearers (Hebrew Gid'on, e.g. Gideon Sa'ar), final stress

entries.notes: US, UK and Canadian registers, plus the biblical Gideon (and Gideon Bibles) in English text, read GID-ee-un.

entries.name: Kenny
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Kenny: /ˈkɛni/
entries.notes: English bearers (US 52k) are the largest group; Dutch, Belgian and Scandinavian bearers also say KEN-ee.

entries.name: Joël
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Joël: /ʒɔ.ɛl/
entries.notes: The diaeresis splits o-ë into two syllables; French names take final stress in English, and French ɔ before ɛ is said 'oh' as in English Noël /noʊˈɛl/. Today's JOHL is the English Joel in one syllable with an English j.

entries.name: Andrzej
entries.source: Wiktionary, Polish Andrzej: /ˈan.dʐɛj/; Wikipedia, Andrzej Wajda: [ˈandʐɛj]
entries.notes: Polish drz is one sound [dʐ], nearest English j; ej is 'ay'. Today's AHN-dray reads rz as r.

entries.name: Aloysius
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Aloysius: RP /æl.əʊˈɪʃ.əs/ (also /æl.əʊˈɪs.ɪəs/)
entries.notes: Today's al-oh-ISH-us matches; Dutch and German bearers (a-lo-EE-zee-us) are few.

entries.name: Pietro
entries.source: Wiktionary, Italian Pietro: /ˈpjɛ.tro/
entries.notes: Today's pee-ET-roh keeps the stressed 'et' and the consonants; the i is the glide, as the Luis precedent.

entries.name: Malcolm
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Malcolm: /ˈmælkəm/

entries.name: Hervé
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Hervé: /ɛʁ.ve/
entries.notes: French h is silent and é is 'ay'; French names take final stress in English. Today's HURV reads it as an English word.

entries.name: Camille
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Camille: /ka.mij/
entries.notes: French bearers (FR register 244k, plus Belgium, Switzerland, Luxembourg and Quebec) outnumber the English kuh-MEEL group. French -ille after i is [j], with no l; the faint final y glide is dropped. Decision to review: this changes US bearers' kuh-MEEL.

entries.name: Zhizhong
entries.source: Pinyin zhìzhōng (志忠): zh [ʈʂ], syllabic zhi [ʈʂʐ̩], -ong [ʊŋ]; precedents Zhi, Zhihong
entries.notes: zh → j (guide); the buzzing vowel of zhi is 'jr' as in the Zhi entry; -ong is 'oong'. Today's guess says ZHIZ-hawng, reading zh as the 'measure' sound and splitting z-h. Tones dropped; primary stress on the last syllable and secondary on the first (the guide's convention for two-syllable Chinese given names, no English source).

entries.name: Jacky
entries.source: French spelling rules: j [ʒ], final -y [i]; a French diminutive of Jacques (Wiktionary gives no IPA)

alternatives.context: English-speaking bearers and Hong Kong/Chinese English names (Jacky Cheung); today's reading

entries.notes: anglo_share 0.01: the FR register (69k births) dwarfs the US, UK and Canada (about 8.6k). French names take final stress in English. Decision to review: Hong Kong, Taiwanese and mainland Chinese English-name bearers (JAK-ee) are hard to count.

entries.name: Sammy
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Sammy: /ˈsæmi/
entries.notes: Kenyan and Belgian bearers use the same reading.

entries.name: Kingsley
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Kingsley: /ˈkɪŋzli/
entries.notes: Nigerian and Ghanaian bearers use the English reading.

entries.name: Maxwell
entries.notes: Also the word 'maxwell' (the CGS unit of magnetic flux) and the surname (James Clerk Maxwell), all said the same as the name. Nothing needs to ship.

entries.name: Manfred
entries.source: Wiktionary, German Manfred: /ˈma(ː)nˌfʁeːd/ [ˈma(ː)nˌfʁ̥eːt]
entries.notes: anglo_share 0.0: German, Austrian and Swiss bearers. German a is 'ah'; the second element keeps its long e ('fray') with secondary stress, and final d is said t (final devoicing). Today's MAN-frid is the English reading.

entries.name: Violet
entries.notes: Ordinary word 'violet' (the flower and the colour). Name and word sound the same, so nothing needs to ship.

entries.name: May
entries.notes: Ordinary word 'may' (the modal verb) and the month May. English bearers say it like the word; Norwegian bearers (NO register 8k) say 'my' (alternative). Never replace the word.

entries.name: Fiona
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Fiona: /fiˈoʊnə/
entries.notes: Scottish, Irish and English bearers all say fee-OH-nuh.

entries.name: Ling
entries.notes: Also the word 'ling' (a fish; heather). The Chinese name 灵/玲 líng is said the same (lˈɪŋ), so nothing needs to ship.

entries.name: Lou
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Lou: /lu/; English Lou: /luː/
entries.notes: French and English readings agree.

entries.name: Nelly
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Nelly: /ˈnɛli/
entries.notes: Readings split: French ne-LEE (FR 64k) against NEL-ee in English, Spanish (Peru, Argentina), German, Dutch and Norwegian. Together the NEL-ee group is likely larger, so today's reading stays; decision to review.

entries.name: Filipe
entries.source: Wiktionary, Portuguese Filipe: Portugal /fiˈli.pɨ/, Brazil /fiˈli.pi/
entries.notes: Portugal leads (wd PT 123, BR 50; most Brazilians write Felipe). Unstressed final [ɨ] → 'uh'. Today's FIL-up stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Artyom
entries.source: Wiktionary, Russian Артём: /ɐrˈtʲɵm/
entries.notes: Russian ё is always stressed, so the stress is on the last syllable; today's guess stresses AR.

entries.name: Jesus
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Jesús: /xeˈsus/
entries.notes: In English text 'Jesus' is overwhelmingly Jesus of Nazareth, read JEE-zus (today's reading). Bearers of the given name are mostly Hispanic (US 239k, Spain 257k, Mexico) and say hay-SOOS; that reading is in us/gb but must not replace the English one (guide).

entries.name: Malika
entries.source: Wikipedia, Malika Oufkir: Arabic مليكة (Malīka, long ī); Arabic stress falls on the long penultimate ī (no IPA on the page)

alternatives.context: Arabic ملكة malika 'queen' and some Hindi bearers (Mālikā)
Uzbek and Central Asian bearers, final stress

entries.notes: The register bearers are mostly Maghrebi (FR 24k, ES 7k, Morocco, Algeria), whose Malika is مليكة with a long stressed ī. Today's MAL-ik-uh stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Chunsheng
entries.source: Pinyin chūnshēng (春生): ch [ʈʂʰ], -un [wən], sh [ʂ], -eng [əŋ]; precedents Chunhua, Sheng
entries.notes: -un after ch is -uen [wən] ('wun', as Chunhua); -eng is 'ung' (as Sheng). Today's guess says CHUN-sheng. Tones dropped; primary stress on the last syllable and secondary on the first (the guide's convention for two-syllable Chinese given names, no English source).

entries.name: Françoise
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Françoise: /fʁɑ̃.swaz/
entries.notes: GB-only fix: today's British fɹanswˈɒz ends in the 'lot' vowel; French [a] here is 'ah'. US already right; nasal ɑ̃ → 'ahn' as in François.

entries.name: Rustam
entries.source: Wiktionary, Tajik Рустам: /rusˈtam/ [ɾus.t̪ʰám]
entries.notes: Russian, Tatar, Uzbek, Tajik and Azerbaijani bearers stress the last syllable (from Persian Rostam). Today's RUS-tum stresses the first.

entries.name: Carolyn
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Carolyn: US /ˈkɛɹəlɪn/, UK /ˈkæɹəlɪn/
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British keeps the 'marry' vowel; today's British reading uses the American merged 'merry' vowel. US unchanged.

entries.name: Janice
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Janice: /ˈdʒænɪs/

entries.name: Tyler
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Tyler: /ˈtaɪlə(ɹ)/

entries.name: Kristina
entries.source: Wiktionary, Kristina: Norwegian Bokmål /krɪˈstiː.na/, Swedish /krɪ²stiːna/, German [kʁɪsˈtiːna]; Russian Кристина [krʲɪˈsʲtʲinə]
entries.notes: Swedish, Norwegian, German, Russian, Slovene and English bearers all stress -STEE-.

entries.name: Innocent
entries.notes: Ordinary word 'innocent'. Nigerian and Ugandan bearers say it like the word; Cameroonian (French) bearers say ee-naw-SAHN. Nothing needs to ship.

entries.name: Xiaotong
entries.source: Pinyin xiǎotóng (晓彤): x [ɕ], -iao [jɑʊ], -ong [ʊŋ]; guide example Xiaoping
entries.notes: x → sh (guide); -iao is 'yow' in one syllable; -ong is 'oong'. Today's guess says ZHOW-tawng. Tones dropped; primary stress on the last syllable and secondary on the first (the guide's convention for two-syllable Chinese given names, no English source).

entries.name: Miên
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese Miên: Hà Nội [miən˧˧], Huế and Saigon [miəŋ˧˧]
entries.notes: iê is the diphthong [iə] in one syllable (as Phương's ươ); tone dropped. Today's US MEEN drops the glide, and British mɪˈɛn makes two syllables stressed on the second.

entries.name: Akhil
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi अखिल: /ə.kʰɪl/ [ɐ.kʰɪl]
entries.notes: Aspirated kh is k; the first vowel is the Hindi schwa. Stress on the heavy final syllable (as Anup, Alok). Today's AK-ul stresses the wrong syllable with the 'cat' vowel.

entries.name: Maureen
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Maureen: /mɔːˈɹiːn/ (US), also /ˈmɔːɹiːn/

alternatives.context: some British and Irish speakers (from Irish Máirín), first-syllable stress

entries.notes: US maw-REEN is the main group (US register 143k).

entries.name: Vishnu
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi विष्णु: /ʋɪʂ.ɳuː/
entries.notes: Today's VISH-noo matches; retroflex ṣ and ṇ become sh and n.

entries.name: Ankit
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi अंकित: /əŋ.kɪt̪/ [ɐ̃ŋ.kɪt̪]
entries.notes: Hindi short a is the schwa, 'uh' when stressed (as Ravi); today's ANK-it uses the 'cat' vowel. First-syllable stress (both syllables heavy; Hindi stresses the non-final one).

entries.name: Ravinder
entries.source: Punjabi ਰਵਿੰਦਰ / Hindi रविंदर (form of Ravindra): ra-vin-dar, the heavy middle syllable carries the stress (Hindi-Punjabi weight rule); no dictionary entry
entries.notes: Hindi short a is the schwa, not today's 'cat' vowel; ʋ → v. Today's RAV-in-der stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Ishita
entries.source: Hindi ईशिता īśitā / Bengali ঈশিতা: long ī, short i, long ā; stress on the heavy first syllable (Hindi weight rule; Bengali stresses the first syllable)
entries.notes: Today's guess stresses -shee- and puts the long vowel on the short i. No dictionary marks the stress; the weight rule and Bengali initial stress agree. Final ā unstressed → 'uh' (as Kalpana).

entries.name: Deep
entries.notes: Ordinary word 'deep'. The Punjabi name ਦੀਪ is said the same (dˈip), so nothing needs to ship.

entries.name: Sumit
entries.source: Hindi सुमित sumit: short u, short i, stress on the heavy final syllable
entries.notes: Today's soo-MIT keeps the stressed 'mit'; the first vowel differs only in length.

entries.name: Inder
entries.source: Punjabi ਇੰਦਰ (Indar): heavy first syllable stressed, final schwa
entries.notes: Today's IN-der matches.

entries.name: Anuradha
entries.source: Hindi अनुराधा anurādhā (Sanskrit; long rā and dhā): the long rā carries the stress (Hindi weight rule); no dictionary entry
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today has the 'lot' vowel in the stressed rā (ɒnʊɹˈɒdə); long ā is 'ah' (as Asha, Seema). US today (ah-noo-RAH-duh) is right: only unstressed vowels differ from the Hindi, and aspirated dh is d.

entries.name: Pritam
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi प्रीतम: /pɾiː.t̪əm/ [pɾiː.t̪ɐ̃m]
entries.notes: Long ī is 'ee' and the final a is the schwa; today's guess says PRY-tam.

entries.name: Girish
entries.source: Wiktionary, Marathi गिरीश: /ɡi.ɾiɕ/ [ɡi.ɾiːɕ]; Sanskrit /ɡi.ɾiː.ɕɐ/
entries.notes: The long ī carries the stress; ś → sh. Today's guess says GY-rish.

entries.name: Gopi
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi गोपी (gopī): long o and ī; first-syllable stress (weight rule, both heavy, the non-final wins)
entries.notes: Today's GOH-pee matches.

entries.name: Megan
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Megan: UK /ˈmɛɡən/; US /ˈmɛɡən/, /ˈmiːɡən/, /ˈmeɪɡən/; Welsh /ˈmɛɡan/

alternatives.context: a US regional variant; today's reading
Australia, New Zealand and some US speakers

entries.notes: Today's MAY-gun is a US regional variant; UK and Welsh bearers and most US ones say MEG-un (first listed in the US too).

entries.name: Amitabh
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi अमिताभ: /ə.mɪ.t̪ɑːbʱ/
entries.notes: The superheavy final tābh carries the stress (Hindi weight rule); aspirated bh → b. Today's guess says AM-it-ab.

entries.name: Ajoy
entries.source: Bengali অজয় (the Bengali form of Ajay); no IPA source found
entries.notes: Bengali spells the inherent vowel o ([ɔ]), so the first vowel is probably 'aw', not today's 'uh'; Bengali stress is weak and initial, while English renderings stress JOY. If JOY carries the stress, today's uh-JOY differs from the candidate only in the unstressed first vowel and is already right (as the Ajay precedent əʤˈA); if Bengali initial stress is wanted, it would be AW-joy (ˈɔʤY). Needs a Bengali IPA or audio-with-text source. Wiktionary has no অজয় entry; Wikipedia's Ajoy Chakrabarty gives no IPA.

entries.name: Prafulla
entries.source: Hindi/Bengali प्रफुल्ल / প্রফুল্ল praphulla: heavy -phul- carries the stress; ph is commonly [f] in this name
entries.notes: Today's pruh-FULL-uh matches the Hindi reading. Bengali bearers (Prafulla Chandra Ray) say pro-FUL-lo, with the same stressed syllable.

entries.name: Sheknar
entries.notes: No bearer, dictionary or name-site entry found for this spelling. Probably a misspelling of Shekhar (शेखर, SHAY-kur, ʃˈAkəɹ) in Wikidata, which would make it a register artefact; today's guess SHEK-ner stays until confirmed.

entries.name: Lijuan
entries.source: Pinyin lìjuān (丽娟): j [tɕ], -uan after j is üan [ɥɛn]; precedent Siyuan
entries.notes: j → j (guide); juan is 'jwen' (ü-glide plus 'en', as Siyuan's yuan). Today's LEE-wahn drops the j of juan and uses 'ah'. Tones dropped; primary stress on the last syllable and secondary on the first (the guide's convention for two-syllable Chinese given names, no English source).

entries.name: Ingrid
entries.source: Wikipedia, Ingrid Bergman: Swedish [ˈɪ̌ŋːrɪd]; English /ˈɪŋɡrɪd/
entries.notes: Swedish, Norwegian, German, French and English bearers all stress ING with the 'bit' vowel. Scandinavian bearers often have no g, a minor difference.

entries.name: Jude
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Jude: /dʒuːd/

entries.name: Phillip
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Phillip: /ˈfɪlɪp/

entries.name: Claire
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Claire: /klɛə(ɹ)/; French /klɛʁ/
entries.notes: French and English readings agree.

entries.name: Johny
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Johnny: /ˈdʒɒni/ (variant spelling)
entries.notes: Bearers in Luxembourg, Indonesia, India and Belgium use it as Johnny; today reads it like Johnny.

entries.name: Nanda
entries.source: Dutch and Indonesian spelling rules: a [ɑ]/[a], first-syllable stress

alternatives.context: Indian bearers (नन्दा, Hindi short a is the schwa)

entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today has the 'lot' vowel (NON-duh); Indonesian [a] and Dutch [ɑ] are 'ah'. US today (NAHN-duh) matches the Dutch and Indonesian bearers; Indian bearers say NUN-daa (alternative).

entries.name: Mù
entries.source: Pinyin mù (穆/牧/睦): [mu]
entries.notes: Today's MYOO adds a y glide; pinyin u after m is plain 'oo'.

entries.name: Jerome
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Jerome: /dʒəˈɹoʊm/
entries.notes: French bearers write Jérôme (the FR count is likely the accent-folded Jérôme); the unaccented spelling in English text is mostly English (Jerome Powell, Jerome K. Jerome).

entries.name: August
entries.notes: Also the month August (and the adjective 'august'). English bearers (US register 57k) say it like the month; German, Scandinavian and Estonian bearers say OW-goost (alternative). Never replace the month.

entries.name: Rahim
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic رحيم: /ra.ħiːm/
entries.notes: Today's ruh-HEEM matches; ḥ → h.

entries.name: Mathias
entries.source: Wiktionary, Norwegian Bokmål Mathias: /maˈtiː.as/ [mɑˈtìː.ɑ̌s]; French /ma.tjas/
entries.notes: Today's muh-THY-us is the English Matthias. Norwegian, Danish, German and Swedish bearers (ma-TEE-as) together outnumber the French group; th is a plain t (as the Matthias precedent).

entries.name: Stéphane
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Stéphane: /ste.fan/
entries.notes: GB-only fix: today's British stɛfˈɒn has the 'lot' vowel; US already right.

entries.name: Clarence
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Clarence: /ˈklæɹəns/
entries.notes: US KLAIR-ence and British KLARR-ence are each right for their accent.

entries.name: Fatou
entries.source: Wikipedia, Fatou Bensouda: /fɑːˈtuː bɛnˈsuːdɑː/ (final stress on Fatou)
entries.notes: Final stress, as Wikipedia gives for the Gambian prosecutor and as the Mamadou precedent; only the unstressed first vowel differs from today's fuh-TOO.

entries.name: Faith
entries.notes: Ordinary word 'faith'. Name and word sound the same, so nothing needs to ship.

entries.name: Dana
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Dana: /ˈdeɪnə/

alternatives.context: Czech, Slovak, Romanian, Hebrew and Arabic bearers

entries.notes: usage english: US register 244k say DAY-nuh.

entries.name: Cyrus
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Cyrus: /ˈsaɪɹəs/
entries.notes: Persian bearers usually write Kourosh; this spelling is read SY-rus.

entries.name: Nathaniel
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Nathaniel: /nəˈθænjəl/

entries.name: Gregorio
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Gregorio: /ɡɾeˈɡoɾjo/
entries.notes: Today's gri-GOR-ee-oh keeps the stressed 'gor'; the 'or' vowel before r is how English renders Spanish o there. Unstressed vowels only differ.

entries.name: Chang
entries.source: Pinyin cháng (常/昌/长): -ang is [ɑŋ]; Korean 창 [tɕʰaŋ]
entries.notes: Today's CHANG (as in 'bang') uses the 'cat' vowel; as the Zhang precedent. Also fits the common surname Chang (張, CHAHNG).

entries.name: Kamran
entries.source: Wiktionary, Persian کامران (kâmrân): Iran formal [kʰɒːm.ɹɒːn]; Behind the Name /kɒːm.ˈɾɒːn/ (Persian)
entries.notes: Matches n0009. Today's CMUdict KAM-run stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Kang
entries.source: Pinyin kāng (康): -ang is [ɑŋ]; Korean 강 [kaŋ]
entries.notes: Today's KANG (as in 'bang') uses the 'cat' vowel; as the Zhang precedent.

entries.name: Jianjun
entries.source: Pinyin jiànjūn (建军): -ian [jɛn], jun [tɕyn]; precedents Jiàn, Jun
entries.notes: -ian is 'yen' (as Jiàn); jun is 'joon' (ü → oo, as Jun). Today's guess says jee-AHN-jun. Tones dropped; primary stress on the last syllable and secondary on the first (the guide's convention for two-syllable Chinese given names, no English source).

entries.name: Shuo
entries.source: Pinyin shuò (硕/烁): -uo [wo], one syllable; precedent Guowei
entries.notes: One syllable with a w glide (as Guo in Guowei); today's SHOO-oh splits it in two. Tone dropped.

entries.name: Xueying
entries.source: Pinyin xuěyíng (雪莹): x [ɕ], -ue [ɥɛ], ying [iŋ]; precedents Xue, Yíng
entries.notes: x → sh (guide); xue is 'shweh' (as Xue); ying as Yíng. Today's ZOO-ee-ing reads x as z. Tones dropped; primary stress on the last syllable and secondary on the first (the guide's convention for two-syllable Chinese given names, no English source).

entries.name: Zhixin
entries.source: Pinyin zhìxīn (志新/志信): zh [ʈʂ], syllabic zhi, x [ɕ]; precedents Zhi, Xinyi
entries.notes: zh → j and x → sh (guide); zhi as the Zhi entry. Today's ZHIK-sin reads x as ks. Tones dropped; primary stress on the last syllable and secondary on the first (the guide's convention for two-syllable Chinese given names, no English source).

entries.name: Pengfei
entries.source: Pinyin péngfēi (鹏飞): -eng [əŋ], -ei [eɪ]; precedent Peng
entries.notes: -eng is 'ung' (as Peng); -ei is 'ay'. Today's PENG-fy reads ei as 'eye'. Tones dropped; primary stress on the last syllable and secondary on the first (the guide's convention for two-syllable Chinese given names, no English source).

entries.name: Jiao
entries.source: Pinyin jiāo (娇/姣): [tɕjɑʊ], one syllable with a y glide
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today drops the y glide (JOW); US already right. Also the rare word 'jiao' (a Chinese money unit), the same Chinese word, said the same.
entries.word_check: gold has 'jiao'; kept: gold lists the Chinese name in lower case; no ordinary word

entries.name: Chunyu
entries.source: Pinyin chūnyǔ (春雨): -un [wən], yu [y]; precedents Chunhua, Xinyu
entries.notes: -un after ch is 'wun' (as Chunhua); yu is 'yoo' (as Xinyu). Today's guess says CHOON-yoo. Tones dropped; primary stress on the last syllable and secondary on the first (the guide's convention for two-syllable Chinese given names, no English source).

entries.name: Shìyīng
entries.source: Pinyin shìyīng (世英): syllabic shi [ʂʐ̩], ying [iŋ]; precedents Shi, Yíng
entries.notes: shi has the retroflex syllabic vowel, 'shr' (as the Shi entry); today's SHY-ing reads it as 'eye'. Tones dropped; primary stress on the last syllable and secondary on the first (the guide's convention for two-syllable Chinese given names, no English source).

entries.name: Yī
entries.source: Pinyin yī (一/伊/依): [i]; precedent Yi
entries.notes: As the Yi precedent: today's 'yih' uses the 'bit' vowel. Tone dropped.

entries.name: Mercedes
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Mercedes: /meɾˈθedes/ (Spain), /meɾˈsedes/ (Latin America)
entries.notes: In English text 'Mercedes' is very often the car maker (Mercedes-Benz), read mer-SAY-deez (Wiktionary English: GA /mɚˈseɪdiz/, RP /məˈseɪdiz/); the name reading (Spanish bearers: ES 121k, Peru, Argentina, US Hispanic) is in us/gb but must not replace the brand's. Today's GB məsˈAdiz matches the English reading; today's US məɹsˈɛdz ('mer-SEDZ') fits neither the car nor the name, so the word needs its own fix outside the names pack (US məɹsˈAdiz).

entries.name: Tito
entries.source: Wiktionary, Italian Tito: /ˈti.to/
entries.notes: Today's TEE-toh matches (American flap t is normal).

entries.name: Matteo
entries.source: Wiktionary, Italian Matteo: /matˈtɛ.o/
entries.notes: Italian stressed e here is open [ɛ] ('eh', guide table as Michele), not today's 'ay'; British today also has the 'lot' vowel in the first syllable. Double t single.

entries.name: Annisa
entries.source: Indonesian spelling rules (from Arabic an-Nisāʾ): penultimate stress, double n single; Wiktionary, Indonesian Annisa: /ˈanisa/ (see notes)
entries.notes: Today's ah-NEE-suh matches the penultimate rule. Wiktionary's /ˈanisa/ marks the first syllable, but the same hand-entered style marks Agustina /ˈaɡʊstina/, and Wiktionary's own Indonesian module gives penultimate stress (Novita /noˈvita/), so it is not taken as evidence of initial stress. Medium confidence.

entries.name: Dong
entries.source: Pinyin dōng (东/冬): -ong [ʊŋ]
entries.notes: Also the vulgar word 'dong' and the Vietnamese currency đồng, read DONG today. The Chinese name 东/冬/栋 dōng is said DOONG (-ong as in Long); Korean 동 is similar. Name reading in us/gb; it must not replace the word.

entries.name: Sushma
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi सुषमा: /sʊʂ.mɑː/ [sʊʃ.mäː] (short u); Wikipedia, Sushma Swaraj: Hindi [suʃmaː sʋəɾaːd͡ʒ]
entries.notes: ṣ → sh. Hindi उ is short [ʊ], the 'book' vowel (as Surinder, Rahul), not today's 'cup' vowel and not a long 'oo'. Stress on the heavy first syllable (weight rule; Wiktionary marks none); final ā unstressed → 'uh'. Reviewer: vowel changed from u to ʊ per Wiktionary.

entries.name: Luc
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Luc: /lyk/
entries.notes: French ü → 'oo' (guide table); today's LOOK matches.

entries.name: Romeo
entries.source: Wiktionary, Italian Romeo: /roˈmɛ.o/; Spanish /roˈmeo/
entries.notes: In English text 'Romeo' is mostly Shakespeare's Romeo (and the NATO letter), read ROH-mee-oh today, as English bearers (US 24k, UK) say it. Most bearers (anglo_share 0.04: Italy, Romania, the Philippines, Latin America) say roh-MAY-oh/roh-MEH-oh; that reading is in us/gb but must not replace the English one.

entries.name: Edmond
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Edmund: /ˈɛdmənd/ (Edmond is its French-derived spelling; Wiktionary's Edmond page gives only French /ɛd.mɔ̃/)

alternatives.context: French, Belgian and Swiss bearers (FR register 26k), final stress

entries.notes: Close call: FR 26k (mostly born 1900–1930) against US 19k since 1925, Ireland and Canada; English text also has Edmond Halley and Edmond, Oklahoma. Kept the English reading; decision to review.

entries.name: Ni
entries.source: Pinyin nī/ní (妮/尼): [ni]
entries.notes: Today's NEE matches.

entries.name: Osvaldo
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Osvaldo: /osˈbaldo/
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today has the 'lot' vowel; US already right. v kept as English speakers say it (as Silvia). Brazilian Portuguese bearers say oz-VOW-doo.

entries.name: Benedict
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Benedict: /ˈbɛnədɪkt/

entries.name: Dũng
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese Dũng: Hà Nội [zʊwŋ͡m˦ˀ˥], Huế [jʊwŋ͡m˧˨], Saigon [jʊwŋ͡m˨˩˦]
entries.notes: Vietnamese plain d is z (north) or y (centre and south), never English d (that is đ). Chose the y shared by Huế and Saigon and most of the diaspora; tones dropped; final ŋ͡m → ng. Decision to review: north vs south.

entries.name: Hà
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese hà: [haː˨˩]
entries.notes: Tone dropped; today's HAH matches.

entries.name: Jamila
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic جميلة: /d͡ʒa.miː.la/
entries.notes: The long ī is 'ee' and carries the stress; today's juh-MIL-uh shortens it.

entries.name: Connie
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Connie: /ˈkɒni/
entries.notes: Today's US 'caw' vowel and the 'cot' vowel are one vowel for many US speakers; British kˈɒni matches.

entries.name: Yevgeni
entries.source: Wikipedia, Yevgeny Zamyatin: Russian Евгений [jɪvˈɡʲenʲɪj]
entries.notes: Stressed Russian e in an open syllable is 'ay' (guide table); today's yev-GEH-nee uses the 'bed' vowel.

entries.name: Sylvain
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Sylvain: /sil.vɛ̃/
entries.notes: French nasal ɛ̃ → English 'an' (as the Alain precedent); today's sil-VAYN reads -ain as in 'lane'.

entries.name: Germán
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Germán: /xeɾˈman/
entries.notes: Today's JUR-mun is the English word 'German'. Spanish g before e [x] → h (guide); the accent marks the final stress.

entries.name: Lewis
entries.notes: Also the word 'lewis' (a stone-lifting device) and very often the surname (C. S. Lewis, Lewis Hamilton). All are read LOO-iss, as the name, so nothing needs to ship.

entries.name: Sarita
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi सरिता: /sə.ɾɪ.t̪ɑː/ [sɐ.ɾɪ.t̪äː]

alternatives.context: Spanish-speaking and US Hispanic bearers; today's reading

entries.notes: Bearers split: Indian Sarita (सरिता, short i) and Spanish/US Hispanic Sarita (sa-REE-ta, today's reading). The Hindi stress is unsourced, as for Kavita: the weight rule would favour -tā, English renderings -ri-. Needs a stress source before the Hindi reading can replace today's.

entries.name: Calvin
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Calvin: /ˈkælvɪn/
entries.notes: South African, Dutch and Indonesian bearers also stress KAL.

entries.name: Ada
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Ada: /ˈeɪdə/

alternatives.context: Italian, Polish, Norwegian, Spanish, Turkish and Igbo bearers

entries.notes: Tech-list term (the Ada language, named after Ada Lovelace) reads AY-duh, as the English name; English bearers (US 54k, UK 11k) are the largest single group, so name and term agree.

entries.name: Devika
entries.source: Hindi देविका devikā: long e, short i, long ā; stress on the heavy first syllable (Hindi weight rule); no dictionary entry
entries.notes: Today's dih-VEE-kuh shortens the long e and lengthens the short i. Final ā unstressed → 'uh' (as Kalpana).

entries.name: Rex
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Rex: /ɹɛks/

entries.name: Rosario
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Rosario: /roˈsaɾjo/
entries.notes: Today's roh-SAR-ee-oh matches; the i is the glide.

entries.name: Ganesh
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi गणेश: /ɡə.ɳeːʃ/
entries.notes: Today's guh-NAYSH matches.

entries.name: Madeleine
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Madeleine: /mad.lɛn/; English /ˈmæd(ə)lɪn/, /ˈmædəlaɪn/
entries.notes: French bearers (FR register 130k, plus Belgium and Switzerland) and Swedish ones (Princess Madeleine, final stress) outnumber the English group. French names take final stress in English. Decision to review: changes English bearers (Madeleine Albright).
entries.word_check: gold has 'madeleine'; kept: the cake is written lower-case mid-sentence; English 'mad-LEN' is close to the name's reading

entries.name: Kalpana
entries.source: Wikipedia, Kalpana Chawla: /ˌkɑːlpənə ˈtʃɑːvlə/
entries.notes: Today's kal-PAN-uh stresses the second syllable with the 'cat' vowel.

entries.name: Filip
entries.source: Wiktionary, Polish Filip: /ˈfi.lip/; Slovak [ˈfilip]; Czech [ˈfɪlɪp]

alternatives.context: Czech bearers and English speakers; today's reading

entries.notes: Polish, Slovak, Swedish, Norwegian, Serbo-Croatian, Romanian and Bulgarian bearers say the stressed i as 'ee'; only Czech has the 'bit' vowel. The GB register (6k) is mostly Polish and Romanian families.

entries.name: Melvin
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Melvin: /ˈmɛlvɪn/

entries.name: Rina
entries.source: Wiktionary, Rina: English /ˈɹiːnə/, Norwegian Bokmål /ˈriː.na/; Japanese リナ [ɾʲi.na]; Hebrew רינה /ˈʁina/
entries.notes: Japanese, Hebrew, Italian, Greek and Indonesian bearers all say REE-nah, as today.

entries.name: Adi
entries.source: Indonesian spelling rules: penultimate stress; Sanskrit/Hindi आदि ādi (Wikipedia, Adi Shankara: Sanskrit [aːd̪i ...])
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today has the 'lot' vowel (OD-ee); the stressed vowel is 'ah'. US today is right. Readings split: Indonesian and Indian AH-dee against Hebrew ah-DEE (wd IL 102, the largest notable count). Indonesia's far larger population of Adis tips it to AH-dee; decision to review.

entries.name: Béchir
entries.source: French-orthography spelling of Arabic بشير Bashīr; Wiktionary, Arabic بشير: /ba.ʃiːr/
entries.notes: French ch = sh and é = 'ay'; the long ī carries the stress. Today's BEK-eer reads ch as k and stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Elsa
entries.source: Wiktionary, Elsa: English /ˈɛlsə/, Spanish /ˈelsa/, Italian /ˈɛl.sa/; German /ˈʔɛlza/

alternatives.context: French bearers (FR register 48k), final stress; German and Czech bearers also have z but stress EL

entries.notes: English, Spanish, Italian, Swedish, Norwegian and Finnish bearers say EL-sah with s, together more than the French (el-ZAH) and German (EL-zah) groups.

entries.name: Erica
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Erica: /ˈɛɹɪkə/

entries.name: Edson
entries.source: Wikipedia, Pelé (Edson Arantes do Nascimento): Brazilian Portuguese [ˈɛd(ʒi)sõ(w) aˈɾɐ̃tʃiz du nasiˈmẽtu]
entries.notes: Brazilian bearers (Pelé's given name) stress ED like today's reading; only the unstressed final nasal vowel differs, and the optional epenthetic 'jee' (ED-jee-sohn) is left out.

entries.name: Lauren
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Lauren: /ˈlɔːɹən/

entries.name: Hamed
entries.source: Wiktionary, Persian حامد: Iran [hɒːˈmed]; Arabic /ħaː.mid/
entries.notes: This spelling is mostly Persian (wd IR 49 leads): final stress, â → 'ah' as Payam. Today's HAMD makes one syllable.

entries.name: Zara
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Zara: /ˈzɑːɹə/
entries.notes: Tech-list term (the Zara retailer) reads ZAH-ruh too, so the name and the term agree.

entries.name: June
entries.notes: Also the month June, said the same as the name. Nothing needs to ship.

entries.name: Agus
entries.source: Indonesian spelling rules: a [a], u [ʊ] in a closed final syllable, penultimate stress (short form of Agustus)
entries.notes: Today's AY-gus reads it as English.

entries.name: Carrie
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Carrie: UK /ˈkæ.ɹi/; US /ˈkæ.ɹi/, merged /ˈkɛɹ.i/
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British keeps the 'marry' vowel; today's British reading uses the American merged 'merry' vowel. US unchanged.

entries.name: Howard
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Howard: /ˈhaʊəd/

entries.name: Farhad
entries.source: Wiktionary, Persian فرهاد (farhâd): Iran formal [fæɹ.hɒ́ːd̪̥]; Behind the Name /fæɾ.ˈhɒːd/
entries.notes: Persian short a before r and a consonant (or at the end) is written English 'ar' (US ɑɹ, GB ɑː), as Parviz and Ardeshir in earlier batches: the voice's 'cat' vowel before r comes out as 'er'. n0009 has US fæɹhˈɑd: harmonise. Today's FAR-had stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Saleh
entries.source: Arabic صالح Ṣāliḥ: long ā stressed, ḥ → h
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today has the 'lot' vowel; US already right. ṣ → s, ḥ → h.

entries.name: Abd al-Salam
entries.source: Arabic عبد السلام ʿAbd as-Salām: s is a sun letter, so al- is said as-; stress on the long ā (Wiktionary, Arabic سلام /sa.laːm/)
entries.notes: Two words, a primary in each (as Abd al-Rahman). ʿayn dropped; the article assimilates to the s and the double s is said once. Today's guess reads 'al' as in 'pal' and stresses AL-sal-um.

entries.name: Hisham
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic هشام: /hi.ʃaːm/
entries.notes: The long ā carries the stress; today's HISH-um stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Antonia
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Antonia: /anˈtonja/
entries.notes: Today's an-TOH-nee-uh keeps the stressed 'toh'; only unstressed vowels differ.

entries.name: Hubert
entries.source: Wiktionary, Polish Hubert: /ˈxu.bɛrt/; Czech [ˈɦubɛrt]; French /y.bɛʁ/; English /ˈhjubɚt/

alternatives.context: English-speaking bearers (US 37k, Hubert Humphrey); today's reading

entries.notes: Readings split three ways. German, Austrian, Polish, Czech and Dutch bearers share HOO-bert (no y glide) and together outnumber both the French (oo-BEHR) and English (HYOO-bert) groups. Decision to review.

entries.name: Anderson
entries.source: Wikipedia, Anderson Silva: Portuguese [ˈɐ̃deʁsõ ˈsiwvɐ]
entries.notes: In English text 'Anderson' is mostly the very common surname (Pamela Anderson, Gillian Anderson, Wes Anderson), read AN-der-sun today, as are English-speaking given-name bearers (US 31.5k; Anderson Cooper). The given name's main bearers are Brazilian (wd BR 194; Anderson Silva [ˈɐ̃deʁsõ]), whose reading is in us/gb; it must not replace the surname.

entries.name: Reginald
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Reginald: /ˈɹɛdʒɪnəld/

entries.name: Valeria
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Valeria: /baˈleɾja/; Italian /vaˈlɛ.rja/; English /vəˈlɪəɹi.ə/
entries.notes: Spanish bearers (ES 51k, Latin America, most of the US 75k) are the largest group: stressed e in an open syllable is 'ay' (guide table). v kept as English speakers say it (as Silvia, Valentina). Today's vuh-LEER-ee-uh is the English reading.

entries.name: Jaya
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi जया: /d͡ʒə.jɑː/ [d͡ʒɐ.jäː]
entries.notes: Hindi schwa before y is heard as English 'jai', so today's JY-uh is the usual rendering (as Maya); Indonesian JAH-yah is close too. Only the unstressed final vowel differs.

entries.name: Marlon
entries.source: Wikipedia, Marlon Brando: /ˈmɑːrlən ˈbrændoʊ/
entries.notes: Brazilian, German and Ecuadorian bearers also stress MAR.

entries.name: Neville
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Neville: /ˈnɛvəl/

entries.name: Meera
entries.source: Hindi मीरा mīrā: long ī stressed
entries.notes: Today's MEE-ruh matches; final ā unstressed.

entries.name: Winston
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Winston: /ˈwɪnstən/
entries.notes: Covered by the tech list on purpose (Winston Churchill); the same reading as the name.

entries.name: Rudi
entries.source: Wikipedia, Rudi Dutschke: German [ˈʁuːdi ˈdʊtʃkə]
entries.notes: Today's ROO-dee matches.

entries.name: Guido
entries.source: Wiktionary, Italian Guido: /ˈɡwi.do/; Spanish Guido the same
entries.notes: Italian and Spanish GWEE-doh (with the US and French registers) outnumber German and Dutch GHEE-doh.

entries.name: Brigitte
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Brigitte: /bʁi.ʒit/

alternatives.context: German, Austrian and Swiss German bearers (bree-GIT-uh)

entries.notes: FR register 201k dwarfs every other group; today's BRIDGE-it is the English Bridget reading. French ʁ → r, final stress.

entries.name: Varun
entries.source: Wikipedia, Varun Dhawan: Hindi [ʋəɾʊɳ]
entries.notes: Today's vɑɹˈun keeps the consonants and the stressed 'oon' (as for Arun, n0001); only the unstressed first vowel differs. Hindi ʋ → v.

entries.name: Benjamín
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Benjamín: /beŋxaˈmin/
entries.notes: The accented spelling is Spanish: j is [x] → h (guide), stress on the last syllable as the accent marks. Today's BEN-juh-min is the English Benjamin.

entries.name: Shiva
entries.source: Merriam-Webster / Collins, Shiva: /ˈʃiːvə/ (also /ˈʃɪvə/)

alternatives.context: some Indian bearers, with the short i of Sanskrit Śiva

entries.notes: Today's SHEE-vuh is the dictionary reading of the deity's name and the usual one for Indian bearers in English (a short stressed vowel in an open syllable is lengthened, as for Uma).

entries.name: Quỳnh
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese quỳnh: Hà Nội [kwïŋ̟˨˩], Huế [kwɨn˦˩], Saigon [wɨn˨˩]
entries.notes: Today's KWIN matches the established English approximation of -inh (as Linh, Minh in earlier batches). Tone dropped.

entries.name: Thảo
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese thảo: Hà Nội [tʰaːw˧˩], Saigon [tʰaːw˨˩˦]
entries.notes: Vietnamese th is an aspirated t, not English th (today says 'thou' with ð). -ao is 'ow'. Tone dropped.

entries.name: Kamil
entries.source: Wiktionary, Polish Kamil: /ˈka.mil/; Czech Kamil [ˈkamɪl]
entries.notes: Polish and Czech bearers (wd PL 301, CZ 69; most UK, Irish and Norwegian births too) stress the first syllable; today's kuh-MIL stresses the second.

entries.name: Neena
entries.source: Hindi नीना nīnā: long ī takes the stress (as Neena Gupta)

entries.name: Kunal
entries.source: Wikipedia, Kunal Nayyar: /kʊˈnɑːl/ ('kuu-NAHL')
entries.notes: Today's KYOO-nul adds a y and stresses the short vowel; the long ā takes the stress.

entries.name: Harish
entries.source: Hindi हरीश harīś: short a, long ī; the long ī takes the stress (as Manish, Satish in earlier batches)
entries.notes: Today's HAIR-ish reads it as an English word.

entries.name: Mohit
entries.source: Hindi मोहित mohit: long ō in the first syllable takes the stress
entries.notes: Today's MOH-heet differs only in the unstressed second vowel.

entries.name: Ashish
entries.source: Hindi आशीष āśīṣ: stress on the long final ī
entries.notes: Today's əʃˈiʃ keeps the stressed 'sheesh'; only the unstressed first vowel is reduced.

entries.name: Akram
entries.source: Arabic أكرم ʾakram: first-syllable stress; guide row for stressed Arabic a ('ah', as Ahmad)

alternatives.context: the usual English reading (Wasim Akram commentary)

entries.notes: Today's ACK-rum uses the 'cat' vowel; Arabic stressed a is 'ah' per the guide (Ahmad, n0002). Urdu bearers say UK-rum, close to this.

entries.name: Pawan
entries.source: Hindi पवन pavan: both vowels short a [ə]; first-syllable stress as for Karan (n0002)

alternatives.context: with a v, as the alternative spelling Pavan is said

entries.notes: Today's PAH-wahn has 'ah' for Hindi short a, which is 'uh'. Hindi ʋ is between v and w; this spelling's w is kept.

entries.name: Salil
entries.source: Hindi सलिल salil: short a and short i; Hindi stress is weak
entries.notes: No source gives the stress. Today's suh-LIL has every sound right; Bengali bearers (Salil Chowdhury) stress the first syllable.

entries.name: Padma
entries.source: Wikipedia, Padma Lakshmi: Tamil [ˈpɐd̪maː]; Hindi पद्मा padmā has the same short a
entries.notes: Today's PAD-muh uses the 'cat' vowel; Indian short a is 'uh' (as Chandra, n0002).

entries.name: Sekhar
entries.source: Wikipedia, Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar: English /ˌtʃəndrəˈʃeɪkər/ (Sanskrit śekhara)
entries.notes: The spelling's s is Sanskrit ś (sh), and e is a long [eː]: 'shay'. Today's SEK-er reads it as English.

entries.name: Wesley
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Wesley: /ˈwɛsli/, /ˈwɛzli/

entries.name: Renata
entries.source: Wiktionary, Polish Renata: /rɛˈna.ta/; Italian /reˈnaːta/
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today says the 'lot' vowel (ruh-NOT-uh); every bearer group says 'ah'. US already right.

entries.name: Léon
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Léon: /le.ɔ̃/
entries.notes: The accented spelling is French (FR register 62k). Today's LEE-on is the English Leon. Nasal ɔ̃ → 'on' plus n (as Alphonse, n0005); French names take final stress in English.

entries.name: Marius
entries.source: Wiktionary, Marius: Dutch /ˈmaː.ri.ʏs/, Classical Latin [ˈma.ri.ʊs], French /ma.ʁjys/; Romanian [ˈmari.us]

alternatives.context: English, and Gaius Marius in English text (MAIR-ee-us)

entries.notes: Romanian (wd RO 304, the largest group), Norwegian (NO 17k), Danish, Dutch and German bearers all say MAH-ree-us, together more than French mar-YOOS. Today's MAIR-ee-us is the English classical reading. Decision to review.

entries.name: Ludwig
entries.source: Wiktionary, Ludwig: English /ˈludvɪɡ/, /ˈlʌdwɪɡ/; German /ˈluːtvɪç/
entries.notes: German bearers dominate (wd DE 2089). Wiktionary's first English reading keeps the German long u and v; final [ç] becomes g, as English speakers say it. Today's US has the 'book' vowel and a w.

entries.name: Hüseyin
entries.source: Turkish spelling rules: ü [y], e, y [j], i; regular final stress
entries.notes: Turkish ü has no English match: 'oo' per the guide. Today's HUZ-ee-in voices the s and misreads every vowel. Turkish stress is weak; final as for Mustafa and Mehmet.

entries.name: Kathleen
entries.source: Merriam-Webster, Kathleen: \kath-ˈlēn, ˈkath-ˌlēn\

entries.name: Pushpa
entries.source: Hindi पुष्पा puṣpā: short u [ʊ] (the 'book' vowel), retroflex ṣ → sh

entries.name: Ayman
entries.source: Arabic أيمن ʾayman [ˈʔaj.man] (Wikipedia transliteration ʾAyman, Ayman al-Zawahiri); guide: ai → 'eye'

alternatives.context: colloquial Egyptian and Levantine, where ay becomes [eː] (AY-mun)

entries.notes: Today's AY-mun is the colloquial Egyptian/Levantine vowel; the name's standard and Maghrebi form has the diphthong 'eye'.

entries.name: Julián
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Julián: /xuˈljan/
entries.notes: Spanish j is [x] → h (guide); the accent marks final stress. Today's JOOL-yun is the English Julian.

entries.name: Wayne
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Wayne: /weɪn/

entries.name: Parveen
entries.source: Wiktionary, Persian پروین: [pʰæɾ.ʋíːn]; Urdu Parveen [pəɾʋiːn]
entries.notes: Today's par-VEEN matches; only the unstressed first vowel differs.

entries.name: Sally
entries.notes: Also the word 'sally' (a sortie; a witty remark). The name is said like the word, SAL-ee; today's sˈæli / sˈali is right, so nothing needs to ship.

entries.name: Jinsheng
entries.source: Mandarin 金生 jīnshēng: jin [tɕin], sheng [ʂəŋ]; guide stress convention for two-syllable Chinese given names
entries.notes: Pinyin -eng is 'ung' (as Peng, Feng). Today's JIN-sheng reads it as English. Tones dropped.

entries.name: Arsalan
entries.source: Persian ارسلان arsalân: stress on the long final â (Persian final stress); Urdu arsalān the same
entries.notes: Today's AR-suh-lun stresses the first syllable and reduces the long final 'ah'.

entries.name: Goran
entries.source: Serbo-Croatian Gòrān [ɡǒraːn]: rising accent on the first syllable, long final ā (as Zoran, n0008)
entries.notes: Today's GORE-un uses the 'law'/'north' vowel; the stressed o is 'oh', as for Zoran.

entries.name: Martina
entries.source: Wiktionary, Italian Martina: /marˈti.na/; Spanish the same

entries.name: Putri
entries.source: Indonesian spelling rules: putri [ˈputri], penultimate stress

entries.name: Ronnie
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Ronnie: /ˈɹɒni/

entries.name: Anju
entries.source: Hindi अंजू añjū: short a [ə] (nasalised), long ū
entries.notes: Today's AN-joo uses the 'cat' vowel; Hindi short a is 'uh'.

entries.name: Adolf
entries.source: Wiktionary, German Adolf: /ˈaːdɔlf/; Dutch /ˈaː.dɔlf/, Czech [ˈadolf]

alternatives.context: the common English reading, especially for Adolf Hitler (AY-dolf)

entries.notes: Bearers are German, Swedish, Austrian and Czech; all say AH-dolf. Decision to review: English text about Hitler often says AY-dolf (today's reading), but he was a German bearer.

entries.name: Jeremiah
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Jeremiah: /ˌd͡ʒɛɹəˈmaɪ.ə/

entries.name: Ömer
entries.source: Turkish spelling rules: ö [œ], e [e], regular final stress
entries.notes: Turkish ö has no English match; unstressed it becomes 'uh'. Today's OH-mer stresses the first syllable with an 'oh'.

entries.name: Aida
entries.source: Wiktionary, Italian Aida: /aˈi.da/; Spanish Aída [aˈiða]

alternatives.context: English, and Verdi's opera in English (eye-EE-duh)

entries.notes: Spanish bearers (ES 15k plus Latin America and most US births) are the largest group. Today's British AY-duh drops a syllable; US eye-EE-duh is the opera's English reading.

entries.name: Manoel
entries.source: Wiktionary, Portuguese Manoel (old spelling of Manuel): Brazil /ma.nuˈɛw/
entries.notes: Three syllables, stress on the last; today's mah-NOH-ul stresses the o. Brazilian final l [w] is kept as l, as for Raul.

entries.name: Zachary
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Zachary: /ˈzæk.ə.ɹi/

entries.name: Huyền
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese huyền: Hà Nội [hwiən˨˩], Saigon [wiəŋ˨˩]
entries.notes: One syllable: h, a w glide and the diphthong [iə]. Today's HINE reads uy as 'eye'. Tone dropped.

entries.name: Thủy
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese thuỷ: Hà Nội [tʰwi˧˩], Saigon [tʰ⁽ʷ⁾ɪj˨˩˦]
entries.notes: Vietnamese th is an aspirated t; uy is [wi]. Today's TOO drops the 'ee'. Tone dropped.

entries.name: Tuyết
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese tuyết: Hà Nội [twiət̚˧˦], Saigon [t⁽ʷ⁾iək̚˦˥]
entries.notes: One syllable: t, a w glide, the diphthong [iə], final t. Today's too-YET splits it in two. Tone dropped.

entries.name: Enrico
entries.source: Wiktionary, Italian Enrico: /enˈri.ko/

entries.name: Sebastião
entries.source: Wiktionary, Portuguese Sebastião: Brazil /se.bas.t͡ʃiˈɐ̃w̃/, Portugal /sɨ.βɐʃ.tiˈɐ̃w̃/
entries.notes: Brazilian bearers (wd BR 207) outnumber Portuguese (42); Brazilian ti is 'chee'. Nasal -ão → 'ow' (guide, as João). Today's suh-BAST-ee-ow has the 'cat' vowel.

entries.name: Stefano
entries.source: Wiktionary, Italian Stefano: /ˈstɛ.fa.no/
entries.notes: Today's STEF-uh-noh differs only in the unstressed middle vowel.

entries.name: Qāsim
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic قاسم qāsim: /ˈqaː.sim/
entries.notes: q → k (guide). The long ā takes the stress; today's kah-SEEM stresses the short i.

entries.name: Ron
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Ron: /ɹɒn/, US /ɹɑn/

entries.name: Majid
entries.source: Wiktionary, Persian مجید: [mæ.d͡ʒíːd]; Arabic مجيد majīd the same

alternatives.context: Arabic ماجد Mājid, a different name written the same in English (MAH-jid)

entries.notes: Iranian bearers dominate (wd IR 67). The stressed vowel is a long ī; today's muh-JID shortens it.

entries.name: Xu
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 徐 xú: [ɕy³⁵]
entries.notes: Pinyin x [ɕ] → sh (guide); ü → 'oo' (as Jun, Yun). Today's SOO reads x as s. Tone dropped.
entries.word_check: gold has 'xu'; kept: gold lists the Chinese name in lower case; no ordinary word

entries.name: Junwen
entries.source: Mandarin 俊文 jùnwén: jun [tɕyn] (as Jun, n0001), wen [wən] (as Wenlong, n0007); guide stress convention
entries.notes: Today's JUN-wun reads jun with the 'cup' vowel. Tones dropped.

entries.name: Qìngxiáng
entries.source: Mandarin 庆祥 qìngxiáng: qing [tɕʰiŋ] (as Qing), xiang [ɕjɑŋ] (as Jiaxiang, n0007); guide stress convention
entries.notes: Pinyin q → ch, x → sh. Today's KING-shyang reads q as k. Tones dropped.

entries.name: Jamie
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Jamie: /ˈd͡ʒeɪmi/

entries.name: Nidhi
entries.source: Hindi निधि nidhi: short i [ɪ] in both syllables; aspirated dʱ → d
entries.notes: Today's NEE-dee lengthens the short first vowel; the closed English syllable keeps it short, as for Aditi (n0003).

entries.name: Ayub
entries.source: Arabic أيوب ayyūb [ʔaj.ˈjuːb], Urdu ayyūb: stress on the long ū
entries.notes: Today's AY-ub stresses the first syllable and loses the long 'oo'.

entries.name: Thiago
entries.source: Wikipedia, Thiago Silva: Portuguese [tʃiˈaɡu]

alternatives.context: Spanish-speaking bearers (Spain, Argentina, US Hispanic families) and English sports commentary (tee-AH-goh)

entries.notes: Brazil, where Thiago is a top name, has the most bearers; Brazilian ti is 'chee' and final o is 'oo'. Today's thee-AH-goh reads th as in 'thin', which no bearer says. Decision to review: Spanish-speaking bearers say tee-AH-goh.

entries.name: Raquel
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Raquel: /raˈkel/

entries.name: Iman
