entries.source: Arabic إيمان īmān and Persian ایمان: stress on the long final ā
entries.notes: Today's EYE-mun is a spelling reading. Arabic (women) and Persian (men) bearers both say ee-MAHN, as does the model Iman.

entries.name: Arjan
entries.source: Punjabi ਅਰਜਨ arjan (Guru Arjan): [əɾ.d͡ʒən], as Arjun (n0001)
entries.notes: Most register births (GB 1503, CA 1567, US 883) are Punjabi Sikh families; with India they outnumber the Dutch. Today's AR-jun is their reading.

entries.name: Samina
entries.source: Urdu ثمینہ samīna: long ī takes the stress
entries.notes: Today's suh-MIN-uh shortens the long ī.

entries.name: Gabriella
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Gabriella: /ˌɡæbɹiˈɛlə/; Italian /ɡa.briˈɛl.la/
entries.notes: Today differs only in the unstressed first vowel.

entries.name: Gerhard
entries.source: Wiktionary, German Gerhard: /ˈɡeːɐ̯haʁt/
entries.notes: German bearers dominate (wd DE 2209, AT 481). German er is 'air' and the final d is t; today's GUR-hard is an English spelling reading.

entries.name: Henny
entries.source: Dutch spelling rules: Henny [ˈɦɛni]

entries.name: Adriano
entries.source: Wiktionary, Italian Adriano: /a.driˈa.no/
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today says the 'lot' vowel in the stressed syllable; bearers say 'ah'. US already right.

entries.name: Astrid
entries.source: Wiktionary, Astrid: Dutch /ˈɑ.strɪt/, Norwegian /²astrɪ/, French /as.tʁid/, English /ˈæstɹɪd/
entries.notes: US-only fix, as for Hans (n0002): Scandinavian, German and Dutch bearers say 'ah', not the US 'cat' vowel; British already right. Norwegian also drops the final d.

entries.name: Sekou
entries.region: Guinea, Mali, Côte d'Ivoire, France, US
entries.source: Dictionary.com, Sékou Touré: Sékou /ˈseɪkuː/
entries.notes: The e is 'ay' (French é), not today's 'sek'.

entries.name: Ailing
entries.source: Mandarin 愛 ài [aɪ], 玲/凌 líng [liŋ]; guide stress convention
entries.notes: Also the word 'ailing', capitalised at the start of sentences and headlines ('Ailing economy...'). The Chinese name 愛玲/愛凌 àilíng (Eileen Chang, Eileen Gu) is 'eye-LING'; that reading is in us/gb, protected so the word keeps today's reading.

entries.name: Guoxiong
entries.source: Mandarin 国雄 guóxióng: guo [ku̯ɔ] (as Guoguang, n0007), xiong [ɕjʊŋ]; guide stress convention
entries.notes: Today's GWOK-see-ong reads x as ks. Tones dropped.

entries.name: Andi
entries.source: Indonesian spelling rules: Andi [ˈandi]; German Andi the same
entries.notes: US-only fix, as for Hans: anglo_share 0.01; Indonesian (wd ID 30) and German bearers say 'ah'. British already right.

entries.name: Shaquille
entries.source: Wikipedia, Shaquille O'Neal: /ʃəˈkiːl/

entries.name: Brahim
entries.source: Maghrebi Arabic form of Ibrahim: stress on the long ī
entries.notes: Today's brah-HEEM matches; British differs only in the unstressed first vowel.

entries.name: Blessing
entries.notes: Ordinary word 'blessing'. The name (Nigeria, Ghana, Zimbabwe) is said like the word; today's blˈɛsɪŋ is right, so nothing needs to ship.

entries.name: Ivana
entries.source: Wiktionary, Ivana: Czech [ˈɪvana], Slovak [ˈiʋana], Serbo-Croatian /ǐʋana/
entries.notes: Czech, Slovak, Croatian, Serbian, Slovene and Macedonian bearers all stress the first syllable and together outnumber the Italian, Spanish and English group. Decision to review: English text about Ivana Trump says ee-VAH-nuh (today's reading).

entries.name: Fábio
entries.source: Wiktionary, Portuguese Fábio: /ˈfa.bju/
entries.notes: Final -io is one syllable 'byoo' (as Antônio, Sérgio); British today also says the 'lot' vowel.

entries.name: Dìngyī
entries.source: Mandarin 定一 dìngyī: ding [tiŋ], yi [i] (as Yi, n0003); guide stress convention
entries.notes: Today's DING-yee only stresses the first syllable; sounds otherwise the same. Tones dropped.

entries.name: Jiāchéng
entries.source: Mandarin 嘉诚 jiāchéng: jia [tɕja] (as Jiaxiang), cheng [ʈʂʰəŋ] (as Cheng, n0005); guide stress convention
entries.notes: Today's JAH-cheng uses the 'eh' vowel; pinyin -eng is 'ung'. Tones dropped.

entries.name: Norbert
entries.region: Germany, France, Austria, Hungary, Poland, US
entries.source: Wiktionary, German Norbert: /ˈnɔʁbɛʁt/; Polish /ˈnɔr.bɛrt/
entries.notes: German, Hungarian, Polish and English bearers stress the first syllable; today's reading differs only in the unstressed vowel.

entries.name: Cesar
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish César: /ˈθesaɾ/, /ˈsesaɾ/ (as César, n0003)
entries.notes: The unaccented spelling is mostly US Hispanic and Spanish bearers (Cesar Chavez). Today's SEE-zer is the English Caesar.

entries.name: Sadia
entries.source: Urdu سعدیہ sādiya: first-syllable stress, the ʿayn heard as a long ā

entries.name: Gaston
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Gaston: /ɡas.tɔ̃/
entries.notes: FR register 34k. Nasal ɔ̃ → 'on' plus n (as Alphonse); French names take final stress in English.

entries.name: Solange
entries.source: Wikipedia, Solange Knowles: /soʊˈlɑːnʒ/; French /sɔ.lɑ̃ʒ/
entries.notes: Today's SAL-unj stresses the first syllable and reads g as j.

entries.name: Guadalupe
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Guadalupe: /ɡwadaˈlupe/; Merriam-Webster Guadalupe Hidalgo \ˌgwä-dᵊl-ˈü-pā\
entries.notes: Today's gwah-duh-LOOP drops the final syllable. Reviewer: US place names (Guadalupe, California; the Guadalupe River) are sometimes said without the final -pe; the change reaches them too.

entries.name: Imtiaz
entries.source: Urdu امتیاز imtiyāz: stress on the long final ā
entries.notes: Today's im-TEE-uz stresses the i and reduces the long 'ah'.

entries.name: Mira
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mira: Finnish /ˈmirɑ/, Italian and Polish /ˈmi.ra/, Serbo-Croatian /mǐːra/
entries.notes: Every bearer group, English included (Mira Sorvino, Mira Nair: MEER-uh), says 'ee'; today's MY-ruh is a spelling reading.

entries.name: Hector
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Héctor: /ˈektoɾ/
entries.notes: Also the word 'hector' (to bully) and, far more often in English text, Hector of Troy and English bearers, all said HEK-ter (today's reading). Spanish-speaking bearers (US Hispanic, ES 53k) say EK-tor with a silent h; that reading is in us/gb, protected so the English uses keep today's reading. The accented Héctor is a separate spelling.

entries.name: Mabel
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Mabel: /ˈmeɪbəl/

entries.name: Jon
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Jon: /d͡ʒɒn/
entries.notes: English JON (US 169k) is the largest single reading; the Scandinavian and Basque readings differ from each other.

entries.name: Zeynep
entries.source: Wiktionary, Turkish Zeynep: /zejˈnep/
entries.notes: Today's ZAY-nep stresses the first syllable; Turkish stresses the last.

entries.name: Theo
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Theo: /ˈθiː.əʊ/
entries.notes: English THEE-oh (GB 43k, US 32k births) is the largest single reading.

entries.name: rafiq
entries.notes: Lowercase spelling: a register/Wikidata artefact (as yenni, n0004). An entry would only touch lowercase 'rafiq'; the capitalised name Rafiq (Arabic rafīq, rah-FEEK) belongs in its own row.

entries.name: Danish
entries.source: Urdu دانش dāniš: long ā takes the stress
entries.notes: Capitalised 'Danish' in English text is overwhelmingly the adjective and language (Danish pastry, the Danish government), read DAY-nish. The Urdu name دانش dāniš (Danish Kaneria) is DAH-nish; that reading is in us/gb, protected so the adjective keeps today's reading.

entries.name: Desmond
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Desmond: /ˈdɛzmənd/

entries.name: Marwan
entries.source: Arabic مروان marwān: the final long ā takes the stress
entries.notes: Today's MAR-wahn stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Josefa
entries.source: Spanish spelling rules (as José, n0001): j [x], stress on -se-
entries.notes: Spain alone has 226k bearers. Spanish j → h (guide); the s stays voiceless. Today's yoh-SEF-uh is a German-style guess.

entries.name: Guillaume
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Guillaume: /ɡi.jom/
entries.notes: French ill is a y sound and au is 'oh'; today's gil-OWM reads it as English.

entries.name: Juma
entries.source: Swahili Juma [ˈd͡ʒuma] (penultimate stress); Arabic جمعة jumʿa

entries.name: Anjum
entries.source: Urdu انجم anjum: short a [ə], short u [ʊ]; first-syllable stress
entries.notes: Today's AN-jum uses the 'cat' vowel; Urdu short a is 'uh'.

entries.name: Shu
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 書 shū: [ʂu⁵⁵]

entries.name: Mehboob
entries.source: Urdu محبوب mahbūb: stress on the long final ū
entries.notes: Today's MEB-oob stresses the first syllable. The h is kept, as for Mehmet (n0002).

entries.name: Pei
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 佩 pèi: [pʰeɪ̯⁵¹]; I. M. Pei /peɪ/

entries.name: Hernán
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Hernán: /eɾˈnan/
entries.notes: Spanish h is silent and the accent marks final stress; today's HER-nun reads it as English.

entries.name: Anqi
entries.source: Mandarin 安琪 ānqí: an [an] (as Ān, n0007), qi [tɕʰi]; guide stress convention
entries.notes: Pinyin q is 'ch'; today's ANG-kee reads it as k.

entries.name: Xiaohong
entries.source: Mandarin 晓红 xiǎohóng: xiao [ɕjɑʊ] (as Xiao), hong [xʊŋ] (as Hong, n0003); guide stress convention
entries.notes: Today's ZHOW-hawng reads x as zh. Tones dropped.

entries.name: Zhou
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 周 zhōu: [ʈ͡ʂoʊ̯⁵⁵]; Zhou Enlai /dʒoʊ/

entries.name: Zhao
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 趙 zhào: [ʈ͡ʂɑʊ̯⁵¹]
entries.notes: Pinyin zh is unaspirated [ʈʂ] → j (as Zhang, Zhou); today's ZHOW uses the 'measure' sound.

entries.name: Ge
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 歌 gē / 戈 gē: [kɤ⁵⁵]; pinyin e is 'uh' (as Ke, He)
entries.notes: Today's JEE is a guess. Reviewer: 'Ge' is also the chemical symbol for germanium, which today's reading doesn't say either.

entries.name: Zhenyu
entries.source: Mandarin 振宇 zhènyǔ: zhen [ʈʂən] (as Zhen, n0002), yu [y] (as Yu, n0001); guide stress convention
entries.notes: Today's ZHEN-yoo reads zh as the 'measure' sound and en as 'en'. Tones dropped.

entries.name: Hu
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 胡 hú: [xu³⁵]

entries.name: Fān
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 帆 fān: [fan⁵⁵]; pinyin an is 'ahn' (as Lán, Ān)
entries.notes: Today's FAN has the 'cat' vowel. Tone mark dropped.

entries.name: Guózhōng
entries.source: Mandarin 国忠 guózhōng: guo [ku̯ɔ] (as Guoguang), zhong [ʈʂʊŋ] (as Zhong, n0008); guide stress convention
entries.notes: Today's GWOHZ-hawng splits zh into z and h. Tones dropped.

entries.name: Xiǎolóng
entries.source: Mandarin 小龍 xiǎolóng: xiao [ɕjɑʊ], long [lʊŋ] (as Long, Wenlong); guide stress convention
entries.notes: Today's ZHOW-lawng reads x as zh and ong as 'awng'. Tones dropped.

entries.name: Jessie
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Jessie: /ˈd͡ʒɛsi/

entries.name: Yash
entries.source: Hindi यश yaś: short a [ə]
entries.notes: Today's YASH uses the 'cat' vowel; Hindi short a is 'uh' (as Sanjay, Karan).

entries.name: Khalil
entries.source: Arabic خليل ḵalīl: stress on the long ī; Wikipedia, Khalil Mack: 'Kah-leel'
entries.notes: kh → k (guide). Today's KAL-ul stresses the first syllable and loses the long 'ee'.

entries.name: Parviz
entries.source: Wiktionary, Persian پرویز (parviz): Iran formal [pʰæɹ.viːz]; Behind the Name /pæɾ.ˈviːz/ (Persian)
entries.notes: Persian short a before r and a consonant (or at the end) is written English 'ar' (US ɑɹ, GB ɑː), as Parviz and Ardeshir in earlier batches: the voice's 'cat' vowel before r comes out as 'er'. Matches n0010. Today's PAR-viz stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Klaus
entries.source: Wiktionary, German Klaus: /klaʊ̯s/

entries.name: Lynn
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Lynn: /lɪn/

entries.name: Sai
entries.notes: Also the word 'sai' (the Okinawan weapon), said SIGH. The Indian name साई sāī is said SIGH in English and by most bearers (a slightly longer two-mora 'saa-ee' in careful Hindi, Telugu and Marathi); today's sˈI is right, so nothing needs to ship.

entries.name: Yannick
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Yannick: /ja.nik/
entries.notes: FR register 92k. French names take final stress in English, and the i is 'ee'.

entries.name: Anushka
entries.source: Wikipedia, Anushka Sharma: /əˈnʊʃka/
entries.notes: The stressed vowel is the short u of 'push'; today's uh-NUSH-kuh uses the 'cup' vowel.

entries.name: Đức
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese đức: Hà Nội [ʔɗɨk̚˧˦], Saigon [ʔɗɨk̚˦˥]
entries.notes: Đ is a d; ư [ɨ] → the 'book' vowel (guide). Today's VUK reads Đ as v. Tone dropped.

entries.name: Nga
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese nga: [ŋaː˧˧] in all three dialects

alternatives.context: closer to Vietnamese, starting with the ng of 'sing' (ngah)

entries.notes: One syllable. It starts with the ng of 'sing', which English words never start with; the nearest English onset is n. No English source gives an approximation (Ngọc, n0005, was left unresolved), hence low. Today spells it out letter by letter (EN-GEE-AY). Tone dropped.

entries.name: Bianca
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Bianca: /biˈɑːŋkə/; Italian /ˈbjaŋ.ka/
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today says the 'lot' vowel (bee-ONK-uh). US already right.

entries.name: Abhinav
entries.source: Hindi अभिनव abhinav: short a, i, a; aspirated bh → b (as Abhishek, n0002)
entries.notes: Today's ab-HEE-nahv splits bh and lengthens both short vowels. Hindi stress is weak and no source gives it; the closed final syllable takes it here.

entries.name: Jerzy
entries.source: Wiktionary, Polish Jerzy: /ˈjɛ.ʐɘ/
entries.notes: Polish j is y, rz is zh. Today's JUR-zee reads it as 'jersey'.

entries.name: Kartik
entries.source: Hindi कार्तिक kārtik: long ā takes the stress

entries.name: Ronaldo
entries.source: Wikipedia, Cristiano Ronaldo: English /rɒˈnældoʊ/, European Portuguese [ʁuˈnaɫdu]; Spanish [roˈnaldo]

alternatives.context: Brazilian bearers, with the Brazilian h-like r and vocalised l (hoh-NOW-doo)

entries.notes: Spanish and European Portuguese (ʁ → r, guide) agree with today's roh-NAHL-doh up to unstressed vowels. Decision to review: Brazilian bearers (wd BR 179) say hoh-NOW-doo.

entries.name: Ankita
entries.source: Hindi अंकिता aṅkitā: short a [ə] in a closed first syllable, short i
entries.notes: Today's an-KEE-tuh has the 'cat' vowel and a long ee. Hindi stress is weak; the heavy first syllable takes it, as in Mayank (Wikipedia [ˈmʌjʌnk]).

entries.name: Jagdeep
entries.source: Punjabi ਜਗਦੀਪ jagdīp: short a [ə], stress on the long ī (as Sandeep, n0002)
entries.notes: Today's JAG-deep has the 'cat' vowel and first-syllable stress.

entries.name: Mayank
entries.source: Wikipedia, Mayank Agarwal: Hindi [ˈmʌjʌnk]
entries.notes: Today's MAY-unk reads ay as 'ay'; Hindi has short a, then y.

entries.name: Neeraj
entries.source: Hindi नीरज nīraj: long ī takes the stress, short a
entries.notes: Today's NEER-eye misreads the final -aj (as Pankaj, n0002).

entries.name: Janaki
entries.source: Hindi जानकी jānakī: long ā in the first syllable takes the stress
entries.notes: Today's juh-NAH-kee stresses the short middle a.

entries.name: Nirmal
entries.source: Hindi निर्मल nirmal: short i, short a
entries.notes: Today's NUR-mul turns the i into the 'nurse' vowel.

entries.name: Purushottam
entries.source: Hindi पुरुषोत्तम puruṣottam: short u, u, long ō before a geminate takes the stress
entries.notes: Today's pyoor-uh-SHAH-tum adds a y and reads o as 'ah'. Geminate tt → single t (guide).

entries.name: Somnath
entries.source: Hindi सोमनाथ somnāth: long ō and long ā; th is an aspirated t
entries.notes: Indian th is an aspirated t, not the 'th' of 'thin'; today's SAHM-nuth also misreads both vowels.

entries.name: Suchitra
entries.source: Hindi सुचित्रा sucitrā: c is 'ch'; short i in the closed syllable takes the stress
entries.notes: Today's soo-KEE-truh reads ch as k.

entries.name: Sydney
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Sydney: /ˈsɪdni/

entries.name: Godwin
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Godwin: /ˈɡɒdwɪn/

entries.name: Hameed
entries.source: Arabic حميد ḥamīd, Urdu hamīd: stress on the long ī (as Hamid, n0002)
entries.notes: Today's HAM-eed stresses the short first vowel.

entries.name: Nisha
entries.source: Hindi निशा niśā: short i, which English keeps short in 'nish'

entries.name: Karla
entries.source: Wiktionary, German Karla: /ˈkaʁla/; English the same (as Carla, n0006)

entries.name: Seth
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Seth: /sɛθ/

entries.name: Dolores
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Dolores: /doˈloɾes/

alternatives.context: English-speaking bearers (Ireland, older US bearers: duh-LOR-is)

entries.notes: Spanish-speaking bearers (ES 160k plus Latin America and many US births) outnumber English ones. Today's US DOH-lerz drops a syllable; today's British is the English reading.

entries.name: Horacio
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Horacio: /oˈɾaθjo/, /oˈɾasjo/
entries.notes: Spanish h is silent, a is 'ah' and -cio is one syllable; today's hor-AY-see-oh reads it as English.

entries.name: Nur
entries.source: Arabic نور nūr; Turkish Nur [nuɾ]
entries.notes: Today's US nˈʊɹ is 'noor'; British drops the r like 'tour'.

entries.name: Aimé
entries.source: Wiktionary, French aimé: /ɛ.me/ (Aimé Césaire)
entries.notes: Two syllables with final stress; today's AIM drops the final é.

entries.name: Mariama
entries.ipa: ma.ri.ˈa.ma (built from the bearer's own respelling; no source transcription)
entries.source: TeachingBooks name recording by author Mariama J. Lockington: 'Ma Ree Ahma'; name sites give mah-ree-AH-mah
entries.notes: West African form of Mariam (Senegal, Guinea, Sierra Leone, the Gambia). Today's mair-ee-AM-uh uses English 'Mary' and 'cat' vowels; bearers say 'ah'.

entries.name: Pavel
entries.source: Wiktionary, Czech Pavel: [ˈpavɛl]; Slovene /páːʋəl/; Russian Павел [ˈpavʲɪl]
entries.notes: Czech, Russian, Slovene and Romanian bearers all say 'ah' in the stressed syllable; today's PAV-ul uses the 'cat' vowel.

entries.name: Randy
entries.notes: Ordinary word 'randy'. Name and word read the same today, and that is the name's main reading, so nothing changes.

entries.name: Camila
entries.source: Wikipedia, Camila Cabello: English /kəˈmiːlə/; Spanish Camila /kaˈmila/
entries.notes: US bearers (117k) are mostly Hispanic and, with Latin American and Brazilian bearers, say the i as 'ee'. Today's kuh-MIL-uh uses the short i.

entries.name: Mai
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese mai: [maːj˧˧]; Japanese まい [mai]; Estonian Mai: all 'my', as today

entries.name: Toni
entries.source: English Toni (pet form of Antonia/Antonio) /ˈtoʊni/; Finnish, German and Croatian Toni [ˈtoni] agree
entries.notes: All bearer groups (US women; Finnish, German, Croatian, Italian men) say TOH-nee.

entries.name: Camilo
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Camilo: /kaˈmilo/
entries.notes: Colombian, Chilean and Argentine bearers say the stressed i as 'ee'; today's kuh-MIL-oh uses the short i.

entries.name: Prasad
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi प्रसाद (prasād): /pɾə.sɑːd̪/
entries.notes: US-only fix: today's US PRASS-ud stresses the short first syllable; GB already says pruh-SAHD. Stress on the long ā (as Prakash).

entries.name: Evan
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Evan: /ˈɛvən/; matches today's reading

entries.name: Dolly
entries.notes: Ordinary word 'dolly'. Name and word read the same today, and that is the name's main reading, so nothing changes. (Dolly Parton, Dolly the sheep, a camera dolly.)

entries.name: Johanna
entries.source: Wiktionary, Johanna: German /joˈhana/, Dutch /ˌjoːˈɦɑ.naː/, Norwegian /juˈhanːa/, Swedish /jʊ²hanːa/; English /d͡ʒəʊˈænə/

alternatives.context: Finland: Finnish stresses the first syllable, YOH-hahn-nuh

entries.notes: anglo_share 0.07: German, Dutch, Swedish, Norwegian, Estonian and Latvian bearers agree on j as y, a sounded h and a stressed 'ah', and together far outnumber English bearers. Decision to review: this also changes English-speaking Johannas in English text. Reviewer: GB stressed vowel is the British front 'a' (German /joˈhana/, Swedish and Norwegian short [a]), as for Hans (n0002) and Hanna (n0007); today's GB already has that vowel there.

entries.name: Joanne
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Joanne: /d͡ʒoʊˈæn/; matches today's reading

entries.name: Theodore
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Theodore: /ˈθiː.əˌdɔː(ɹ)/; matches today's reading

entries.name: Lilian
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Lilian /ˈlɪli.ən/; German and Swedish Lilian also stress the first syllable

alternatives.context: France (FR 27k births), where Lilian is a boy's name: lee-LYAHN

entries.notes: Close call: the French boys' name (FR 27k) is the largest single register group, but English bearers (US 18k, UK, Ireland, Canada, plus many unregistered older British Lilians) together with German, Swedish, Dutch and Estonian bearers all stress LIL-. Worth a look alongside the Annie/Jacqueline decision.

entries.name: Jawad
entries.source: Arabic جواد jawād /d͡ʒaˈwaːd/, stress on the long ā
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today says juh-WOD (lot vowel) for the long ā. US unchanged.

entries.name: Dean
entries.notes: Ordinary word 'dean'. Name and word read the same today, and that is the name's main reading, so nothing changes.

entries.name: Frankie
entries.source: English pet form of Frank/Frances: /ˈfɹæŋki/ (as the word 'frank' + -ie); matches today's reading

entries.name: Leonel
entries.source: Spanish Leonel /leoˈnel/ (stress on the last syllable by the written-accent rule for words ending in l)
entries.notes: US bearers (26k) are mostly Hispanic; with Argentina, Brazil and Portugal they stress the last syllable. Today's LEE-oh-nul is an English spelling reading. Not Lionel.

entries.name: Morgan
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Morgan: /ˈmɔːɡən/, /ˈmɔɹɡən/; the tech list reads it the same way

alternatives.context: France (FR 34k births), where Morgan is unisex and stressed on the last syllable

entries.notes: Verify (tech list): the list's reading (Morgan as in J.P. Morgan) is also the English and Welsh name reading. English-speaking bearers (US 265k, UK, Canada) are the largest group.

entries.name: Fabrice
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Fabrice: /fa.bʁis/
entries.notes: French names take final stress in English (as Patrice); today's FAH-briss stresses the first syllable and shortens the i.

entries.name: Alpha
entries.source: French Alpha (Alpha Condé, Guinea) /al.fa/
entries.notes: Common word 'alpha' (Alpha Centauri, alpha version) and a tech-list term, both read ˈælfə. The West African given name (Guinea, Senegal, Sierra Leone) is AL-fa: the same sounds, so the name needs no entry and the term reading stays.

entries.name: Ayesha
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Aisha: /ˈaɪʃə/, /ɑːˈiːʃə/ (the earlier Aisha entry); no IPA found for the spelling Ayesha

alternatives.context: candidate for Pakistani, Indian and Bangladeshi bearers (Urdu عائشہ with long e: ah-YAY-shuh); unsourced

entries.notes: Today's US eye-EE-shuh and GB ah-YEE-shuh are both the established three-syllable English reading. South Asian bearers (UK register 6.8k) may say the middle vowel as 'ay'; no source found, so today's reading is kept. Worth a check with a native speaker.

entries.name: Hawa
entries.source: Wiktionary, Northern Kurdish Hawa: /ˈhɑːwɑ/; Swahili Hawa (Eve) by spelling: penultimate stress, a = 'ah'
entries.notes: Form of Ḥawwāʾ (Eve) used in West and East Africa (Senegal, Guinea, Uganda, Ghana). Bearers say 'ah'; today's HAW-wuh uses the 'law' vowel.

entries.name: Sunita
entries.source: Hindi सुनीता (sunītā): long ī stressed; today's sunˈitə matches

entries.name: Kumari
entries.source: Hindi कुमारी (kumārī): stress on the long ā; today's kumˈɑɹi matches

entries.name: Cameron
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Cameron: /ˈkæməɹən/; matches today's reading

entries.name: Mirza
entries.source: Bosnian Mirza [mîrza] (Serbo-Croatian two-syllable words are stressed on the first syllable); Urdu مرزا mirzā [ˈmɪɾzaː]

alternatives.context: Iran: Persian میرزا mirzâ, stressed on the last syllable

entries.notes: Bosnian, Pakistani and Indian bearers say i before r, not the 'ur' of today's MUR-zuh.

entries.name: Gavin
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Gavin: /ˈɡævɪn/; matches today's reading

entries.name: Caleb
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Caleb: /ˈkeɪləb/; matches today's reading

entries.name: Shreya
entries.source: Hindi श्रेया (śreyā): long ē stressed; today's ʃɹˈAə matches (the y glide follows 'ay')

entries.name: Vân
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese vân: (Hà Nội) [vən˧˧], (Saigon) [jəŋ˧˧]
entries.notes: â is [ə] ('uh', as the earlier Sơn); today's VAN uses the 'cat' vowel. Tone dropped.

entries.name: Bảo
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese bảo: [ɓaːw˧˩˧]; today's bˈW matches

entries.name: Hải
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese hải: [haːj˧˩˧]; today's hˈI matches

entries.name: Sameer
entries.source: Hindi समीर (samīr): /sə.miːɾ/; Arabic سمير samīr [saˈmiːr]: stress on the long ī, as today
entries.notes: Today's stress and stressed vowel match; the first vowel (US 'sah', GB 'som') differs only in reduction.

entries.name: Geraldo
entries.source: Brazilian Portuguese Geraldo [ʒeˈɾawdu]: g before e is zh, syllable-final l is [w], final o is [u] (Wiktionary, Portuguese Geraldo)

alternatives.context: Spanish-speaking bearers and Geraldo Rivera (US): heh-RAHL-doh

entries.notes: Wikidata bearers are overwhelmingly Brazilian (BR 238); Brazil's l before a consonant is 'w', so -ral- is 'row'. Decision to review: this changes Geraldo Rivera, said heh-RAHL-doh in US English text.

entries.name: Sylvester
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Sylvester: /sɪlˈvɛstə(ɹ)/; matches today's reading
entries.notes: Nigerian and German bearers stress -ves- too; today's reading is the English one.

entries.name: İbrahim
entries.source: Turkish İbrahim [ibɾaːˈhim]: stress on the last syllable; today's ˌɪbɹɑhˈim matches

entries.name: Júlio
entries.source: Wiktionary, Portuguese Júlio: Brazil /ˈʒu.li.u/, Portugal /ˈʒu.lju/
entries.notes: Portuguese j is zh and final unstressed -io is 'yoo' (as the earlier Sérgio entry); today's JOO-lee-oh is an English reading.

entries.name: Leopoldo
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Leopoldo: /leoˈpoldo/; Italian /le.oˈpɔl.do/
entries.notes: Stress and stressed vowel already match; the first syllable is Spanish and Italian e ('lay'), not today's 'lee'.

entries.name: Suraj
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi सूरज (sūraj): /suː.ɾəd͡ʒ/
entries.notes: Today's guess says SHOOR-uj; the first consonant is a plain s.

entries.name: Joana
entries.source: Wiktionary, Portuguese Joana: Portugal /ʒuˈɐ.nɐ/, Brazil /ʒoˈɐ.nɐ/; Catalan /ʒuˈanə/
entries.notes: Portuguese and Catalan bearers (PT, ES 13k, Brazil) say j as zh and stress a full 'ah'; today's joh-AN-uh is an English reading.

entries.name: Faruk
entries.source: Turkish Faruk [faˈɾuk]; Wikipedia, Farouk of Egypt: English /fəˈruːk/
entries.notes: Today's FARE-ik misreads both vowels and the stress.

entries.name: Christy
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Christy: /ˈkɹɪsti/; matches today's reading

entries.name: Halima
entries.source: Arabic حليمة ḥalīma: stress on the long ī; today's həlˈimə matches

entries.name: Abdul Haq
entries.source: Arabic عبد الحق ʿAbd al-Ḥaqq: ḥaqq [ħaqq], a backed after ḥ and q; Abdul as in the earlier Abdul entry

alternatives.context: Pakistan and India: Urdu حق [ɦəq], HUCK

entries.notes: Abdul is kept as today (precedent). Haq is 'hahk' for the Moroccan and Algerian bearers (q → k, ḥ → h, guide); today's HACK uses the 'cat' vowel. Reviewer: lowered to low. The wd counts (MA 12, DZ 7) are thin, Maghrebi bearers usually write Abdelhak, and Pakistani and Afghan bearers of this spelling (Urdu [ɦəq], HUCK) may be the larger group; no count settles it.

entries.name: Deepika
entries.source: Hindi दीपिका (dīpikā): long ī stressed, short i; today's dˈipɪkə matches

entries.name: Percy
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Percy: /ˈpɜːsi/, /ˈpɝsi/; the tech list reads it the same way

alternatives.context: Peru (Wikidata PE 47), where Percy is said in Spanish, PEHR-see

entries.notes: Verify (tech list): the list's reading is the English name reading. US, UK, Australian and New Zealand bearers outnumber the Peruvian ones.

entries.name: Nirmala
entries.source: Hindi निर्मला (nirmalā) by Devanagari spelling: short a [ə] in the middle; stress on the heavy closed first syllable (as Namrata)
entries.notes: Today's nir-MAH-luh stresses the light middle syllable and gives its schwa a long 'ah'. Tamil bearers (Nirmala Sitharaman) also stress the first syllable.

entries.name: Trupti
entries.source: Marathi/Gujarati तृप्ती (tṛptī): ṛ is said [ru] in Marathi and Gujarati, hence the spelling 'Tru-'
entries.notes: The vowel is the short u of 'put' (as Atul), not the 'cup' vowel of today's TRUP-tee. No pronunciation source for the name itself.

entries.name: Balram
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi बलराम (balrām): /bəl.ɾɑːm/; stress pattern as the earlier Jagannath entry (first syllable, secondary on the long final)
entries.notes: Today's BAL-rum has the 'cat' vowel for the schwa and reduces the long ā. Hindi stress is weak; no source marks it.

entries.name: Dawn
entries.notes: Ordinary word 'dawn'. Name and word read the same today, and that is the name's main reading, so nothing changes.

entries.name: Désiré
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Désiré: /de.zi.ʁe/
entries.notes: Today reads it as English 'desire'. French and Belgian/Congolese bearers say three syllables with final stress.

entries.name: Constantin
entries.source: Wikipedia, Constantin Brâncuși: Romanian [konstanˈtin brɨŋˈkuʃʲ]

alternatives.context: Germany: German Constantin, stressed on the first syllable

entries.notes: Romanian and Moldovan bearers (wd RO 880) dominate; French bearers also stress the last syllable. Today's kun-STAN-tin is an English reading.

entries.name: Silvio
entries.source: Wikipedia, Silvio Berlusconi: Italian [ˈsilvjo]; Wiktionary Italian Silvio /ˈsil.vjo/
entries.notes: Italian and Brazilian bearers say the stressed i as 'ee' (as the earlier Silvia entry); today's SIL-vee-oh uses the short i.

entries.name: Marat
entries.source: Wiktionary, Russian Марат (Marat): [mɐˈrat]

alternatives.context: Jean-Paul Marat, the French revolutionary (The Death of Marat): French /ma.ʁa/, muh-RAH

entries.notes: Russian, Kazakh, Tatar and Ukrainian bearers stress the last syllable with 'ah'; today's MAIR-ut fits no group. In English text this also changes Jean-Paul Marat, whose French reading muh-RAH is closer to the new reading than to today's.

entries.name: Giacomo
entries.source: Wiktionary, Italian Giacomo: /ˈd͡ʒa.ko.mo/
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today says JOCK-uh-moh (lot vowel); the Italian a is 'ah'. US unchanged.

entries.name: Célestin
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Célestin: /se.lɛs.tɛ̃/
entries.notes: Final stress; nasal ɛ̃ → 'an' as for the earlier Augustin. Today's SEL-iss-tin stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Yasmine
entries.source: French Yasmine /jas.min/; Arabic ياسمين yāsamīn, stress on the long ī
entries.notes: anglo_share 0.05: French (FR 33k) and Maghrebi bearers stress the last syllable. Same reading as the earlier Yasmin entry.

entries.name: Wenxiong
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 文 (wén) /wən/ and 雄 (xióng) /ɕi̯ʊŋ/
entries.notes: x → sh (guide), -en → 'un' (as Zhen), -iong → 'yoong' (as Yong). Tones dropped; primary on the last syllable (guide). Today's guess is garbled (WENK-shyawng).

entries.name: Gigi
entries.source: Wiktionary, Italian Gigi: /ˈd͡ʒi.d͡ʒi/ (pet form of Luigi); English Gigi /ˈd͡ʒiːd͡ʒiː/

alternatives.context: French Gigi (Colette's novel, the musical): zhee-ZHEE

entries.name: Hani
entries.source: Arabic هاني hānī: long ā stressed
entries.notes: Egyptian, Palestinian and Saudi bearers say a long 'ah'; today's HAN-ee uses the 'cat' vowel.

entries.name: Kennedy
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Kennedy: /ˈkɛnədi/; matches today's reading

entries.name: Manuela
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Manuela: /maˈnwela/; today's mænwˈAlə differs only in the unstressed first vowel

entries.name: Sahar
entries.source: Arabic سحر saḥar (dawn), stressed on the first syllable

alternatives.context: Iran: Persian سحر sahar, stressed on the last syllable

entries.notes: Arab bearers (Egypt, Iraq and others) outnumber Iranian ones; ḥ → h, stressed a is 'ah'. Today's SAA-hur uses the 'cat' vowel.

entries.name: Noureddine
entries.source: Arabic نور الدين Nūr ad-Dīn: stress on the long ī of dīn; French spelling ou = oo
entries.notes: Tunisian, Algerian and Moroccan bearers. Today's NOR-ed-dine reads ou as 'or' and -ine as 'eye-n'.

entries.name: Rahman
entries.source: Arabic رحمان raḥmān (stress on the long ā); Persian رحمان rahmân; Bengali রহমান [rɔɦman]
entries.notes: Conflicting bearer groups: as a given name (Iran, Turkey, Afghanistan, Arab countries) it is rah-MAHN, stressed on the long ā; as the very common Bangladeshi and Indian name element and surname (Mujibur Rahman, A. R. Rahman) it is stressed on the first syllable, as today's RAH-mun, which is also the usual English reading. Needs a decision on whether surname use in English text outweighs given-name bearers. GB today says ROM-un.

entries.name: Fatma
entries.source: Turkish Fatma [ˈfatma]: Turkish a is 'ah'
entries.notes: Turkish and Tunisian bearers say 'ah'; today's FAT-muh uses the 'cat' vowel.

entries.name: Bradley
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Bradley: /ˈbɹædli/; matches today's reading

entries.name: Rizwan
entries.source: Urdu رضوان rizwān (Arabic riḍwān): stress on the long final ā
entries.notes: Pakistani bearers stress the long ā (riz-WAHN); today's RIZ-wahn stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Markus
entries.source: Wiktionary, German Markus: /ˈmaʁkʊs/; today's mˈɑɹkəs differs only in the unstressed vowel

entries.name: Émile
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Émile: /e.mil/; today's Amˈil matches

entries.name: Celso
entries.source: Wiktionary, Portuguese Celso: Brazil /ˈsɛw.su/, Portugal /ˈsɛɫ.su/

alternatives.context: Brazil, with Brazilian final [u]: SEL-soo (Brazilians vocalise the l: SEW-soo)

entries.notes: Reviewer: changed from corrected. With the l kept (misaki has no 'ew' glide), the only difference from today's SEL-soh was the unstressed final vowel (Portuguese final [u] is the reduced form of o), which the guide does not churn; same call as Edson (n0009). Spanish-speaking and Filipino bearers say SEL-soh too.

entries.name: Rodney
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Rodney: /ˈɹɒdni/; matches today's reading

entries.name: Vincenzo
entries.source: Wiktionary, Italian Vincenzo: /vinˈt͡ʃɛn.t͡so/
entries.notes: Italian ce is ch and z here is ts; today's vin-SEN-zoh reads both as English.

entries.name: Antoinette
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Antoinette /ˌæntwəˈnɛt/; French /ɑ̃.twa.nɛt/
entries.notes: US bearers (61k) and French bearers (FR 32k, Belgium, Switzerland) share the stressed final -NET; only unstressed vowels differ.

entries.name: Andres
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Andrés: /anˈdɾes/ (the unaccented spelling is the US and Latin American register form)

alternatives.context: Estonia (wd EE 355): Estonian Andres, stressed on the first syllable

entries.notes: Hispanic US bearers (94k births) plus Spain and Latin America far outnumber Estonian ones. Today's AHN-drayz is French André plus s. Same reading as the earlier Andrés entry.

entries.name: Clifford
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Clifford: /ˈklɪfəd/; matches today's reading

entries.name: Dragan
entries.source: Wiktionary, Serbo-Croatian Dragan: /drǎːɡan/
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today says DROG-un (lot vowel); the stressed vowel is a long 'ah'. US unchanged.

entries.name: Patience
entries.notes: Ordinary word 'patience'. Name and word read the same today, and that is the name's main reading, so nothing changes. Nigerian, Ugandan and Ghanaian bearers (the largest groups) say it as the English word.

entries.name: Matt
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Matt: /mæt/; matches today's reading

entries.name: Moisés
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Moisés: /moiˈses/

alternatives.context: Brazil and Portugal: Portuguese Moisés, moy-ZES

entries.notes: Peruvian, Mexican and Argentine bearers outnumber Brazilian ones; the accent marks final stress. Today's MOY-ziz reads it as English Moses.

entries.name: Abdi
entries.source: Somali Abdi (short for Abdullahi/Abdirahman): first-syllable stress, as today
entries.notes: Somali bearers (Norway, UK, US, Kenya) are the largest group; Somali a in this word is front, close to today's 'cat' vowel.

entries.name: Derrick
entries.notes: Ordinary word 'derrick'. Name and word read the same today, and that is the name's main reading, so nothing changes.

entries.name: Shiv
entries.source: Hindi शिव (śiv): /ʃɪʋ/
entries.notes: Also the slang word 'shiv' (a makeshift knife). The Hindi name शिव is said SHIV, the same as the word and as today, so nothing changes.

entries.name: Farhan
entries.source: Arabic فرحان farḥān: stress on the long ā; Wikipedia, Farhan Akhtar: Hindustani [fəɾɦaːn]
entries.notes: Today's FAR-hun stresses the first syllable and reduces the long ā.

entries.name: Sabita
entries.source: Nepali/Odia सबिता (sabitā, eastern form of Savitā): short a and short i; Nepali, Odia and Bengali stress the first syllable
entries.notes: Today's sah-BEE-tuh lengthens and stresses the short i. The b spelling marks eastern bearers (Nepal, Odisha, Bengal), whose languages stress the first syllable; no source for the name itself.

entries.name: Upendra
entries.source: Hindi उपेन्द्र (upendra): stress on the heavy -pen-; pattern as Devendra and Jitendra
entries.notes: Today's UP-en-druh reads it as English 'up' with first-syllable stress.

entries.name: Xuân
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese xuân: (Hà Nội) [swən˧˧], (Saigon) [sʷəŋ˧˧]
entries.notes: Vietnamese x is s and â is 'uh'; today's ZHWAHN reads x as zh.

entries.name: Quân
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese quân: (Hà Nội) [kwən˧˧], (Saigon) [wəŋ˧˧]
entries.notes: â is 'uh' (as Sơn); today's KWAWN uses the 'law' vowel.

entries.name: Meena
entries.source: Hindi मीना (mīnā): long ī stressed; today's mˈinə matches

entries.name: Raimundo
entries.source: Wiktionary, Portuguese Raimundo: Brazil /ʁajˈmũ.du/
entries.notes: ai is 'eye' in Portuguese and Spanish; today's ruh-MOON-doh drops it. Brazilian bearers (BR 213) are the largest group; French/Portuguese r → English r (guide).

entries.name: Vaishnavi
entries.source: Hindi वैष्णवी (vaiṣṇavī): ai is [ɛː] (Wiktionary, Hindi वैष्णव /ʋɛːʂ.ɳəʋ/); stress on the heavy first syllable

alternatives.context: Marathi and South Indian bearers, who say ai as 'eye': VYSH-nuh-vee

entries.notes: Hindi ai is [ɛː] as in the earlier Kailash and Aishwarya entries; ṣ → sh, ʋ → v. Today's vah-ish-NAH-vee splits ai and stresses the wrong syllable.

entries.name: Minghui
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 明 (míng) /miŋ/ and 慧/輝 (huì/huī) /xu̯eɪ̯/
entries.notes: hui is 'hway' (as the earlier Hui). Tones dropped; primary on the last syllable (guide). Today says MING-hwee.

entries.name: Mónica
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Mónica: /ˈmonika/
entries.notes: The accented spelling is Spanish and Portuguese only; today's MAH-nik-uh is English Monica.

entries.name: Aarti
entries.source: Hindi आरती (ārtī): /ɑːɾ.t̪iː/
entries.notes: Today adds a secondary stress on -ti (AR-TEE); one stress on the long first syllable (as the earlier Swati entry).

entries.name: Rohini
entries.source: Hindi रोहिणी (rohiṇī): long ō in the first syllable, short i; Hindi stress on the heavy first syllable
entries.notes: Today's roh-HEE-nee stresses and lengthens the short i. Retroflex ṇ → n.

entries.name: Supriya
entries.source: Hindi सुप्रिया (supriyā); today's supɹˈiə matches the reading kept for Priya (PREE-yuh)

entries.name: Suhas
entries.source: Marathi/Hindi सुहास (suhās): stress on the long ā
entries.notes: Today's guess SOO-uz drops the h and reduces the long ā.

entries.name: Anurag
entries.source: Hindi अनुराग (anurāg): /ə.nʊ.ɾɑːɡ/; stress on the long ā
entries.notes: Today's AN-yoo-rag reads it as an English word with 'cat' vowels.

entries.name: Arpita
entries.source: Hindi अर्पिता (arpitā) by Devanagari spelling: schwa before r, short i; stress on the heavy closed first syllable (as Nandita, Aparna)
entries.notes: Today's ar-PEE-tuh lengthens and stresses the short i. Bengali bearers say the first vowel as [ɔ]; no source marks the stress.

entries.name: Deepti
entries.source: Hindi दीप्ति (dīpti): long ī stressed; today's dˈipti matches

entries.name: Sarada
entries.source: Wikipedia, Sarada Devi: Bengali [ʃarod̪a]; Sanskrit शारदा (śāradā), Telugu శారద: initial ś and a long first ā
entries.notes: 'Sarada' is a diacritic-free spelling of Śāradā (Bengali, Telugu, Malayalam bearers), whose first consonant is sh. Stress on the long first syllable; today's sar-AH-duh stresses the second. Some South Indian bearers say s: low confidence on the first consonant.

entries.name: Sourav
entries.source: Wikipedia, Sourav Ganguly: Bengali [ʃou̯ɾɔbʱ]; English IPA given there /ˈsaʊərˌav/

alternatives.context: the English reading of the spelling (cricket commentary): SOW-ruv

entries.notes: Bengali s is sh and ou is an 'oh' diphthong, stressed on the first syllable; the spelling's v is kept (Bengali bh is often softened). Today's suh-RAHV stresses the second syllable.

entries.name: Sudha
entries.source: Hindi सुधा (sudhā): short u [ʊ] in an open stressed syllable, aspirated dh → d; the Uma precedent (n0003) maps that to English 'oo', which is today's sˈudə
entries.notes: Reviewer: changed from corrected. A short [ʊ] in an open stressed syllable is English 'oo' by the Uma precedent (n0003: ˈumə); the Atul and Anushka 'book' vowel is for closed syllables. Today's SOO-duh therefore matches: stress, consonants and stressed vowel are the bearers'.

entries.name: Arundhati
entries.source: Hindi अरुन्धती (arundhatī); Wikipedia, Arundhati Roy: Bengali [orundʱoti]
entries.notes: u is short [ʊ], not the 'cup' vowel; the a after dh is a schwa, not today's secondary-stressed 'dah'. Stress on the heavy closed -run-.

entries.name: Kasturi
entries.source: Hindi कस्तूरी (kastūrī): stress on the long ū; today's kɑstˈʊɹi says 'TOO-ree' (misaki writes oo before r + vowel as ʊɹ, as in 'jury')
entries.notes: Only the unstressed first vowel differs in reduction.

entries.name: Chandrasekhar
entries.source: Wikipedia, Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar: English /ˌtʃəndrəˈʃeɪkər/
entries.notes: ś is sh, e is long 'ay' and stressed, and the first a is a schwa ('chun'). Today's chan-druh-SEK-er reads it as English.

entries.name: Nirupama
entries.source: Hindi निरुपमा (nirupamā) by Devanagari spelling: short i, u and a, long final ā; no source marks the stress
entries.notes: Today's nir-oo-PAH-muh gives the short a a long 'ah'; the candidate keeps today's stress with the schwa ('uh'). Stress is unsourced: the Hindi weight rule points at the long final -mā, while Kannada and Odia bearers stress the first syllable. Needs a stress source.

entries.name: Ramakant
entries.source: Hindi रमाकांत (ramākānt) by Devanagari spelling: short first a, long ā in -mā- and -kānt; no source marks the stress
entries.notes: Today's RAH-muh-kunt has the vowel lengths backwards (long first a, schwa in -kānt). The stress is unsourced: the weight rule allows -mā- or the superheavy -kānt, and the Jagannath precedent stresses the first syllable. Needs a stress source.

entries.name: Sunday
entries.notes: Capitalised 'Sunday' in English text is overwhelmingly the day of the week. The name (mostly Nigerian bearers, wd NG 35) is said the same way, so nothing changes.

entries.name: Ilham
entries.source: Arabic إلهام ilhām: stress on the long ā; Azerbaijani İlham [ilˈhɑm]
entries.notes: Moroccan, Algerian (FR and ES registers) and Azerbaijani bearers stress the long ā; today's IL-hum reduces it.

entries.name: Gerson
entries.source: Brazilian Portuguese Gerson [ˈʒɛʁ.sõ] by spelling (g before e = zh); Wikipedia, Gérson (footballer)

alternatives.context: Spanish-speaking bearers (Central American and US Hispanic): HAIR-sohn

entries.notes: Brazilian bearers (BR 71) are the largest group; today's JUR-sun is an English spelling reading. The final nasal [õ] is reduced as an unstressed vowel.

entries.name: Yongchang
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 永 (yǒng) /i̯ʊŋ/ and 昌 (chāng) /ʈ͡ʂʰɑŋ/
entries.notes: -ong is 'oong' (as Yong), -ang is 'ahng' (as Zhang). Tones dropped; primary on the last syllable (guide).

entries.name: Hendra
entries.source: Collins (via Dictionary.com), Hendra: /ˈhɛndrə/ (the Brisbane suburb and Hendra virus); Indonesian Hendra stressed on the first syllable
entries.notes: Indonesian bearers (wd ID 27). Indonesian e can be [ɛ] or schwa and the spelling doesn't show which; no source found for the name. Today's HEN-druh is also the English reading of Hendra virus, so it is kept.

entries.name: Amr
entries.source: Wikipedia, Amr Diab: Egyptian Arabic [ˈʕɑmɾe]

alternatives.context: common English reading with the vowel before r: AH-mer (today's US)

entries.notes: Egyptian bearers (wd EG 42) put the helping vowel after the r ([ˈʕɑmɾe]), which also keeps the r in British speech; today's GB says OM-uh with no r.

entries.name: Marcela
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Marcela: /maɾˈθela/, Latin America /maɾˈsela/
entries.notes: Argentine, Mexican, Chilean and US Hispanic bearers say c as s; today's mar-CHEL-uh is Italian. Vowel as in the earlier Marcelo entry.

entries.name: Saïd
entries.source: Wikipedia, Edward Said: English /sɑːˈiːd/; Arabic سعيد saʿīd
entries.notes: The diaeresis marks two syllables; today's SED reads it as English 'said'. ʿayn dropped with the vowels kept apart (guide). Same reading as the earlier Said entry, which is protect-word only because of the English verb.

entries.name: Abdulla
entries.region: Uzbekistan, Azerbaijan, Russia (Tatar, Bashkir, North Caucasus)
entries.source: Wiktionary, Azerbaijani Abdulla: [ɑbduˈɫːɑ], stress on the last syllable; Uzbek, Tatar and Uyghur also stress the last syllable (regular rule)

alternatives.context: Maldivian and South Asian bearers, and the reading chosen for Abdullah (n0001): ahb-DOO-luh, today's

entries.notes: Reviewer: changed from already-correct. Spellings are researched for their own bearers (guide). The h-less Abdulla is the Uzbek and Azerbaijani standard spelling and the usual transliteration of Russian Абдулла (Tatar, Bashkir, North Caucasus), and those bearers (Uzbekistan alone has 36M people) far outnumber the Maldivian ones; all stress the last syllable, as the Rustam entry (n0009) does for Central Asian names. Decision to review: Abdullah (n0001) keeps ab-DOO-luh.

entries.name: Chelsea
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Chelsea: /ˈt͡ʃɛlsi/; matches today's reading
entries.notes: Also the London district and football club, said the same way.

entries.name: Issam
entries.source: Arabic عصام ʿiṣām: stress on the long ā, backed after emphatic ṣ
entries.notes: Today's ISS-um stresses the first syllable and reduces the long ā. ʿayn dropped (guide).

entries.name: Liliana
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Liliana: /liˈljana/; Italian /li.liˈa.na/
entries.notes: US bearers (72k) are mostly Hispanic; with Argentina, Italy, Romania, Peru and Poland they say the stressed a as 'ah'. Today's lil-ee-AN-uh uses the 'cat' vowel.

entries.name: Anas
entries.source: Wiktionary, Malay Anas [a.nas]; Arabic أَنَس anas, stressed on the first syllable (like Hasan)
entries.notes: Today's US AN-us sounds like 'anus' and GB AH-nuz voices the s. Bearers (Morocco, Syria, Egypt, Malaysia) say a full a in both syllables; the second a is kept full.

entries.name: Mireille
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Mireille: /mi.ʁɛj/
entries.notes: French -eille is [ɛj] ('ay'), with no l; today's mih-RAYL adds one.

entries.name: Thérèse
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Thérèse: /te.ʁɛz/
entries.notes: French th is t and the stress is final; today's THERR-eess reads it as English Theresa without the a.

entries.name: Min
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 敏 (mǐn) /min/; Korean 민 [min]; today's mˈɪn matches

entries.name: Piotr
entries.source: Wiktionary, Polish Piotr: /pjɔtr/
entries.notes: One syllable: pi is 'py' and final tr is a cluster. Today's PIE-uh-ter splits it into three syllables.

entries.name: Sitaram
entries.source: Hindi सीताराम (sītārām): compound of सीता (sītā) and राम (rām), all long vowels; first-syllable stress with a secondary on rām (as Jagannath, and as Telugu stresses the first syllable)
entries.notes: Today's SIT-uh-ram shortens both long vowels. Stress is weak in Hindi and unsourced here.

entries.name: Heinz
entries.source: Wiktionary, German Heinz: /haɪ̯nt͡s/

alternatives.context: the Heinz food brand (H. J. Heinz), Heinz Field and English-speaking surname bearers: HINES (today's reading)

entries.notes: Capitalised 'Heinz' in English text is mostly the ketchup and baked-beans brand, read HINES; a name entry would change it. The German given name (DE, AT, CH) ends in ts: that reading is in us/gb.

entries.name: Jianhua
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 建 (jiàn) /t͡ɕi̯ɛn/ and 華 (huá) /xu̯a/
entries.notes: -ian is 'yen' (as Jiànpíng), hua is 'hwah'. Tones dropped; primary on the last syllable (guide). Today's JAHN-hoo-uh misreads both.

entries.name: Fabian
entries.source: Wiktionary, German Fabian /ˈfaː.bi.an/; Polish /ˈfa.bjan/; English /ˈfeɪ.bi.ən/

alternatives.context: English bearers and the adjective (Fabian Society, Fabian strategy): FAY-bee-un, today's reading
Spanish-speaking bearers (Fabián, often written without the accent in the US): fah-BYAHN

entries.notes: Capitalised 'Fabian' is also an English adjective and noun (the Fabian Society, Fabian tactics), read FAY-bee-un, so a name entry would change it. The name's bearers are mostly German, Austrian, Swiss, Polish and Scandinavian (anglo_share 0.08), who say FAH-bee-ahn: that reading is in us/gb.

entries.name: Hope
entries.notes: Ordinary word 'hope'. Name and word read the same today, and that is the name's main reading, so nothing changes.

entries.name: Isha
entries.source: Hindi ईशा (īśā): long ī
entries.notes: Indian bearers (Isha Ambani, Isha Koppikar) say a long 'ee'; today's ISH-uh uses the short i.

entries.name: Francesca
entries.source: Wiktionary, Italian Francesca /franˈt͡ʃe.ska/; English /fɹænˈt͡ʃɛskə/
entries.notes: Italian and English bearers agree; today's reading differs from Italian only in the unstressed first vowel.

entries.name: Saba
entries.source: Wiktionary, Persian صبا (sabâ): Classical /sa.ˈbaː/, Iran [sæ.bɒ́ː]; Behind the Name lists the name as Persian and Urdu صبا

alternatives.context: Georgia (Georgian Saba, a man's name) and Italy: SAH-buh, today's reading

entries.notes: Pakistani, Indian, Iranian and Arab bearers (and the UK, US and Norwegian registers) stress the long final ā; Georgian bearers (wd GE 13) are a smaller group. No Urdu IPA source found.

entries.name: Andrej
entries.source: Wiktionary, Andrej: Slovene /andrɛ̀ːj/ (stressed long final vowel); Czech [ˈandrɛj], Slovak /ˈandrɛj/

alternatives.context: Slovakia and Czechia: AHN-dray, stressed on the first syllable (today's US reading)

entries.notes: Slovene bearers (wd SI 817) far outnumber Slovak and Czech ones, and Russian bearers of this transliteration (Андрей [ɐnˈdrʲej]) also stress the last syllable.

entries.name: Gui
entries.source: Wiktionary, Portuguese Gui (pet form of Guilherme): /ˈɡi/; Walloon Gui (= Guy): /ɡi/

alternatives.context: China: Mandarin 桂/贵 guì, GWAY

entries.notes: Tech-list clash: the list reads GUI (graphical user interface) as GOO-ee; the name is settled at merge. Brazilian, Portuguese, Belgian and French bearers say GHEE (u only marks the hard g); Chinese bearers are fewer.
entries.word_check: gold has 'gui'; kept: lower-case 'gui' and 'GUI' stay with the tech list's GUI; only the casing 'Gui' is the name

entries.name: Hanif
entries.source: Arabic حنيف ḥanīf: stress on the long ī; Wikipedia, Hanif Kureishi
entries.notes: Pakistani, Iranian and Arab bearers stress the long ī; today's HAN-if stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Valentine
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Valentine: /va.lɑ̃.tin/

alternatives.context: English bearers and the everyday English use: VAL-en-tine (today's reading)

entries.notes: Capitalised 'Valentine' in English text is mostly St Valentine and Valentine's Day (VAL-en-tine), so a name entry must not change it. The largest bearer group is French women (FR 40k): va-lahn-TEEN, given in us/gb. French nasal ɑ̃ → 'ahn'.

entries.name: Zhèngzhōng
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 正 (zhèng) /ʈ͡ʂɤŋ/ and 中 (zhōng) /ʈ͡ʂʊŋ/
entries.notes: zh → j (guide), -eng → 'ung' (as Zhēng), -ong → 'oong' (as Zhong). Tones dropped; primary on the last syllable (guide). Today reads zh as 'measure' zh.

entries.name: Dézhì
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 德 (dé) /tɤ/ and 志 (zhì) /ʈ͡ʂʐ̩/
entries.notes: de [tɤ] is 'duh' (as Zhe); syllabic zhi is 'jr' (as Zhi, Zhiming). Tones dropped; primary on the last syllable (guide). Today's DEZ-ee reads zh as z.

entries.name: Mina
entries.source: Wiktionary, Japanese みな (Mina) [mʲina]; Norwegian and Serbian Mina stress the first syllable; today's mˈinə matches

alternatives.context: Iran: Persian مینا mina, stressed on the last syllable

entries.name: Russell
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Russell: /ˈɹʌsəl/; matches today's reading

entries.name: Lee
entries.notes: Ordinary word 'lee'. Name and word read the same today, and that is the name's main reading, so nothing changes. Chinese 李 Lǐ and Korean 이 bearers who write Lee are also called LEE in English.

entries.name: Márcio
entries.source: Wiktionary, Portuguese Márcio: Brazil /ˈmaʁ.si.u/, Portugal /ˈmaɾ.sju/
entries.notes: Final unstressed -io is 'yoo' (as Sérgio); today's MAR-see-oh. Stressed syllable already right.

entries.name: Yasin
entries.source: Turkish Yasin [jaːˈsin]; Arabic ياسين yāsīn, stress on the long ī
entries.notes: Turkish, German-Turkish and Arab bearers stress the last syllable; today's YASS-in stresses the first. First vowel as in the earlier Yasmin entry.

entries.name: Luka
entries.source: Wiktionary, Serbo-Croatian Luka: /lûːka/; today's lˈukə matches

entries.name: Ting
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 婷 (tíng): /tʰiŋ³⁵/
entries.notes: Also the word 'ting' (a ringing sound). Mandarin tíng [tʰiŋ] reads tˈɪŋ, the same as the word and as today, so nothing changes.

entries.name: Zhixiang
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 志 (zhì) /ʈ͡ʂʐ̩/ and 祥 (xiáng) /ɕi̯ɑŋ/
entries.notes: zhi → 'jr' (as Zhiming), x → sh, -iang → 'yahng'. Tones dropped; primary on the last syllable (guide). Today's guess says ZHIK-syang.

entries.name: Shǒurén
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 守 (shǒu) /ʂoʊ̯/ and 仁 (rén) /ʐən/
entries.notes: Two syllables: ou is 'oh', r [ʐ] is English r, -en is 'un' (as Zhen). Tones dropped; primary on the last syllable (guide). Today's guess reads it as one syllable, SHOWERN.

entries.name: Paulina
entries.source: Wiktionary, Polish Paulina: /pawˈli.na/; Spanish /pawˈlina/
entries.notes: Polish, Mexican, German and Swedish bearers say au as 'ow' (as the earlier Paula and Paulo entries); today's first syllable is 'paw'.

entries.name: Behnam
entries.source: Wiktionary, Persian بهنام (behnâm): Iran formal [beɦ.nɒ́ːm]; Behind the Name /beh.ˈnɒːm/
entries.notes: Matches n0012. Today's BEN-um drops the h and stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Wasim
entries.source: Arabic وسيم (wasīm), Urdu وسیم: long ī in the final closed syllable, which Arabic and Urdu stress (as Rasheed, Majid)
entries.notes: Today's WAW-sim stresses the first syllable and uses the 'law' vowel. Wasim Akram is wuh-SEEM. No IPA found for this exact spelling, so medium.

entries.name: İsmail
entries.source: Turkish İsmail: three syllables, i-a-i, final stress (Turkish personal names); same reading as the Ismail entry (n0002, Wiktionary)
entries.notes: US today is already is-mah-EEL; the British reading IZ-mile is the English Ishmael-style guess. GB-only fix, as for Ismail in n0002.

entries.name: Rosemary
entries.notes: Ordinary word 'rosemary' (the herb). The name is said like the word (ROHZ-mair-ee); today's reading is right for both, so nothing needs to ship.

entries.name: Heather
entries.notes: Ordinary word 'heather' (the plant). The name is said like the word (HEDH-er); today's reading is right for both, so nothing needs to ship.

entries.name: An
entries.source: Vietnamese an [ʔaːn]; Mandarin 安 ān [an] (as Ān, n0007); Korean 안 [an]
entries.notes: The English article 'an' must not change. The name reading (Vietnamese An, Chinese Ān, Korean An, Japanese 杏 An, Flemish An short for Anna) is 'ahn' and is kept in us/gb.

entries.name: Anjana
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi अंजना (añjnā): /ənd͡ʒ.nɑː/; Malayalam, Kannada and Telugu keep three syllables (añjana)

alternatives.context: Hindi, with the middle vowel dropped (UNJ-nuh)

entries.notes: Short a [ə] in the stressed first syllable is 'uh' (as Anjali, Ranjana); today's an-JAN-uh uses the 'cat' vowel and stresses the second syllable. Three syllables follow the Ranjana precedent (n0008).

entries.name: Amine
entries.source: French spelling of Arabic أمين (amīn), French [a.min]; Arabic stresses the long final syllable (as Amin, n0006, and Lamine, n0008)
entries.notes: Also the rare chemistry word 'amine', which the app's GB reads AY-meen. Treated as a name under the guide's rare-technical-word rule: the word is rare and written lower-case, the name has 26,525 French births (and MA/DZ/TN bearers). US already says uh-MEEN (also a dictionary reading of the word); this fixes GB.
entries.word_check: gold has 'amine' read əmˈin, the same as the name: kept

entries.name: Taylor
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Taylor: /ˈteɪ.lə/, /ˈteɪ.lɚ/
entries.notes: Today's reading is the established English one.

entries.name: Lukas
entries.source: Wiktionary, German Lukas [ˈluːkas]; English Lukas rhymes -uːkəs; Lithuanian [ˈlʊkɐs], Slovak [ˈlukas]
entries.notes: Every reading ends in s; today's LOO-kuz has a z. German, Scandinavian and English bearers differ only in the unstressed vowel.

entries.name: Taha
entries.source: Wikipedia, Taha Hussein: Egyptian Arabic [ˈtˤɑːhɑ]
entries.notes: Emphatic ṭ is English t. US today is right; GB's 'lot' vowel (TOH-huh) becomes 'ah'.

entries.name: Ammar
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic عمار: /ʕam.maːr/; Urdu /(ʔ)əm.mɑːɾ/; Arabic stress falls on the final long-vowel-plus-consonant syllable
entries.notes: Initial ʿayn is silent in English and the double m is single (guide). Today's AM-er stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Chun
entries.source: Korean 전 Chun [tɕʌn] (Chun Doo-hwan) and Cantonese 'Chun' (俊 [tsɵn]) are 'chun'; Mandarin 春 chūn [ʈʂʰu̯ən] is 'chwun'

alternatives.context: Mandarin pinyin chūn 春 (mainland bearers), as Chunhua and Chunsheng

entries.notes: Kept: the registers (US 120, CA 127, GB 91) point to Korean and Cantonese diaspora bearers, and English text uses Chun mostly for the Korean surname. Mixed groups; mainland Mandarin bearers would say chwun.

entries.name: Gustav
entries.source: Wiktionary, German Gustav: /ˈɡʊstaf/; Czech [ˈɡustaf]
entries.notes: US today matches; GB's 'lot' vowel in the second syllable (GUUS-tof) becomes 'ah'. German bearers (wd DE 1,428) outnumber Swedish and Norwegian ones.

entries.name: Ria
entries.notes: Ordinary word 'ria' (a drowned river valley). The name is said like the word (REE-uh); today's reading is right for both, so nothing needs to ship. Dutch, German, Indian and Japanese (りあ) bearers say REE-uh too.

entries.name: Sébastien
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Sébastien: /se.bas.tjɛ̃/
entries.notes: French names take final stress in English; -ien [jɛ̃] is 'yan' (as Augustin, Sylvain). Today's suh-BAS-chun is the English Sebastian.

entries.name: Fǎng
entries.source: Mandarin 昉 fǎng [fɑŋ]; -ang is 'ahng' (as Fang, n0004)
entries.notes: Today's FANG uses the 'cat' vowel.

entries.name: Jiaju
entries.source: Mandarin 家駒/嘉聚 jiājū/jiājù: jia [tɕja] (as Jiā, n0005), ju [tɕy] (ü → 'oo', as Jun)
entries.notes: Today's jee-AH-joo splits jia into two syllables. Tones dropped; primary stress on the last syllable, secondary on the first (guide convention for two-syllable Chinese given names).

entries.name: Edgardo
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Edgardo: /edˈɡaɾdo/; Italian /edˈɡar.do/
entries.notes: Today's ed-GAR-doh matches.

entries.name: Lidia
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Lidia: /ˈlidja/; Polish and Italian /ˈli.dja/
entries.notes: Today's LID-ee-uh uses the 'bit' vowel; every bearer group says 'lee'. Brazilian Lídia (IBGE 88,259) has the same stress and vowel.

entries.name: Trang
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese trang: Saigon [ʈaːŋ˧˧], Hà Nội [t͡ɕaːŋ˧˧]
entries.notes: Vietnamese a is 'ah' (as Quang, Hoàng); today's TRANG uses the 'cat' vowel. Southern and most overseas bearers have a retroflex t, which English speakers hear as 'tr'.

entries.name: Józef
entries.source: Wiktionary, Polish Józef: /ˈju.zɛf/
entries.notes: Polish j is y and ó is 'oo'; today's JOH-zuf reads it as English Joseph.

entries.name: Anson
