entries.notes: Today's MAH-rek matches (GB's short ɑ as for Tarek, n0007).

entries.name: Matheus
entries.source: Brazilian Portuguese spelling: th = t, stressed diphthong eu [ew] (as Mateus [maˈtews]); IBGE 2010: 350,434 Brazilians named Matheus
entries.notes: Today's MATH-oyz reads th and eu as English. The diphthong [ew] has no English match: 'eh' plus 'oo' is the usual approximation.

entries.name: Selma
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Selma: /ˈsɛlmə/; Faroese /ˈsɛlma/
entries.notes: Every bearer group stresses the first syllable 'sel'; Brazilian Selma (IBGE 102,364) vocalises the l (SEW-muh). Also Selma, Alabama.

entries.name: Eli
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Eli: /ˈilaɪ/
entries.notes: English bearers (US 145,941 births) are the largest group.

entries.name: Juliet
entries.region: US, UK, Uganda, Nigeria, New Zealand
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Juliet: /ˈd͡ʒuːlɪɛt/, /ˌd͡ʒuliˈɛt/, /ˈd͡ʒuliət/
entries.notes: Today's US joo-lee-ET and GB JOO-li-et are both listed English readings.

entries.name: Lourdes
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish and Tagalog Lourdes: /ˈluɾdes/; English (the town) /lʊɹd(z)/
entries.notes: Bearers (ES 39,275, the Philippines, Mexico, Peru, US Hispanic, Lourdes Leon) say LOOR-des, kept in us/gb. Protected because the spelling's everyday English use is the French town and shrine (Our Lady of Lourdes, and the many schools, hospitals and churches named after it), read LOORD(Z), today's reading. Needs a decision, like Milan and Orlando (n0005).

entries.name: Luna
entries.source: English, Spanish and Italian Luna: /ˈluːnə/, [ˈluna] (gold dictionary, today's reading)
entries.notes: English LOO-nuh and Spanish/Italian/German [ˈluna] differ only in the unstressed final vowel.

entries.name: Mahdi
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Mahdi: /ˈmɑːdi/

alternatives.context: Persian Mahdi (Iran, the largest Wikidata group): final stress, as the Mehdi entry (n0002)

entries.notes: Kept: 'the Mahdi' (the Islamic eschatological figure, the Sudanese Mahdi) is the spelling's everyday English use, read MAH-dee; Arabic [ˈmahdiː] also stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Esra
entries.source: Turkish Esra (from Arabic isrāʾ): regular orthography [es.ɾa], final stress like other Turkish personal names (Zeynep, Ömer)
entries.notes: Today's EZ-ruh reads it as English Ezra.

entries.name: Idrissa
entries.region: Senegal, Mali, Niger, Côte d'Ivoire, France
entries.source: West African form of Arabic Idrīs; the stressed syllable is the long drī of the Arabic stem
entries.notes: Today's ih-DREE-suh matches how English commentators say it (Idrissa Gueye). Low: no IPA source for Wolof, Fula or Mandinka stress; French says ee-dree-SAH.

entries.name: Siti
entries.source: Wikipedia, Siti Nurhaliza: Malay [ˈsiti]; Wiktionary Malay siti /ˈsiti/
entries.notes: Today's SIT-ee uses the 'bit' vowel.

entries.name: Josué
entries.region: Mexico, Guatemala, Puerto Rico, Honduras, US, Peru
entries.source: Spanish Josué [xoˈswe]: regular orthography, the accent marks final stress; j [x] → h (guide)
entries.notes: Forebears 2014: Spanish-speaking bearers (Mexico 99,002, Guatemala 23,332, Puerto Rico 17,969, Honduras 16,871, US 16,248, Peru 13,656 and others, about 236,000) outnumber Brazil (110,218). Today's JOH-zhoo fits nobody.

entries.name: Lulu
entries.notes: Ordinary word 'lulu' (slang: a remarkable person or thing). The name is said like the word (LOO-loo); today's reading is right for both, so nothing needs to ship. Chinese 露露 lùlù is loo-LOO.

entries.name: Idris
entries.source: Wikipedia, Idris Elba: English /ˈɪdrɪs/

alternatives.context: Arabic Idrīs, Turkish İdris and Urdu: stress on the long final syllable (id-REES)

entries.notes: Today's EYE-druss fits nobody. Close population call: first-syllable ID-ris (Idris Elba, Welsh Idris, Malay/Indonesian [ˈidris]) against final-stress id-REES (Arabic, Turkish, Urdu). Forebears 2014 puts Nigeria first (483,624; stress unknown), then Indonesia 68,780 and Turkey 60,828. The English IPA for the spelling's best-known English-text bearer decides it.

entries.name: Rasheed
entries.source: Arabic رشيد (rašīd) [raˈʃiːd]; as Rashid (n0003, Wiktionary English /ɹəˈʃiːd/)
entries.notes: Today's ruh-SHEED matches.

entries.name: Maxime
entries.source: French Maxime [mak.sim], final stress in English (as Yannick, n0010)
entries.notes: Today's mak-SEEM matches.

entries.name: Mandy
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Mandy: /ˈmændi/
entries.notes: German and Dutch Mandy is the borrowed English name, said the English way.

entries.name: Giorgio
entries.source: Wiktionary, Italian Giorgio: /ˈd͡ʒɔr.d͡ʒo/, /ˈd͡ʒor.d͡ʒo/
entries.notes: Italian gi before o is just j (Giorgio Armani); today's JOR-jee-oh adds a syllable.

entries.name: Amrit
entries.source: Hindi अमृत (amŕt) [əmɾɪt̪]; Punjabi ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤ; short a is 'uh' (as Amrita, n0004)
entries.notes: GB already says UM-rit; US AHM-rut is aligned with it.
entries.word_check: gold has 'amrit'; kept: 'amrit' is a Sikh religious term, written lower-case

entries.name: Duncan
entries.source: English/Scottish Duncan /ˈdʌŋkən/ (CMUdict, today's reading)
entries.notes: Today's reading is the established English one.

entries.name: Odette
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Odette: /ɔ.dɛt/
entries.notes: Today's oh-DET matches.

entries.name: Christoph
entries.source: Wiktionary, German Christoph: /ˈkrɪstɔf/
entries.notes: Today's KRIS-tof matches.

entries.name: Thu
entries.drop_detail: Core reads it as a month or weekday abbreviation ('Jun 5', 'Thu 3pm') after the lexicon runs
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese thu [tʰu˧˧] (autumn); th as in Thảo (n0010)
entries.notes: Vietnamese th is an aspirated t; today's guess reads it as the voiced 'th' of 'the'. The weekday abbreviation is safe: the app already expands 'Mon–Thu', 'Thu 5 Oct' and 'Thu, Oct 9' to Thursday before phonemizing.

entries.name: Tanvi
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi तन्वी: /t̪ən.ʋiː/
entries.notes: Short a [ə] is 'uh' (as Anjali); today's TAN-vee uses the 'cat' vowel.

entries.name: Kedar
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi केदार: /keː.d̪ɑːɾ/; the final long-vowel-plus-consonant syllable takes the stress (as Rajesh, Ramesh)
entries.notes: Hindi e is 'ay'; today's KEE-dur reads it as 'ee' and reduces the long ā.

entries.name: Sanjana
entries.source: Hindi संजना (sañjanā): short a, first-syllable stress; as Anjana and Ranjana (n0008)

alternatives.context: Hindi, with the middle vowel dropped (SUNJ-nuh)

entries.notes: Today's sahn-YAH-nuh reads j as y and stresses the second syllable.

entries.name: Reena
entries.source: Hindi रीना (rīnā): long ī, first-syllable stress; as Leena and Reema (n0007, n0008)
entries.notes: Today's REE-nuh matches.

entries.name: Amalia
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Amalia: /aˈmalja/; Italian and Polish /aˈma.lja/; English /əˈmɑli.ə/
entries.notes: US today matches; GB's 'lot' vowel (uh-MOL-yuh) becomes 'ah'.

entries.name: Giuse
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese Giuse: alternative spelling of Giu-se (Joseph); no pronunciation given
entries.notes: Catholic baptismal name (Joseph). Regular orthography gives Hà Nội [zu.sɛ] (zoo-SEH) and Saigon [ju.ʂɛ] (yoo-SHEH/yoo-SEH); which syllable English should stress has no source. The candidate follows the southern (overseas) reading. Today's JOO-see (like Italian Giuse, short for Giuseppe) is wrong for Vietnamese bearers.

entries.name: Khánh
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese khánh: Saigon [kʰan˧˦], Hà Nội [xajŋ̟˧˦]; -anh as Anh and Thanh
entries.notes: US today is right; GB's 'lot' vowel (KON) becomes 'ah'. Tone dropped.

entries.name: Nguyên
entries.source: Wikipedia, Nguyen: Vietnamese [ŋwiən] (northern), [ŋwiəŋ] (southern); English approximations /wɪn/, /nuːˈjɛn/, /ˈnjuːən/

alternatives.context: the commonest English approximation of the surname Nguyễn (Wikipedia)

entries.notes: One syllable in Vietnamese. English never starts a word with ng, so n keeps the onset (as Nga, n0010); iê as in Huyền and Miên. Today's noo-YEN is one of Wikipedia's English approximations for the surname but splits the syllable and stresses 'yen'. Low: no source gives an approximation for the given name.

entries.name: Việt
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese việt [viət̚]; English 'Viet' in Vietnam /viˈɛt/
entries.notes: Today's vee-ET is the established English rendering (Vietnam, Viet Cong); Vietnamese has one syllable.

entries.name: Harsh
entries.source: Hindi हर्ष (harṣ) [ɦəɾʂ]
entries.notes: Common English word 'harsh'. The Indian name has the short a [ə] before r, 'hur' (as Varsha), kept in us/gb.

entries.name: Anoop
entries.source: Hindi अनूप (anūp) [ənuːp]; as Anup (n0006)
entries.notes: Today's uh-NOOP matches.

entries.name: Shruti
entries.source: Hindi श्रुति (śruti) [ʃɾʊt̪i]; English 'oo' for a short u in an open syllable (as Uma, Usha)
entries.notes: Today's SHROO-tee matches the usual English rendering (Shruti Haasan).

entries.name: Arnaud
entries.source: French Arnaud [aʁ.no], final stress in English
entries.notes: Today's ar-NOH matches.

entries.name: Neera
entries.source: Hindi नीरा (nīrā): long ī before r is 'ee'; as Meera (n0009)
entries.notes: GB today says NIRR-uh (the 'mirror' vowel); US ɪɹ becomes iɹ as for Samira (n0007).

entries.name: Aruna
entries.source: Hindi अरुणा (aruṇā); as Arun (n0001, uh-ROON)
entries.notes: Today's ah-ROO-nuh differs from uh-ROO-nuh only in the unstressed first vowel.

entries.name: Nishant
entries.source: Hindi निशांत (niśānt): the long ā plus consonants is the heaviest syllable and takes the stress (as Prashant, n0004)
entries.notes: Today's NISH-unt stresses the first syllable and reduces the long ā.

entries.name: Tushar
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi तुषार: /t̪ʊ.ʂɑːɾ/
entries.notes: The long final ā plus r takes the stress (as Sardar, n0002); today's TUUSH-er stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Mallika
entries.source: Wiktionary, Sanskrit मल्लिका /mɐl̪.l̪i.kɑː/; Hindi [məlːɪkɑː]
entries.notes: Short a [ə] in the heavy first syllable is 'uh' (as Nalini); today's MAL-ik-uh uses the 'cat' vowel.

entries.name: Ashwini
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi अश्विनी: /əʃ.ʋɪ.niː/; the heavy first syllable takes the stress (as Aishwarya)
entries.notes: Today's ash-WEE-nee stresses the light middle syllable and uses the 'cat' vowel.

entries.name: Shikha
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi शिखा: /ʃɪ.kʰɑː/
entries.notes: Short i [ɪ] and first-syllable stress, as Smita and Richa (n0008); today's SHEE-kah lengthens the i.

entries.name: Bhupinder
entries.source: Punjabi ਭੁਪਿੰਦਰ (bhupindar): short u, stress on the heavy pin syllable (as Surinder, n0007)
entries.notes: Punjabi bh carries a tone; English speakers say b. Today's BOW-pine-der reads u as 'ow' and i as 'eye'.

entries.name: Usha
entries.source: Wikipedia, Usha Vance: /ˈuːʃə/; Hindi उषा (uṣā)
entries.notes: Today's UH-shuh uses the 'cup' vowel.

entries.name: Niranjan
entries.source: Hindi निरंजन (niranjan): short i, two schwa a's; the Hindustani weight rule stresses the heavy closed syllable 'ran'
entries.notes: Today's nih-RAHN-jun uses the long 'ah' for the Hindi schwa; Indian short a is 'uh' (as Sanjay, Pankaj).

entries.name: Hardev
entries.source: Punjabi ਹਰਦੇਵ / Hindi हरदेव (har + dev): schwa a; Wiktionary Hindi देव /d̪eːʋ/ has a long e
entries.notes: Today's HAR-dev uses 'ah' for the schwa and a short 'eh' for the long e. Final stress follows the Hindustani weight rule for a superheavy last syllable (as Ramesh, Vinod); Punjabi stress for this name is not documented.

entries.name: Latha
entries.source: Wikipedia, Lata Mangeshkar: Marathi [ləˈt̪aː] (the same name, latā); the -th- spelling is South Indian and marks a dental t

alternatives.context: Hindi and Marathi Lata, final stress as Wikipedia gives for Lata Mangeshkar: luh-TAH

entries.notes: th is a dental t, not the 'th' of thin (today's LATH-uh), and the first a is 'uh'. The -th- spelling's bearers are mostly Tamil, Telugu and Kannada speakers, whose languages stress the first syllable; the unstressed final ā is 'uh' as for Geeta and Asha. The stress is the uncertain part.

entries.name: Srinivas
entries.source: Sanskrit श्रीनिवास (śrīnivāsa); South Indian bearers say 'sree', long ī and long ā; Dravidian languages stress the first syllable

alternatives.context: Hindi-speaking bearers: 'shree', and the weight rule stresses the final -VAHS

entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today says the 'lot' vowel for the long ā (-vos). US already right.

entries.name: Dilip
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi दिलीप: /d̪ɪ.liːp/; the long final syllable takes the stress (weight rule, as Sunil)
entries.notes: Today's DIL-ip shortens the long ī and stresses the wrong syllable.

entries.name: Prahlad
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi प्रह्लाद: /pɾəɦ.lɑːd̪/ [pɾɛʱ.läːd̪]
entries.notes: The h after the schwa only colours the vowel (a breathy 'eh'), so English drops it; the long ā of the superheavy last syllable takes the stress (weight rule). Today's PRAH-lud has the wrong vowels and stress.

entries.name: Hemant
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi हेमंत: /ɦeː.mənt̪/; the superheavy last syllable takes the stress (weight rule, as Vasant, Prashant)
entries.notes: Today's HEM-unt shortens the long e and stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Pabitra
entries.source: Sanskrit पवित्र (pavitra, 'pure'); Odia ପବିତ୍ର, Bengali পবিত্র (pobitro): stress on the heavy closed syllable 'bit'

alternatives.context: Odia and Bengali speakers' own vowels: paw-BEE-traw

entries.notes: Today's puh-BIT-ruh is the usual Indian-English shape with the right stressed syllable (as Debendra, n0007). Odia, Bengali and Assamese bearers have o-like unstressed vowels.

entries.name: Biju
entries.source: Malayalam ബിജു, Odia ବିଜୁ (biju): [bid͡ʒu]. Wikipedia's Malayalam and Odia phonology pages list a close /i/ only (Malayalam short /i/ vs long /iː/; Odia has no length contrast), not Hindi's lax [ɪ]; the guide maps i to English 'ee'. First-syllable stress
entries.notes: Reviewer: changed from corrected (BIJ-oo). The Smita precedent (n0008) is for Hindi lax [ɪ]; Biju's bearers (Kerala, Odisha: Biju Patnaik, Biju Menon) have a short tense [i], i → 'ee' by the guide's table. Today's BEE-joo has the right stress, consonants and stressed vowel; the GB final u is only unlengthened.

entries.name: Purnima
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi पूर्णिमा: /puːɾ.ɳɪ.mɑː/; the superheavy first syllable takes the stress
entries.notes: Today's PUR-ni-muh uses the 'her' vowel for the long ū. Retroflex ɳ → n; final ā unstressed → 'uh'.

entries.name: Shashi
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi शशि: /ʃə.ʃiː/ [ʃɐ.ʃiː]
entries.notes: Today's SHAH-shee uses 'ah' for the schwa; Indian short a is 'uh' (as Hari, Ravi).

entries.name: Shubha
entries.source: Sanskrit/Hindi शुभा (śubhā, from शुभ śubh 'auspicious'): short u in an open stressed syllable, aspirated bh, long final ā; the Uma precedent (n0003) maps that u to English 'oo'
entries.notes: Today's SHUB-huh reads bh as two sounds and the u as 'cup'. A short [ʊ] in an open stressed syllable is English 'oo' (Uma, n0003; Sudha, n0011 review); the 'book' vowel is for closed syllables (Atul). Aspirated bh → b (as Bharat); the unstressed final ā is 'uh' (as Asha). Reviewer: changed from ʃˈʊbə.

entries.name: Anasuya
entries.source: Sanskrit अनसूया (anasūyā): short a's, long ū, which takes the stress
entries.notes: Today's secondary 'an' uses the 'cat' vowel; Indian short a is 'uh' (as Sanjeev, n0001). The stressed SOO is already right.

entries.name: Bhaskar
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi भास्कर: /bʱɑːs.kəɾ/; the superheavy first syllable takes the stress
entries.notes: Today gives the second syllable a full 'ar' (and British the 'lot' vowel in the first); the second a is a schwa (as Shankar).

entries.name: Bipin
entries.source: Hindi बिपिन, Bengali বিপিন (bipin): two short i's; first-syllable stress as for Nitin (n0004) and Bengali initial stress
entries.notes: Today's BY-pin reads the i as 'eye'.

entries.name: Debasish
entries.source: Bengali দেবাশীষ (debashish): e, a, ī; Bengali শ/ষ are both sh; Bengali stresses the first syllable (Wikipedia, Bengali phonology)
entries.notes: Today's duh-BAY-sis reads the a as 'ay' and the s as s. The stress is the weak Bengali initial stress; no English source gives one for this name.

entries.name: Dipankar
entries.source: Bengali দীপঙ্কর (dipongkor): Bengali's inherent vowel is [ɔ]; Bengali stresses the first syllable (Wikipedia, Bengali phonology)

alternatives.context: Hindi and pan-Indian English reading of Sanskrit Dīpaṅkara: dee-PUNG-kur

entries.notes: Today's dip-ANG-kar uses the 'cat' vowel. Bearers (Dipankar Bhattacharya, Dipankar Gupta) are mostly Bengali; the stress is unsourced.

entries.name: Gopinath
entries.source: Wiktionary, Sanskrit गोपीनाथ: /ɡoː.piː.n̪ɑː.t̪ʰɐ/; modern languages drop the final a
entries.notes: th is an aspirated dental t, not the 'th' of thin (today's GOH-pi-nuth), and the last a is a long 'ah'. Stress pattern as the Jagannath precedent (n0005).

entries.name: Prajakta
entries.source: Marathi प्राजक्ता (prājaktā): long ā, j as in 'jam', schwa, long final ā
entries.notes: Today's prah-YAHK-tuh reads j as y. Marathi stress is weak; the first syllable (long ā) is chosen as for Aditya (n0003); no source gives it.

entries.name: Santanu
entries.source: Bengali শান্তনু (Shantanu), written Santanu in the usual Bengali romanisation: [ʃan̪t̪onu], s-letter said sh, initial stress (Wikipedia, Bengali phonology); English Wikipedia's Santanu articles are mostly Bengali bearers (Sen, Pramanik, Bhowmik, Dey, Das, Bose, Chaudhuri, Ghatak, Bhattacharya) against one Odia (Acharya)

alternatives.context: Odia bearers (ଶାନ୍ତନୁ), who say the letter as s: SAHN-tuh-noo

entries.notes: Today's sahn-TAH-noo stresses the short middle syllable. Reviewer: switched the main reading from Odia s to Bengali sh, because the bearers of this spelling are mostly Bengali (as Debasish in this batch and Sourav, Sarada in n0011, where Bengali s-spellings are read sh). The initial stress is Bengali's weak stress; no source gives an English stress.

entries.name: Sunder
entries.source: Wikipedia, Sundar Pichai: English /ˈsʌndɑːr/ (Sunder is another spelling of सुंदर sundar)
entries.notes: Also the archaic verb 'sunder'. The name's English reading (SUN-dur) already matches today's sˈʌndəɹ, so nothing needs shipping.

entries.name: Fazlur
entries.notes: Fazl + ur (the article of Fazl-ur-Rahman). Bengali bearers (Fazlur Rahman Khan) say fozlur, Urdu speakers fuzlur, Arabic fadlur; the 'ur' is 'oor' in all, so today's FAZ-ler is off, but no source gives the stress or settles the first vowel. Candidate is the Urdu reading.

entries.name: Lorena
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Lorena: /loˈɾena/; Italian /loˈrɛ.na/, /loˈre.na/; Brazilian /loˈɾẽ.nɐ/
entries.notes: Spanish-speaking bearers (Spain 62k, Mexico, Argentina, US Hispanic) dominate; Spanish e in an open syllable is 'ay'. Today's lor-EN-uh.

entries.name: Juana
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Juana: /ˈxwana/; same as the Juan entry (n0001)
entries.notes: Spanish j → h (guide); British today also says the 'lot' vowel.

entries.name: Erich
entries.source: Wiktionary, German Erich: [ˈeːʁɪç]

alternatives.context: some US bearers, who say it like English Eric

entries.notes: German long e is 'ay'; German ch → k (guide). German-speaking bearers (wd DE 1591, AT 389) far outnumber the US group (11k). Today's EH-rik is the English Eric.

entries.name: Antoni
entries.source: Wiktionary, Polish Antoni: /anˈtɔ.ɲi/; Catalan Antoni [ənˈtɔni] has the same stressed vowel
entries.notes: Polish and Catalan o is open [ɔ] ('aw', as António, n0004); today's 'toh'. Polish bearers (wd PL 1370, plus most of GB-EAW 3.1k) dominate.

entries.name: Celina
entries.source: English /səˈliːnə/; Spanish Celina [seˈlina] (regular orthography); s and second-syllable stress shared
entries.notes: English (US 15k), Spanish, Portuguese, French and Norwegian bearers all say s-LEE-na, more than the Polish and German ts group. Reviewer: Poland has about 17.6k living Celinas (PESEL, as reported by Eska), so the ts group is roughly Poland plus part of Germany; still smaller than the s group together.

entries.name: Éric
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Éric: /e.ʁik/
entries.notes: The accented spelling is French; today reads it as English Eric. French names take final stress in English.

entries.name: Dwi
entries.source: Indonesian dwi (from Sanskrit dvi, 'two'; a name for a second child): one syllable, regular spelling
entries.notes: Today spells it out as letters (D-W-I).

entries.name: Eileen
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Eileen: /ˈaɪliːn/, US also /aɪˈliːn/

entries.name: Sabina
entries.source: Wiktionary, Polish/Italian Sabina: /saˈbi.na/; English /səˈbiːnə/
entries.notes: Today's reading differs only in the unstressed first vowel.

entries.name: Martine
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Martine: /maʁ.tin/
entries.notes: French bearers (FR 319k) dominate; today's mar-TEEN matches.

entries.name: Adrián
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Adrián: /aˈdɾjan/
entries.notes: The accented spelling is Spanish; today reads it as English Adrian (AY-dree-un). -ián is said in two English syllables, as Gabriel (n0001).

entries.name: Ardeshir
entries.source: Wiktionary, Persian اردشیر: Iranian formal [ʔæɹ.d̪e.ʃíːɹ], Classical /ʔar.da.ˈʃiːr/; stress on the last syllable
entries.notes: Today's AR-di-shur stresses the first syllable; Persian stresses the last. Persian æ before r is said with English 'ar', the nearest English sequence; ī before r is the 'eer' of 'sheer'.

entries.name: Arie
entries.source: Wiktionary, Dutch Arie: /ˈaː.ri/
entries.notes: Dutch bearers (wd NL 308) and Dutch-American ones dominate; today's AIR-ee is an English spelling reading.

entries.name: Moustapha
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic مصطفى: /musˤ.tˤa.faː/; same reading as the Mustapha entry (n0005)
entries.notes: French ou is 'oo'; today's MUS-taf-uh has the wrong vowels. Senegalese and Ivorian bearers' own stress is unsourced; 'ta' stress follows the Mustapha precedent.

entries.name: Christelle
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Christelle: /kʁis.tɛl/

entries.name: Sandrine
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Sandrine: /sɑ̃.dʁin/
entries.notes: Today's SAN-drin stresses the first syllable with the 'cat' vowel. Nasal ɑ̃ → 'ahn' (as Laurent, n0006); final stress.

entries.name: Theresia
entries.source: Wiktionary, German Theresia: /teˈʁeː.zi̯a/
entries.notes: Th is a plain t; today's 'the-RAY-see-uh' uses the 'th' of 'this'. Indonesian bearers (wd ID 21) say s rather than z.

entries.name: Oswald
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Oswald: /ˈɒzwəld/

alternatives.context: German, Austrian and Swiss bearers: OSS-vahlt

entries.notes: Covered by the tech list on purpose. Also the surname (Lee Harvey Oswald), the spelling's main use in English text.

entries.name: Mateo
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Mateo: /maˈteo/

entries.name: Elvira
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Elvira: /elˈbiɾa/; Russian Эльвира [ɪlʲˈvʲirə]; Italian /elˈvi.ra/
entries.notes: Spanish, Russian, Italian, Portuguese and Swedish bearers all say el-VEE-ra; today's el-VY-ruh is an English spelling reading. Spanish b/v [β] → v as English speakers say it.

entries.name: Etienne
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Étienne: /e.tjɛn/
entries.notes: French often drops the accent on a capital É, so this spelling is mostly French bearers (FR 62k, Quebec 8k). Today stresses the first syllable. -tienne is said in two English syllables, as Gabriel's -iel.

entries.name: Jake
entries.notes: Also the slang word 'jake' (fine, all right). Name and word sound the same.

entries.name: Emile
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Émile: /e.mil/

entries.name: Léonard
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Léonard: /le.ɔ.naʁ/
entries.notes: The accented spelling is French (three syllables, silent d); today reads it as English Leonard (LEN-urd). Final stress.

entries.name: Ami
entries.source: Hebrew עמי and Japanese あみ (a-mi) both have the 'ah' vowel, first-syllable stress in English

alternatives.context: some English-speaking bearers who use it as a spelling of Amy
Gujarati bearers (અમી, India, UK, US), whose inherent a is a schwa: UH-mee

entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today says the 'lot' vowel (OM-ee). US already right. Reviewer: the source no longer claims Gujarati says 'ah' (Gujarati અ is [ə]); Gujarati UH-mee added as an alternative.

entries.name: Shishir
entries.source: Hindi शिशिर, Bengali শিশির (śiśir, 'winter'): two short i's; first-syllable stress as Nitin and Bengali initial stress
entries.notes: Today's shi-SHUR uses the 'her' vowel; both vowels are i. The stress is unsourced.

entries.name: Ava
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Ava: /ˈeɪvə/

entries.name: Melanie
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Melanie: /ˈmɛləni/

entries.name: Youssouf
entries.region: Mali, Chad, Côte d'Ivoire, Comoros, France
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic يوسف: /juː.suf/; French ou is 'oo'
entries.notes: Today's YOO-sawf reads the second ou as 'aw'. Stress on the long first syllable as Arabic and the Youssef entry (n0006).

entries.name: Hamdi
entries.source: Turkish Hamdi (from Arabic حمدي ḥamdī): a is 'ah'; final stress as other Turkish names (Ahmet, Mehmet, Murat)
entries.notes: Today's HAM-dee uses the 'cat' vowel. Turkish bearers (wd TR 73) are the largest group; Arabic bearers stress the first syllable.

entries.name: Dora
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Dora: /ˈdɔːɹə/

alternatives.context: German, Hungarian, Croatian and Greek bearers: DOH-rah

entries.name: Cedric
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Cedric: /ˈsɛdɹɪk/
entries.notes: The FR register (133k) folds in the accented Cédric, which French writers use and which is its own entry. Without the accent the spelling is mostly English (US 41k, Cedric Diggory).

entries.name: Phoebe
entries.notes: Also the word 'phoebe' (a North American flycatcher). Name and word sound the same.

entries.name: Ezekiel
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Ezekiel: /ɪˈziːki.əl/

entries.name: Boniface
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Boniface: /ˈbɒnɪfeɪs/
entries.notes: English-speaking African bearers (Kenya, Nigeria, Uganda) and Saint Boniface use the English reading.

entries.name: Sandro
entries.source: Wiktionary, Italian Sandro: /ˈsan.dro/
entries.notes: US-only fix, as Hans and Andi: Italian, Brazilian and Swiss bearers say 'ah'. British already right.

entries.name: Marion
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Marion: /ˈmæɹ.i.ən/, US /ˈmɛɹ.i.ən/
entries.notes: Close call: English bearers (US 150k, UK, Ireland) are the largest single group against French (FR 126k) and German (wd DE 245). Also a surname and US place name.

entries.name: Marlene
entries.source: Wikipedia, Marlene (given name): English /mɑːrˈliːn/; German [maʁˈleːn(ə)]

alternatives.context: German and Austrian bearers (Marlene Dietrich): mar-LAY-nuh

entries.notes: Today stresses the first syllable (MAR-leen).

entries.name: Stephan
entries.source: Wiktionary, German Stephan: [ˈʃtɛfan]
entries.notes: Unlike Stefan (n0004, kept STEF-ahn because Polish, Swedish, Dutch and Balkan bearers write it that way), the ph spelling is mainly German: wd DE 769, CH 135, AT 97. German st- is 'sht'.

entries.name: Shaun
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Shaun: /ʃɔːn/

entries.name: Jürgen
entries.source: Wiktionary, German Jürgen: /ˈjʏrɡən/
entries.notes: German j is y (today's JUR-gun uses English j). Short ü has no English match: 'oo' per the guide.

entries.name: Benoît
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Benoît: /bə.nwa/
entries.notes: oî is 'wah' and the t is silent; today's buh-NOYT.

entries.name: Emeka
entries.source: Igbo Emeka (short for Chukwuemeka): e-me-ka, Igbo e is [e]; Igbo is tonal (high-high-low)
entries.notes: Today's eh-MAY-kuh matches the usual Nigerian English rendering, with the stress on the second syllable; no source gives an English stress.

entries.name: Shun
entries.source: Japanese しゅん (shun): [ɕɯɴ]; Mandarin 舜 Shùn [ʂwən]
entries.notes: Also the word 'shun', often capitalised at the start of a sentence. Japanese bearers (wd JP 84) say SHOON, not today's 'shun'; that reading is recorded here.

entries.name: Adamu
entries.source: Hausa Adamu (Adam): all 'ah' vowels; stress as the Adama entry (n0007)
entries.notes: Today's AD-uh-moo uses the 'cat' vowel. Hausa is tonal, so the English stress is unsourced; the vowels are the fix.

entries.name: Blaise
entries.source: English Blaise /bleɪz/ (US and UK bearers); Wiktionary, French Blaise: /blɛz/

alternatives.context: French bearers (Blaise Pascal, Blaise Matuidi): BLEZ

entries.notes: English-speaking bearers (US 9.3k, UK, Ireland, Canada) outnumber the French group (FR 3.5k).

entries.name: Tadeusz
entries.source: Wiktionary, Polish Tadeusz: /taˈdɛ.uʂ/
entries.notes: Today's TAD-ee-ooz is a spelling reading; sz is sh.

entries.name: Wanda
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Wanda: /ˈwɒndə/, US /ˈwɑndə/
entries.notes: US bearers (254k) are the largest group.

entries.name: Georgina
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Georgina: /dʒɔːˈdʒiːnə/

entries.name: Phyllis
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Phyllis: /ˈfɪlɪs/

entries.name: Luz
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Luz: /ˈlus/ (Latin America), /ˈluθ/ (Spain)
entries.notes: Today's LUZZ reads it as English. Latin American and US Hispanic bearers say LOOS.

entries.name: Glen
entries.notes: Also the word 'glen' (a valley). Name and word sound the same.

entries.name: Marjorie
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Marjorie: /ˈmɑːdʒəɹi/

entries.name: Jasmin
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Jasmin: /ˈd͡ʒæzmɪn/; German Jasmin [ˈjasmiːn]

alternatives.context: German, Austrian and Swiss bearers (YAHS-meen) and Bosnian men (Jasmin, YAHS-min)

entries.notes: usage english, so the English reading (guide, as Michele). Decision to review: anglo_share is 0.11 and Jasmin was a top-20 girls' name in Germany for years, so German-speaking plus Bosnian bearers may outnumber the English ones.

entries.name: Navin
entries.source: Hindi नवीन (navīn): /nə.ʋiːn/; stress on the long last syllable
entries.notes: Today differs only in the unstressed first vowel (as Naveen, n0004).

entries.name: Petar
entries.source: Wiktionary, Serbo-Croatian Petar: /pětar/ (first-syllable stress); Bulgarian Петър also stresses the first
entries.notes: Today's puh-TAR stresses the last syllable, which no bearer group does.

entries.name: Govinda
entries.source: Hindi गोविंद (govind, Sanskrit govinda): stress on the heavy closed syllable 'vin'
entries.notes: Today's guh-VIN-duh differs only in the unstressed first vowel.

entries.name: Dirk
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Dirk: UK /dɜːk/, US /dɝk/; Dutch /dɪrk/
entries.notes: Also the word 'dirk' (a dagger). English says the name like the word (Wiktionary UK /dɜːk/, US /dɝk/), which is today's reading; Dutch and German bearers' short [ɪ] before r has no closer English match, so nothing needs shipping. Reviewer: the earlier citation (Nowitzki /ˈdɜːrk/) was wrong; his article gives only German [ˈdɪʁk].

entries.name: Ion
entries.source: Wiktionary, Romanian Ion: /iˈon/
entries.notes: Also the common word 'ion' (EYE-un), today's reading. Romanian and Moldovan bearers say ee-OHN; that reading is recorded here.

entries.name: Tammy
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Tammy: /ˈtæmi/

entries.name: Dara
entries.source: Wikipedia, Dara Ó Briain: English /ˈdɑːrə/, /ˈdærə/; Irish [ˈd̪ˠaɾˠə]

alternatives.context: Irish-English variant (DAH-ruh), also given for Dara Ó Briain

entries.notes: Today's DARR-uh is one of the two English readings Wikipedia gives for the best-known Irish bearer.

entries.name: Bakary
entries.source: French spelling of the Mande form of Abu Bakr: a is 'ah'; French usage stresses the last syllable (as Aboubacar, n0007)
entries.notes: Today's BACK-uh-ree uses the 'cat' vowel. The bearers' own (tonal) languages give no English stress; final stress follows the French-spelling precedents.

entries.name: Murad
entries.source: Wiktionary, مراد: Urdu /mʊ.ɾɑːd̪/, Classical Persian /mu.ˈraːd/; as Murat (n0008)
entries.notes: Today's MYOOR-ad adds a y and stresses the short first syllable.

entries.name: Doreen
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Doreen: /dɔːˈɹiːn/

entries.name: Carole
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Carole: /ˈkæɹəl/; French Carole /ka.ʁɔl/

alternatives.context: French bearers (France 106k, Switzerland, Luxembourg, Belgium): ka-ROLL

entries.notes: Close call: English bearers (US 110k plus UK, Ireland, Australia) narrowly outnumber French ones (FR 106k plus Switzerland, Belgium, Luxembourg) on the registers. Worth a review.

entries.name: Ted
entries.notes: Also the word 'ted' (to spread hay) and TED talks. Name and word sound the same.

entries.name: Massimo
entries.source: Wiktionary, Italian Massimo: /ˈmas.si.mo/
entries.notes: Today's US MASS-i-moh uses the 'cat' vowel; British already has the continental short a and only loses the secondary stress on -mo.

entries.name: Petr
entries.source: Wiktionary, Czech Petr: /ˈpɛtr̩/
entries.notes: Today's PET-er is the nearest English rendering of the syllabic r. Russian Пётр is usually written Pyotr.

entries.name: Awa
entries.source: West African form of Eve (Hawa), French spelling: both a's are 'ah'
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today says the 'lot' vowel (OW-uh with o of 'hot'). US already right.

entries.name: Qamar
entries.notes: Arabic قمر is [ˈqa.mar] (KAH-mar, first-syllable stress); Urdu speakers say qəmər with two short schwas, and the Hindustani weight rule would stress the final closed syllable (kuh-MUR). Today's kuh-MAR mixes the two. Most bearers are Pakistani or British Pakistani, but no source gives their stress.

entries.name: Aslam
entries.source: Urdu اسلم (aslam), from Arabic أسلم /ʔas.lam/: s is voiceless; Urdu short a is 'uh'; the weight rule stresses the first heavy syllable
entries.notes: Today's AZ-lum voices the s and uses the 'cat' vowel.

entries.name: Prosper
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Prosper: /pʁɔs.pɛʁ/
entries.notes: Also the verb 'prosper', capitalised at the start of a sentence. French, Belgian and Congolese bearers say pross-PAIR; Ghanaian bearers say it like the word. Name reading recorded here.

entries.name: Dung
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese dung: Hà Nội [zuŋ˧˧], Saigon [juŋ˧˧]; as Dũng (n0009)
entries.notes: Also the English word 'dung'. Vietnamese d is z (north) or y (centre, south), never English d; the y reading follows Dũng. Name reading recorded here.

entries.name: Lloyd
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Lloyd: /lɔɪd/

entries.name: Dave
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Dave: /deɪv/

entries.name: Giang
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese giang: Hà Nội [zaːŋ˧˧], Huế and Saigon [jaːŋ˧˧]
entries.notes: One syllable; gi is y (south, as Dũng's d) or z (north). Today's jee-AHNG adds a syllable and an English j. Tone dropped.

entries.name: Thịnh
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese thịnh: Hà Nội [tʰïŋ˧˨ʔ], Huế [tʰɨn˨˩ʔ], Saigon [tʰɨn˨˩˨]
entries.notes: Vietnamese th is an aspirated t, not the 'th' of thin (today's THIN). -inh as in Linh and Minh. Tone dropped.

entries.name: Tâm
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese tâm: [təm˧˧] (all dialects)
entries.notes: â is a short schwa, the 'cup' vowel (as Sơn); today's TAM uses the 'cat' vowel. Tone dropped.

entries.name: Văn
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese văn: Hà Nội [van˧˧], Saigon [vaŋ˧˧]
entries.notes: ă is a short open 'ah', rendered as for Anh, Thanh and Lan; today's VAN uses the 'cat' vowel. Usually a men's middle name. Tone dropped.

entries.name: Lara
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Lara: /ˈlɑːɹə/; Italian, Spanish, German [ˈlaːra]
entries.notes: All main groups say LAH-ruh, as today.

entries.name: Aya
entries.region: France, Spain, Japan, Egypt, US, UK
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Aya /a.ja/, Turkish Aya; Arabic آية (āya), Japanese あや (a-ya)
entries.notes: Arabic-heritage (France, Spain, UK, US), Japanese (wd JP 119) and Egyptian bearers all say AH-yah; today's EYE-uh is the English reading.

entries.name: Eugenia
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Eugenia: /euˈxenja/; as Eugenio (n0008)
entries.notes: Spanish-speaking bearers (Spain 12.6k plus Argentina, Mexico, US Hispanic) are the largest single group; Spanish g [x] → h. Today's yoo-JEE-nee-uh is the English reading.

entries.name: Ashwin
entries.source: Hindi अश्विन (aśvin): schwa a, ś = sh; the weight rule stresses the first of two heavy syllables
entries.notes: Today's ASH-win uses the 'cat' vowel; Indian short a is 'uh' (as Akshay).

entries.name: Meiling
entries.source: Pinyin Měilíng (美玲): mei = 'may', ling = 'ling'; guide convention: primary stress on the last syllable, secondary on the first
entries.notes: Today's MY-ling reads ei as 'eye'. Tones dropped.

entries.name: Huda
entries.source: Arabic هدى (hudā): /hu.daː/, first-syllable stress

entries.name: Matías
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Matías: /maˈtias/
entries.notes: The accented spelling is Spanish. Today's MAH-shuz is garbled (t read as sh, a syllable lost).

entries.name: Viraj
entries.source: Hindi/Sanskrit विराज (virāj): short i, long ā; the superheavy last syllable takes the stress (as Vishal)
entries.notes: Today's VIR-uj stresses the short first syllable and reduces the long ā.

entries.name: Darko
entries.source: Wiktionary, Serbo-Croatian Darko: /dâːrko/

entries.name: Debra
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Debra: /ˈdɛbɹə/

entries.name: Claudine
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Claudine: /klo.din/
entries.notes: Today's klaw-DEEN has the right stressed syllable; only the unstressed first vowel differs (as Monique, n0008).

entries.name: Frederik
entries.source: Danish Frederik [ˈfʁeðˀəʁek]; English for King Frederik X /ˈfrɛdərɪk/
entries.notes: Danish bearers (the largest group) have a short e and a soft d that English renders FRED-er-ik, today's reading.

entries.name: Felicia
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Felicia: /fəˈlɪʃə/, /fəˈliːʃə/

entries.name: Helmut
entries.source: Wiktionary, German Helmut: /ˈhɛlmuːt/
entries.notes: Today's HEL-mut keeps the stressed syllable; only the unstressed vowel is reduced.

entries.name: Kabir
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi कबीर: /kə.biːɾ/; the long last syllable takes the stress
entries.notes: Today's KAB-ur stresses the short first syllable and loses the long ī.

entries.name: Karin
entries.source: Wiktionary, German Karin: /ˈkaːʁɪn/, /ˈkaːʁiːn/; Swedish and Norwegian also KAH-rin; English /ˈkærɪn/
entries.notes: Scandinavian (NO 10k, wd SE 596) and German-speaking bearers far outnumber the English group.

entries.name: Serena
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Serena: /səˈɹiːnə/; Italian /seˈrɛ.na/
entries.notes: usage english, so the English reading (guide, as Michele). Italian bearers may be the larger group (anglo_share 0.13); worth a review.

entries.name: Filippo
entries.source: Wiktionary, Italian Filippo: /fiˈlip.po/

entries.name: Poonam
entries.source: Hindi पूनम (pūnam): long ū, schwa a; first-syllable stress

entries.name: Shannon
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Shannon: /ˈʃænən/

entries.name: Kishore
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi किशोर: /kɪ.ʃoːɾ/; the long last syllable takes the stress
entries.notes: Today's KEE-shor lengthens the short i and stresses it.

entries.name: Subhash
entries.source: Hindi सुभाष (subhāṣ): short u, aspirated bh, long ā, retroflex ṣ = sh; the superheavy last syllable takes the stress
entries.notes: Today's SUB-hash reads bh as two sounds and stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Rene
entries.source: Wiktionary, English René/Rene: /ɹəˈneɪ/

alternatives.context: Spanish, Dutch and Estonian bearers who write it without the accent: REH-neh

entries.notes: US bearers (70k) are the largest group.

entries.name: Yvette
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Yvette: /i.vɛt/; English /ɪˈvɛt/

entries.name: Leonid
entries.source: Wiktionary, Russian Леонид: [lʲɪɐˈnʲit]; Ukrainian Леонід also stresses the last syllable
entries.notes: Today reads it as the meteor (a Leonid, LEE-uh-nid, Wiktionary English). Russian devoices the final d (t) but Ukrainian keeps it, as does English spelling, so d is kept.

entries.name: Saeid
entries.source: Wiktionary, Persian سعید: Iranian formal [sæ.ʔíːd̪̥]
entries.notes: Today's SAYD merges the two syllables; the glottal stop is dropped with the vowels kept apart (guide).

entries.name: Miloš
entries.source: Wiktionary, Serbo-Croatian Miloš: /mǐloʃ/; Czech [ˈmɪloʃ]; Slovak /ˈmiɫɔʃ/
entries.notes: Today's MY-lohz reads i as 'eye' and š as z.

entries.name: Domingos
entries.source: Wiktionary, Portuguese Domingos: Brazil /doˈmĩ.ɡus/, Portugal /duˈmĩ.ɡuʃ/
entries.notes: Today's duh-MING-gohz reads it like English Domingo. The nasal ĩ before g is 'eeng'.

entries.name: Tracy
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Tracy: /ˈtɹeɪsi/

entries.name: Maha
entries.source: Arabic مها (mahā): two short-then-long a's, first-syllable stress
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today says muh-HAH. US already right.

entries.name: Nellie
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Nellie: /ˈnɛli/

entries.name: Rogelio
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Rogelio: /roˈxeljo/
entries.notes: Spanish g before e is [x] → h; today's roh-GEE-lee-oh is a spelling reading.

entries.name: Josefina
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Josefina: /xoseˈfina/
entries.notes: Spanish j → h; today's yoh-si-FEE-nuh reads j as y. Spanish bearers (ES 37k plus Latin America) dominate.

entries.name: Luan
entries.source: Brazilian Portuguese Luan (Luan Santana) and Albanian Luan [luˈan]: two syllables, final stress on 'ahn'
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today says loo-ON with the 'lot' vowel. US already right.

entries.name: Mathieu
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Mathieu: /ma.tjø/
entries.notes: Today's MATH-yoo reads th as in 'thin' and stresses the first syllable. French ø has no English match: US 'oo', GB 'ur' as Dieudonné and Eugène (n0008).

entries.name: Haitham
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic هيثم: /haj.θam/

alternatives.context: Egyptian Arabic speakers, who say ay as 'ay' and th as s: HAY-sahm

entries.notes: Arabic ay is 'eye'; today's HAY-thum.

entries.name: Oswaldo
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Oswaldo: /osˈbaldo/ [ozˈβ̞al̪.d̪o]; Brazil /oˈzwaw.du/
entries.notes: Today's US 'ahs' and British 'oz-WOL-doh' have the wrong vowels. Wiktionary's Spanish w is a soft [β̞]; many Latin American speakers say w, the nearest English sound, so w is kept.

entries.name: Angelica

alternatives.context: Spanish Angélica (usually written with the accent): ahng-HAY-lee-kah

entries.notes: Also the plant 'angelica'. The English name and the word sound the same (usage english).

entries.name: Georgi
entries.source: Bulgarian Георги (Georgi): hard g, stress on o
entries.notes: Both g's are hard; today's jee-AR-jee uses English j.

entries.name: Ivo
entries.source: Wiktionary, Ivo: Italian /ˈi.vo/, Serbo-Croatian /ǐːʋo/, Czech [ˈɪvo], Portuguese /ˈi.vu/
entries.notes: Today's EYE-vee-oh adds a syllable. Continental bearers far outnumber the English group.

entries.name: Elina
entries.source: Swedish, Norwegian, Greek Ελίνα and Russian Элина stress the second syllable; Wiktionary Finnish /ˈelinɑ/

alternatives.context: Finnish and Estonian bearers (wd FI 289): EH-lee-nah

entries.notes: Finland is the largest single country group, but second-syllable stressers (Sweden, Norway, Greece, Russia, Ukraine, France, English) are more together.

entries.name: Alisha
entries.source: English Alisha: /əˈliːʃə/

entries.name: Asad
entries.notes: Arabic أسد is [ˈʔa.sad] (AH-sahd); Urdu speakers say əsəd with two schwas, and the weight rule would stress the final closed syllable (uh-SUD). Today's ASS-ud has the 'cat' vowel, wrong for both. Bearers are mostly Pakistani and British Pakistani; no source gives their stress.

entries.name: Bosco
entries.source: Wikipedia, John Bosco: Italian [ˈdɔm ˈbɔsko]
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today says BORE-skoh with the 'thought' vowel; the name (after Don Bosco) has the short o of 'boss'. US already right.

entries.name: Hauwa
entries.source: Hausa Hauwa (Eve): au is 'ow'

entries.name: Dante
entries.source: Wiktionary, Italian Dante: /ˈdan.te/; English US /ˈdɑnteɪ/, UK /ˈdænteɪ/

entries.name: Nico
entries.source: Wiktionary, Nico: Italian /ˈni.ko/, Dutch /ˈni.koː/

entries.name: Raphaël
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Raphaël: /ʁa.fa.ɛl/; same reading as the Raphael entry's name reading (n0006)
entries.notes: The diaeresis spelling is French only, so unlike Raphael (protected for the painter and archangel) it can carry the French reading. Today's RAF-ee-ul.

entries.name: Johnson
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Johnson: /ˈd͡ʒɒnsən/
entries.notes: Given name in Nigeria and Uganda; also the common surname. Same reading.

entries.name: Damien
entries.region: France, Belgium, Rwanda, Burundi, DR Congo
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Damien (fr-IPA): /da.mjɛ̃/; Forebears 2014: France 65.8k, DR Congo 20.6k, Rwanda 15.2k, Burundi 12.3k, Belgium 7.3k against US 20.4k, Australia 16.1k, England 10.6k, Ireland 6.7k

alternatives.context: English (US, Australia, Ireland, UK; Damien Hirst, Damien Lewis, The Omen); today's reading

entries.notes: Population call: French-speaking bearers outnumber English ones even without Africa (France+Belgium ~73k vs ~63k; registers FR 125.7k vs US 64k + IE 6.4k + CA 6.2k). French [a] is 'ah' (US) and British 'a' (Jeanne/Jacques precedent); the nasal ɛ̃ is English 'an' as in Chopin. Decision to review: this changes Damien Hirst, Damien Lewis, Damien Chazelle and The Omen in English text.

entries.name: Ruìlín
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 瑞 ruì [ʐu̯eɪ̯] and 麟 lín [lin]; guide convention for two-syllable Chinese given names (primary on the last syllable, secondary on the first)
entries.notes: Pinyin r → r (as Rong); -ui is one syllable 'way' with a w glide (as Hui). Today's ROO-lin drops the ei. Tones dropped.

entries.name: Jakob
entries.region: Germany, Denmark, Switzerland, Austria, Sweden, Slovenia
entries.source: Wiktionary, German Jakob: /ˈjaːkɔp/; Dutch /ˈjaː.kɔp/; Norwegian /ˈjɑː.kɔp/, /ˈjɑː.kup/

alternatives.context: English-speaking bearers (US 31.8k births), as English Jacob; today's reading

entries.notes: Forebears 2014: Germany 80.6k, Denmark 16.5k, Switzerland 14.6k, Sweden, Austria, Slovenia (all a y-initial 'YAH-kob') against US 3.0k. German j is 'y'; final b is devoiced to p. German short o: US ɔ, GB ɒ (Wolfgang precedent).

entries.name: Sahil
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi साहिल: /sɑː.ɦɪl/ [säː.ɦɪl]; the long first syllable takes the stress (weight rule)

alternatives.context: Azerbaijani Sahil (final stress); close to today's guess

entries.notes: Today's sah-HEEL stresses the short second vowel and lengthens it. Hindi ɦ → h.

entries.name: Domenico
entries.source: Wiktionary, Italian Domenico (it-pr Doménico): /doˈme.ni.ko/; today's dOmˈAnikO matches

entries.name: Driss
entries.source: Moroccan Arabic Driss, the short form of Idris (إدريس, Idrīs, long ī); French spelling i = [i]
entries.notes: Moroccan bearers (wd MA 78; FR and ES registers ~4.9k each, mostly Moroccan families). The vowel is the long 'ee' of Idrīs; today's DRISS has the KIT vowel.

entries.name: Wilfried
entries.source: German spelling rules: w = [v], ie = [iː], final d devoiced; Wiktionary French Wilfried /vil.fʁid/ also has v
entries.notes: anglo_share 0.0: German, Austrian and Belgian bearers. Every bearer group says v, not today's English w. Wiktionary's German section has no IPA.

entries.name: Andrei
entries.source: Wiktionary, Romanian Andrei: /anˈdrej/; Russian Андрей [ɐnˈdrʲej]
entries.notes: Romanian, Moldovan and Russian bearers stress the second syllable. Today's AN-dray has the 'cat' vowel, which no source gives. Unstressed a kept as 'ah' (as Andrés, n0003).

entries.name: Sherif
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic شريف (ar-pr شَرِيف, šarīf): long ī in the last syllable; Egyptian pronunciation [ʃeˈɾiːf]
entries.notes: Egyptian spelling of Sharif (wd EG 38). The long ī carries the stress; today's SHERR-if reads it as English 'sheriff'.

entries.name: Ila
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi इला: /ɪ.lɑː/ [ɪ.läː]; a short stressed vowel in an open syllable is lengthened in English, as for Shiva (/ˈʃiːvə/, n0010) and Uma (n0003)

alternatives.context: Hindi short i kept short (IL-uh), as Nidhi and Smita

entries.notes: Forebears 2014: India 96.2k against US 14.4k and Indonesia 12.5k. Today's EE-luh is the Shiva/Uma rendering of the Hindi short i and also how Hungarian (Wiktionary /ˈilɒ/) and Indonesian bearers say it. Earlier batches split on this (Nidhi and Smita kept the short vowel), so it is not churned.

entries.name: Omer
entries.source: Hebrew עומר Omer [ˈo.meʁ]; English word omer /ˈoʊmɚ/

alternatives.context: Turkish Ömer written without dots, Bosnian and Albanian Omer (final stress)

entries.notes: Also the word 'omer' (a Hebrew measure; the Counting of the Omer, usually capitalised). The Hebrew name (wd IL 66, the largest group) is said like the word and as today (OH-mer), so nothing needs to ship.

entries.name: Tristan
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Tristan: /ˈtɹɪstən/ (Collins); enPR trĭstən, trĭstän, trĭstăn (AHD, MW)
entries.notes: Today's TRIS-tan with a full second vowel is one of the listed English readings. English bearers (US 129.6k, GB, CA, IE, AU) outnumber French ones.

entries.name: Yousef
entries.source: Arabic يوسف (yūsuf), colloquial [ˈjuːsef]: the long ū takes the stress; as Youssef (n0006, high)

alternatives.context: Persian یوسف (Iranian bearers, wd IR 15): final stress

entries.notes: Today's YOO-sef matches the Arabic reading.

entries.name: Gilles
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Gilles (fr-IPA): /ʒil/
entries.notes: FR register 174.4k plus Belgium, Switzerland and Quebec. Today's GILZ reads it as English Giles.

entries.name: Ade
entries.source: Indonesian spelling rules (penultimate stress, e = [e]); Wiktionary lists Indonesian Ade as a male given name from Javanese; Forebears 2014: Indonesia 649.6k, Nigeria 35.7k

alternatives.context: Yoruba Adé (Nigeria): high tone on the second syllable
British nickname for Adrian (Ade Edmondson); today's reading

entries.notes: Indonesian bearers dominate. Today's AYD is the British nickname.

entries.name: Octavio
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Octavio (es-pr): /okˈtabjo/ [okˈt̪a.β̞jo]
entries.notes: Today's ok-TAY-vee-oh has the English 'ay' for the stressed a. Spanish [β] → v; closed o as in Gonzalo (n0007).

entries.name: Alvaro
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Álvaro (es-pr): /ˈalbaɾo/; the unaccented spelling is the same name (ES register 171.3k)
entries.notes: Same reading as Álvaro (n0005). Today's al-VAR-oh stresses the second syllable; Italian Alvaro [ˈalvaro] also stresses the first.

entries.name: Yassine
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic ياسين: /jaː.siːn/; the superheavy last syllable takes the stress; French spelling -ine = [in]
entries.notes: Maghrebi bearers (FR register 22.3k, ES 9.1k, CA). Today's yah-SEE-nee adds a final vowel.

entries.name: Florian
entries.source: Wiktionary, German Florian: /ˈfloːʁi̯aːn/; Forebears 2014: Germany 76.1k, Austria 16.4k, Switzerland 6.6k against France 34.9k, Romania 22.4k
entries.notes: German, Austrian and Swiss bearers are the largest group; Polish and English bearers share their first-syllable stress. The German long o is 'oh'; British today says FLAW-ree-un.

entries.name: Dilshad
entries.source: Wiktionary, Persian دلشاد (fa-IPA dilšād): stress on the long final ā; Urdu dilšād the same
entries.notes: Today's DIL-shud stresses the first syllable and reduces the long 'ah'.

entries.name: Cornelius
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Cornelius: GA /kɔɹˈniliəs/, RP /kɔːˈniːlɪəs/; today's kɔɹnˈiljəs differs only in the unstressed -ius
entries.notes: Forebears 2014: South Africa 41.5k (Afrikaans, same stressed syllable), US 24.7k, Kenya 18.1k, Nigeria 14.3k, Ghana 6.5k against Germany 4.8k. English is the largest reading.

entries.name: Lijun
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 麗 lì /li/ and 君 jūn /t͡ɕyn/; guide convention for two-syllable Chinese given names (primary on the last syllable, secondary on the first)
entries.notes: Pinyin jun is [tɕyn]: ü → 'oo' (as Jun, n0001). Today's LEE-jun has the 'cup' vowel and first-syllable stress. Tones dropped.

entries.name: Zhixiong
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 志 zhì [ʈ͡ʂʐ̩] and 雄 xióng [ɕi̯ʊŋ]; guide convention for two-syllable Chinese given names (primary on the last syllable, secondary on the first)
entries.notes: zhi as in Zhi (n0004) and Zhizhong (n0009); xiong as in Guoxiong (n0010). Today's ZHIK-see-ong reads x as ks.

entries.name: Blanca
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Blanca (es-pr): /ˈblanka/ [ˈblãŋ.ka]
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today says the 'lot' vowel (BLONK-uh). US today is right.

entries.name: Rogério
entries.source: Wiktionary, Portuguese Rogério (pt-IPA): Brazil /ʁoˈʒɛ.ɾju/, Portugal /ʁuˈʒɛ.ɾju/

alternatives.context: Brazilian 'strong r' as h (common in Brazil)

entries.notes: Brazilian bearers (wd BR 166) outnumber Portuguese (PT 38). g before e is zh; final -io is 'yoo'. Initial R → r per the guide (ʁ → ɹ). Today's guess roh-JEER-ee-oh reads g as j.

entries.name: Abdallah
entries.source: Arabic عبد الله ʿabd allāh; colloquial [ʕabˈdalla] with the stress on 'dal' (as Abdullah, n0001); Wiktionary French Abdallah (fr-IPA) /ab.da.la/

alternatives.context: careful Arabic, stress on the final llāh

entries.notes: Kept the Abdullah precedent's stress ('dal') but with the Arabic 'ah' vowel; today's ab-DAL-uh has the 'cat' vowel.

entries.name: Gene
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Gene: /ˈd͡ʒiːn/
entries.notes: Ordinary word 'gene'. The English name is said the same (JEEN), as today, so nothing needs to ship.

entries.name: Ijaz
entries.source: Wiktionary, Persian اعجاز: /ʔiʔ.ˈd͡ʒaːz/ (Urdu اعجاز iʿjāz the same word): stress on the long final ā
entries.notes: Pakistani bearers (wd PK 10; GB register 104). ʿayn dropped (guide). Today's IJ-uz stresses the first syllable and reduces the long 'ah'.

entries.name: Isidore
entries.region: DR Congo, Burundi, Cameroon, Benin, Rwanda, France, Belgium
entries.source: French Isidore /i.zi.dɔʁ/ (French spelling rules; Wiktionary has no French section); Forebears 2014: DR Congo 22.1k, Burundi 10.1k, Cameroon 9.2k, Benin 7.9k, Rwanda 6.0k against US 1.7k, Nigeria 1.5k

alternatives.context: English (St Isidore of Seville; US, Nigeria); today's reading

entries.notes: Francophone bearers dominate, and on the registers alone France (2.6k) still leads the US (1.2k). French names take final stress in English (guide). Decision to review: changes St Isidore in English text.

entries.name: Bojan
entries.source: Wiktionary, Serbo-Croatian Bojan: /bǒjan/ (rising accent on the first syllable)
entries.notes: j is 'y'; today's BOH-jun reads it as English j.

entries.name: Safdar
entries.source: Urdu صفدر safdar: both vowels short a [ə]; stress on the heavy first syllable (weight rule, as Ranjana); no dictionary entry
entries.notes: Urdu short a is 'uh' (as Ankit, Padma); today's SAF-dar uses the 'cat' vowel and a full second vowel.

entries.name: Shanta
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi शांता: /ʃɑːn.t̪ɑː/; Forebears 2014: India 202.2k, Bangladesh 89.8k, US 7.1k
entries.notes: The long ā is 'ah'; today's SHAN-tuh uses the 'cat' vowel. Bengali শান্তা has the same 'ah'.

entries.name: Trung
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese trung (vi-IPA): Saigon [ʈʊwŋ͡m˧˧], Hà Nội [t͡ɕʊwŋ͡m˧˧]
entries.notes: Southern and most overseas bearers have a retroflex t, heard as 'tr' (as Trang, n0012); -ung has the 'book' vowel (as -ong in Chinese names). Today's TRUNG rhymes with 'rung'. Tone dropped.

entries.name: Reynaldo
entries.region: Peru, Argentina, Cuba, Philippines, US Hispanic
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Reynaldo (es-pr): /reiˈnaldo/
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today says the 'lot' vowel (ray-NOL-doh). US today is right.

entries.name: Wenzhong
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 文 wén /wən/ and 忠 zhōng [ʈ͡ʂʊŋ]; guide convention for two-syllable Chinese given names (primary on the last syllable, secondary on the first)
entries.notes: -en is 'un' (as Wenbin); zhong as Zhong (n0008). Today's WEN-zhawng reads zh as two sounds.

entries.name: Guózhì
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 國 guó [ku̯ɔ] and 志 zhì [ʈ͡ʂʐ̩]; guide convention for two-syllable Chinese given names (primary on the last syllable, secondary on the first)
entries.notes: guo as in Guohua (n0004); zhi as in Zhi (n0004). Today's GWOH-zee reads zhi as 'zee'.

entries.name: Wénruì
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 文 wén /wən/ and 瑞 ruì [ʐu̯eɪ̯]; guide convention for two-syllable Chinese given names (primary on the last syllable, secondary on the first)
entries.notes: -en is 'un'; rui is one syllable 'rway' (as Hui 'hway'). Today's wen-ROO-ee splits rui in two.

entries.name: Krzysztof
entries.source: Wiktionary, Polish Krzysztof (pl-pr): /ˈkʂɘʂ.tɔf/
entries.notes: rz after k and sz are both 'sh'; Polish y [ɘ] is the KIT vowel. Today's KREES-tof reads it as English letters.

entries.name: Molly
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Molly: RP /ˈmɒ.li/, GA /ˈmɑ.li/
entries.notes: Also the word 'molly' (the fish; slang for MDMA). The name is said the same, as today, so nothing needs to ship.

entries.name: László
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hungarian László (hu-IPA): /ˈlaːsloː/
entries.notes: Hungarian sz is s and á is a long 'ah'; today's LAZ-loh reads sz as z with the 'cat' vowel.

entries.name: Ari
entries.source: Hebrew אֲרִי Ari and Finnish Ari [ˈɑri]: first-syllable stress with 'ah'; today's ˈɑɹi matches
entries.notes: US (26.9k), Israeli and Finnish bearers agree.

entries.name: Satya
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi सत्य: /sət̪.jᵊ/ [sɐt̪.jᵊ]
entries.notes: Hindi short a is 'uh' (as Ankit, Padma); today's SAHT-yuh has 'ah' (British 'lot').

entries.name: Chetan
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi चेतन: /t͡ʃeː.t̪ən/ [t͡ʃeː.t̪ɐ̃n]
entries.notes: The long e in an open syllable is 'ay' (guide table); today's CHET-un shortens it.

entries.name: Sonal
entries.source: Hindi/Gujarati सोनल sonal: long o stressed, final schwa; today's sˈOnəl matches

entries.name: Vaibhav
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi वैभव: /ʋɛː.bʱəʋ/; Marathi /ʋəi.bʱəʋ/; stress on the heavy first syllable
entries.notes: Hindi ai is [ɛː] (as Kailash, n0004); aspirated bh → b (guide). Today's VAYB-huv splits b and h.

entries.name: Hema
entries.source: Hindi हेमा hemā by Devanagari spelling: long e stressed (as Hema Malini, Hindi [ɦeːmaː])
entries.notes: Hindi long e is 'ay'; today's HEE-muh reads e as 'ee'.

entries.name: Rajeev
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi राजीव: /ɾɑː.d͡ʒiːʋ/; the superheavy last syllable takes the stress (weight rule)
entries.notes: Today's ruh-JEEV differs only in the unstressed first vowel.

entries.name: Pallavi
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi पल्लवी: /pəl.lə.ʋiː/; stress on the heavy closed first syllable (weight rule, as Vandana)
entries.notes: Hindi short a is 'uh'; today's pah-LAH-vee stresses the light middle syllable with 'ah'. Geminate ll is single (guide).

entries.name: Antara
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi अंतरा: /ən.t̪ə.ɾɑː/ (also /ən.t̪ɾɑː/); stress on the heavy closed first syllable (weight rule)
entries.notes: Today's ahn-TAR-uh stresses the light middle syllable.

entries.name: Anupama
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi अनुपमा: /ə.nʊp.mɑː/ (heavy 'nup' carries the stress, weight rule); South Indian and Bengali bearers keep the third vowel
entries.notes: Hindi drops the third vowel (uh-NOOP-muh); it is kept here as Malayalam, Telugu and Bengali bearers say it. Short u is the 'book' vowel (as Sushma). Today's ah-noo-PAH-muh stresses pa with 'ah'. Stress unsourced beyond the weight rule.

entries.name: Mitali
entries.source: Hindi मिताली / Bengali মিতালী mitālī: the long tā carries the stress (weight rule)
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today says the 'lot' vowel (mi-TOL-ee). US today is right.

entries.name: Himanshu
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi हिमांशु: /ɦɪ.mɑːn.ʃuː/; the heavy 'mān' takes the stress (weight rule)
entries.notes: Today's HY-mun-shoo reads hi as 'high' and stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Abhijit
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi अभिजित: /ə.bʱɪ.d͡ʒɪt̪/; closed final syllable stressed as Abhinav (n0010) and Abhishek (n0002)
entries.notes: Aspirated bh → b (guide); today's ub-HIJ-it splits b and h. Stress is weak in Hindi and unsourced.

entries.name: Sushant
entries.source: Wikipedia, Sushant Singh Rajput (note a): Hindi /suːˈʃɑːnt sɪŋ(h) ˈrɑːdʒpuːt/
entries.notes: Stress on the long final 'shahnt'; today's SUSH-unt stresses the first syllable and reduces the long 'ah'.

entries.name: Achyut
entries.source: Wiktionary, Sanskrit अच्युत: /ɐt͡ɕ.ju.t̪ɐ/ (Hindi drops the final a); stress on the heavy first syllable
entries.notes: c is ch (not today's k); short a is 'uh'. Today's AYK-yut misreads both.

entries.name: Umesh
entries.source: Wiktionary, Sanskrit उमेश: /u.meː.ɕɐ/; Hindi umeś, stress on the closed final syllable (as Mukesh, Ramesh)
entries.notes: Closed final eː → ɛ (guide table, as Mukesh n0008). Today's UM-ish stresses the wrong syllable.

entries.name: Rasika
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi रसिका: /ɾə.sɪ.kɑː/; first-syllable stress as for Kamala and Nalini (no heavy syllable before the last)
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today says the 'lot' vowel (ROSS-i-kuh). US today kept (Kamala precedent: 'ah' for the stressed short a). Stress is the Kavita/Sarita question: no source marks it.

entries.name: Geetanjali
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi गीतांजलि: /ɡiː.t̪ɑːn.d͡ʒliː/; the heavy 'tān' takes the stress (weight rule)
entries.notes: g is hard; today's jee-tahn-JAH-lee reads it as j and stresses 'ja'. The third vowel (dropped in Hindi) is kept, as in Tagore's Gitanjali.

entries.name: Bimal
entries.source: Bengali বিমল bimol [bimɔl] and Nepali बिमल [bimʌl]: i is a plain 'ee', initial stress; Wiktionary Hindi विमल: /ʋɪ.məl/
entries.notes: The b-spelling is the eastern (Bengali, Nepali, Odia) form of Vimal; Bengali and Nepali i has no short/long contrast and is said 'ee'. Today's BY-mul reads i as 'eye'.

entries.name: Jehangir
entries.source: Wiktionary, Persian جهانگیر: [d͡ʒæhɒŋˈɡʲiːɾ]; Wikipedia, Jahangir: [d͡ʒa.hɑːn.ˈɡiːɾ]; final stress
entries.notes: Indian/Parsi spelling of Jahangir. The long ā is 'ah' (today has the 'cat' vowel) and the long final ī takes the stress.

entries.name: Niladri
entries.source: Sanskrit नीलाद्रि nīlādri (nīla + adri): long ā in 'lād' takes the stress (weight rule)
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today says the 'lot' vowel (nee-LOD-ree). US kept. Bengali bearers stress the first syllable lightly; unsourced.

entries.name: Pranab
entries.source: Wikipedia, Pranab Mukherjee: Bengali [pɾɔnob]
entries.notes: The spelling with b is the Bengali form; Bengali inherent a is [ɔ] and the final o [o]. Today's PRAH-nub fits neither. Initial stress (Bengali).

entries.name: Ramarao
entries.source: Telugu రామారావు Rāmārāvu (Rama + Rao); Dravidian initial stress; Rao is English 'row' (Wikipedia, Rao: /raʊ/)
entries.notes: A compound of Rama and the title Rao; today's rah-MAR-ow stresses the middle. Stress unsourced beyond the Telugu initial-stress rule.

entries.name: Shailesh
entries.source: Hindi शैलेश śaileś by Devanagari spelling: ai [ɛː] (as Kailash, n0004); the superheavy last syllable takes the stress (as Hemant, Kailash)
entries.notes: Today's SHAYL-esh stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Shakuntala
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi शकुंतला: /ʃə.kʊn.t̪lɑː/; the heavy 'kun' takes the stress (weight rule)
entries.notes: Short u is the 'book' vowel; today's shah-kun-TAH-luh stresses the light 'ta'. The fourth vowel (dropped in Hindi) is kept, as in the play's English name.

entries.name: Shripad
entries.source: Marathi श्रीपाद śrīpād by Devanagari spelling: long ī and ā; the superheavy last syllable takes the stress (as Pradeep, Hemant)
entries.notes: Today's SHRY-pad reads ī as 'eye' and ā as the 'cat' vowel.

entries.name: Sucheta
entries.source: Hindi सुचेता sucetā by Devanagari spelling: c = ch, long e stressed (the heavy non-final syllable, weight rule); Wikipedia, Sucheta Kriplani: Bengali [ʃut͡ʃeta]
entries.notes: Today's soo-KAY-tuh reads ch as k, which no bearer says.

entries.name: Kemal
entries.source: Wiktionary, Turkish Kemal: [cʰeˈmal̥ʲ]; Wikipedia, Mustafa Kemal Atatürk: Turkish [kɛˈmal]
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today says the 'lot' vowel (kuh-MOL). US today is right (only the unstressed first vowel differs).

entries.name: Zi
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 子 zǐ [t͡sz̩]; z as dz and the apical vowel as 'uh' (as Zihao, n0006)
entries.notes: Pinyin z is unaspirated [ts] → dz; zi is not 'zee'. Register births (GB 497, CA 455) are mostly Chinese families.

entries.name: Zoya
entries.source: Wiktionary, Russian Зоя: [ˈzojə]; Ukrainian [ˈzɔjɐ]; Urdu/Persian زویا Zoya the same shape
entries.notes: Today's zˈYə (ZOY-uh) is the same sequence of sounds as [zo.jə].

entries.name: Marianne
entries.region: Germany, Switzerland, Austria, Netherlands, Denmark, Norway
entries.source: Wiktionary, German Marianne: [maˈʁi̯anə]; Forebears 2014: Germany 450.3k, Switzerland 51.3k, Austria 38.0k, Netherlands 51.3k, Denmark 36.1k against US 106.2k, Canada 11.0k, England 10.9k

alternatives.context: English (US, Canada, UK, Philippines; Marianne Faithfull, Marianne Williamson); today's reading
French (France, Belgium; also France's national symbol)

entries.notes: German-speaking bearers alone (~540k) are about 3.5 times the English ones (~150k); Dutch and Scandinavian bearers also stress 'AH-n'. German short a: US 'ah', GB 'a' (Manfred precedent). Decision to review: this changes Marianne Faithfull, Marianne Williamson and France's Marianne in English text.

entries.name: Cornelis
entries.source: Wiktionary, Dutch Cornelis: /ˌkɔrˈneː.lɪs/ [ˌkɔrˈnei̯.lɪs]
entries.notes: Dutch long e is 'ay'; today's kur-NEL-is shortens it.

entries.name: Samba
entries.source: Wolof/Fula Samba (a traditional second-son name) with the 'ah' vowel; Forebears 2014: Senegal 129.0k, Mali 43.2k, Guinea-Bissau 32.8k
entries.notes: Also the word 'samba' (the dance, English SAM-buh) and the tech-list term (Samba, the file-sharing software, read SAM-buh today). Capitalised 'Samba' in English text is mostly those, so the name reading should not replace them; it is recorded in us/gb.

entries.name: Bambang
entries.source: Indonesian spelling rules (penultimate stress, a = [a]); Wiktionary lists Indonesian Bambang as a male given name from Javanese ꦧꦩ꧀ꦧꦁ

entries.name: Yifeng

entries.name: Madison
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Madison: /ˈmædɪsən/

entries.name: Larissa
entries.source: Wiktionary, Portuguese Larissa (pt-IPA): Brazil /laˈɾi.sɐ/; Forebears 2014: Brazil 340.5k, Madagascar 22.7k, US 16.3k, Germany 13.0k
entries.notes: Brazilian bearers outnumber all others several times over; Madagascar (French) and Russian Larisa also say 'REE'. Decision to review: also changes the Greek city Larissa in English text (English /ləˈrɪsə/).

entries.source: Wiktionary, Persian زهره: Iranian [zoɦ.ɹé] (final stress)
entries.notes: Persian final stress; final open e → 'ay' (guide table). Today's ZOR-eh drops the h and stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Tiago

alternatives.context: Spanish and English speakers (tee-AH-goh); today's US reading

entries.name: Sherry

entries.notes: Ordinary word 'sherry'. The name is said the same, as today, so nothing needs to ship.

entries.notes: The tech list (Kali Linux) reads it kˈɑli too, so the name and the term agree.

entries.source: Wiktionary, French Edouard (alternative spelling of Édouard, fr-IPA): /e.dwaʁ/
entries.notes: FR register 48.2k and Quebec (CA 9.4k). Today's ED-oo-ard reads it as English letters. French names take final stress in English (guide).

entries.name: Koffi
entries.source: Wiktionary, Akan Kofi: [kòfí]; Forebears 2014: Ivory Coast 434.8k, Togo 192.3k
entries.notes: French spelling of the Akan day name Kofi, used by Baoulé (Ivory Coast) and Ewe (Togo) bearers. Akan Kofi has [o] (KOH-fee, as Kofi Annan), but I found no source for the vowel Ivorian and Togolese bearers use, and the French spelling ff suggests open [ɔ] (today's KAW-fee). Candidate in us/gb.

entries.name: Fan
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 凡 fán /fan/ (as Fán, n0005); English Fan (Chinese place names): enPR fän
entries.notes: Ordinary word 'fan'. The Chinese name is FAHN; protected so the word keeps its reading.

entries.name: Yuxiang

entries.notes: yu as Yu (n0001); xiang as Xiang (n0003). Today's YUK-see-ang reads x as ks.

entries.name: Anis
entries.source: Arabic أنيس anīs: the long ī in the last syllable takes the stress
entries.notes: Collision triage: the word 'anis' (anise liqueur) is rare in English, and the name is what readers meet (FR register 10.8k, TN, MA), so it is treated as a name. GB-only fix: British today says AH-neez; US today is right.
entries.word_check: gold has 'anis' read ɑnˈis, the same as the name: kept

entries.name: Simeon

alternatives.context: Bulgarian Симеон, Greek, Romanian, Filipino and Spanish-speaking bearers (see-meh-ON)

entries.notes: Close population call: English-speaking bearers (mostly anglophone Africa) ~110k against final-stress readings ~90k (Philippines 18.9k, Bulgaria 16.8k, DR Congo 15.5k, Peru 9.8k, Cameroon, Rwanda, Burundi, Mexico). Without Africa the final-stress group would lead. Also the biblical Simeon in English text.

entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 宏 hóng /xʊŋ/ and 傑 jié /t͡ɕi̯ɛ/; guide convention for two-syllable Chinese given names (primary on the last syllable, secondary on the first)
entries.notes: hong as Hóng (n0004); jie as Jie (n0002). Today's HONG-jee drops the e.

entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 傑/杰 jié: /t͡ɕi̯ɛ³⁵/ (as Jie, n0002)
entries.notes: Today's JEE drops the e of -ie.

entries.name: Qingling
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 慶 qìng [t͡ɕʰiŋ] and 齡 líng [liŋ]; Soong Ching-ling (Song Qingling); guide convention for two-syllable Chinese given names (primary on the last syllable, secondary on the first)

entries.name: Yùtíng
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 玉 yù /y/ and 婷 tíng /tʰiŋ/; guide convention for two-syllable Chinese given names (primary on the last syllable, secondary on the first)
entries.notes: Today's YOO-ting stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Babatunde
entries.source: Yoruba Babátúndé ('father has returned'); English renderings stress 'tun' (Babatunde Olatunji, Babatunde Fashola)
entries.notes: Yoruba is tonal; English speakers put the stress on 'toon'. Today's guess BAB-uh-tund drops the final vowel and uses the 'cat' vowel.

entries.name: Gheorghe
entries.source: Wikipedia, Gheorghe Hagi: Romanian [ˈɡe̯orɡe ˈhad͡ʒʲ]
entries.notes: gh is hard g; eo is one syllable 'yo'; final e is a full vowel (guide: final unstressed -e → A). Today's GEE-org has three wrong sounds and drops the final vowel.

entries.name: Rosanna
entries.source: Italian spelling rules: stress on the penultimate, a = [a], intervocalic s = [z] in standard Italian; Forebears 2014: Italy 136.1k, Philippines 22.2k, US 19.1k, Dominican Republic 13.4k

alternatives.context: English (US, UK; Rosanna Arquette); today's reading

entries.notes: Italian bearers far outnumber English ones; Spanish bearers share the 'ah'. Geminate nn is single (guide).

entries.name: Néstor
entries.source: Spanish spelling rules: the written accent marks first-syllable stress, /ˈnestoɾ/; today's nˈɛstəɹ differs only in the unstressed vowel

entries.name: Selina

entries.source: English Selina /səˈliːnə/ (as Selena); Forebears 2014: Tanzania 56.7k, South Africa 25.4k, Ghana 23.5k, Kenya 18.3k, US 14.6k, Uganda, Zimbabwe

alternatives.context: Bengali সেলিনা (Bangladesh 111.3k): sh and initial stress

entries.notes: English and Swahili bearers (stress on 'lee') outnumber Bangladesh, the largest single non-English group.

entries.name: Gauri
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi गौरी: /ɡɔː.ɾiː/; today's ɡˈɔɹi matches (Hindi au [ɔː], as Gaurav, n0004)

entries.name: Jia
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Jia: enPR jyä; Mandarin 佳 jiā /t͡ɕi̯ä/ (as Jiā, n0005); Forebears 2014: Malaysia 17.0k, US 6.2k, China 3.0k, Taiwan 2.7k, Macau 1.8k against India 6.4k, Pakistan 2.8k
entries.notes: Chinese bearers (Malaysia, China, Taiwan, Macau, Singapore) outnumber South Asian ones (Hindi जिया jiyā, JEE-uh, today's reading). jia is one syllable.

entries.source: Wiktionary, English Eleanor: GA /ˈɛləˌnoɹ/, /ˈɛlənɚ/; UK /ˈɛlənə/

entries.notes: Ordinary word 'precious'. The name is said the same, as today, so nothing needs to ship.

entries.source: Wiktionary, English Isaiah: US/Canada /aɪˈzeɪ.ə/, UK /aɪˈzaɪ.ə/; today's US IzˈAə and GB IzˈIə match

entries.name: Carina
entries.source: Wiktionary, Norwegian Bokmål Carina: /kaˈriː.na/; Swedish and German Carina the same; today's kəɹˈinə differs only in the unstressed first vowel
entries.notes: Collision triage: 'carina' (a keel-shaped structure; the constellation) is rare and technical, while the name is common, so it is treated as a name.

entries.source: Wiktionary, English Erin: /ˈɛɹɪn/

entries.name: Hiroyuki
entries.source: Japanese ひろゆき Hiroyuki; penultimate stress in English (guide, as Haruki); today's hˌɪɹOjˈuki matches
entries.notes: The secondary-stressed first vowel (ɪ before r) is close enough to 'ee'.

entries.name: Petrus
entries.source: Wiktionary, Indonesian Petrus (id-pr Pètrus): [ˈpɛt̪̚.rʊs]; Classical Latin [ˈpɛ.trʊs]; Forebears 2014: South Africa 119.7k, Indonesia 93.8k, Namibia 27.9k
entries.notes: Today's PET-rus matches Indonesian and Latin. The Afrikaans bearers (South Africa, Namibia; the largest group) have no IPA source; Afrikaans open-syllable e is usually [iə] (PEER-trus), which would need a source before changing anything.

entries.name: Daud
entries.region: Tanzania, Indonesia, Somalia, Pakistan, India, Kenya
entries.source: Swahili and Indonesian/Malay penultimate stress (Wiktionary Malay Daud: ms-IPA daod); Arabic داود /daː.wud/; Forebears 2014: Tanzania 64.5k, Indonesia 44.8k, Somalia 43.2k, Pakistan 35.9k, India 31.2k, Kenya 22.9k

alternatives.context: Urdu, Pashto and Arabic-influenced bearers (Pakistan, India, Afghanistan): final stress

entries.notes: Today's DAWD makes it one syllable, which no bearer says. The hiatus a-u is bridged with the w glide Malay/Indonesian speakers insert (and Arabic dāwūd has), so the voice keeps two syllables (dˈɑud came out as one in the audio check). Swahili and Malay/Indonesian bearers (~140k) slightly outnumber the final-stress Urdu/Somali groups (~110k); stress weak and unsourced.

entries.notes: gh [ɣ] → g (guide); today's guh-FOOR keeps the stressed long 'oo' before r.

entries.notes: Today's MING-zhee reads zh as the 'measure' sound and e as 'ee'.

entries.name: Liliane
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Liliane (fr-IPA): /li.ljan/
entries.notes: FR register 108.3k. French [a]: US 'ah', GB 'a' (Jeanne precedent); -iane is one syllable 'lyahn'. Today's li-lee-AN has the 'cat' vowel and an extra syllable.

entries.notes: Today's YOH-yoh matches.

entries.notes: Only the unstressed first vowel differs.

entries.notes: Hausa Abdu, Wolof and Arabic ʿAbduh all stress the first syllable, with 'ah'. Today's ab-DOO follows French phrase-final stress.

entries.name: Zhiwen

entries.name: Qiuxia

entries.notes: Today's guess says only a bare k. Tone mark dropped.

entries.name: Shuāng
entries.source: Pinyin shuāng [ʂwɑ́ŋ]: sh [ʂ] → ʃ (guide table); one syllable; same reading as Shuang (n0002)
entries.notes: Today's ʃˈuŋ drops the a.

entries.name: Sījìng
entries.source: Pinyin sī [sɹ̩́] + jìng [tɕîŋ]: the apical vowel of si → 'suh' (Si, Siyuan precedents, n0006); j [tɕ] → ʤ
entries.notes: Today's SY-jing reads si as 'sigh'. Tones dropped; with no English source for this given name, primary stress on the last syllable and secondary on the first (the guide's Chinese convention).

entries.name: Wénlín
entries.source: Pinyin wén [wə̌n] + lín [lǐn]: -en is [ən] ('wun'), as Wenbin (n0002)
entries.notes: Today's WEN-lin has the DRESS vowel and first-syllable stress. Tones dropped; with no English source for this given name, primary stress on the last syllable and secondary on the first (the guide's Chinese convention).

entries.name: Wēiwēi
entries.source: Pinyin wēi [wéɪ] twice; -ei is English 'ay' (Wei, Wēi precedents, n0001-n0002); Wikipedia, Ai Weiwei: English /ˈaɪ weɪˈweɪ/ (EYE way-WAY), final stress on the romanised Weiwei
entries.notes: Today's WY-way reads the first ei as 'eye'. Tones dropped; primary stress on the last syllable and secondary on the first, as Wikipedia's English IPA for Ai Weiwei (way-WAY).

entries.name: Wěiwěi
entries.source: Pinyin wěi [wěɪ] twice (the first becomes wéi by third-tone sandhi); -ei is English 'ay'; Wikipedia, Ai Weiwei: English /ˈaɪ weɪˈweɪ/ (EYE way-WAY), final stress on the romanised Weiwei
entries.notes: Today's WY-way reads the first ei as 'eye'. Tones dropped; primary stress on the last syllable and secondary on the first, as Wikipedia's English IPA for Ai Weiwei (way-WAY).

entries.name: Xiǎowén
entries.source: Pinyin xiǎo [ɕjɑ̀ʊ] + wén [wə̌n]: x [ɕ] → ʃ (guide table), -iao 'yow', -en 'un' (Xiaoyan, Wenbin precedents)
entries.notes: Today's ZHOW-un reads x as zh and drops the w. Tones dropped; with no English source for this given name, primary stress on the last syllable and secondary on the first (the guide's Chinese convention).

entries.name: Yè
entries.source: Pinyin yè [jɛ̂]: the Ye entry's name reading (n0005)
entries.notes: Today's YEE is the archaic word 'ye'. The grave-accent spelling is only the Chinese name, so it can ship (the unaccented Ye is a protect-word). Also the very common surname 叶/葉 Yè.

entries.name: Yě
entries.source: Pinyin yě [jɛ̀]: the Ye entry's name reading (n0005)
entries.notes: Today's YEE is the archaic word 'ye'. The caron spelling is only the Chinese name, so it can ship.

entries.name: Zǐmíng
entries.source: Pinyin zǐ [tsɹ̩̀] + míng [mǐŋ]: unaspirated z [ts] → dz and the apical vowel → 'uh', as Zǐ and Zihao (n0006, n0012)
entries.notes: Today's ZY-ming reads zi as 'zye'. Tones dropped; with no English source for this given name, primary stress on the last syllable and secondary on the first (the guide's Chinese convention).

entries.name: Patricio
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Patricio: /paˈtɾisjo/ (Latin America), /paˈtɾiθjo/ (Spain)
entries.notes: Today's puh-TRISS-ee-oh has the short 'bit' vowel in the stressed syllable; Spanish i is 'ee' (as Mauricio). Bearers: Spain (ES 5k), Chile, Argentina, Ecuador, US Hispanic (US 4k).

entries.name: Mourad
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Mourad: /mu.ʁad/; Arabic مراد murād [muˈraːd] stresses the long final syllable
entries.notes: French-orthography spelling of Murad (ou = 'oo'), used by Maghrebi bearers (FR 8.3k, ES 3.8k, Tunisia, Algeria, Morocco). Today's MOO-rad stresses the first syllable with the 'cat' vowel.

entries.name: Reem
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic ريم (rīm): /riːm/
entries.notes: Today's ɹˈim matches.

entries.name: Fathi
entries.source: Arabic فتحي fatḥī: t + ḥ, not English th; Arabic stress falls on the heavy first syllable (fat-) since final -ī is not superheavy; ḥ → h (guide table)

alternatives.context: French-speaking Maghrebi bearers (FR 1k) often drop the h: fah-TEE

entries.notes: Today's FATH-ee reads th as in 'path'. Bearers: Egypt, Tunisia, Palestine, France.

entries.name: Ba
entries.notes: Ordinary word 'ba' (the Egyptian soul; also 'baa'). The name (Vietnamese Ba, Chinese 巴 Bā, Korean 바, Fula Bâ) is said BAH, the same as today's bˈɑ, so nothing needs to ship.

entries.name: Flora
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Flora: /ˈflɔːɹə/; Spanish /ˈfloɾa/, Italian /ˈflɔ.ra/
