entries.notes: Also the word 'flora' (plant life; 'Flora and fauna' at a sentence start). The name's readings (English FLOR-uh, French, Spanish and Italian FLOH-rah) all match today's flˈɔɹə closely, so nothing needs to ship.

entries.name: Fidel
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Fidel: /fiˈdel/; English /fɪˈdɛl/
entries.notes: Today's fɪdˈɛl differs only in the unstressed first vowel.

entries.name: Spencer
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Spencer: /ˈspɛnsɚ/, /ˈspɛnsə/
entries.notes: Also the word 'spencer' (a short jacket) and the common surname. Name and word read the same today, so nothing needs to ship.

entries.name: Lucie
entries.drop_detail: St. Lucie (the Florida city, county and river) is LOO-see, as English bearers say it (Lucie Arnaz); the French loo-SEE would change the place (Tests/g2p/regression.json pins Port St. Lucie)
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Lucie: /ly.si/; French names take final stress in English

alternatives.context: English-speaking bearers (US 6k, England and Wales 6k): LOO-see

entries.notes: French bearers (FR 155k births, Belgium, Switzerland, Quebec) are the largest group; French ü [y] becomes 'oo' (guide table). Today's LOO-see is the English reading.

entries.name: Alma
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Alma: /ˈalma/ (also Finnish /ˈɑlmɑ/, Dutch /ˈɑl.maː/); Dictionary.com gives English /ˈæl mə/ beside /alˈmɑ/
entries.notes: US-only fix, as for Hans and Andi: Forebears (2014) counts Mexico 437k, the Philippines 187k, Guatemala, Honduras, El Salvador and Spain, plus Sweden, Norway and Germany, all with 'ah', far more than the English AL-muh group (part of the US 152k). The British front a is already close to [a], so GB stays.

entries.name: Alexandru
entries.source: Wiktionary, Romanian Alexandru: /a.lekˈsan.dru/
entries.notes: Today's al-ig-ZAN-droo uses the English 'cat' vowel and gz; Romanian has ks and 'ah'. Bearers: Romania (wd RO 840), Moldova.

entries.name: Aurelio
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Aurelio: /auˈɾeljo/ (Italian /awˈrɛ.ljo/)

alternatives.context: Italian bearers: ow-REH-lyoh, with an open e

entries.notes: Spanish bearers (ES 12k, Mexico, Peru, US Hispanic 7.7k) outnumber Italian ones; open-syllable e is 'ay' (guide table), as today's WɹˈAliO. Only the unstressed -io split differs.

entries.name: Ayu
entries.source: Wiktionary, Malay ayu: /aju/; Indonesian two-syllable words stress the first syllable (Wiktionary gives Indonesian Arya /ˈarja/, Halim /ˈhalim/); Japanese あゆ Ayu is also [a.jɯ]
entries.notes: Indonesian (wd ID 20) name, Javanese 'beautiful'. Today's EYE-yoo reads the a as the English 'eye' diphthong.

entries.name: Christiane
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Christiane: /kʁis.tjan/; Forebears (2014): France 305k, Germany 224k, Belgium 47k

alternatives.context: German and Austrian bearers (Forebears: Germany 224k): kris-tee-AH-nuh

entries.notes: French-speaking bearers (France, Belgium, Switzerland, Madagascar, Benin, DR Congo, Cameroon) outnumber German ones. US today already has the stressed 'ahn' (kris-tee-AHN); the British reading has the 'lot' vowel (kɹɪstiˈɒn), the guide's GB-only fix. Christophe precedent (n0007) for the krees- vowel.

entries.name: Nestor
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Nestor: /ˈnɛstɚ/, /ˈnɛstə/; Spanish Néstor [ˈnestoɾ]
entries.notes: English, Spanish, Portuguese and Filipino bearers all stress NES-; Spanish's full final o differs from today's nˈɛstəɹ only in the unstressed vowel.

entries.name: István
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hungarian István: [ˈiʃtvaːn]
entries.notes: Hungarian s is sh and á is a long 'ah'; today's IST-vun reads the English spelling. Initial stress as in all Hungarian words.

entries.name: Amita
entries.source: Hindi अमिता (amitā): short a, short i, long final ā; no dictionary or Wiktionary entry marks the stress

alternatives.context: Hindustani weight rule (stress on the only heavy syllable, the long final ā): uh-mi-TAA

entries.notes: Same shape as Kavita (n0005, unresolved): today's ah-MEE-tuh lengthens the short i, but no source marks the stress. Candidate follows English renderings that stress -mi-; the weight rule points to the last syllable. Needs a stress source before shipping.

entries.name: Arya
entries.source: Wiktionary, Indonesian Arya: /ˈarja/; English Arya (Arya Stark) is AR-yuh / AR-ee-uh; Hindi आर्या āryā
entries.notes: Every group stresses the first syllable with 'ah' + r; today's ˈɑɹiə only splits the unstressed y glide into a syllable.

entries.name: Josiah
entries.source: Dictionary.com, Josiah: /dʒoʊˈsaɪ ə/ (Collins /dʒəʊˈsaɪə/); Wiktionary also gives /d͡ʒoʊˈzaɪə/

entries.name: Bijay
entries.source: Eastern spelling of Vijay (Sanskrit विजय vijaya): short i, final -ay; follows the Vijay precedent (n0001), vɪʤˈA
entries.notes: Today's BY-jay reads the short i as 'eye'. The b spelling marks Nepali, Odia and Bengali bearers.

entries.name: Debashish
entries.source: Bengali দেবাশিস / দেবাশীষ (debashish): e, a, i; Bengali stresses the first syllable (Wikipedia, Bengali phonology); same reading as Debasish (n0013)
entries.notes: Today's DEB-uh-shish uses the 'bed' vowel for Bengali open-syllable [e] and reduces the long ā. Reviewer: changed from already-correct to match Debasish (n0013), the same name in another romanisation. The stress is the weak Bengali initial stress; no English source gives one for this name.

entries.name: Damian
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Damian: /ˈdeɪmɪən/ (Polish /ˈda.mjan/); Forebears (2014): Poland 143k, US 31k, Mexico 28k, England 18k, Nigeria 16k, Australia 13k

alternatives.context: Spanish Damián and Romanian bearers: dah-MYAHN

entries.notes: Today's dˈAmiən matches the English reading. Reviewer: changed back from Polish DAHM-yahn. The row is usage english (anglo_share 0.27), and the guide keeps English for those rows (as Michele, and Jasmin and Serena in n0013), even though Polish bearers (about 143k) are the largest single group. English text means Damian Lewis, Damian Marley and Damian Lillard.

entries.name: Halil
entries.source: Turkish Halil: regular Turkish orthography with final stress (Wiktionary's Turkish entry has no IPA); Arabic خليل ḫalīl also stresses -līl
entries.notes: Today's HAL-ul stresses the first syllable and loses the long 'ee'. Turkish unstressed a written as in Ahmet (n0004). Bearers: Turkey (wd TR 273), Albania, Kurdish and German-Turkish communities.

entries.name: Faiz
entries.source: Wikipedia, Faiz Ahmad Faiz: Urdu [fɛːz ɛɦməd̪ fɛːz]
entries.notes: Pakistani and British-Pakistani bearers (wd PK, GB-EAW 401) say Urdu فیض [fɛːz]; today's FAYZ is the usual English rendering of that long open e.

entries.name: Flavio
entries.source: Wiktionary, Italian Flavio: /ˈfla.vjo/ (Spanish /ˈflabjo/)
entries.notes: GB-only fix, as Fabio (n0006): British today says FLOV-ee-oh with the 'lot' vowel. US already right.

entries.name: Bella
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Bella: /ˈbɛlə/ (Hungarian and Italian also BEL-)

entries.name: Bijan
entries.source: Wiktionary, Persian بیژن (bižan): Iran formal [biː.ʒǽn]
entries.notes: The j is the French-style spelling of zh [ʒ] (as in Bijan, Jaleh). Matches n0015. Today's CMUdict BIJ-un reads j as English j.

entries.name: Noël
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Noël: /nɔ.ɛl/
entries.notes: Today's nOˈɛl matches.

entries.name: Kofi
entries.source: Wiktionary, Akan Kofi: [kòfí]; the established English reading (Kofi Annan) is KOH-fee
entries.notes: Akan tones dropped; today's kˈOfi is the English rendering used for Ghanaian bearers.

entries.name: Kate
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Kate: /keɪt/

entries.name: Prisca
entries.source: Latin and Italian Prisca: first-syllable stress with 'ee' (Latin Prīsca); no dictionary entry for the name

alternatives.context: French-speaking bearers (FR 4.4k, Switzerland, DR Congo): final stress in English, prees-KAH

entries.notes: Readings are close: today's PREES-kuh matches the Italian, Latin and East African (Uganda) bearers; French usage would put the stress last.

entries.name: Nasir
entries.region: Pakistan, India, Bangladesh, Saudi Arabia, Nigeria
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic ناصر (nāṣir, given name 'Nasir', 'Nasser'): /naː.sˤir/; Urdu /nɑː.sɪɾ/; stress on the long first syllable; Forebears (2014): Pakistan 513k, India 182k, Bangladesh 120k, Saudi Arabia 73k, Indonesia 70k, Nigeria 61k

alternatives.context: US bearers after Nas (Nasir Jones; Wikipedia /nɑːˈsɪər/), and the separate name نصير naṣīr: nah-SEER

entries.notes: Today's nuh-SEER stresses the short second syllable. Reviewer: changed from already-correct. The spelling's bearers are overwhelmingly South Asian, Arab, Indonesian and Nigerian (anglo_share 0.03), and they carry ناصر nāṣir, NAH-sir (as Aamir, n0006). Nas's nah-SEER is the US reading. Some Pakistani bearers of نصیر naṣīr also write Nasir; the usual spelling for that name is Naseer.

entries.name: Tuan
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese Tuấn: Hà Nội [twən˧˦], Saigon [t⁽ʷ⁾əŋ˦˥]; one syllable
entries.notes: Unaccented spelling of Vietnamese Tuấn (US 1.4k, Canada, France): u is a w glide and â is 'uh', as Quân (n0011). Today's too-AHN (US) and TYOO-un (GB) make two syllables. Tone dropped.

entries.name: Vinh
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese Vinh: Hà Nội [viŋ̟˧˥], Saigon [vɨn˧˧]
entries.notes: Today's VIN matches the English rendering used for Linh and Minh (n0005, n0008). Tone dropped.

entries.name: Gertrude
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Gertrude: /ˈɡɝtɹud/, /ˈɡɜːtɹuːd/
entries.notes: English bearers (US 48k) dominate this spelling.

entries.name: Israr
entries.source: Urdu اسرار isrār (from Arabic أسرار ʔasrār, /ʔas.raːr/): the long final syllable takes the stress, as Iqbal and Irfan (n0003-n0004)
entries.notes: Today's IS-rer reduces the long 'ah' and stresses the first syllable. Bearers: Pakistan, India, British Pakistanis (GB-EAW 114).

entries.name: Travis
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Travis: /ˈtɹævɪs/

entries.name: Nazim
entries.source: Wiktionary, Urdu ناظم (nāzim): /nɑː.zɪm/; Arabic /naː.ðˤim/

alternatives.context: Azerbaijani Nazim (wd AZ 28) and Turkish Nazım: nah-ZEEM, final stress

entries.notes: Also the rare word 'nazim' (a South Asian administrator), said the same; treated as a name. Arabic and South Asian bearers (Algeria, Pakistan, India, UK) stress the long first syllable as today; Azerbaijani bearers are the largest Wikidata group but a smaller population.

entries.name: Bích
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese Bích: Hà Nội [ʔɓïk̟̚˧˦], Saigon [ʔɓɨt̚˦˥]; final ch is a k-like stop, not English ch

alternatives.context: Southern (Saigon) pronunciation: final t and a central vowel

entries.notes: Today's bˈɪʧ says the English swear word; Vietnamese final ch is never [tʃ]. Northern 'bik' is the usual English approximation. Tone dropped.

entries.name: Huê
entries.source: Wikipedia, Huế: Vietnamese [hwě]; Wiktionary Huế [hwe˧˦]: one syllable, h + w glide + e
entries.notes: Today's HYOO is the English word 'hue'. The name is the same syllable without the tone mark; open-syllable e is 'ay' (guide table).

entries.name: Thái
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese Thái: [tʰaːj˧˦]
entries.notes: Vietnamese th is an aspirated t; today's tˈI matches. Tone dropped.

entries.name: Tùng
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese Tùng: [tʊwŋ͡m˨˩]
entries.notes: Today's TUNG ('tongue') uses the 'cup' vowel; Vietnamese -ung is 'oong', as Dũng (n0009). The final labial-velar stays ng. Tone dropped.

entries.name: Ánh
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese Ánh: Hà Nội [ʔajŋ̟˧˦], Saigon [ʔan˦˥]; the Anh precedent (n0004) uses the southern 'ahn'
entries.notes: Today's 'Ann' uses the 'cat' vowel. Tone dropped.

entries.name: Moïse
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Moïse: /mɔ.iz/
entries.notes: The diaeresis splits o and i into two syllables; today's MOYZ reads oï as 'oy'. French names take final stress in English; o as in Noël (nOˈɛl). Bearers: France, DR Congo, Switzerland, Cameroon, Haiti.

entries.name: Nour
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic نور: /nuːr/; French Nour /nuʁ/
entries.notes: French-orthography ou is 'oo'; today's NOWR reads it as English 'our'. Same reading as Noor and Nur (n0006, n0010).

entries.name: Ayşe
entries.source: Wiktionary, Turkish Ayşe: /ajʃe/ (no stress mark); Turkish names take final stress (Mehmet, Emre precedents)
entries.notes: Today's ˈAz ('AYZ') drops a syllable and reads ş as z. Final open-syllable e is 'ay' (guide table, Emre n0012).

entries.name: Faustin
entries.source: French spelling: au is [o] and -in is the nasal [ɛ̃] (as Sylvain, Alain); French names take final stress in English
entries.notes: Today's FAW-stin is an English reading. Bearers: France (FR 2k), DR Congo, Rwanda, Burundi, Cameroon.

entries.name: Halim
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic حليم (ḥalīm): /ħa.liːm/; Turkish Halim also final stress

alternatives.context: Indonesian and Malay bearers (wd ID 12, MY 6): HAH-lim

entries.notes: Arabic, Turkish (wd TR 37), Albanian and French-Maghrebi (FR 1.6k) bearers stress the long ī; today's HAL-im stresses the first syllable. ḥ → h (guide table); unstressed a as Nabil (n0004).

entries.name: Haris
entries.source: Wiktionary, Greek Χάρης: /ˈxa.ris/; Malay/Indonesian Haris [ha.res]
entries.notes: Greek, Bosnian and Pakistani (حارث) bearers all stress the first syllable with 'ah'; Greek x [x] → h. Today's hˈɑɹis matches.

entries.name: Chad
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Chad: /t͡ʃæd/
entries.notes: Also the country and the word 'chad' (paper punched from a ballot). Name and words read the same, so nothing needs to ship.

entries.name: Edmundo
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Edmundo: /edˈmundo/ (Portuguese /ɛdˈmũ.du/)
entries.notes: Today's ed-MUN-doh reads u as in 'fun'; Spanish and Portuguese u is 'oo'. Bearers: Peru, Brazil, Mexico, Chile, US Hispanic.

entries.name: Munir
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic منير (munīr): /mu.niːr/
entries.notes: Today's MYOO-neer adds a y glide and stresses the first syllable. Same reading as the French spelling Mounir (already right today). Bearers: Pakistan, Palestine, Iraq, Indonesia.

entries.name: Stacey
entries.source: Dictionary.com, Stacey: /ˈsteɪ si/

entries.name: Riley
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Riley: /ˈɹaɪ.li/

entries.name: Jérôme
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Jérôme: /ʒe.ʁom/
entries.notes: The accented spelling is French (FR 23k, Belgium, Switzerland); today's juh-ROHM is the English Jerome (whose unaccented entry stays English, n0009). é → 'ay' as Frédéric (n0008).

entries.name: Ngozi
entries.source: Wikipedia, Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala: English /əŋˈɡoʊzi/; Igbo [ŋ́gɔ́zí]
entries.notes: Today's ɛŋɡˈOzi differs from the English IPA only in the unstressed first vowel.

entries.name: Femi
entries.source: Yoruba Fẹ́mi (short for Olúfẹ́mi): open ẹ [ɛ] with a high tone on the first syllable; no dictionary entry
entries.notes: Today's FEM-ee matches; tones dropped, the high-toned first syllable takes the English stress.

entries.name: Clément
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Clément: /kle.mɑ̃/
entries.notes: The accented spelling is French (FR 162k births); today's KLEM-unt is the English Clement. Nasal ɑ̃ → 'ahn' as Jean (guide), é → 'ay' as Frédéric; final t silent.

entries.name: Lukman
entries.source: Arabic لقمان luqmān /luq.maːn/, Urdu /lʊq.mɑːn/ (Wiktionary); Indonesian penultimate stress, as Wiktionary gives for Halim /ˈhalim/

alternatives.context: Arabic and Urdu: the long final syllable stressed, look-MAHN

entries.notes: Every group has the 'book' vowel, not today's 'luck'. Stress is the open question: Indonesian (wd ID 9) and Nigerian (NG 7) bearers are the largest groups; Indonesian stresses the first syllable, Arabic and Urdu the last, and I found no source for Nigerian usage.

entries.name: Mason
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Mason: /ˈmeɪsən/
entries.notes: Also the word 'mason' (stoneworker; Freemason) and the surname. Name and word read the same, so nothing needs to ship.

entries.name: Tobias
entries.source: Wiktionary, German Tobias: [toˈbiː.as] (English /təˈbaɪəs/); Forebears (2014): Germany 97k, Sweden 12.5k, US 8.7k
entries.notes: Decision to review: German, Austrian, Swiss, Swedish, Norwegian (NO 11k births), Danish and Dutch bearers all say toh-BEE-ahs (Norwegian and Swedish with an 'oo'-ish first vowel), well over the English group even counting Zimbabwe, Kenya and Nigeria (Forebears 13k, 12k, 9k) as English. Changes English bearers (Tobias Menzies).

entries.name: Kanika
entries.source: Hindi कनिका (kanikā): short a, short i, long final ā; no dictionary or Wiktionary entry

alternatives.context: Bengali bearers (Kanika Banerjee): initial stress, KAW-nee-kuh

entries.notes: Same shape as Kavita (n0005, unresolved). Today's KAN-ik-uh has the 'cat' vowel, which no group uses, but the stress is unsourced: English renderings stress -ni-, Bengali the first syllable, and the Hindustani weight rule the long final ā.

entries.name: Lalita
entries.source: Hindi ललिता (lalitā): short a, short i, long final ā; no dictionary or Wiktionary entry
entries.notes: Same shape as Kavita (n0005, unresolved): today's luh-LEE-tuh (CMUdict) lengthens the short i, but no source marks the stress. Needs a stress source before shipping.

entries.name: Suman
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi सुमन (suman): /sʊ.mən/

alternatives.context: Hindustani weight rule (heavy closed final): soo-MUN

entries.notes: Short u in an open syllable is 'oo' (Sudha precedent, n0011). Today's first-syllable stress matches Bengali and Nepali (initial stress) and the Karan precedent; the Hindustani weight rule would stress -man. Low until a stress source is found.

entries.name: Aïssata
entries.source: West African form of ʿĀʾisha (Aïcha) in French spelling: stressed a is 'ah'; no source for the stress (as Aminata, Adama)

alternatives.context: careful French reading of the diaeresis: ah-ee-SAH-tah

entries.notes: GB-only fix, as Adama (n0007): British today says eye-SOT-uh with the 'lot' vowel. US kept.

entries.name: Basanta
entries.source: Sanskrit वसन्त vasanta ('spring'): short a throughout; stress on the heavy closed syllable, as the Vasant precedent (n0004, vəsˈʌnt)
entries.notes: Today's buh-SAN-tuh uses the 'cat' vowel, which no group has. The b spelling marks Nepali, Odia, Assamese and Bengali bearers, whose languages stress the first syllable; no source for the name.

entries.name: Birendra
entries.source: Sanskrit वीरेन्द्र (vīrendra): long ī, then a heavy closed 'ren' that takes the stress (as Upendra, n0011; Mahendra, n0002)
entries.notes: Today's bih-REN-druh has the right stress and stressed vowel; the unstressed first vowel differs only in length (as Sumit). King Birendra of Nepal.

entries.name: Verónica
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Verónica: /beˈɾonika/

alternatives.context: as English speakers often say Spanish v: veh-ROH-nee-kuh

entries.notes: The accented spelling is Spanish (Argentina, Peru, Mexico, Chile). Today's vuh-RON-ih-kuh is the English Veronica (whose entry stays English, n0006). Stressed o is 'oh'; Spanish word-initial v is [b], kept as for Víctor and Vicente (n0003).

entries.name: Ed
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Ed: /ɛd/
entries.notes: Dutch Ed (wd NL 76) is the same apart from the final devoicing.

entries.name: Su
entries.source: Wiktionary, Turkish su /su/; Korean 수 [su]; Chinese 素 sù
entries.notes: Every bearer group says 'soo', as today.

entries.name: Dieter
entries.source: Wiktionary, German Dieter: /ˈdiːtɐ/
entries.notes: Also the English word 'dieter' (one who diets), read DY-uh-ter today. The German name (wd DE 1685, AT, CH; Dieter Rams) is DEE-ter; that reading is given here. The word is uncommon and the capitalised spelling is almost always the name, so the merge could reasonably ship it as a name (as for rare words).

entries.name: Melody
entries.notes: Ordinary word 'melody'. Name and word read the same, so nothing needs to ship.

entries.name: Fernand
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Fernand: /fɛʁ.nɑ̃/
entries.notes: Today's fer-NAND uses the 'cat' vowel and sounds the d. French nasal ɑ̃ → 'ahn' (as Jean), final d silent. Bearers: France (FR 48k), Belgium, Luxembourg, Switzerland.

entries.name: Burak
entries.source: Wiktionary, Turkish Burak: /buˈɾak/
entries.notes: Today's BYOO-ruk adds a y glide and stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Amara
entries.source: Wiktionary, Portuguese Amara: /aˈma.ɾɐ/; English and Igbo Amara stress the second syllable
entries.notes: English (US 27k, UK 5k), Igbo, Spanish and West African bearers all stress -MA- with 'ah'; today's ɑmˈɑɹə matches (GB's first vowel is unstressed).

entries.name: Fawad
entries.source: Urdu فواد fawād (Fawad Khan, Fawad Alam): short a, long final ā that takes the stress, as Iqbal and Irfan; no IPA source
entries.notes: Today's FAW-wahd stresses the first syllable. Urdu ʋ → w (as English speakers say it). Not the Arabic فؤاد Fuad.

entries.name: Celia
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Celia: /ˈselja/ (Latin America), /ˈθelja/ (Spain)
entries.notes: anglo_share 0.1: Spanish bearers (ES 54k, Argentina, Uruguay, Mexico, Cuba, US Hispanic) are the largest group; open-syllable e is 'ay' (guide table). Today's SEEL-yuh is the English reading. Seseo s chosen (Latin America and the US).

entries.name: Daniele
entries.source: Wiktionary, Italian Daniele: /daˈnjɛ.le/; Forebears (2014): Italy 186k, Brazil 173k, France 39k
entries.notes: Italian (men) and Brazilian (women, [daniˈɛli]) bearers share the stressed open e and a final vowel; together far more than the French. Today's dan-YEL is the French reading. The guide's own example: dænjˈɛlA.

entries.name: Céline
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Céline: /se.lin/
entries.notes: Today's səlˈin differs only in the unstressed first vowel.

entries.name: Charmaine
entries.source: CMUdict CHARMAINE: SH AA0 R M EY1 N (stress on the second syllable)
entries.notes: Light verification.

entries.name: Jared
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Jared: /ˈd͡ʒæɹəd/
entries.notes: Today's JARD (gold) is one syllable with the 'car' vowel. American English merges the vowel before r with 'air' (JAIR-ud); British keeps the 'cat' vowel (JARR-ud).

entries.name: Selim
entries.source: Wiktionary, Turkish Selim: /seˈlim/
entries.notes: Turkish (wd TR 145) and Maghrebi (FR 6.2k, Tunisia) bearers stress the last syllable; today's SEL-im stresses the first.

entries.name: Aníbal
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Aníbal: /aˈnibal/
entries.notes: Today's AN-ih-bul is the English Hannibal. Bearers: Argentina, Portugal, Peru, Uruguay.

entries.name: Fausto
entries.source: Wiktionary, Italian Fausto: /ˈfaws.to/; Spanish /ˈfausto/
entries.notes: au is 'ow' in Italian, Spanish and Portuguese (as Claudio, n0005); today's FAW-stoh reads it as English au.

entries.name: Tamer
entries.drop_detail: 'tamer' (comparative of tame; a lion tamer) is an ordinary word
entries.source: Arabic تامر tāmir, Egyptian Tamer: the long first syllable takes the stress; Forebears (2014): Egypt 288k, Turkey 34k

alternatives.context: Turkish bearers (wd TR 70): final stress, tah-MEHR

entries.notes: Also the rare word 'tamer' (lion tamer), read TAY-mer today; the capitalised spelling is almost always the name (Tamer Hosny), so treated as a name. Egyptian bearers dominate; long ā is 'ah' (as Tarek, Hala).

entries.name: Marilyn
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Marilyn: /ˈmæɹ.ɪ.lɪn/, /ˈmɛɹ.ɪ.lɪn/

entries.name: Arief
entries.source: Indonesian Arief is the old (Dutch-era) spelling of Arif, ie = i; Indonesian stresses the penultimate (Wiktionary: Halim /ˈhalim/), as Arabic ʿārif stresses its long first ā
entries.notes: Indonesian bearers only (wd ID 19). Today's uh-REEF is the Turkish reading of Arif (n0006). Closed final i as the Agus precedent's u (n0009).

entries.name: Rizki
entries.source: Indonesian Rizki (from Arabic rizq): penultimate stress; same reading as Rizky (n0012)
entries.notes: Today's RIZ-kee matches.

entries.name: Virgilio
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Virgilio: /biɾˈxiljo/; Tagalog /viɾˈhiljo/, /biɾˈhiljo/; Italian /virˈd͡ʒi.ljo/

alternatives.context: Filipino and English-influenced Spanish speakers: veer-HEE-lyoh

entries.notes: Spanish (ES 2.9k, Peru, Argentina, US Hispanic 1.4k) and Filipino bearers dominate. Spanish g before i is [x] → h (as Rogelio); stressed i is 'ee'. Word-initial v is [b], kept as for Vicente (n0003). Today's ver-JIL-ee-oh is Italian-English.

entries.name: Lamin
entries.source: Gambian form of al-Amīn (Arabic stress on the long ī); name sites give 'lah-MEEN'; same reading as the French spelling Lamine (n0008)
entries.notes: Today's LAM-in stresses the first syllable with the 'cat' vowel. No pronunciation source for Gambian (Mandinka) usage itself; bearers: the Gambia, and Gambians in Spain (ES 1k) and the UK.

entries.name: Alessandra
entries.source: Wiktionary, Italian Alessandra: /a.lesˈsan.dra/; Portuguese /a.leˈsɐ̃.dɾɐ/
entries.notes: Italian (wd IT 441) and Brazilian bearers say 'ah' in the stressed syllable; today's al-es-SAN-druh uses the 'cat' vowel.

entries.name: Bertha
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Bertha: GA /ˈbɝθə/, RP /ˈbɜːθə/; Spanish Berta /ˈbeɾta/; Forebears (2014): Mexico 236k, US 135k, Peru 61k, Colombia 47k

alternatives.context: Spanish-speaking bearers (Mexico, Peru, Colombia, Ecuador, US Hispanic) and German and Dutch bearers: BEHR-tuh

entries.notes: Today's bˈɜɹθə matches the English reading. Reviewer: changed back from Spanish BEHR-tuh. The row is usage english (anglo_share 0.15), and the guide keeps English for those rows (as Michele), even though Spanish-speaking bearers are more numerous. English text also means Big Bertha and Bertha Mason.

entries.name: Kayla
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Kayla: /ˈkeɪ.lə/

entries.name: Lena
entries.source: Wiktionary, German Lena: /ˈleːna/ (Polish /ˈlɛ.na/; English /ˈli.na/)

alternatives.context: English-speaking bearers (Lena Horne, Lena Dunham): LEE-nuh

entries.notes: German (wd DE 440), Swedish, Norwegian, Danish, Greek and Russian bearers all say LAY-na/LEH-na, more than the English LEE-nuh group; today's lˈAnə matches.

entries.name: Annabelle
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Annabelle: /ˈænəbɛl/ (French /a.na.bɛl/)
entries.notes: Today's AN-uh-bul reduces the final 'bell' to a schwa; English keeps a full 'bel' (secondary stress), as in Isabelle and Annabel.

entries.name: Marcelino
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Marcelino: /maɾseˈlino/ (Spain /maɾθeˈlino/); Portuguese /maʁ.seˈlĩ.nu/
entries.notes: Today's mar-cheh-LEE-noh is Italian-style; Spanish (ES 13k, Mexico, Argentina, US Hispanic) and Portuguese bearers use s, as Marcelo (n0003).

entries.name: Geraldine
entries.source: Dictionary.com, Geraldine: /ˈdʒɛr əlˌdin/
entries.notes: Today's jer-ul-DEEN puts the primary stress on the last syllable; English bearers (US 166k, Ireland 6.6k) stress the first.

entries.name: Tomasz
entries.source: Wiktionary, Polish Tomasz: /ˈtɔ.maʂ/
entries.notes: US fix: today's TAH-mush has the 'spa' vowel for Polish o [ɔ] (the Piotr precedent, n0011, uses ɔ). British today (tˈɒməʃ) already has the right stressed vowel; sz [ʂ] → sh.

entries.name: Marcia
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Marcia: /ˈmɑɹʃə/, /ˈmɑːʃə/

alternatives.context: Brazilian Márcia written without the accent: MAR-syuh

entries.notes: English bearers (US 129k) dominate the unaccented spelling; Brazilian bearers write Márcia, a separate name.

entries.name: Kitty
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Kitty: /ˈkɪti/
entries.notes: Also the word 'kitty' (kitten; a shared fund). Name and word read the same, so nothing needs to ship.

entries.name: Darius
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Darius: /dəˈɹaɪ.əs/ (also /ˈdæɹi.əs/); Lithuanian [²ˈdɑːrʲʊ̟s]

alternatives.context: Lithuanian and Romanian bearers (Forebears: 19k and 18k): DAH-ryoos

entries.notes: English text mostly means Darius the Great, said duh-RY-us; English-speaking bearers (US 54k births, UK, anglophone Africa) are also the largest group using this spelling (Iranian bearers write Dariush).

entries.name: Ifeanyi
entries.source: Igbo Ifeanyi (Ifeanyịchukwu, 'nothing is impossible for God'): i-fe-a-nyi, with high tones on fe and a; regular Igbo orthography, no IPA source
entries.notes: Today's eye-FEEN-yee reads the i as 'eye' and drops the a. Tones dropped; English stress placed on the high-toned 'a', as Nigerian English speakers say it, but unsourced.

entries.name: Dale
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Dale: /deɪl/
entries.notes: Also the word 'dale' (valley; the Yorkshire Dales). Name and word read the same, so nothing needs to ship.

entries.name: Nita
entries.source: English Nita (from Juanita/Anita) and Hindi नीता nītā both have a long stressed 'ee'; Finnish /ˈnitɑ/ (Wiktionary)

entries.name: Michał
entries.source: Wiktionary, Polish Michał: /ˈmi.xaw/
entries.notes: Polish ch [x] → h (its English approximation, as Spanish j) and ł → w, as Stanisław (n0008). Today's MY-kup is garbled.

entries.name: Shabnam
entries.source: Wiktionary, Persian شبنم (šabnam, 'dew'): Iran formal [ʃæb.nǽm]; Behind the Name /ʃæb.ˈnæm/ (Persian)

alternatives.context: Urdu, Hindi and Bengali bearers (SHUB-num); n0015 chose this as the larger group

entries.notes: Iranian reading. Conflicts with n0015, which chose the South Asian SHUB-num: one of the two must be picked when the pack is merged.

entries.name: Enoch
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Enoch: /ˈiːnək/, /ˈiːnɒk/

entries.name: Greg
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Greg: /ɡɹɛɡ/

entries.name: Georgia
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Georgia: /ˈd͡ʒɔɹ.d͡ʒə/, /ˈd͡ʒɔː.d͡ʒə/
entries.notes: Covered by the tech list (the Georgia typeface) with the same reading as the name, the US state and the country; nothing to change.

entries.name: Kathryn
entries.source: CMUdict KATHRYN: K AE1 TH R IH0 N
entries.notes: Light verification.

entries.name: Can
entries.source: Wiktionary, Turkish Can: /ˈd͡ʒan/
entries.notes: The modal verb 'can' at a sentence start ('Can you...'). Never replace it. The Turkish name (wd TR 356) is JAHN, the guide's own example; that reading is given here.

entries.name: Majdi
entries.source: Arabic مجدي majdī: heavy first syllable takes the stress (final -ī is not superheavy); Arabic stressed a → 'ah' (guide table)

alternatives.context: Egyptian bearers, usually spelled Magdy: MAG-dee

entries.notes: Today's MY-dee drops the j. The j spelling is the Levantine and Maghrebi romanisation (Palestine, Tunisia, FR 310); Egyptians mostly write Magdy.

entries.name: Salam
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic سلام (salām): /sa.laːm/
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today says the 'lot' vowel in both syllables (suh-LOM). US already right. Long final ā takes the stress.

entries.name: Valérie
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Valérie: /va.le.ʁi/
entries.notes: The accented spelling is French (FR 250k births, Belgium, Switzerland); today's VAL-uh-ree is the English Valerie. French names take final stress in English (Nathalie, n0007); é → 'ay' (Frédéric).

entries.name: Dalia
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic داليا (dālyā): /daː.li.jaː/; Spanish Dalia /ˈdalja/
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today says DOL-yuh with the 'lot' vowel. US already right. Arabic, Spanish (ES 2.7k, Mexico) and English bearers stress DAHL-.

entries.name: Constance
entries.source: Dictionary.com, Constance: /ˈkɒn stəns/
entries.notes: English bearers (US 123k, UK 4k) outnumber the French.

entries.name: Jefferson
entries.source: Forebears (2014): Brazil 209k, Philippines 48k, Ecuador 19k, US 14k; Wiktionary Spanish /ˈʝefeɾson/, English /ˈd͡ʒɛfɚsən/

alternatives.context: English (Thomas Jefferson; US and Filipino bearers): JEF-er-sun

entries.notes: Capitalised 'Jefferson' in English text is overwhelmingly the surname (Thomas Jefferson, Jefferson City, Jefferson Airplane), read JEF-er-sun today: keep it. The given name's largest bearer group is Brazilian, ZHEF-er-sohn (nasal final vowel rendered 'sohn'); that reading is given here.

entries.name: Edna
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Edna: /ˈɛdnə/; Portuguese /ˈɛd.nɐ/, Spanish /ˈedna/
entries.notes: Brazilian (Forebears 221k), US, Filipino, Angolan, English, Mexican and Hebrew bearers all say ED-na; Brazilians sometimes insert a vowel (ED-jee-nah).

entries.name: Sidney
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Sidney: /ˈsɪdni/; Forebears (2014): Brazil 79k, US 70k, England 18.5k, South Africa 8.7k
entries.notes: English-speaking bearers (US, England, South Africa, Canada, Kenya) narrowly outnumber the Brazilian and Lusophone African group.

entries.name: Hicham
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic هشام (hišām): /hi.ʃaːm/
entries.notes: French-orthography ch is sh; today's HITCH-um reads it as English ch and stresses the first syllable. Bearers: Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia, France (5.9k), Spain (8.6k).

entries.name: Aman
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi अमन (aman): /ə.mən/; stress on the heavy closed final syllable (Wikipedia's Hindustani weight rule), as Amit and Anil (n0001)

alternatives.context: first-syllable stress, as the Karan precedent (n0002): UH-mun

entries.notes: Hindi and Punjabi short a is 'uh', not today's 'ah' (AH-mun). Indian, Punjabi and British Indian bearers (GB 2.1k, US 2.6k). The stress is weakly sourced: Karan (same shape) took the first syllable.

entries.name: Sofiane
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic سفيان (sufyān): /suf.jaːn/; French Sofiane [sɔ.fjan]
entries.notes: Today's soh-fee-AN uses the 'cat' vowel and splits fya into two syllables; -ane is 'ahn' (as Ousmane). Bearers: France (FR 25k), Algeria, Tunisia.

entries.name: Dario
entries.source: Wiktionary, Italian Dario: /ˈda.rjo/

alternatives.context: Spanish Darío (usually written with the accent) and Brazilian Dario: dah-REE-oh

entries.notes: The unaccented spelling is the Italian, Croatian and Swiss name (wd IT 392, CH 31, HR 29; Dario Fo, Dario Amodei); Spanish bearers write Darío. Today's DAIR-ee-oh is an English reading.

entries.name: Freddie
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Freddie: /ˈfɹɛdi/

entries.name: Abdel Fattah
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic عبد الفتاح: /ʕabd al.fat.taːħ/; the long final ā of Fattāḥ takes the stress
entries.notes: Today's FAH-tuh stresses the first syllable of Fattah and drops the final ḥ. ʿayn dropped, ḥ → h (guide table); ʿAbd as the guide's example. Bearers: Egypt (Abdel Fattah el-Sisi), Palestine, Syria.

entries.name: Hala
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic هالة (hāla): /haː.la/
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today says HOL-uh with the 'lot' vowel. US already right.

entries.name: Tasneem
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic تسنيم (tasnīm): /tas.niːm/
entries.notes: The long final ī takes the stress in Arabic and Urdu; today's TAS-neem stresses the first syllable. Bearers: Pakistan, South Africa, India, UK.

entries.name: Vladislav
entries.source: Wiktionary, Russian Владислав: [vɫədʲɪsˈɫaf] (Ukrainian [wɫɐdesˈɫau̯]; Czech Vladislav [ˈvlaɟɪslaf])

alternatives.context: Czech and Slovak bearers (wd CZ 44): VLAH-dih-slahf

entries.notes: Russian, Belarusian, Ukrainian and Bulgarian bearers stress the last syllable and outnumber Czech and Slovak ones, as for Stanislav (n0007); final v is devoiced to f. Today's VLAD-uh-slahv is an English reading.

entries.name: Jordi
entries.source: Wiktionary, Catalan Jordi: [ˈʒɔr.di]

alternatives.context: Spanish speakers outside Catalonia and Dutch bearers: YOR-dee

entries.notes: Catalan j is zh; today's JOR-dee is an English reading. Bearers: Catalonia (ES 82k), Andorra, Netherlands.

entries.name: Salvatore
entries.source: Wiktionary, Italian Salvatore: /sal.vaˈto.re/
entries.notes: Italian bearers (wd IT 902; one of southern Italy's commonest names) outnumber Italian-American ones. Final e is 'ay' (the guide's Daniele example); today's TOR-ee is the Italian-American reading.

entries.name: Gail
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Gail: /ɡeɪl/

entries.name: Sana
entries.source: Urdu ثنا sanā and Arabic سناء sanāʾ: short a then a long final ā that carries the stress; Forebears (2014): Pakistan 305k, Iraq 108k, India 77k, Sudan 48k

alternatives.context: Japanese, Finnish and Bosnian bearers: SAH-nuh

entries.notes: Pakistani, Indian and Arab bearers dominate; today's SAH-nuh stresses the first syllable. Hindustani weight rule: the only heavy syllable is the final ā.

entries.name: Mounir
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic منير (munīr): /mu.niːr/
entries.notes: Today's munˈɪɹ matches. Bearers: Tunisia, Morocco, Algeria, France (6.1k), Spain.

entries.name: János
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hungarian János: [ˈjaːnoʃ]
entries.notes: Hungarian j is y, á a long 'ah' and s is sh; today's JAN-ohs reads the English spelling.

entries.name: Courtney
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Courtney: /ˈkɔː(ɹ)tni/

entries.name: Darren
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Darren: /ˈdæɹən/ (US also /ˈdɛɹən/)
entries.notes: Today's dˈɑɹən says DAHR-en with the 'car' vowel in both accents. US uses the merged 'Mary/marry' vowel as the app does for Sharon and Gary; British keeps the 'a' of 'cat'.

entries.name: Petra
entries.source: Wiktionary: Czech Petra /ˈpɛtra/, English /ˈpɛtɹə/; today's pˈɛtɹə matches

alternatives.context: German, Slovene and Scandinavian bearers, whose long close e is nearer 'ay'

entries.notes: As the Daniela precedent: bearers split between an open e (Czech, Slovak, English) and a close e (German, Spanish, Slovene); today's PET-ruh is an accepted reading for all of them.

entries.name: Norberto
entries.source: Spanish orthography: Norberto [noɾˈβeɾto], stress on the penultimate; Italian [norˈbɛrto] agrees
entries.notes: Today's nor-BUR-toh uses the 'her' vowel; every bearer group says 'ehr' (as Roberto, already right).

entries.name: Nam
entries.source: Vietnamese Nam [naːm] (long a), Korean 남 [nam]
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today says nˈam with the 'cat' vowel; bearers say 'ah' (as Anh, Lan). US already right. Tone dropped.

entries.name: Tawfik
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic توفيق (tawfīq): /taw.fiːq/; Arabic stress falls on the final superheavy syllable
entries.notes: Today's TAW-fik stresses the first syllable and loses the 'ow' of aw. q → k (guide).

entries.name: Shanti
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi शांति (śānti): long ā, first-syllable stress; today's ʃˈɑnti / ʃˈɑːnti matches
entries.notes: Also the rare word 'shanti' (peace), the same Sanskrit word said the same way.

entries.name: Yogi
entries.source: Wiktionary, English yogi: /ˈjoʊɡi/; Hindi योगी yogī
entries.notes: Also the word 'yogi' (and Yogi Bear, Yogi Berra). The name (Hindi योगी, Indonesian Yogi) sounds the same as the word, YOH-gee, so nothing needs to ship.

entries.name: Leanne
entries.source: NameDrop: Leann ɫiˈæn (lee-AN); LeAnn Rimes is /liˈæn/; today's liˈæn matches

alternatives.context: some British and Australian bearers stress the first syllable (LEE-an)

entries.notes: A coinage from Lee + Ann; no dictionary lists it. The second-syllable stress is the usual reading.

entries.name: Anish
entries.source: Hindi अनीश (anīś): short a, long ī; the Hindustani weight rule stresses the long ī
entries.notes: Today's AN-ish reads it as an English word (as Manish, n0002).

entries.name: Flávio
entries.source: Wiktionary, Portuguese Flávio: Brazil /ˈfla.vju/; final unstressed -io is [ju]
entries.notes: Today's FLAH-vee-oh is the Italian/Spanish ending; Portuguese -io is one syllable 'vyoo' (as Fábio, n0010). British today also has the 'lot' vowel.

entries.name: Fatemeh
entries.source: Wiktionary, Persian فاطمه: Iran formal [fɒː.t̪ʰe.mé], final stress
entries.notes: Today's FAH-tim-eh stresses the first syllable. Persian â → 'ah' (as Payam); final open e → 'ay' (guide table).

entries.name: Orhan
entries.source: Wikipedia, Orhan Pamuk: Turkish [feˈɾit oɾˈhan paˈmuk]
entries.notes: Today's OR-hun stresses the first syllable and reduces the 'ah'.

entries.name: Luciana
entries.region: Argentina, Peru, Spain, US, Brazil, Italy
entries.source: Spanish orthography: Luciana [luˈsjana] (Latin America; Spain [luˈθjana]); Portuguese [lusiˈɐ̃nɐ]

alternatives.context: Brazilian bearers (nasal a, as Juliana, n0006)

entries.notes: Spanish-speaking bearers (US Hispanic 15k, Spain 5.5k, Argentina, Peru) are the largest group and Brazilians share the s; today's LOO-chuh-nuh fits nobody (Italians stress -CHA-).

entries.name: Tunde
entries.source: Yoruba Túndé (short for Babátúndé): regular orthography, u [u], final e [e]
entries.notes: Today's TUND is one syllable; the final e is a full vowel ('ay', guide table). Yoruba is tonal; English speakers stress the first syllable.

entries.name: Huy
entries.source: Vietnamese Huy [hwi]: uy is [wi] (as Thủy, Huyền)
entries.notes: Today's HIGH reads uy as English 'eye'. One syllable: h, a w glide, 'ee'. Tone dropped.

entries.name: Shriya
entries.source: Hindi श्रिया (śriyā); today's ʃɹˈiə matches the Priya pattern (n0002, already correct)

entries.name: Duy
entries.source: Vietnamese Duy: Hà Nội [zwi], Saigon [jwi]; uy is [wi]
entries.notes: Plain d is z (north) or y (centre, south), never English d (that is đ). The y follows Dũng (n0009) and Giang (n0013). Today's DIE reads it as English. Tone dropped. The audio round trip heard 'we': the voice may weaken the y before w; worth a listen.

entries.name: Eugen
entries.source: Wiktionary, German Eugen: /ˈɔʏ̯ɡən/, also /ɔʏ̯ˈɡeːn/
entries.notes: German-speaking bearers (DE, CH, AT) outnumber Romanian ones. German eu is 'oy'; today's YOO-gun reads it as English Eugene.

entries.name: Binta
entries.source: West African Binta: i, a; today's bˈɪntə keeps the stressed BIN and differs only in the unstressed final vowel

entries.name: Maurício
entries.source: Wiktionary, Portuguese Maurício: Brazil /mawˈɾi.sju/; final -io is [ju]
entries.notes: Today's mow-REE-see-oh has the Spanish ending; Portuguese -io is 'syoo' (as Márcio, n0011). The stressed syllable is already right.

entries.name: Tarun
entries.source: Hindi तरुण (taruṇ): short a, u; stress on the closed final syllable as Arun (n0001)
entries.notes: Today's TAIR-un reads it as English. Retroflex ɳ → n.

entries.name: Châu
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese châu: Hà Nội [t͡ɕəw˧˧], Saigon [cəw˧˧]
entries.notes: Vietnamese ch is 'ch', not today's 'sh'. âu [əw] is nearest to English 'oh' (as Hồng's ô, n0007). Tone dropped.

entries.name: Dương
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese dương: Hà Nội [zɨəŋ˧˧], Saigon [jɨəŋ˧˧]
entries.notes: Plain d is y (south, as Dũng, n0009); ươ as in Phương and Hương. Today's DOO-ohng reads d as English d and splits the syllable. Tone dropped.

entries.name: Khôi
entries.source: Vietnamese Khôi [xoj]: kh [x] → k (as Khánh, n0012), ôi = 'oy'; today's kˈY matches
entries.notes: Tone dropped.

entries.name: Như
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese như: [ɲɨ˧˧]
entries.notes: One syllable: nh is the ny of 'canyon', ư [ɨ] → ʊ (guide; as Đức, n0010). Today's EN-hyoo spells out the letters. Usually a second given name (Quỳnh Như). Tone dropped.

entries.name: Karthik
entries.source: Tamil கார்த்திக் (Kārttik): long ā, dental t; first-syllable stress
entries.notes: In Indian spelling th is a dental t, not the 'th' of thin (as Siddharth, n0005; Latha, n0013).

entries.name: Lester
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Lester: /ˈlɛstə/, US /ˈlɛstɚ/

entries.name: Madhav
entries.source: Hindi माधव (mādhav): long ā, short a; the weight rule stresses the long first syllable
entries.notes: Today's MAD-hav reads dh as two sounds and uses the 'cat' vowel. Aspirated dh → d.

entries.name: Silas
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Silas: /ˈsaɪləs/

entries.name: Nirav
entries.source: Hindi/Sanskrit नीरव (nīrav): long ī, short a; the weight rule stresses the long first syllable
entries.notes: Today's NIR-ahv shortens the long ī and gives the schwa a full 'ah'.

entries.name: Kriti
entries.source: Hindi कृति (kṛti): ṛ is 'ri' with a short i; Kriti Sanon [kɾɪt̪i]
entries.notes: Today's KREE-tee lengthens the short i (as Smita, n0008).

entries.name: Ritu
entries.source: Hindi ऋतु (ṛtu): ṛ is 'ri' with a short i; stress on the first syllable
entries.notes: Today's ree-TOO lengthens the i and stresses the short final vowel.

entries.name: Vineet
entries.source: Hindi विनीत (vinīt): the long ī takes the stress; today's vɪnˈit matches
entries.notes: ʋ → v.

entries.name: Irena
entries.source: Wikipedia, Irena Sendler: Polish [iˈrɛna ˈsɛndlɛrɔva]; Polish penultimate stress

alternatives.context: Slovene bearers (close long e, ih-RAY-nuh, today's reading)

entries.notes: Polish bearers (wd PL 692) are the largest group; their stressed e is open [ɛ] ('eh'), not today's 'ay'.

entries.name: Ananth
entries.source: Sanskrit अनन्त (ananta): two short a's, dental t; the weight rule stresses the final superheavy -nant (as Hemant, n0013)
entries.notes: Today's AN-unth uses the 'cat' vowel and the 'th' of thin; in Indian spelling th is a dental t (as Latha). The -th spelling is South Indian, where Dravidian stress is weak and initial; no source marks the stress.

entries.name: Alois
entries.source: Wiktionary, Czech Alois: [ˈaloɪs], [ˈalojs]; German (Duden) [ˈaːloɪ̯s]
entries.notes: German, Swiss and Czech bearers stress the first syllable; today's ah-LOYS stresses the second. Review: Austria (wd AT 385) is the largest single country and Austrians often say a-LO-is; France's register (3.8k) says Aloïs.

entries.name: Rajat
entries.source: Hindi रजत (rajat): two short a's (schwa); first-syllable stress as Karan (n0002)
entries.notes: Today's RAJ-ut uses the 'cat' vowel; Hindi short a is 'uh'.

entries.name: Prarthana
entries.source: Hindi प्रार्थना (prārthanā): long ā in a closed first syllable takes the stress; th is an aspirated dental t
entries.notes: Today's prar-THAN-uh reads th as in 'thin' and stresses the light middle syllable.

entries.name: Chandan
entries.source: Hindi चन्दन (candan): two short a's (schwa); first-syllable stress
entries.notes: Today's CHAN-dun uses the 'cat' vowel. The name is common across the Hindi belt, Odisha and Bengal; the Hindi reading is chosen.

entries.name: Deepali
entries.source: Hindi दीपाली (dīpālī): long ī, ā, ī; stress on the long ā
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today says the 'lot' vowel (dee-POL-ee); bearers say 'ah'. US already right.

entries.name: Ashutosh
entries.source: Hindi आशुतोष (āśutoṣ): the weight rule stresses the superheavy final -toṣ (as Santosh, n0003)
entries.notes: Today's ASH-oo-tahsh uses the 'cat' vowel and an 'ah' for the long o. Retroflex ṣ → sh.

entries.name: Satpal
entries.source: Punjabi ਸਤਪਾਲ (Satpāl): short a, long ā; stress on the long final syllable (as Gopal, n0002)
entries.notes: Today's SAT-pal uses the 'cat' vowel twice and stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Geetha
entries.source: Sanskrit गीता (gītā), Tamil கீதா: th is a dental t; same reading as Geeta (n0003)
entries.notes: Today's GEE-thuh reads th as in 'this'.

entries.name: Abdulkadir
entries.source: Arabic عبد القادر (ʿAbd al-Qādir): the long ā of Qādir takes the stress; ʿayn dropped, q → k (guide)
entries.notes: Today's ab-dul-KAY-dur reads the long ā as 'ay'. Somali (NO register), Nigerian and Arab bearers stress KAH; Turkish bearers usually write Abdülkadir and stress the last syllable.

entries.name: Indu
entries.source: Hindi इन्दु (indu): the closed first syllable takes the stress (weight rule)
entries.notes: Today's in-DOO stresses the short final vowel (as Indra, n0006, which is right).

entries.name: Acharya
entries.source: Merriam-Webster, acharya: \ə-ˈchär-yə\; today's gold reading ʌʧˈɑɹiə keeps the stressed CHAR
entries.notes: Also the word 'acharya' (a spiritual teacher), the same reading. Today's only difference is the unstressed -ya said as two syllables (ree-uh). Mostly a surname.

entries.name: Anirban
entries.source: Bengali অনির্বাণ (onirbāṇ): inherent vowel [ɔ], long ā; Bengali stress is weak and initial (as Dipankar, n0013)
entries.notes: Today's AN-ur-ban uses the 'cat' vowel. Bearers are mostly Bengali; no source marks how they stress it in English.

entries.name: Harikrishna
entries.source: Hari + Krishna: Hari हरि [ˈɦəɾi] (n0004), Krishna KRISH-nuh (n0001); the weight rule stresses kriṣ
entries.notes: Today's HAIR-ih-krish-nuh stresses Hari with the 'cat' vowel.

entries.name: Narayanswamy
entries.source: Narayan (n0002, nah-RAH-yun) + swamy (svāmī): the weight rule stresses the long swā
entries.notes: Today's nuh-RAY-unz-wah-mee reads the long ā as 'ay' and splits n-sw. Main stress between the two parts is unsourced.

entries.name: Nityanand
entries.source: Hindi नित्यानन्द (nityānand): the long ā takes the stress (rightmost non-final heavy syllable; as Anand, n0001)
entries.notes: Today's NIT-yah-nund has the right sounds; only the stress moves. Hindi stress is weak and unsourced for this name.

entries.name: Ramdas
entries.source: Hindi रामदास (rāmdās): both a's long; the heavy first syllable takes the stress
entries.notes: Today's RAM-duz (from a custom list) uses the 'cat' vowel and reduces the long ā of dās.

entries.name: Yashpal
entries.source: Hindi यशपाल (yaśpāl): short a, long ā; stress on the long final syllable (as Satpal, Gopal)
entries.notes: Today's YASH-pawl uses the 'cat' vowel and the 'law' vowel.

entries.name: Muhammad
entries.source: Oxford: Muhammad /mʊˈhamɪd/; Merriam-Webster \mō-ˈha-məd, -ˈhä-\; today's US mOhˈɑməd and GB mʊhˈamɪd match
entries.notes: Control-like case: both accents already use a dictionary reading of this spelling.

entries.name: Lida
entries.source: Czech Lída, Russian Лида [ˈlʲidə], Italian and Dutch Lida: all LEE-da; today's lˈidə matches

alternatives.context: older US usage (as in the song 'Lida Rose')

entries.name: Nabila
entries.source: Arabic نبيلة (nabīla): the long ī takes the stress; today's nɑbˈilə matches
entries.notes: British today's unstressed first vowel (nob-) differs only in reduction.

entries.name: Gabrielle
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Gabrielle: /ɡæbɹiːˈɛl/; French /ɡa.bʁi.jɛl/
entries.notes: Today's GAB-ree-el stresses the first syllable; English and French bearers both stress the last.

entries.name: Achmad
entries.source: Indonesian old (Dutch-based) spelling: ch = [x] (kh), from Arabic Aḥmad; Indonesian penultimate stress

alternatives.context: said with h, as the Ahmad entry (n0002)

entries.notes: Today's AHK-mad keeps the stressed 'ah' and renders [x] as k (guide's kh rule); only the unstressed second vowel differs.

entries.name: Germain
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Germain: /ʒɛʁ.mɛ̃/
entries.notes: FR register 17.8k against US 953. French g before e is zh; nasal ɛ̃ → English 'an' (as Alain, Sylvain); French names take final stress in English.

entries.name: Catalina
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Catalina: /kataˈlina/

alternatives.context: the English place name (Santa Catalina Island) and macOS Catalina, today's tech-list reading

entries.notes: Tech-list clash (macOS Catalina), settled at merge. The name reading only changes the secondary-stressed first vowel ('cat' → 'ah'); the stressed LEE is already right. Spanish-speaking bearers (ES 50k, Chile, Colombia, US Hispanic) dominate. Review: Catalina Island would also get 'kah-'.

entries.name: Ignace
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Ignace: /i.ɲas/
entries.notes: French gn is ny (guide: ɲ → nj); final stress. Today's IG-nus reads it as English. French [a] as for Jacques (US ɑ, GB a).

entries.name: Ioan
entries.source: Wiktionary, Romanian Ioan: /joˈan/
entries.notes: Romanian bearers (wd RO 910, ES register 5.1k) outnumber the Welsh (GB-EAW 2.3k). Today's eye-OH-un reads the I as 'eye'.

entries.name: Imad
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic عماد (ʿimād): /ʕi.maːd/; the final superheavy syllable takes the stress
entries.notes: Today's EYE-mad reads it as English. ʿayn dropped (guide).

entries.name: Heidi
entries.source: Wiktionary, Heidi: English /ˈhaɪdi/, German /ˈhaɪ̯di/

entries.name: Consuelo
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Consuelo: /konˈswelo/; today's kɑnswˈɛlO keeps the stressed SWE
entries.notes: Spanish close e is rendered 'eh' as for Daniela (n0005); the unstressed first vowel (kahn/kohn) differs only in quality.

entries.name: Souad
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic سعاد (suʿād): /su.ʕaːd/; final superheavy stress
entries.notes: Maghrebi French spelling: ou = 'oo'. Today's SOH-ad reads ou as 'oh' and stresses the first syllable. ʿayn dropped (guide).

entries.name: Marisa
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Marisa: /məˈɹɪsə/

entries.name: Ewa
entries.source: Wiktionary, Polish Ewa: /ˈɛ.va/
entries.notes: Polish w is v. Today's YOO-uh reads it as English. Polish bearers (wd PL 1692) dominate.

entries.name: Lilly
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Lilly: /ˈlɪli/

entries.name: Miroslav
entries.source: Wiktionary, Czech Miroslav: /ˈmɪroslaf/
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today ends in the 'lot' vowel (-slov); the Czech a is 'ah'. US already right (final devoicing is not marked in English renderings).

entries.name: Stuart
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Stuart: UK /ˈstjuːət/, US /ˈstuːɚt/

entries.name: Nikki
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Nikki: /ˈnɪki/

entries.name: Ester
entries.source: Spanish orthography: Ester ends in r with no accent, so the last syllable is stressed [esˈteɾ]

alternatives.context: Swedish, Finnish, Estonian, Italian and Czech bearers (EH-ster), the same as the word

entries.notes: Also the chemistry word 'ester' (word_freq uncommon), capitalised at the start of a sentence. Spanish bearers (ES 21k plus Latin America) are the largest group and say es-TEHR; that reading is given here. The European EH-ster matches the word.

entries.name: Kara
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Kara: /ˈkɑːɹə/, /ˈkæɹə/, /ˈkɛɹə/; today's US KAIR-uh and GB KAH-ruh are both listed

entries.name: Deniz
entries.source: Wiktionary, Turkish deniz: /deˈniz/
entries.notes: Today's DAY-neez stresses the first syllable; Turkish names take final stress.

entries.name: Wallace
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Wallace: UK /ˈwɒlɪs/, US /ˈwɔləs/, /ˈwɑləs/
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today says WAWL-us with the vowel of 'wall'; British English has the 'lot' vowel. US already right.

entries.name: Benito
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish/Italian Benito: /beˈnito/

entries.name: Sione
entries.source: Tongan/Samoan Sione (John): regular orthography, three syllables, penultimate stress
entries.notes: Today's SHOHN reads it as one English syllable. Final e is a full vowel ('ay', guide table).

entries.name: Levi
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Levi: /ˈliːvaɪ/

entries.name: Elsie
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Elsie: /ˈɛlsi/

entries.name: Jiří
entries.source: Wiktionary, Czech Jiří: /ˈjɪr̝iː/; English renders ř as 'rzh' (Dvořák /ˈdvɔːrʒɑːk/)
entries.notes: Czech j is the y sound; ř has no English match, so it becomes 'rzh'. Today's JEER-ee reads j as English j and drops the zh.

entries.name: Parker
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Parker: /ˈpɑːkə/, US /ˈpɑɹkɚ/

entries.name: Maurizio
entries.source: Wiktionary, Italian Maurizio: /mauˈrit.tsjo/
entries.notes: Today's maw-RIZ-ee-oh reads au as 'aw' and z as English z; Italian z here is ts and i is 'ee'.

entries.name: Toshio
entries.source: Japanese としお (to-shi-o); English stresses Japanese names on the penultimate (guide); today's tOʃˈiO matches

entries.name: Graciela
entries.source: Spanish orthography: Graciela [ɡɾaˈsjela], penultimate stress
entries.notes: Today's GRAY-see-el-uh stresses the first syllable and reads a as 'ay'. Close e rendered 'eh' as for Daniela (n0005).

entries.name: Sonam
entries.source: Hindi सोनम (sonam): long o, schwa; Tibetan བསོད་ནམས (bsod nams) [sø̃̀nam], also SOH-
entries.notes: Indian (Sonam Kapoor) and Tibetan/Bhutanese bearers both say a long 'oh'; today's SAH-num uses 'ah'.

entries.name: Chioma
entries.source: Igbo Chioma: regular orthography, ch = [tʃ]
entries.notes: Today's kee-OH-muh reads ch as k; Igbo ch is English ch. Igbo is tonal; the second-syllable stress is the usual Nigerian English one.

entries.name: Obinna
entries.source: Igbo Obinna: regular orthography, plain i is [i] (dotted ị would be [ɪ]); bi + syllabic n + na
entries.notes: Today's oh-BIN-uh uses the short 'bit' vowel; Igbo i without a dot is 'ee'.

entries.name: Nizar
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic نزار (nizār): /ni.zaːr/; final superheavy stress
entries.notes: Today's NY-zar reads the i as 'eye' and stresses it.

entries.name: Soraya
entries.source: Spanish Soraya [soˈɾaʝa]; French [sɔʁaja]
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today has the 'lot' vowel (so-ROY-uh); Spanish and French bearers say 'ah'. US already right.

entries.name: Lia
entries.source: Wiktionary, Italian Lia: /ˈli.a/; today's lˈiə matches

entries.name: Siva
entries.source: Tamil சிவா (Civā), the Tamil spelling of Shiva: Tamil speakers say s or sh; today's sˈivə matches
entries.notes: Same shape as Shiva (n0010, already correct).

entries.name: Binod
entries.source: Eastern spelling of Vinod विनोद: long o takes the stress (as Vinod, n0002)
entries.notes: Today's BY-nud reads the i as 'eye' and loses the long o.

entries.name: Naved
entries.source: Urdu نوید (navīd), spelled Naved for the [eː] pronunciation; the long e takes the stress
entries.notes: Today's NAYVD is one syllable; the name has two, stressed on the second. ʋ → v.

entries.name: Maja
entries.source: Wiktionary, Polish Maja: /ˈma.ja/
entries.notes: j is the y sound in every bearer language; today's MY-uh reads aj as 'eye'.

entries.name: Myriam
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Myriam: /mi.ʁjam/
entries.notes: FR register 99.5k dominates (anglo_share 0.04). French names take final stress in English; French [a] as for Jacques (US ɑ, GB a). Today's MIRR-ee-um is the English Miriam.

entries.name: Laurence
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Laurence: /lɔ.ʁɑ̃s/

alternatives.context: English bearers, mostly men (Laurence Olivier, Laurence Fishburne): today's reading

entries.notes: Bearer choice (review), as for Laurent (n0006): FR register 174.8k (women) plus Belgium, Switzerland and Quebec against about 50k English bearers. Nasal ɑ̃ → 'ahn', final stress. This changes Laurence Olivier and Laurence Sterne in English text.

entries.name: Katie
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Katie: /ˈkeɪti/

entries.name: Katharina
entries.source: Wiktionary, German Katharina: /kataˈʁiːna/
entries.notes: German th is t; today's kath-er-EE-nuh reads it as in 'thin'. German-speaking bearers (DE, AT, CH) dominate.

entries.name: Ines
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Inés: /iˈnes/; French Inès /i.nɛs/
entries.notes: Spanish (ES 64.9k) and French (13.6k) registers write names without accents, so this row carries most Inés and Inès bearers; both stress the last syllable. Today's IN-iss fits no group.

entries.name: Bernhard
entries.source: Wiktionary, German Bernhard: /ˈbɛʁnhaʁt/
entries.notes: Today's BURN-hard uses the 'her' vowel; German e before r is 'eh', and the final d is a t.

entries.name: Pier
entries.source: Italian Pier (short form of Piero: Pier Paolo Pasolini): [pjɛr]
entries.notes: Ordinary word 'pier'. Italian bearers (wd IT 142) say PYEHR, as Pierre (n0001); that reading is given here. Dutch Pier (PEER) matches the word.

entries.name: Chérif
entries.source: French spelling of Arabic Sharīf شريف: Chérif [ʃeʁif]; é is 'ay' (as Cédric, n0008)
entries.notes: Today's SHERR-uf stresses the first syllable and reduces the long ī.

entries.name: Conrad
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Conrad: /ˈkɒnɹæd/, US /ˈkɑnɹæd/

entries.name: Harriet
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Harriet: /ˈhæɹi.ət/
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today says HAIR-ee-ut; British English keeps the 'a' of 'cat' before r (as Sharon, n0004). US today has the merged vowel and is right.

entries.name: Emerson
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Emerson: /ˈɛməsən/, US /ˈɛmɚsən/

entries.name: Veronika
entries.source: Duden/Wiktionary, German Veronika: [veˈroːnika]; Slovene, Norwegian and Swedish also stress the second syllable

alternatives.context: Czech, Slovak and Hungarian bearers (first-syllable stress)

entries.notes: Bearers split three ways; the second-syllable stress of German, Austrian, Slovene and Scandinavian bearers is the largest group. Today's veh-roh-NEE-kuh is the Russian stress.

entries.name: Surya
entries.source: Hindi सूर्य (sūrya): long ū, first-syllable stress; today's sˈʊɹiə keeps the stressed SOOR
entries.notes: Long ū before r is the 'oor' vowel (as Purnima, n0013). Today's only difference is the unstressed -ya said as two syllables (ree-uh).

entries.name: Davide
entries.source: Wiktionary, Italian Davide: /daˈvi.de/; today's dˌʌvˈidˌA matches
entries.notes: Only the unstressed first vowel differs.

entries.name: Haidar
entries.source: Arabic حيدر (ḥaydar): the closed first syllable takes the stress; ay → 'eye' (guide); today's hˈIdˌɑɹ matches
entries.notes: ḥ → h.

entries.name: Alonso
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Alonso: /aˈlonso/
entries.notes: Stressed Spanish o is 'oh' (as Alfonso, n0003); today's uh-LAHN-soh (GB uh-LON-so) is an English spelling reading.

entries.name: Darío
entries.source: Wikipedia, Rubén Darío: Spanish [ruˈβen daˈɾi.o]; the written accent marks the stress
entries.notes: Today's DAIR-ee-oh stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Pilar
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Pilar: /piˈlaɾ/
entries.notes: Today's PY-lur reads it as English. Spanish bearers (ES 123k) dominate.

entries.name: Nigel
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Nigel: /ˈnaɪdʒəl/

entries.name: Zoe
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Zoe: /ˈzəʊi/, US /ˈzoʊi/

entries.name: Muhammed
entries.source: Turkish Muhammed [muˈhamːed]; Arabic stressed a is 'ah' (as Mohamed, n0001)
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today says the 'lot' vowel (mu-HOM-ed); bearers say 'ah'. US already right.

entries.name: Shuhua
entries.source: Pinyin Shūhuá 淑华: sh → sh, h [x] → h; guide convention for two-syllable Chinese given names: primary on the last syllable
entries.notes: Today's SHOO-hwah stresses the first syllable; tones dropped.

entries.name: Étienne
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Étienne: /e.tjɛn/
entries.notes: Same reading as Etienne (n0013): é is 'ay' and French names take final stress. Today's ET-ee-en stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Mokhtar
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic مختار (muḵtār): /mux.taːr/; Maghrebi Mokhtar; final superheavy stress
entries.notes: kh → k (guide). Today's MOCK-ter stresses the first syllable and reduces the long ā. Bearers are mostly Maghrebi (Tunisia, Algeria).

entries.name: Simona
entries.source: Wiktionary, Italian Simona: /siˈmo.na/; today's sɪmˈOnə matches
entries.notes: Only the unstressed first vowel differs.

entries.name: Francine
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Francine: /fʁɑ̃.sin/; today's fɹænsˈin keeps the stressed SEEN
entries.notes: French (FR 75k) and English (US 36k) bearers both stress -SEEN; only the unstressed first vowel differs (as Martine, Claudine).

entries.name: Magda
entries.source: Wiktionary, Polish Magda: /ˈmaɡ.da/
entries.notes: Today's MAG-duh uses the 'cat' vowel; every bearer group has an open back vowel.

entries.name: Zubair
entries.source: Urdu زبیر (Zubair) [zʊˈbɛːr]; today's zʌbˈɛɹ keeps the stressed BAIR
entries.notes: Pakistani and British Pakistani bearers dominate. Only the unstressed first vowel differs.

entries.name: Bogdan
entries.source: Wiktionary, Polish Bogdan: /ˈbɔɡ.dan/; today's bˈɑɡdən (GB bˈɒɡdən) keeps the stressed BOG
entries.notes: Polish bearers (wd PL 466, Norwegian and UK registers) are the largest group. US ɑ is the American 'lot' vowel; only the unstressed second vowel differs.

entries.name: Nicolae
entries.source: Wiktionary, Romanian Nicolae: /ni.koˈla.e/
entries.notes: Four syllables with the stress on la; today's NIK-oh-lye merges ae into 'eye'. Final e → 'ay' (guide table).

entries.name: Ira
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Ira: /ˈaɪɹə/

alternatives.context: Russian, German and Latvian bearers (EE-rah, often short for Irina)

entries.notes: US register (43.8k) is by far the largest documented group.

entries.name: Wojciech
entries.source: Wiktionary, Polish Wojciech: /ˈvɔj.t͡ɕɛx/
entries.notes: Polish w is v; ć is ch; final ch [x] → k (as German ch, guide). Today's WOY-check has an English w.

entries.name: Roberta
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Roberta: /ɹəˈbɜːtə/

entries.name: Pema
entries.source: Tibetan པདྨ (padma): Lhasa [pɛ́ma], 'pe-ma'
entries.notes: Today's PEE-muh lengthens the e; the Tibetan e is 'eh'. Tone dropped.

entries.name: Javed
entries.source: Wikipedia, Javed Akhtar: Hindustani [dʒaːˈʋeːd ˈəxt̪ər]
entries.notes: Today's JAYVD is one syllable; two syllables with the stress on the long e. ʋ → v.

entries.name: Ajmal
entries.source: Urdu اجمل (ajmal): short a [ə] in both syllables; the closed first syllable takes the stress
entries.notes: Today's AYJ-mul reads a as 'ay'. Pakistani bearers dominate; Urdu short a is 'uh' (as Amjad, Akhtar).

entries.name: Abdul Monem
entries.source: Arabic عبد المنعم (ʿAbd al-Munʿim), Egyptian ʿAbd el-Monʿem; Abdul as already right (n0001); Monem [ˈmonʕem] keeps today's stressed MOH
entries.notes: Today's æbdˈul mˈOnəm matches: each word has the right stressed syllable; only the unstressed e is reduced. ʿayn dropped.

entries.name: Micheal
entries.source: Variant spelling of Michael /ˈmaɪkəl/ (Wiktionary); US register 153.9k

alternatives.context: Irish bearers (Mícheál written without the fadas, MEE-hawl)

entries.name: Diogo
entries.source: Wiktionary, Portuguese Diogo: /diˈo.ɡu/; final unstressed o is [u]
entries.notes: Today's dee-OH-goh has the Spanish ending; Portuguese final o is 'oo' (as Paulo, Thiago).

entries.name: Nadir
entries.source: Turkish Nadir [naːˈdiɾ] (final stress); French Nadir [na.diʁ]; Arabic نادر (nādir)
entries.notes: Treated as a name, not protected: the word 'nadir' is rare (word_freq rare) and almost always lowercase mid-sentence ('reached its nadir'), while the capitalised spelling is mostly the name. French (FR 5.5k, mostly Algerian), Spanish, Turkish and Azerbaijani bearers stress the last syllable; Arabic speakers NAH-dir.
entries.word_check: gold has 'nadir'; kept: 'nadir' (the lowest point) is used mid-sentence ('the nadir of'); sentence-initial use is rare

entries.name: Yacine
entries.source: French spelling of Yāsīn ياسين: Yacine [ja.sin], final stress; same reading as Yasin (n0011)
entries.notes: Today's yah-CHEE-nee reads it as Italian. French c before i is s and the final e is silent.

entries.name: Jigme
entries.source: Wikipedia, Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuck: English /ˈdʒɪɡ.miː .../
entries.notes: Today's ʤˈɪɡmi matches.

entries.name: Fateh
entries.source: Punjabi ਫ਼ਤਿਹ / Urdu فتح (fatḥ), not Arabic فاتح (fātiḥ): Hindustani a + h → [ɛ] gives fə-tɛ(h); no IPA source found; a name site gives Fuh-TEH for the compound Fatehveer
entries.notes: Registers point to Punjabi Sikh families (CA 1,161, US 557, GB 456), whose first vowel is the schwa ('uh'), not today's 'ah'; the stress is unsourced (candidate: second syllable). Algerian bearers spell Arabic Fātiḥ this way too.

entries.name: Islam
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic إسلام (ʾislām): /ʔis.laːm/; final superheavy stress
entries.notes: In English text 'Islam' is overwhelmingly the religion (GB ˈɪzlɑːm, today's British reading). The given name (Egyptian, Chechen, Kazakh bearers: Islam Makhachev) is iss-LAHM; that reading is given here. US today already says it.

entries.name: Philipp
entries.source: Wiktionary, German Philipp: /ˈfiːlɪp/
entries.notes: The double-p spelling is German (wd DE 1100, AT, CH); German bearers say a long 'ee'. Today's FIL-ip is the English Philip.

entries.name: Faye
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Faye: /feɪ/

entries.name: Sani
entries.source: Hausa Sani (from Arabic Thānī 'second'): long ā
entries.notes: Today's SAN-ee uses the 'cat' vowel. Nigerian bearers (wd NG 19; Sani Abacha) dominate. Hausa is tonal; first-syllable stress as Nigerian English says it.

entries.name: Taiwo
entries.source: Yoruba Táíwò (first-born twin): a-i is said as English 'eye' in Nigerian English; today's tˈIwO matches
entries.notes: Tone dropped.

entries.name: Serdar
entries.source: Turkish Serdar: final stress (as Orhan, Deniz); e before r is 'eh'
entries.notes: Today's SUR-dar uses the 'her' vowel and stresses the first syllable (as Sardar, n0002).

entries.name: Debbie
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Debbie: /ˈdɛbi/

entries.name: Leticia
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Leticia: /leˈtiθja/, Latin America /leˈtisja/

alternatives.context: some US bearers (luh-TISH-uh, today's US reading)

entries.notes: US-only fix: Spanish-speaking bearers (ES 22k, Mexico, Argentina, much of the US register) say TEE with s; British today already says it. US today's luh-TISH-uh.

entries.name: Daouda
entries.source: French spelling of Dāwūd (David); the Gambian spelling Dawda shows the two-syllable [dawda]; no IPA or pronunciation source found
entries.notes: Today's DOW-duh has the right sounds. French-spelled West African names took final stress in earlier batches (Mamadou, Oumar, Ousmane), which would give dow-DAH, but the Mande and Wolof languages use tone, not stress, and no source settles it.

entries.name: Joao
entries.source: Wiktionary, Portuguese João: /ʒuˈɐ̃w̃/; same name without the tilde
entries.notes: Same reading as João (n0001): nasal -ão → 'ow' per the guide. Today's JOH-oh reads it as English.

entries.name: Marcello
entries.source: Wikipedia, Marcello Mastroianni: Italian [marˈtʃɛllo mastroˈjanni]
entries.notes: Italian c before e is ch; today's mar-SEL-oh is the Spanish/Portuguese Marcelo.

entries.name: Annette
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Annette: /əˈnɛt/
entries.notes: French a-NET and German a-NET-eh share the stressed syllable.

entries.name: Jayden
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Jayden: /ˈdʒeɪdən/

entries.name: Lila
entries.source: Wiktionary Lila: German /ˈliːla/, Finnish /ˈli(ː)lɑ/, Tagalog /ˈlila/ (no English IPA); today's CMUdict LEE-luh
entries.notes: LEE-luh matches the French (FR 19,485), Spanish, Greek and many English-speaking bearers; LYE-luh is a common US alternative.

entries.name: Auguste
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Auguste: /o.ɡyst/
entries.notes: French ü has no English match: 'oo' (guide). Today's AW-gust is the month August; this entry only matches the spelling with final e.

entries.name: April
entries.source: Wiktionary, English April: /ˈeɪ.pɹɪl/, /ˈeɪ.pɹəl/; today's gold reading
entries.notes: Also the month, said the same way.

entries.name: Theodor
entries.source: German Theodor [ˈteːodoːɐ̯] (Duden); Norwegian and Swedish Theodor [ˈteːʊdɔr]: th is t, first-syllable stress
entries.notes: NO register 5,460 and wd DE 1,067, SE 201 dominate; today's THEE-uh-der is English Theodore. Wiktionary's German section gives audio but no IPA.

entries.name: Timur
entries.source: Wikipedia, Timur: English /tɪˈmʊər/; Wiktionary, Russian Тимур [tʲɪˈmur]; Turkish [tiˈmuɾ]: final stress
entries.notes: Today's US TIM-er stresses the first syllable; GB already stressed the last (only the unstressed vowel differs).

entries.name: Chan
entries.source: Korean 찬 [tɕʰan]; Mandarin chán 婵/蟾 [ʈʂʰan]; Khmer, Thai and Burmese Chan also 'chahn': a is 'ah' (as Han, Shan and Chang in earlier batches). Forebears 2014, forename Chan: China 265k, Thailand 171k, Myanmar 158k, Cambodia 147k, Singapore 33k, US 11k

alternatives.context: established English reading of the Cantonese surname Chan 陳 (Jackie Chan); natively [tsʰɐn]

entries.notes: Protect-word: in English text the capitalised spelling is overwhelmingly the Cantonese surname Chan 陳 (Jackie Chan, Priscilla Chan, the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative), whose established English reading is CHAN ('cat' vowel, today's). That surname is not a bearer of this given name, so the name reading must not replace it (guide: 'a spelling that means someone else in English text'). The given-name bearers (Chinese, Thai, Burmese, Khmer, Korean) say CHAHN, recorded in us/gb. Decision to review: the Han and Chang precedents were shipped as corrected despite similar surname collisions.

entries.name: Rolf
entries.source: German Rolf [ʁɔlf]; Wiktionary, English Rolf: /ɹɒlf/; today's ɹˈɔlf / ɹˈɒlf matches

entries.name: Mara
entries.source: Italian Mara [ˈmaːra]; Spanish [ˈmaɾa]; Wiktionary, Portuguese Mara /ˈma.ɾɐ/: today's MAH-ruh matches
entries.notes: Some US bearers say MAR-uh or MAIR-uh; the Spanish, Italian and German bearers say MAH-ruh.

entries.name: József
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hungarian József: [ˈjoːʒɛf]
entries.notes: Hungarian j is y and zs is zh; today's JOSS-if reads it as English.

entries.name: Monalisa
entries.source: Wikipedia, Mona Lisa: English /ˌmoʊnə ˈliːsə/; the name is the painting's title written as one word
entries.notes: Today's mon-uh-LEE-suh puts the 'lot' vowel in Mona (MOH-nuh, as the earlier Mona entry).

entries.name: Husam
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic حسام: /ħu.saːm/; the final long syllable takes the stress (Arabic stress rule)
entries.notes: ḥ → h (guide). Today's HOO-sum stresses the first syllable and reduces the long ā.

entries.name: Donny
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Donny: /ˈdɒni/; today's dˈɑni / dˈɒni

entries.name: Rhea
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Rhea: /ˈɹiː.ə/
entries.notes: Also the word 'rhea' (the bird), the Titaness and the moon of Saturn, all said REE-uh as today. The name reading is the same; nothing to change.

entries.name: Shireen
entries.source: Wiktionary, Persian شیرین: /ʃiː.ˈriːn/; as Shirin (n0012)
entries.notes: South Asian spelling of Shirin; the double e marks the long ī. Today's shy-REEN reads the first i as 'eye'.

entries.name: Maximiliano
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Maximiliano: /maɡsimiˈljano/
entries.notes: Spanish a is 'ah'; i before a is the glide y. Today's US mak-suh-mee-lee-AH-noh uses the 'cat' vowel and adds a syllable; GB's 'lot' vowel in the stressed syllable is the bigger miss.

entries.name: Thelma
entries.source: English Thelma /ˈθɛlmə/ (CMUdict, today)

entries.name: Lucky
entries.notes: Ordinary word 'lucky'. The name is said like the word; nothing to change.

entries.name: Cường
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese cường: [kɨəŋ˨˩] (Hà Nội, Saigon), [kɨəŋ˦˩] (Huế); ươ as Phương and Hương in earlier batches
entries.notes: Today's KWAWNG reads ư as w. Tone dropped.

entries.name: Thúy
entries.source: Vietnamese thúy/thuý [tʰwi˧˦]; as Thủy (n0010, Wiktionary thuỷ: Hà Nội [tʰwi˧˩]) and Thùy (n0013)
entries.notes: Vietnamese th is an aspirated t; uy is 'wee'. Today's TOO drops the y. Tone dropped.

entries.name: Trường
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese trường: Saigon [ʈɨəŋ˨˩], Huế [ʈɨəŋ˦˩], Hà Nội [t͡ɕɨəŋ˨˩]; tr as Trang, ươ as Phương in earlier batches
entries.notes: Today's TRAWNG reads ư as w. Southern and most overseas bearers have a retroflex t, heard in English as 'tr'. Tone dropped.

entries.name: Tông
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese tông: [təwŋ͡m˧˧] (all regions); ô before ng as Hồng (n0007)
entries.notes: Vietnamese ô before ng is a closing 'oh' [əw]; today's TAWNG opens it.

entries.name: Reinaldo
entries.source: Spanish Reinaldo [rejˈnaldo]: ei is 'ay', penultimate stress (regular orthography; as Rinaldo/Reynaldo); Forebears 2014: Brazil 154k, Colombia 50k, Cuba 43k, Venezuela 38k, Argentina 18k, Paraguay 14k, Mozambique 14k, Chile 12k, US 9k, Honduras 6k

alternatives.context: Brazilian bearers (wd BR 80): initial r is h, l before a consonant is w

entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today says the 'lot' vowel (ray-NOL-doh); US is right. Forebears confirms the Spanish-speaking total (about 220k across Colombia, Cuba, Venezuela, Argentina, Paraguay, Chile, the US, Honduras and others) exceeds the Portuguese one (Brazil 154k, Mozambique 14k), though Brazil is the largest single country.

entries.name: Ezequiel
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Ezequiel: /eθeˈkjel/; Latin American seseo gives [eseˈkjel]
entries.notes: Argentina (wd AR 157) and Latin America say s for z; e in an open syllable is 'ay' (guide). Today's ih-ZEK-weel reads it as English.

entries.name: Celine
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Celine: /səˈliːn/; French Céline [se.lin]
entries.notes: Today's suh-LEEN differs from French say-LEEN only in the unstressed vowel.

entries.name: Kazimierz
entries.source: Wiktionary, Polish Kazimierz: /kaˈʑi.mjɛʂ/
entries.notes: Polish zi [ʑ] is nearest English zh; final rz is devoiced to sh; penultimate stress. Today's KAZ-im-eerz is a spelling reading.

entries.name: Lucía
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Lucía: /luˈθia/, Latin America /luˈsia/
entries.notes: The accent marks stress on í. Today's LOO-shuh is the English Lucia; the Latin American bearers (wd PE, AR, UY, MX) say s.

entries.name: Landry
entries.region: Madagascar, DR Congo, Central African Republic, Burundi, Cameroon, Gabon, France
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Landry: [lɑ̃.dʁi]; Forebears 2014, forename Landry: Madagascar 21.8k, DR Congo 11.7k, Central African Republic 10.4k, Burundi 8.7k, Cameroon 6.8k, Gabon 6.2k, Congo 4.5k, Côte d'Ivoire 4.4k, Benin 3.1k, Togo 2.6k against US 1.1k

alternatives.context: English: US given-name bearers (Landry Fields; US 11,185 births, mostly since 2010) and the Louisiana/Acadian surname (Tom Landry, Jeff Landry); today's reading

entries.notes: Francophone African bearers far outnumber the US ones, so the name reading is French lahn-DREE (final stress as for French names in English; GB unstressed nasal as Henri, n0004). But in English text the spelling is mostly the American surname (Tom Landry, Governor Jeff Landry) and US bearers, read LAN-dree as today, so it is protected rather than corrected. Today's reading stays.

entries.name: Henk
entries.source: Dutch Henk [ɦɛŋk] (short for Hendrik); Dutch h → English h; today's hˈɛŋk matches

entries.name: Florent
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Florent: /flɔ.ʁɑ̃/
entries.notes: French names take final stress in English; nasal ɑ̃ → 'ahn' and the t is silent (as Laurent, n0006). Today's FLOR-unt is a spelling reading.

entries.name: Fodé
entries.source: French spelling of a West African (Mandinka, Susu) name: é is [e]; final stress as for other French-spelled West African names (Abdoulaye, Souleymane)
entries.notes: Today's FOHD drops the final é. No source gives the name's stress; the French-convention final stress follows earlier batches.

entries.name: Josh
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Josh: /ˈd͡ʒɒʃ/, /ˈd͡ʒɑʃ/
entries.notes: Also the word 'josh' (to tease). The name is said like the word, as today.

entries.name: Mohannad
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic مهند: /mu.han.nad/; the heavy penultimate han takes the stress (Arabic stress rule)
entries.notes: Geminate nn is single in English (guide). The Mo- spelling follows Mohamed (n0001, mOhˈɑmɛd). Today's MOH-han-ad stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Rigoberto
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Rigoberto: /riɡoˈbeɾto/; today's ɹˌiɡObˈɛɹtO matches

entries.name: Paweł
entries.source: Wiktionary, Polish Paweł: /ˈpa.vɛw/
entries.notes: Polish w is v and ł is w; penultimate stress. Today's guess PAWD is garbled.

entries.name: Abd al-Hakim
entries.source: Arabic عبد الحكيم ʿAbd al-Ḥakīm: stress on the long -kīm; ʿAbd as in Abd al-Karīm (n0004)
entries.notes: ʿayn dropped and ḥ → h (guide). Today's GB AL-hak-im stresses the article; US differs from this only in Abd's vowel.

entries.name: Robby
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Robby: rhyme -ɒbi; today's ɹˈɑbi / ɹˈɒbi

entries.name: Anastasia
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Anastasia: /æn.əˈsteɪ.ʒə/ (first of several); today's ænəstˈAʒə

alternatives.context: Russian, Greek, Spanish and other European bearers (ah-nuh-STAH-see-uh)

entries.name: Curtis
