entries.name: Kwame
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Kwame: /ˈkwɑː.meɪ/
entries.notes: Akan day name (Saturday-born boy). Today's KWAYM drops the final vowel.

entries.name: Romesh
entries.source: Bengali রমেশ (Romesh, the Bengali form of Ramesh): first-syllable stress, as Bengali words are stressed initially; no source transcription for this spelling
entries.notes: Today's ROHMSH loses the second vowel. The stress is the uncertain part: Hindi Ramesh is ruh-MESH (n0001), but this spelling is Bengali and Sri Lankan (Romesh Chunder Dutt, Romesh Ranganathan), whose languages stress the first syllable. No source gives either bearer's own reading.

entries.name: Marguerite
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Marguerite: /ˌmɑː(ɹ)ɡəˈɹiːt/; French /maʁ.ɡə.ʁit/
entries.notes: Also the word 'marguerite' (the daisy). The name reading drops the y-glide of today's US mar-gyuh-REET; GB today already matches.

entries.name: Henriette
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Henriette: /ɑ̃.ʁjɛt/; Forebears 2014: DR Congo 211k, Cameroon 24k, France 21k, Benin 16k, Germany 13k, Denmark 11k, Madagascar 11k, Netherlands 9k

alternatives.context: Norwegian, Danish, German and Dutch bearers (NO register 5,017)

entries.notes: French-speaking bearers (France, DR Congo, Cameroon, Benin, Madagascar) far outnumber the Germanic ones. French h is silent and nasal ɑ̃ → 'ahn', as Henri (n0004). Today's hen-ree-ET mixes the two.

entries.name: Bushra
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic بشرى: /buʃ.raː/; first-syllable stress; today's bˈʊʃɹə matches

entries.name: Allison
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Allison: /ˈælɪsən/

entries.name: Carson

entries.name: Justo
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish justo: /ˈxusto/
entries.notes: Spanish j [x] → h (guide). Today's JUST-oh reads it as English.

entries.name: Harrison
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Harrison: /ˈhæ.ɹɪ.sən/, /ˈhɛɹ.ɪ.sn̩/

entries.name: Shama
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi शमा: /ʃə.mɑː/ (from Persian/Arabic šamʕ, 'candle'); Hindustani weight rule: the only heavy syllable is the long final ā, which takes the stress, as Sana (n0015) and Saba (n0011). Forebears 2014: India 173k, Pakistan 110k, Sudan 18k

alternatives.context: Arabic Shāma (Moroccan bearers; also today's reading)

entries.notes: Today's SHAH-muh stresses the short first syllable and lengthens it. Indian and Pakistani bearers dominate (Forebears). Reviewer change: the researcher's SHUM-uh followed Latha, a Dravidian name with initial stress; Shama is a Hindi/Urdu name of the Sana and Saba shape, so the final long ā is stressed.

entries.name: Bina
entries.source: Hindi बीना (bīnā): long ī, stress on the long first syllable; today's bˈinə matches; Hebrew Bina is also BEE-nah

entries.name: Eliza

entries.name: Jianhong

entries.name: Guorong
entries.source: Pinyin guóróng 国荣: guo as Guohua (n0004), rong as Rong (n0004); final primary stress (guide convention)
entries.notes: Today's GOR-awng drops the w glide and stresses the first syllable. Pinyin r [ʐ] → English r, as earlier. Tones dropped.

entries.name: Yùfèng
entries.source: Pinyin yùfèng 玉凤: yu as Yulan (n0005), feng as Feng (n0003); final primary stress (guide convention)
entries.notes: Today's YOO-feng uses the 'bed' vowel for -eng [ɤŋ]. Tones dropped.

entries.name: Naresh
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi नरेश: /nə.ɾeːʃ/; stress on the long e; today's nɑɹˈɛʃ differs only in the unstressed vowel (as Ramesh, n0001)

entries.name: Punam
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi पूनम: /puː.nəm/; as Poonam (n0013)
entries.notes: Today's PYOO-num adds a y glide.

entries.name: Manjula
entries.source: Sanskrit मञ्जुला (mañjulā): short a [ə], short u; the heavy closed first syllable takes the stress (Hindustani weight rule; Dravidian languages stress the first syllable, as Lalitha)
entries.notes: Today's mahn-JOO-luh stresses the light second syllable and uses 'ah' for the Indian short a (as Pankaj, Ranjana).

entries.name: Pratap
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi प्रताप: /pɾə.t̪ɑːp/; the long final ā takes the stress (as Prakash, Pradeep)
entries.notes: Today's PRAH-tup puts the long vowel and stress on the short first syllable.

entries.name: Rainer

entries.notes: German ai is 'eye'; today's RAY-ner reads it as English.

entries.name: Abdelkrim
entries.source: Maghrebi form of عبد الكريم ʿAbd al-Karīm (the short a of karīm drops); stress on the long final ī, as Abdelaziz and Abdelkader
entries.notes: Today's AB-del-krim stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Lino
entries.drop_detail: 'lino' (linoleum, lino prints) is everyday British English
entries.source: Wiktionary, Italian Lino: /ˈli.no/
entries.notes: Treated as a name, not protected: the word 'lino' (linoleum) is rare and lowercase, while the capitalised spelling is the name (Lino Ventura). Today's LYE-noh is the floor covering.

entries.name: Mayra
entries.source: Spanish Mayra [ˈmajɾa]: ay is 'eye' (regular orthography)
entries.notes: Mostly Hispanic bearers (US 33,475 births, Mexico, Peru). Today's MAY-ruh reads ay as English.

entries.name: Yohanes
entries.source: Indonesian Yohanes: penultimate stress (regular orthography); today's jOhˈɑnɛs matches

entries.name: Gil
entries.region: Philippines, US, Brazil, Portugal, Mozambique, Angola, Israel, Mexico
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Gil: /ɡɪl/; Spanish /ˈxil/. Forebears 2014, forename Gil: Philippines 51.3k, Mozambique 32.6k, US 25.9k, Angola 16.9k, Brazil 13.5k, Mexico 12.2k, Portugal 9.6k, East Timor 9.1k, Colombia 4.4k, Peru 3.8k, Canada 3.2k, France 3.0k

alternatives.context: English (US, Canada; Gil Scott-Heron, Gil Hodges); today's reading

entries.notes: Conflicting population evidence, so not already-correct: Forebears puts the Portuguese/French 'zheel' bearers (Brazil, Portugal, East Timor, Lusophone Africa, France) and the Philippines (reading of Filipino Gil unverified) ahead of the English group, while Israel (Hebrew 'geel', wd IL 70) is missing from Forebears and the US register is small (4,864 births). The Lusophone African counts look inflated. Needs a decision between English GIL (today's; what English text mostly contains) and a bearer reading.

entries.name: Andrey
entries.source: Wiktionary, Russian Андрей: [ɐnˈdrʲej]
entries.notes: Final stress; ey is 'ay', as Andrej (n0011). Today's AN-dree is English Andre/Andrey.

entries.name: Özlem
entries.source: Wiktionary, Turkish Özlem: /œz.lɛm/; Turkish names stress the last syllable (as Ömer, Zeynep, n0010)
entries.notes: Turkish ö has no English match; unstressed it becomes 'uh' (as Ömer). Today's OZ-lum stresses the first syllable with the 'lot' vowel.

entries.name: Ezra
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Ezra: /ˈɛzɹə/

entries.name: Abdul Qayyum
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic قيوم: /qaj.juːm/; the long ū takes the stress; Abdul as in the earlier Abdul entry

alternatives.context: Urdu-speaking bearers often reduce the first vowel (kuh-YOOM)

entries.notes: q → k (guide); geminate yy is single. Today's KAY-um stresses the first syllable and loses the long ū.

entries.name: Aryan
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi आर्यन: /ɑːɾ.jən/
entries.notes: Also the English word 'Aryan' (Indo-Aryan, Aryan race), always capitalised and said AIR-ee-un as today: never replace. The name of the Indian-heritage bearers (US 8,574, GB 4,346 births) is AHR-yun, given here.

entries.name: Gino
entries.source: Wiktionary, Italian Gino: /ˈd͡ʒi.no/; today's ʤˈinO matches

entries.name: Washington
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Washington: /ˈwɑʃɪŋtən/, /ˈwɔʃɪŋtən/; Portuguese bearers [ˈwɔʃĩtõ]
entries.notes: In English text the spelling is overwhelmingly the US capital, state and George Washington, read as today. The South American given name is borrowed from it; nothing to change.

entries.name: Yaya
entries.source: West African Yaya (Yaya Touré): both a's are 'ah'
entries.notes: Also the word 'yaya' (a nanny or grandmother), uncommon. US today already says YAH-yah; the name reading keeps GB's 'ah' too.

entries.name: Cláudio
entries.source: Wiktionary, Portuguese Cláudio: Brazil /ˈklaw.d͡ʒju/, Portugal /ˈklaw.dju/
entries.notes: Brazil (wd BR 155) dominates; Brazilian d before unstressed i is j. Today's KLAW-dee-oh reads au as 'aw' and final o as 'oh'.

entries.name: Fauzia
entries.source: Arabic فوزية (fawziyya): the heavy ziy syllable takes the stress; Urdu فوزیہ by the Hindustani weight rule (last heavy non-final syllable) and Swahili penultimate stress agree
entries.notes: Today's FAW-zee-uh stresses the first syllable; the 'aw' of Urdu au is kept.

entries.name: Yawen
entries.source: Pinyin yǎwén 雅雯: ya as Jiayi/Jiahao (n0003), wen as Wenbin (n0002); final primary stress (guide convention)
entries.notes: Today's YAW-un reads it as one English syllable plus schwa. Tones dropped.

entries.name: Meiyun
entries.source: Pinyin měiyún 美云: mei as Mei (n0003), yun as Yun (n0002); final stress; today's mAjˈun matches

entries.name: Troy
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Troy: /tɹɔɪ/
entries.notes: Also the ancient city and troy weight, said the same way; nothing to change.

entries.name: Jonah
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Jonah: /ˈd͡ʒoʊnə/, /ˈd͡ʒəʊnə/

entries.name: Zehra
entries.source: Wiktionary, Turkish Zehra: /zehˈɾaː/, [zɛhˈɾɑː]
entries.notes: Final stress and the h is said (as Zahra, n0008). Today's ZAY-ruh drops the h and stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Riccardo
entries.source: Wiktionary, Italian Riccardo: /rikˈkar.do/; today's ɹɪkˈɑɹdO matches (geminate single)

entries.name: Afonso
entries.source: Wiktionary, Portuguese Afonso: /aˈfõ.su/ (Brazil), /ɐˈfõ.su/ (Portugal)
entries.notes: Nasal õ → 'ohn' (English speakers keep an n before s); final o is 'oo'. Today's uh-FAHN-soh uses the 'ah' vowel.

entries.name: Josie
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Josie: rhymes -əʊzi; today's ʤˈOzi

entries.name: Adrien
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Adrien: /a.dʁi.jɛ̃/
entries.notes: French names take final stress in English; nasal ɛ̃ → 'an' (as Julien, n0008). Today's AY-dree-un is English Adrian.

entries.name: Fanta
entries.source: Mandinka Fanta: a is 'ah'; Wiktionary, English Fanta (the drink): /ˈfæn.tə/ first
entries.notes: Also the soft drink Fanta, said FAN-tuh in English: never replace. The West African name (FR 3,420 births) is FAHN-tuh: US today already says it, GB today uses the 'lot' vowel.

entries.name: Jakub
entries.region: Poland, Czechia, Slovakia, UK, Ireland, Norway
entries.source: Wiktionary, Polish Jakub: /ˈja.kup/; Czech and Slovak [ˈjakup]
entries.notes: Polish j is y; final b is devoiced to p. Today's JACK-ub reads it as English Jacob.

entries.name: Zbigniew
entries.source: Wiktionary, Polish Zbigniew: /ˈzbi.ɡɲɛf/
entries.notes: ni [ɲ] → ny (guide), final w is f. Today's ZBIG-noo drops the last syllable.

entries.name: Adrianus
entries.source: Dutch Adrianus (Latin form of Adriaan): open a is long [aː], stress on the penultimate as in Latin
entries.notes: Today's ay-dree-AN-is reads the a's as English 'ay' and 'cat'.

entries.name: Colette
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Colette: /kɔ.lɛt/; English /kɒˈlɛt/; today's kəlˈɛt differs only in the unstressed vowel

entries.name: Władysław
entries.source: Wiktionary, Polish Władysław: /vwaˈdɘ.swaf/
entries.notes: Polish w is v, ł is w, final w is f; Polish y is the English 'ih' vowel. Today's guess WAY-dis-kaw is garbled.

entries.name: Horst
entries.source: Wiktionary, German Horst: /hɔʁst/, [hɔɐ̯st]; today's hˈɔɹst / hˈɔːst matches
entries.notes: Treated as a name: the word 'horst' (geology) is rare and technical; the name reading is the same anyway.

entries.name: Hakan
entries.source: Wiktionary, Turkish Hakan: /haːˈkan/
entries.notes: Today's HAY-kun stresses the first syllable with 'ay'. Swedish Håkan is a different spelling.

entries.name: Vittorio
entries.source: Wiktionary, Italian Vittorio: /vitˈtɔ.rjo/; today's vitˈɔɹiO matches

entries.name: Reda
entries.source: Arabic رضا (riḍā): Wiktionary /ri.dˤan/, /radˤ.dˤaː/; with no heavy non-final syllable the stress is on the first (as Huda); Maghrebi and French spelling Reda/Réda; Wikipedia, Reda Kateb: French [ʁeda]. Forebears 2014, forename Reda: Ethiopia 152k, Egypt 150k, Morocco 70k, Syria 33k, Iraq 25k, Algeria 19k, Libya 13k

alternatives.context: French speakers (Réda) and the Persian cognate Reza stress the last syllable

entries.notes: Today's RAY-duh fits the Arabic first-syllable stress of the Egyptian, Levantine and Iraqi bearers, which Forebears puts ahead of the Maghrebi and French ones (re-DAH, final stress); the Ethiopian Reda (ረዳ, a separate name) is a large group whose stress is unsourced. No source covers this spelling's stress.

entries.name: Efraín
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Efraín: /efɾaˈin/
entries.notes: The accent marks a separate stressed í. Today's ih-FRAYN makes 'ai' one syllable.

entries.name: Sarmad
entries.source: Urdu/Arabic سرمد sarmad: two heavy syllables; Arabic stresses the penultimate heavy sar, and the Hindustani weight rule (final syllable excluded) agrees

entries.name: Gisela
entries.source: German Gisela [ɡiˈzeːla] (Duden): s before a vowel is z, e is long; Wiktionary, Spanish Gisela: /xiˈsela/; Forebears 2014: Germany 601k, Argentina 34k, Mexico 31k, Cuba 23k, Venezuela 20k, US 17k, Austria 10k, Spain 9k
entries.notes: German bearers clearly outnumber the Spanish-speaking ones (Forebears: Germany and Austria about 610k against about 130k across Argentina, Mexico, Cuba, Venezuela, the US and Spain). Both say the e stressed; today's GEE-zuh-luh stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Yunus
entries.region: Turkey, UK, France, Bangladesh, Indonesia, Malaysia
entries.source: Wiktionary, Indonesian Yunus: /ˈjunus/; Turkish Yunus: /juˈnus/, /juːnus/; Arabic يونس yūnus stresses the long ū; Forebears 2014: Turkey 162k, Indonesia 93k, India 78k, Nigeria 12k, Bangladesh 10k, Egypt 5k, Malaysia 4k
entries.notes: Turkey is the largest single country (Forebears 162k), but the bearers who say YOO-nus (Indonesia, India, Bangladesh, Malaysia, Egypt and others: about 200k) outnumber it, and Wiktionary also gives a Turkish variant without final stress.

entries.name: Rahma
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic رحمة: /raħ.ma/
entries.notes: ḥ → h and is said (guide); today's RAH-muh drops it, and GB today uses the 'lot' vowel.

entries.name: Becky
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Becky: /ˈbɛki/

entries.name: Déchāng
entries.source: Pinyin déchāng 德昌: de as De (n0007), chang as Chang (n0009); final primary stress (guide convention)
entries.notes: Today's DECH-ang reads e as 'bed' and a as 'cat'. Tones dropped.

entries.name: Héng
entries.source: Pinyin héng 恒: -eng [ɤŋ] as Feng, Peng and Cheng in earlier batches
entries.notes: Today's HENG uses the 'bed' vowel. Tone dropped.

entries.name: Junxian
entries.source: Pinyin jùnxián 俊贤: jun as Jùnjié (n0003), xian as Xian (n0007); final primary stress (guide convention)
entries.notes: Pinyin x is sh (guide). Today's JUNK-see-un reads it as English. Tones dropped.

entries.name: Zhide
entries.source: Pinyin zhìdé 志德: zhi as Zhiming (n0003), de as De (n0007); final primary stress (guide convention)
entries.notes: Today's ZHEED reads it as one English syllable. Tones dropped.

entries.name: Ramona
entries.source: Wiktionary: English Ramona /ɹəˈmoʊnə/, Spanish /raˈmona/, German /ʁaˈmoːna/; today's ɹəmˈOnə

entries.name: Patrícia
entries.source: Wiktionary, Portuguese Patrícia: /paˈtɾi.sjɐ/ (Brazil), /pɐˈtɾi.sjɐ/ (Portugal)
entries.notes: The accent marks a stressed 'ee'; ci is 'sy'. Today's puh-TRISH-uh is English Patricia.

entries.name: Marija
entries.region: Croatia, Serbia, Bosnia, North Macedonia, Latvia, Montenegro
entries.source: Wiktionary, Serbo-Croatian Marija: /mà.ri.ja/ (Марија /mǎrija/); Macedonian Марија [ˈmaɾi(j)a]; Latvian stress is always initial. Forebears 2014, forename Marija: Croatia 103k, Slovenia 69k, Serbia 54k, Lithuania 31k, Latvia 28k, Bosnia 15k, North Macedonia 12.5k, Montenegro 4.7k

alternatives.context: Slovene, Lithuanian and Maltese bearers (second-syllable stress; today's reading)

entries.notes: Reversed from already-correct: the wd SI 327 lead is a Wikidata artefact. By Forebears the first-syllable group (Croatian, Serbian, Bosnian, Montenegrin, Macedonian, Latvian: about 220k) is roughly twice the second-syllable group (Slovene, Lithuanian, Maltese: about 100k). Serbo-Croatian has a rising accent on the first syllable, which some listeners hear as prominence on the second; Macedonian and Latvian are unambiguous.

entries.name: Aly
entries.source: Egyptian romanisation of علي ʿAlī: stress on the long final ī; as Ali (n0002); Forebears 2014: Egypt 95k, Guinea 58k, Mali 57k, Saudi Arabia 48k, Senegal 38k, Mauritania 20k, Burkina Faso 20k

alternatives.context: US and Canadian women's name, short for Alison (Aly Raisman)

entries.notes: Francophone West African bearers (Guinea, Mali, Senegal, Mauritania, Burkina Faso: about 190k, French final stress) and the Ali precedent agree on ah-LEE; today's AY-lee matches no group.

entries.name: Layla
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Layla: /ˈleɪlə/

entries.name: Aubrey
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Aubrey: /ˈɔːbɹi/

entries.name: Djamel
entries.source: Algerian form of جمال jamāl, French spelling Dj- = j: stress on the long second syllable, as Jamal (n0003)
entries.notes: Algerian ā next to m is fronted toward 'e', hence the -el spelling. Today's JAM-ul stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Sammi
entries.source: English Sammi, as Sammy /ˈsæmi/; today's sˈæmi

entries.name: Leroy
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Leroy: /ˈliːˌɹɔɪ/

entries.name: Siegfried
entries.source: Wiktionary, German Siegfried: /ˈziːk.fʁiːt/
entries.notes: German bearers (wd DE 830, AT 147) dominate; s before a vowel is z, final g and d are devoiced. Today's SEEG-freed is the English reading.

entries.name: Jovan
entries.source: Wiktionary, Serbo-Croatian Jovan: /jǒʋan/ (rising accent on the first syllable); Forebears 2014: Serbia 53k, North Macedonia 13k, Bosnia 7k, US 5k, Philippines 5k, Montenegro 3k
entries.notes: Serbian j is y. Serbian, Macedonian, Bosnian and Montenegrin bearers (about 77k by Forebears) far outnumber the US ones.

entries.name: Kent
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Kent: /kɛnt/
entries.notes: Also the English county; the name (English and Scandinavian) is said the same way. Nothing to change.

entries.name: Bertrand
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Bertrand: /bɛʁ.tʁɑ̃/
entries.notes: France (FR 64,990) dominates; final stress, nasal ɑ̃ → 'ahn', silent d (as Bernard, n0002). Today's BURT-rund is the English reading.

entries.name: Adalberto
entries.source: Spanish Adalberto [aðalˈβeɾto]: penultimate stress, a is 'ah' (regular orthography)
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today puts the 'lot' vowel in both unstressed a's (od-ol-BAIR-toh); US is right.

entries.name: Grant
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Grant: /ɡɹɑːnt/, /ɡɹænt/
entries.notes: Ordinary word 'grant'. The name is said like the word (US 'cat' vowel, British 'ah'), as today.

entries.name: Stéphanie
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Stéphanie: /ste.fa.ni/
entries.notes: French names take final stress in English (as Stéphane, n0009). Today's STEF-uh-nee is English Stephanie; the accented spelling is French (FR 235,995).

entries.name: Béatrice
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Béatrice: /be.a.tʁis/
entries.notes: Final stress; é is 'ay' (as Beatriz, n0007). Today's BEE-uh-tris is English Beatrice.

entries.name: Oskar
entries.source: Wiktionary: German Oskar /ˈɔskaʁ/, Polish /ˈɔs.kar/, Swedish /¹ɔskar/: short open o; British English renders it with the 'lot' vowel, as Oscar /ˈɒskə/ (Wiktionary, read so today, n0002)
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today says ˈɔːskə ('AWS-kuh', the long 'thought' vowel), unlike its own Oscar ˈɒskə and Rolf ɹˈɒlf; the short German/Scandinavian/Polish o is GB 'lot'. US today (ˈɔskəɹ) is right; it differs from OS-kar only in the unstressed vowel.

entries.name: Bertram
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Bertram: /ˈbɜːtɹəm/; German /ˈbɛrtram/. Forebears 2014, forename Bertram: Germany 8.0k, US 6.4k, England 2.1k, Jamaica 1.8k, South Africa 1.2k, Nigeria 1.0k, Austria 0.9k, Bahamas 0.5k, Sri Lanka 0.5k, Canada 0.4k

alternatives.context: German and Danish bearers (Germany, Austria; a popular Danish boys' name in the 2000s)

entries.notes: Reverted from the German BAIR-trahm: the researcher's anglo_share 0.03 is contradicted by Forebears, where the English-reading bearers (US, England, Jamaica, Nigeria, Bahamas, Sri Lanka, Canada, about 13k) at least match the German and Austrian ones (about 9k); the Danish count is unverified and at most makes it a tie. With no clear majority, the established English reading stays (Bertram Wooster, Shakespeare's Bertram).

entries.name: Bela
entries.source: Wikipedia, Bela Lugosi: English /ˈbeɪlə/; Hindi बेला (belā) [beːlaː]; Hungarian Béla [ˈbeːlɒ]
entries.notes: English (Bela Lugosi, Bela Fleck), Indian, Spanish and Hungarian bearers all say 'ay'; today's BEL-uh matches only the Portuguese nickname.

entries.name: Milena
entries.region: Slovenia, Czechia, Italy, Germany, Spain, US
entries.source: Wiktionary: Polish and Italian Milena /miˈlɛ.na/; Portuguese /miˈle.nɐ/

alternatives.context: Czech, Slovak and Serbo-Croatian bearers (first-syllable stress)

entries.notes: Today's mi-LEE-nuh reads e as 'ee'. Most groups (Polish, Italian, Slovene, German, Spanish, Bulgarian, Russian) say LEH.

entries.name: Mateus
entries.source: Wiktionary, Portuguese Mateus: /maˈtews/ (Brazil), /mɐˈtewʃ/ (Portugal); as Matheus (n0012)
entries.notes: The diphthong [ew] has no English match: 'eh' plus 'oo'. Today's muh-TAY-us splits it.

entries.name: Abiola
entries.source: Yoruba Abíọ́lá ('born into wealth', ọlá 'wealth'): ọ is open [ɔ]; tone dropped, English stress on the penultimate (as Babatunde, n0014)
entries.notes: Today's ah-bee-OH-luh uses the closed 'oh'; Yoruba ọ is the open 'aw'.

entries.name: Ebenezer
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Ebenezer: /ɛbəˈnizɚ/, /ɛbəˈniːzə/

entries.name: Adebayo
entries.source: Yoruba Adébáyọ̀ ('the crown meets joy', ayọ̀ 'joy'): e is [e], ọ is open [ɔ]; tone dropped, English stress on the penultimate (as Babatunde, n0014)
entries.notes: Today's ad-uh-BAY-oh reads the a's as 'cat' and 'ay'. Yoruba e in an open syllable is 'ay' (guide).

entries.name: Hadiza
entries.source: Hausa Hadiza (from Arabic Khadīja): long ī takes the stress; Hausa i is 'ee' (regular orthography)
entries.notes: Today's huh-DYE-zuh reads i as 'eye'.

entries.name: Abiodun
entries.source: Yoruba Abíọ́dún ('born at the festival', ọdún 'festival, year'): ọ is open [ɔ]; tone dropped, stress on the final high-tone dún as English speakers place it
entries.notes: Today's ab-ee-oh-DOON uses the 'cat' vowel for the first a and the closed 'oh' for ọ.

entries.name: Graham
entries.region: UK, Scotland, Ireland, Australia, New Zealand, US
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Graham: /ˈɡɹeɪ.əm/, US also /ɡɹæm/
entries.notes: Also the word 'graham' (graham cracker, graham flour), said GRAM in the US. Today's US GRAM and GB GRAY-um are both established readings of the name; nothing to change.

entries.name: Mao
entries.source: Japanese Mao 真央 [ma.o], two morae (Mao Asada); Wiktionary, English Mao: /maʊ̯/

alternatives.context: Chinese 毛/茂 Mao (Mao Zedong), today's reading

entries.notes: In English text the spelling is overwhelmingly Mao Zedong, said MOW as today: never replace. Japanese bearers (wd JP 12) say MAH-oh; that reading is recorded here.

entries.name: Meifang
entries.source: Pinyin měifāng 美芳: mei as Mei (n0003), fang as Fang (n0004); final primary stress (guide convention)
entries.notes: Today's MY-fang reads ei as 'eye' and a as 'cat'. Tones dropped.

entries.name: Huiying
entries.source: Pinyin huìyīng 慧英: hui as Huiling (n0006), ying as Ying (n0002); final primary stress (guide convention)
entries.notes: Today's HY-ying reads ui as 'eye'. Tones dropped.

entries.name: Wellington
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Wellington: /ˈwɛlɪŋtən/; Portuguese /ˈwɛ.lĩ.tõ/
entries.notes: Also the city, the Duke and the boot, said as today. The Brazilian given name is borrowed from it; nothing to change.

entries.name: Samia
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic سامية: /saː.mi.ja/; the long first syllable takes the stress
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today uses the 'lot' vowel (SOM-ee-uh); US is right.

entries.name: Guangyao
entries.source: Pinyin guāngyào 光耀: guang as Guang (n0002), yao as Yao (n0005); final primary stress (guide convention)
entries.notes: Today stresses the first syllable; GB uses the 'lot' vowel. Tones dropped.

entries.name: Pèiyù
entries.source: Pinyin pèiyù 佩玉: pei 'pay', yu as Yu (n0001); final stress; today's pAjˈu matches

entries.name: Yù
entries.source: Pinyin yù: ü → 'yoo' (guide), as Yu (n0001); today's jˈu matches

entries.name: Sofía
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Sofía: /soˈfia/
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today stresses the first syllable (SOH-fee-uh); US is right. As Sofia (n0004).

entries.name: Aleksandra
entries.source: Wiktionary, Polish Aleksandra: /a.lɛkˈsan.dra/; Norwegian /a.lɛkˈsan.dra/; Slovene /alɛ̀ksáːndra/
entries.notes: a is 'ah' (as Aleksandar, n0007). Today's al-uk-SAN-druh is English Alexandra.

entries.name: Belinda
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Belinda: /bəˈlɪndə/

entries.name: Narciso
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Narciso: /naɾˈθiso/ (Latin America [naɾˈsiso])
entries.notes: Spain (ES 4,596) and the Spanish-speaking Americas are the largest group. Today's nar-CHEE-soh is the Italian reading.

entries.name: Jackie
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Jackie: /ˈd͡ʒæki/

entries.name: Paulin
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Paulin: /po.lɛ̃/
entries.notes: French au is 'oh'; final nasal ɛ̃ → 'an' (as Julien, n0008), final stress. Today's PAW-lin is a spelling reading.

entries.name: Gisèle
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Gisèle: /ʒi.zɛl/
entries.notes: French g before i is zh; s between vowels is z; final stress. Today's GISS-ul is a spelling reading.

entries.name: Honoré
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Honoré: /ɔ.nɔ.ʁe/
entries.notes: French h is silent; é is 'ay'; final stress (Honoré de Balzac). Today's ON-er drops the last syllable.

entries.name: Shazia
entries.source: Urdu شازیہ (shāziya): long first ā takes the stress (Hindustani weight rule)
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today uses the 'lot' vowel (SHOZ-ee-uh); US is right.

entries.name: Loïc
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Loïc: /lɔ.ik/
entries.notes: The diaeresis splits o and i into two syllables; final stress. Today's LOH-ik stresses the first.

entries.name: Shahla
entries.source: Wiktionary, Persian شهلا: /ʃah.ˈlaː/, Iran [ʃæɦ.lɒ́ː]
entries.notes: Iranian bearers (wd IR 11) stress the last syllable and say the h. Today's SHAH-luh drops the h and stresses the first.

entries.name: Titus
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Titus: /ˈtaɪtəs/

alternatives.context: Dutch, German, Romanian and Indonesian bearers

entries.name: Sona
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi सोना: /soː.nɑː/; stress on the long first syllable; today's SOH-nuh matches

alternatives.context: Armenian and Azerbaijani bearers (wd AM 5, AZ 4): final stress, 'soh-NAH'

entries.notes: Indian bearers (and the US register, likely Indian-American) keep today's reading; Armenian and Azerbaijani bearers stress the last syllable.

entries.name: Vladimir
entries.source: Wiktionary, Russian Влади́мир: [vɫɐˈdʲimʲɪr]; Wiktionary Vladimir gives only the anglicised UK /ˈvlæ.dɪ.miə(ɹ)/

alternatives.context: Serbian, Croatian and Czech (Vladimír) bearers: first-syllable stress

entries.notes: Population call: Russian-speaking bearers (wd RU 100, plus Belarus, Bulgaria and Estonia's Russian speakers) far outnumber the Serbian, Croatian and Czech ones. Changes Vladimir Putin, Lenin and Nabokov in English text from VLAD-ih-meer to vluh-DEE-meer; needs a decision.

entries.name: Dhruv
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi ध्रुव: /d̪ʱɾʊʋ/
entries.notes: Hindi उ is short [ʊ], the 'book' vowel in a closed syllable (as Atul); today's long 'oo' lengthens it. Aspirated dh → d.

entries.name: Samad
entries.source: Arabic صمد ṣamad (CV.CVC, first-syllable stress by Arabic rule); Persian صمد samad [sæˈmæd], final stress (Samad Behrangi); Urdu ṣamad [ˈsəməd]

alternatives.context: Iranian and Azerbaijani bearers (wd IR 12, AZ 2): 'sa-MAD'

entries.notes: Each group differs: Persian and Azerbaijani stress the last syllable, Arabic and Urdu the first with different vowels, Bengali 'SHAW-mad'. Iran leads the notable counts, while the GB, FR and US registers likely hold South Asian and Maghrebi bearers. Today's SAM-ud matches no group exactly. Needs a population decision.

entries.name: Juanita
entries.source: English usage wah-NEE-tuh (CMUdict); Wiktionary, Spanish Juanita: /xwaˈnita/; same stress and vowels, English drops the h

alternatives.context: Spanish-speaking bearers (Spain, Latin America, many US Hispanic bearers): 'hwah-NEE-tah'

entries.notes: usage english (US 157,790), so the English reading stays (guide). The GB 'lot' vowel falls on an unstressed syllable only.

entries.name: Holly
entries.notes: Ordinary word 'holly' (the plant). The name sounds the same, so today's reading fits both and nothing needs shipping.

entries.name: Aiden
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Aidan: /ˈeɪdən/; Aiden is a respelling of Aidan

entries.name: Hazel
entries.notes: Ordinary word 'hazel' (the tree, the eye colour). The name sounds the same, so today's reading fits both and nothing needs shipping.

entries.name: Heba
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic هبة (female given name Hiba or Heba): /hi.ba/; the e spelling follows Egyptian Arabic, where this short i is [e]

alternatives.context: the Hiba spelling's Classical and Levantine reading

entries.notes: Today's HEE-buh lengthens a short vowel. Bearers are mostly Egyptian (wd EG 24).

entries.name: Hanan
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic حنان (ḥanān): /ħa.naːn/, stress on the long last syllable; Hebrew חָנָן (Hanan, a male name) also stresses the last syllable
entries.notes: Arabic ḥ and Hebrew ח both → h. Today's HAY-nun is a spelling guess with the wrong stress.

entries.name: Pranav
entries.source: Hindi प्रणव (praṇav), regular Devanagari reading: short a [ə] in both syllables, retroflex ṇ as n; first-syllable stress as for Karan and Kapil (CV.CVC precedent)
entries.notes: Today's PRAH-nahv gives both short a's a long 'ah'.

entries.name: Mickey
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Mickey: /ˈmɪki/ (RP and GA)
entries.notes: US register (32,762) dwarfs the Israeli, Danish and Dutch notable bearers.

entries.name: Song
entries.source: Mandarin 松 sōng: [sʊŋ] (as Sōng, n0012); Korean 송 [soŋ]
entries.notes: Common word 'song'. The name reading (Chinese 'soong', Korean 'sohng') differs from the word, so it is recorded in us/gb but must not ship as a general entry.

entries.name: Neel
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi नील: /niːl/; today's NEEL matches

entries.name: Ludovic
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Ludovic: /ly.dɔ.vik/; French names take final stress in English (guide)
entries.notes: French u [y] → 'oo'. Today's LOO-doh-vik stresses the first syllable. Romanian Ludovic also stresses the last syllable.

entries.name: Hǎidōng
entries.source: Mandarin 海东/海東 hǎidōng: hai [xaɪ̯] + dong [tʊŋ] (standard pinyin values, Help:IPA/Mandarin); -ong → oong as in earlier batches; primary stress on the last syllable, secondary on the first (guide's convention)
entries.notes: Today's HAY-dawng stresses the first syllable and misreads both vowels.

entries.name: My
entries.source: Vietnamese My/Mỹ: [mi]; Swedish My: [myː]

alternatives.context: Swedish My (Little My): front rounded [y], English 'mew'

entries.notes: Common word 'my'. The name reading differs (Vietnamese 'mee', Swedish 'mew'), recorded in us/gb only.

entries.name: Sabine
entries.source: Wiktionary, German Sabine: /zaˈbi.nə/; French /sa.bin/; English given name /səˈbiːn/; English 'Sabine' (the ancient tribe) is /ˈseɪbaɪn/, today's reading

alternatives.context: the ancient Sabines and the Sabine River (Texas/Louisiana)

entries.notes: German, Austrian and Swiss bearers are the largest group (wd DE 735, AT 126, CH 56; a top name in 1960s Germany), ahead of the French. Today's SAY-byne is the tribe/river word, wrong for every bearer. Flag: the entry also changes 'the Sabine women' and 'Sabine River' in English text; make it protect-word if that use matters more.

entries.name: Xenia
entries.source: Wiktionary, German Xenia: /ˈkseːni̯a/; Russian Ксения [ˈksʲenʲɪjə] (Xenia is its German and English transliteration); Greek Ξένια also starts ks-
entries.notes: Collision triage: the botanical word 'xenia' is rare and technical, so treated as a name. Russian, German, Belarusian and Ukrainian bearers (wd RU 132, DE 29, BY 12, UA 11) all start with 'ks'. Russian and German stressed e in an open syllable → 'ay' (as Elena). Flag: changes Xenia, Ohio, in English text.
entries.word_check: gold has 'xenia'; kept: 'xenia' is a rare botanical term

entries.name: Le
entries.source: Mandarin 乐/樂 lè: [lɤ] (Help:IPA/Mandarin); Vietnamese Lê: [le]

alternatives.context: Vietnamese Lê, 'lay' (US register bearers are likely Vietnamese)

entries.notes: Capitalised Le in English text is mostly the French article (Le Monde, Le Mans, Marine Le Pen, Le Corbusier), which today's unstressed 'luh' already reads correctly. Protected; the name readings are recorded in us/gb and alternatives.

entries.name: Cheick
entries.source: French Wiktionary, cheikh/cheik: \ʃɛk\ (also \ʃɛjk\); Cheick is the West African French spelling of the Arabic title shaykh

alternatives.context: the other French reading \ʃɛjk\ and English 'sheikh': 'SHAYK'

entries.notes: Bearers: Cheick Tioté, Cheick Modibo Diarra. Today's CHIKE reads ch as in English.

entries.name: Gabriele
entries.source: German Wiktionary, Gabriele: [ɡabʁiˈeːlə]; English Wiktionary, Italian Gabriele: /ɡa.briˈɛ.le/
entries.notes: Forebears: Germany 257k, Austria 39k, Switzerland 4k (women) against Italy 127k (men) and Brazil 48k, so the German reading wins. Both stress the e; today's gah-bree-EL drops the last syllable. Changes Gabriele D'Annunzio in English text.

entries.name: Nath
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi नाथ: /nɑːt̪ʰ/

alternatives.context: English nickname for Nathan or Nathaniel

entries.notes: In Indian spelling th is an aspirated t, not the 'th' of thin (today's NATH). Bearers are Indian (US register only 17).

entries.name: You
entries.source: Mandarin 友/有/佑 yǒu/yòu: [joʊ̯] (as Xueyou here; Liu, n0006)
entries.notes: Common pronoun 'you'. The name reading 'yoh' is recorded in us/gb only.

entries.name: Nadiyah
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic نادية: /naː.di.ja/, the long first syllable carries the stress; the -iyah spelling transliterates the Arabic; as Nadia (n0002, NAHD-yuh)

alternatives.context: Ukrainian Nadiya (Надія) and possibly US bearers: 'nuh-DEE-yuh', today's reading

entries.notes: Conflicting groups: the spelling is Arabic, and the registers (US 1,066, GB 142) point to Muslim bearers, but the notable count is mostly Ukrainian (wd UA 28), possibly a Wikidata merge with Nadiya. US bearers may also stress 'DEE' as in Aaliyah. Low; needs review.

entries.name: Lele
entries.source: Italian Lele, pet form of Gabriele and Emanuele: stressed open e [ɛ], final -e (regular Italian orthography; Gabriele /ɡa.briˈɛ.le/)
entries.notes: Today's LEEL drops a syllable. Final unstressed Italian -e → 'ay' (guide, Daniele).

entries.name: Om
entries.source: Hindi ओम (om): [oːm]; Wiktionary, Sanskrit ओम /oː.mɐ/
entries.notes: Also the word 'om' (the mantra, the same Sanskrit word, said 'ohm'). Today's US reading is right; British today says 'om' with the 'lot' vowel, so the name reading (GB ˈQm) is recorded here for a word-safe fix later.

entries.name: Shivam
entries.source: Hindi शिवम् (śivam): short i, short a [ə]; today's SHIV-um matches (CV.CVC first-syllable precedent)

entries.name: Denzil
entries.source: Wiktionary: Denzil is an alternative form of Denzel, /ˈdɛnzɛl/; today's DEN-zul differs only in the unstressed vowel

entries.name: Duan
entries.source: Mandarin 端/段 duān/duàn: [tu̯an] (standard pinyin value, Help:IPA/Mandarin)
entries.notes: Today's DWAN uses the 'cat' vowel; pinyin -uan after d is [wan], 'wahn' (as Guan, Huan). Some US register bearers may be a Duane variant.

entries.name: Yuxin
entries.source: Mandarin 雨鑫/禹欣 yǔxīn: yu [y] + xin [ɕin] (standard pinyin values, Help:IPA/Mandarin); ü → yoo/w, x → sh as in earlier batches; primary stress on the last syllable, secondary on the first (guide's convention)
entries.notes: Today's YUK-sin reads x as ks.

entries.name: Ya
entries.source: Mandarin 亚/雅 yà/yǎ: [ja]; Korean 야 [ja]
entries.notes: Common informal word 'ya' (you). The name reading 'yah' is recorded in us/gb only.

entries.name: Yuhan
entries.source: Mandarin 语涵/钰函 yǔhán: yu [y] + han [xan] (standard pinyin values, Help:IPA/Mandarin); ü → yoo/w as in earlier batches; primary stress on the last syllable, secondary on the first (guide's convention)
entries.notes: Today's YOO-un drops the h and the 'ah' vowel.

entries.name: Kadiatou
entries.source: French spelling of Khadija used in Guinea and Mali: French ka-dja-tou, final stress as for Mamadou and Boubacar (earlier batches)
entries.notes: Today's KAD-ee-uh-too has the wrong stress and the 'cat' vowel. The stress follows the French-spelling precedent; Fatoumata (n0005) stayed unresolved on the same question.

entries.name: Ze
entries.drop_detail: 'ze' is a pronoun, which starts sentences
entries.source: Mandarin 泽/则 zé: [tsɤ] (standard pinyin value, Help:IPA/Mandarin); z → dz, e → 'uh' as Zǐ and De (earlier batches)
entries.notes: Today's ZEE reads it as an English letter name.

entries.name: Xiaofeng
entries.source: Mandarin 小峰 xiǎofēng: xiao [ɕi̯ɑʊ̯] + feng [fɤŋ] (standard pinyin values, Help:IPA/Mandarin); x → sh, -eng → ung as in earlier batches; primary stress on the last syllable, secondary on the first (guide's convention)
entries.notes: Today's ZHOW-feng reads x as zh and stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Weiwei
entries.source: Mandarin 薇薇/伟伟 wēiwēi: wei [weɪ̯] + wei [weɪ̯] (standard pinyin values, Help:IPA/Mandarin); primary stress on the last syllable, secondary on the first (guide's convention)
entries.notes: Today's WY-way reads the first wei as 'why'; both syllables are 'way' (as Feifei, fay-FAY).

entries.name: Fen
entries.source: Mandarin 芬/分 fēn: [fən]; -en → 'un' (as Wen, Sēn)
entries.notes: The word 'fen' (a marsh) is rare, but capitalised Fen is common in English place names (Wicken Fen, Fen Ditton, Fen Drayton), which a name entry would turn into 'fun'. Protected; the name reading is recorded in us/gb.

entries.name: Yixin
entries.source: Mandarin 一昕/宜鑫 yīxīn: yi [i] + xin [ɕin] (standard pinyin values, Help:IPA/Mandarin); x → sh as in earlier batches; primary stress on the last syllable, secondary on the first (guide's convention)
entries.notes: Today's YIK-sin reads x as ks; yi is 'ee' (as Yifan, Yiming).

entries.name: Ziyi
entries.source: Mandarin 子怡/子弈 zǐyí: zi [tsɹ̩] + yi [i] (standard pinyin values, Help:IPA/Mandarin); z → dz, zhi/zi/si vowel → ur/uh as in earlier batches; primary stress on the last syllable, secondary on the first (guide's convention)
entries.notes: Today's ZEE-ee gives zi an 'ee' vowel; pinyin zi has the buzzing apical vowel, 'dzuh' as for Zǐ (n0012). Wikipedia, Zhang Ziyi: Mandarin [ʈʂáŋ tsɹ̩̀.ǐ].

entries.name: Shanshan
entries.source: Mandarin 杉杉 shānshān: shan [ʂan] + shan [ʂan] (standard pinyin values, Help:IPA/Mandarin); primary stress on the last syllable, secondary on the first (guide's convention)
entries.notes: Today's SHAN-shun uses the 'cat' vowel and reduces the second syllable.

entries.name: Mang
entries.source: Mandarin 莽 mǎng: [mɑŋ] (standard pinyin value, Help:IPA/Mandarin)
entries.notes: Today's MANG uses the 'cat' vowel; pinyin -ang is 'ahng' (as Kang, Zhang).

entries.name: Xiaoyu
entries.source: Mandarin 小宇/晓宇 xiǎoyǔ: xiao [ɕi̯ɑʊ̯] + yu [y] (standard pinyin values, Help:IPA/Mandarin); x → sh, ü → yoo/w as in earlier batches; primary stress on the last syllable, secondary on the first (guide's convention)
entries.notes: Today's ZHOW-yoo reads x as zh and stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Xiaoming
entries.source: Mandarin 晓明 xiǎomíng: xiao [ɕi̯ɑʊ̯] + ming [miŋ] (standard pinyin values, Help:IPA/Mandarin); x → sh as in earlier batches; primary stress on the last syllable, secondary on the first (guide's convention)
entries.notes: Today's ZHOW-ming reads x as zh and stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Kun
entries.source: Mandarin 坤/堃 kūn: [kʰu̯ən] (standard pinyin value, Help:IPA/Mandarin)
entries.notes: Today's KUN drops the w of pinyin -un [u̯ən] (as Kūn, n0007).

entries.name: Xinran
entries.source: Mandarin 欣然 xīnrán: xin [ɕin] + ran [ʐan] (standard pinyin values, Help:IPA/Mandarin); x → sh as in earlier batches; primary stress on the last syllable, secondary on the first (guide's convention)
entries.notes: Today's ZIN-ran reads x as z.

entries.name: Tianyi
entries.source: Mandarin 天一/天怡 tiānyī: tian [tʰi̯ɛn] + yi [i] (standard pinyin values, Help:IPA/Mandarin); -ian → yen as in earlier batches; primary stress on the last syllable, secondary on the first (guide's convention)
entries.notes: Today's tee-AHN-yee splits tian into two syllables; pinyin -ian is one syllable 'yen' (as Tian).

entries.name: Ru
entries.source: Mandarin 如/儒 rú: [ʐu] (Help:IPA/Mandarin); pinyin r → English r; today's ROO matches
entries.notes: Korean 루 (Ru) is said the same.

entries.name: Hongmei
entries.source: Mandarin 红梅/紅梅 hóngméi: hong [xʊŋ] + mei [meɪ̯] (standard pinyin values, Help:IPA/Mandarin); -ong → oong as in earlier batches; primary stress on the last syllable, secondary on the first (guide's convention)
entries.notes: Today's HAWNG-my reads mei as 'my' (it is 'may').

entries.name: Ziyang
entries.source: Mandarin 子扬/紫阳 zǐyáng: zi [tsɹ̩] + yang [jɑŋ] (standard pinyin values, Help:IPA/Mandarin); z → dz, zhi/zi/si vowel → ur/uh as in earlier batches; primary stress on the last syllable, secondary on the first (guide's convention)
entries.notes: Today's zhee-ANG reads z as zh and uses the 'cat' vowel.

entries.name: Wenjun
entries.source: Mandarin 文君/文骏 wénjūn: wen [wən] + jun [tɕyn] (standard pinyin values, Help:IPA/Mandarin); -en → un, ü → yoo/w as in earlier batches; primary stress on the last syllable, secondary on the first (guide's convention)
entries.notes: Today's WEN-jun reduces jun; pinyin jun is 'joon' (as Jun, Jianjun).

entries.name: Yaxin
entries.source: Mandarin 雅欣 yǎxīn: ya [ja] + xin [ɕin] (standard pinyin values, Help:IPA/Mandarin); x → sh as in earlier batches; primary stress on the last syllable, secondary on the first (guide's convention)
entries.notes: Today's YAK-sun reads x as ks.

entries.name: Jinping
entries.source: Mandarin 近平/金平 jìnpíng: jin [tɕin] + ping [pʰiŋ] (standard pinyin values, Help:IPA/Mandarin); primary stress on the last syllable, secondary on the first (guide's convention)
entries.notes: Today's JIN-ping has the right sounds but stresses the first syllable; English news usage and the guide's convention stress ping. Wikipedia, Xi Jinping: Mandarin [ɕǐ tɕîn.pʰǐŋ].

entries.name: Hongyan
entries.source: Mandarin 红燕 hóngyàn: hong [xʊŋ] + yan [jɛn] (standard pinyin values, Help:IPA/Mandarin); -ong → oong as in earlier batches; primary stress on the last syllable, secondary on the first (guide's convention)
entries.notes: Today's HAWNG-yahn misreads pinyin -yan, which is 'yen' (as Yan, Xiaoyan).

entries.name: Tianyu
entries.source: Mandarin 天宇/天予 tiānyǔ: tian [tʰi̯ɛn] + yu [y] (standard pinyin values, Help:IPA/Mandarin); -ian → yen, ü → yoo/w as in earlier batches; primary stress on the last syllable, secondary on the first (guide's convention)
entries.notes: Today's tee-AHN-yoo splits tian into two syllables (pinyin -ian is 'yen').

entries.name: Shaolin
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Shaolin: /ˈʃaʊlɪn/; Mandarin 少林 shàolín [ʂɑʊ̯ lin]
entries.notes: US-only fix: US today says three syllables (SHAH-oh-lin); British already says SHOW-lin. The same reading serves the temple and the kung-fu style.

entries.name: Zhiyu
entries.source: Mandarin 志宇 zhìyǔ: zhi [ʈʂɻ̩] + yu [y] (standard pinyin values, Help:IPA/Mandarin); zh → j, zhi/zi/si vowel → ur/uh, ü → yoo/w as in earlier batches; primary stress on the last syllable, secondary on the first (guide's convention)
entries.notes: Today's ZHEE-oo reads zh as the 'measure' sound and drops the y.

entries.name: Yulin
entries.source: Mandarin 玉林/禹林 yùlín: yu [y] + lin [lin] (standard pinyin values, Help:IPA/Mandarin); ü → yoo/w as in earlier batches; primary stress on the last syllable, secondary on the first (guide's convention)
entries.notes: Today's YOO-lin has the right sounds but stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Chenchen
entries.source: Mandarin 晨晨 chénchén: chen [ʈʂʰən] + chen [ʈʂʰən] (standard pinyin values, Help:IPA/Mandarin); -en → un as in earlier batches; primary stress on the last syllable, secondary on the first (guide's convention)
entries.notes: Today's CHEN-chun stresses the first syllable; pinyin -en is a schwa, 'chun' (as Yichen, n0012).

entries.name: Zhiying
entries.source: Mandarin 之莹/智英 zhīyíng: zhi [ʈʂɻ̩] + ying [iŋ] (standard pinyin values, Help:IPA/Mandarin); zh → j, zhi/zi/si vowel → ur/uh as in earlier batches; primary stress on the last syllable, secondary on the first (guide's convention)
entries.notes: Today's ZHEE-ing reads zh as the 'measure' sound.

entries.name: Zhijian
entries.source: Mandarin 智健 zhìjiàn: zhi [ʈʂɻ̩] + jian [tɕi̯ɛn] (standard pinyin values, Help:IPA/Mandarin); zh → j, zhi/zi/si vowel → ur/uh, -ian → yen as in earlier batches; primary stress on the last syllable, secondary on the first (guide's convention)
entries.notes: Today's ZHEE-jee-un reads zh as the 'measure' sound and splits jian.

entries.name: Jiayan
entries.source: Mandarin 佳妍/佳言 jiāyán: jia [tɕi̯a] + yan [jɛn] (standard pinyin values, Help:IPA/Mandarin); primary stress on the last syllable, secondary on the first (guide's convention)
entries.notes: Today's jee-EYE-un misreads both syllables.

entries.name: Zijian
entries.source: Mandarin 子健/梓健 zǐjiàn: zi [tsɹ̩] + jian [tɕi̯ɛn] (standard pinyin values, Help:IPA/Mandarin); z → dz, zhi/zi/si vowel → ur/uh, -ian → yen as in earlier batches; primary stress on the last syllable, secondary on the first (guide's convention)
entries.notes: Today's ZEE-jee-un gives zi an 'ee' and splits jian.

entries.name: Xiangyu
entries.source: Mandarin 翔宇 xiángyǔ: xiang [ɕi̯ɑŋ] + yu [y] (standard pinyin values, Help:IPA/Mandarin); x → sh, ü → yoo/w as in earlier batches; primary stress on the last syllable, secondary on the first (guide's convention)
entries.notes: Today's ZHAWNG-yoo reads x as zh and drops the i of -iang.

entries.name: Sijia
entries.source: Mandarin 思佳/思嘉 sījiā: si [sɹ̩] + jia [tɕi̯a] (standard pinyin values, Help:IPA/Mandarin); zhi/zi/si vowel → ur/uh as in earlier batches; primary stress on the last syllable, secondary on the first (guide's convention)
entries.notes: Today's SEE-jee-uh gives si an 'ee'; pinyin si has the apical vowel, 'suh' (as Siyuan).

entries.name: Qianyi
entries.source: Mandarin 倩怡 qiànyí: qian [tɕʰi̯ɛn] + yi [i] (standard pinyin values, Help:IPA/Mandarin); q → ch, -ian → yen as in earlier batches; primary stress on the last syllable, secondary on the first (guide's convention)
entries.notes: Today's kee-AHN-yee reads q as k.

entries.name: Zilong
entries.source: Mandarin 子龙/子龍 zǐlóng: zi [tsɹ̩] + long [lʊŋ] (standard pinyin values, Help:IPA/Mandarin); z → dz, zhi/zi/si vowel → ur/uh, -ong → oong as in earlier batches; primary stress on the last syllable, secondary on the first (guide's convention)
entries.notes: Today's ZY-lawng reads zi as 'zy'.

entries.name: Jiaqiang
entries.source: Mandarin 家强/家強 jiāqiáng: jia [tɕi̯a] + qiang [tɕʰi̯ɑŋ] (standard pinyin values, Help:IPA/Mandarin); q → ch as in earlier batches; primary stress on the last syllable, secondary on the first (guide's convention)
entries.notes: Today's jee-AK-ee-ang reads q as k and splits both syllables.

entries.name: Akshara
entries.source: Wiktionary, Sanskrit अक्षरा: /ɐ́k.ʂɐ.ɾɑː/ (accent on the first syllable); Hindi akṣarā has short a [ə] in the first two syllables; as Akshay /ˈəkʃɛ/ (n0003)
entries.notes: Today's ak-SHAR-uh stresses the second syllable with an 'ah'. ṣ → sh.

entries.name: Ang
entries.source: Wikipedia, Ang Lee: 'Pronounced /æŋ liː/' (English); Mandarin 安 ān [an]

alternatives.context: Mandarin 昂 áng [ɑŋ] (mainland bearers who spell the pinyin syllable ang)

entries.notes: The best-known bearer, Ang Lee, gives his name as /æŋ/ in English, which is today's reading. Mainland bearers of 昂 áng say 'ahng'.

entries.name: Guan
entries.source: Mandarin 冠/关/官 guān: [ku̯an] (Help:IPA/Mandarin); today's GWAHN matches (as Huan, n0008)
entries.notes: Collision triage: the word 'guan' (a bird) is rare and technical; treated as a name. Today's reading already fits the name.

entries.name: Bu
entries.source: Mandarin 步 bù: [pu] (Help:IPA/Mandarin; unaspirated p is English b); today's BOO matches
entries.notes: Korean 부 (Bu) is said the same.

entries.name: Bǐngliáng
entries.source: Mandarin 炳良 bǐngliáng: bing [piŋ] + liang [li̯ɑŋ] (standard pinyin values, Help:IPA/Mandarin); primary stress on the last syllable, secondary on the first (guide's convention)
entries.notes: Today's BING-glee-ang adds a g and splits liang.

entries.name: Dekang
entries.source: Mandarin 德康 dékāng: de [tɤ] + kang [kʰɑŋ] (standard pinyin values, Help:IPA/Mandarin); primary stress on the last syllable, secondary on the first (guide's convention)
entries.notes: Today's duh-KANG uses the 'cat' vowel.

entries.name: Guǎng
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 光 (guāng): /ku̯ɑŋ⁵⁵/; 广 guǎng is the same syllable with another tone
entries.notes: Today's GWANG uses the 'cat' vowel (as Guang, n0002).

entries.name: Huì
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 慧 (huì): /xu̯eɪ̯⁵¹/; 卉 huì is the same syllable
entries.notes: Today's HOO-ee splits the syllable; pinyin hui is [xweɪ], 'hway' (as Hui, n0002).

entries.name: Jintao
entries.source: Mandarin 锦涛/錦濤 jǐntāo: jin [tɕin] + tao [tʰɑʊ̯] (standard pinyin values, Help:IPA/Mandarin); primary stress on the last syllable, secondary on the first (guide's convention)
entries.notes: Today's JIN-tow has the right sounds but stresses the first syllable. Wikipedia, Hu Jintao: Mandarin [xǔ tɕìn.tʰáʊ].

entries.name: Jiāhuì
entries.source: Mandarin 佳慧 jiāhuì: jia [tɕi̯a] + hui [xu̯eɪ̯] (standard pinyin values, Help:IPA/Mandarin); primary stress on the last syllable, secondary on the first (guide's convention)
entries.notes: Today's JAH-hwee misreads hui, which is 'hway' (as Hui).

entries.name: Jiālín
entries.source: Mandarin 家林 jiālín: jia [tɕi̯a] + lin [lin] (standard pinyin values, Help:IPA/Mandarin); primary stress on the last syllable, secondary on the first (guide's convention)
entries.notes: Today's jee-AH-lun splits jia and reduces lin.

entries.name: Jīnpíng
entries.source: Mandarin 金萍 jīnpíng: jin [tɕin] + ping [pʰiŋ] (standard pinyin values, Help:IPA/Mandarin); primary stress on the last syllable, secondary on the first (guide's convention)
entries.notes: Today's JIN-ping has the right sounds but stresses the first syllable (as Jinping).

entries.name: Kuí
entries.source: Mandarin 逵/魁 kuí: [kʰu̯eɪ̯] (standard pinyin value, Help:IPA/Mandarin)
entries.notes: Today's KOO-ee splits the syllable; pinyin kui is [kʰweɪ], 'kway' (as Hui).

entries.name: Manying
entries.source: Mandarin 满籝/滿籯 mǎnyíng: man [man] + ying [iŋ] (standard pinyin values, Help:IPA/Mandarin); primary stress on the last syllable, secondary on the first (guide's convention)
entries.notes: Today's MEN-ee-ing reads it as an English -ing form.

entries.name: Minyi
entries.source: Mandarin 敏仪/敏儀 mǐnyí: min [min] + yi [i] (standard pinyin values, Help:IPA/Mandarin); primary stress on the last syllable, secondary on the first (guide's convention)
entries.notes: Today's MIN-yee has the right sounds but stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Mèng
entries.source: Mandarin 梦/夢 mèng: [mɤŋ] (standard pinyin value, Help:IPA/Mandarin)
entries.notes: Today's MENG uses 'eh' for the schwa; pinyin -eng is 'ung' (as Meng, n0007).

entries.name: Méng
entries.source: Mandarin 盟/蒙/檬 méng: [mɤŋ] (standard pinyin value, Help:IPA/Mandarin)
entries.notes: Today's MENG uses 'eh' for the schwa; pinyin -eng is 'ung' (as Meng, n0007).

entries.name: Míngzhū
entries.source: Mandarin 明珠 míngzhū: ming [miŋ] + zhu [ʈʂu] (standard pinyin values, Help:IPA/Mandarin); zh → j as in earlier batches; primary stress on the last syllable, secondary on the first (guide's convention)
entries.notes: Today's MING-gzhoo adds a g and reads zh as the 'measure' sound.

entries.name: Nǎiguāng
entries.source: Mandarin 乃光 nǎiguāng: nai [naɪ̯] + guang [ku̯ɑŋ] (standard pinyin values, Help:IPA/Mandarin); primary stress on the last syllable, secondary on the first (guide's convention)
entries.notes: Today's NAY-gwang reads nai as 'nay' and uses the 'cat' vowel.

entries.name: Pengnian
entries.source: Mandarin 彭年/鹏年 péngnián: peng [pʰɤŋ] + nian [ni̯ɛn] (standard pinyin values, Help:IPA/Mandarin); -eng → ung, -ian → yen as in earlier batches; primary stress on the last syllable, secondary on the first (guide's convention)
entries.notes: Today's PENG-nee-un splits nian.

entries.name: Pengyu
entries.source: Mandarin 鹏宇/鵬宇 péngyǔ: peng [pʰɤŋ] + yu [y] (standard pinyin values, Help:IPA/Mandarin); -eng → ung, ü → yoo/w as in earlier batches; primary stress on the last syllable, secondary on the first (guide's convention)
entries.notes: Today's PENG-yoo stresses the first syllable and uses 'eh' for the schwa of peng.

entries.name: Qinghong
entries.source: Mandarin 庆红/慶紅 qìnghóng: qing [tɕʰiŋ] + hong [xʊŋ] (standard pinyin values, Help:IPA/Mandarin); q → ch, -ong → oong as in earlier batches; primary stress on the last syllable, secondary on the first (guide's convention)
entries.notes: Today's KING-hawng reads q as k.

entries.name: Qiān
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 千 (qiān): /t͡ɕʰi̯ɛn⁵⁵/; q → ch, -ian → 'yen'
entries.notes: Today's KEE-ahn reads q as k and splits the syllable (as Qian, n0004).

entries.name: Qìngwén
entries.source: Mandarin 庆文/慶文 qìngwén: qing [tɕʰiŋ] + wen [wən] (standard pinyin values, Help:IPA/Mandarin); q → ch, -en → un as in earlier batches; primary stress on the last syllable, secondary on the first (guide's convention)
entries.notes: Today's KING-wun reads q as k.

entries.name: Qìngzhōu
entries.source: Mandarin 庆洲/慶洲 qìngzhōu: qing [tɕʰiŋ] + zhou [ʈʂoʊ̯] (standard pinyin values, Help:IPA/Mandarin); q → ch, zh → j as in earlier batches; primary stress on the last syllable, secondary on the first (guide's convention)
entries.notes: Today's KING-zhoo reads q as k and zhou as 'zhoo'.

entries.name: Ruòyú
entries.source: Mandarin 若瑜 ruòyú: ruo [ʐu̯ɔ] + yu [y] (standard pinyin values, Help:IPA/Mandarin); ü → yoo/w as in earlier batches; primary stress on the last syllable, secondary on the first (guide's convention)
entries.notes: Today's ROO-yoo drops the 'aw' of ruo.

entries.name: Weilian
entries.source: Mandarin 威廉 wēilián: wei [weɪ̯] + lian [li̯ɛn] (standard pinyin values, Help:IPA/Mandarin); -ian → yen as in earlier batches; primary stress on the last syllable, secondary on the first (guide's convention)
entries.notes: Today's WY-lee-un reads wei as 'why' and splits lian. 威廉 is the Chinese transcription of William.

entries.name: Wenyao
entries.source: Mandarin 文耀 wényào: wen [wən] + yao [jɑʊ̯] (standard pinyin values, Help:IPA/Mandarin); -en → un as in earlier batches; primary stress on the last syllable, secondary on the first (guide's convention)
entries.notes: Today's WEN-yow stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Xiaogang
entries.source: Mandarin 晓刚/曉剛 xiǎogāng: xiao [ɕi̯ɑʊ̯] + gang [kɑŋ] (standard pinyin values, Help:IPA/Mandarin); x → sh as in earlier batches; primary stress on the last syllable, secondary on the first (guide's convention)
entries.notes: Today's ZHOW-gang reads x as zh and uses the 'cat' vowel (as Xiǎogāng, n0012).

entries.name: Ximing
entries.source: Mandarin 喜明/锡明 xǐmíng: xi [ɕi] + ming [miŋ] (standard pinyin values, Help:IPA/Mandarin); x → sh as in earlier batches; primary stress on the last syllable, secondary on the first (guide's convention)
entries.notes: Today's ZY-ming reads xi as 'zy'.

entries.name: Xiuquan
entries.source: Mandarin 修全/秀全 xiùquán: xiu [ɕi̯oʊ̯] + quan [tɕʰɥɛn] (standard pinyin values, Help:IPA/Mandarin); x → sh, q → ch, ü → yoo/w as in earlier batches; primary stress on the last syllable, secondary on the first (guide's convention)
entries.notes: Today's zhoo-KWAHN reads x as zh and q as k. Hong Xiuquan is the best-known bearer.

entries.name: Xián
entries.source: Mandarin 贤/賢 xián: [ɕi̯ɛn] (Help:IPA/Mandarin); Galician Xián (= Julián): [ʃiˈaŋ]

alternatives.context: Galician Xián, the Galician form of Julián: 'shee-AHN', which is today's US reading

entries.notes: Two different names share this exact accented spelling. Chinese bearers rarely write tone marks in running text, while Galician bearers always write Xián. The input lists only Wikidata CN:3, PT:1 and no register counts, so I can't tell which group is larger. The candidate is the Chinese reading (shyen, as Xian, n0007). If the Galician name is the main one, today's US reading is already right and only British needs the 'ah' vowel (ʃiːˈɑːn).

entries.name: Xuebin
entries.source: Mandarin 学斌/學斌 xuébīn: xue [ɕɥɛ] + bin [pin] (standard pinyin values, Help:IPA/Mandarin); x → sh, ü → yoo/w as in earlier batches; primary stress on the last syllable, secondary on the first (guide's convention)
entries.notes: Today's ZUU-bin reads x as z.

entries.name: Xueyou
entries.source: Mandarin 学友/學友 xuéyǒu: xue [ɕɥɛ] + you [joʊ̯] (standard pinyin values, Help:IPA/Mandarin); x → sh, ü → yoo/w as in earlier batches; primary stress on the last syllable, secondary on the first (guide's convention)
entries.notes: Today's ZOO-yoo reads x as z and you as 'yoo'.

entries.name: Xuéliáng
entries.source: Mandarin 学良/學良 xuéliáng: xue [ɕɥɛ] + liang [li̯ɑŋ] (standard pinyin values, Help:IPA/Mandarin); x → sh, ü → yoo/w as in earlier batches; primary stress on the last syllable, secondary on the first (guide's convention)
entries.notes: Today's ZOOL-yung reads x as z. Zhang Xueliang is the best-known bearer.

entries.name: Yaobang
entries.source: Mandarin 耀邦 yàobāng: yao [jɑʊ̯] + bang [pɑŋ] (standard pinyin values, Help:IPA/Mandarin); primary stress on the last syllable, secondary on the first (guide's convention)
entries.notes: Today's YOW-bang stresses the first syllable and uses the 'cat' vowel. Hu Yaobang is the best-known bearer.

entries.name: Yáo
entries.source: Mandarin 瑶/瑤 yáo: [jɑʊ̯]; today's YOW matches (as Yao, n0005)

entries.name: Zhìliàng
entries.source: Mandarin 志亮 zhìliàng: zhi [ʈʂɻ̩] + liang [li̯ɑŋ] (standard pinyin values, Help:IPA/Mandarin); zh → j, zhi/zi/si vowel → ur/uh as in earlier batches; primary stress on the last syllable, secondary on the first (guide's convention)
entries.notes: Today's ZHEEL-yang reads zh as the 'measure' sound.

entries.name: Zhù
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 住/柱 (zhù): /ʈ͡ʂu⁵¹/; zh → j
entries.notes: Today's ZOO reads zh as z (as Zhu, n0012).

entries.name: Zimeng
entries.source: Mandarin 子萌/梓萌 zǐméng: zi [tsɹ̩] + meng [mɤŋ] (standard pinyin values, Help:IPA/Mandarin); z → dz, zhi/zi/si vowel → ur/uh, -eng → ung as in earlier batches; primary stress on the last syllable, secondary on the first (guide's convention)
entries.notes: Today's ZY-mung reads zi as 'zy'.

entries.name: Phong
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese phong: Hà Nội and Saigon [fawŋ͡m˧˧], Huế also [fɔŋ˧˧]; today's FAWNG is the usual English 'fong'
entries.notes: Vietnamese -ong ends with closed lips; English has no closer match than 'fawng'/'fong'.

entries.name: Sneha
entries.source: Wiktionary, Marathi स्नेहा: /sne.ɦa/; Hindi स्नेह: /sneːɦ/
entries.notes: Today's SNEE-huh reads e as 'ee'; Indian e is 'ay' (as Neha).

entries.name: Maxim
entries.source: Wiktionary, Russian Максим: [mɐkˈsʲim], stress on the last syllable (as Moldovan/Romanian Maxim)

alternatives.context: German and Dutch Maxim, and the English word: first-syllable stress

entries.notes: Ordinary word 'maxim' (uncommon), plus Maxim the magazine and the Maxim gun. The name reading differs (final stress), so it is recorded in us/gb only.

entries.name: Charity
entries.notes: Ordinary word 'charity'. The name (Nigerian, Ugandan, Kenyan and US bearers) sounds the same, so nothing needs shipping.

entries.name: Mandeep
entries.source: Punjabi ਮਨਦੀਪ / Hindi मनदीप (man + dīp; Wiktionary, Hindi दीप: /d̪iːp/): short a [ə], long ī; stress on the long last syllable as Sandeep (n0002)
entries.notes: Today's MAN-deep uses the 'cat' vowel and stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Manda
entries.source: English pet form of Amanda (/əˈmændə/): MAN-duh, today's reading
entries.notes: US register 2,321 is the only register count. Swedish Manda (a popular recent name in Sweden, wd SE:2) and Indian bearers (wd IN:5) say 'MAHN-dah'/'MUN-dah'; no count shows they outnumber US bearers. A population call.

entries.name: Naina
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi नैना: /nɛː.nɑː/
entries.notes: Standard Hindi ai is [ɛː] (as Kailash, Aishwarya); today's NY-nuh is the spelling's English reading.

entries.name: Mahima
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi महिमा: /mə.ɦɪ.mɑː/; stress on 'hi' by the Hindustani weight rule (as Aditi)
entries.notes: Today's muh-HEE-muh lengthens the short i (as Smita, n0008).

entries.name: Farouk
entries.source: Wikipedia, Farouk of Egypt: English /fəˈruːk/; today's reading matches

entries.name: Thierno
entries.source: Pulaar ceerno ('teacher', a title used as a name): c is the 'ch'-like palatal stop, long ee; the Gambian English spelling is Cherno
entries.notes: Today's THEER-noh reads th as in 'thin'; in this French spelling th is a t. Stress on the long first syllable is unsourced.

entries.name: Sagar
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi सागर: /sɑː.ɡəɾ/; stress on the long first syllable
entries.notes: US today stresses the last syllable (sah-GAR); British already says SAH-guh.

entries.name: Hiếu
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese hiếu: Hà Nội [hiəw˧˦], Huế and Saigon [hiw]; today's HYOO is the nearest English match

entries.name: Phượng
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese phượng: Hà Nội [fɨəŋ˧˨ʔ], Saigon [fɨəŋ˨˩˨]; ươ as in Phương (n0005)
entries.notes: Today's foo-AWNG splits the syllable with the wrong vowel. ư [ɨ] has no English match; 'book' vowel as for Phương.

entries.name: Quốc
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese quốc: Hà Nội [kuək̚˧˦], Saigon [wək̚˦˥]; qu → kw and the schwa nucleus as for Quân (n0011)
entries.notes: Today's KWAHK/KWOK uses an 'ah'/'lot' vowel; both northern and southern speech have a schwa nucleus.

entries.name: Disha
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi दिशा: /d̪ɪ.ʃɑː/; today's DISH-uh matches

entries.name: Tulsi
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi तुलसी: /t̪ʊl.siː/; today's tˈʊlsi matches
entries.notes: Collision triage: the word 'tulsi' (holy basil) is rare and the same Hindi word, said the same; treated as a name.

entries.name: Hardeep
entries.source: Punjabi ਹਰਦੀਪ (har + dīp; Wiktionary, Hindi दीप: /d̪iːp/): short a [ə], long ī; stress on the long last syllable as Sandeep and Mandeep
entries.notes: Today's HAR-deep gives the short a a long 'ah' and stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Amba
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi अंबा: /əm.bɑː/
entries.notes: Hindi short a is 'uh' (as Anjali, Amrita). Low: the England and Wales register (365 births, against US 10) suggests a British group whose reading is unknown and may be today's AM-buh.

entries.name: Medha
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi मेधा: /meː.d̪ʱɑː/
entries.notes: Today's MED-uh shortens the long e; aspirated dh → d.

entries.name: Veena
entries.source: Wiktionary, Sanskrit/Hindi वीणा: /ʋiː.ɳɑː/; today's VEE-nuh matches

entries.name: Shilpa
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi शिल्पा: /ʃɪl.pɑː/; today's SHIL-puh matches

entries.name: Niharika
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi निहारिका: /nɪ.ɦɑː.ɾɪ.kɑː/; stress on the long ā (Hindustani weight rule)
entries.notes: Today's nee-huh-REE-kuh stresses a short i and reduces the long ā.

entries.name: Vibha
entries.source: Hindi विभा (vibhā): short i, aspirated bh, final ā (regular Devanagari reading)
entries.notes: Today's VIB-huh says b and h as two sounds; aspirated bh → b (guide).

entries.name: Javad
entries.source: Wikipedia, Mohammad Javad Zarif: Persian [... d͡ʒæˌvɒːd ...]; Wiktionary, Arabic جواد: /d͡ʒa.waːd/; Persian stresses the last syllable
entries.notes: Bearers are overwhelmingly Iranian (wd IR 51). Today's JAH-vud stresses the first syllable. Persian â [ɒː] → 'ah' (guide, Payam).

entries.name: Mayur
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi मयूर: /mə.juːɾ/; stress on the long last syllable
entries.notes: Today's MAY-ur reads it as English.

entries.name: Shakti
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi शक्ति: /ʃək.t̪iː/; Sanskrit /ɕɐ́k.ti/ (first-syllable accent)
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today stresses the last syllable (shuk-TEE); US is already right.

entries.name: Bhavesh
entries.source: Hindi/Gujarati भावेश (bhāveś, bhāv + īś): long ā and long e; stress on the superheavy last syllable (as Yogesh, Dinesh); Wiktionary, Hindi भाव: /bʱɑːʋ/
entries.notes: Today's BAH-vish stresses the first syllable and reduces the long e.

entries.name: Sadhana
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi साधना: /sɑːd̪ʱ.nɑː/ (the middle schwa is dropped)
entries.notes: Hindi schwa deletion makes it two syllables. Today's US sah-DAN-uh and GB SAH-duh-nah both misread it.

entries.name: Pravin
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi प्रवीण: /pɾə.ʋiːɳ/; same name as Praveen (n0004, pruh-VEEN)
entries.notes: Today's PRAV-in shortens the long ī and stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Ike
entries.source: English pet form of Isaac/Eisenhower's nickname: /aɪk/, today's reading
entries.notes: Population call. US register 4,838 is the only count; the Igbo name is common in Nigeria but uncounted. Ike Eisenhower, Ike Turner and Hurricane Ike keep today's reading. Needs a decision if Nigerian bearers are judged larger.

entries.name: Chaitanya
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi चैतन्य: /t͡ʃɛː.t̪ən.jᵊ/; Marathi /t͡ɕəi.t̪ən.jə/; stress on the heavy 'tan' (Hindustani weight rule)
entries.notes: Today's chy-TAHN-yuh gives the stressed short a a long 'ah'. The first syllable keeps 'chy', as Marathi, Telugu and Kannada bearers say it.

entries.name: Aravind
entries.source: South Indian spelling of Sanskrit aravinda (Wiktionary, Hindi अरविंद: /əɾ.ʋɪnd̪/, n0002 Arvind ur-VIND); this spelling keeps the middle a; stress on the heavy -vind

alternatives.context: first-syllable stress, as Dravidian languages stress words (Srinivas precedent)

entries.notes: Today's AR-vund drops a syllable. The stress is unsourced: the weight rule gives -VIND, Dravidian initial stress gives UH-ruh-vind.

entries.name: Harinder
entries.source: Punjabi ਹਰਿੰਦਰ (harindar): short a [ə], short i in the heavy syllable 'rin', which carries the stress (as Surinder, n0007)
entries.notes: Today's HAIR-in-der stresses the first syllable with an 'air' vowel.

entries.name: Manjeet
entries.source: Punjabi ਮਨਜੀਤ (man + jīt; Wiktionary, Hindi जीत: /d͡ʒiːt̪/): short a [ə], long ī; stress on the long last syllable as Sandeep
entries.notes: Today's MAN-jeet uses the 'cat' vowel and stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Kavitha
entries.source: South Indian spelling of कविता (Wiktionary, Hindi /kə.ʋɪ.t̪ɑː/): th is a dental t; first-syllable stress as Latha and Lalitha (n0008, n0013)

alternatives.context: Hindi Kavita's usual Indian-English stress (n0005, unresolved)

entries.notes: Today's KAV-ith-uh reads th as in 'thin'. Stress unsourced, as for Kavita.

entries.name: Sangita
entries.source: Hindi संगीता (saṅgītā): stress on the long ī; today's differs only in the unstressed first vowel

entries.name: Venkata
entries.source: Telugu వెంకట (veṅkaṭa): first-syllable stress (Dravidian; as Srinivas, n0013); ṅk → ŋk, retroflex ṭ → t
entries.notes: Today's ven-KAH-tuh stresses the short middle a with a long 'ah'.

entries.name: Darshana
entries.source: Hindi दर्शना (darśanā; Wiktionary, Hindi दर्शन: /d̪əɾ.ʃən/): short a [ə] before r, stress on the heavy first syllable (as Archana, Varsha)
entries.notes: Today's dar-SHAN-uh stresses a short syllable with the 'cat' vowel.

entries.name: Manju
entries.source: Hindi मंजु (mañju): short a [ə] in the heavy first syllable, long final ū (regular Devanagari reading)
entries.notes: Today's MAN-joo uses the 'cat' vowel for the short a.

entries.name: Shantanu
entries.source: Wiktionary, Sanskrit शांतनु: /ɕɑːn.tɐ.nu/; stress on the heavy first syllable (as Santanu, n0013)
entries.notes: Today's shahn-TAH-noo stresses the short middle syllable.

entries.name: Madhuri
entries.source: Hindi माधुरी (mādhurī): long ā stressed, short u, long ī (regular Devanagari reading; weight rule)
entries.notes: Today's mud-HOOR-ee stresses the short u and says d and h separately.

entries.name: Urvashi
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi उर्वशी: /ʊɾ.ʋə.ʃiː/; stress on the heavy first syllable (Hindustani weight rule)
entries.notes: Today's ur-VAH-shee stresses the short a with a long 'ah'.

entries.name: Vidhya
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi विद्या (vidyā): /ʋɪd̪.jɑː/; Vidhya is the South Indian spelling of the same name; today's vˈɪdjə matches (Vidya, n0008)
entries.notes: The h in 'dh' is a transliteration habit of this spelling, not an aspirate the bearers say. Hindi ʋ → v.

entries.name: Parvati
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi पार्वती: /pɑːɾ.ʋə.t̪iː/, Marathi /paɾ.ʋə.t̪i/; heavy first syllable stressed, as today
entries.notes: Today's pˈɑɹvəTi has the long 'ah', the schwa and the stress on the first syllable.

entries.name: Neelima
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi नीलिमा: /niː.lɪ.mɑː/; the heavy first syllable takes the stress (Hindustani weight rule ignores the final mora)

entries.name: Lalit
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi ललित: /lə.lɪt̪/ [lɐ.lɪt̪], short a and short i

alternatives.context: the same vowels with the stress on the closed last syllable, as Wikipedia's Hindustani weight rule gives (luh-LIT)

entries.notes: Today's luh-LEET has a long 'ee' the name doesn't have. Stress follows the batch precedent for short-vowel CV.CVC names (Nitin, Kapil, Bipin: first syllable); the vowel fix stands either way.

entries.name: Vinit
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi विनीत (vinīt): /ʋɪ.niːt̪/; Vinit is a spelling of this name (as Vineet, n0016, vi-NEET); the long ī takes the stress
entries.notes: Today's VIN-it misses the long ī and stresses the first syllable. Hindi ʋ → v.

entries.name: Sonu
entries.source: Hindi सोनू (sonū): long o, long ū; the first syllable carries the stress (Hindustani weight rule ignores the final mora), as today

entries.name: Dalip
entries.source: Hindi/Punjabi दलीप/ਦਲੀਪ (dalīp), a form of Dilip: short a, long ī; the heavy last syllable takes the stress, as Dilip (n0013, di-LEEP)
entries.notes: Today's DAL-ip has the 'cat' vowel, a short i and the stress on the first syllable.

entries.name: Mathai
entries.source: Wikipedia, Mathai: Malayalam മത്തായി, the Malayalam form of Matthew; no pronunciation source found

alternatives.context: Kenyan (Kikuyu) bearers, where th is the 'this' sound (Wikipedia, Wangari Maathai: /mɑːˈðaɪ/): mah-THIGH

entries.notes: Malayalam മത്തായി (the Malayalam form of Matthew) has a geminate dental t: mat-taa-yi, three syllables, long ā. Reviewer: Forebears puts India at 26,257 against Kenya 348, so the Malayalam reading is the target, not the Kikuyu one. The entry's claim that the consonant is t 'either way' is wrong for Kenyans: Kikuyu th is [ð] (Wikipedia gives Wangari Maathai /mɑːˈðaɪ/), which is why today's CMUdict mah-THAH-ee suits them. Still missing: a source for the Malayalam stress and whether English speakers keep three syllables. Candidate mut-TAH-ee.

entries.name: Anupam
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi अनुपम: /ə.nʊ.pəm/ [ɐ.nʊ.pɐ̃m]; short vowels throughout; the second-syllable stress follows the Anupama precedent (n0014), not a sourced rule

alternatives.context: the same vowels stressed on the closed last syllable, as Wikipedia's Hindustani weight rule gives (uh-noo-PUM)

entries.notes: Today's an-yuh-PAM adds a y, uses the 'cat' vowel and stresses the last syllable. A short [ʊ] in an open stressed syllable is English 'oo' (Uma, Shubha precedents). Reviewer: the entry said all syllables are light, but pam is closed (heavy), so Wikipedia's weight rule would stress it (as kidhar); the stress is unsourced either way and belongs to the open Hindi-stress question (Lalit, Madhur, Kapil). Low, as Anupama and Kapil.

entries.name: Nanditha
entries.source: Nandita नंदिता (nanditā); South Indian spellings write the dental t as 'th'; Nandita precedent (n0006) NUN-dih-tuh; heavy first syllable stressed (Dravidian initial stress agrees)
entries.notes: Today's nan-DITH-uh reads 'th' as in 'thin' and stresses the second syllable.

entries.name: Parvesh
entries.source: Hindi/Punjabi प्रवेश/परवेश (pravesh, 'entrance'): long e in the heavy last syllable takes the stress; closed eːʃ → ɛ (guide table; Rajesh precedent)
entries.notes: Today's pˌɑɹvˈɛʃ has the right stressed syllable and consonants; the secondary-stressed first vowel ('par' for the bearers' short 'pur') is a small quality difference, not worth churning.

entries.name: Kashmira
entries.source: Hindi कश्मीरा (kaśmīrā), from कश्मीर (Wiktionary: /kəʃ.miːɾ/): short a, long ī; the Hindustani weight rule stresses mī
entries.notes: Today's kash-MY-ruh reads the long ī as 'eye' and the short a as 'cat'.

entries.name: Chandrakant
entries.source: Hindi/Marathi चंद्रकांत (candrakānt): short a in chan-, long ā in -kānt; the superheavy last syllable takes the stress (Hindustani weight rule); Chandra precedent (n0002) CHUN-druh
entries.notes: Today's CHAN-druh-kunt uses the 'cat' vowel, stresses the first syllable and reduces the long ā.

entries.name: Jagadish
entries.source: Wiktionary, Sanskrit जगदीश: /d͡ʑɐ.ɡɐ.d̪iː.ɕɐ/, Hindi /d͡ʒəɡ.d̪iːʃ/; this spelling keeps the middle a (South Indian and Bengali bearers, Jagadish Chandra Bose); the long ī takes the stress as Jagdish (n0008)
entries.notes: Today's JAG-uh-dish stresses the first syllable with the 'cat' vowel and shortens the ī.

entries.name: Jayasree
entries.source: Malayalam ജയശ്രീ (jayaśrī) = Jaya + Sree; Jaya precedent (n0009) JY-uh; the Kerala spelling 'Sree' is said 'sree' (Srinivas precedent, n0013); Dravidian initial stress
entries.notes: Today's JAY-uh-sree uses 'ay' for the first vowel; Jaya is said JY-uh in Indian English.

entries.name: Jyotshna
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi ज्योत्स्ना (jyotsnā): /d͡ʒjoːt̪.snɑː/; Jyotshna is an eastern Indian spelling of the same name; Jyoti precedent (n0008) JYOH-tee
entries.notes: Today's JYAHCH-nuh has the wrong vowel and turns tsh into ch. Low: the 'tsh' spelling may stand for a 'sh' some bearers say (JYOHT-shnuh); not sourced.

entries.name: Madhur
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi मधुर: /mə.d̪ʱʊɾ/ [mɐ.d̪ʱʊɾ], short a and short u; aspirated dh → d

alternatives.context: the same vowels stressed on the closed last syllable, as Wikipedia's Hindustani weight rule gives (muh-DOOR)

entries.notes: Today's MAD-hur has the 'cat' vowel and splits dh into d + h. Stress follows the CV.CVC precedent (Nitin, Kapil); Madhu precedent (n0004) MUH-doo.

entries.name: Mandar
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi मंदार: /mən.d̪ɑːɾ/ [mɐ̃n̪.d̪äːɾ]; short a, long ā; the superheavy last syllable takes the stress (weight rule, as Parveen, n0010)
entries.notes: Today's MAN-dar has the 'cat' vowel and first-syllable stress. A Marathi name; Marathi stress is weak and no source gives it, hence medium.

entries.name: Ranjini
entries.source: Sanskrit रञ्जिनी / Malayalam രഞ്ജിനി (rañjinī): short a, short i, long final ī; the heavy first syllable takes the stress (Hindustani weight rule; Dravidian and Bengali initial stress agree); Ranjana precedent (n0008) RUN-juh-nuh
entries.notes: Today's rahn-JEE-nee stresses the second syllable and lengthens its short i.

entries.name: Satyajit
entries.source: Sanskrit/Hindi सत्यजित (satyajit): short a's, short i; the heavy first syllable takes the stress (Hindustani weight rule). Wikipedia gives the Bengali [ʃot̪ːod͡ʒit̪] for Satyajit Ray
entries.notes: Today's SAT-yah-jit uses the 'cat' vowel. The Sanskrit reading is chosen because Marathi, Hindi and Odia bearers say s and a short a; Bengali bearers (Satyajit Ray) say SHOH-toh-jeet. Review if Bengali bearers are thought to dominate (Santanu precedent, n0013). Reviewer: Forebears 2014: India 67,806 and Bangladesh 10,631 (Bengali); the Bengali share inside India is unknown, so this stays a decision.

entries.name: Srinivasan
entries.source: Tamil ஸ்ரீனிவாசன் (śrīnivācaṉ): long ī and ā; Tamil stresses the first syllable; Srinivas precedent (n0013) SREE-ni-vahs
entries.notes: Today's sree-nee-vah-SAHN stresses the short last syllable (British adds the 'lot' vowel).

entries.name: Sundar
entries.source: Wikipedia, Sundar Pichai: /ˈsʌndɑːr pɪˈtʃaɪ/ 'SUHN-darr'
entries.notes: Today's SOON-dar uses a long 'oo' for the short u.

entries.name: Vijayalakshmi
entries.source: Sanskrit विजयलक्ष्मी (vijayalakṣmī) = Vijaya + Lakshmi; Lakshmi (n0006, Merriam-Webster \ˈlək-shmē\) LUCK-shmee; Jaya (n0009) JY-uh
entries.notes: Only the stressed vowel changes: today's LAK- has the 'cat' vowel for the short a.

entries.name: Yogita
entries.source: Hindi योगिता (yogitā): hard g, long o, short i; the heavy first syllable takes the stress (Hindustani weight rule ignores the final mora)
entries.notes: Today's yoh-JEE-tuh softens the g to j and stresses the short i.

entries.name: Festus
entries.source: English reading of the Latin name (Latin [ˈfɛs.tus], Wiktionary); Nigerian and Ghanaian bearers say FES-tus, as today

entries.name: Gholamreza
entries.source: Wiktionary, Persian غلام: Iranian formal [qo.lɒ́ːm]; Reza (n0003) reh-ZAH; Persian compounds stress the last syllable
entries.notes: Today's goh-lum-RAY-zuh stresses Reza's first syllable and reduces the â. Persian gh [q~ɢ] → g; â → 'ah' (Payam).

entries.name: Ruhollah
entries.source: Persian روح‌الله (ruhollâh, 'spirit of God'): long u, short o, â; Persian stresses the last syllable
entries.notes: Today's roo-HAH-luh stresses the wrong syllable. Geminate ll → single l; final h dropped; â → 'ah'.

entries.name: Gbenga
entries.source: Wikipedia, Gbenga Akinnagbe: /ˈbɛŋɡə/ 'BENG-gə'

alternatives.context: closer to Yoruba labial-velar gb: GBENG-gah

entries.notes: Yoruba gb [ɡ͡b] has no English match; the English source drops the g. Today's JEE-beng-guh reads G as j and adds a syllable. Tones dropped.

entries.name: Aleksander
entries.source: Wiktionary, Aleksander: Polish /a.lɛkˈsan.dɛr/, Norwegian Bokmål /a.lɛkˈsan.dər/, Slovene /alɛksàːndər/

alternatives.context: English-speaking bearers (US, UK): al-ig-ZAN-der, today's reading

entries.notes: Polish (wd PL 1062), Norwegian (NO register 7.7k), Slovene and Estonian bearers far outnumber English ones (anglo_share 0.04) and say ks, not gz. Continental short a: US 'ah', GB 'a' (Magdalena precedent).

entries.name: Lutfia
entries.source: Arabic لطفية (luṭfiyya), feminine of Lutfi: the heavy penultimate syllable takes the stress (Arabic stress rule)
entries.notes: Today's LUT-fee-uh stresses the first syllable. The input's native spelling (Latifa/لطيفة) is a different name.

entries.name: Bülent
entries.source: Wikipedia, Bülent Ecevit: Turkish [byˈlænt]; final stress
