entries.notes: Persian â [ɒː] -> English 'ah'. Matches Ilham (n0011).

entries.name: Ken'ichi
entries.source: Japanese けんいち Ken'ichi [keɴ.i.tɕi]; English stresses the penultimate (guide convention, cf. Hiroshi)

entries.name: Ameya
entries.source: Marathi अमेय ameya: long e carries the stress

entries.name: Mihir
entries.source: Hindi मिहिर mihir [mɪ.ɦɪɾ]; Hindi weight rule as in earlier batches (stress the heaviest non-final syllable, the last of tied heavies; CV.CVC takes the first)
entries.notes: Today's reading has no primary stress (mˌihɪɹ). CV.CVC with first-syllable stress as Bipin and Nitin.

entries.name: Edy
entries.source: Indonesian Edy [ˈe.di] and Spanish/Swiss Edy: e = [e~ɛ], short (regular orthography)
entries.notes: Today's EE-dee reads e as English 'ee'.

entries.name: Navneet
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi नवनीत: /nəʋ.niːt̪/; long final syllable stressed (as Sandeep, Jagdeep)
entries.notes: Today's NAV-neet stresses the first syllable with the 'cat' vowel.

entries.name: Phi
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese Phi: [fi˧˧]
entries.notes: Tech list and the Greek letter phi (FY) read this token. Capitalised 'Phi' is common in English text for the letter (Phi Beta Kappa, Kappa Phi), so a name entry would break those. Name reading FEE recorded in us/gb.

entries.name: Ikbal
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic إقبال: /ʔiq.baːl/; stress on the long final syllable; same reading as Iqbal (n0003)
entries.notes: Today's IK-bul stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Sonali
entries.source: Hindi सोनाली sonālī: long ā carries the stress
entries.notes: US already right except an unstressed vowel; GB 'lot' vowel fixed.

entries.name: Piero
entries.source: Wiktionary, Italian Piero: /ˈpjɛ.ro/
entries.notes: Today's PEER-oh splits the 'ie' into an English 'eer'.

entries.name: Ranvir
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi रणवीर: /ɾəɳ.ʋiːɾ/ [ɾɐ̃ɳ.wiːɾ]; long ī in the final syllable stressed (Ranveer Singh)
entries.notes: Today's RAN-ver stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Nandini
entries.source: Wiktionary, Sanskrit नन्दिनी /nɐn.di.niː/; Hindi weight rule as in earlier batches (stress the heaviest non-final syllable, the last of tied heavies; CV.CVC takes the first); same as Nandita (n0006)
entries.notes: Today's nahn-DEE-nee stresses the light middle syllable.

entries.name: Romain
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Romain: /ʁɔ.mɛ̃/
entries.notes: Nasal ɛ̃ becomes English 'an' as in Julien, Alain and Sylvain (earlier batches). Today's roh-MAYN reads -ain as English 'ain'. FR register 191k.

entries.name: Hoài
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese Hoài: [hwaːj˨˩] (south [waːj˨˩]); oa as in Hoàng (n0006)
entries.notes: Today's HOH-ee reads o and i as separate vowels.

entries.name: Kiệt
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese Kiệt: [kiət̚˧˨ʔ] (south [kiək̚]); same pattern as Tuyết (n0010)
entries.notes: Today's KEET drops the glide to schwa.

entries.name: Lý
entries.source: Vietnamese Lý: y = [i] (regular orthography)
entries.notes: Today's LIE reads y as English 'eye'.

entries.name: Lộc
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese Lộc: [ləwk͡p̚˧˨ʔ] in all three dialect transcriptions
entries.notes: Same problem as Ngọc (n0005): the labial-velar coda k͡p has no English approximation source. The vowel [əw] is close to English 'oh', so LOHK is the candidate; today's LOCK reads ô as the 'lot' vowel.

entries.name: Ngân
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese Ngân: [ŋən˧˧] (south [ŋəŋ]); â -> 'u' as Vân and Quân (n0011), initial ng -> n as Nguyên (n0012)
entries.notes: Today's eng-GAHN adds a syllable.

entries.name: Phêrô
entries.source: Vietnamese Catholic form of Peter: Phê [fe] + rô [ɹo~zo]
entries.notes: Like Giuse (n0012): Vietnamese has no word stress and r is [z] in the north, [ɹ] in the south; no English source gives a reading. Candidate puts stress on the last syllable.

entries.name: Chirag
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi चिराग़: /t͡ʃɪ.ɾɑːɡ/; long final syllable stressed
entries.notes: Today's shi-RAG reads ch as 'sh' and uses the 'cat' vowel.

entries.name: Sonya
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Sonya: /ˈsoʊnjə/, /ˈsɑnjə/; Russian Соня [ˈsonʲə]

entries.name: Mansi
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi मानसी: /mɑːn.siː/
entries.notes: Today's MAN-see uses the 'cat' vowel.

entries.name: Sumeet
entries.source: Hindi सुमीत sumīt: long ī in the final syllable stressed (as Sunil, Pradeep)
entries.notes: Today's SUM-eet stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Soumya
entries.source: South Indian Soumya സൗമ്യ/ಸೌಮ್ಯ [saumja] (Soumya Swaminathan); Wiktionary, Hindi सौम्या: /sɔːm.jɑː/
entries.notes: The ou spelling is mostly South Indian, where au is a diphthong. Today's SOOM-yuh reads ou as 'oo'.

entries.name: Ambika
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi अंबिका: /əm.bɪ.kɑː/; Hindi weight rule as in earlier batches (stress the heaviest non-final syllable, the last of tied heavies; CV.CVC takes the first)
entries.notes: Today's AM-bi-kuh uses the 'cat' vowel for Hindi short a [ə].

entries.name: Jacobus
entries.source: Wiktionary, Latin Jacobus: [jaːˈkoː.bʊs]; Dutch keeps the Latin stress and says j as [j] (Dutch orthography)
entries.notes: Dutch and Afrikaans j is 'y'; today's juh-KOH-bus is the English reading.

entries.name: Adem
entries.source: Wikipedia, Adem (name): Turkish [ɑ:ˈdem], English /ˈædɛm/; Wiktionary, Albanian Adem: /aˈdem/
entries.notes: Turkish and Albanian bearers stress -DEM; today's AD-im is the English /ˈædɛm/ pattern. Reviewer: Forebears 2014 gives Ethiopia 268,748 and Turkey 228,231, then Bosnia 6,335, North Macedonia 6,240, Kosovo 4,753, Albania 2,141, France 831. The Ethiopian (Oromo, Somali and Amharic Adem) stress is not sourced, so the Turkish reading, sourced and the next largest, stays. Maghrebi and Bosnian bearers stress the first syllable.

entries.name: Parminder
entries.source: Punjabi ਪਰਮਿੰਦਰ parmindar; stress on -min- as Surinder and Ravinder in earlier batches
entries.notes: Today's PAR-mine-der reads i as 'eye'.

entries.name: Gagan
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi गगन: /ɡə.ɡən/
entries.notes: Today's GAY-gun reads a as English 'ay'.

entries.name: Farooq
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic فاروق: /faː.ruːq/; q -> k; same reading as Farouk (n0018)
entries.notes: Today's fuh-RUUK has the short 'book' vowel; the Arabic ū is long.

entries.name: Vaishali
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi वैशाली: /ʋɛː.ʃɑː.liː/; long ā carries the stress
entries.notes: Stress already right in US; GB had the 'lot' vowel. Hindi ai is [ɛː], 'eh' as Vaishnavi (n0011), not today's 'ay'.

entries.name: Malini
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi मालिनी: /mɑː.lɪ.niː/; long first syllable stressed
entries.notes: Today's mah-LEE-nee stresses the light middle syllable.

entries.name: Shraddha
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi श्रद्धा: /ʃɾəd̪.d̪ʱɑː/
entries.notes: Today's SHRAD-uh uses the 'cat' vowel.

entries.name: Hiren
entries.source: Gujarati હિરેન hiren: long e in the closed final syllable takes the stress (as Ramesh, Mukesh)
entries.notes: Today's HY-run reads i as 'eye'.

entries.name: Sangeeta
entries.source: Hindi संगीता saṅgītā: long ī carries the stress
entries.notes: Only the unstressed first vowel differs.

entries.name: Mohini
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi मोहिनी: /moː.ɦɪ.niː/; long first syllable stressed
entries.notes: Today's moh-HEE-nee lengthens and stresses the short i.

entries.name: Manasi
entries.source: Marathi मानसी mānasī; long first syllable stressed
entries.notes: Today's mah-NAH-see stresses the short middle a.

entries.name: Daksha
entries.source: Hindi दक्षा dakṣā; closed first syllable stressed
entries.notes: Today's DAK-shuh uses the 'cat' vowel.

entries.name: Shivangi
entries.source: Hindi शिवांगी śivāṅgī: long ā carries the stress; g is hard
entries.notes: Today's shi-VAN-jee softens the g and uses the 'cat' vowel.

entries.name: Nima
entries.source: Wiktionary, Persian نیما (nimâ), from Mazanderani (no IPA); Behind the Name Nima (2), Persian; Persian final stress
entries.notes: As n0021 (US). Today's NEE-muh stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Kamla
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi कमला: /kəm.lɑː/; Wikipedia, Kamla Persad-Bissessar: [kəmlɑː]
entries.notes: Today's KAM-luh uses the 'cat' vowel.

entries.name: Anuja
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi अनुजा: /ə.nʊ.d͡ʒɑː/
entries.notes: Today's ah-NOO-yuh reads j as 'y'.

entries.name: Vinesh
entries.source: Hindi विनेश vineś (Vinesh Phogat): long e in the final syllable stressed

entries.name: Mithun
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi मिथुन: /mɪ.t̪ʰʊn/ (th is an aspirated t, not English th)
entries.notes: Today's MITH-un uses English θ.

entries.name: Parul
entries.source: Hindi पारुल pārul; long first syllable stressed
entries.notes: Today's PAIR-ul reads a as in 'parent'.

entries.name: Suyash
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi सुयश: /sʊ.jəʃ/

alternatives.context: first-syllable stress, the convention for unprefixed CV.CVC names (Mihir, Mukul, Sanat in this batch): SOO-yush

entries.notes: Today's SY-ash merges u-y into 'eye'. Reviewer: final stress kept because su- is a prefix (su + yaś); prefixed CV.CVC names keep the root stressed, as Sumit (n0009) and Anil (n0001), while unprefixed ones (Nitin, Mihir) take the first syllable.

entries.name: Nupur
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi नूपुर: /nuː.pʊɾ/
entries.notes: Only the unstressed vowel differs.

entries.name: Malvika
entries.source: Hindi मालविका mālvikā; long first syllable stressed
entries.notes: Today's MAL-vi-kuh uses the 'cat' vowel.

entries.name: Karthika
entries.source: Malayalam കാർത്തിക kārttika; th is a dental t; long first syllable stressed (Dravidian initial stress)
entries.notes: Today's kar-THEE-kuh uses English θ and stresses the short i.

entries.name: Aanchal
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi आँचल: /ɑ̃ː.t͡ʃəl/; long nasal first syllable stressed
entries.notes: US already right; GB-only fix ('lot' vowel today).

entries.name: Saurabh
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi सौरभ: /sɔː.ɾəbʱ/

entries.name: Sidhant
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi सिद्धांत: /sɪd̪.d̪ʱɑːnt̪/; long final syllable stressed (as Siddharth)
entries.notes: Today's SID-unt reduces the long ā.

entries.name: Prerna
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi प्रेरणा: /pɾeːɾ.ɳɑː/
entries.notes: Closed syllable e before r: today's 'air' vowel is the usual English approximation.

entries.name: Nitish
entries.source: Hindi नीतीश nītīś (Nitish Kumar): both i long; the final superheavy syllable is stressed (as Satish)
entries.notes: Today's NY-tish reads i as 'eye'.

entries.name: Chand
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi चंद: /t͡ʃənd̪/ (the name element in Dhyan Chand, Premchand); चाँद 'moon': /t͡ʃɑːnd̪/

alternatives.context: चाँद/چاند cā̃d 'moon' (CHAHND), Urdu and Punjabi use

entries.notes: Today's CHAND with the 'cat' vowel matches neither. Which of the two the bearers of this spelling use is not sourced.

entries.name: Laxman
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi लक्ष्मण: /lək.ʂməɳ/ (x spells kṣ, as in Lakshmi)
entries.notes: Today's LAX-mun reads x as English 'ks'.

entries.name: Sanat
entries.source: Hindi सनत sanat; CV.CVC with first-syllable stress as Bipin and Nitin
entries.notes: Today's SAN-ut uses the 'cat' vowel.

entries.name: Anwesha
entries.source: Sanskrit अन्वेषा anveṣā; long e carries the stress by the Hindi weight rule
entries.notes: Open syllable e is 'ay', not today's 'eh'. Bengali stresses the first syllable; not sourced.

entries.name: Chhaya
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi छाया: /t͡ʃʰɑː.jɑː/
entries.notes: Today's CHY-uh merges ā-y into 'eye'.

entries.name: Bharti
entries.source: Hindi भारती bhārtī (Sanskrit /bʱɑː.ɾɐ.tiː/); aspiration has no English equivalent

entries.name: Sushmita
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi सुष्मिता: /sʊʂ.mɪ.t̪ɑː/ (short i); Hindi weight rule as in earlier batches (stress the heaviest non-final syllable, the last of tied heavies; CV.CVC takes the first) (the closed first syllable); Bengali stresses the first syllable too
entries.notes: Today's soosh-MEE-tuh lengthens the short i (cf. Smita, n0008) and stresses it.

entries.name: Balwant
entries.source: Hindi/Punjabi बलवंत balvant [bəl.ʋənt̪]; Wikipedia, Hindustani phonology: the final syllable is stressed if it is extra-heavy and no other syllable is (here ʋənt̪, VCC), as Hemant (n0013) and Vasant (n0004)

alternatives.context: first-syllable stress (BUL-wunt); Punjabi stress for this name is not sourced

entries.notes: Reviewer: the entry cited the weight rule but stressed the closed first syllable; under that rule the extra-heavy final syllable wins (Hemant hay-MUNT, with a heavy first syllable, is the precedent). Short a is 'uh' in both syllables. Today's BAHL-wunt uses 'ah' for short a.

entries.name: Lokesh
entries.source: Hindi लोकेश lokeś; final superheavy syllable stressed as Mukesh and Ramesh
entries.notes: Today's LOHKSH drops a syllable.

entries.name: Sudip
entries.source: Hindi/Bengali सुदीप sudīp; long final syllable stressed (as Pradip, Dilip)
entries.notes: Today's SOO-dip shortens the long ī.

entries.name: Anindita
entries.source: Sanskrit अनिन्दिता aninditā; closed syllable -nin- stressed as Arindam (n0008)
entries.notes: Today's ah-nin-DEE-tuh stresses the short i.

entries.name: Mukul
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi मुकुल: /mʊ.kʊl/; CV.CVC with first-syllable stress as Bipin and Nitin

alternatives.context: final stress by Wikipedia's Hindustani rule (moo-KOOL)

entries.notes: Today's MYOO-kul adds a 'y'. Stress is the open Hindi CV.CVC question.

entries.name: Jamuna
entries.source: Wikipedia, Yamuna: Hindustani [jəmʊnɑː], no stress marked (Jamuna is the same name with j); every syllable is light once the final mora is ignored, so the penult takes the stress (Wikipedia, Hindustani phonology), as Anuja in this batch and Anupam (n0019); Forebears 2014: India 404,217, Bangladesh 2,383

alternatives.context: first-syllable stress, Tamil and Telugu bearers (Singapore, Sri Lanka, Malaysia) by Dravidian initial stress, and Bengali initial stress: JUM-oo-nuh

entries.notes: Reviewer: the first-syllable stress was unsourced (the Yamuna article gives no English IPA) and combined Hindi vowels with Bengali stress. Forebears puts nearly all bearers in India, where the Hindi reading is the main one. A short [ʊ] in an open stressed syllable is English 'oo' (Anupam precedent). Today's juh-MYOO-nuh adds a 'y'.

entries.name: Ratan
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi रतन: /ɾə.t̪ən/; Wikipedia, Ratan Tata: [rətən]
entries.notes: Today's RAY-tun reads a as English 'ay'.

entries.name: Deepthi
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi दीप्ति: /d̪iːp.t̪iː/; South Indian spelling Deepthi writes the dental t as th
entries.notes: Today's DEEP-thee uses English θ.

entries.name: Amruta
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi अमृता: /əm.ɾɪ.t̪ɑː/ (heavy first syllable); Marathi says ṛ as ru, which the spelling records; as Amrita (n0004)
entries.notes: Today's am-ROO-tuh uses the 'cat' vowel and stresses the middle.

entries.name: Sunetra
entries.source: Sanskrit सुनेत्रा sunetrā; e in the closed syllable carries the stress

entries.name: Madhumita
entries.source: Sanskrit मधुमिता madhumitā; first-syllable stress as Madhu (n0004) and Bengali initial stress

alternatives.context: Hindustani weight rule: every syllable light, so the penult (muh-doo-MIT-uh)

entries.notes: Today's mud-HYOO-muh-tuh splits dh and adds a 'y'.

entries.name: Ranjan
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi रंजन: /ɾən.d͡ʒən/
entries.notes: Today's RAN-jun uses the 'cat' vowel.

entries.name: Amrut
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi अमृत: /əm.ɾɪt̪/ (heavy first syllable); Marathi/Gujarati ṛ as ru, as the spelling records
entries.notes: Today's AM-rut uses the 'cat' vowel.

entries.name: Bal
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi बाल: /bɑːl/; Marathi बाळ bāḷ (Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Bal Thackeray), long ā
entries.notes: Today's BAL uses the 'cat' vowel.

entries.name: Bhanu
entries.source: Wiktionary, Sanskrit भानु: /bʱɑː.nu/
entries.notes: US already right; GB-only fix ('lot' vowel today).

entries.name: Bibhuti
entries.source: Odia ବିଭୂତି / Bengali বিভূতি bibhūti; long ū stressed by the Hindi weight rule
entries.notes: Today's bib-HOO-tee splits the aspirated bh into b + h.

entries.name: Chinmayee
entries.source: Sanskrit चिन्मयी cinmayī; closed first syllable stressed by the Hindi weight rule
entries.notes: Today's chin-my-EE stresses the final vowel.

entries.name: Debabrata
entries.source: Bengali দেবব্রত [d̪ebobrɔt̪o]; Bengali stresses the first syllable (as Debasish, n0013)
entries.notes: Today's dih-bah-BRAH-tuh is a spelling reading. Bengali vowels not sourced beyond the script.

entries.name: Gajanan
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi गजानन: /ɡə.d͡ʒɑː.nən/; long ā carries the stress
entries.notes: Today's guh-JAN-un uses the 'cat' vowel.

entries.name: Ganapati
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi गणपति: /ɡəɳ.pə.t̪iː/ (syncopated, heavy first syllable); South Indian Ganapati/Ganapathi has Dravidian first-syllable stress
entries.notes: Today's guh-nuh-PUH-tee (dictionary) stresses the third syllable; neither Hindi nor the South Indian bearers do.

entries.name: Ghanshyam
entries.source: Hindi घनश्याम ghanśyām; long final syllable stressed (Shyam, n0004)
entries.notes: Today's GAHN-shyahm stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Gunjan
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi गुंजन: /ɡʊn.d͡ʒən/
entries.notes: Today's GUN-jun uses the 'cup' vowel for short u.

entries.name: Jayanta
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi जयंत: /d͡ʒə.jənt̪/ (Hindi drops the final a); Bengali জয়ন্ত

alternatives.context: Bengali/Odia initial stress and o vowels (JAW-yon-toh)

entries.notes: Spelling with -a is mostly Bengali, Assamese and Odia, whose speakers stress the first syllable with o vowels; Indian English says juh-YUN-tuh. No source settles it. Today's jy-AHN-tuh is wrong either way.

entries.name: Jogendra
entries.source: Hindi जोगेन्द्र jogendra; -gen- stressed as Rajendra and Narendra

entries.name: Kedarnath
entries.source: Hindi केदारनाथ kedārnāth: Kedar (long ā, stressed) + nath with secondary stress; th is aspirated t (as Jagannath, Gopinath)
entries.notes: Today's KED-ar-nath uses English θ and the 'bed' vowel.

entries.name: Kuriakose
entries.source: Malayalam കുര്യാക്കോസ് kuryākkōs (Kerala Syrian Christian form of Cyriacus)
entries.notes: No pronunciation source found. The script gives ku-ryaa-kkoo-s; whether Kerala English speakers stress the first syllable or -ryaa- is not sourced. Today's koo-ree-uh-KOHS is a guess.

entries.name: Naval
entries.source: Wikipedia, Ratan Tata: Hindi [rətən nəʋəl ʈaːʈaː] (Naval as a given/middle name)
entries.notes: Ordinary English word 'naval' (NAY-vul), common. The Hindi name नवल is NUV-ul; the name reading is in us/gb but must not replace the adjective.

entries.name: Pandurang
entries.source: Marathi पांडुरंग pāṇḍuraṅg; long first syllable stressed, final g sounded
entries.notes: Today's pan-DOOR-ung stresses the short u.

entries.name: Pradnya
entries.source: Wiktionary, प्रज्ञा: Hindi /pɾəd͡ʒ.ɲɑː/ [pɾɐɡ.jäː]; Marathi says jñ as [dɲ], which the spelling Pradnya records
entries.notes: Today's PRAD-nyuh uses the 'cat' vowel.

entries.name: Priyamvada
entries.source: Sanskrit प्रियंवदा priyaṃvadā; closed syllable -yam- stressed (as Priyanka, n0004)
entries.notes: Today's pree-yahm-VAH-duh stresses the short va.

entries.name: Rajagopal
entries.source: Tamil/Telugu Rājagōpāl: rāja + gōpāl, primary on gō, secondary on rā (as Gopinath, n0013)

alternatives.context: Dravidian first-syllable stress, as Srinivas (n0013) and Karthika in this batch: RAH-juh-goh-pahl
Hindustani weight rule (extra-heavy final syllable) and the Gopal precedent (n0002, goh-PAHL): rah-juh-goh-PAHL

entries.notes: Today's ruh-JAG-uh-pul is a spelling reading. Reviewer: the chosen primary on goh is the usual Indian English compound stress but follows neither batch rule; the Gopinath precedent cited stresses the first syllable. No source found for this name (web search, name sites disagree). Low confidence; the two rule-based readings are in alternatives.

entries.name: Ratilal
entries.source: Gujarati રતિલાલ ratilāl: rati + lāl, first-syllable primary and secondary on lal (as Sitaram, n0011)
entries.notes: Today's RAT-uh-lul uses the 'cat' vowel and reduces lāl.

entries.name: Rituparna
entries.source: Bengali ঋতুপর্ণা [ritupɔrna] (Rituparna Sengupta); Bengali stresses the first syllable
entries.notes: Today's rit-uh-PAR-nuh reads par as in 'car'.

entries.name: Satyadev
entries.source: Hindi सत्यदेव satyadev: satya + dev, final superheavy syllable stressed (as Hardev, n0013)
entries.notes: Today's SAT-yah-dev uses the 'cat' and 'bed' vowels.

entries.name: Somayajulu
entries.source: Telugu సోమయాజులు sōmayājulu; long yā stressed by the Hindi weight rule, secondary on sō (as Satyanarayana, n0008)

alternatives.context: Telugu initial stress, as Srinivas (n0013): SOH-muh-yah-joo-loo

entries.notes: Today's soh-mah-yah-JOO-loo stresses the short u.

entries.name: Sooraj
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi सूरज: /suː.ɾəd͡ʒ/
entries.notes: Today's SUR-eye misreads the final j.

entries.name: Soundarya
entries.source: Kannada ಸೌಂದರ್ಯ saundarya (Soundarya, actress); ou is a diphthong; Dravidian initial stress

alternatives.context: Hindi सौंदर्या with Hindi au [ɔː]: SAWN-dur-yuh (the Hindi weight rule also stresses the extra-heavy first syllable)

entries.notes: Today's sown-DAR-ee-uh adds a syllable. Reviewer: the old alternative put the stress on -dur- 'by the Hindi weight rule', but that rule stresses the extra-heavy first syllable too, so both readings stress the first syllable and differ only in the vowel.

entries.name: Sripati
entries.source: Wiktionary, Sanskrit श्रीपति: /ɕɾiː.pɐ.ti/; long first syllable stressed, Sri as in Srinivas (n0013)
entries.notes: Today's sree-PAH-tee stresses the short a.

entries.name: Subrahmanyan
entries.source: Tamil சுப்பிரமணியன் Cuppiramaṇiyaṉ (Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar); Sanskrit subrahmaṇya, all short a; Wikipedia gives his surname as English /ˌtʃəndrəˈʃeɪkər/, short a as ə; stress on the heavy -man- by the Hindustani weight rule
entries.notes: Today's soo-bruh-MAY-nee-un reads a as English 'ay'. Reviewer: the stressed vowel is a short a, so 'uh' (as Priyanka, Ambika), not 'ah'. Tamil speakers also say a six-syllable Subramaniyan; the spelling with -nyan is the Sanskritised form.

entries.name: Suniti
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi सुनीति: /sʊ.niː.t̪iː/; long ī stressed

entries.name: Susheela
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi सुशीला: /sʊ.ʃiː.lɑː/; long ī stressed

entries.name: Triloki
entries.source: Hindi त्रिलोकी (trilokī): short i, long o and ī; the long -lō- takes the stress (Hindustani weight rule)
entries.notes: Today's tri-LOH-kee matches.

entries.name: Tripti
entries.source: Hindi तृप्ति (tṛpti): [t̪ɾɪp.t̪iː]; the closed first syllable takes the stress
entries.notes: Today's TRIP-tee matches; Hindi dental t is English t. (The input's native form संतुष्टि is a synonym, not this name.)

entries.name: Umakant
entries.source: Hindi उमाकांत (umākānt): short u, long ā in -mā- and -kānt; the superheavy last syllable takes the stress (Hindustani weight rule, as Chandrakant n0019)
entries.notes: Today's YOO-muh-kunt adds a y, reduces both long ā and stresses the first syllable. The vowels are certain; the stress is not sourced (Ramakant, n0011, was left unresolved over the same -mā-/-kānt choice). Review together with Ramakant.

entries.name: Vartika
entries.source: Hindi वर्तिका (vartikā): [ʋəɾ.t̪ɪ.kɑː]; the closed first syllable takes the stress
entries.notes: Today's VAR-ti-kuh matches: English has no 'uh' before r, so 'ar' is the usual approximation of ər (as Arjun, n0001); Hindi ʋ is English v.

entries.name: Viswanathan
entries.source: Tamil விசுவநாதன் / Sanskrit Viśvanātha: ś is sh, long ā in -nā-, 'th' marks a dental t (no θ); nickname 'Vishy' (Viswanathan Anand) confirms the sh
entries.notes: Today's VIZ-wuh-nuh-thun reads s as z, th as in 'thin' and stresses the first syllable. No source marks the stress; Indian English speakers stress the long -nā-. Dental t (spelled th in Tamil names) is English t.

entries.name: Román
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Román: /roˈman/ (the written accent marks final stress)
entries.notes: Today's ROH-mun is the English Roman.

entries.name: Casper
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Casper: /ˈkæspə(ɹ)/; Danish and Norwegian Casper also stress KAS-
entries.notes: English (US 4.3k, GB 3.5k) and Scandinavian bearers say it like today.

entries.name: Naim
entries.region: France, Spain, US, Turkey, Palestine, Albania
entries.source: Arabic نعيم Naʿīm [naˈʕiːm]; Turkish and Albanian Naim [naˈim]: stress on the long ī
entries.notes: Today's NY-im reads 'ai' as one vowel. ʿayn dropped with the vowels kept apart (guide).

entries.name: Fransisca
entries.source: Indonesian spelling of Francisca: penultimate stress, i in the closed syllable [ɪ] (Indonesian orthography)
entries.notes: Today's fran-SIS-kuh has the right stressed syllable and consonants; only the unstressed first vowel ('cat' for Indonesian a) differs.

entries.name: Elif
entries.source: Turkish Elif: final stress, i is 'ee' (Turkish names stress the last syllable)
entries.notes: Today's EL-if stresses the first syllable. Turkish bearers (wd TR 274; FR register 5.2k) dominate.

entries.name: Macy
entries.source: English Macy: /ˈmeɪsi/ (CMUdict)
entries.notes: Light verification.

entries.name: Aisyah
entries.source: Indonesian/Malay spelling of ʿĀʾisha: a-i-syah, sy is sh, penultimate stress (Indonesian orthography)
entries.notes: Today's eye-ZY-uh reads s as z and y as a vowel.

entries.name: Agung
entries.source: Indonesian agung [ˈaɡʊŋ] ('great'): penultimate stress, a is 'ah', u in the closed final syllable [ʊ] (Indonesian orthography)
entries.notes: Today's AY-gung reads a as 'ay' and u as 'cup'.

entries.name: Abdul Ghaffar
entries.source: Arabic عبد الغفار ʿAbd al-Ghaffār: stress on the long ā; gh [ɣ] → g (guide); Abdul as kept in earlier batches
entries.notes: Today's ab-DOOL guh-FAR matches (as Abdul Ghafoor, n0014).

entries.name: Armin
entries.source: German Armin: [ˈaʁmiːn] (Armin Laschet); long i in the second syllable
entries.notes: German-speaking bearers (wd DE 317, AT 75, CH 67) dominate. Today's AR-mun reduces the long ee, which German, Bosnian and Persian bearers all keep.

entries.name: Mihai
entries.source: Wiktionary, Romanian Mihai: /miˈhaj/
entries.notes: Today's mee-HY matches.

entries.name: Ross
entries.source: English Ross: /ɹɒs/, US /ɹɔs/, /ɹɑs/
entries.notes: Light verification.

entries.name: Alphonsus
entries.source: English Alphonsus: /ælˈfɒnsəs/
entries.notes: Today's al-FON-sus matches the Irish, Dutch (Latin form) and Nigerian usage.

entries.name: Jeanette
entries.source: English Jeanette: /dʒəˈnɛt/

alternatives.context: Norwegian, Swedish and Danish bearers: sha-NET

entries.notes: US bearers (137.8k) far outnumber the Scandinavian ones (NO 3.9k).

entries.name: Valeri
entries.source: Russian Валерий [vɐˈlʲerʲɪj]: stress on -le-; stressed e in an open syllable is 'ay' (guide table, as Valeria n0009)

alternatives.context: US women's variant of Valerie (US 1.9k): VAL-uh-ree

entries.notes: Today's vah-LERR-ee is close (same stressed syllable); the fix is the stressed vowel, as Valeria. Bulgarian Валери has open [ɛ].

entries.name: Corey
entries.source: English Corey: /ˈkɔɹi/
entries.notes: Light verification.

entries.name: Chinedu
entries.source: Igbo Chinedu [tʃinedu]: e in an open syllable is 'ay' (guide); Nigerian English stresses the second syllable (as Emeka, n0013)
entries.notes: Today's chi-NAY-doo matches; tones dropped.

entries.name: Ruqayyah
entries.source: Arabic رقية Ruqayya [ru.qaj.ja]: q → k, -ay- is 'eye', the heavy -qay- takes the stress; geminate yy said once
entries.notes: Today's roo-KAY-uh reads -ay- as 'ay'. British Muslim bearers (GB register 1.7k) say roo-KYE-yah.

entries.name: Bìxiá
entries.source: Mandarin 碧霞 bìxiá: bi [pi] + xia [ɕja] (standard pinyin values, Help:IPA/Mandarin); x → sh (guide), -ia one syllable as Xia (n0005); primary stress on the last syllable, secondary on the first (guide's convention)
entries.notes: Today's BIK-see-uh reads x as ks.

entries.name: Marcin
entries.source: Wiktionary, Polish Marcin: /ˈmar.t͡ɕin/; ci [t͡ɕ] → ch (guide)
entries.notes: Today's mar-SEEN reads c as s and stresses the last syllable; Polish stresses the penultimate.

entries.name: Yasir
entries.region: US, UK, Spain, Turkey, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia
entries.source: Arabic ياسر Yāsir [ˈjaːsir]: first-syllable stress on the long ā
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today says the 'lot' vowel (YOSS-uh); bearers say 'ah'. US already right.

entries.name: Ola
entries.source: Norwegian and Swedish Ola (from Olav/Olof): long o is [uː] in both, first-syllable stress (Wiktionary has no IPA; Norwegian/Swedish orthography)

alternatives.context: the US women's name of the late 1800s (US 13.1k since 1925): OH-luh, today's reading

entries.notes: Population call to review: Norwegian (NO register 9.3k) and Swedish (wd SE 214) men outnumber the US group (13.1k). Today's reading comes from the tech list (OLA, the Indian ride-hailing company); that clash is settled at merge.

entries.name: Bárbara
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Bárbara: /ˈbaɾbaɾa/
entries.notes: Today's BAR-buh-ruh matches the stress and stressed vowel; only unstressed vowels are reduced.

entries.name: Nino
entries.source: Italian Nino /ˈni.no/; Georgian ნინო [nino]; Spanish [ˈnino]

alternatives.context: French bearers (FR register 24.8k): final stress, nee-NOH

entries.notes: French bearers are the largest register count, but Italian, Georgian (Nino is among Georgia's most common women's names), Spanish, Slovene and German bearers all stress the first syllable and together outnumber them.

entries.name: Monday
entries.notes: The weekday 'Monday', always capitalised. Nigerian bearers say the name like the day, so today's reading fits both and nothing needs shipping.

entries.name: Rosalie
entries.source: English Rosalie: /ˈɹoʊzəli/
entries.notes: usage english: US 67.7k against FR 10.5k and Quebec.

entries.name: Dele
entries.source: Yoruba Délé (short for Bámidélé, Adédèlé): e (not ẹ) is [e], 'ay' in open syllables (guide table, as Tunde and Adebayo); tones dropped

alternatives.context: Dele Alli, the English footballer: DEL-ee

entries.notes: Collides with the proofreading word 'dele' (rare, technical, never capitalised in running text), so it is treated as a name (guide). Today's DEE-lee is that word.
entries.word_check: gold has 'dele'; kept: 'dele' is a proofreading mark

entries.name: Naoki
entries.source: Japanese なおき Naoki [naoki]: three syllables, a is 'ah'; English stresses the penultimate (guide)
entries.notes: Today's nay-OH-kee reads the a as 'ay'.

entries.name: Natacha
entries.source: French Natacha: /na.ta.ʃa/; French names take final stress in English (guide)

alternatives.context: the English and Russian-style Natasha: nuh-TAH-shuh

entries.notes: FR register 29.9k dominates. Today's nuh-TATCH-uh reads ch as in 'church'. Review: English speakers often say nuh-TAH-shuh for French bearers too (Natacha Atlas).

entries.name: Saud
entries.source: Wikipedia, House of Saud: Arabic ʾĀl Suʿūd [ʔaːl sʊʕuːd]; ʿayn dropped with the vowels kept apart (guide)

alternatives.context: common English and South Asian rendering: sah-OOD
English one-syllable rendering in 'House of Saud': SOWD

entries.notes: Today's SAWD fits no group. Arabic سعود is Suʿūd, two syllables with the stress on the long ū.

entries.name: Alexey
entries.source: Wiktionary, Russian Алексей: [ɐlʲɪkˈsʲej], final stress
entries.notes: Today's uh-LEK-see is the English Alexei guess with the wrong stress and final vowel.

entries.name: Mehrdad
entries.source: Behind the Name, Mehrdad: /mehɾ.ˈdɒːd/; Wiktionary مهرداد Iran formal [meɦɹ.d̪ɒ́ːd̪̥]
entries.notes: h before r in the same syllable is dropped, as English speakers do (and Manouchehr, Mehrdad in earlier batches). Matches n0022. Today's MAIR-dad stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Afsaneh
entries.source: Behind the Name, Afsaneh: /ʔæf.sɒː.ˈne/; Wiktionary افسانه Iran formal [ʔæf.sɒː.né]
entries.notes: Final -eh is Persian [e]; written 'ay' (A), the nearest full English vowel, as Fatemeh and Afsaneh in earlier batches (Iranians' own vowel has no glide). Matches n0022 (plus a secondary stress). Today's af-SAHN-eh stresses the second syllable.

entries.name: Jojo
entries.source: English Jojo /ˈdʒoʊdʒoʊ/; Ghanaian (Fante) Jojo, the Monday-born name, is said the same
entries.notes: Today's JOH-joh matches every group.

entries.name: Cornelia
entries.region: Netherlands, Germany, Austria, Romania, Spain, US
entries.source: Wiktionary, Dutch Cornelia: /ˌkɔrˈneː.li.aː/; Italian /korˈnɛ.lja/; English /kɔɹˈniliə/
entries.notes: anglo_share 0.04: Dutch, German, Austrian, Romanian, Spanish and Norwegian bearers all say kor-NAY-lee-a and together outnumber the English group.

entries.name: Beth
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Beth: /bɛθ/
entries.notes: Collision with 'beth' (the Hebrew letter, uncommon). Today's 'BAYT' is that letter's reading, which a capitalised Beth almost never is: it is the very common name (US 155k), and names like Beth Israel are also said BETH in English. Treated as a name (guide).
entries.word_check: gold has 'beth'; kept: 'beth' (the Hebrew letter) is rare

entries.name: Remi
entries.source: English Remi: /ˈɹɛmi/; Yoruba Rẹ̀mí and Japanese レミ also stress the first syllable
entries.notes: US (24.7k), GB (5.1k), Canada and Nigerian bearers say REM-ee; French bearers mostly write Rémi.

entries.name: Noura
entries.region: France, Spain, US, UK, Tunisia, Egypt
entries.source: Arabic نورة Nūra [ˈnuːra]: first-syllable stress on the long ū
entries.notes: Today's nˈʊɹə (NOOR-uh) matches, as Noor (n0006) and Nour (n0015).

entries.name: Adib
entries.source: Arabic أديب Adīb [ʔaˈdiːb]; Persian ادیب [æˈdiːb]: stress on the long ī
entries.notes: Today's uh-DIB uses the short 'bit' vowel for the long ī.

entries.name: Fayçal
entries.source: Arabic فيصل Fayṣal [ˈfajsˤal]; ç is French s (as Faisal, n0002, FY-sul)
entries.notes: Today's FAY-kul reads ç as k. Same reading as Faisal.

entries.name: Modeste
entries.region: France, Belgium, DR Congo, Côte d'Ivoire
entries.source: French Modeste: /mɔ.dɛst/, final stress in English
entries.notes: Today's moh-DEST has the right stress and consonants; only the unstressed o differs (oh vs aw).

entries.name: Daphne
entries.source: English Daphne: /ˈdæfni/
entries.notes: Light verification.

entries.name: Celestino
entries.source: Spanish Celestino: /selesˈtino/ (Latin America; Spain /θ/), penultimate stress (Spanish orthography); Italian /tʃelesˈtiːno/
entries.notes: Spanish bearers (ES 5.9k, US 2.3k, Argentina, Mexico) outnumber Italian ones; Spanish c before e is s (Spain's θ is said s by English speakers).

entries.name: Katrina
entries.source: English Katrina: /kəˈtɹiːnə/
entries.notes: Light verification.

entries.name: Flavia
entries.source: Italian Flavia /ˈflaːvja/, Spanish /ˈflaβja/, Portuguese Flávia: all stress 'flah'
entries.notes: Every bearer group says 'ah'; today's FLAV-ee-uh uses the 'cat' vowel.

entries.name: Habiba
entries.source: Arabic حبيبة Ḥabība [ħaˈbiːba]: stress on the long ī; ḥ → h (guide)
entries.notes: Today's huh-BEE-buh matches.

entries.name: Clemente
entries.source: Spanish Clemente /kleˈmente/, Italian /kleˈmɛnte/: penultimate stress, final e is 'ay' (guide table)
entries.notes: Today's kluh-MEN-tay matches; only the unstressed first vowel is reduced.

entries.name: Lilia
entries.source: Spanish and Italian Lilia /ˈlilja/; Russian Лилия [ˈlʲilʲɪjə]: first-syllable stress with 'ee'
entries.notes: Today's LEE-lee-uh matches.

entries.name: Rudolph
entries.source: English Rudolph: /ˈɹuːdɒlf/
entries.notes: Light verification; German bearers write Rudolf.

entries.name: Isidro
entries.source: Spanish Isidro /iˈsidɾo/: penultimate stress, i is 'ee', s is never z (Spanish orthography)
entries.notes: Today's iz-ID-roh reads s as z and uses the 'bit' vowel. Spanish bearers (ES 17.4k, US 7.8k) dominate.

entries.name: Wuxiong
entries.source: Mandarin 武雄 wǔxióng: wu [u] + xiong [ɕjʊŋ] (Help:IPA/Mandarin); x → sh, -ong 'oong' as earlier batches; final primary stress (guide's convention)
entries.notes: Today's WUK-see-awng reads x as ks.

entries.name: Efe
entries.source: Turkish Efe [eˈfe]: final stress; final open e is 'ay' (guide table, as Emre n0012)
entries.notes: Today's EEF is one syllable. Turkish bearers (wd TR 98, FR register 805) dominate.

entries.name: Dimitri
entries.source: French Dimitri: /di.mi.tʁi/; French names take final stress in English (guide, as Cyril n0005)

alternatives.context: English (US 9.5k, Canada), Greek, Flemish and Italian bearers: di-MEE-tree, today's reading

entries.notes: Population call to review: FR register 38.8k plus Belgium and Switzerland against US 9.5k, CA 1.3k, GB 0.4k. Follows the Cyril and Damien precedents; English text about Dimitri Payet etc. will change.

entries.name: Abderrahmane
entries.source: Arabic عبد الرحمن ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān: ḥ → h, double rr said once, stress on the long final ā; French -ane is 'ahn' (as Ousmane, n0007)
entries.notes: Today's ab-DERR-uh-mayn stresses -der- and reads -ane as 'lane'.

entries.name: Darwin
entries.source: English Darwin: /ˈdɑːwɪn/; Latin American Spanish Darwin [ˈdaɾwin] stresses the same syllable
entries.notes: Covered by the tech list (Darwin, Charles Darwin). The list's DAR-win is also the bearers' reading; Spanish speakers differ only in the unstressed vowel.

entries.name: Inès
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Inès: /i.nɛs/ (as Ines, n0016)
entries.notes: Today's IN-iss is the English Agnes-style guess. FR register 102k.

entries.name: Dwayne
entries.source: English Dwayne: /dweɪn/
entries.notes: Light verification.

entries.name: Chun-hui
entries.source: Korean 춘희 Chun-hui [tɕʰun.ɦi]: 춘 chun is 'choon', 희 after a consonant is said [hi] (Korean phonology); English stresses the last syllable of a two-syllable given name
entries.notes: Today's CHUN-hoo-ih reads ui as two syllables. Korean has no lexical stress; final stress follows how English speakers say Korean hyphenated names (as for Chinese, guide). No source for this exact name.

entries.name: Wafa
entries.source: Arabic وفاء Wafāʾ [waˈfaːʔ]: stress on the long final ā; hamza dropped (guide)
entries.notes: Today's WAH-fuh stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Khamis
entries.source: Arabic خميس Khamīs [xaˈmiːs]: kh → k (guide), stress on the long ī
entries.notes: Today's KAM-iss stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Paige
entries.source: English Paige: /peɪdʒ/
entries.notes: Light verification.

entries.name: Babak
entries.source: Wiktionary, Persian بابک (bâbak): Iran formal [bɒː.bǽkʰʲ]; Behind the Name /bɒː.ˈbæk/
entries.notes: Matches n0022. Today's BAH-buk stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Kaori
entries.source: Japanese かおり Kaori [kaoɾi]: three syllables; English stresses the penultimate (guide)
entries.notes: Today's KOR-ee merges a and o into one syllable.

entries.name: Lea
entries.region: US, Canada, Germany, France, Slovenia, Estonia
entries.source: German Lea [ˈleːa]; English bearers Lea Michele, Lea Thompson, Lea Salonga say LAY-uh
entries.notes: Collision with the word 'lea' (meadow, uncommon); capitalised Lea is also the River Lea and Lea Valley in London (LEE, today's reading). German, French, Slovene, Estonian and most English bearers say LAY-uh, recorded in us/gb only. Review: could ship as a name if the river is judged rare enough.

entries.name: Lorraine
entries.source: English Lorraine: /ləˈɹeɪn/
entries.notes: Light verification.

entries.name: Bruna
entries.source: Portuguese Bruna /ˈbɾunɐ/, Italian /ˈbruːna/
entries.notes: Today's BROO-nuh matches.

entries.name: Eleonora
entries.source: Wiktionary, Italian Eleonora: /e.le.oˈnɔ.ra/; Polish [ɛlɛɔˈnɔra] and Swedish also stress -NO-
entries.notes: Today's el-ee-uh-NOR-uh reads the second e as 'ee'; Italian, Polish and Swedish bearers say 'eh/ay' and keep the o. Stress already right.

entries.name: Brent
entries.source: English Brent: /bɹɛnt/
entries.notes: Light verification.

entries.name: Mansoor
entries.source: Arabic منصور Manṣūr [manˈsˤuːr], Urdu [mənˈsuːr]: stress on the long ū (as Mansour, n0008)
entries.notes: Today's MAN-soor stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Jeannie
entries.source: English Jeannie: /ˈdʒiːni/
entries.notes: Light verification.

entries.name: Shabana
entries.source: Wikipedia, Shabana Azmi: Hindustani [ʃəbɑːnɑ]; the long -bā- takes the stress
entries.notes: Today's shuh-BAN-uh uses the 'cat' vowel for the long ā.

entries.name: Aina
entries.region: Spain (Catalonia, Balearics), Norway, Sweden, Latvia, Finland
entries.source: Catalan Aina [ˈajnə] (Wiktionary); Norwegian and Swedish Aina also begin with 'eye' (ai is a diphthong)
entries.notes: Spanish register (ES 17.7k, mostly Catalan and Balearic) and Norway (NO 3.9k) dominate. Today's AY-nuh reads ai as 'ay'.

entries.name: Faouzi
entries.source: Arabic فوزي Fawzī [ˈfawzi]: French 'ou' here is w, so aw is one syllable (as Fouad, n0008, for ou)
entries.notes: Today's fow-OO-zee adds a syllable.

entries.name: Payam
entries.source: Wiktionary, Persian پیام (payâm): Iran formal [pʰæ.jɒ́ːm]; Behind the Name /pæ.ˈjɒːm/
entries.notes: The guide's worked example. Short a is the 'cat' vowel; â [ɒː] becomes English 'ah'. Today's guessed PAY-um stresses the first syllable.
entries.reading_decision: Owner decision (Payam, 2026-10-09): option E of the listening page, PAH-yuhm; the researched pæjˈɑm sounded like PAY-yahm

entries.name: İhsan
entries.source: Turkish İhsan [ihˈsan]: final stress, h sounded (as Ehsan, n0008)
entries.notes: Today's ISS-un drops the h and stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Devon
entries.source: English Devon: /ˈdɛvən/
entries.notes: Light verification.

entries.name: Dustin
entries.source: English Dustin: /ˈdʌstɪn/
entries.notes: Light verification.

entries.name: Donatien
entries.source: French Donatien: /dɔ.na.sjɛ̃/; -tien is [sjɛ̃]; nasal ɛ̃ → 'an' and final stress as Lucien and Sébastien (n0012)
entries.notes: Today's doh-NAY-shun reads it as English.

entries.name: Boban
entries.source: Serbian Бобан [bǒban]: rising accent on the first syllable
entries.notes: Today's BOH-bun matches; only the unstressed a is reduced.

entries.name: Ryszard
entries.source: Wiktionary, Polish Ryszard: /ˈrɘ.ʂart/; y [ɘ] → 'bit' vowel (as Krzysztof, n0014), sz → sh
entries.notes: Today's RISH-erd reduces the a and keeps the final d voiced; Polish has 'art'.

entries.name: Dionisio
entries.source: Spanish Dionisio /djoˈnisjo/: penultimate stress on -ni- (Spanish orthography); Italian /djoˈniːzjo/
entries.notes: Today's dy-uh-NISS-ee-oh reads the first i as 'eye' and the stressed i as 'bit'. Spanish bearers (ES 9.2k) dominate.

entries.name: Babacar
entries.source: Wolof Babacar (from Abū Bakr): c is k in this French spelling; Wolof stresses the first syllable (as Abdou, n0014); name sites give bah-bah-kar
entries.notes: Today's BAB-uh-kar has the 'cat' vowel. Stress is not sourced beyond Wolof's initial stress; French speakers put it on -CAR.

entries.name: Lìlíng
entries.source: Mandarin 丽玲/麗玲 lìlíng: li [li] + ling [liŋ] (Help:IPA/Mandarin); final primary stress (guide's convention, as Liping n0007)
entries.notes: Today's LY-ling reads the first i as 'eye'.

entries.name: Jamshid
entries.source: Behind the Name, Jamshid: /d͡ʒæm.ˈʃiːd/ (Persian); Wiktionary جمشید Iran formal [d͡ʒæm.ʃiːd̪̥]
entries.notes: Matches n0022. US fix: today's jam-SHID has the short 'bit' vowel; GB already right.

entries.name: Zahid
entries.source: Arabic زاهد Zāhid [ˈzaːhid], Urdu [ˈzaːɦɪd]: first-syllable stress on the long ā
entries.notes: Today's zuh-HEED stresses the short i.

entries.name: Abdur Razzaq
entries.source: Arabic عبد الرزاق ʿAbd ar-Razzāq: q → k (guide), stress on the long ā; Abdur kept as today (as Abdul, n0001)
entries.notes: Today's RAZ-uk stresses the first syllable of Razzaq and reduces the long ā.

entries.name: Mahmut
entries.source: Turkish Mahmut [mahˈmut]: final stress, h sounded (as Mahmoud, n0001)
entries.notes: Today's MAH-mut stresses the first syllable and drops the h.

entries.name: Tevita
entries.source: Tongan Tevita (David): penultimate stress, i is 'ee' (Tongan orthography)
entries.notes: Today's teh-VEE-tuh matches.

entries.name: Brooke
entries.source: English Brooke: /bɹʊk/
entries.notes: Light verification.

entries.name: Cyrille
entries.source: French Cyrille: /si.ʁil/ (same as Cyril, Wiktionary)
entries.notes: Today's SY-rill reads it as English; FR register 36.2k. Same reading as Cyril (n0005).

entries.name: Abed
entries.source: Arabic عابد ʿĀbid [ˈʕaːbid] and Levantine ʿAbed (colloquial ʿAbd): first-syllable stress; ʿayn dropped (guide)
entries.notes: Collides with the archaic word 'abed' (in bed), which is rare and almost never capitalised, so it is treated as a name (guide). Today's uh-BED is that word.
entries.word_check: gold has 'abed'; kept: 'abed' (in bed) is archaic

entries.name: Vania
entries.source: Italian Vania /ˈvaːnja/, Portuguese Vânia /ˈvɐnjɐ/, Spanish /ˈbanja/: stressed 'ah'
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today says the 'lot' vowel (VON-ee-uh); bearers say 'ah'. US already right.

entries.name: Azra
entries.region: France, US, UK, Norway, Bosnia, Turkey, Pakistan
entries.source: Bosnian Azra [ǎzra] (first-syllable stress) and Urdu عذرا; a is 'ah', not the 'cat' vowel
entries.notes: Today's AZ-ruh uses the 'cat' vowel. Bosnian (NO, FR registers) and Pakistani (GB) bearers stress the first syllable.

entries.name: Salem
entries.source: Arabic سالم Sālim [ˈsaːlim], Maghrebi and Gulf Salem [ˈsaːlem]: first-syllable stress on the long ā
entries.notes: In English text 'Salem' is mostly the places (Salem, Massachusetts and Oregon; the Salem witch trials; Winston-Salem), read SAY-lum as today. The Arabic name reading SAH-lem is recorded in us/gb only.

entries.name: Dickson
entries.source: English Dickson: /ˈdɪksən/
entries.notes: Nigerian, Ugandan and Kenyan bearers use the English reading.

entries.name: Serkan
entries.source: Turkish Serkan [seɾˈkan]: final stress, e is 'eh' (as Serdar, n0016)
entries.notes: Today's SUR-kun uses the 'her' vowel and stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Marcella
entries.source: English Marcella: /mɑɹˈsɛlə/
entries.notes: usage english (US 47.3k), so the English reading, as Michele in the guide.

entries.name: Micheline
entries.source: French Micheline: /miʃ.lin/; French names take final stress in English
entries.notes: Today's MISH-uh-lin has no primary stress and the 'bit' vowel. FR register 100k.

entries.name: Margarida
entries.source: Wiktionary, Portuguese Margarida: /mɐɾ.ɡɐˈɾi.dɐ/; Catalan /məɾ.ɣəˈɾi.ðə/
entries.notes: Today's stress and stressed vowel match; unstressed vowels differ only in reduction.

entries.name: Terrence
entries.source: English Terrence: /ˈtɛɹəns/
entries.notes: Light verification.

entries.name: Reinhard
entries.source: Wikipedia, Reinhard Heydrich: German [ˈʁaɪnhaʁt ...]
entries.notes: German final d is devoiced: RINE-hart, not today's RINE-hard. German bearers (wd DE 775, AT 152) dominate.

entries.name: Sándor
entries.source: Wikipedia, Sándor Petőfi: Hungarian [ˈʃaːndor]; s is sh, á is a long 'ah' (as László, n0014)
entries.notes: Today's SAN-der reads s as s and á as the 'cat' vowel.

entries.name: Frida
entries.source: Swedish and Norwegian Frida [ˈfrîːda]; Spanish (Frida Kahlo) [ˈfɾiða]
entries.notes: Today's FREE-duh matches every group.

entries.name: Edison
entries.source: English Edison: /ˈɛdɪsən/; Spanish Edison [ˈedison] also stresses the first syllable
entries.notes: Latin American bearers stress the same syllable with the same vowel; only unstressed vowels differ.

entries.name: Elliot
entries.source: English Elliot: /ˈɛliət/
entries.notes: Light verification.

entries.name: Rómulo
entries.source: Spanish Rómulo /ˈromulo/: the written accent marks first-syllable stress (Spanish orthography)
entries.notes: Today's RAHM-yuh-loh uses the 'spa' vowel and adds a y.

entries.name: Abdurahman
entries.source: Arabic عبد الرحمن ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān: ḥ → h, stress on the long final ā (as Abd al-Rahman, n0001)
entries.notes: Today's ab-DOOR-uh-mun stresses -dur- and reduces the long ā.

entries.name: Faustino
entries.source: Spanish Faustino /fawsˈtino/: au is 'ow' (Spanish orthography); Italian /fawsˈtiːno/ agrees
entries.notes: Today's faw-STEE-noh reads au as in 'fault'.

entries.name: Marwa
entries.source: Arabic مروة Marwa [ˈmarwa]: first-syllable stress
entries.notes: Today's MAR-wuh matches.

entries.name: Kerry
entries.source: English Kerry: /ˈkɛɹi/
entries.notes: Light verification.

entries.name: Caterina
entries.source: Wiktionary, Italian Caterina: /ka.teˈri.na/
entries.notes: Today's stress and stressed vowel match; only unstressed vowels are reduced.

entries.name: Aurélie
entries.source: French Aurélie: /o.ʁe.li/; au is 'oh', é is 'ay', final stress in English
entries.notes: Today's OR-lee drops a syllable. FR register 178k.

entries.name: Hadja
entries.region: Guinea, Senegal, Côte d'Ivoire, France, Belgium
entries.source: West African female form of Arabic Ḥājja (pilgrim) in French spelling: dj is j (as Elhadj, n0019, el-HAHJ)
entries.notes: Today's HAD-yuh reads dj as d + y and uses the 'cat' vowel.

entries.name: Carter
entries.notes: Ordinary word 'carter' and the common surname. The name is said the same, so nothing needs shipping.

entries.name: León
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish León: /leˈon/ (the written accent marks final stress)
entries.notes: Today's LEE-ahn is the English Leon. The accented spelling is Spanish (also the cities León, said the same).

entries.name: Tahira
entries.source: Arabic طاهرة Ṭāhira, Urdu طاہرہ [ˈt̪aːɦɪɾaː]: the long first ā takes the stress (the -hi- is short)
entries.notes: Today's tah-HEER-uh stresses the short i.

entries.name: Irène
entries.source: French Irène: /i.ʁɛn/
entries.notes: Today's eye-REEN is the English Irene. The accented spelling is French.

entries.name: Agnès
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Agnès: /a.ɲɛs/; gn → ny (guide); French [a] US ɑ, GB a (as Ignace, n0016)
entries.notes: Today's AG-niss is the English Agnes. The accented spelling is French (FR register 101k).

entries.name: Crispin
entries.source: English Crispin: /ˈkɹɪspɪn/
entries.notes: Today's KRIS-pin matches.

entries.name: Gustave
entries.source: French Gustave: /ɡys.tav/ (Gustave Eiffel [ɡystav ɛfɛl]); ü → 'oo' (guide), final stress
entries.notes: Today's goo-STAH-vee adds a final syllable; French final e is silent.

entries.name: Paulino
entries.source: Spanish Paulino /pawˈlino/: au is 'ow' (Spanish orthography); Portuguese [pawˈlinu]
entries.notes: Today's paw-LEE-noh reads au as in 'Paul'.

entries.name: Vahid
entries.source: Persian وحید (vahid): [væˈhiːd], final stress
entries.notes: Today's vah-HEED matches the stress and stressed vowel; only the unstressed first vowel differs (as Hamid, n0002).

entries.name: Ihab
entries.source: Arabic إيهاب Īhāb [ʔiːˈhaːb]: long ī, stress on the long final ā
entries.notes: Today's EYE-hab reads the i as 'eye' and stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Mahamane
entries.source: West African form of Muhammad (Hausa Mahaman) in French spelling: final -e only marks a sounded n, -ane is 'ahn' with final stress (as Ousmane, n0007, and Mamadou, n0002)
entries.notes: No pronunciation source for this exact spelling (Mahamane Ousmane, former president of Niger). Today's MAH-huh-mayn reads -ane as 'lane'.

entries.name: Uchenna
entries.source: Igbo Uchenna [utʃenːa] ('God's will'): ch is English ch, closed e before the double n is 'eh', double n said once; Nigerian English stresses -CHEN-
entries.notes: Today's yoo-KEN-uh reads u as 'yoo' and ch as k.

entries.name: Arina
entries.source: Russian Арина [ɐˈrʲinə]: stress on -ri-
entries.notes: Today's ah-REE-nuh matches; only the unstressed first vowel differs.

entries.name: Kayode
entries.source: Yoruba Káyọ̀dé: ọ [ɔ] is 'aw' (as Abiola, Adebayo n0017), final e is 'ay' (guide); tones dropped, English stress on the second syllable
entries.notes: Today's kay-OHD drops the final vowel and reads a as 'ay'.

entries.name: Amirhossein
entries.source: Persian امیرحسین (amir + hosein): final stress on -sein; amir as Amir (n0001, uh-MEER)
entries.notes: Today's AM-er-haw-seen reads it as English. One word in Persian spelling, so one primary (on -SAYN) and a secondary on -MEER.

entries.name: Cherie
entries.source: English Cherie: /ˈʃɛɹi/ (CMUdict; Cherie Blair)

alternatives.context: some US bearers, after French chérie: shuh-REE

entries.notes: Light verification: SHERR-ee is the common English reading.

entries.name: Yemi
entries.source: Yoruba Yẹmí: ẹ [ɛ] is 'eh'; tones dropped (as Femi, n0015)
entries.notes: Today's YEM-ee matches.

entries.name: Matthieu
entries.source: French Matthieu: /ma.tjø/ (as Mathieu, n0013)
entries.notes: Today's MATH-yoo reads th as in 'thin'. French ø: US 'oo', GB 'ur' as Mathieu (n0013).

entries.name: Hussain
entries.source: Arabic حسين Ḥusayn [ħuˈsajn]; Urdu [ɦʊˈseːn] (as Hussein, n0002)
entries.notes: Today's hoo-SAYN matches.

entries.name: Yijun
entries.source: Mandarin 怡君 yíjūn: yi [i] + jun [tɕyn] (Help:IPA/Mandarin); j → j, ü → oo (guide; Jun n0001, Jianjun n0009)
entries.notes: Today's YEE-jun reads jun as 'jun' (cup vowel) and stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Yaling
entries.source: Mandarin 雅玲 yǎlíng: ya [ja] + ling [liŋ] (Help:IPA/Mandarin); final primary stress (guide's convention)
entries.notes: Today's YAY-ling reads ya as 'yay'.

entries.name: Laurie
entries.source: English Laurie: /ˈlɔːɹi/
entries.notes: usage english: US 167k against FR 29.8k.

entries.name: Meihui
entries.source: Mandarin 美惠 měihuì: mei [meɪ] + hui [xweɪ] (Help:IPA/Mandarin); hui is 'hway' (Hui n0002, Huiling n0006)
entries.notes: Today's may-HOO-ee splits hui into two syllables.

entries.name: Shujun
entries.source: Mandarin 淑君 shūjūn: shu [ʂu] + jun [tɕyn] (Help:IPA/Mandarin); sh → sh, j → j, ü → oo (guide)
entries.notes: Today's SHOO-jun reads jun with the 'cup' vowel and stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Guanyu
entries.source: Mandarin 冠宇 guànyǔ: guan [kwan] + yu [y] (Help:IPA/Mandarin); final primary stress (guide's convention)
entries.notes: Today's GWAHN-yoo has the right sounds but the primary stress on the first syllable.

entries.name: Christ
entries.region: Côte d'Ivoire, DR Congo, France, US
entries.source: French Christ (the name and the word): [kʁist]
entries.notes: In English text 'Christ' is Jesus Christ, read KRYST (today's reading), and must not change. Francophone bearers (Côte d'Ivoire, DR Congo, France) say KREEST, recorded in us/gb only.

entries.name: Destiny
entries.notes: Ordinary word 'destiny'. The name is said the same, so nothing needs shipping.

entries.name: Ciro
entries.source: Wiktionary, Italian Ciro: /ˈtʃi.ro/; Spanish /ˈθiɾo/, /ˈsiɾo/

alternatives.context: Spanish (Spain, US, Peru, Colombia) and Portuguese (Brazil) bearers: SEE-roh

entries.notes: Population call to review: Italian bearers (wd IT 118; Ciro is common around Naples) are the largest single group against Spanish and Portuguese speakers (US 2.3k, ES 1.6k, BR, PE). Today's SIRR-oh fits neither.

entries.name: Ludmila
entries.source: Russian Людмила [lʲʊdˈmʲilə]: stress on -mi-

alternatives.context: Czech and Slovak bearers (wd CZ 65): LOOD-mi-luh, first-syllable stress

entries.notes: Today's lud-MY-luh reads the i as 'eye'. Russian, Ukrainian and Moldovan bearers (wd 112) outnumber Czech ones (65); both say 'oo' and 'ee'.

entries.name: Yùlín
entries.source: Mandarin 毓麟 yùlín: yu [y] + lin [lin] (Help:IPA/Mandarin); final primary stress (guide's convention)
entries.notes: Today's YOO-lin has the right sounds but stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Vitali
entries.source: Russian Виталий [vʲɪˈtalʲɪj]: stress on -ta-
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today says the 'lot' vowel (vi-TOL-ee); bearers say 'ah'. US already right.

entries.name: Giulio
entries.source: Wiktionary, Italian Giulio: /ˈd͡ʒu.ljo/
entries.notes: Today's JOO-lee-oh adds a syllable: -lio is one syllable, 'lyoh' (as Giovanni, n0003).

entries.name: Giselle
entries.region: US, Brazil, DR Congo, Latin America
entries.source: Wiktionary, Giselle: English /ʒɪˈzɛl/, /dʒɪˈzɛl/; French /ʒi.zɛl/

alternatives.context: Spanish (Latin America, US Hispanic bearers): yee-SEL

entries.notes: Today's zhih-SEL has a voiceless s; the English, French and Brazilian readings all voice it (z). Forebears 2014: Brazil 33k, DR Congo 31k, US 11k, then Spanish-speaking countries.

entries.name: Clarissa
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Clarissa: /kləˈɹɪsə/
entries.notes: Forebears 2014: US 24k, Philippines 20k (English reading), Brazil 14k (kla-REE-sa).

entries.name: Josiane
entries.source: French spelling: j [ʒ], s between vowels [z], -iane [jan] with silent final e; French names take final stress in English
entries.notes: FR register 122,610 births (anglo_share 0.01; also Quebec, Belgium, Cameroon). Today's joh-see-AH-nee reads j and s as English and sounds the final e.

entries.name: Emilie
entries.source: French Émilie /e.mi.li/ (French spelling: é 'ay', final stress in English, as Nathalie /na.ta.li/); Wiktionary, Norwegian Emilie /eˈmiː.li.ə/
entries.notes: The FR register records this unaccented spelling for 173,810 births (Émilie, its own entry, has 5,685). Forebears 2014: France 221k, DR Congo 52k, Czechia 16k, Germany 15k, US 15k, Belgium 9k. The French reading is the largest group by far. Decision to review: unlike Cedric (n0013), the English bearers here are not the largest reading group.

entries.name: Sina
entries.source: Wiktionary, Persian سینا (Sina, male given name): Iran formal [siː.nɒ́ː], Dari [siː.nɑ́ː]; final stress
entries.notes: Covered by the tech list (Sina Weibo, sˈinə); that clash is settled when the pack is merged. Forebears 2014: Iran 79,604, Cambodia 54,359, India 18,901, Germany 9,201, Nigeria 6,351, South Africa 5,972, Indonesia 5,602, Afghanistan 3,783. Persian and Dari bearers are the largest group; â [ɒː] → 'ah'. Khmer stresses the last syllable of a word (Wikipedia, Khmer language), so the Cambodian bearers very likely stress -NA as well (their vowel is not sourced). Decision to review: the Wikidata bearers are mostly German (DE 135).

entries.name: Mahir
entries.source: Turkish personal names take final stress (as Nadir, n0016); Arabic ماهر māhir stresses the long first syllable
entries.notes: Today's muh-HEER differs from Turkish mah-HEER only in the unstressed first vowel. Turkish bearers (wd TR 46, AZ 5) are the largest group.

entries.name: Stefanie
entries.source: Wiktionary, German Stefanie: [ˈʃtɛfani]
entries.notes: Forebears 2014: Germany 208.6k, US 45.7k, Austria 19.9k, Switzerland 4.8k: German-speaking bearers far outnumber the English group. German st- at the start is 'sht'. Decision to review: the 'english' usage flag rests on per-head rates, not totals.

entries.name: Sasha
entries.source: Wiktionary, Russian Саша: [ˈsaʂə]; Wikipedia, Sasha (name): English SASH-ə and SAH-shə

alternatives.context: English SASH-uh (today's; many US and UK bearers)

entries.notes: Forebears 2014: Russia 193k, Belarus 25k, US 23k, Uzbekistan 12k, England 6k; FR register 20.7k (French [sa.ʃa]). Russian, Belarusian, French and many English bearers have 'ah' (as Nadia, n0002).

entries.name: Seydou
entries.source: Wikipedia, Seydou Keita: French [sɛdu kɛjta]; French-spelled West African names take final stress in English (Mamadou, Fodé)
entries.notes: From Arabic Sayyid (Mali, Côte d'Ivoire, Senegal, Burkina Faso). Today's SAY-doo has 'ay' and first-syllable stress; the French IPA has [ɛ]. Decision to review: the bearers' own tonal languages give no English stress.

entries.name: Dewi
entries.source: Wiktionary, Indonesian dewi ('goddess'): /ˈdewi/ [ˈde.wi]
entries.notes: Forebears 2014: Indonesia 735.7k, Malaysia 3.6k, Wales 2.1k: Indonesian bearers dominate. Indonesian e in an open syllable is [e] → 'ay' (guide table). Today's DEH-wee is the Welsh reading.

entries.name: Branko
entries.source: Wiktionary, Serbo-Croatian Branko: /brâːnko/, [brâːŋko]
entries.notes: Today's BRANK-oh uses the 'cat' vowel; bearers (wd SI 238, RS 61, HR 59) say 'ah'.

entries.name: Magnus
entries.source: Wiktionary, Magnus: Swedish /¹maŋnɵs/ [ˈmǎŋnɵ̂s], Norwegian /ˈmaŋ.nʉs/; English /ˈmæɡnəs/

alternatives.context: English MAG-nus (today's; Nigeria, Scotland, US, UK)

entries.notes: Forebears 2014: Sweden 26.3k, Nigeria 11.3k, Norway 9.1k, Tanzania 4.5k, Germany 3.8k, Denmark 3.1k: Swedish and Norwegian MAHNG-nus (gn = [ŋn]) is the largest single reading. Unstressed rounded ɵ/ʉ → 'uu'; GB short a as Hans (n0002).

entries.name: Jérémie
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Jérémie: /ʒe.ʁe.mi/
entries.notes: Accented spelling: French bearers (FR 4,975, Belgium, Switzerland, DR Congo). Today's JERR-uh-mee is the English Jeremy. French é is 'ay'; French names take final stress in English (as Frédéric).

entries.name: Zouheir
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic زهير (Zuhayr, male given name): /zu.hajr/; the French spelling ou = [u], ei = the Maghrebi [ej] of ay
entries.notes: Today's ZOO-hire stresses the first syllable. The heavy last syllable takes the stress; the Tunisian and Algerian spelling writes the diphthong as ei, rendered 'air' before r.

entries.name: Vivi
entries.source: Regular spelling in Danish, Norwegian and Indonesian: [ˈviːvi]
entries.notes: Forebears 2014: India 55.7k, Indonesia 45.9k, Nepal 8.2k, Denmark 5.8k: all VEE-vee, as today. Greek Βιβή (vee-VEE) is written in Greek script.

entries.name: Matilde
entries.source: Wiktionary, Matilde: Spanish /maˈtilde/, Italian /maˈtil.de/
entries.notes: Spanish (ES 28,108), Italian, Argentine and Portuguese bearers say three syllables with 'ee'; today's muh-TILD drops the final vowel. Final unstressed e → 'ay' (guide table, as Felipe).

entries.name: Nuno
entries.source: Wiktionary, Portuguese Nuno: Portugal /ˈnu.nu/, Brazil /ˈnũ.nu/
entries.notes: Portuguese final unstressed o is [u] (as Paulo, Diogo). Bearers are Portuguese (wd PT 254).

entries.name: Adeline
entries.region: France, DR Congo, Cameroon, Haiti, US
entries.source: Wiktionary, Adeline: French /ad.lin/; English /ˈædəlɪn/, /ˈædəliːn/, /ˈædəlaɪn/
entries.notes: Forebears 2014: DR Congo 53.6k, Cameroon 23.3k, France 22.5k, US 19.4k, Haiti 18.6k, Madagascar 10k, then Chad, Rwanda, Burkina Faso, Benin and Côte d'Ivoire; the FR register (50.7k) almost equals the US one (56.9k), and English bearers split three ways. French ad-LEEN (two syllables, final stress, as Madeleine n0009) is the largest single reading. Decision to review: the recent US name is mostly AD-uh-line.

entries.name: Clayton
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Clayton: /ˈkleɪtən/

entries.name: Wilfredo
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Wilfredo: /wilˈfɾedo/ [wilˈfɾe.ð̞o]; open-syllable e → 'ay' (as Alfredo, n0002)
entries.notes: Today's wil-FAY-doh drops the r. Bearers: US Hispanic (9,548 births), Peru, Cuba, Venezuela, Spain. Spanish d between vowels [ð] → d.

entries.name: Emine
entries.source: Turkish spelling and stress: final stress in personal names (Zeynep, Emre); final open e → 'ay' (as Emre, n0012)
entries.notes: Today's EM-un drops a syllable. Bearers are Turkish (wd TR 258; FR, NO, GB Turkish families).

entries.name: Erol
entries.source: Wiktionary, Turkish Erol (er + ol); Turkish personal names take final stress (Mehmet, Onur)
entries.notes: Today's ERR-ul stresses the first syllable. Bearers are Turkish (wd TR 256).

entries.name: Kassim
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic قاسم (qāsim): /ˈqaː.sim/ (as Qāsim, n0010); Swahili stresses the penultimate
entries.notes: Forebears 2014: Tanzania 27.5k, Mali 26.6k, Kenya 12.5k, Uganda 9.4k, Ethiopia, Somalia, Nigeria: East and West African forms of Qasim. They keep the 'ah' of the long ā; today's KASS-im has the 'cat' vowel.

entries.name: Colleen
entries.source: Wiktionary, Colleen (given name): UK /kəˈliːn/, /kɒˈliːn/; US /kəˈlin/, /kɔˈlin/, /kɑˈlin/; Dictionary.com, colleen: American ˈkɒl in, kɒˈlin; British kɒˈliːn, ˈkɒliːn

alternatives.context: KOL-een (today's; Irish English, after Irish cailín, and some British and US speakers)

entries.notes: Treated as a name, not protect-word: the word 'colleen' (an Irish girl) is uncommon and lowercase, so it meets this capitalised spelling only at the start of a sentence, while the name has 161k US births. The second-syllable stress chosen here is also a dictionary reading of the word in both accents (Dictionary.com's British reading lists it first), so a sentence-initial 'Colleen' (the word) is not harmed. Today's KAH-leen stresses the first syllable, which no source gives for US speakers of the name. Changed in review from protect-word.
entries.word_check: gold has 'colleen'; kept: 'colleen' (an Irish girl) is rare and old-fashioned

entries.name: Lakshman
entries.source: Hindi लक्ष्मण (lakṣmaṇ): short a [ə] in both syllables, kṣ → 'ksh' (as Akshay, n0003: Wiktionary /ˈəkʃɛ/)
entries.notes: Today's LACK-shmun uses the 'cat' vowel; Hindi short a is 'uh' (as Akshay, Sanjay).

entries.name: Suzhen
entries.source: Mandarin 素珍/素貞 sùzhēn: su [su] + zhen [ʈʂən] (as Zhen, n0002)
entries.notes: Today's SUZZ-un reads zh as z and drops the u. two-syllable Chinese given name: final primary stress (guide convention).

entries.name: Meizhu
entries.source: Mandarin 美珠 měizhū: mei [meɪ̯] (as Mei, n0003) + zhu [ʈʂu] (as Zhù, n0018)
entries.notes: Today's MEE-zhoo reads ei as 'ee'. two-syllable Chinese given name: final primary stress (guide convention).

entries.name: Ubaidullah
entries.source: Arabic عبيد الله ʿUbayd Allāh; stress as Abdullah (n0001: ab-DOO-lah, the Urdu and Malay -dul-)
entries.notes: Today's yoo-bay-DOO-luh adds a y glide: ʿUbayd starts with a plain u (ʿayn dropped, guide). Bearers: Pakistan, UK (GB-EAW 89).

entries.name: Guanlin
entries.source: Mandarin 冠霖 guànlín: guan [ku̯an] (as Guan, n0018) + lin [lin] (as Lin, n0002)
entries.notes: Today's GWAHN-lin stresses the first syllable (British with the 'lot' vowel). two-syllable Chinese given name: final primary stress (guide convention).

entries.name: Sri
entries.source: Indonesian and Malay Sri [sri], from Sanskrit श्री śrī
entries.notes: Today's unstressed sɹˌi ('sree', as in Sri Lanka) matches the Indonesian bearers (wd ID 11), the largest group.

entries.name: Leopold
entries.region: DR Congo, Cameroon, Burundi, Rwanda, Benin, Belgium, France
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Léopold: /le.ɔ.pɔl(d)/; French names take final stress in English (guide); Wiktionary, Leopold: German /ˈleːopɔlt/, English /ˈliːəpoʊld/

alternatives.context: German, Dutch and Czech LAY-oh-polt (Austria 29.8k, Germany 7.3k, Czechia, Slovenia, Slovakia, Flanders)
English LEE-uh-pold (today's; US, Jamaica, UK; Leopold Bloom and King Leopold in English text)

entries.notes: Forebears 2014 for this unaccented spelling: DR Congo 15,599, Cameroon 11,926, Burundi 10,138, Rwanda 5,076, Benin 3,633, Senegal 1,874, Burkina Faso 1,420, Côte d'Ivoire 1,030, France 781, Togo 742 (about 52k francophone, plus French-speaking Belgium and Quebec, so about 57k) against Austria 29,757, Germany 7,321, Czechia 1,761, Slovenia 1,712, Slovakia 803 and Flanders (about 44k first-syllable LAY-oh-polt); the FR register also has 7,210 births with no accent. French lay-oh-POLD is the largest single reading. The accent argument (French bearers write Léopold) is not applied, to match Emilie and Angelique in this batch, which were also decided on unaccented French and francophone-African counts. Wiktionary marks the French final d optional; Belgian and African bearers usually sound it, so it is kept. Changed in review from German LAY-oh-polt; still close.

entries.name: Sutan
entries.source: Indonesian and Malay spelling: [ˈsu.tan], penultimate stress
entries.notes: Today's SOO-tun differs only in the unstressed vowel.

entries.name: Anselmo
entries.source: Italian Anselmo /anˈsɛl.mo/, Spanish /anˈselmo/: penultimate stress
entries.notes: Today's ahn-SEL-moh matches.

entries.name: Jocelyn
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Jocelyn: /ˈd͡ʒɒsəlɪn/, /ˈd͡ʒɒslɪn/

alternatives.context: Spanish (Chile, Mexico, US Hispanic bearers): YOH-seh-leen

entries.notes: Today's British JAWSS-lin has the 'thought' vowel; the name has the 'lot' vowel (GB ɒ, US ɑ). Today's two-syllable form is kept (Wiktionary's second reading). English-reading bearers (Forebears 2014: Philippines 408k, US 46k, Canada 23k) are the largest group.

entries.name: Nazir
entries.source: Arabic نذير nadhīr, Urdu نذیر nazīr: stress on the long ī
entries.notes: Today's nah-ZEER matches; ḏ is z in Urdu and in English renderings.

entries.name: Denys
entries.source: Wiktionary, Ukrainian Денис: [deˈnɪs]
entries.notes: Denys is the official Latin spelling of Ukrainian Денис (wd UA 104). Today's duh-NIZE is an English spelling reading.

entries.name: Süleyman
entries.source: Turkish Süleyman: ü → 'oo' (guide), ey [ej] → 'ay', final stress (as Souleymane, n0005; Osman, n0006)
entries.notes: Today's SOO-lee-mun stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Zofia
entries.source: Wiktionary, Polish Zofia: /ˈzɔ.fja/
entries.notes: Two syllables with the open o; today's ZOH-fee-uh adds a syllable. Bearers are Polish (wd PL 1,142; GB-EAW 2,842 Polish families).

entries.name: Özgür
entries.source: Turkish Özgür: unstressed ö → 'uh' (as Özlem, n0017), ü before r → 'oor' (as Uğur, n0020), final stress
entries.notes: Today's OZ-gur stresses the first syllable. Bearers are Turkish (wd TR 259).

entries.name: Harris
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Harris: /ˈhæɹɪs/, /ˈhaɹɪs/, (merged US) /ˈhɛɹɪs/
entries.notes: Today's US hˈɛɹɪs is the Mary–marry–merry-merged American reading Wiktionary lists.

entries.name: Myra
entries.source: CMUdict MYRA: M AY1 R AH0 (today's source); Wiktionary, English Myra: rhymes -aɪɹə
entries.notes: Forebears 2014: Philippines 72k, US 69k: both English MY-ruh.

entries.name: Angelique
entries.source: French Angélique /ɑ̃.ʒe.lik/ (Wiktionary, Angelique: 'from French Angélique'); the FR register records the unaccented spelling (73,810 births)
entries.notes: Forebears 2014: DR Congo 155k, France 67k, Rwanda 32k, Netherlands 26k, US 19k, Burundi 12k: French and Dutch bearers say ahn-zhay-LEEK. Nasal ɑ̃ → 'ahn' (as Laurent, Chantal; GB ɒn as Henri); é 'ay'; g before e is zh.

entries.name: Vladimír
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vladimír: Czech [ˈvlaɟɪmiːr], Slovak [ˈʋlaɟimiːr]
entries.notes: Czech and Slovak stress the first syllable and keep 'ah' and the long í; today's US VLAD-uh-meer uses the 'cat' vowel. Palatal ď → d.

entries.name: Léo
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Léo: /le.o/
entries.notes: Accented spelling: FR register 124,520. Today's LEE-oh is the English Leo. French names take final stress in English (as Léon, n0010).

entries.name: Kenan
entries.source: Wiktionary, Turkish Kenan (Ottoman kenʿân); final stress (as Kemal, n0014)

alternatives.context: English KEE-nun (biblical Kenan, Kenan Thompson; US)

entries.notes: Forebears 2014: Turkey 123.5k, Azerbaijan 3.9k, Germany 2k, US 1.9k. Today's KEE-nun is the English reading.

entries.name: Stanislaus
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Stanislaus: /ˈstænɪslɔːs/; Wikipedia, Stanislaus County: /ˈstænɪslɔː(s)/
entries.notes: Today's STAN-iss-lows mixes the English start with a German ending. Forebears 2014: Indonesia 5,292 (Flores Catholics; reading not sourced), Germany 1,691, Saudi Arabia 933 and UAE 304 (mostly expatriates), Nigeria 723, Tanzania 595, Ghana 562, US 534, Austria 325, Zimbabwe 302, Namibia 297. No single group dominates; the English reading covers the English-speaking African and US bearers and the saint and county met in English text. German bearers say SHTAH-niss-lowss.

entries.name: Trinidad
entries.source: Wiktionary, Trinidad: Spanish /tɾiniˈdad/ [t̪ɾi.niˈð̞að̞]; English (the island) /ˈtɹɪnɪdæd/
entries.notes: In English text 'Trinidad' is overwhelmingly the island (Trinidad and Tobago), read TRIN-ih-dad as today: never replace it. The Spanish given name (ES 26,511, Mexico, Peru, the Philippines) is tree-nee-DAHD, recorded here.

entries.name: Pınar
entries.source: Turkish pınar ('spring'): ı [ɯ] → 'uh' unstressed (guide), final stress
entries.notes: The dotless ı marks the Turkish spelling (wd TR 259). Today's PEE-nur reads ı as 'ee' and stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Chandrika
entries.source: Hindi चंद्रिका (candrikā): short a and short i, as Chandra (n0002; Wiktionary Hindi चंद्र /t͡ʃən.d̪ɾᵊ/)
entries.notes: Today's chahn-DREE-kuh uses 'ah' and a long 'ee'; Hindi short a is 'uh' and the i is short. Hindi stress is weak; the heavy first syllable takes it, as in Chandra.

entries.name: Chengen
entries.source: Mandarin 承恩 chéng'ēn: cheng [ʈʂʰɤŋ] (as Zhicheng, n0006) + en [ən] ('un', as Wen, n0014)
entries.notes: Today's CHENG-un uses the 'bed' vowel and stresses the first syllable. two-syllable Chinese given name: final primary stress (guide convention).

entries.name: Dilara
entries.source: Turkish Dilara (from Persian dilârâ 'heart-adorning'): final stress (as Leyla, Esra)
entries.notes: Today's dih-LAH-rah stresses the middle syllable. Bearers are Turkish (wd TR 67, DE, AZ; FR 1,325 Turkish families).

entries.name: Azim
entries.source: Arabic عظيم ʿaẓīm: stress on the long ī
entries.notes: Today's uh-ZEEM matches; ẓ is z for Urdu, Persian and English speakers.

entries.name: Amer
entries.source: Arabic عامر ʿĀmir /ʕaː.mir/: the long ā takes the stress (as Qādir in Abdulkadir, n0016)
entries.notes: Today's AY-mer reads the long ā as 'ay'. Arab (wd IQ 11, EG, PS) and Bosnian (Amer, AH-mer) bearers say 'ah'. ʿayn dropped (guide).

entries.name: Delia
entries.source: Wiktionary, Delia: Spanish /ˈdelja/ [ˈd̪e.lja]; English (UK) /ˈdiːlɪə/
entries.notes: Forebears 2014: Philippines 116k, Argentina 113k, Mexico 76k, Peru 54k, US 54k, Venezuela 26k, Ecuador 25k, Romania 20k: Spanish, Filipino, Romanian and Italian bearers say DEH-lya, far more than the English group. Open-syllable e → 'ay' (guide table, as Elena).

entries.name: Chiara
entries.source: Italian Chiara /ˈkja.ra/ (ch = k, ia one syllable)
entries.notes: Today's KYAH-ruh matches.

entries.name: Francesc
entries.source: Catalan Francesc: Central /fɾənˈsɛsk/, Valencian /fɾanˈsesk/
entries.notes: Today's fran-SESK keeps the stress and the stressed vowel; only the unstressed first vowel differs.

entries.name: Oliverio
entries.source: Spanish spelling: penultimate stress on -ve-, -rio one syllable (Wiktionary, Tagalog Oliverio: /ʔoliˈveɾjo/); open-syllable e → 'ay' (as Valeria, n0009)
entries.notes: Today's ah-lih-VEER-ee-oh uses the 'eer' vowel. Intervocalic v stays v, as careful English speakers say it (Javier, Iván). Bearers: Colombia, Mexico, Argentina, Spain.

entries.name: Toby
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Toby: UK /ˈtəʊbi/, US /ˈtoʊbi/

entries.name: Karol
entries.source: Wiktionary, Karol: Polish /ˈka.rɔl/, Slovak /ˈkarɔɫ/
entries.notes: Forebears 2014: Poland 177k, Slovakia 27k, US 15k. Today's KERR-awl is the English Carol; GB short a as Hans (n0002).

entries.name: Dwight
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Dwight: /ˈdwaɪt/

entries.name: Asaf
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hebrew אסף (male given name): /(ʔ)aˈsaf/
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today says the 'lot' vowel (os-OFF). US already right. Bearers: Israel (wd IL 71), Turkey (Asaf).

entries.name: Meriem
entries.source: French spelling of Arabic Maryam used in Algeria, Tunisia and Morocco: e [ɛ], ie [jɛ]; final stress as for French-spelled names (Maryam, n0003: mar-YAM)
entries.notes: Today's MEER-ee-um is the English Miriam. Bearers: FR 6,335, ES 2,998 (Maghrebi families), wd DZ 20, TN 20, MA 8.

entries.name: Nasrin
entries.source: Wiktionary, Persian نسرین (female given name): Iranian formal [næs.ɹiːn], Classical /nas.ˈriːn/
entries.notes: Today's NAS-rin stresses the first syllable; Persian stresses the last.

entries.name: Akin
entries.source: Yoruba Akin ('brave man', short for Akinwale, Akintunde): a 'ah', nasal ĩ with high tone (as Kehinde, n0019)
entries.notes: Also the word 'akin' (uh-KIN, today's reading), which starts sentences ('Akin to ...'): never replace it. Forebears 2014: Nigeria 18.1k of about 24k bearers. The Yoruba name is ah-KEEN (tones dropped; the high-toned second syllable takes the stress), recorded here.

entries.name: Ariana
entries.source: Wiktionary, Ariana: Spanish /aˈɾjana/, Brazilian Portuguese /a.ɾiˈɐ̃.nɐ/, English /ɑːɹiˈænə/; Wikipedia, Ariana Grande: /ˌɑːriˈɑːnə/

alternatives.context: English ah-ree-AN-uh (Wiktionary's English reading; many US bearers)

entries.notes: Forebears 2014: Brazil 23k, Mexico 22.6k, US 11.4k, Venezuela, Indonesia, Spain, Angola; US register 118k births, many of them Hispanic. Spanish, Portuguese and Persian/Afghan bearers and many English ones (Ariana Grande) have 'ah' in the stressed syllable; today's US 'cat' vowel is one English variant. Decision to review.

entries.name: Dee
entries.source: CMUdict DEE: D IY1 (today's gold reading)

entries.name: Kirsten
entries.source: Wiktionary, Kirsten: Danish [ˈkʰiɐ̯sdn̩]; English GA /ˈkɝstən/, /ˈkɪɹstən/; Wikipedia, Kirsten Dunst and Kirsten Gillibrand: /ˈkɪərstən/

alternatives.context: English KUR-stin (today's; many US and UK bearers)

entries.notes: Forebears 2014: Germany 79k, US 47k, Denmark 46k, Netherlands 16.5k, Norway 11.6k, England 8.3k. German, Danish and Dutch bearers and a share of American ones say KEER-sten; Norwegians say KHISH-ten (kj [ç]).

entries.name: Aliou
entries.source: French spelling of a West African form of Ali: ou = [u]; no pronunciation source found
entries.notes: Senegalese and Guinean form of Ali (Aliou Cissé). The vowels are clear (ah, ee, oo) but no source gives the stress: today's AH-lee-oo stresses the first syllable, while the French-spelling convention of earlier batches (Alioune n0020, ah-lee-OON) would put it last. Candidate in us/gb.

entries.name: Lauro
entries.source: Italian Lauro [ˈlau.ro], Spanish [ˈlawɾo]: au is 'ow' (Wiktionary, Polish Lauro /ˈlaw.rɔ/ likewise)
entries.notes: Forebears 2014: Brazil 56k, Mexico 26k, Philippines 19k, Ecuador 6k, Italy 5k, US 5k: every group says LOW-; today's LOR-oh reads au as 'aw'. Spanish, Filipino and Italian bearers end in 'oh', Brazilians in 'oo' (an unstressed-vowel difference).

entries.name: Carine
entries.source: Wiktionary, Carine: French /ka.ʁin/; Norwegian Bokmål /kaˈriː.nə/
entries.notes: FR register 46,065 (also Belgium, Cameroon). Today's kah-REE-nee sounds the final e, which French leaves silent.

entries.name: Lingling
entries.source: Mandarin 玲玲 línglíng: ling [liŋ] twice (as Huiling, n0006)
entries.notes: Today's LING-guh-ling inserts a g and a schwa. two-syllable Chinese given name: final primary stress (guide convention).

entries.name: Theodorus
entries.source: Wiktionary, Latin Theodorus: Ecclesiastical [te.oˈdɔː.rus]; Dutch keeps the Latin stress on -do- and says th as t
entries.notes: Bearers are Dutch (wd NL 271, plus Indonesia and Belgium), often the baptismal name behind Theo or Dorus. Today's THEE-uh-duh-rus uses English th and stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Xiuqin
entries.source: Mandarin 秀琴 xiùqín: xiu [ɕi̯oʊ̯] (as Xiuzhen, n0008) + qin [tɕʰin] (as Qin, n0003)
entries.notes: Today's zee-OO-kin reads x as z and q as k. two-syllable Chinese given name: final primary stress (guide convention).

entries.name: Masato
entries.source: Wiktionary, Masato: romaji of まさと [masato]; English stresses Japanese names on the penultimate (guide)
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today says the 'lot' vowel (mos-OT-oh). US already right.

entries.name: Zhenghao
entries.source: Mandarin 政豪/正浩 zhènghào: zheng [ʈʂɤŋ] (as Zhēng, n0002) + hao [xɑʊ̯] (as Zhihao, n0006)
