entries.notes: Today's ZHENG-how reads zh as the 'measure' sound and stresses the first syllable. two-syllable Chinese given name: final primary stress (guide convention).

entries.name: Xiuling
entries.source: Mandarin 秀玲 xiùlíng: xiu [ɕi̯oʊ̯] (as Xiuying, n0008) + ling [liŋ]
entries.notes: Today's ZHOW-ling misreads xiu. two-syllable Chinese given name: final primary stress (guide convention).

entries.name: Shuhui
entries.source: Mandarin 淑慧 shūhuì: shu [ʂu] (as Shuhua, n0016) + hui [xu̯eɪ̯] (as Hui, n0002)
entries.notes: Today's SHOO-hwee reads hui as 'hwee'. two-syllable Chinese given name: final primary stress (guide convention).

entries.name: Jiāqí
entries.source: Mandarin 佳琪 jiāqí: as Jiaqi (n0012); Wiktionary 琪 qí /t͡ɕʰi³⁵/
entries.notes: Today's jee-AH-kee reads q as k and splits jia. two-syllable Chinese given name: final primary stress (guide convention).

entries.name: Wénqìng
entries.source: Mandarin 文庆/文慶 wénqìng: wen [wən] + qing [tɕʰiŋ] (as Wénqīng, n0005)
entries.notes: Today's WENG-king reads q as k. two-syllable Chinese given name: final primary stress (guide convention).

entries.name: Xǐ
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 喜 xǐ [ɕi]; Wikipedia, Xi Jinping: English /ˈʃiː/
entries.notes: Today's ZYE is the Greek letter xi. Characters 玺/璽/禧 are all read xǐ/xī [ɕi].

entries.name: Ānní
entries.source: Mandarin 安妮 ānní: an [an] (as Ān, n0007) + ni [ni]
entries.notes: 安妮 is the Chinese rendering of Annie, but with tone marks the spelling is Mandarin pinyin. Today's AN-ee is the English Annie. two-syllable Chinese given name: final primary stress (guide convention).

entries.name: Burcu
entries.source: Turkish spelling: c = [dʒ], u [u]; final stress
entries.notes: Today's bur-KOO reads c as k. Bearers are Turkish (wd TR 257).

entries.name: Ximena
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Ximena: /xiˈmena/ [xiˈme.na]
entries.notes: US 37,976 births (mostly Mexican-American) plus Peru, Chile and Mexico. X is the old spelling of Spanish j [x] → h (guide); today's ZIM-in-uh reads it as English. Open-syllable e → 'ay'.

entries.name: Kristin
entries.source: CMUdict KRISTIN: K R IH1 S T IH0 N; Norwegian and Swedish Kristin also stress KRIS-
entries.notes: US 180,924 births against NO 16,958; both say KRIS-tin.

entries.name: Ziaur
entries.source: Wikipedia, Ziaur Rahman: Bengali জিয়াউর রহমান [dʒijau̯r ˈɾɔɦoman]
entries.notes: The first part of Ziaur Rahman (Ḍiyāʾ al-Raḥmān, 'light of the Merciful'), like Fazlur (n0013, also unresolved). Bengali bearers (Bangladesh) say jee-YOWR; Urdu speakers (Pakistan, the Wikidata country here) say zee-AH-oor; which group leads and whether English should keep z is undecided. Today's zee-OWR has no stress mark.

entries.name: Nader
entries.source: Wiktionary, نادر: Arabic /naː.dir/; Persian Iran formal [nɒː.d̪éɹ], Dari [nɑː.d̪ɪ́ɾ]
entries.notes: In English text 'Nader' is very often Ralph Nader (a Lebanese-American surname), read NAY-der as today: never replace it. Forebears 2014: Iran 119k, Egypt 93k, Syria 28k, Yemen 21k, Sudan 18k, Afghanistan 17k, Libya, Jordan, Kuwait, Palestine: Arabic NAH-dir (stress on the long ā) is the largest group, Persian nah-DEHR the next. Decision to review: protect-word follows the Chan review (n0017).

entries.name: Alcides
entries.source: Spanish spelling: penultimate stress (word ends in s), c before i [s], d [ð] → d
entries.notes: Forebears 2014: Brazil 98k, Colombia 23k, Paraguay 22k, Argentina 20k, Mozambique 19k, Angola 15k, Venezuela 13k, Peru 13k, Cuba 12k: Spanish-speaking bearers together (about 120k) slightly outnumber Brazil, and African and European Portuguese (al-SEE-desh) are close to the Spanish. Today's AL-sudz loses a syllable. Decision to review.

entries.name: Thi
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese thị: (Hà Nội) [tʰi˧˨ʔ] (as Thị, n0004)
entries.notes: Unaccented Thị, the common middle name of Vietnamese women (the US, CA, FR and NO registers are diaspora). Vietnamese th is an aspirated t; today's THEE reads it as English th.

entries.name: Avery
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Avery: /ˈeɪ.və.ɹi/, /ˈeɪv.ɹi/

entries.name: Frits
entries.source: Dutch Frits [frɪts] (short for Frederik), as German Fritz (n0007)

entries.name: Sameh
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic سامح (male given name): /saː.miħ/
entries.notes: Egyptian spelling (wd EG 19, TN 9). The long ā takes the stress and ḥ → h (guide), as Saleh (n0009). Today's US drops the h; British has the 'lot' vowel.

entries.name: Dimas
entries.source: Indonesian and Spanish spelling: [ˈdi.mas], first-syllable stress
entries.notes: Forebears 2014: Indonesia 73k, Brazil 22k, Venezuela 8k, Mexico 8k. Today's DYE-muz reads i as 'eye' and s as z.

entries.name: Davud
entries.source: Wiktionary, Persian داوود (male given name): Iran formal [d̪ɒː.vúːd̪̥], Classical /daː.ˈwuːd/
entries.notes: Today's DAY-vud reads a as 'ay' and stresses the first syllable. Bearers: Iran (wd IR 29), Azerbaijan.

entries.name: Coco
entries.notes: Word 'coco' (coconut palm, cocoa). Name and word are read alike: KOH-koh (Coco Chanel, Coco Gauff), as today.

entries.name: Madina
entries.source: Arabic مدينة madīna [maˈdiː.na]; Russian Мадина: stress on the long dī
entries.notes: Today's mah-DEE-nuh matches Russian, Chechen, Indian, Ugandan and Arabic usage. Forebears 2014: Uzbekistan 318k, Tajikistan 233k, Russia 115k, India 113k, Kazakhstan 102k, Uganda 47k. Low: Uzbek, Tajik and Kazakh usually stress the last syllable, which I could not confirm for this name. Decision to review.

entries.name: Jamaal
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic جمال: /d͡ʒa.maːl/ (as Jamal, n0003)
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today has the 'lot' vowel (juh-MOL). US already right; the double a spells the long ā (US 8,561 births).

entries.name: Malak
entries.source: Wiktionary, ملاك ('angel'): Egyptian /ma.laːk/ [mæˈlæːk], Moroccan /ma.laːk/, South Levantine [maˈlæːk]
entries.notes: Forebears 2014: Egypt 167k, Morocco 18k, Iraq 17k, Sudan 12k. The long ā takes the stress; today's MAL-uk stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Hiroaki
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hiroaki: romaji of ひろあき [çiɾoaki]; penultimate stress in English (guide; as Hiroyuki, n0014)
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today says the 'lot' vowel (-OCK-ee). US already right.

entries.name: Gaspard
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Gaspard: /ɡas.paʁ/
entries.notes: FR register 28,890. The final d is silent (as Gérard, Bernard); today's guh-SPARD says it.

entries.name: Melinda
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Melinda: /məˈlɪn.də/, /mɛˈlɪn.də/
entries.notes: Forebears 2014: US 194k, Philippines 66k, Hungary 46k: English muh-LIN-duh is the largest group.

entries.name: Vlado
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vlado: Serbo-Croatian /ʋlǎːdo/, Slovene /ʋláːdɔ/
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today says the 'lot' vowel (VLOD-oh). US already right.

entries.name: Miranda
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Miranda: /mɪˈɹændə/

alternatives.context: Dutch, Italian, Portuguese and Albanian mee-RAHN-dah (Netherlands 34k)

entries.notes: Forebears 2014: US 53k, Netherlands 34k, England 8k, Italy 7.5k, Mozambique 7.2k: the English groups together are the largest.

entries.name: Ikechukwu
entries.source: Igbo Ikechukwu ('the strength of God', ike + Chukwu): i 'ee', e 'eh', u 'oo'; Nigerian English stresses -chu-
entries.notes: Today's ih-kuh-CHOO-kwoo keeps the stressed syllable; the secondary-stressed first vowel and the unstressed ke differ only slightly (as Hiroyuki, n0014). Tones dropped.

entries.name: Viola
entries.source: Wiktionary, Viola: German [viˈoːla], Italian /viˈɔ.la/, Swedish /vɪ²uːla/; English /vaɪˈəʊlə/, /viˈəʊlə/, /ˈvaɪələ/; Wikipedia, Viola Davis: /vaɪˈoʊlə/
entries.notes: Word 'viola' (the instrument), read vee-OH-luh as today. Most bearers (anglo_share 0.18: Germany, Sweden, Italy, Finland) say vee-OH-la too, so the name needs no change.

entries.name: Yvon
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Yvon: /i.vɔ̃/
entries.notes: FR register 36,225 (also Quebec, Belgium, Haiti). Today's EYE-vahn reads Y as 'eye' and stresses the first syllable. Nasal ɔ̃ → 'on' (as Léon, Gaston); final stress.

entries.name: Najla
entries.source: Arabic نجلاء najlāʾ: stress on the long final ā; hamza dropped (as Asma, n0007; Wafa, n0022)
entries.notes: Today's NY-luh drops the j and reads a as 'eye'. Bearers: Tunisia, Egypt, Lebanon (FR 465, US 640).

entries.name: Christiana
entries.source: Forebears 2014 (bearers); Wikipedia, Ghanaian English: seven vowels, /a/ the only open vowel, as in other African Englishes; Wiktionary, English Christiana: /ˈkɹɪs.tiˌænə/

alternatives.context: US and UK English kris-tee-AN-uh (today's reading)

entries.notes: Forebears 2014: Nigeria 327,818, Ghana 49,949, Sierra Leone 23,499, US 6,263, Indonesia 4,713, Haiti 4,378, Germany 4,353, Belgium 4,054, Madagascar 3,325, Cameroon 3,063, Liberia 2,929, Austria 2,409. West African English has a single open vowel [a] for the 'cat' and 'father' sets, which the guide maps to 'ah' as for Spanish a; the Indonesian, Haitian, German, Belgian and Malagasy bearers also say 'ah'. Only the US and UK group (under 10k) uses the 'cat' vowel. Stress stays on the a, as today and as these bearers say it (Wiktionary's primary on the first syllable is not followed). Changed in review from already-correct.

entries.name: Djibril
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic جبريل (Jibrīl, Gabriel): /d͡ʒib.riːl/; the long ī takes the stress, as in French [dʒi.bʁil]
entries.notes: French spelling (dj = j) of Jibrīl, used in Senegal and Mali (wd SN 11; FR 9,085). Today's JIB-ril stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Anila
entries.source: Hindi अनिला (anilā): short a and short i (as Anil, n0001: /ə.nɪl/)
entries.notes: Forebears 2014: India 241k, Pakistan 49k, Nepal 43k, Albania 8.7k. Today's uh-NIL-uh matches the South Asian reading (as Anil).

entries.name: Rory
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Rory: /ˈɹɔːɹi/

entries.name: Abimbola
entries.source: Yoruba Abímbọ́lá ('born into wealth', ọlá 'wealth'): ọ is open [ɔ], as Abiola (n0017)
entries.notes: Today's ah-beem-BOH-luh uses the closed 'oh'; Yoruba ọ is the open 'aw'. Tones dropped; stress as Abiola.

entries.name: Adekunle
entries.source: Yoruba Adékúnlé ('the crown fills the house'): e [e] → 'ay' (as Adebayo, n0017), final e a full vowel (as Tunde, n0016)
entries.notes: Today's AD-uh-kun-ul misreads every vowel and drops the final e. Tones dropped; English speakers stress KOON.

entries.name: Bolaji
entries.source: Yoruba Bọ́lájí (native spelling): ọ is open [ɔ] (as Abiola, n0017)
entries.notes: Today's boh-LAH-jee uses the closed 'oh'; British today also says the 'lot' vowel in LAH.

entries.name: Osita
entries.source: Igbo Osita: regular spelling, o [o], plain i [i]
entries.notes: Today's oh-SEE-tuh matches the usual Nigerian English stress.

entries.name: Manzoor
entries.source: Urdu منظور (manzūr): short a, long ū; the long last syllable takes the stress (as Mansour, n0008; Mayur, n0018)
entries.notes: Today's MAN-zoor uses the 'cat' vowel and stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Ilija
entries.source: Wiktionary, Serbo-Croatian Ilija: /ǐlija/
entries.notes: Today's il-EE-juh reads j as English j; it is the y sound, and the stress is on the first syllable.

entries.name: Merve
entries.source: Turkish Merve: final stress; final open e → 'ay' (as Emre, Ayşe)
entries.notes: Today's MURV drops the final syllable. Bearers are Turkish (wd TR 251; FR 1,780 Turkish families).

entries.name: Alfie
entries.source: CMUdict ALFIE: AE1 L F IY0 (today's source)
entries.notes: GB-EAW 88,511 births.

entries.name: Arsène
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Arsène: /aʁ.sɛn/
entries.notes: Accented spelling: French bearers (FR 5,460, Belgium, Luxembourg, Côte d'Ivoire; Arsène Wenger). Today's AR-seen reads è as 'ee'; French names take final stress in English.

entries.name: Jone
entries.source: Wiktionary, Basque Jone: Southern and Gipuzkoan /jone/, Navarro-Lapurdian /ɟone/, Biscayan /d͡ʒone/
entries.notes: Bearer groups read it differently: Basque women (ES 3,097) YOH-neh, Norwegian men (NO 1,228) YOO-neh, Fijian men (Forebears 6.3k; Fijian j is [tʃ]) CHOH-neh, and the largest Forebears group, Mozambique (15.4k), whose reading I could not find. Today's JOHN (Joan) fits none. Basque candidate in us/gb.

entries.name: Perry
entries.notes: Word 'perry' (pear cider). Name and word are read alike: PERR-ee, as today.

entries.name: Zaid
entries.source: Arabic زيد zayd; Iraqi, Levantine and Gulf Arabic [zeːd]
entries.notes: Forebears 2014: Iraq 52k, Yemen 28k, Jordan 19k, UAE 12k, Morocco 11k, Kuwait 10k. Today's ZAYD matches the Iraqi, Levantine and Gulf monophthong.

entries.name: Gustaf
entries.source: sv.wiktionary, Gustaf: older spelling of Gustav; in this old spelling f is said v, and the stressed u is short [ɵ] (German Gustav [ˈɡʊstaf], n0012)
entries.notes: Bearers are Swedish (wd SE 2,125) and Finland-Swedish. Today's GOOS-tahf has the long 'oo'; the short vowel follows Gustav (n0012). No IPA source found for the final v.

entries.name: Zoltán
entries.source: Wikipedia, Zoltán Kodály: Hungarian [ˈkodaːj ˈzoltaːn]
entries.notes: Hungarian stresses the first syllable and keeps the long á full ('tahn', with secondary stress as in Manfred, n0009); today's ZOHL-tun reduces it.

entries.name: Sang
entries.source: Korean 상 Sang [saŋ]; Vietnamese Sang [saːŋ]
entries.notes: Word 'sang' (past of sing), read SANG as today: never replace it. Korean and Vietnamese bearers (wd VN 7, KR 1) say SAHNG, recorded here.

entries.name: Lenny
entries.source: CMUdict LENNY: L EH1 N IY0; Indonesian Lenny [ˈlɛni]
entries.notes: Forebears 2014: Indonesia 27k, US 18k, Philippines 8k, Venezuela 6k, all LEN-ee. The FR register's 29,670 are a French borrowing of the English name; as for Enzo (n0012), French phrase-final prominence is not treated as a separate reading.

entries.name: Tomoko
entries.source: Wiktionary, Tomoko: romaji of ともこ; Tagalog /toˈmoko/; penultimate stress in English (guide)
entries.notes: Today's tuh-MOH-koh differs only in the unstressed first vowel.

entries.name: Aissatou
entries.source: Name sites disagree: familyeducation.com 'eye-sah-TOO'; the diaeresis spelling Aïssatou suggests a-i-sa-tou; no dictionary source
entries.notes: West African form of Aisha (Senegal, Guinea). Today's AY-suh-too has 'ay' and first-syllable stress; the one respelling found and the French-spelling convention (Kadiatou, n0018) give eye-sah-TOO, but the opening (eye or ah-ee) and the stress are unsourced. Candidate in us/gb.

entries.name: Alena
entries.region: Russia, Ukraine, Kazakhstan, Czechia, Slovakia, Belarus
entries.source: Wiktionary, Russian Алёна: [ɐˈlʲɵnə]; Forebears files Russia's Алена (Алёна written without the optional ё; ICAO passport romanization Alena) under this spelling; Wiktionary, Belarusian Алена: [aˈlʲena]; Czech Alena: [ˈalɛna]

alternatives.context: Czech and Slovak AH-leh-nah (Czechia 110k, Slovakia 27k; most of the notable bearers)
Belarusian Alena and US English ah-LAY-nuh (today's reading; Belarus 25k, US 7k)

entries.notes: Forebears 2014 lists this spelling under Russian Алена: Russia 457,865, Czechia 109,791, Ukraine 53,599, Kazakhstan 27,945, Slovakia 26,718, Belarus 24,671, Uzbekistan 12,421, US 7,408. Russian writes Алёна mostly without the ё, and passports romanize it Alena (Alena Kostornaia is Алёна), so the Russian-speaking bearers (about 570k with Ukraine, Kazakhstan and Central Asia) say ah-LYOH-nuh. That outnumbers Czech and Slovak AH-leh-nah (about 137k) and the Belarusian and US ah-LAY-nuh (about 32k) together. Today's ah-LAY-nuh has the right stress but the wrong stressed vowel for them. Russian ё [ɵ] after a soft l → 'yoh' (as Artyom, n0009). Changed in review from already-correct.

entries.name: Ramin
entries.source: Wiktionary, Persian رامین (râmin): Iran formal [ɹɒː.míːn]; Behind the Name /ɾɒː.ˈmiːn/ (Persian)
entries.notes: Today's US RAM-in stresses the first syllable; GB has the 'cat' vowel for â.

entries.name: Tobi
entries.source: Yoruba Tobi (short for Oluwatobi, Tobiloba) [tó.bi]; German Tobi [ˈtoːbi]
entries.notes: Forebears 2014: Nigeria 29.6k, Iran 22.7k (reading not found), US 5.1k. Today's TOH-bee matches the Yoruba, German and English readings.

entries.name: Franciszek
entries.source: Wiktionary, Polish Franciszek: /franˈt͡ɕi.ʂɛk/
entries.notes: Today's frun-CHISH-ek has the short 'bit' vowel; Polish i is 'ee'. ć [tɕ] → ch, sz [ʂ] → sh (guide). Bearers: Poland (wd PL 1,133) and Polish families in the UK and Ireland.

entries.name: Ching
entries.source: Mandarin 清/青 qīng [t͡ɕʰiŋ] written Ching in Wade–Giles (as Qing, n0002)
entries.notes: Word 'ching' (and the I Ching). The name is CHING, as today, so nothing changes.

entries.name: Zhiyuan
entries.source: Mandarin 志远/志遠 zhìyuǎn: zhi as Zhiming (n0003) + yuan [ɥɛn] (as Siyuan, n0006)
entries.notes: Today's ZHEE-oo-ahn reads zh as the 'measure' sound and splits yuan. two-syllable Chinese given name: final primary stress (guide convention).

entries.name: Sinh
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese sinh: Hà Nội [sïŋ˧˧], Huế and Saigon [ʂɨn˧˧] ~ [sɨn˧˧]
entries.notes: Today's SIN matches the southern reading, as Minh and Linh in earlier batches.

entries.name: Lâm
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese lâm: [ləm˧˧] (all three regions)
entries.notes: â is [ə], English 'u' (as Tâm, n0013); today's LAM uses the 'cat' vowel.

entries.name: Thiên
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese thiên: Hà Nội [tʰiən˧˧], Huế and Saigon [tʰiəŋ˧˧]
entries.notes: th is an aspirated t and iê a centring diphthong (as Miên, n0009); today's THEEN reads th as English th.

entries.name: Trâm
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese trâm: Huế and Saigon [ʈəm˧˧], Hà Nội [t͡ɕəm˧˧]
entries.notes: tr as Trang (n0012), â as Tâm (n0013); today's TRAM uses the 'cat' vowel.

entries.name: Tài
entries.source: Vietnamese tài [taːj˨˩] (as Thái, n0015)
entries.notes: Today's TIE matches.

entries.name: Đình
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese đình: Hà Nội [ʔɗïŋ˨˩], Huế [ʔɗɨn˦˩], Saigon [ʔɗɨn˨˩]
entries.notes: Đ is d (as Đức, n0010); -inh as Minh. Today's SIN misreads the first letter.

entries.name: Đạt
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese đạt: Hà Nội [ʔɗaːt̚˧˨ʔ], Saigon [ʔɗaːk̚˨˩˨]
entries.notes: Đ is d (as Đức, n0010) and a is long 'ah'; today's EET drops the first letter.

entries.name: Meiyu
entries.source: Mandarin 美玉 měiyù: mei [meɪ̯] (as Mei, n0003) + yu [y] (as Yu, n0001)
entries.notes: Today's mAjˈu matches (as Meiyun, n0017).

entries.name: Huán
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 歡 huān [xu̯an] (Huan, n0008); 桓/環 huán have the same syllable
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today says the 'lot' vowel (HWON). US already right.

entries.name: Jianquan
entries.source: Mandarin 建全 jiànquán: jian as Jian (n0003) + quan [tɕʰɥɛn] (as Xiuquan, n0018)
entries.notes: Today's wee-ANG-kwahn misreads both syllables. two-syllable Chinese given name: final primary stress (guide convention).

entries.name: Jiāhuá
entries.source: Mandarin 家驊/家骅 jiāhuá: jia [tɕja] (as Jiā, n0005) + hua [xu̯a] (as Hua, n0004)
entries.notes: Today's JY-uh-hoo-uh reads jia as 'jye' and splits hua. two-syllable Chinese given name: final primary stress (guide convention).

entries.name: Měiqín
entries.source: Mandarin 美琴 měiqín: mei [meɪ̯] (as Mei, n0003) + qin [tɕʰin] (as Qin, n0003)
entries.notes: Today's MEE-kin reads ei as 'ee' and q as k. two-syllable Chinese given name: final primary stress (guide convention).

entries.name: Tiān
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 天 tiān /tʰi̯ɛn⁵⁵/; 添 tiān has the same syllable (as Tian, n0003)
entries.notes: Today's TYAHN reads -ian as 'yahn'; pinyin -ian is [jɛn].

entries.name: Wényù
entries.source: Mandarin 文裕 wényù: as Wenyu (n0014): wen [wən] + yu [y]
entries.notes: Today's WEN-yoo uses the 'bed' vowel and stresses the first syllable. two-syllable Chinese given name: final primary stress (guide convention).

entries.name: Yuǎn
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mandarin 遠 yuǎn [ɥɛn]; as the standalone Yuan (n0003)
entries.notes: Today's yoo-AHN reads -uan as 'wahn'; pinyin yuan is [ɥɛn].

entries.name: Zōngyì
entries.source: Mandarin 宗义/宗義 zōngyì: zong [tsʊŋ] (z → dz as Zijian, n0018; -ong as Hong) + yi [i] (as Jiayi, n0006)
entries.notes: Today's ZAWNG-yee reads z as English z and stresses the first syllable. two-syllable Chinese given name: final primary stress (guide convention).

entries.name: Mari
entries.source: Wiktionary, Mari: Finnish /ˈmɑri/, English /ˈmɑɹi/ (UK /ˈmɑːɹi/), Hungarian [ˈmɒri], Welsh /ˈmaːri/

alternatives.context: some English-speaking bearers who say it like Mary

entries.notes: Every main group (Norwegian, Finnish, Estonian, Welsh, Japanese, Spanish diminutive) says MAH-ree, as today.

entries.name: Rocío
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish rocío: /roˈθio/ (Spain), /roˈsio/ (Latin America); the accent marks stress on í
entries.notes: Today's ROH-see-oh stresses the first syllable; the written accent puts it on -cí-. Latin American s (the bearers are mostly Peruvian, Argentine, Mexican).

entries.name: Estelle
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Estelle: /ɛs.tɛl/; English /ɛˈstɛl/
entries.notes: French (FR 71,805) and English bearers agree on final stress, as today.

entries.name: Alper
entries.source: Turkish Alper [alˈpeɾ]: regular Turkish orthography; Turkish names stress the last syllable (as Mehmet, Murat in earlier batches)
entries.notes: Today's AL-per is an English spelling reading with first-syllable stress and the 'cat' vowel.

entries.name: Berta
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Berta: /ˈbeɾta/; German Berta [ˈbɛʁta]

alternatives.context: English-speaking bearers who say it like Bertha

entries.notes: Spanish bearers (ES 20,618) and German, Austrian, Swedish and Hungarian ones say BEHR-tuh; today's BUR-tuh is the English Bertha (n0015 kept that reading for the -th- spelling).

entries.name: Yasuo
entries.source: Japanese やすお Yasuo [jasɯo]: three syllables; Japanese names take penultimate stress in English (guide)
entries.notes: Today's US yah-SOO-oh matches. GB has a 'lot' vowel in the unstressed first syllable only.

entries.name: Michèle
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Michèle: /mi.ʃɛl/
entries.notes: Today's mɪʃˈɛl differs only in the unstressed first vowel.

entries.name: György
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hungarian György: [ˈɟørɟ]; one syllable (gy is one consonant)
entries.notes: Hungarian gy [ɟ] has no English match: English speakers use j. ö [ø] → the 'ur' vowel (guide). Today's JOR-jee adds a second syllable from the spelling's final y.

entries.name: Eden
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Eden: /ˈiːdən/
entries.notes: English-speaking bearers (US 59k, GB, CA, IE, AU) are the largest group.

entries.name: Grzegorz
entries.source: Wiktionary, Polish Grzegorz: /ˈɡʐɛ.ɡɔʂ/
entries.notes: Polish rz is zh, devoiced to sh at the end; penultimate stress. Today's GUR-zuh-gorz is a spelling guess. Polish o as in Krzysztof (n0014).

entries.name: Jeannette
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Jeannette: /dʒəˈnɛt/
entries.notes: US bearers (52k) are the largest group.

entries.name: Umberto
entries.source: Wiktionary, Italian Umberto: /umˈbɛr.to/
entries.notes: Today's əmbˈɛɹtˌO has the stressed BEHR and the consonants right; only the unstressed first vowel is reduced.

entries.name: Hailey
entries.source: English Hailey: /ˈheɪli/ (as Haley, Hayley)

entries.name: Chanda
entries.source: NamePlay (name-site model for US usage): CHAN-duh most likely, SHAN-duh second; Hindi चंदा candā [t͡ʃən.d̪aː]

alternatives.context: Bemba Chanda (Zambia, where it is very common): CHAHN-duh

entries.notes: Population call: the registers are dominated by US bearers (6,094 births), for whom CHAN-duh is the usual reading. Zambian bearers are probably numerous but are not in the counts; review if Zambia is weighted.

entries.name: Karima
entries.region: France, Spain, Algeria, Tunisia, Egypt, Morocco
entries.source: Arabic كريمة karīma [kaˈriːma]: stress on the long ī
entries.notes: Today's kɑɹˈimə matches: stressed REE, consonants right.

entries.name: Giulia
entries.source: Wiktionary, Italian Giulia: /ˈd͡ʒu.lja/
entries.notes: Two syllables: the i only marks the soft g and the li is a glide. Today's JOO-lee-uh adds a syllable.

entries.name: Renzo
entries.source: Wikipedia, Renzo Piano: Italian [ˈrɛntso ˈpjaːno]

alternatives.context: Peruvian and other Spanish-speaking bearers: REN-soh

entries.notes: Italian z here is ts (as Lorenzo, n0005); today's REN-zoh voices it.

entries.name: Nolan
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Nolan: /ˈnoʊlən/
entries.notes: English-speaking bearers (US 129k, CA 17k, GB, IE) outnumber the French.

entries.name: Hideki
entries.source: Japanese ひでき Hideki [çideki]; penultimate stress in English (guide), e open → 'ay' (guide table)
entries.notes: Today's hɪdˈAki matches apart from the unstressed first vowel.

entries.name: Renée
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Renée: /ʁə.ne/

entries.name: Hilary
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Hilary: /ˈhɪləɹi/

entries.name: Memet
entries.source: Turkish/Uyghur Memet, a colloquial form of Mehmet [mehˈmet]: final stress as Turkish names (Mehmet n0002)
entries.notes: Today's MEM-it stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Tsutomu
entries.source: Japanese つとむ Tsutomu [tsɯtomɯ]; penultimate stress in English (guide)
entries.notes: Today's tsutˈOmu matches.

entries.name: Shafiq
entries.source: Arabic شفيق šafīq [ʃaˈfiːq]: stress on the long ī; q → k (guide)
entries.notes: Today's ʃəfˈik matches.

entries.name: Ayad
entries.source: Arabic إياد Iyād [ʔiˈjaːd] (Wikipedia, Ayad Allawi: 'also spelled Iyad or Eyad'); stress on the long ā; the Ayad spelling records the colloquial a
entries.notes: Today's ˌIˈɑd (eye-AHD; GB eye-OD) has no y glide and GB turns the long ā into 'lot'. Some Egyptian bearers spell عياد ʿAyyād the same way, also ay-YAHD.

entries.name: Geneviève
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Geneviève: /ʒə.nə.vjɛv/, /ʒən.vjɛv/

alternatives.context: English Genevieve (usually written without accents): JEN-uh-veev

entries.notes: The accented spelling is the French name (FR 136,220); French names take final stress in English. Today's JEN-uh-veev is the English Genevieve.

entries.name: Sohail
entries.source: Urdu سہیل Sohail [soˈɦeːl] (Arabic سهيل suhayl [suˈhajl]): stress on the long final syllable
entries.notes: Today's SOH-hail stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Aidan
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Aidan: /ˈeɪdən/
entries.notes: Today's ˈAdɑn has the stressed AY and the consonants right; only the unstressed vowel is full (guide: not a correction). Aiden (n0018) is the same reading.

entries.name: Lindsey
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Lindsey: /ˈlɪndzi/

entries.name: Kawthar
entries.source: Arabic كوثر kawṯar [ˈkawθar]: aw is the 'ow' diphthong, stress on the first syllable

alternatives.context: Maghrebi bearers (Kaoutar, Kawtar), who say t for ṯ

entries.notes: Today's KAW-thur uses the 'law' vowel for the aw diphthong.

entries.name: Izhar
entries.source: Urdu اظہار izhār [ɪzˈɦaːr]; Hebrew יזהר Yizhar (Izhar Cohen) [izˈhaʁ]: both keep the h and stress the second syllable
entries.notes: Today's iz-AHR drops the h.

entries.name: Salah ad-Din
entries.source: Wikipedia, Saladin: Arabic Ṣalāḥ ad-Dīn [sˤaˈlaːħ adˈdiːn]

alternatives.context: the English name Saladin, for the sultan

entries.notes: Ḥ → h, geminate dd single (guide). Salah as Salah (n0005). Today's SAL-uh ad-DIN stresses Salah on the wrong syllable.

entries.name: Sahir
entries.source: Urdu/Arabic ساحر sāḥir [ˈsaːhɪr] (Sahir Ludhianvi, ساحر لدھیانوی): stress on the long first syllable
entries.notes: Today's suh-HEER stresses the short second syllable.

entries.name: Nawal
entries.source: Arabic نوال nawāl (Wikipedia, Nawal El Saadawi: Nawāl): stress on the long final ā, as Jamal (n0003)
entries.notes: Today's NAY-wul stresses the first syllable and reads a as 'ay'.

entries.name: Khairul
entries.source: Malay Khairul (from Arabic khayr ul-): kh → k, ai → 'eye'; Malay regular orthography
entries.notes: Today's kˈIɹəl matches apart from the unstressed second vowel.

entries.name: Brad
entries.notes: Also the word 'brad' (a small nail). Name and word read the same, BRAD, as today.

entries.name: Vitor
entries.source: Wikipedia, Vitor Belfort: Portuguese [ˈvitoʁ viˈejɾɐ bɛwˈfɔʁ]
entries.notes: Today's VY-ter reads it as English. Portuguese r → r (guide).

entries.name: Bahareh
entries.source: Behind the Name, Bahareh: /bæ.hɒː.ˈɾe/ (a variant of Bahar)
entries.notes: Final -eh is Persian [e]; written 'ay' (A), the nearest full English vowel, as Fatemeh and Afsaneh in earlier batches (Iranians' own vowel has no glide). Matches n0024. Today's buh-HAR-eh stresses the second syllable.

entries.name: Rima
entries.source: Arabic ريما Rīmā [ˈriːma]; Lithuanian Rima [ˈrʲɪma]: first-syllable stress
entries.notes: Today's ɹˈimə matches.

entries.name: Severino
entries.source: Spanish/Italian Severino [seveˈriːno]: penultimate stress
entries.notes: Today's sɛvəɹˈinO matches apart from an unstressed vowel.

entries.name: Noriko
entries.source: Japanese のりこ Noriko [noɾiko]; penultimate stress in English (guide)
entries.notes: Today's nˌɔɹˈikO keeps the stressed REE; the secondary-stressed first vowel is close enough (as Hiroyuki, n0014).

entries.name: Gianluca
entries.source: Wikipedia, Gianluca Vialli: Italian [dʒanˈluːka]
entries.notes: Today's JAHN-loo-kuh stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Ilona
entries.source: Wiktionary, Polish Ilona: /iˈlɔ.na/; German [iˈloːna]; Hungarian [ˈilonɒ]
entries.notes: Population call: French (FR 13,695), German, Polish, English and Czech bearers stress -LO-; Hungarian and Finnish stress the first syllable.

entries.name: Žarko
entries.source: Serbo-Croatian Жарко Žarko [ʒǎːrko]: ž is zh; first-syllable stress (as Darko, Marko)
entries.notes: Today's ZAR-koh reads ž as z.

entries.name: Elio
entries.source: Wiktionary, Italian Elio: /ˈɛ.ljo/; Spanish Elio [ˈeljo]
entries.notes: Two syllables: io is a diphthong. Today's EL-ee-oh adds a syllable.

entries.name: Newton
entries.notes: Also the word 'newton' (unit of force), and in English text mostly Isaac Newton. Read the same as the name today; Brazilian bearers (NEW-tong) are a small group.

entries.name: Fidelis
entries.source: Wiktionary, Latin fidēlis: /fiˈdeː.lis/; German Fidelis [fiˈdeːlɪs]
entries.notes: The church-Latin name keeps the long e. Nigerian Catholic bearers are probably the largest group and may say fi-DEH-lis; no source found for them, so confidence is low.

entries.name: Jenna
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Jenna: /ˈdʒɛnə/

entries.name: Atif
entries.source: Wikipedia, Atif Aslam: Punjabi [ɑːt̪ɪf əsləm]; Arabic عاطف ʿāṭif, stress on the long ā
entries.notes: Today's uh-TEEF stresses the short second syllable (as Asif, Abid in earlier batches).

entries.name: Tamanna
entries.source: Hindi/Urdu तमन्ना / تمنا tamannā [t̪əˈmənːaː]: Hindi short a is 'uh' (as Chandra, n0002); geminate nn single

alternatives.context: Bengali তামান্না (Bangladesh, many UK bearers): tah-MAHN-nah

entries.notes: Today's tuh-MAN-uh uses the 'cat' vowel.

entries.name: Percival
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Percival: /ˈpɜːsɪvəl/

entries.name: Lennox
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Lennox: /ˈlɛnəks/

entries.name: Gilson
entries.source: Brazilian Portuguese Gilson [ˈʒiwsõ]: g before i is zh, coda l is w (Gilberto /ʒiwˈbɛʁ.tu/, n0007); first-syllable stress as Edson [ˈɛdsõ] (n0009)
entries.notes: Today's GIL-sun reads g as hard. Brazilian bearers dominate (wd BR 86).

entries.name: Masaaki
entries.source: Japanese まさあき Masaaki [masaːki]: aa is one long vowel, so three syllables; penultimate stress in English (guide)
entries.notes: Today's mah-sah-AH-kee splits the long aa into two syllables; GB uses 'lot' vowels.

entries.name: Brendon
entries.source: English Brendon /ˈbɹɛndən/ (as Brendan)

entries.name: Arlette
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Arlette: /aʁ.lɛt/
entries.notes: Final stress as today.

entries.name: Rupa
entries.source: Hindi/Bengali रूपा / রূপা rūpā [ˈruːpaː]
entries.notes: Today's ɹˈupə matches; the unstressed final ā is 'uh' (as Geeta, Asha in earlier batches).

entries.name: Suying
entries.source: Mandarin 素英 sùyīng: su [su] + ying [iŋ] (Help:IPA/Mandarin); final primary stress (guide's convention)
entries.notes: Today's SY-ing reads su-y as 'sigh'.

entries.name: Lata
entries.source: Wikipedia, Lata Mangeshkar: Marathi [ləˈt̪aː məŋˈɡeːʃkəɾ]

alternatives.context: South Indian bearers, first-syllable stress (as the Latha spelling, n0013)

entries.notes: Hindi short a is 'uh' and the long final ā takes the stress; today's LAH-tuh reverses them. Matches the alternative recorded for Latha (n0013).

entries.name: Armel
entries.source: French/Breton Armel [aʁ.mɛl]: final stress
entries.notes: Today's ɑɹmˈɛl matches.

entries.name: Amanullah
entries.source: Wikipedia, Amanullah Khan: Dari [ʔä.mɑːn‿ʊl.lɑ́ː(ʱ)], Pashto [ʔa.mɑ.nu(l).lɑ(h)]: stress on the final -lāh
entries.notes: Today's am-uh-NULL-uh puts the stress on -ul-. Geminate ll single; final h dropped as bearers do.

entries.name: Kiyoshi
entries.source: Japanese きよし Kiyoshi [kʲijoɕi]: ki-yo-shi; penultimate stress in English (guide)
entries.notes: Today's kee-OH-shee drops the y between i and o.

entries.name: Dany
entries.source: Wikipedia, Dany Boon: French [dani bun]; French names take final stress in English (guide), front a as Yannick (n0010)
entries.notes: Today's DAY-nee reads the a as 'ay'. French-speaking bearers (FR 26,145, CA 1,604, BE, CH, LB) dominate.

entries.name: Abdel
entries.source: Arabic عبد ال ʿAbd al- [ˈʕabdel]: ʿayn dropped (guide); Egyptian and Maghrebi a is front, as in Abdelaziz (n0003)

alternatives.context: AHB-del, the form used for Abdel Fattah (n0015)

entries.notes: Today's ˈæbdˌɛl keeps the stress and consonants. Precedents differ on the first vowel (Abdelaziz æ, Abdel Fattah ɑ); kept today's.

entries.name: Lamia
entries.source: Arabic لمياء lamyāʾ: the final long ā (with hamza) takes the stress by Arabic stress rules; Maghrebi bearers in France say [la.mja] with French final stress

alternatives.context: the word lamia (Greek myth, Keats): LAY-mee-uh, today's reading

entries.notes: The collision is a rare literary word, while the name's bearers are many (FR 4,110, US 1,378, ES 730, Arab world), so treated as a name (guide). Today's LAY-mee-uh is the word. Stress is the uncertain part: some bearers may say LAHM-yah.
entries.word_check: gold has 'lamia'; kept: 'lamia' (a mythical monster) is rare

entries.name: Takao
entries.source: Japanese たかお Takao [takao]: three syllables; penultimate stress in English (guide)
entries.notes: US today is right; GB tˌɒkˈɒQ turns the stressed 'ah' into 'lot' (a GB-only fix, as Khalid in the guide).

entries.name: Predrag

entries.name: Savannah
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Savannah: /səˈvænə/

entries.name: Chico
entries.source: Spanish chico [ˈtʃiko]; US bearers (US 946) and Cuban bearers use the Spanish reading

entries.notes: Population call: registered bearers are mostly US (Spanish/English CHEE-koh, today's); Brazilian notables (SHEE-koo) are many on Wikidata but the name there is a nickname for Francisco. The same spelling is also Chico, California (CHEE-koh). Review if Brazilian bearers should win.

entries.name: Ayan

entries.source: Hindi/Urdu अयान / ایان Ayaan [əˈjaːn]: stress on the long ā; Somali Ayan [aˈjan] also stresses -yan

entries.name: Fátima

entries.name: Vital
entries.source: French Vital [vi.tal]: final stress, front a (as Pascal, Yannick)
entries.notes: Also the common word 'vital' (VY-tul), which must not change. The French name reading vee-TAL is recorded in us/gb.

entries.name: Manal
entries.source: Arabic منال manāl [maˈnaːl]: stress on the long final syllable (as Jamal, n0003)
entries.notes: Today's MAY-nul stresses the first syllable and reads a as 'ay'.

entries.name: Nils
entries.source: Swedish and Norwegian Nils [nɪls]; Wiktionary, German Nils: /niːls/; all end in s
entries.notes: Today's NILZ voices the final s; Scandinavian and German bearers say s.

entries.name: Aaliyah
entries.source: Wikipedia, Aaliyah: English /ɑːˈliːə/
entries.notes: Today's AH-li-yuh stresses the first syllable. The name's popularity in the US comes from the singer Aaliyah.

entries.name: Janina

entries.notes: Polish j is y; today's juh-NEE-nuh uses the English j.

entries.name: Aurélien

entries.notes: French names take final stress in English; -ien [jɛ̃] is 'yan' (as Julien, Sébastien). Today's ow-RAY-lee-un is a spelling guess.

entries.name: Dede

entries.notes: Also the word 'bailey' (castle courtyard; the Old Bailey). Name and word read the same, as today.

entries.source: Wiktionary, English Jeffery: /ˈdʒɛfəɹi/

entries.name: Mian

entries.name: Xiaoli

alternatives.context: Timothée Chalamet's English reading (Wikipedia /ˈtɪməθi/, TIM-uh-thee); he says his name like English Timothy when speaking English

entries.notes: French names take final stress in English; unstressed French o rendered 'oh' (as Nicolas, Ludovic). Today's TIM-uh-thee also voices the th (ð), wrong even for the English reading. Decision to review: in English text this spelling is mostly Timothée Chalamet. Wikipedia gives his English reading as TIM-uh-thee and says he uses the English 'Timothy' pronunciation when speaking English, calling the French one pretentious there. The French bearers (FR register 23,955 births) were kept as the main reading per the guide; switching to TIM-uh-thee (tˈɪməθi) would follow Chalamet's own English usage.

entries.notes: Today's TA-hur has the 'cat' vowel in the stressed syllable. Maghrebi spelling of Tahir; the second vowel is a in Maghrebi Arabic, hence the spelling. Low (review): no source gives IPA or stress for the Maghrebi form; first-syllable stress follows the Arabic long-ā rule (as Tahira, n0022), while Wikipedia's Taher (name) page gives final-stress [tˤɑːˈher] (likely the Persian form) and French speakers say ta-AR.

alternatives.context: English-speaking bearers (US, UK, Canada) and every other English use (Dorian Gray, the Dorian mode, the Dorians): DOR-ee-un, today's reading

entries.notes: Protected: capitalised Dorian in English text is mostly the Greek Dorians, the Dorian mode, Dorian Gray and Hurricane Dorian, all DOR-ee-un (today's reading). Among bearers, the French group (FR register 33.9k plus Belgium and Congo) is the largest single reading; Spanish, Romanian and Albanian bearers also stress the last syllable. entries.region: Spain, Latin America, Poland, Romania, Italy, Germany
entries.source: Wiktionary Aurelia: Spanish /auˈɾelja/, Polish /awˈrɛ.lja/, Latin /au̯ˈreː.li.a/; today's ow-RAY-lee-uh keeps the stressed 'ray' and differs only in the unstressed -lia
entries.notes: Spanish, Polish, Romanian, Italian and German bearers say ow-REH-lya and together outnumber the English group (anglo_share 0.11).

entries.name: Bintou
entries.source: French spelling of Mande Bintu: regular orthography gives i and u; first-syllable stress as for Binta (n0016, today's BIN-tuh kept)
entries.notes: Mande languages are tonal and no source gives an English stress; today's first-syllable stress follows the Binta precedent. French speakers stress the last syllable.

entries.name: Stacy
entries.source: English Stacy /ˈsteɪsi/ (as Stacey); today's STAY-see matches

entries.name: Kelechi
entries.source: Igbo Kelechi ('thank God'): Igbo orthography is phonemic, e = [e], ch = [tʃ]; open-syllable e as 'ay' and second-syllable stress as for Emeka (n0013) and Chinedu (n0022)

alternatives.context: British sports commentary (Kelechi Iheanacho): keh-LETCH-ee, today's reading

entries.notes: Tones dropped. Igbo has no [ɛ]; its close-mid e is 'ay' in an open syllable (guide table). Today's keh-LEH-chee differs only in the stressed vowel.

entries.name: Reginaldo
entries.source: Brazilian Portuguese spelling rules: g before i is [ʒ], syllable-final l is [w], final -o is [u]; stress on -nal- (as Geraldo [ʒeˈɾawdu], n0011)
entries.notes: Brazilian bearers dominate (wd BR 63). Today's rej-uh-NAHL-doh is an English reading with English j. Initial r kept as r (guide), as Rogério and Raimundo.

entries.name: Ángela
entries.source: Spanish spelling rules: the accent marks the first syllable, g before e is [x] ([ˈaŋxela]); as Ángel (n0004)
entries.notes: Spanish g before e [x] becomes h (guide). Today's AN-juh-luh is English Angela; the accented spelling is only the Spanish name.

entries.name: Scarlett
entries.source: English Scarlett /ˈskɑɹlɪt/, as the word scarlet; today's SKAR-lit matches

entries.name: Anicet
entries.source: French spelling rules: final -et is [ɛ] with a silent t ([a.ni.sɛ]); English renders French final -et as 'ay' (ballet, Monet); final stress as French names take in English (Florent, n0017)
entries.notes: French form of Anicetus (FR register 1.8k, Congo, Cameroon). Today's AN-uh-set reads it as English.

entries.name: Boualem
entries.source: Wikipedia, Boualem Sansal: French [bwalɛm]; Arabic بوعلام

alternatives.context: Algerian Arabic Bū-ʿallām with the vowels kept apart: boo-ah-LEM

entries.notes: Algerian bearers (wd DZ 29, FR register 835). Stress on the last syllable in French and on the long final syllable in Arabic. Today's boo-AH-lum stresses the middle.

entries.name: Chalifa
entries.source: Arabic خليفة khalīfa [xaˈliːfa]; this spelling's ch transliterates kh [x] (Dutch, German and Hebrew-style romanisation); guide: Arabic kh → k
entries.notes: Same name as Khalifa. Today's chuh-LEE-fuh reads ch as English ch.

entries.name: Montserrat
entries.source: Wiktionary Montserrat: Spanish /montseˈrat/; Catalan [mun.səˈrat]; English /ˌmɑntsəˈɹæt/ (US), /mɒn(t)səˈɹæt/ (UK)

alternatives.context: English: the Caribbean island and the Catalan mountain, today's reading

entries.notes: Covered by the tech lexicon with the English place reading. In English text Montserrat is mostly the British island and the Catalan mountain and monastery, mont-suh-RAT, so it stays protected. Spanish bearers (ES register 103k, Mexico) say mohnt-say-RAHT, in us/gb.

entries.name: Segun
entries.source: Yoruba Ṣẹ́gun ('victory'), the second part of Olúṣẹ́gun; Wikipedia, Olusegun Obasanjo: [ōlúʃɛ́ɡũ̄]; ṣ is 'sh', ẹ is open 'eh' (as Olusegun, n0020)
entries.notes: The plain spelling drops the dot under s, but bearers say 'sh'. Today's SEE-gun misreads both. Tones dropped; English stress on the high-toned first syllable.

entries.name: Aminu
entries.source: Hausa Aminu (from Amīn): ā-mī-nu; today's uh-MEE-noo keeps the stressed 'mee' and differs only in the unstressed first vowel
entries.notes: Tones and vowel length dropped.

entries.name: Roma
entries.source: Wiktionary Roma: English /ˈɹoʊmə/ (GA), /ˈɹəʊmə/ (RP); German /ˈroːma/; Russian Рома and Polish Roma also stress ROH
entries.notes: Same reading for the English, Slavic and Italian uses (and the Romani people).

entries.name: Cahya
entries.source: Indonesian spelling rules: c is [tʃ], h is pronounced; penultimate stress (Indonesian cahya 'light')
entries.notes: Today's KAH-yuh reads c as k and drops the h.

entries.name: Wahyu
entries.source: Wiktionary Indonesian Wahyu (id-pr wahyu); Indonesian spelling rules: h before a consonant is pronounced; penultimate stress
entries.notes: Today's WAH-yoo drops the h; British today also says the 'lot' vowel.

entries.name: Polly
entries.source: English Polly /ˈpɒli/ (UK), /ˈpɑli/ (US); today's reading matches

entries.name: Isla
entries.source: Wiktionary Isla: English given name /aɪlə/ (from the river Isla and Islay)
entries.notes: Today's EE-luh is wrong for the Scottish name, now a top name in the UK; the s is silent.

entries.name: Elżbieta
entries.source: Wiktionary Polish Elżbieta: /ɛlʐˈbjɛ.ta/
entries.notes: ż is 'zh' and bie is 'bye'; penultimate stress. Today's el-z-BEE-tuh misreads ż and ie.

entries.name: Lance
entries.source: Wiktionary Lance: /læns/, /lɑːns/
entries.notes: Ordinary word 'lance' (uncommon; also Lance corporal). The name sounds the same as the word, and today's US læns / GB lɑːns is right; nothing to change.

entries.name: Abba
entries.source: Wikipedia, Abba Eban: English /ˈɑːbə ˈiːbən/; Hebrew אבא [ˈaba]

alternatives.context: the Aramaic and liturgical 'Abba, Father' in British dictionaries (Wiktionary: /ˈæb.ə/)

entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today says AB-uh; Israeli and Nigerian bearers (Abba Eban, Abba Kyari) say AH-buh. US already right. ABBA the band is all capitals and not matched.

entries.name: Corinne
entries.source: French Corinne [kɔ.ʁin] (Wiktionary fr-IPA); today's kuh-REEN differs only in the unstressed first vowel
entries.notes: French bearers (FR register 163k) far outnumber English ones (US 42k).

entries.name: Sheikh
entries.source: English sheikh /ʃeɪk/, /ʃiːk/ (Wiktionary sheikh); Arabic شيخ shaykh, Urdu and Bengali [ʃeːx]
entries.notes: The title 'Sheikh' (capitalised before names: Sheikh Mohammed, Sheikh Hasina) is an ordinary English word, read 'sheek' (today's US) or 'shake' (today's GB), both accepted. Bearers of the given name (GB register 1.3k) say SHAYK, recorded in us/gb.

entries.name: Demetrio
entries.source: Spanish spelling rules: penultimate stress, e in the open syllable me- is [e] ([deˈmetɾjo]); Wiktionary Italian Demetrio: Demètrio (open ɛ)

alternatives.context: Italian bearers: deh-MEH-tree-oh, today's stressed vowel

entries.notes: Spanish bearers (ES register 4.1k, US 2.9k mostly Hispanic, Peru, Mexico) outnumber Italian ones. Stressed e in an open syllable is 'ay' (guide table; as Valeria, n0009). Today's deh-MEH- is the Italian vowel.

entries.name: Elia
entries.source: Wiktionary Italian Elia: it-pr Elìa (stress on li); Spanish Elia [eˈli.a] (penultimate)

alternatives.context: English speakers' spelling reading: EE-lee-uh, today's

entries.notes: Italian men (wd IT 81) and Spanish women (ES register 11k) agree on eh-LEE-uh; together they outnumber the English group (US 9k). Today's EE-lee-uh stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Callum
entries.source: English Callum /ˈkæləm/ (Scottish Gaelic Calum); today's KAL-um matches

entries.name: Roque
entries.source: Wiktionary Roque: Spanish (es-pr) [ˈroke]; Portuguese Róque [ˈʁɔki]
entries.notes: The word 'roque' (a croquet variant) is rare and technical, while the name is the one readers meet (ES register 5.1k, US 2.5k, Argentina, Brazil), so it is treated as a name (guide). Today's ROHK drops the final vowel.
entries.word_check: gold has 'roque'; kept: 'roque' (a croquet variant) is rare

entries.name: Jean-de-Dieu
entries.source: French spelling: Jean [ʒɑ̃], de [də], Dieu [djø]; final stress; Dieu as in Dieudonné (n0008: djudɔnˈA / djɜːdɒnˈA)
entries.notes: One hyphenated word, one primary stress. Today's zhahn-duh-DOO drops the y glide of Dieu. French ø is 'yoo' in US English and the 'her' vowel in British, as Dieudonné and Mathieu.

entries.name: Violeta
entries.source: Spanish spelling rules: penultimate stress, e in the open syllable le- is [e] ([bjoˈleta]); Wiktionary Violeta: Spanish (es-pr), Portuguese Violêta (closed e)

alternatives.context: Lithuanian, Romanian and Bulgarian bearers: vee-oh-LEH-tuh, today's reading

entries.notes: Spanish bearers (ES register 11.8k, US 8.3k mostly Hispanic, Peru, Argentina) are the largest group: stressed e in an open syllable is 'ay' (guide table; as Valeria, n0009). v kept as English speakers say it (as Valeria).

entries.name: Gianni
entries.source: Wiktionary Italian Gianni: it-pr Giànni [ˈdʒanni]
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today says JON-ee with the 'lot' vowel. US already right. gi before a is just j (as Gian, n0005).

entries.name: Randall
entries.source: English Randall /ˈɹændəl/; today's RAN-dul matches

entries.name: Mattia
entries.source: Wiktionary Italian Mattia: it-pr Mattìa [matˈtiːa]
entries.notes: Today's MAH-shuh reads -tia as English -tia (as in 'Alicia'). Italian t is a plain t; double tt said once (guide).

entries.name: Marcelle
entries.source: Wiktionary French Marcelle (fr-IPA) [maʁ.sɛl]; today's mar-SEL matches (as Marcel, n0004)

entries.name: Nicky
entries.source: English Nicky /ˈnɪki/; Dutch Nicky is said the same; today's NIK-ee matches

entries.name: Safia
entries.source: Arabic صفية ṣafiyya [sˤaˈfij.ja]: stress on the heavy syllable fiy; ṣ → s (guide)
entries.notes: Maghrebi (FR register 7.4k, Algeria, Tunisia) and South Asian bearers (UK) stress 'fee'. Today's SAH-fee-uh stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Régis
entries.source: Wiktionary French Régis: fr-IPA 'régiss' [ʁe.ʒis] (final s pronounced); Forebears 2014: Régis 43.7k (French-speaking); unaccented Regis: Brazil 17.6k, France 17.3k, Rwanda 13.1k, Burundi 8.7k
entries.notes: French-speaking bearers (France, Belgium, Switzerland, Rwanda, Burundi) are the largest group. Today's REE-jis is the English Regis.

entries.name: Madeline
entries.source: English Madeline /ˈmædəlɪn/; today's MAD-uh-lin matches

entries.name: Mavis
entries.source: Wiktionary Mavis: /ˈmeɪvɪs/; today's MAY-vis matches
entries.notes: Also the rare, poetic word 'mavis' (song thrush). The name is what readers meet and the word sounds the same, so it is treated as a name (guide); nothing changes.

entries.name: Florentino
entries.source: Spanish Florentino [floɾenˈtino] (Wiktionary es-pr); today's flor-en-TEE-noh keeps the stressed 'tee' and differs only in unstressed vowels

entries.name: Peace
entries.source: English peace /piːs/
entries.notes: Ordinary word 'peace' (common, capitalised at a sentence start and in titles). The name (Uganda, Nigeria, Ghana) sounds the same as the word; today's reading is right.

entries.name: Lesley
entries.region: UK, Scotland, US, Australia, New Zealand
entries.source: Wiktionary Leslie: /ˈlɛzli/, /ˈlɛsli/; Lesley is listed there as the usual UK spelling of the women's name

alternatives.context: US and some British speakers: LES-lee

entries.notes: GB-only fix: British and Scottish speakers usually voice the s (LEZ-lee); US keeps today's LES-lee, also accepted there.

entries.name: Akio
entries.source: Japanese あきお a-ki-o; guide convention: Japanese names take penultimate stress in English (Haruki, Takeshi n0012)
entries.notes: Japanese has pitch accent, not stress; English speakers stress the penultimate mora. Today's AH-kee-oh stresses the first.

entries.name: Mathilde
entries.source: Wiktionary French Mathilde (fr-IPA) [ma.tild]; th is a plain t

alternatives.context: Norwegian, Danish and German bearers (NO register 6k, wd DE 103): mah-TIL-duh

entries.notes: French bearers (FR register 125.6k, Belgium, Switzerland) far outnumber the others. Today's MATH-ild reads th as English th.

entries.name: Elisha
entries.source: Wiktionary Elisha: /ɪˈlaɪʃə/ (the prophet and the traditional name); today's ih-LYE-shuh matches

entries.name: Lynda
entries.source: English Lynda /ˈlɪndə/ (as Linda); today's LIN-duh matches

entries.name: Amna
entries.source: Urdu آمنہ / Arabic آمنة (Āmina, shortened Āmna): long ā in the stressed first syllable
entries.notes: Pakistani and Arab bearers say the long 'ah'; today's AM-nuh uses the 'cat' vowel.

entries.name: Adele
entries.source: Wiktionary Adele: English /əˈdɛl/, German /aˈdeːlə/; today's uh-DEL matches the English reading
entries.notes: English bearers (US 27k, Canada, UK) plus French Adèle (same ah-DEL) are the largest reading group; German and Italian bearers say three syllables.

entries.name: Ioannis
entries.source: Wiktionary Greek Ιωάννης: /ioˈa.nis/
entries.notes: Four syllables with the stress on a. Today's eye-oh-AN-us reads it as English.

entries.name: Mamdouh
entries.source: Arabic ممدوح mamdūḥ: stress on the long final ū (superheavy syllable); ḥ → h (guide)
entries.notes: French-style ou is 'oo'. Today's MAM-dow stresses the first syllable and reads ou as 'ow'.

entries.name: Yakubu
entries.source: Wiktionary Hausa Yakubu: Yā̀kubù (long ā); English stress on 'koo' as today
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today says the 'lot' vowel (yok-OO-boo); bearers say 'ah'. US already right. Tones dropped.

entries.name: Aura
entries.source: Spanish Aura [ˈau̯ɾa] (Spanish spelling: au is 'ow'); Finnish Aura [ˈɑurɑ]
entries.notes: Ordinary word 'aura' (uncommon, capitalised at a sentence start), OR-uh, today's reading. Bearers (ES register 2.4k, Colombia, Mexico, Finland, Romania) say OW-ruh, recorded in us/gb.

entries.name: Renee
entries.source: English Renee /ɹəˈneɪ/ (from French Renée); today's ruh-NAY matches

entries.name: Saran
entries.region: Guinea, Mali, Ivory Coast, Cambodia, India
entries.source: Forebears 2014: Guinea 1 in 222, Mali 1 in 553, Cambodia 1 in 547, India, Thailand, Ivory Coast
entries.notes: Bearers are mostly Guinean and Malian women (Mande Saran, a-a) plus Cambodian, Thai and South Asian (Saran, Sharan) men, each said differently. The Mande vowels are 'ah' (today's suh-RAN has the 'cat' vowel), but no source gives the stress (French speakers say sa-RAN, Mande is tonal). 'Saran' is also the plastic-wrap trademark. Needs a Mande pronunciation source.

entries.name: Anders
entries.source: Wiktionary Anders: Swedish /ˈânːdɛʂ/, Norwegian [ˈɑ̂nː.əʂ], Danish [ˈɑnɐs]
entries.notes: Scandinavian bearers (wd SE 2232, NO register 18.8k, Denmark) dominate. Short a is 'ah' (as Hans, Axel); s is voiceless. Swedish and Norwegian fuse rs into 'sh'; 'ders' is the English approximation, as Lars (n0020). Today's AN-derz has the 'cat' vowel and a z.

entries.name: Adilson
entries.source: Brazilian Portuguese spelling rules: di is [dʒi], syllable-final l is [w]; stress on -dil- (also written Adílson); as Gilson (n0024: ʒˈiwsən)
entries.notes: Brazilian bearers dominate (wd BR 65). The final nasal vowel is reduced to 'sun' as for Gilson. Today's AD-ul-sun reads it as English.

entries.name: Lincoln
entries.source: English Lincoln /ˈlɪŋkən/ (silent second l); today's reading matches

entries.name: Henrik
entries.source: Scandinavian Henrik [ˈhɛnːrɪk] (Hungarian [ˈhɛnrik], Slovene Hẹ̑nrik); today's HEN-rik matches

entries.name: Shantha
entries.source: Tamil சாந்த / Sinhala Shantha from Sanskrit śānta: long ā, dental t (th in the spelling); as Shanta (n0014, Hindi शांता /ʃɑːn.t̪ɑː/)
entries.notes: South Asian th is a dental t, not English th. Today's SHAN-thuh uses the 'cat' vowel and th.

entries.name: Ismaël
entries.source: French spelling: the diaeresis splits a-ë into two syllables [is.ma.ɛl]; final stress; as Ismael (n0007) and Raphaël (n0013)
entries.notes: Today's IZ-mayl merges aë into one syllable.

entries.name: Raed
entries.source: Arabic رائد rāʾid ('pioneer'): long ā stressed, hamza between the vowels; Levantine [ˈraːʔed]
entries.notes: Two syllables: hamza dropped with the vowels kept apart (guide); the voice merges a bare ɑɛ into one syllable ('right'), so a y glide keeps them apart, as English speakers say it. Today's REED merges them.

entries.name: Basit
entries.source: Arabic باسط bāsiṭ (Urdu bāsit): long ā stressed, s voiceless, ṭ → t (guide)
entries.notes: Today's BAZ-it uses the 'cat' vowel and a z.

entries.name: Pape
entries.source: Senegalese Pape (from Papa): French spelling, final e silent [pap]

alternatives.context: English surname Pape (Wiktionary UK /peɪp/), today's reading

entries.notes: Senegalese bearers (wd SN 39, FR register 515). Today's PAYP is an English spelling reading. French [a] as Jacques (US ɑ, GB a).

entries.name: Fabien
entries.source: Wiktionary French Fabien (fr-IPA) [fa.bjɛ̃]; nasal ɛ̃ → 'an' and final stress as Damien (n0014)
entries.notes: Today's FAB-een reads it as English.

entries.name: Conrado
entries.source: Wiktionary Conrado: Spanish (es-pr) [konˈɾaðo]
entries.notes: GB-only in effect: British today says kon-ROD-oh with the 'lot' vowel; US today differs only in the unstressed first vowel.

entries.name: Redouane
entries.source: Wiktionary French Redouane: fr-IPA 'Rédouane' [ʁe.dwan] (from Arabic رضوان riḍwān)
entries.notes: Two syllables with final stress; -ouane is 'dwahn'. Today's ree-doo-AYN reads ou as two vowels and -ane as in 'lane'.

entries.name: Valerio
entries.source: Wiktionary Italian Valerio: it-pr Valèrio (open ɛ)
entries.notes: Italian bearers (wd IT 272) dominate. Today's vuh-LEER-ee-oh is an English reading.

entries.name: Mackenzie
entries.source: English Mackenzie /məˈkɛnzi/; today's reading matches

entries.name: Zaki
entries.source: Arabic زكي zakī; English and colloquial (Egyptian) usage stress the first syllable with 'ah'

alternatives.context: careful Standard Arabic, stress on the long final ī: zah-KEE

entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today says ZOK-ee with the 'lot' vowel. US already right.

entries.name: Emin
entries.source: Turkish and Azerbaijani Emin (Arabic amīn 'trustworthy'): final stress, as Turkish names regularly take (Metin, n0019)
entries.notes: Turkish (wd TR 138) and Azerbaijani bearers dominate. Today's EM-in stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Nadège
entries.region: France, Switzerland, Ivory Coast, DR Congo
entries.source: Wiktionary French Nadège (fr-IPA) [na.dɛʒ]
entries.notes: Today's NAD-ij reads -ège as English -age.

entries.name: Constantino
entries.source: Spanish Constantino [konstanˈtino] (Wiktionary es-pr); today's reading keeps the stressed 'tee' and differs only in unstressed vowels

entries.name: Nicolau
entries.source: Wiktionary Nicolau: Portuguese (pt-IPA) and Catalan; final stress on the diphthong -au
entries.notes: Today's NIK-uh-low stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Abdelhamid
entries.source: Arabic عبد الحميد ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd: stress on the long ī; ḥ → h, ʿayn dropped (guide); as Abdulhamid (n0004)
entries.notes: Today's ab-DEL-uh-mid stresses the article and drops the h.

entries.name: Genevieve
entries.source: English Genevieve /ˈdʒɛnəviːv/; today's reading matches

entries.name: Abdelmalek
entries.source: Arabic عبد الملك ʿAbd al-Malik: Malik stressed on ma; Maghrebi spelling -lek; as Abdelkader (n0008)
entries.notes: Today's ab-DEL-muh-lek stresses the article.

entries.name: Bert
entries.source: Wiktionary Bert: English /bɜːt/ (RP), /bɝt/ (GA); Dutch /bɛrt/; Swedish /ˈbæʈ/

alternatives.context: Dutch, Flemish and German bearers (wd NL 321, BE 135, DE 62): BEHRT

entries.notes: Row is usage english; English bearers (US 20.7k, Australia) and English text (Bert and Ernie, Mary Poppins) keep BURT. Population close with the Dutch and Flemish group; review.

entries.name: Adèle
entries.source: Wiktionary French Adèle (fr-IPA) [a.dɛl]; today's uh-DEL differs only in the unstressed first vowel

entries.name: Jaroslav
entries.source: Czech Jaroslav [ˈjaroslaf] (initial stress; Wiktionary cs-IPA); Slovak /ˈjarɔsɫau̯/
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today ends in the 'lot' vowel (-slov); the Czech a is 'ah' (as Miroslav, n0016). US already right; final devoicing is not marked in English renderings.

entries.name: Yara
entries.region: Brazil, Egypt, Lebanon, Netherlands, UK, US
entries.source: Arabic يارا yārā and Brazilian Yara [ˈjaɾa]: stress on the first syllable with 'ah'; today's YAH-ruh matches

entries.name: Léopold
entries.source: Wiktionary French Léopold: fr-IPA 'léopol(d)' [le.ɔ.pɔl(d)]

alternatives.context: French speakers who drop the final d: lay-aw-POL

entries.notes: Belgian (wd BE 72) and French bearers. Final stress; é is 'ay'. Today's LEE-uh-pold is the English Leopold.

entries.name: Loretta
entries.source: English Loretta /ləˈɹɛtə/; today's reading matches

entries.name: Intan
entries.source: Indonesian and Malay intan ('diamond'; Wiktionary Malay ms-IPA): penultimate stress; today's IN-tun differs only in the unstressed final vowel

entries.name: Tarik
entries.source: Arabic طارق ṭāriq /tˤaː.riq/ (Wiktionary, as Tarek n0007): long ā stressed; ṭ → t, q → k (guide)
entries.notes: Today's TERR-ik reads the a as in 'Terry'.

entries.name: Marjan
entries.source: Wiktionary Marjan: Slovene Mȃrjan, Serbo-Croatian Mȁrjan (stress on the first syllable; j is y)
entries.notes: Slovene men (wd SI 373) are the largest group. Today's MAR-jun reads j as English j.

entries.name: Deo
entries.region: Uganda, Burundi, Rwanda, DR Congo, Tanzania
entries.source: Forebears 2014: Uganda 41.8k, Burundi 36.9k, Rwanda 12.3k, DR Congo 11.0k, Tanzania 9.6k, India 9.0k (short for Deogratias); Latin dēō, Wiktionary German /ˈdeː.o/

alternatives.context: English spelling reading (some US bearers), today's

entries.notes: East African Catholic bearers (Deogratias, 'thanks be to God') say DAY-oh; Latin Deo in English text (Deo gratias, Deo volente) is DAY-oh too. Today's DEE-oh is a spelling reading.

entries.name: Aleksandr
entries.source: Wiktionary Russian Александр: /ɐlʲɪkˈsandr/
entries.notes: Russian-speaking bearers (Russia, Estonia's Russian community, Ukraine). Russian has ks and 'ah' where today's al-ig-ZAN-der (English Alexander) has gz and the 'cat' vowel. Russian ends in -ndr with no vowel; the voice turns a bare final dɹ into 'Alexandra', so the English 'der' is kept.

entries.name: Arash
entries.source: Wiktionary, Persian آرش (âraš): Iran formal [ʔɒː.ɹǽʃ]; Behind the Name /ʔɒː.ˈɾæʃ/
entries.notes: Today's ˈæɹəʃ (ARR-ush) stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Hamilton
entries.source: Wiktionary Hamilton: /ˈhæməltən/ (GA, RP)
entries.notes: In English text Hamilton is mostly the surname and the places (Alexander and Lewis Hamilton, the musical, Hamilton in Ontario, Bermuda and New Zealand), HAM-ul-tun, today's reading. English-speaking bearers of the given name say the same. Brazilian bearers (wd BR 36) say it the Portuguese way, unsourced here.

entries.name: Mieczysław
entries.source: Wiktionary Polish Mieczysław: /mjɛˈt͡ʂɘ.swaf/
entries.notes: cz is 'ch', y is the 'bit' vowel, ł is w and final w is f; penultimate stress (as Stanisław, n0008). Today's guess is garbled.

entries.name: Riya
entries.source: Hindi रिया / Bengali রিয়া riyā: stress on the first syllable; today's REE-uh matches

entries.name: Jörg
entries.source: Wiktionary German Jörg: /jœʁk/
entries.notes: German j is y; ö has no English match: the 'her' vowel (guide); final g is k (as Georg, n0006). Today's JORG uses English j and 'or'.

entries.name: Bahadur
entries.source: Hindi बहादुर / Urdu بہادر bahādur ('brave'): stress on the long ā (as Bahadur Shah Zafar)
entries.notes: Today's US BAH-uh-dur drops the h and stresses the first syllable; GB already stresses 'hah' but with a different first syllable.

entries.name: Emmanuelle
entries.source: Wiktionary French Emmanuelle (fr-IPA) [e.ma.nɥɛl]; ɥ → w; as the French alternative of Emmanuel (n0001)
entries.notes: Final stress, three syllables. Today's ih-MAN-yoo-el reads it as English.

entries.name: Olive
entries.region: US, UK, Ireland, Australia, New Zealand
entries.source: English olive /ˈɒlɪv/
entries.notes: Ordinary word 'olive' (common: olive oil, olive green). The name sounds the same as the word; today's reading is right.

entries.name: Burhan
entries.source: Turkish Burhan [buɾˈhan] and Arabic برهان burhān: stress on the last (long) syllable
entries.notes: Today's BUR-hun stresses the first syllable and reduces the long ā.

entries.name: Roseline
entries.region: France, Canada, Nigeria, Ivory Coast, Cameroon
entries.source: Wiktionary French Roseline (fr-IPA) [ʁoz.lin]
entries.notes: French-speaking bearers (FR register 18.2k, Canada, Ivory Coast, Cameroon) are the largest group. Today's ROHZ-line reads -ine as in 'line'.

entries.name: Miles
entries.source: English Miles /maɪlz/; today's reading matches

entries.name: Simón
entries.source: Wiktionary Simón: Spanish (es-pr) [siˈmon]
entries.notes: The accent marks final stress. Today's SY-mun is the English Simon; the accented spelling is only the Spanish name.

entries.name: Ashton
entries.source: English Ashton /ˈæʃtən/; today's reading matches

entries.name: Angeline
entries.source: English Angeline: AN-juh-leen /ˈændʒəliːn/ (French Angéline /ɑ̃ʒ.lin/, Wiktionary); English g before e is soft
entries.notes: English-speaking bearers (US 22.6k) are the largest group. Today's AYNG-gil-ine reads a hard g.

entries.name: Ronit
entries.source: Hebrew רונית ronít: final stress, as Hebrew women's names in -it regularly take
entries.notes: Israeli bearers (wd IL 41) dominate. Today's RON-it stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Gert
entries.source: Wiktionary Gert: German /ɡɛʁt/, Dutch /ɣɛrt/
entries.notes: German (wd DE 240), Dutch and Flemish bearers say 'e' as in 'bed'; Dutch g [ɣ] becomes g. Today's GURT is an English spelling reading.

entries.name: Brendan
entries.source: English Brendan /ˈbɹɛndən/; today's reading matches

entries.name: Naila
entries.source: Arabic نائلة nāʾila / Urdu نائلہ: long ā stressed, hamza between the vowels
entries.notes: Three syllables, hamza dropped with the vowels kept apart (guide), with the y glide English speakers use between them (a bare ɑɪ is read as 'eye'). Today's NAY-luh reads ai as 'ay'.

entries.name: Saliou
entries.source: Senegalese Saliou (Wolof form of Arabic Ṣāliḥ): French spelling ou = u; a name site gives first-syllable stress 'SAH-lee-oo'
entries.notes: Today's SAY-lyoo reads the a as 'ay'. Stress kept on the first syllable as today.

entries.name: Deven
entries.source: US register 11.9k births; Forebears 2014: India 8.8k, US 2.9k, Mauritius 0.5k
entries.notes: Two groups of similar size: US bearers (a Devin variant, probably DEV-in) and Indian bearers (short for Devendra, DAY-ven). Today's DEE-vun fits neither, but I found no source for either group's reading of this spelling.

entries.name: Anja
entries.source: Wiktionary German Anja: [ˈanja]
entries.notes: j is y in German, Slovene and Scandinavian; today's AHN-juh uses English j.

entries.name: Angèle
entries.source: Wiktionary French Angèle (fr-IPA) [ɑ̃.ʒɛl]
entries.notes: Nasal ɑ̃ → 'ahn' (as Ange, n0014); final stress. Today's AN-jul reads it as English.

entries.name: Dumitru
entries.source: Romanian Dumitru [duˈmitru] (penultimate stress); today's doo-MEE-troo matches

entries.name: Inácio
entries.source: Wiktionary Portuguese Inácio (pt-IPA) [iˈna.sju]
entries.notes: Final -io is 'yoo' (as Maurício, n0016). Today's in-AY-see-oh reads the a as 'ay'.

entries.name: Deena
entries.source: English Deena /ˈdiːnə/ (as Dina); today's DEE-nuh matches; Hindi दीना is also DEE-nah

entries.name: Liz
entries.source: English Liz /lɪz/; today's reading matches

entries.name: Yoshiaki
entries.source: Japanese よしあき yo-shi-a-ki; guide convention: penultimate stress in English
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today says the 'lot' vowel (-OCK-ee); Japanese a is 'ah'. US already right.

entries.name: Recep
entries.source: Wiktionary Turkish Recep: /ɾeˈd͡ʒep/
entries.notes: Turkish c is j; final stress. Today's REE-sep reads c as s.

entries.name: Wilmer
entries.source: English Wilmer /ˈwɪlmər/; Latin American bearers use the English name (as Wilson, n0004)

alternatives.context: Venezuelan, Peruvian and Colombian bearers: WEEL-mehr

entries.notes: US bearers (11.2k) plus Latin American ones who adapt the English reading.

entries.name: Adelaide
entries.source: English Adelaide /ˈædəleɪd/ (also the Australian city); today's reading matches

entries.name: Emanuele
entries.source: Wiktionary Italian Emanuele: it-pr (stress on è) [emanuˈɛle]
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today says the 'lot' vowel in -man-; Italian a is 'ah'. US already right.

entries.name: Malek
entries.source: Arabic مالك mālik: long ā stressed; Maghrebi French spelling -lek (as Abdelmalek)
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today says MOL-ek with the 'lot' vowel. US already right.

entries.name: Remy
entries.source: English Remy /ˈɹɛmi/ (Wiktionary English section); today's reading matches

alternatives.context: French Rémy without the accent: ray-MEE

entries.notes: Row is usage english; English-speaking bearers (US 19.5k, UK 4.7k) keep REM-ee.

entries.name: Lázaro
entries.source: Wiktionary Lázaro: Spanish (es-pr) [ˈlasaɾo] (Latin America), [ˈlaθaɾo] (Spain); the accent marks the first syllable
entries.notes: Today's luh-ZAR-oh stresses the second syllable.

entries.name: Celestine
entries.source: English Celestine: SEL-uh-steen for the modern given name; Merriam-Webster gives SEL-uh-styne for the popes; c before e is s

alternatives.context: the popes Celestine and some English bearers: SEL-uh-styne

entries.notes: Today's cheh-les-TEE-nee reads it as Italian with an extra syllable, which fits nobody.

entries.name: Husein
entries.source: Arabic حسين ḥusayn [ħuˈsajn]; today's hoo-SAYN matches (as Hussein, n0002)

entries.name: Andrija
entries.source: Wiktionary Serbo-Croatian Andrija: /ǎndrija/ (Àndrija, rising accent on the first syllable); Wikipedia Andrija [ǎndrija]
entries.notes: Today's ahn-DREE-yuh stresses the second syllable.

entries.name: Harouna
entries.source: West African Harouna (Hārūn, Aaron): ou = u; stress on 'roo' as for Haruna (n0019); today differs only in the unstressed first vowel

entries.name: Muzaffer
entries.source: Turkish Muzaffer (Arabic muẓaffar 'victorious'): final stress as Turkish names regularly take (Mehmet, Mustafa precedents)
entries.notes: Today's MYOO-za-fer reads u as 'yoo' and stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Vinícius
entries.source: Wiktionary Portuguese Vinícius: pt-IPA Brazil [viˈnisjus]; as Vinicius (n0024)
entries.notes: Today's vih-NISH-us reads ci as 'sh'.

entries.name: Hernando
entries.source: Wiktionary Hernando: Spanish (es-pr) [eɾˈnando], h silent (Old Spanish /heɾˈnando/)

alternatives.context: English place names (Hernando County, Hernando de Soto in US usage): her-NAN-doh

entries.notes: Spanish h is silent (as Fernando, n0001). Today's hur-NAHN-doh sounds the h and reads 'er' as in 'her'.

entries.name: Abdellah
entries.source: Arabic عبد الله ʿabd allāh, colloquial with the stress on the second syllable; as Abdallah (n0014: ˌæbdˈɑlə) with the Maghrebi e

alternatives.context: careful Arabic, stress on the final llāh: ahb-del-LAH

entries.notes: Today's ab-DEL-uh follows the Abdallah precedent's stress and the spelling's e.

entries.name: Léa
entries.source: Wiktionary French Léa (fr-IPA) [le.a]
entries.notes: Two syllables with final stress. Today's LEE merges them into one.

entries.name: Kokou
entries.source: Ewe day name for a Wednesday-born boy (Akan Kwaku); Wikipedia lists the spelling Kɔku, with open ɔ
entries.notes: Togolese bearers (French spelling). Today's KOH-koo may be right or may need the open 'aw' of Kɔku; I found no IPA or Ewe dictionary entry for the vowel or an English stress. As Koffi (n0014), left unresolved.

entries.name: Eliseo
entries.source: Wiktionary Eliseo: Spanish (es-pr) [eliˈseo]; Italian Elisèo
entries.notes: Spanish bearers (US 11k mostly Hispanic, ES register 4.8k, Argentina, Mexico) dominate. Today's uh-LIZ-ee-oh stresses the wrong syllable.

entries.name: Željko
entries.source: Wiktionary Serbo-Croatian Željko: /ʒêːʎ.ko/; Slovene Žêljko
entries.notes: ž is 'zh'. The palatal lj [ʎ] is said as plain l, as English speakers do; with an added y glide (ʒˈɛljkO) the voice inserts a third syllable. Today's ZEL-j-koh reads ž as z and j as English j.

entries.name: Valentín
entries.source: Spanish Valentín [balenˈtin] (Wiktionary es-pr); today's vah-layn-TEEN keeps the stressed 'teen' and differs only in unstressed vowels
entries.notes: v kept as English speakers say it (as Valentin, n0007).

entries.name: Amiya
entries.source: Forebears 2014: India 56.9k, Bangladesh 3.4k, US 0.2k; US register 8.6k births
entries.notes: Indian bearers dominate, but the reading depends on the language: Bengali and Odia অমিয় / ଅମିୟ (men) start with an 'aw' vowel and stress the first syllable (AW-mee-yoh), Hindi amiya differs again; US bearers (girls, mostly recent) say uh-MEE-uh or uh-MY-uh. No source settles the main reading of this spelling.

entries.name: Chidi
entries.source: Igbo Chidi ('God exists'): chi [tʃi] + di; today's CHEE-dee matches
entries.notes: Tones dropped.

entries.name: Julieta
entries.source: Wiktionary Julieta: Spanish (es-pr) [xuˈljeta]
entries.notes: Spanish j is h (guide); stressed e in an open syllable is 'ay'. Today's yoo-LEE-tuh misreads j and ie.

entries.name: Chijioke
entries.source: Igbo Chijioke ('God holds the share'): chi + ji + oke; Igbo orthography is phonemic, final e is [e] ('ay', as Uche n0021)
entries.notes: Tones dropped; English stress on 'oh'. Today's chi-jee-OH-kee ends in 'kee'.

entries.name: Bernardino
entries.source: Wiktionary Italian Bernardino: it-pr Bernardìno
entries.notes: Today's bur-nuh-DEE-noh has the right stress but drops the r of -nar-.

entries.name: Modupe
entries.source: Yoruba Modúpẹ́ ('I give thanks'): o, u, and open ẹ [ɛ]; English stress on the high-toned 'doo'
entries.notes: Tones dropped. English has no word-final 'eh': the final ẹ is said 'ay' (the voice drops a final ɛ), as Yoruba e in Babatunde. Today's MAH-joop reads d as j and drops the final vowel.

entries.name: Seyi
entries.source: Yoruba Ṣèyí (short for Olúwaṣèyí): ṣ is [ʃ] (as Olusegun, n0020), e is [e]
entries.notes: The plain spelling drops the dot under s, but bearers say 'sh'. Tones dropped; first-syllable stress kept as today.

entries.name: Wim
entries.source: Dutch Wim (short for Willem): w is [ʋ], said v by English speakers; as Willem (n0008: vˈɪləm)
entries.notes: Dutch and Flemish bearers (wd NL 640, BE 220).

entries.name: Priscila
entries.source: Brazilian Priscila [pɾiˈsilɐ] (Wiktionary pt-IPA), Spanish [pɾiˈsila]; today's prih-SEE-luh matches

entries.name: Maxine
entries.source: English Maxine /mækˈsiːn/; today's reading matches

entries.name: Gaspar
entries.source: Wiktionary Gaspar: Spanish (es-pr) [ɡasˈpaɾ]; Portuguese [ɡɐʃˈpaɾ]
entries.notes: Final stress (word ending in r). Today's GAS-per reads it as English.

entries.name: Darlene
entries.source: Wiktionary Darlene: /ˈdɑːliːn/ (RP); today's DAR-leen matches

alternatives.context: also heard with final stress: dar-LEEN

entries.name: Unni
entries.source: Norwegian Unni [ˈʉnːi]: short close u (as Malayalam Unni)
entries.notes: Norwegian bearers (NO register 8.1k) and Malayali bearers (India) both say 'oo'. Today's UN-ee uses the 'cup' vowel.
entries.word_check: gold has 'unni'; kept: gold lists the name in lower case; no ordinary word

entries.name: Cláudia
entries.source: Wiktionary, Portuguese Cláudia: Brazil /ˈklaw.d͡ʒjɐ/, Portugal /ˈklaw.djɐ/
entries.notes: The accented spelling is Portuguese; Brazilian bearers (wd BR 83) outnumber Portuguese (53). au is 'ow' (as Claudia, n0003) and Brazilian d before i is 'j' (as Thiago's ti, n0010). Today's KLAW-dee-uh is the English Claudia.

entries.name: Harun
entries.source: Turkish Harun [haːˈɾun] and Arabic هارون hārūn: stress on the long last syllable; today's həɹˈun differs only in the unstressed first vowel
entries.notes: Turkish (wd TR 86), Bosnian, Arab and South Asian bearers all stress -ROON.

entries.name: Ndeye
entries.source: familyeducation.com, Ndeye: 'en-day'; Wolof ndey 'mother' [ndɛj] (regular Wolof spelling)
entries.notes: Senegalese women's name (Ndèye Fatou). Wolof prenasalised nd starts the word; English speakers add a short vowel before it (as Ngozi, n0015). -eye is 'ay', not today's 'eye' (en-DYE).

entries.name: Romuald
entries.source: Wiktionary, Romuald: French /ʁɔ.mɥald/, Polish /rɔˈmu.alt/; Forebears 2014: Central African Republic 16.9k, France 10.1k, Cameroon 6.2k, Madagascar 5.4k, Benin 4.4k against Poland 15.9k
entries.notes: French-speaking bearers (France, Central Africa, Madagascar, Benin, Quebec; about 47k) outnumber Polish ones (about 16k). French ɥ is said w by English speakers; final stress as for French names. Today's roh-myoo-AHLD fits neither.

entries.name: Edmilson
entries.source: Brazilian Portuguese spelling rules: the name is written Edmílson (Wikipedia, Edmílson the footballer), stress on -mil-; Brazilian d before a consonant takes an epenthetic [i] and becomes [d͡ʒi]

alternatives.context: a careful English rendering without the Brazilian epenthetic 'ee'

entries.notes: Brazilian name (wd BR 42). Today's ED-mil-sun stresses the first syllable. Brazilians vocalise the l ([miw]); English speakers keep it, as here. Final nasal õ is 'ohn'.

entries.name: Kristine
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Kristine (variant of Christine /krɪˈstiːn/); today's kɹɪstˈin matches
entries.notes: US births 84k make English the largest group.

entries.name: Esha
entries.source: Hindi ईशा (īśā): long ī stressed; today's ˈiʃə matches

entries.name: Rika
entries.source: Japanese りか (ri-ka); penultimate stress in English (guide); today's ɹˈikə matches
entries.notes: Dutch and South African Rika (from Frederika) say the same.

entries.name: Mama
entries.source: West African Mama [mama]: both a's 'ah' (as Nana, n0007)
entries.notes: Capitalised 'Mama' in English text is mostly the word for mother used as a form of address ('Mama said'), which keeps today's readings (US MAH-muh, GB MAM-uh). Bearers (FR 1.1k, ES 0.4k registers; Senegal, Guinea, Benin) say MAH-mah, given here; protected so the word keeps its readings.

entries.name: Horace
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Horace: /ˈhɒɹɪs/ (UK), /ˈhɔɹəs/ (US); today's reading matches
entries.notes: English-usage name; the app's dictionary reading is the established one.

entries.name: Gastón
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Gastón: /ɡasˈton/
entries.notes: The accent marks final stress; today's GAS-tun is an English spelling reading.

entries.name: Atef
entries.source: Arabic عاطف ʿāṭif: the long first syllable takes the stress (Arabic stress rule); Egyptian and Tunisian say the second vowel e, as the spelling shows
entries.notes: Egyptian, Tunisian and Palestinian bearers. ʿayn and emphatic ṭ have no English sound (dropped and t). Today's uh-TEF stresses the short last syllable.

entries.name: Rochelle
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Rochelle: /ɹoʊˈʃɛl/; today's reading matches
entries.notes: English-usage name; the app's dictionary reading is the established one.

entries.name: Lana
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Lana: /ˈlɑːnə/; Slovene /láːna/; Wikipedia, Lana Del Rey: /ˈlɑːnə/
entries.notes: English (Lana Del Rey, Lana Turner), French (FR register 28k), Croatian, Slovene and Russian bearers all say LAH-na. Today's LAN-uh has the 'cat' vowel.

entries.name: Marlène
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Marlène: /maʁ.lɛn/
entries.notes: FR register 32k. è is the 'bed' vowel and French names take final stress in English; today's MAR-leen is the English Marlene with first-syllable stress.

entries.name: Hira
entries.source: Hindi हीरा / Urdu ہیرا hīrā ('diamond'): long ī; Forebears 2014: India 522k, Nepal 98k, Bangladesh 45k, Pakistan 25k
entries.notes: South Asian bearers dominate. ī is 'ee'; today's HIR-uh (as 'here') uses the near vowel.

entries.name: Lazarus
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Lazarus: /ˈlæzəɹəs/; today's lˈæzəɹəs matches
entries.notes: English-speaking bearers (US 3.7k births, Nigeria) and the biblical figure; the English reading is the largest.

entries.name: Robyn
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Robyn: /ˈɹɒbɪn/ (as Robin); today's reading matches
entries.notes: English-usage name; the app's dictionary reading is the established one.

entries.name: Nikolaus
entries.source: Wiktionary, German Nikolaus: /ˈnɪkoˌlaʊ̯s/ (normal), /ˈniːkoˌlaʊ̯s/ (regional)
entries.notes: German, Austrian and Swiss bearers. The final s is voiceless and -laus has a secondary stress; today's NIK-uh-lowz voices the s.

entries.name: Feliciano
entries.source: Spanish spelling: Latin American [feliˈsjano] (Spain [feliˈθjano]); today's fəlisiˈɑnO keeps the stressed 'AH' and its consonants
entries.notes: Today's fuh-lee-see-AH-noh differs from Spanish only in unstressed vowels and the i/y glide before the stress.

entries.name: Abeer
entries.source: Arabic عبير ʿabīr: the long last syllable takes the stress; today's əbˈɪɹ ('beer') matches
entries.notes: ʿayn is dropped; only the unstressed first vowel differs.

entries.name: Roshan
