entries.source: Wikipedia, Hrithik Roshan: Hindi [ˈrɪt̪ɪk ˈroːʃən]; today's ɹˈOʃən matches
entries.notes: Persian روشن stresses the last syllable; the Indian and Pakistani bearers (US, UK registers) say ROH-shun.

entries.name: Kadir
entries.source: Wiktionary, Turkish kadir (from Arabic qādir): /kaːˈdiɾ/

alternatives.context: Arabic Qādir (stress on the long first syllable)

entries.notes: Turkish bearers (wd TR 125, FR 1k) dominate; Turkish names stress the last syllable (as Kemal, Murat). Today's KAD-eer has the 'cat' vowel and first-syllable stress. US 'eer' is ɪɹ (as Jair, n0019).

entries.name: Tatjana
entries.source: Wiktionary, German Tatjana: [tatˈjaːna]
entries.notes: Slovene, German, Estonian, Serbian and Norwegian bearers agree. Today's taht-YAH-NAH gives the unstressed final a secondary stress and a full vowel.

entries.name: Casey
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Casey: /ˈkeɪsi/; today's reading matches
entries.notes: English-usage name; the app's dictionary reading is the established one.

entries.name: Christiaan
entries.source: Wiktionary, Dutch Christiaan: /ˈkrɪstiˌ(j)aːn/
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today says the 'lot' vowel in -aan (KRIS-tee-on); Dutch aa is a long 'ah'. US already right.

entries.name: Cheikh
entries.source: Wiktionary, French cheikh: /ʃɛk/ (the French spelling of Arabic shaykh)
entries.notes: Senegalese given name (Cheikh Anta Diop), FR 1.6k and ES 1.9k registers. French ch is sh; Wolof speakers end it in a k-like [x], said k in English. Today's CHEEK reads ch as English ch.

entries.name: Soledad
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish soledad: /soleˈdad/ [so.leˈð̞að̞]
entries.notes: ES register 27.5k plus Peru, Argentina, Chile. Today's SOL-ih-dad is the California town; the name stresses the last syllable. Spanish d between vowels [ð] is said d by English speakers.

entries.name: Theophilus
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Theophilus: /θiˈɒfɪləs/; Merriam-Webster: thē-ˈä-fə-ləs
entries.notes: English-speaking bearers (US, Nigeria, Ghana) and the biblical addressee. Stress on the second syllable; today's thee-uh-FIL-us stresses the third.

entries.name: Chloé
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Chloé: /klɔ.e/
entries.notes: FR register 160k: the accented spelling is French, final stress in English. Today's KLOH-ee is the English Chloe.

entries.name: Younes
entries.source: Arabic يونس yūnus: stress on the long first syllable; the Yunus entry (n0017) is YOO-nus
entries.notes: Moroccan, Algerian and Tunisian bearers (FR 18.8k, ES 5.1k registers). French ou is 'oo'. Today's YUNZ loses a syllable.

entries.name: Teja
entries.source: Telugu తేజ / Hindi-Nepali तेजा (tējā): long e, j; Forebears 2014: India 73k, Nepal 60k, Indonesia 3.9k, Slovenia 3.4k
entries.notes: South Asian bearers (India and Nepal, about 133k) far outnumber Slovenian ones (3.4k). Today's TAY-yuh is the Slovene reading.

entries.name: Hudson
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Hudson: /ˈhʌdsən/; today's reading matches
entries.notes: English-usage name; the app's dictionary reading is the established one.

entries.name: Ümit
entries.source: Wiktionary, Turkish ümit: /yˈmit/
entries.notes: Turkish ü [y] has no English match: 'oo' per the guide (as Hüseyin, n0010). Turkish final stress; today's YOO-mit stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Shigeo
entries.source: Japanese しげお (shi-ge-o): penultimate stress in English (guide, as Hiroshi); today's ʃɪɡˈAO matches
entries.notes: Only the unstressed first vowel differs.

entries.name: Davis
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Davis: /ˈdeɪvɪs/; today's reading matches
entries.notes: English-usage name; the app's dictionary reading is the established one.

entries.name: Bethany
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Bethany: /ˈbɛθəni/; today's reading matches
entries.notes: English-usage name; the app's dictionary reading is the established one.

entries.name: Errol
entries.source: Wikipedia, Errol Flynn: /ˈɛrəl/; today's ˈɛɹəl matches
entries.notes: English-speaking bearers (US, Jamaica, Australia, New Zealand).

entries.name: Matias
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Matías: /maˈtias/; Forebears 2014: Mexico 20k, Spain 16k, Argentina 15k, Uruguay 8k against Mozambique 20k, Brazil 16k, Angola 10k, Finland smaller
entries.notes: Unaccented spelling of Matías (as n0013); Spanish-speaking bearers (US Hispanic 23k births, ES 18.6k, Argentina, Chile) are the largest group. Today's MAH-shuz is garbled (t read as sh, a syllable lost).

entries.name: Harpreet
entries.source: Punjabi ਹਰਪ੍ਰੀਤ (har + prīt): short a [ə], long ī; stress on the superheavy last syllable (as Hardeep, n0018)
entries.notes: Today's HAR-preet gives the short a a long 'ah' and stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Elton
entries.source: Wikipedia, Elton John: /ˈɛltən/; today's ˈɛltən matches
entries.notes: US births 16.6k make English the largest group.

entries.name: Ajith
entries.source: Tamil அஜித் / Malayalam അജിത് (ajit): th in South Indian spelling marks a dental t; the Ajit entry (n0003) is uh-JIT
entries.notes: The th is a dental t, not the 'th' of thin (today's uh-JITH). Stress follows Ajit; Tamil's weak stress may fall on the first syllable, unsourced.

entries.name: Wagner
entries.source: Wikipedia, Wagner Moura: English /ˈvɑːɡnər/, Portuguese [ˈvaɡneʁ]
entries.notes: Protect-word: capitalised 'Wagner' in English text is mostly the surname (Richard Wagner, Robert Wagner, the Wagner Group, many US Wagners), whose bearers are not bearers of this given name; an entry would turn every one into VAHG-ner. As a given name it is Brazilian (wd BR 87): v and 'ah', as in Wikipedia's English IPA for Wagner Moura, kept here in us/gb. Same treatment as Delong (n0025) and Chan/Chong (n0017, n0024).

entries.name: Nhi
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese nhi: [ɲi˧˧]
entries.notes: One syllable: nh is [ɲ] → 'ny' (guide). Today spells it out (N-H-I). Tone dropped.

entries.name: Agostinho
entries.source: Wiktionary, Portuguese Agostinho: Brazil /a.ɡosˈt͡ʃĩ.ɲu/, Portugal /ɐ.ɡuʃˈti.ɲu/
entries.notes: Brazil (wd BR 42) leads Portugal (27). Brazilian ti is 'chee' (as Thiago, n0010), nh is 'ny', final o is 'oo'. Today's guess says the h (teen-HOH).

entries.name: Roxana
entries.source: Spanish and Romanian spelling: Roxana [rokˈsana] (x = ks, penultimate stress)

alternatives.context: English (the Defoe novel, some US bearers)

entries.notes: anglo_share 0.05: Hispanic US (11.7k births), Spain, Peru, Argentina and Romania all say 'ah' in the stressed syllable; today's rok-SAN-uh has the 'cat' vowel.

entries.name: Fathima
entries.source: South Indian spelling of Fatima (Malayalam ഫാത്തിമ): th = dental t; Wiktionary Arabic فاطمة /faː.tˤi.ma/, stress on the long first syllable (as Fatima, n0002)
entries.notes: Today's FATH-ih-muh reads th as the voiced 'th' of 'this'. Same reading as Fatima.

entries.name: Cory
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Cory: /ˈkɔːɹi/; today's reading matches
entries.notes: English-usage name; the app's dictionary reading is the established one.

entries.name: Samarth
entries.source: Hindi समर्थ (samarth, 'capable'): schwas, aspirated th = t; stress on the superheavy last syllable (Hindustani weight rule (Wikipedia, Hindustani phonology): the heaviest syllable takes the stress, the last non-final one on a tie)
entries.notes: Today's SAM-arth has the 'cat' vowel, first-syllable stress and reads th as in 'thin'. Schwa before r is the 'her' vowel (as Archana, n0004).

entries.name: Wyatt
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Wyatt: /ˈwaɪ.ət/; today's reading matches
entries.notes: English-usage name; the app's dictionary reading is the established one.

entries.name: Ishika
entries.source: Wikipedia, Ishika: Hindi ईशिका (long ī, short i, long ā); Hindustani weight rule (Wikipedia, Hindustani phonology): the heaviest syllable takes the stress, the last non-final one on a tie (heavy first syllable, as Ishita, n0009)

alternatives.context: hindutone.com respells i-SHI-ka (इशिका, short first i)

entries.notes: Both spellings have a short middle i, so today's ish-EE-KAH (long ee, final secondary stress) is wrong. Wikipedia's Devanagari is ईशिका (long ī), whose heavy first syllable takes the stress under the Hindustani weight rule (final mora ignored), as Ishita (n0009, medium).

entries.name: Ambroise
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Ambroise: /ɑ̃.bʁwaz/
entries.notes: FR register 7k. Nasal ɑ̃ → 'ahm' (English adds the m before b); the final s is z. Today's US am-BRWAH drops the z, and GB also loses the r.

entries.name: Muskan
entries.source: Hindi मुस्कान (muskān, 'smile'): short u, long ā; Hindustani weight rule (Wikipedia, Hindustani phonology): the heaviest syllable takes the stress, the last non-final one on a tie (superheavy kān)
entries.notes: Today's MUS-kun stresses the first syllable and reduces the long ā.

entries.name: Manya
entries.source: Hindi मान्या (mānyā): long first syllable stressed; today's mˈɑnjə matches
entries.notes: Russian Manya (Маня) is said the same.

entries.name: Gagandeep
entries.source: Punjabi ਗਗਨਦੀਪ (gagan + dīp): short a's [ə], long ī; stress on the long last syllable (as Sandeep, n0002)
entries.notes: Today's GAG-un-deep has the 'cat' vowel and first-syllable stress.

entries.name: Jihan
entries.source: Arabic جيهان jīhān: the long final syllable takes the stress; Forebears 2014: Egypt 24k, Iraq 10.8k, Yemen 8.5k, Indonesia 6k, Saudi Arabia, Palestine, Morocco, Lebanon, Jordan

alternatives.context: Egypt (Egyptian Arabic g for j; Jehan Sadat)

entries.notes: Arabic bearers stress the long last syllable; today's JEE-hahn is the Indonesian stress. Iraqi, Yemeni, Gulf and Maghreb bearers say j; Egyptians g.

entries.name: Mala
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi माला (mālā): /mɑː.lɑː/; today's mˈɑlə (GB mˈɑːlɑː) matches
entries.notes: Only the unstressed final vowel differs (GB).

entries.name: Théo
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Théo: /te.o/
entries.notes: FR register 128k. French th is t; final stress in English. Today's THEE-oh is the English Theo.

entries.name: Luana
entries.source: Wiktionary, Portuguese Luana: Brazil /luˈɐ̃.nɐ/; Forebears 2014: Brazil 318,566 of about 350k bearers

alternatives.context: Italy (17k), the US, Hawaii, Romania, Spain: loo-AH-nuh

entries.notes: Brazil holds about 90% of bearers. Brazilian stressed a before a nasal is [ɐ̃], rendered 'uh' as for Juliana (n0006). Today's loo-AN-uh has the 'cat' vowel no group uses.

entries.name: Hoa
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese hoa: [hwaː˧˧] (Saigon [waː˧˧])
entries.notes: oa is [wa] (as Hoàng, n0006). Today's HOH-uh reads o as a vowel and adds a syllable. Tone dropped.

entries.name: Fumio
entries.source: Wiktionary, Japanese ふみお: /fumio/ (from */pumiwo/); penultimate stress in English (guide; as Toshio n0016, Yasuo n0024, Akio n0026)
entries.notes: Japanese f is a light f and u is 'oo', not 'yoo'; penultimate stress as for Hiroshi and Hiroyuki. Today's FYOO-mee-oh adds a y and stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Kajal
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi काजल (kājal): /kɑː.d͡ʒəl/
entries.notes: Long ā in the stressed first syllable. Today's US kuh-JAHL stresses the second syllable, and GB's KUJ-ul shortens the ā.

entries.name: Sitara
entries.source: Hindi सितारा / Urdu ستارہ (sitārā): long tā stressed (Hindustani weight rule (Wikipedia, Hindustani phonology): the heaviest syllable takes the stress, the last non-final one on a tie); today's sɪtˈɑɹə matches

entries.name: Dorcas
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Dorcas: /ˈdɔː(ɹ)kəs/; today's dˈɔɹkəs matches
entries.notes: English-speaking bearers (US, Nigeria, Kenya, Ghana) and the biblical Dorcas.

entries.name: Kavish
entries.source: Hindi कविश (kaviś, from kavi 'poet'): short a and i; parentingpatch.com gives first-syllable stress (KAH-vish)

alternatives.context: the Hindustani weight rule would stress the closed last syllable (kuh-VISH)

entries.notes: Today's KAY-vish reads a as 'ay'. Indian short a is 'uh'; first-syllable stress as the name site and the Kapil/Karan precedent, but no dictionary marks it.

entries.name: Dilpreet
entries.source: Punjabi ਦਿਲਪ੍ਰੀਤ (dil + prīt): stress on the long last syllable; today's dɪlpɹˈit matches

entries.name: Meghna
entries.source: Hindi मेघना (meghnā): e in the closed first syllable → ɛ (guide table), as Mahesh (n0002); today's mˈɛɡnə matches
entries.notes: Aspirated gh is g.

entries.name: Phan
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese phan: [faːn˧˧]
entries.notes: Vietnamese a is 'ah' (as Lan, Văn); today's FAN uses the 'cat' vowel. Tone dropped.

entries.name: Chương
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese chương: Hà Nội [t͡ɕɨəŋ˧˧], Saigon [cɨəŋ˧˧]
entries.notes: One syllable; ươ as in Phương and Hương (n0005, n0008). Today's choo-AWNG splits it in two. Tone dropped.

entries.name: Công
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese công: [kəwŋ͡m˧˧]
entries.notes: ô before ng is a closing 'oh' [əw], as Hồng (n0007); today's KAWNG opens it. Tone dropped.

entries.name: Lê
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese lê: [le˧˧]
entries.notes: Open-syllable e is 'ay' (guide). Today reads it as an unstressed 'luh'. Tone dropped.

entries.name: Lương
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese lương: [lɨəŋ˧˧]
entries.notes: One syllable; ươ as in Phương (n0005). Today's loo-AWNG splits it in two. Tone dropped.

entries.name: Lệ
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese lệ: Hà Nội [le˧˨ʔ]
entries.notes: As Lê: open-syllable e is 'ay'. Today reads 'luh'. Tone dropped.

entries.name: Mạnh
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese mạnh: Saigon [man˨˩˨], Hà Nội [majŋ̟˧˨ʔ]
entries.notes: -anh as Anh, Thanh (n0004, n0005): southern 'ahn'. Today's MAN uses the 'cat' vowel. Tone dropped.

entries.name: Nguyện
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese nguyện: Hà Nội [ŋwiən˧˨ʔ], Saigon [ŋwiəŋ˨˩˨]
entries.notes: As Nguyên (n0012): English never starts a word with ng, so n keeps the onset; uyê is w + [iə]. Today's noo-YEN is the common English approximation of Nguyen. Tone dropped.

entries.name: Nhật
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese nhật: [ɲət̚˧˨ʔ]
entries.notes: nh is 'ny' (as Nhi), â is 'uh' (as Vân, Tâm). Today spells out N and splits the name. Tone dropped.

entries.name: Phaolô
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese Phaolô (Paul): two syllables, pha-ô [faːw] + lô [lo]; today's fˈWlO has the same sounds
entries.notes: Catholic baptismal name (Paul). Vietnamese syllables carry equal weight; today's first-syllable stress is the natural English reading of two syllables.

entries.name: Phúc
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese phúc: Hà Nội [fʊwk͡p̚˧˦], Saigon [fʊwk͡p̚˦˥]
entries.notes: Vietnamese -úc has the 'book' vowel (as Đức, n0010); today's reading is the English swear word. Tone dropped.

entries.name: Phước
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese phước: [fɨək̚˧˦]
entries.notes: One syllable; ươ as in Phương (n0005). Today's reading has no stress and splits the vowel. Tone dropped.

entries.name: Vũ
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese vũ: Hà Nội [vu˦ˀ˥], Saigon [ju˨˩˦]; today's vˈu matches the northern reading kept for Vân (n0011)
entries.notes: Tone dropped.

entries.name: Định
entries.source: Wiktionary, Vietnamese định: Hà Nội [ʔɗïŋ˧˨ʔ], Saigon [ʔɗɨn˨˩˨]
entries.notes: Đ is d; -inh as Linh and Minh. Today's SIN reads Đ as s. Tone dropped.

entries.name: Miloud
entries.source: Arabic ميلود mīlūd: the long last syllable takes the stress; French ou = [u]
entries.notes: Algerian and Moroccan bearers (FR 1.9k, ES 1.4k registers). Today's mil-OWD reads ou as 'ow'.

entries.name: Meghana
entries.source: Kannada ಮೇಘನಾ / Telugu మేఘన (mēghanā): long open ē; Dravidian first-syllable stress (as Srinivas, n0013)
entries.notes: The three-syllable spelling is South Indian. e in an open syllable is 'ay' (guide); today's MEG-uh-nuh shortens it.

entries.name: Nithya
entries.source: Sanskrit नित्या (nityā); South Indian spelling th = dental t; first-syllable stress
entries.notes: Today's NITH-yuh reads th as in 'thin'.

entries.name: Kaur
entries.source: Punjabi ਕੌਰ (kaur): au is [ɔː]; today's kˈɔɹ matches
entries.notes: Sikh women's name, the largest group by far.

entries.name: Endi
entries.source: Indonesian and Albanian spelling: Endi [ˈɛndi], first-syllable stress; today's ˈɛndi matches

entries.name: Lajos
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hungarian Lajos: [ˈlɒjoʃ]
entries.notes: Hungarian j is y and s is sh; Hungarian short a [ɒ] is the British 'lot' vowel, US 'ah'. Initial stress. Today's LAH-zhohz reads j as zh and s as z.

entries.name: Achille
entries.source: Wiktionary, Achille: French /a.ʃil/, Italian /aˈkil.le/; Forebears 2014: Cameroon 15k, Central African Republic 14.3k, DR Congo 6.6k, Madagascar 5.7k, Rwanda 4.8k, Benin, Togo, Côte d'Ivoire against Italy 15.4k
entries.notes: French-speaking bearers (France FR 14k, Central and West Africa, Belgium) clearly outnumber Italian ones. Today's uh-KIL-ee fits neither.

entries.name: Konstantin
entries.source: Wiktionary, Russian Константин: [kənstɐnʲˈtʲin]; Bulgarian [konstɐnˈtin]
entries.notes: This spelling is the standard romanisation of Russian and Bulgarian Константин (Konstantin Stanislavski, Tsiolkovsky), a far larger group than German bearers; both stress the last syllable. Today's KON-stin-teen is the German stress.

entries.name: Himani
entries.source: Hindi हिमानी (himānī): long ā carries the stress (Hindustani weight rule (Wikipedia, Hindustani phonology): the heaviest syllable takes the stress, the last non-final one on a tie)
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today says the 'lot' vowel (hi-MON-ee). US already right.

entries.name: Mae
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Mae: /meɪ/; today's reading matches
entries.notes: English-usage name; the app's dictionary reading is the established one.

entries.name: Sheela
entries.source: Hindi शीला (śīlā): long ī stressed; today's ʃˈilə matches

entries.name: Juhi
entries.source: Hindi जूही (jūhī, jasmine): long ū stressed; today's ʤˈuhi matches

entries.name: Manas
entries.source: Hindi मानस (mānas): long ā stressed, final s voiceless
entries.notes: Today's MAH-nuz voices the s.

entries.name: Sruthi
entries.source: Sanskrit श्रुति (śruti); Malayalam ശ്രുതി: th = dental t; first-syllable stress
entries.notes: Today's SHROO-thee reads th as in 'thin'; the sh onset is kept (ś).

entries.name: Nishtha
entries.source: Hindi निष्ठा (niṣṭhā): retroflex ṣ (sh) + ṭh (t); first-syllable stress
entries.notes: Today's NISH-uh drops the t.

entries.name: Deeksha
entries.source: Hindi दीक्षा (dīkṣā): long ī stressed, kṣ = ksh; today's dˈikʃə matches

entries.name: Ravina
entries.source: Hindi रवीना (ravīnā, as Raveena Tandon): long ī stressed; today's ɹɑvˈinə differs only in the unstressed first vowel

entries.name: Harshita
entries.source: Hindi हर्षिता (harṣitā): schwa before r, short i, long ā; Hindustani weight rule (Wikipedia, Hindustani phonology): the heaviest syllable takes the stress, the last non-final one on a tie (heavy har; as Arpita, n0011)
entries.notes: Today's har-SHEE-tuh lengthens and stresses the short i. No dictionary marks the stress.

entries.name: Hansa
entries.source: Hindi हंसा / Gujarati હંસા (hansā): short a [ə] in the stressed first syllable; Dictionary.com, Hansa (the medieval merchant guild, Hanseatic League): ˈhæn sə, -zə
entries.notes: Protect-word: capitalised 'Hansa' in English text is mostly the Hanseatic League ('the Hansa'), Hansa Rostock and German brands, read HAN-suh (Dictionary.com), which is today's reading; the name entry would turn them into HUN-suh. The Gujarati/Indian given name (GB register 97) is said HUN-suh (Indian short a is 'uh'), kept here in us/gb.

entries.name: Amol
entries.source: Marathi अमोल (amol, 'priceless'): long o; stress on the superheavy last syllable (Hindustani weight rule (Wikipedia, Hindustani phonology): the heaviest syllable takes the stress, the last non-final one on a tie)
entries.notes: Today's ah-MAWL uses the 'law' vowel for the long o.

entries.name: Sheetal
entries.source: Hindi शीतल (śītal): long ī stressed; today's ʃˈitəl matches

entries.name: Pal
entries.source: Hindi पाल (pāl) [paːl]; Hungarian Pál [paːl]
entries.notes: Ordinary word 'pal' (friend), read PAL; never replace. The Indian and Hungarian name is said PAHL, given here.

entries.name: Ekta
entries.source: Hindi एकता (ektā): e in the closed first syllable → ɛ (guide table), as Mahesh (n0002); today's ˈɛktə matches

entries.name: Rachana
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi रचना (racnā): /ɾət͡ʃ.nɑː/

alternatives.context: South Indian (Kannada, Telugu) bearers keep the middle vowel: RUH-chuh-nuh

entries.notes: Hindi drops the middle a; the short first a is 'uh'. Today's ruh-CHAN-uh stresses the middle with the 'cat' vowel.

entries.name: Baljit
entries.source: Punjabi ਬਲਜੀਤ (bal + jīt): short a, long ī; stress on the long last syllable (as Jagdeep, n0010)
entries.notes: Punjabi writes the second part with a long ī (ਜੀਤ) though English spells -jit. Today's BAL-jit has the 'cat' vowel and first-syllable stress.

entries.name: Varshini
entries.source: Sanskrit वर्षिणी (varṣiṇī), Tamil வர்ஷினி: short i; Dravidian first-syllable stress (as Srinivas, n0013)
entries.notes: Today's var-SHEE-nee lengthens and stresses the short i. Stress unsourced.

entries.name: Kuldeep
entries.source: Hindi कुलदीप (kul + dīp): short u, long ī; stress on the long last syllable (as Sandeep, n0002)
entries.notes: Today's KUL-deep has the 'cup' vowel and first-syllable stress.

entries.name: Narinder
entries.source: Punjabi ਨਰਿੰਦਰ (narindar): short a, short i in the heavy 'rin', which carries the stress (as Surinder, n0007, Harinder, n0018)
entries.notes: Today's NAIR-in-der stresses the first syllable with an 'air' vowel.

entries.name: Surabhi
entries.source: Sanskrit/Hindi सुरभि (surabhi): short u, a and i, all three syllables light; Wikipedia, Hindustani phonology: the final mora is ignored, so when all syllables are light the penult takes the stress (samiti [sə.ˈmɪ.t(ɪ)])
entries.notes: Penultimate stress, as Aditi (n0003, uh-DIT-ee), which has the same three light syllables. Today's soo-RAH-bee has the right stress but a long 'ah' for the short a, which is 'uh' (as Sachin, Karan).

entries.name: Nishanth
entries.source: Hindi निशांत (niśānt): long ā; stress on the superheavy last syllable (as Prashant, n0004); South Indian th = dental t
entries.notes: Today's NISH-unth stresses the first syllable and reads th as in 'thin'.

entries.name: Hitesh
entries.source: Hindi हितेश (hiteś): short i, long e; stress on the superheavy last syllable; closed-syllable e → ɛ (guide, as Mahesh)
entries.notes: Today's high-TESH reads the short i as 'eye'.

entries.name: Parag
entries.source: Hindi पराग (parāg, 'pollen'): long ā; stress on the superheavy last syllable
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today says the 'lot' vowel (puh-ROG). US already right.

entries.name: Sujan
entries.source: Hindi/Nepali सुजन, Bengali সুজন (sujan): short a; Forebears 2014: India 96k, Bangladesh 72k, Nepal 22k
entries.notes: Bengali and Nepali stress the first syllable (as Bimal, n0014); the a is short 'uh', not today's long 'ah' (soo-JAHN). Bengali bearers say sh.

entries.name: Sindhu
entries.source: Hindi सिंधु (sindhu): aspirated dh is one sound, said d by English speakers; first-syllable stress
entries.notes: Today's SIND-hoo splits dh into d + h.

entries.name: Savita
entries.source: Hindi सविता (savitā): short a and i, long final ā (Devanagari spelling)

alternatives.context: first-syllable stress, as Sabita (n0011) for eastern bearers

entries.notes: Same shape as Kavita (n0005, unresolved): the middle i is short, so today's sah-VEE-tuh is wrong in its vowels, but no source marks the stress (weight rule: final -tā; English renderings: -vi-).

entries.name: Jaydeep
entries.source: Hindi जयदीप (jay + dīp): stress on the long last syllable (as Sandeep, n0002); jay [d͡ʒəj] as in Sanjay
entries.notes: Today stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Sandip
entries.source: Hindi संदीप (sandīp): short a, long ī; stress on the long last syllable (as Sandeep, n0002, and Pradip, n0007)
entries.notes: Today's SAN-dip has the 'cat' vowel and first-syllable stress.

entries.name: Apoorva
entries.source: Hindi अपूर्वा (apūrvā): superheavy pūr stressed; today's əpˈʊɹvə ('poor') matches

entries.name: Gulshan
entries.source: Hindi गुलशन / Urdu گلشن (gulśan): short u [ʊ]; first-syllable stress (Gulshan Kumar)
entries.notes: Today's GULL-shun has the 'cup' vowel; Indian short u is the 'book' vowel.

entries.name: Neeta
entries.source: Hindi नीता (nītā): long ī stressed; today's nˈitə matches

entries.name: Srihari
entries.source: Sanskrit श्रीहरि (śrīhari): long ī; South Indian first-syllable stress, Sri as in Srinivas (n0013) and Sripati (n0021)
entries.notes: Today's sree-HAH-ree stresses the short a with a long 'ah'.

entries.name: Kuldip
entries.source: Hindi कुलदीप (kuldīp): the -dip spelling is the same long ī (as Pradip, n0007)
entries.notes: Same name as Kuldeep. Today's KUL-dip shortens the ī and stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Mamta
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi ममता (mamtā): /məm.t̪ɑː/
entries.notes: Indian short a is 'uh'; today's MAM-tuh has the 'cat' vowel.

entries.name: Roshani
entries.source: Hindi रोशनी (rośnī, Wiktionary /ɾoːʃ.niː/); the -shani spelling keeps the middle schwa (Marathi, Gujarati); long first o stressed
entries.notes: Today's roh-SHAH-nee stresses the short a with a long 'ah'.

entries.name: Hugues
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Hugues: /yɡ/
entries.notes: FR register 24.5k. One syllable: French u [y] has no English match, 'oo' per the guide (as Hüseyin, n0010); the -es is silent. Today's YOOGZ adds a y and a z.

entries.name: Bindu
entries.source: Hindi बिंदु (bindu): first-syllable stress; today's bˈɪndu matches

entries.name: Parvez
entries.source: Wikipedia, Pervez Musharraf: Urdu [pəɾʋeːz]; superheavy last syllable stressed, closed-syllable e → ɛ (guide); today's pɑɹvˈɛz differs only in the unstressed first vowel

entries.name: Tejinder
entries.source: Punjabi ਤੇਜਿੰਦਰ (tejindar): long e, short i in the heavy 'jin', which carries the stress (as Surinder, n0007)
entries.notes: Today's TEE-jine-der reads e as 'ee' and i as 'eye'.

entries.name: Nivedita
entries.source: Hindi निवेदिता (niveditā): long e in the heavy second syllable; Hindustani weight rule (Wikipedia, Hindustani phonology): the heaviest syllable takes the stress, the last non-final one on a tie
entries.notes: Today's nee-ved-EE-tuh stresses the short i and shortens the e.

entries.name: Piyush
entries.source: Hindi पीयूष (pīyūṣ): superheavy last syllable stressed; today's pijˈuʃ matches

entries.name: Sowmya
entries.source: Wiktionary, सौम्य: Classical Sanskrit /s̪ɑu̯m.jɐ/ (diphthong au), Hindi /sɔːm.jᵊ/; the -ow- spelling is South Indian, where au stays a diphthong; first-syllable stress
entries.notes: Today's SOHM-yuh is the North Indian [ɔː] reading; this spelling is South Indian (Kannada, Telugu, Tamil), which keeps 'ow'.

entries.name: Rao
entries.source: Telugu రావు / Marathi राव (rāv); today's ɹˈW matches the usual reading
entries.notes: Chinese 饒 Ráo is also said 'row'.

entries.name: Vipul
entries.source: Hindi विपुल (vipul): short i and u; first-syllable stress as Nitin (n0004) and Bipin (n0013)

alternatives.context: the Hindustani weight rule would stress the closed last syllable (vi-PUL)

entries.notes: Today's vee-POOL lengthens both short vowels. Stress unsourced.

entries.name: Bibek
entries.source: Nepali बिबेक / Bengali বিবেক (bibek, eastern form of Vivek): plain i; Nepali and Bengali stress the first syllable (as Bimal, n0014)
entries.notes: Today's BIB-ik reduces the e and shortens the i.

entries.name: Sharada
entries.source: Hindi शारदा (śāradā): long first ā stressed (weight rule), as Sarada (n0011)
entries.notes: Today's shar-AH-duh stresses the short middle a.

entries.name: Shri
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi श्री (śrī): /ʃɾiː/; today's ʃɹˈi matches
entries.notes: Also the honorific (Shri Ram), said the same.

entries.name: Utkarsh
entries.source: Hindi उत्कर्ष (utkarṣ): short u, schwa before r; stress on the superheavy last syllable (Hindustani weight rule (Wikipedia, Hindustani phonology): the heaviest syllable takes the stress, the last non-final one on a tie)
entries.notes: Today's UT-karsh stresses the first syllable and gives the schwa a long 'ah'.

entries.name: Jyotsna
entries.source: Hindi ज्योत्स्ना (jyotsnā): jy + long o + tsn; first-syllable stress
entries.notes: Today's JYOHS-nuh drops the t.

entries.name: Hardik
entries.source: Hindi हार्दिक (hārdik): superheavy first syllable stressed; today's hˈɑɹdɪk matches

entries.name: Manik
entries.source: Bengali মানিক / Hindi माणिक (mānik, 'ruby'): long first ā stressed
entries.notes: Today's MAN-ik has the 'cat' vowel.

entries.name: Unnati
entries.source: Hindi उन्नति (unnati, 'progress'): short u in the heavy first syllable, stressed (Hindustani weight rule (Wikipedia, Hindustani phonology): the heaviest syllable takes the stress, the last non-final one on a tie); double n said single
entries.notes: Today's un-NAH-tee stresses the short middle a with a long 'ah'.

entries.name: Kamlesh
entries.source: Hindi कमलेश (kamleś): short a, long e; stress on the superheavy last syllable; closed-syllable e → ɛ (guide, as Mahesh)
entries.notes: Today's KAM-lesh has the 'cat' vowel and first-syllable stress.

entries.name: Arnab
entries.source: Wiktionary, Bengali অর্ণব (arṇab): Rarh [ˈɔɾnob], Dhaka [ˈɔɹnob]; first-syllable stress, second vowel o
entries.notes: The -b spelling is Bengali/Assamese (Hindi spells Arnav). Bengali's inherent vowel is [ɔ] in the first syllable but [o] in the second, as Pranab (n0014, PRAW-nobe). Today's ar-NAB has the 'cat' vowel and final stress.

entries.name: Haritha
entries.source: Sanskrit हरिता (haritā), Telugu హరిత: th = dental t; Dravidian first-syllable stress (as Srinivas, n0013)
entries.notes: Today's huh-RITH-uh reads th as the 'th' of 'this'. Stress is unsourced (South Indian initial stress assumed).

entries.name: Bhawna
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hindi भावना (bhāvnā): /bʱɑːʋ.nɑː/
entries.notes: The w spelling is Hindi ʋ (between v and w), said v as in other entries; aspirated bh is b. Today's BAW-nuh drops the v.

entries.name: Rupesh
entries.source: Hindi रूपेश (rūpeś): stress on the superheavy last syllable, closed-syllable e → ɛ (guide); today's ɹˌupˈɛʃ matches

entries.name: Sujit
entries.source: Bengali সুজিত (sujit): first-syllable stress; Forebears 2014: India 404k, Bangladesh 27k; today's sˈuʤɪt has that stress
entries.notes: Bearers are split between Bengali/Odia (initial stress) and Hindi/Marathi (often soo-JEET for सुजीत). Today's SOO-jit is kept, as Sujan; low confidence.

entries.name: Animesh
entries.source: Hindi अनिमेष (animeṣ): short a and i, long e; stress on the superheavy last syllable; closed-syllable e → ɛ (guide, as Mahesh)
entries.notes: Today's AN-uh-mesh has the 'cat' vowel and first-syllable stress.

entries.name: Mugdha
entries.source: Hindi मुग्धा (mugdhā): short u [ʊ] in the stressed first syllable; aspirated dh is d
entries.notes: Today's MOOG-duh has the long 'oo' of 'food'; the Hindi vowel is short (book).

entries.name: Priyanshu
entries.source: Hindi प्रियांशु (priyānśu) by Hindi orthography: short i, long ā, short u; Hindi weight rule (stress the heaviest syllable, the rightmost non-final one in a tie) puts it on the superheavy 'yān'
entries.notes: Today's pɹijˈɑnʃu has the stress and the stressed 'ah'; it differs only in the unstressed first vowel (as Priyanka, pɹɪjˈʌŋkə).

entries.name: Sayali
entries.source: Marathi सायली (sāyalī, a jasmine flower) by Devanagari orthography: long ā, inherent a as schwa, long ī; stress on the heavy first syllable
entries.notes: Today's suh-YAH-lee reduces the long first ā and stresses the short middle syllable.

entries.name: Damayanti
entries.source: Sanskrit/Hindi दमयन्ती (damayantī) by Devanagari orthography: three short a's (schwa), long ī; Hindi weight rule (stress the heaviest syllable, the rightmost non-final one in a tie) puts it on the closed 'yan'; Forebears 2014: India 90,967 against Indonesia 12,358

alternatives.context: Indonesian (Javanese, Balinese) bearers, about 12% (Forebears); today's reading

entries.notes: Indian bearers dominate (Forebears), and Hindi short a is 'uh' (as Sanjay, Vasant), so the stressed 'yahn' becomes 'yun'.

entries.name: Srikanth
entries.source: Telugu శ్రీకాంత్ / Kannada ಶ್ರೀಕಾಂತ (śrīkānt): ś [ʃ], long ī and ā; the spelling's th is a dental t; Dravidian initial stress (as Srinivas, n0013)

alternatives.context: Tamil bearers, who say 'sree' (Tamil ஸ்ரீகாந்த்), as the Srinivas entry

entries.notes: The th is a dental t, not the 'th' of thin (today's -kahnth). Today's shree onset is kept.

entries.name: Devaki
entries.source: Hindi देवकी (devakī) by Devanagari orthography: long e, inherent a, long ī; stress on the heavy first syllable (Hindi weight rule; Malayalam and Tamil bearers also stress the first)
entries.notes: Today's di-VAH-kee stresses the short schwa syllable with 'ah'; the first e is a long 'ay'.

entries.name: Monali
entries.source: Hindi/Marathi मोनाली (monālī) by Devanagari orthography: long o, long ā, long ī; Hindi weight rule (stress the heaviest syllable, the rightmost non-final one in a tie) gives the rightmost non-final heavy syllable 'nā'

alternatives.context: Bengali bearers (Monali Thakur, মোনালি), with Bengali initial stress

entries.notes: Stress unsourced for this exact name; the weight rule matches today's reading.

entries.name: Pratima
entries.source: Hindi प्रतिमा (pratimā) by Devanagari orthography: /pɾə.t̪ɪ.mɑː/, stress unmarked; Bengali প্রতিমা stresses the first syllable

alternatives.context: Bengali bearers (Pratima Barua, Pratima Bose), initial stress

entries.notes: Same shape as Kavita, Sarita and Lalita (light-light-long, all unresolved): today's prah-TEE-muh lengthens the short i and uses 'ah' for the schwa, but no source marks the Hindi stress. Needs a stress source before shipping.

entries.name: Vimala
entries.source: Tamil விமலா / Malayalam വിമല (vimalā): short i, short a, final long ā; Dravidian initial stress (as Shalini, Malini)

alternatives.context: Hindi speakers, who drop the middle schwa (usually spelled Vimla)

entries.notes: The -a- spelling (Hindi usually writes Vimla) points to South Indian bearers. Today's vee-MAH-luh lengthens the short i and stresses the short middle syllable.

entries.name: Sweety
entries.source: English sweetie /ˈswiːti/ (Wiktionary); the Indian pet name is the English word respelled

entries.name: Jitu
entries.source: Hindi जीतू (jītū), pet form of Jitendra, by Devanagari orthography: long ī, long ū; stress on the first of two heavy syllables (as Raju, RAH-joo)
entries.notes: Today's jee-TOO stresses the final syllable.

entries.name: Tanushree
entries.source: Hindi तनुश्री (tanu + śrī) by Devanagari orthography: short a (schwa), u, long ī; the compound keeps the stress of its first member 'tanu' (first syllable), as Bengali তনুশ্রী does
entries.notes: Today's TAN-uh-shree uses the 'cat' vowel for the Hindi schwa. Stress unsourced for this name.

entries.name: Aparajita
entries.source: Hindi अपराजिता (aparājitā) by Devanagari orthography: schwas, long ā, short i; Hindi weight rule (stress the heaviest syllable, the rightmost non-final one in a tie) puts it on 'rā'

alternatives.context: Bengali and Odia bearers, initial stress

entries.notes: Today's ap-uh-ruh-JEE-tuh stresses the short i and lengthens it.

entries.name: Manjari
entries.source: Hindi मंजरी (mañjarī) by Devanagari orthography: schwa + nasal, j, schwa, long ī; stress on the heavy closed first syllable
entries.notes: Today's mahn-YAH-ree reads j as the y sound and stresses the schwa.

entries.name: Mukunda
entries.source: Sanskrit मुकुन्द (mukunda) by Devanagari orthography: two short u's; stress on the heavy closed 'kun'
entries.notes: Today's muh-KUN-duh uses the English 'cup' vowel for the short u (as Surinder sʊɹˈɪndəɹ).

entries.name: Padmini
entries.source: Hindi पद्मिनी (padminī) by Devanagari orthography: schwa, short i, long ī; stress on the heavy closed first syllable (Tamil and Malayalam bearers also stress it)
entries.notes: Today's pahd-MEE-nee stresses and lengthens the short i.

entries.name: Pratyusha
entries.source: Telugu ప్రత్యూష / Bengali প্রত্যূষা (pratyūṣā): short a, long ū, ṣ [ʃ]; both languages stress the first syllable

alternatives.context: Hindi weight rule, stress on the long 'yū'

entries.notes: Today's PRAHT-yoo-shuh has the right stress but 'ah' for the short a. Stress unsourced for this name.

entries.name: Sharat
entries.source: Hindi शरत् (śarat) by Devanagari orthography: two short a's; first-syllable stress as the Sharad entry (n0004)
entries.notes: Today's shuh-RAHT gives the last short a a long stressed 'ah'.

entries.name: Sankar
entries.source: Tamil சங்கர் / Malayalam ശങ്കർ (Shankar): short a in both syllables, initial stress; same reading as the Shankar entry (n0002) with s
entries.notes: Today's SANG-kar uses the 'cat' vowel and a full second 'ar'.

entries.name: Amrapali
entries.source: Hindi आम्रपाली (āmrapālī) by Devanagari orthography: long ā, schwa, long ā, long ī; Hindi weight rule (stress the heaviest syllable, the rightmost non-final one in a tie) puts it on the superheavy 'ām'
entries.notes: Today's ahm-rah-PAH-lee gives the schwa a full 'ah' and stresses 'pā'. Stress unsourced for this name.

entries.name: Amrish
entries.source: Hindi अमरीश (amrīś) by Devanagari orthography: schwa, long ī; Hindi weight rule (stress the heaviest syllable, the rightmost non-final one in a tie) puts it on the superheavy final 'rīś'
entries.notes: Today's AM-rish uses the 'cat' vowel and shortens the long ī.

entries.name: Babasaheb
entries.source: Marathi बाबासाहेब (bābā + sāheb) by Devanagari orthography: three long ā's, e in a closed syllable; Marathi stresses the first syllable
entries.notes: Honorific name (Babasaheb Ambedkar). Today's buh-BAS-uh-heb shortens the long ā's.

entries.name: Bharati
entries.source: Hindi भारती (bhāratī) by Devanagari orthography, as Wiktionary's भारत /bʱɑː.ɾət̪/: long ā, schwa, long ī; stress on the heavy first syllable (as Bharat)
entries.notes: Aspirated bh as plain b (guide). Today's bar-AH-tee stresses the schwa.

entries.name: Bhimrao
entries.source: Marathi भीमराव (bhīm + rāv) by Devanagari orthography: long ī; -rāv as the English 'rao' diphthong; first-syllable stress
entries.notes: Today's BIM-row shortens the long ī.

entries.name: Chirayu
entries.source: Sanskrit/Hindi चिरायु (cirāyu) by Devanagari orthography: c is ch, short i, long ā, short u; Hindi weight rule (stress the heaviest syllable, the rightmost non-final one in a tie) puts it on 'rā'
entries.notes: Today's shi-RYE-oo reads ch as sh and a-y as 'eye'.

entries.name: Damodar
entries.source: Hindi दामोदर (dāmodar) by Devanagari orthography: long ā, long o, schwa; Hindi weight rule (stress the heaviest syllable, the rightmost non-final one in a tie) gives the rightmost non-final heavy syllable 'mo'

alternatives.context: Bengali and Odia bearers, initial stress

entries.notes: Today's DAM-uh-dar uses the 'cat' vowel for the long ā. Stress unsourced for this name.

entries.name: Dorjee
entries.source: Tibetan རྡོ་རྗེ་ (rdo rje, Dorje); the -ee spelling is the Indian (Sikkim, Arunachal: Dorjee Khandu) one, said DOR-jee, as written

alternatives.context: Standard Tibetan and the Dorje spelling: final 'jay'

entries.name: Eldhose
entries.source: Malayalam എൽദോസ് (Eldos, Syriac Christian name): dh is a dental d, long o, final s; initial stress
entries.notes: Today's ELD-hohz splits dh into d + h and voices the s.

entries.name: Erode
entries.notes: Erode is a city in Tamil Nadu; the Wikidata bearers carry it as a place-of-origin prefix in the Tamil naming style, not as a given name. It is also the English verb 'erode' (today ɪɹˈOd, which also fits the city).

entries.name: Farokh
entries.source: Wiktionary, Persian فرخ (farrux, Iranian farrokh): final stress; kh → k (guide)
entries.notes: Parsi bearers (Farokh Engineer) keep the Persian name. Today's FARR-uk stresses the first syllable and reduces the o.

entries.name: Girija
entries.source: Hindi गिरिजा (girijā) by Devanagari orthography: two short i's, long ā; stress unmarked

alternatives.context: Kannada and Malayalam bearers (Dravidian initial stress)

entries.notes: Same light-light-long shape as Kavita and Lalita (unresolved). Today's gi-REE-juh (CMUdict) lengthens the short i, but no source marks the stress.

entries.name: Haldhar
entries.source: Odia ହଳଧର (haḷadhara; Haldhar Nag): Odia's inherent vowel is [ɔ], aspirated dh as d, initial stress
entries.notes: The input's native form is Odia. Today's HAWLD-har splits dh and gives the last a a full 'ar'.

entries.name: Kurian
entries.source: Malayalam കുര്യൻ (Kuriyan, the Syriac Christian form of Cyriac): k + u with no y glide, initial stress
entries.notes: Today's KYOOR-ee-un (CMUdict) adds an English y glide after k.

entries.name: Linthoingambi
entries.source: Meitei name (Leima Linthoingambi, Wikipedia); no source gives IPA or stress
entries.notes: Parts lin-thoi-ngam-bi: Meitei th is an aspirated t (not English th, as today's θ), oi is 'oy', ng is the ŋ sound. Stress unsourced; candidate only.

entries.name: Malati
entries.source: Hindi मालती (mālatī) by Devanagari orthography: long ā, schwa, long ī; stress on the heavy first syllable (Bengali and Marathi stress it too)
entries.notes: Today's mah-LAH-tee stresses the schwa.

entries.name: Manjusha
entries.source: Marathi मंजूषा (mañjūṣā) by Devanagari orthography: schwa, long ū, ṣ [ʃ]; Hindi weight rule (stress the heaviest syllable, the rightmost non-final one in a tie) gives the rightmost non-final heavy syllable 'jū'
entries.notes: Today's man-JOO-shuh differs only in the unstressed first vowel.

entries.name: Mrinal
entries.source: Hindi मृणाल (mṛṇāl) by Devanagari orthography: ṛ as 'ri', long ā; Hindi weight rule (stress the heaviest syllable, the rightmost non-final one in a tie) puts it on the superheavy final 'ṇāl'
entries.notes: Today's MRY-nul reads i as 'eye' and reduces the long ā.

entries.name: Muni
entries.drop_detail: 'muni' (muni bonds; San Francisco's Muni) starts sentences in finance and Bay Area news, read MYOO-nee
entries.source: Hindi मुनि (muni, 'sage') by Devanagari orthography: short u in an open syllable → 'oo' (as Uma, n0003), short i; first-syllable stress
entries.notes: Today's MYOO-nee adds an English y glide.

entries.name: Munin
entries.source: Assamese মুনিন (Munin Barua, Munin Barkotoki): u is 'oo', initial stress
entries.notes: Today's MYOO-nin adds an English y glide.

entries.name: Nachiketa
entries.source: Sanskrit नचिकेता (naciketā) by Devanagari orthography: long e; Hindi weight rule (stress the heaviest syllable, the rightmost non-final one in a tie) gives the rightmost non-final heavy syllable 'ke'
entries.notes: Today's nach-i-KAY-tuh differs from the Sanskrit/Hindi reading only in the unstressed first vowel.

entries.name: Nataraja
entries.source: Sanskrit नटराज (naṭarāja) by Devanagari orthography: j is English j, long ā; Hindi weight rule (stress the heaviest syllable, the rightmost non-final one in a tie) puts it on 'rā'
entries.notes: Today's nah-tah-RAH-yuh reads j as the y sound.

entries.name: Navinchandra
entries.source: Gujarati/Hindi નવીનચંદ્ર / नवीनचंद्र (navīn + candra): long ī; candra as the Chandra entry (n0002, CHUN-druh); compound stress as Chandrasekhar and Ramachandra
entries.notes: Today's nah-vin-CHAHN-druh shortens the long ī and uses 'ah' for the schwa.

entries.name: Niren
entries.source: Bengali নীরেন (nīren, short for Nirendra): long ī, e, initial stress
entries.notes: Today's NIRR-un shortens the long ī and reduces the e.

entries.name: Noshir
entries.source: Only a name site respells it NO-sheer; no dictionary or IPA source
entries.notes: Parsi name (Noshir Gowadia, Noshir Contractor), from Middle Persian Anoshirvan. Today's noh-SHEER stresses the second syllable; the first-syllable candidate comes from one name site only.

entries.name: Oommen
entries.source: Malayalam ഉമ്മൻ (Oommen Chandy): u is 'oo', geminate m single (guide), initial stress

entries.name: Parikshit
entries.source: Sanskrit परीक्षित् (parīkṣit) by Devanagari orthography: long ī, kṣ [kʃ]; Hindi weight rule (stress the heaviest syllable, the rightmost non-final one in a tie) puts it on the superheavy 'rīk'
entries.notes: Today's PARR-ik-shit stresses the schwa syllable and shortens the long ī.

entries.name: Paromita
entries.source: Bengali পারমিতা (pāramitā): the inherent a after r is [o] (hence the o spelling), initial stress
entries.notes: Today's pair-uh-MY-tuh reads i as 'eye'. Bengali stress is weak and initial; no English source for this name.

entries.name: Phiroze
entries.source: Wikipedia, Phiroze: Parsi name from Middle Persian Pērōz; Persian Firuz has final stress; the -oze spelling gives 'ohz'
entries.notes: Today's FY-rohz reads i as 'eye' and stresses the first syllable. No source gives the Parsi English stress directly.

entries.name: Pratīk
entries.source: Hindi प्रतीक (pratīk): /pɾə.t̪iːk/; stress on the superheavy final 'tīk' (Hindi weight rule, as Pramod)
entries.notes: The macron marks the long ī. Today's PRAH-tik stresses the schwa and shortens the ī.

entries.name: Rabindranath
entries.source: Merriam-Webster, Rabindranath (Tagore): rə-ˈbin-drə-ˌnät; Wikipedia Bengali [ˈrobind̪ɾonat̪ʰ]
entries.notes: th is an aspirated t, not the 'th' of thin; the last a is 'ah' (today's -nath with the 'cat' vowel).

entries.name: Rajasekhar
entries.source: Telugu రాజశేఖర్ (rājaśekhar): long ā, ś [ʃ], long e; stress as the Chandrasekhar entry (n0011, chun-druh-SHAY-ker)
entries.notes: Today's ruh-JAH-sik-ur reads s as s and the long e as 'i'.

entries.name: Rajshri
entries.source: Hindi राजश्री (rāj + śrī) by Devanagari orthography: long ā, j, śr [ʃɾ], long ī; stress on the superheavy first syllable
entries.notes: Today's RAH-zhree turns j into zh and drops the sh.

entries.name: Rakshit
entries.source: Sanskrit/Hindi रक्षित (rakṣit) by Devanagari orthography: short a (schwa), kṣ [kʃ]; stress on the heavy first syllable
entries.notes: Today's RAK-shit uses the 'cat' vowel for the short a (as Lakshmi, Ranjan).

entries.name: Ramachandra
entries.source: Sanskrit रामचन्द्र (rāma + candra): long ā, schwas; candra as the Chandra entry (n0002) and Chandrasekhar (n0011, ʧˌʌndɹə-)
entries.notes: Today's rah-muh-CHAHN-druh uses 'ah' for the schwa in chandra.

entries.name: Ramānī
entries.source: Ramānī by its diacritics: schwa, long ā, long ī; Hindi weight rule (stress the heaviest syllable, the rightmost non-final one in a tie) gives 'mā'

entries.name: Ranganathan
entries.source: Tamil ரங்கநாதன் (Raṅganātaṉ): short a, long ā, th as a dental t; Tamil initial stress, as the Srinivasan entry (n0019, SREE-ni-vah-sun)
entries.notes: Today's RANG-guh-nuh-thun uses the 'cat' vowel and the 'th' of thin.

entries.name: Ravindranath
entries.source: Hindi रवीन्द्रनाथ (ravīndra + nāth): Ravindra as Wiktionary रवींद्र /ɾə.ʋiːn.d̪ɾᵊ/ (Ravindra entry, n0004), nāth as Jagannath (n0005)
entries.notes: Today's ruh-VIN-druh-nath shortens the long ī and reads th as in thin.

entries.name: Reddy
entries.notes: Collision with the rare word 'reddy'. The Telugu name (రెడ్డి) sounds the same as today's RED-ee, so nothing changes.

entries.name: Sabyasachi
entries.source: Bengali সব্যসাচী (sabyasācī): Bengali s is [ʃ], the inherent a [ɔ], bya [bːo]; initial stress
entries.notes: Bengali bearers (Sabyasachi Mukherjee, Sabyasachi Chakraborty). Today's sah-byah-SAH-chee follows neither language.

entries.name: Sagnik
entries.source: Bengali সাগ্নিক (sāgnik): Bengali s is [ʃ], ā [a], initial stress
entries.notes: Today's SAG-nik uses s and the 'cat' vowel.

entries.name: Sarla
entries.source: Hindi सरला (saralā, said sarlā) by Devanagari orthography: schwa before r, long ā; stress on the closed first syllable; as Archana and Varsha (ɜɹ)
entries.notes: Today's SAR-luh uses 'ah' for the schwa.

entries.name: Satyendra
entries.source: Hindi सत्येन्द्र (satya + indra): long e in a closed syllable → ɛ, stressed, as Jitendra, Devendra, Mahendra
entries.notes: Today's SAT-yen-druh stresses the first syllable with the 'cat' vowel.

entries.name: Shantilal
entries.source: Hindi/Gujarati शांतिलाल (śānti + lāl) by Devanagari orthography: long ā twice; Hindi weight rule (stress the heaviest syllable, the rightmost non-final one in a tie) gives the superheavy non-final 'śān'
entries.notes: Today's SHAN-tuh-lul uses the 'cat' vowel and reduces the long ā of lāl.

entries.name: Shirish
entries.source: Sanskrit शिरीष (śirīṣ) by Devanagari orthography: short i, long ī; Hindi weight rule (stress the heaviest syllable, the rightmost non-final one in a tie) puts it on the superheavy final
entries.notes: Today's SHY-rish reads i as 'eye'.

entries.name: Shyamal
entries.source: Hindi श्यामल (śyāmal): śyā as Wiktionary श्याम /ʃjɑːm/ (Shyam entry, n0004), schwa; stress on the heavy first syllable
entries.notes: Today's SHY-uh-mul reads ya as 'eye'. Bengali bearers may well be the larger group; decision for review.

entries.name: Souvik
entries.source: Bengali সৌভিক (saubhik): s is [ʃ], au an 'oh' diphthong, initial stress; the spelling's v kept, as the Sourav entry (n0011)
entries.notes: Today's SOO-vik reads ou as 'oo' and s as s.

entries.name: Subhashish
entries.source: Bengali শুভাশিস (śubhāśis): s is [ʃ], bh as b, initial stress; same pattern as Debasish (n0013, DAY-bah-sheesh)

alternatives.context: Odia and Hindi bearers (s, weight-rule stress)

entries.notes: Today's SUB-huh-shish splits bh into b + h.

entries.name: Subramaniam
entries.source: Tamil சுப்பிரமணியம் (Cuppiramaṇiyam): stressed short a as 'uh', as the Subrahmanyan entry (n0021, sˌʊbɹəmˈʌnjən)
entries.notes: Today's soo-bruh-MAY-nee-um reads a as English 'ay'.

entries.name: Sundaram
entries.source: Tamil சுந்தரம் (cuntaram) by Tamil orthography: short a's, final -am; initial stress; Sundar as the n0019 entry (sˈʌndɑɹ, SUN-dar)
entries.notes: Today's SUN-duh-ram gives the final -am a secondary stress with the 'cat' vowel; Tamil -am is a short unstressed 'um'.

entries.name: Surendra
entries.source: Hindi सुरेन्द्र (surendra) by Devanagari orthography; e in the closed syllable 'ren' → ɛ and stressed, as Jitendra and Upendra
entries.notes: Today's səɹˈɛndɹə differs from sʊɹˈɛndɹə only in the unstressed first vowel.

entries.name: Tilottama
entries.source: Sanskrit तिलोत्तमा (tilottamā) by Devanagari orthography: long o, geminate t single (guide); Hindi weight rule (stress the heaviest syllable, the rightmost non-final one in a tie) puts it on the superheavy 'lot'

alternatives.context: Bengali bearers (Tilottama Shome, Tilottama Majumdar), initial stress

entries.notes: Today's tee-loh-TAH-muh stresses the short schwa syllable.

entries.name: Udaya
entries.source: Kannada/Telugu ಉದಯ / ఉదయ (udaya): u is 'oo', short a's, initial stress (as Uday, n0003, OO-day)
entries.notes: The final -a spelling marks South Indian and Sri Lankan bearers. Today's oo-DAH-yuh stresses and lengthens a short a.

entries.name: Utpal
entries.source: Bengali উৎপল (utpal; Utpal Dutt): u in a closed syllable → book vowel (as Atul), inherent a [ɔ], initial stress; Hindi उत्पल /ʊt̪.pəl/ has the same stressed syllable
entries.notes: Today's UT-pawl uses the 'cup' vowel for the u.

entries.name: Vasundhara
entries.source: Hindi वसुंधरा (vasundharā) by Devanagari orthography: schwa, short u, aspirated dh as d; Hindi weight rule (stress the heaviest syllable, the rightmost non-final one in a tie) puts it on the closed 'sun'
entries.notes: Today's vah-soon-DAH-ruh stresses the schwa.

entries.name: Venu
entries.source: Malayalam വേണു / Telugu వేణు (vēṇu): long e in an open syllable → 'ay' (guide table), initial stress
entries.notes: Today's VEN-oo shortens the long e.

entries.name: Yagnesh
entries.source: Gujarati યજ્ઞેશ (yajñeś, Sanskrit jñ said 'gn' in Gujarati): schwa, long e in a closed syllable → ɛ (as Ramesh); stress on the superheavy final
entries.notes: Today's YAG-nesh stresses the schwa with the 'cat' vowel.

entries.name: Yogeshwar
entries.source: Hindi योगेश्वर (yoga + īśvar) by Devanagari orthography: long o, long e, schwa; Hindi weight rule (stress the heaviest syllable, the rightmost non-final one in a tie) puts it on the superheavy 'geś' (as Yogesh, n0004)
entries.notes: Today's YOHG-shwor drops the e and gives the last a a full 'or'.

entries.name: Cole
entries.notes: Ordinary word 'cole' (cabbage; coleslaw). The name sounds the same, so nothing changes.

entries.name: Susanna
entries.source: CMUdict (today's source): soo-ZAN-uh; English Susanna is Susan (Wiktionary /ˈsuː.zən/) + -anna with the stress on -zan-
entries.notes: English bearers (US 17.5k) are the largest single reading group.

entries.name: Rayan
entries.region: France, Spain, Morocco, UK, US, Canada
entries.source: French Rayan [ʁa.jan] (from Arabic ريان rayyān): final stress; Arabic rayyān also stresses the long final syllable
entries.notes: France is the largest group (FR 45,385), then Spain (10,390) and the US. Today's RAY-un fits none of them.
entries.reading_decision: Consistency with Payam's fix (2026-10-09): GB 'a' before the y glide sounds like 'ay'; rah-YAHN takes the open ɑː as the US reading and Shayan already do

entries.name: Walther
entries.source: German Walther, the older spelling of Walter (Wiktionary German Walter /ˈvaltɐ/); German th is t

alternatives.context: English spelling pronunciation (US bearers); today's reading

entries.notes: German bearers dominate (wd DE 391). Today's WALL-thur reads w and th as in English.

entries.name: Gervais
entries.source: French Gervais [ʒɛʁ.vɛ] by French orthography (final -ais [ɛ], final stress); Wiktionary gives only the English surname /dʒəˈveɪ(z)/
entries.notes: Today's ʒəɹvˈA matches the French name apart from the unstressed first vowel.

entries.name: Diah
entries.source: Indonesian orthography: i [i], penultimate stress; final -ah as the Aisyah entry (n0022)
entries.notes: Today's DYE-uh reads i as 'eye'.

entries.name: Raymundo

entries.notes: Today's ray-MUN-doh (CMUdict) uses English 'ay' and the 'cup' vowel.

entries.name: Rob
entries.notes: Ordinary verb 'rob'. The English name sounds the same; Dutch Rob is [rɔp].

entries.name: Ghazi
entries.source: Wiktionary, English ghazi: /ˈɡɑːzi/; Arabic غازي (ḡāzī) [ˈɣaːziː], gh → ɡ (guide)

entries.notes: Today's chay-ZAH-ray stresses the second syllable.

entries.name: Bahram

entries.notes: Today's ed-WAR-doh (CMUdict) merges o-a into one syllable.

entries.name: Tatsuo

entries.name: Jeannot

entries.name: Annick

entries.notes: Today's PIE-oh (CMUdict) reads i as 'eye'.

entries.name: Raffaele

entries.notes: Today's rah-fye-EL-ay reads ae as 'eye'.

entries.notes: Today's EE-vee is the English Evie.

entries.notes: Gambian form of Ali. Syllable count and stress are unsourced (sites disagree between two and three syllables). Today's al-YUU is a guess.

entries.notes: Ordinary word 'emir'. Turkish and Bosnian Emir [eˈmiɾ] sounds like the word (today əmˈɪɹ), so nothing changes.

entries.name: Fredrick
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Frederick: /ˈfɹɛd(ə)ɹɪk/; Fredrick is a spelling of it

entries.name: Albino
entries.source: Wiktionary, Italian Albino: /alˈbi.no/ (Spanish the same by orthography)
entries.notes: Ordinary word 'albino' (English AL-BY-noh / al-BEE-noh). The name reading ahl-BEE-noh is in us/gb but must not replace the word.

entries.name: Tinashe

entries.notes: Today's TIN-ash drops the final vowel and stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Benigno

entries.name: Oluwaseun

entries.notes: Today's MARTH (CMUdict) reads th as in 'this'.

entries.notes: Ordinary word 'ton' (tˈʌn). The Dutch and Catalan name has a short o, so its reading is in us/gb, but it must not replace the word.

entries.source: Wiktionary, English Rhonda: /ˈɹɒndə/, US /ˈɹɑndə/

entries.name: Elodie

entries.notes: French bearers dominate (FR 155,285, plus Quebec).

entries.name: Muriel

alternatives.context: English-speaking bearers (US 28.8k, UK; Muriel Spark); today's reading

entries.notes: Population call to review: the French register (70,965) outnumbers US births (28,796), but the UK register starts too late to count Britain's many early-20th-century Muriels, and English text mostly means English bearers (Muriel Spark, Muriel's Wedding).

entries.name: Adenike

entries.name: Tope

entries.notes: Collision with the rare, archaic verb 'tope' (to drink heavily); the name is what readers meet, so it is treated as a name. Today's TOHP drops the final vowel.
