entries.region: Central African Republic, France, Albania, Kosovo, Madagascar
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Alban: /al.bɑ̃/; French names take final stress in English. Forebears 2014: Central African Republic 20,752, France 7,856, Albania 5,079, Kosovo 4,090, Madagascar 3,930, Gabon 2,486, Germany 1,799; Albanian Alban also stresses the last syllable
entries.notes: French-speaking bearers (CAR, France, Madagascar, Gabon, Congo, Benin; FR register 27,840 births) dominate, and Albanian and Kosovar bearers also say al-BAHN. Nasal ɑ̃ → 'ahn' (as Jean, Fernand). Today's AHL-bun is the English reading. Changes 'Alban Berg' in English text.

entries.name: Lizzie
entries.source: English pet form of Elizabeth: LIZ-ee; matches today's CMUdict lˈɪzi

entries.name: Awais
entries.source: Urdu اویس (Awais/Owais, from Arabic أويس Uways): two syllables ending in s, stress on the long final syllable; Urdu ʋ → w as English speakers say it (as Fawad, n0015)
entries.notes: Today's uh-WAY drops the final s. Pakistani bearers (GB-EAW 1,157, ES 299).

entries.name: Arlene
entries.source: Wikipedia, Arleen (covers the Arlene spelling): /ˈɑːrliːn/; matches today's CMUdict ˈɑɹlˌin

entries.name: Mitra
entries.source: Wiktionary, Persian میترا (mitrâ): Iran formal [miːt̪ʰ.ɹɒː]; Behind the Name Mitra (2) /miːt.ˈɾɒː/ (Persian)

alternatives.context: Indian (Bengali) bearers, mostly as a surname: MIT-ruh, today's reading

entries.notes: Today's CMUdict MIT-ruh is the Indian surname's English reading.

entries.name: Marianna
entries.source: Italian Marianna [maˈrjanna], Russian Марианна, Greek Μαριάννα, Polish: stressed 'ah' in -an-; Forebears 2014: Italy 52,501, Hungary 48,415, Russia 34,439, US 15,377, Brazil 11,189, Greece 10,889, Poland 9,519
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today says the 'lot' vowel (mar-ee-ON-uh). US already right.

entries.name: Nassim
entries.source: Arabic نسيم (nasīm): stress on the long ī; French spelling Nassim (FR register 18,120); same reading as Nasim (n0019)
entries.notes: Today's NASS-im stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Amado
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Amado: /aˈmado/ [aˈma.ð̞o]
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today says the 'lot' vowel (om-OD-oh). US already right.

entries.name: Majed
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic ماجد (mājid): /maː.d͡ʒid/; stress on the long first ā; the spelling Majed reflects colloquial [ˈmaːd͡ʒed]
entries.notes: Today's one-syllable MAYJD reads a as 'ay' and drops the second vowel. Not Persian Majid (مجید, majīd, n0010).

entries.name: Fredrik
entries.source: Wikipedia, Fredrik Reinfeldt: Swedish [ˈfrěːdrɪk]
entries.notes: Norwegian (NO register 14,847) and Swedish bearers dominate; long e [eː] is 'ay' (guide). Today's FRED-rik is the English Frederick.

entries.name: Barnabas
entries.source: English (biblical) Barnabas: BAR-nuh-bus; matches today's CMUdict bˈɑɹnəbəs

entries.name: Antonella
entries.source: Italian Antonella [antoˈnɛlla]; Forebears 2014: Italy 249,808, Brazil 7,323, Switzerland 2,479, US 2,387, Chile 1,322
entries.notes: Italian bearers dominate. Today's ɑntOnˈɛlə matches; British today's unstressed first vowel differs only in reduction.

entries.name: Uwe
entries.source: Wiktionary, German Uwe: /ˈuːvə/
entries.notes: Today reads it as English 'you'. German bearers (wd DE 933) dominate.

entries.name: Amon
entries.language: Thai / Swahili and East African (biblical) / Akan
entries.source: Forebears 2014: Thailand 45,380, Uganda 26,283, Ivory Coast 22,150, Tanzania 20,149, Zambia 12,301, Zimbabwe 11,860, Malawi 8,355, Kenya 8,004; Wiktionary gives only the English 'alternative form of Amun' sense, no English IPA

alternatives.context: Thai อมร (RTGS Amon, final syllable prominent): ah-MAWN, today's reading; Hebrew אָמוֹן also stresses the last syllable
East African bearers of the biblical name (Swahili penultimate stress): AH-mon (unsourced)

entries.notes: Bearer groups conflict: Thai (the largest single group, if Forebears' estimates hold) puts the weight on the last syllable as today does, while the East and Southern African bearers together outnumber them but have no pronunciation source; Wikidata (pool 5, GH 3, ID 3, CI 2) and US 2,398 births add little. Today's ah-MAWN is left as it is.

entries.name: Braulio
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Braulio: /ˈbɾauljo/ [ˈbɾau̯.ljo]
entries.notes: Today's BRAW-lee-oh reads au as English 'aw'; Spanish au is 'ow' (as Paulo, n0002). Final -io split into two syllables as accepted for Mauricio (n0005).

entries.name: Mouloud
entries.source: Wikipedia, Mouloud Mammeri: Tamazight 'Mulud'; Arabic مولود (mawlūd) stresses the long final ū; French ou = 'oo'; matches today's mulˈud

entries.name: Virginie
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Virginie: /viʁ.ʒi.ni/; French names take final stress in English
entries.notes: FR register 165,125 births dominates. i before r as in Myriam (n0016); French g before i is zh. Today's VUR-juh-nee is an English spelling reading.

entries.name: Fabienne
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Fabienne: /fa.bjɛn/
entries.notes: FR register 104,445; final stress in English (as Fabien, n0026). Today's FAB-ee-en stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Abida
entries.source: Arabic عابدة (ʿābida), Urdu عابدہ: stress on the long first ā (as Abid, n0007); ʿayn dropped (guide)
entries.notes: Today's uh-BEE-duh stresses the second syllable. Pakistani bearers dominate (Abida Parveen).

entries.name: Rémi
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Rémi: /ʁe.mi/; final stress in English
entries.notes: The accented spelling is French (FR 86,625). Today's REM-ee is the English/Yoruba Remi (n0022).

entries.name: Gottfried
entries.source: German Gottfried [ˈɡɔtfʁiːt]: short o, final d devoiced (Wiktionary has German audio only); same treatment as Siegfried (n0017) and Konrad (n0020)
entries.notes: German bearers (wd DE 637, AT 141, CH 123) dominate. Today's GAWT-freed has British long 'aw' and a voiced d.

entries.name: Wilma
entries.source: English Wilma: WIL-muh; matches today's CMUdict wˈɪlmə

entries.name: Didi
entries.source: Hebrew דידי, Indonesian and Dutch Didi: DEE-dee; matches today's dˈidi
entries.notes: Today's reading comes from a tech-list lexicon entry (the DiDi ride-hailing company); the name reading is the same, so nothing needs to change.

entries.name: Aqeel
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic عقيل (ʕaqīl): /ʕa.qiːl/; stress on the long ī; matches today's əkˈil

entries.name: Shaheen
entries.source: Wiktionary, Persian شاهین: Classical /ʃaː.ˈhiːn/, Iran [ʃɒː.ɦíːn]; today's ʃəhˈin differs only in the unstressed first vowel

entries.name: Waqas
entries.source: Arabic وقاص (Waqqāṣ, as Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ): stress on the long ā; q → k, geminate single, ṣ → s (guide)
entries.notes: Today's WACK-uz stresses the first syllable. Pakistani bearers say wuh-KAHS.

entries.name: Tidiane
entries.source: French spelling of Tijani (Arabic al-Tijānī), as in Cheikh Tidiane: French [ti.djan]; -ane is 'ahn' with final stress (as Ousmane, n0007; Souleymane, n0005)
entries.notes: Today's tid-ee-AN uses the 'cat' vowel. Senegalese and Ivorian bearers (FR 2,115).

entries.name: Zeinab
entries.source: Arabic زينب (zaynab): stress on the first syllable, Egyptian [ˈzeːnab]; same reading as Zainab (n0007). Forebears 2014: Egypt 138,935, Sudan 37,679, Somalia 19,188, Kenya 13,010, Saudi Arabia 6,936

alternatives.context: Iranian and Azerbaijani bearers (Persian zeynab, final stress)

entries.notes: Today's ZYE-nab reads ei as 'eye'. Arabic-speaking and Horn of Africa bearers dominate; the Persian final stress is a small group.

entries.name: Sienna
entries.source: English Sienna: see-EN-uh; matches today's gold reading siˈɛnə
entries.notes: Collision triage: the pigment word 'sienna' is rare and said the same way; treated as a name (guide: rare word), and nothing changes.

entries.name: Abou
entries.language: Arabic / Hausa / West African (French spelling of Arabic Abū)
entries.region: Syria, Niger, Côte d'Ivoire, Senegal, Mali, Mauritania
entries.source: Forebears 2014: Syria 243,552, Niger 90,418, Côte d'Ivoire 47,713, Senegal 40,089, Mali 20,048, Mauritania 16,038, Burkina Faso 12,797, Benin 8,457, Morocco 7,725, Egypt 5,118; Wiktionary, Arabic أبو (abū): Levantine /ˈʔa.bu/, first-syllable stress

alternatives.context: French phrase-final stress (ah-BOO), as francophone West African bearers are often heard in French; today's reading

entries.notes: Today's uh-BOO follows French final stress. The largest group is Syrian (Arabic AH-boo), and Niger's Hausa bearers also stress the first syllable (Abdou, n0014: Hausa Abdu, Wolof and Arabic ʿAbduh all stress the first syllable, so French phrase-final stress was rejected there). Same reading as Abu in this batch.

entries.name: Vasco
entries.source: Wiktionary, Portuguese Vasco: Portugal /ˈvaʃ.ku/, Brazil /ˈvas.ku/; Italian /ˈvas.ko/. Forebears 2014: Mozambique 70,559, Portugal 28,456, Angola 17,275, DR Congo 7,560, Italy 7,212, East Timor 6,618, Brazil 3,450

alternatives.context: Italian and Spanish bearers (VAHS-koh); Brazil VAHS-koo
English for Vasco da Gama (VAS-koh), today's reading

entries.notes: Lusophone Africa and Portugal follow the European Portuguese [ʃ] before k. Today's VAS-koh is the English reading. Changes Vasco da Gama in English text; review.

entries.name: Keiji
entries.source: Japanese けいじ (Keiji): kei is a long e [eː], 'ay' (guide), ji is 'jee'; first-syllable weight as English speakers say it
entries.notes: Today's KEE-jee reads ei as 'ee'.

entries.name: Niti
entries.source: Hindi नीति (nīti): long ī then dental t; matches today's nˈiti

entries.name: Muzaffar
entries.source: Wiktionary, Persian مظفر: Classical /mu.zaf.ˈfar/, Dari [mʊ.zäf.fáɾ], Tajik [mu.zäf.fáɾ]; Forebears 2014: Uzbekistan 92,770, Pakistan 68,770, India 13,869, Iraq 6,378, Saudi Arabia 5,712, Tajikistan 4,498, Afghanistan 2,539, Kyrgyzstan 2,426
entries.notes: Population call: the final-stress Central Asian and Persian reading (about 103k) narrowly outnumbers the Urdu one (about 84k). Today's MYOO-zuh-far adds a y and stresses the first syllable, wrong for every group. Review.

entries.name: Télesphore
entries.source: French Télesphore [te.lɛs.fɔʁ]: é = 'ay'; French names take final stress in English
entries.notes: The accented spelling is French. Today's TEL-us-for stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Turki
entries.source: Arabic تركي (turkī): short u in a closed, stressed first syllable
entries.notes: Today's TUR-key is the English 'turkey'. Saudi bearers (wd SA 18; Turki al-Faisal).

entries.name: Palwasha
entries.source: Wikipedia, Palwasha: Pashto پلوشه, 'ray of light'; no IPA. Name sites give pahl-wah-sha without stress; another puts the weight on 'pal'
entries.notes: The vowels are 'ah' throughout, but no source gives the Pashto stress. The candidate keeps today's second-syllable stress and fixes only British, where today's 'lot' vowel (pol-WOSH-uh) is wrong whatever the stress.

entries.name: Ghazala
entries.source: Arabic/Urdu غزالہ (ghazāla): stress on the long ā; gh → g (guide)
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today says the 'lot' vowel (guh-ZOL-uh). US already right.

entries.name: Ishtiaq
entries.source: Arabic/Urdu اشتیاق (ištiyāq): stress on the final long syllable yāq; q → k (guide)
entries.notes: Today's ISH-tee-ack stresses the first syllable with the 'cat' vowel.

entries.name: Nisar
entries.source: Urdu نثار (nisār): stress on the long ā; matches today's nɪsˈɑɹ

entries.name: Altaf
entries.source: Arabic ألطاف (alṭāf), Urdu الطاف: stress on the long final syllable ṭāf
entries.notes: Today's AWL-taf stresses the first syllable with 'aw'. Pakistani bearers (Altaf Hussain).

entries.name: Athar
entries.source: Urdu اطہر / Arabic أطهر (aṭhar) or أثر (athar); no pronunciation source for this spelling
entries.notes: The spelling is ambiguous: aṭhar (t + h, 'AT-har') or athar (θ). The candidate follows Azhar (n0020, h kept, first-syllable stress) and Akhtar (n0005, Urdu short a as 'uh'). Today's AY-thur is wrong either way.

entries.name: Tehmina
entries.source: Urdu تہمینہ (from Persian تهمینه Tahmina): stress on the long ī; the h is kept (as Mehboob, n0010; Mehdi, n0002)
entries.notes: Today's tuh-MEE-nuh drops the h.

entries.name: Hazem
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic حازم (ḥāzim): /ħaː.zim/; stress on the long ā; the spelling Hazem reflects colloquial [ˈħaːzem]
entries.notes: Today's HAY-zum reads ā as 'ay'. ḥ → h (guide). The row's native form ناصر (Nasser) is a data error.

entries.name: Shaina
entries.source: Yiddish שיינע (sheyne, 'beautiful'): SHAY-nuh; US bearers (11,935 births) say the same; matches today's ʃˈAnə

entries.name: Cruz
entries.region: Mexico, Venezuela, Colombia, US, Central America
entries.source: Wiktionary, Cruz: Spanish /ˈkɾus/ (Latin America), /ˈkɾuθ/ (Spain); English /kɹuːz/. Forebears 2014 forename Cruz: Mexico 108,976, Venezuela 57,012, Colombia 33,853, US 33,674, Guatemala 22,201, Peru 13,078, El Salvador 11,224, Honduras 7,882, Nicaragua 6,744

alternatives.context: English reading of the surname and place names in English text (Ted Cruz, Penélope Cruz, Santa Cruz): KROOZ, today's reading

entries.notes: Protect-word (surname and place-name collision). The given name's bearers are overwhelmingly Spanish-speaking (about 270k against US 34k, many of them Hispanic), so the name reading is KROOS, not the English KROOZ that 'already-correct' implied. But capitalised 'Cruz' in English text is mostly the surname (Ted Cruz, Penélope Cruz, Celia Cruz) and place names (Santa Cruz, Vera Cruz), conventionally read KROOZ as today, so the name reading must not replace it (as Wagner, n0027). KROOS kept in us/gb.

entries.name: Penelope
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Penelope: /pɪˈnɛləpi/

entries.name: Salif
entries.language: Mandinka / Bambara (French spelling, from Arabic Ṣāliḥ)
entries.region: Mali, Burkina Faso, Senegal, Côte d'Ivoire
entries.source: West African form of Arabic Ṣāliḥ (Salif Keïta), French spelling: [sa.lif] with final stress (as Seydou, n0023; Mamadou, n0002); Forebears 2014: Mali 55,670, Burkina Faso 23,772, Senegal 17,061, Côte d'Ivoire 7,279, Guinea 4,624; today's səlˈif differs only in the unstressed first vowel

entries.name: Vlatko
entries.source: Croatian Vlatko [ʋlâtko]: first-syllable stress, 'ah'
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today says the 'lot' vowel (VLOT-koh). US already right.

entries.name: Subhi
entries.source: Arabic صبحي (ṣubḥī): stressed closed first syllable; ṣ → s, ḥ → h (guide)
entries.notes: Today's SOO-bee drops the ḥ.

entries.name: Amélia
entries.source: Wiktionary, Portuguese Amélia: Brazil /aˈmɛ.ljɐ/, Portugal /ɐˈmɛ.ljɐ/
entries.notes: Today's uh-MEEL-yuh is the English Amelia. Forebears counts 138,025 Amélia worldwide but gives no country table; for unaccented Amelia it puts Brazil (80k) and Angola (34k) far above France. Population call between Portuguese and French; review.

entries.name: Károly
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hungarian Károly: [ˈkaːroj]
entries.notes: Hungarian ly is y, so -oly is 'oy'; á is a long 'ah'; first-syllable stress. Today's kuh-ROH-lee is a spelling reading.

entries.name: Avraham
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hebrew אברהם: Modern Israeli /av.ʁaˈham/ (Ashkenazi /avrɔˈhɔm/, [avˈrɔ.hɔm])

alternatives.context: Ashkenazi bearers, including many US Orthodox families (av-RAW-hum)

entries.notes: Israeli bearers (wd IL 256) dominate. Today's AYV-ruh-ham is an English spelling reading.

entries.name: Abderrahim
entries.source: Arabic عبد الرحيم (ʿAbd ar-Raḥīm): stress on the long ī of raḥīm; Maghrebi French spelling (as Abderrahmane, n0022)
entries.notes: Today's ab-DERR-uh-him stresses -der-. ʿayn dropped and geminate r single (guide).

entries.name: Ilse
entries.source: Wiktionary, German Ilse: /ˈʔɪlzə/
entries.notes: Today's one-syllable 'ills' drops the final vowel. German and Austrian bearers dominate (wd DE 249, AT 90).

entries.name: Evaristo
entries.source: Spanish Evaristo [eβaˈɾisto]: penultimate stress by the spelling rule; matches today's ɛvɑɹˈistO

entries.name: Hocine
entries.language: Kabyle / Algerian Arabic (French spelling of Ḥusayn)
entries.source: Wikipedia, Hocine Aït Ahmed: Kabyle Ḥusin, Arabic حسين (Ḥusayn); stress on the last syllable
entries.notes: Today's hoh-CHEE-nee reads c as Italian 'ch' and sounds the final e. Algerian bearers (wd DZ 24, FR 4,480).

entries.name: Sylvestre
entries.region: France, Côte d'Ivoire, Senegal, DR Congo
entries.source: French Sylvestre [sil.vɛstʁ]: stress on -ves- in English; today's sɪlvˈɛstəɹ keeps the stress and consonants, differing only in unstressed vowels
entries.notes: French ends in a bare -tr; English 'ter' (as Sylvester) is the usual approximation and is what today's sɪlvˈɛstəɹ says. Respelling made to match today's reading (was seel-VES-truh, the French).

entries.name: Pasquale
entries.source: Wiktionary, Italian Pasquale: /pasˈkwa.le/; final -e is 'ay' (guide)
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today says the 'lot' vowel (pos-KWOL-ay). US already right.

entries.name: Carmelo
entries.region: Italy, Mexico, Spain, US, Argentina, Philippines
entries.source: Italian Carmelo [karˈmɛːlo]; Forebears 2014: Italy 111,013, Mexico 29,578, Spain 21,205, US 13,853, Argentina 13,710, Philippines 13,508, Bolivia 11,458, Colombia 10,945

alternatives.context: Spanish-speaking bearers (kar-MAY-loh, Spanish e in an open syllable)

entries.notes: Close call, kept. Forebears: Italy 111k plus the US 14k (Carmelo Anthony, kar-MEL-oh) and the Philippines 13.5k (Tagalog e is open) say the open 'eh', about 140k; the Spanish-speaking countries (Mexico, Spain, Argentina, Bolivia, Colombia, Venezuela, Paraguay, Peru, Cuba, Dominican Republic, Equatorial Guinea) sum to about 120k with kar-MAY-loh. The stressed vowel is the only difference.

entries.name: Arslan
entries.source: Wiktionary, Turkish arslan: /ɑɾsˈɫɑn/ (Azerbaijani [ɑɾsˈɫɑn]); Persian/Urdu ارسلان (arsalān) also stresses the last syllable (as Arsalan, n0010)
entries.notes: Today's AR-slun stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Albertina
entries.source: Italian, Spanish and Portuguese Albertina: stress on -ti- (penultimate rule); matches today's ɑlbəɹtˈinə

entries.name: Segundo
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish segundo: /seˈɡundo/
entries.notes: Today's seh-GOOND-oh has the short 'book' vowel; Spanish u is 'oo'.

entries.name: Pascaline
entries.source: French Pascaline [pas.ka.lin]: -ine is 'een'; French names take final stress in English
entries.notes: Today's PAS-kuh-line reads -ine as in 'line'. FR register 10,635.

entries.name: Zarina
entries.source: Russian Зарина [zɐˈrʲinə], Persian/Urdu zarīna: stress on the long ī; matches today's zɑɹˈinə

entries.name: Hamidreza
entries.source: Persian حمیدرضا (Hamid + Reza): one word stressed on the last syllable, as Gholamreza (n0019)
entries.notes: Today's huh-MEE-dreh-zuh stresses Hamid; Persian compounds with Reza stress -ZAH. â → 'ah' (Payam).

entries.name: Khosrau
entries.source: Wiktionary, Persian خسرو: Iran formal [xos.ɹow], Classical /xus.ˈraw/, Dari [xʊs.ɾäw]; final stress

alternatives.context: Classical Persian and Dari xusraw (koos-ROW), the form the -au spelling transcribes

entries.notes: Today's KAHS-row stresses the first syllable. kh → k (guide). Most notable bearers are historical (the Sasanian kings); modern Iranian readers say kohs-ROH.

entries.name: Kaitlyn
entries.source: English Kaitlyn: KAYT-lin (as Caitlin, n0020); matches today's kˈAtlɪn

entries.name: Amale
entries.source: Arabic آمال (āmāl, 'hopes'): stress on the final superheavy syllable māl; the final e is a French silent e

alternatives.context: Arabic أمل (amal), if the bearer's name is Amal: AH-mal

entries.notes: Today's ah-MAH-lee sounds the final e. Bearers: France (FR 630), Morocco, Egypt.

entries.name: Pavlo
entries.source: Wiktionary, Ukrainian Павло: [pɐu̯ˈɫɔ]
entries.notes: Ukrainian stresses the last syllable; today's PAV-loh stresses the first with the 'cat' vowel. The в before л is a w-like glide; English speakers use v (as Pavel). Ukrainian о is 'aw' (as Dmytro, n0021).

entries.name: Toussaint
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Toussaint: /tu.sɛ̃/; nasal ɛ̃ → 'an' with final stress (as Sylvain, Julien); matches today's tusˈæn

entries.name: Ivonne
entries.region: Mexico, DR Congo, Chile, US, Germany
entries.source: Forebears 2014: Mexico 54,882, DR Congo 40,600, Chile 16,544, US 13,434, Germany 11,610, Ecuador 8,399, Venezuela 8,031; respelling of French Yvonne [i.vɔn]
entries.notes: Every bearer group stresses the second syllable with 'ee' first; today's IV-un is wrong for all. Whether Spanish-speaking bearers sound the final e is unsourced, so the candidate keeps the shared core (as French Yvonne). Low confidence.

entries.name: Justice
entries.notes: Ordinary word 'justice' (also the title, as in 'Justice Ginsburg'). The name sounds the same (JUS-tis, today's reading), so nothing needs to ship.

entries.name: Modesto
entries.source: Spanish Modesto [moˈðesto], Italian [moˈdɛsto]: stress on -des-; today's mədˈɛstO differs only in the unstressed first vowel

entries.name: Félicien
entries.source: French Félicien [fe.li.sjɛ̃]: é = 'ay', -ien = 'yan' with final stress (as Lucien and Sébastien, n0012)
entries.notes: Today's fuh-LISH-un is an English spelling reading.

entries.name: Salome
entries.language: Swahili and East African English (biblical name)
entries.source: Forebears 2014: Tanzania 142,111, Kenya 51,024, Nigeria 39,861, Philippines 23,320, DR Congo 21,591, Cameroon 19,427, South Africa 16,623, Mexico 16,516, Georgia 16,197 (accented Salomé, 14,183, counted separately); Swahili stresses the penultimate syllable

alternatives.context: Spanish-speaking bearers (Mexico, Peru, Spain): sah-loh-MAY, today's US reading
English biblical Salome (Wilde, Strauss): suh-LOH-mee, today's GB reading

entries.notes: Today's US and GB readings disagree (US sah-luh-MAY, GB suh-LOH-mee). The chosen reading follows the East African bearers and keeps the biblical stress, so GB changes only its final vowel. It rests on Forebears' African estimates, the open policy question from n0003; without them the bearers are split between Spanish, Georgian and Filipino. Review.

entries.name: Helga
entries.source: Wiktionary Helga: English /ˈhɛlɡə/; German [ˈhɛlɡa]; matches today's hˈɛlɡə

entries.name: Hilal
entries.source: Wiktionary, Turkish hilal: /hiˈlal/ (Azerbaijani [hiˈlɑl]); Arabic هلال (hilāl) also stresses the long ā
entries.notes: Today's HY-lul is an English spelling reading. Bearers: Turkish (wd TR 58, FR 1,625) and Arab.

entries.name: Ewald
entries.source: German Ewald [ˈeːvalt]: long e 'ay', w = v, final d devoiced (Wiktionary has German audio only)
entries.notes: Today's YOO-uld reads Ew as English 'ew'. German and Austrian bearers dominate (wd DE 209, AT 57). Final d → t as Konrad (n0020).

entries.name: Rasul
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic رسول (rasūl): /ra.suːl/; Persian Classical /ra.ˈsuːl/, Iran [ɹæ.súːl̥]
entries.notes: Today's RASS-ul stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Tanja
entries.source: Wiktionary Tanja: German /ˈtanja/, Czech [ˈtanja], Finnish /ˈtɑnjɑ/
entries.notes: j is y in every bearer language; today's TAN-juh reads it as English j. Same reading as Tania (n0006).

entries.name: Winifred
entries.source: English Winifred: WIN-ih-frid; matches today's CMUdict wˈɪnɪfɹɪd

entries.name: Moshe
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hebrew משה: Modern Israeli /moˈʃe/ (Ashkenazi /mɔjˈʃɛ/, [ˈmɔj.ʃɛ]); matches today's mOʃˈɛ

alternatives.context: Ashkenazi/Yiddish reading of many US bearers (MOY-sheh)

entries.name: Zamir
entries.source: Albanian Zamir, Hebrew זמיר (zamír) and Urdu ضمیر (zamīr) all stress the last syllable; matches today's zəmˈɪɹ apart from the unstressed vowel

entries.name: Maki
entries.source: Japanese まき (Maki): two short syllables with 'ah'; first-syllable stress as English speakers say it
entries.notes: Collision triage: the sushi word 'maki' is rare and lowercase; treated as a name. GB-only fix: British today says MACK-ee. US already right.
entries.word_check: gold has 'maki' read mˈɑki, the same as the name: kept

entries.name: Rehana
entries.source: Urdu ریحانہ / Bengali Rehana (from Arabic rayḥāna): stress on the long ā; h kept
entries.notes: Today's ruh-HAN-uh uses the 'cat' vowel.

entries.name: Tereza
entries.source: Forebears 2014: Brazil 229,678, Czechia 85,400, Uganda 47,513, South Sudan 22,273, Malawi 9,984, Mexico 7,817, Peru 5,422, Bolivia 4,879, Angola 4,049; Brazilian Portuguese Tereza [teˈɾezɐ] (stress on -re-, e in an open syllable is 'ay'); today's təɹˈAzə differs only in the unstressed first vowel

alternatives.context: Czech and Slovak bearers (TEH-reh-zuh; Wiktionary, Czech Tereza [ˈtɛrɛza])

entries.notes: The Wikidata sample (CZ 245) hides the Brazilian majority: Brazil alone has about 2.7 times the Czech bearers, and the East African and Spanish-speaking bearers also stress the second syllable. Today's reading is the majority reading.

entries.name: German
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Germán: /xeɾˈman/
entries.notes: Ordinary word 'German'. Bearers are Spanish-speaking (ES 24,059, US 10,008), writing Germán without the accent: the name reading is hehr-MAHN, as Germán (n0009), kept in us/gb.

entries.name: Jolie
entries.source: Wikipedia, Angelina Jolie: /dʒoʊˈliː/ joh-LEE
entries.notes: Today's JOH-lee stresses the first syllable. US bearers (13,855 births) follow the actress.

entries.name: Desiree
entries.source: English Desiree: DEZ-uh-ray and dez-uh-RAY are both established; today US dˌɛzəɹˈA, GB dˈɛzɪɹA

entries.name: Yoshiyuki
entries.source: Japanese よしゆき (Yoshiyuki): penultimate stress in English (guide); matches today's jˌOʃɪjˈuki apart from the unstressed i

entries.name: Volkan
entries.source: Wiktionary, Turkish volkan: /voɫkɑn/; Turkish names stress the last syllable (as Erol, n0023; Kadir, n0027)
entries.notes: Today's VOHL-kun stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Eugénie
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Eugénie: /ø.ʒe.ni/; French names take final stress in English
entries.notes: The accented spelling is French (FR 21,565). French ø has no English match: US 'oo', GB 'ur', as Eugène (n0008). Today's yoo-JEE-nee is an English spelling reading. Princess Eugenie (no accent) is unaffected.

entries.name: Charlene
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Charlene: US /ʃɑɹˈlin/

entries.name: Flor
entries.source: Spanish flor /ˈfloɾ/; today's flˈɔɹ matches (o before r)

entries.name: Ina
entries.source: German, Dutch and Norwegian Ina [ˈiːna], Indonesian Ina; Forebears 2014: Indonesia 85,093, Germany 71,087, US 26,069, India 13,340, Netherlands 12,279; matches today's ˈinə

alternatives.context: many older US bearers (Wikipedia, Ina Garten: /ˈaɪnə/, EYE-nuh)

entries.notes: EE-nuh is the reading of the Indonesian, German, Dutch and Scandinavian bearers, well ahead of the US group, where EYE-nuh is common.

entries.name: Heri
entries.source: Indonesian Heri: penultimate stress, e as 'eh'; Swahili heri the same; matches today's hˈɛɹi

entries.name: Anwara
entries.source: Forebears 2014: Bangladesh 13,655, India 3,998, Pakistan 1,643, England 917; Bengali আনোয়ারা, Bengali stresses the first syllable (Wikipedia, Bengali phonology; Abul n0007, Enamul n0019)

alternatives.context: Pakistani (Urdu) bearers, stress on the long ā of Arabic anwār: ahn-WAH-ruh

entries.notes: The bearers are mostly Bangladeshi (Forebears), not Pakistani as the Wikidata sample (PK 3) suggested, so the Bengali initial stress replaces the Urdu candidate, which moves to alternatives. Today's an-WAIR-uh reads ā as 'air' and is wrong for both. No source transcribes this spelling, hence low.

entries.name: Dexter
entries.notes: Also the word 'dexter' (heraldry: the bearer's right). The name sounds the same (DEK-ster, today's reading), so nothing needs to ship.

entries.name: Évariste
entries.source: Wikipedia, Évariste Galois: French [evaʁist ɡalwa]; French names take final stress in English
entries.notes: Today's EV-uh-rist is an English spelling reading.

entries.name: Umut
entries.source: Wiktionary, Turkish umut: /uˈmut/
entries.notes: Today's YOO-mut adds a y and stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Klara
entries.source: Wiktionary Klara: German [ˈklaːʁa], Polish /ˈkla.ra/, Norwegian /¹klɑːra/ (as Clara, n0006)
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today has a short ɑ; the 'ah' is long in British (as Clara). US already right.

entries.name: Petre
entries.source: Romanian Petre [ˈpetre] (Petre Roman): first-syllable stress, both e's sounded; e in an open syllable is 'ay' (guide, as Pedro). Wiktionary has Romanian audio only

alternatives.context: the English surname Petre (Lord Petre, Wiktionary RP /ˈpiːtə/): PEE-ter, today's reading

entries.notes: Today reads it as English Peter. Romanian bearers dominate (wd RO 211).

entries.name: Candice
entries.source: English Candice: KAN-dis; matches today's CMUdict kˈændɪs
entries.notes: usage english: the French register is large, but US 68,114 plus GB, CA and ZA keep the English reading.

entries.name: Virgil
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Virgil: UK /ˈvɜːdʒɪl/, US /ˈvɝdʒɪl/

entries.name: Jeanine
entries.region: DR Congo, France, Burundi, Belgium, Netherlands
entries.source: Wiktionary, Jeanine: French /ʒa.nin/, Dutch /ʃaːninə/. Forebears 2014: DR Congo 49,577, France 45,955, US 39,710, Burundi 21,000, Belgium 15,382, Netherlands 7,781, Rwanda 6,526, Haiti 3,997
entries.notes: Population call as Janine (n0020). Forebears puts the French-reading bearers (DR Congo, France, Burundi, Belgium, Rwanda, Haiti, Cameroon: about 150k) at more than three times the US (39.7k). Review only because it changes English-speaking Jeanines (Jeanine Pirro).

entries.name: Morris
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Morris: UK /ˈmɒɹɪs/, US /ˈmɔɹɪs/
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today says MAW-ris (long ɔː); RP has the 'lot' vowel. US already right.

entries.name: Arianna
entries.source: English Arianna: today's ar-ee-AN-uh (CMUdict) is an established US reading; no dictionary gives English IPA for this spelling

alternatives.context: Italian bearers and many US speakers (ar-ee-AH-nuh)

entries.notes: usage english (US 102,884 births). Name guides disagree between AN and AH for US bearers; Italians say AH. Left as today's reading; worth a decision.

entries.name: Masami
entries.source: Japanese まさみ (Masami): 'ah' vowels; penultimate stress in English (guide)
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today says the 'lot' vowel (mos-OM-ee). US already right.

entries.name: Bento
entries.drop_detail: 'bento' (a bento box) is an everyday word
entries.source: Wiktionary, Portuguese Bento: /ˈbẽ.tu/ (Brazil and Portugal); final unstressed o is [u] (as Paulo, n0002)
entries.notes: Today's BEN-toh is the Japanese lunch-box word (rare; capitalised Bento is the name). Brazilian and Portuguese bearers (wd BR 59, PT 18).

entries.name: Shahin
entries.source: Wiktionary, Persian شاهین (šâhin): Iran formal [ʃɒː.ɦíːn]; Behind the Name /ʃɒː.ˈhiːn/ (Persian)
entries.notes: Today's CMUdict SHA-hin stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Gillian
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Gillian: /ˈd͡ʒɪliən/, /ˈd͡ʒɪljən/

entries.name: Phil
entries.source: English Phil (short for Philip): FIL; matches today's gold fˈɪl

entries.name: Aydın
entries.source: Wiktionary, Turkish Aydın: /ajˈdɯn/
entries.notes: Turkish ı [ɯ] → ʊ (guide, as Hafız, n0008); final stress. Today's AY-dun stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Cristóbal
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Cristóbal: /kɾisˈtobal/
entries.notes: Today's KRIS-tuh-bul is an English spelling reading; the accent marks stress on -tó-.

entries.name: Rabah
entries.source: Arabic رابح (rābiḥ), Algerian Rabah: stress on the long first ā; ḥ → h, kept (as Saleh, n0009; Salah, n0005)
entries.notes: Today's RAH-buh drops the final ḥ. Algerian bearers (wd DZ 23, FR 2,995). No source gives the Algerian stress.

entries.name: Takeo
entries.source: Japanese たけお (Takeo): ta-ke-o, e in an open syllable is 'ay'; penultimate stress in English (guide)
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today gives the secondary-stressed first syllable the 'lot' vowel (tok-AY-oh). US already right.

entries.name: Albertus
entries.source: Dutch Albertus [ɑlˈbɛrtʏs] (Latin form used as a Dutch and Afrikaans baptismal name); Wiktionary: Latin [aɫˈbɛr.tʊs], Indonesian /alˈbɛrtus/: e before r is 'eh'

alternatives.context: English reading of the Latin (Albertus Magnus): al-BUR-tus, today's reading

entries.notes: Dutch, Belgian and South African bearers dominate (wd NL 169, BE 12, ZA 8). Changes how 'Albertus Magnus' is read in English text; review.

entries.name: Grégoire
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Grégoire: /ɡʁe.ɡwaʁ/; today's ɡɹɪɡwˈɑɹ differs only in the unstressed first vowel

entries.name: Ramazan
entries.source: Wiktionary, Turkish Ramazan: /ɾɑmɑˈzɑn/
entries.notes: Today's RAM-uh-zun stresses the first syllable with the 'cat' vowel.

entries.name: Lúcia
entries.source: Wiktionary, Portuguese Lúcia: /ˈlu.sjɐ/ (Brazil and Portugal)
entries.notes: Today's LOO-shuh is the English Lucia; Portuguese has s.

entries.name: Anibal
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Aníbal: /aˈnibal/; Anibal is the same name with the accent dropped (registers strip accents)
entries.notes: Same reading as Aníbal (n0015). Today's AN-ih-bul is the English Hannibal.

entries.name: Patrik
entries.region: Sweden, Czech Republic, Slovakia, Finland, Norway
entries.source: Wiktionary Patrik: Czech [ˈpatrɪk], Slovak [ˈpatrik], Finnish /ˈpɑtrik/
entries.notes: Every bearer language has 'ah'; today's PAT-rik is the English Patrick.

entries.name: Sidiki
entries.region: Côte d'Ivoire, Mali, Burkina Faso, France
entries.source: West African form of Arabic Ṣiddīq (long ī in the middle syllable), French spelling; today's sɪdˈiki stresses that syllable
entries.notes: Mande languages are tonal; no source gives the English stress. Left as today's reading.

entries.name: Ruy
entries.source: Wiktionary, Portuguese Rui: /ˈʁuj/ (Brazil [ˈhuɪ̯]); Ruy is the older spelling of the same name, Spanish Ruy [ˈruj]; same reading as Rui (n0001)
entries.notes: Today's RYE reads uy as English 'buy'. Brazilian and Portuguese bearers (wd BR 54, PT 20); r kept as English r (guide).

entries.name: Parfait
entries.region: Cameroon, DR Congo, Côte d'Ivoire, France
entries.source: French parfait /paʁ.fɛ/; French names take final stress in English
entries.notes: Also the dessert 'parfait', which heads menus and recipes capitalised, and which British today reads PAH-fay. The French-spelled name (FR 535, Cameroon, DR Congo) is par-FAY with final stress, kept in us/gb.

entries.name: Abu
entries.region: Nigeria, Bangladesh, Indonesia, India, Sierra Leone
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic أبو (abū): Levantine /ˈʔa.bu/; stress on the first syllable, 'ah'. Forebears 2014: Nigeria 129,432, Bangladesh 127,480, Indonesia 103,199, India 96,004, Sierra Leone 94,541, Egypt 21,146

alternatives.context: English reading in 'Abu Dhabi' (AB-oo), today's reading

entries.notes: Today's AB-oo uses the 'cat' vowel (as Abdou, n0014). Hausa, Bengali (initial stress), Indonesian (penultimate) and Arabic bearers all say AH-boo. Also changes 'Abu Dhabi' to AH-boo, which is the reading Wiktionary gives for US English (Abu Dhabi: /ˈɑ.bu ˈdɑ.bi/); British AB-oo becomes AH-boo too; review.

entries.name: Shakir
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic شاكر (šākir, also a male given name): /ʃaː.kir/; stress on the long first ā
entries.notes: Today's SHACK-eer uses the 'cat' vowel. -ir as in Abdulkadir (n0016).

entries.name: Faris
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic فارس (fāris, 'horseman'): romanized fāris, no IPA; stress on the long first ā; Bosnian Faris also first-syllable

alternatives.context: English surname (Anna Faris): FAIR-is, today's reading

entries.notes: Today's FAIR-is is the English surname. Changes 'Anna Faris' in English text; review.

entries.name: Chinyere
entries.source: Wikipedia, Chinyere: Igbo given name, 'God provides' (no IPA); Igbo e is [e], 'ay' (as Uche, n0021; Chinedu, n0022)
entries.notes: Today's CHIN-yeer drops the final syllable. Igbo is tonal; second-syllable stress follows Chinedu (chi-NAY-doo) and is unsourced.

entries.name: Damir
entries.source: Russian Дамир [dɐˈmʲir], final stress; Forebears 2014: Russia 69,292, Kazakhstan 46,287, Croatia 31,733, Uzbekistan 16,322, Kyrgyzstan 3,325, Slovenia 2,274, Bosnia 2,081; matches today's dəmˈɪɹ
entries.notes: Russian, Tatar and Central Asian bearers (about 140k) outnumber South Slavic ones (about 38k).

entries.name: Loan
entries.notes: Ordinary word 'loan'. Bearers are French boys (FR 16,930, the Breton Loan, loh-AHN) and Vietnamese women (Loan [lwaːn], lwahn). The French reading is kept in us/gb.

entries.name: Yahaya
entries.source: Hausa Yahaya (from Arabic Yaḥyā): 'ah' vowels, stress on the second syllable
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today says the 'lot' vowel (yah-HOY-uh); US already right (as Yakubu, n0026).

entries.name: Georgette
entries.region: DR Congo, France, Belgium, Cameroon, Lebanon
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Georgette: /ʒɔʁ.ʒɛt/. Forebears 2014: DR Congo 130,297, France 30,709, Belgium 19,431, US 18,884, Cameroon 14,778, Syria 11,945, Madagascar 11,185, Benin 10,511, Lebanon 8,774
entries.notes: French-reading bearers (francophone Africa, France, Belgium, Lebanon) are about ten times the US group; French g before e is zh. Decided with Janine (n0020) and Jeanine.
entries.word_check: gold has 'georgette'; kept: 'georgette' (a fabric) is written lower-case

entries.name: Fermín
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Fermín: /feɾˈmin/
entries.notes: Today's FUR-min stresses the first syllable; the accent marks final stress.

entries.name: Péter
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hungarian Péter: [ˈpeːtɛr]
entries.notes: Hungarian é is a long 'ay'; today's PEE-ter is English Peter.

entries.name: Kader
entries.source: Wiktionary, Turkish kader: /kaˈder/; French Kader (short for Abdelkader) [ka.dɛʁ] also stresses the last syllable
entries.notes: Today's KAY-der reads a as 'ay'. Bearers: France (FR 1,845) and Turkey (wd TR 23).

entries.name: Bola
entries.source: Yoruba Bọ́lá (Bola Tinubu): ọ [ɔ] is 'aw' (as Bolaji, n0023); tones dropped, first-syllable stress
entries.notes: Collision triage: 'bola' (a throwing weapon) is rare; capitalised Bola is the Yoruba name (Nigeria's president), so treated as a name. Today's US BOH-lus adds an s.
entries.word_check: gold has 'bola'; kept: 'bola' (a throwing weapon) is rare

entries.name: Abdur
entries.source: Forebears 2014: Bangladesh 360,811, India 74,773, Pakistan 33,053, Indonesia 32,776, Saudi Arabia 8,975; Bengali stresses the first syllable (Wikipedia, Bengali phonology), as do Urdu by the Hindustani weight rule (final consonant ignored, so heavy 'ab' wins), Indonesian by the penultimate rule and Arabic ʿabdu-r

alternatives.context: second-syllable stress by analogy with Abdul (n0001, ab-DOOL): today's reading

entries.notes: Today's ab-DOOR copies Abdul (n0001), whose bearers are mostly Indonesian and Malaysian. About 70% of Abdurs are Bangladeshi, and every bearer language puts the weight on the first syllable; Bengali আ is 'ah' and short u the 'book' vowel, as Abul (n0007, AH-bool) and Enamul (n0019). No source transcribes this spelling, hence low.

entries.name: Cipriano
entries.source: Wiktionary Cipriano: Spanish /siˈpɾjano/ (Latin America, Philippines), /θiˈpɾjano/ (Spain); Italian /t͡ʃiˈprja.no/; Portuguese /si.pɾiˈɐ̃.nu/
entries.notes: Spanish-speaking bearers (ES 3,660, US 1,989, MX, PE) dominate; Spanish c before i is s (Latin American, as Cecilia, Lucía). Today's ch is Italian; GB 'lot' fixed too.

entries.name: Damián
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Damián: /daˈmjan/
entries.notes: Today's DAY-mee-un is the English Damian.

entries.name: Azamat
entries.source: Wiktionary, Kazakh Азамат: /ɑzɑˈmɑt/; Bashkir [ɑ.zɑˈmɑt]; Persian عظمت azaˈmat. Forebears 2014: Uzbekistan 137k, Kazakhstan 119k, Russia 59k, Kyrgyzstan 23k
entries.notes: Today's AZ-uh-mat stresses the first syllable; Kazakh, Bashkir, Uzbek and Russian (Азамат) bearers stress the last.

entries.name: Viviana
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Viviana (es-pr): /biˈbjana/; Italian [viˈvjaːna]. Forebears 2014: Argentina 101k, Colombia 52k, Chile 48k, Mexico 34k, Ecuador 24k, Italy 18k, US 11k

alternatives.context: English spelling reading (today's), some US bearers

entries.notes: Today's viv-ee-AN-uh has the 'cat' vowel in the stressed syllable; Spanish and Italian bearers say 'ah'. Spanish v is [b]; v is kept as English speakers and the Italian bearers say it (Valeria, Valentina precedent). usage is english only because of US births (26k), mostly Hispanic.

entries.name: Gracia
entries.region: DR Congo, Congo, Spain, Philippines, Mexico
entries.source: Spanish orthography with Latin American seseo /ˈɡɾasja/; Wiktionary Indonesian Gracia /ˈɡrasi(j)a/. Forebears 2014: DR Congo 62k, Congo 15k, Spain 6k, Philippines 5k, Mexico 5k, US 3k

alternatives.context: French-style final stress, as English renders French names; possibly the Congolese bearers (unsourced)

entries.notes: Today's GRAH-chuh (Italian-style ch) fits no group: every population says s (Spain θ). The largest group is Congolese (French and Lingala speakers); no source gives their stress, so the Spanish first-syllable stress is used and confidence is low. Review.

entries.name: Emery
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Emery: /ˈɛm(ə)ɹi/
entries.notes: Ordinary word 'emery' (emery board). The name is said like the word, EM-uh-ree, as today, so nothing needs to ship.

entries.name: Fouzia
entries.source: Forebears 2014: Pakistan 328k, Algeria 94k, Morocco 79k, Bangladesh 21k; Behind the Name, Arabic Fawziyya /faw.ˈziː.ja/; name sites give Urdu Fauzia as fow-zee-uh with no stress

alternatives.context: Algeria, Morocco, France (Maghrebi Fouzia, ou = oo)

entries.notes: Pakistani bearers are the largest group, but no source gives the Urdu vowel (au as 'ow' or 'aw') or stress for فوزیہ. Arabic Fawziyya stresses -zi-, and today's FOO-zee-uh stresses the first syllable. The candidate follows the Arabic stress; needs an Urdu source.

entries.name: Gregorius
entries.source: Latin Gregorius stresses -go- (penultimate is long); Indonesian and Dutch keep the Latin stress. Forebears 2014: Indonesia 12.7k of 13.2k bearers
entries.notes: Today's ɡɹəɡˈɔɹiɪs has the stress and stressed vowel (o before r) of the Indonesian and Dutch reading; only unstressed vowels differ.

entries.name: Udo
entries.source: German Udo: long u, first-syllable stress (Wiktionary audio, Berlin). Forebears 2014: Germany 176k, Nigeria 47k (Igbo Udo, also OO-doh)
entries.notes: Today's OO-doh is the German reading.

entries.name: Pascual
entries.source: Spanish orthography /pasˈkwal/ (a word ending in -l stresses the last syllable); Wiktionary Cebuano Pascual: Paskuwál, Tagalog Pascuwál. Forebears 2014: Mexico 76k, Spain 19k, Peru 19k
entries.notes: Today's PASK-yoo-ul is an English spelling reading with first-syllable stress.

entries.name: Dominik
entries.source: Wiktionary, Polish Dominik (pl-pr: penultimate stress, /dɔˈmi.ɲik/). Forebears 2014: Poland 105k, Czechia 33k, Germany 26k, Austria 7k, Switzerland 6k, Slovakia 4k

alternatives.context: Czechia, Slovakia, Hungary, Germany, Austria (Dominik Hašek [ˈdomɪnɪk]; German [ˈdɔmiˌnɪk])

entries.notes: Polish bearers (105k) outnumber the first-syllable readings combined (about 85k). Today's duh-MIN-ik has the Polish stress position but a short i; Polish says 'ee'.

entries.name: Aïssa
entries.source: French spelling: the diaeresis splits a-ï into two syllables [a.i.sa] (as Joël, Anaïs). Forebears 2014 (this spelling): Mali 16k, Chad 1.7k, Benin 0.7k; unaccented Aissa: Algeria 138k, Niger 104k
entries.notes: Today's AY-suh merges the two vowels into one. Stress on ï follows the long ī of Arabic ʿĪsā (Algerian men) and the West African bearers' a-ee-sa; no source gives IPA for this spelling.

entries.name: Gemma
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Gemma: /ˈd͡ʒɛmə/; Italian Gèmma. Forebears 2014: Philippines 163k, England 94k, Spain 36k, Italy 18k
entries.notes: Covered by the tech list (Google's Gemma models), which reads it the same way. English, Filipino and Italian bearers all say JEM-uh.

entries.name: Yanis
entries.source: French Yanis [ja.nis] (French orthography; French names take final stress in English, as Yannick n0010). FR register 66,405 births against GB-EAW 697, US 755; Wikipedia, Yanis Varoufakis: English /ˈjænɪs/, Greek [ˈʝanis]

alternatives.context: Greek Yanis (Γιάνης), as Yanis Varoufakis is known in English

entries.notes: French bearers dominate (a top-50 French boys' name since 2000, of Kabyle use). Decision to review: this changes Yanis Varoufakis, the spelling's main bearer in English text, whose English reading is YAN-iss.

entries.name: Teodora
entries.source: Spanish /teoˈðoɾa/; Wiktionary Italian Teodòra, Portuguese Teodóra, Greek Θεοδώρα /θeoˈðoɾa/. Forebears 2014: Mexico 50k, Philippines 43k, Peru 42k, Romania 36k, Bulgaria 17k
entries.notes: Today's tee-oh-DOR-uh has the stress right but reads te- as 'tee'; every bearer group says 'teh/tay'.

entries.name: Chase
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Chase: /t͡ʃeɪs/
entries.notes: Ordinary word 'chase'. The name is said like the word, as today; nothing needs to ship.

entries.name: Edwige
entries.source: Wikipedia, Edwige Fenech: French [ɛdviʒ]; Wiktionary French Edwige (w = v). Forebears 2014: Cameroon 16k, Benin 13k, France 12k, Ivory Coast 9k
entries.notes: Today's ED-wije reads w and g as English. French names take final stress in English.

entries.name: Mladen
entries.source: Wikipedia, Mladen Petrić: Croatian [ˈmladɛn]
entries.notes: Today's MLAY-dun reads a as 'ay'.

entries.name: Sue
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Sue: /suː/
entries.notes: Ordinary word 'sue' (to take legal action). The name is said like the word, as today.

entries.name: Perla
entries.source: Spanish orthography /ˈpeɾla/ (Wiktionary Spanish Perla, given name). Forebears 2014: Mexico 101k, Philippines 43k, US 14k, Paraguay 12k, Argentina 10k
entries.notes: Light verification miss: usage is english because of US births (20,662), but US Perlas are mostly Hispanic and say PEHR-lah. Today's PUR-luh is an English spelling reading.

entries.name: Joëlle
entries.source: French Joëlle /ʒɔ.ɛl/ (Wiktionary French Joëlle, audio France); as Joël (n0009). FR register 93,670 births
entries.notes: Today's joh-EL has the right syllables but English j; French j is zh.

entries.name: Darryl
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Darryl: UK /ˈdæɹɪɫ/
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today says the merged American DERR-ul (dˈɛɹəl); British bearers keep the 'marry' vowel, as Larry, Carrie, Sharon and Darren. US unchanged. Note: Daryl (n0020) was left already-correct with the same British reading; it should get the same fix.

entries.name: Najma
entries.source: Forebears 2014: Pakistan 394k, India 216k, Bangladesh 47k, Kenya 16k, Iraq 15k; Urdu نجمہ has short a [ə] in the first syllable (Urdu/Hindi short a = 'uh', as Sanjay, Karan); Wiktionary Arabic نجمة: Hijazi /nad͡ʒ.ma/, Egyptian [ˈnɪɡ.mæ]
entries.notes: Today's NYE-muh reads 'aj' as 'eye'. South Asian bearers are the large majority.

entries.name: Victoire
entries.region: Benin, Central African Republic, Congo, France
entries.source: French Victoire [vik.twaʁ] (French orthography; final stress in English). Forebears 2014: Benin 21k, Central African Republic 13k, Congo 10k; FR register 29,565 births
entries.notes: Today's vɪktwˈɑɹ matches the French reading apart from the unstressed first vowel.

entries.name: Yasushi
entries.source: Japanese やすし ya-su-shi; English convention stresses the penultimate (as Hiroshi n0008, Yasuo n0024). Forebears 2014: Japan 112k
entries.notes: Today's yah-SOO-shee follows the convention. The British unstressed 'lot' vowel in the first syllable was accepted for Yasuo.

entries.name: Stefania
entries.source: Wiktionary, Italian Stefània; Polish Stefania (pl-pr, Ste.fan.ia). Forebears 2014: Italy 193k, Romania 26k
entries.notes: Today's stih-FAY-nee-uh reads a as 'ay'.

entries.name: Marisol
entries.source: Spanish orthography /maɾiˈsol/ (final stress on a word ending in -l); Wiktionary Tagalog Marisól. Forebears 2014: Mexico 164k, Colombia 44k, Chile 40k, US 38k
entries.notes: Today's MAIR-ih-sol stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Akmal
entries.source: Forebears 2014: Uzbekistan 200k, Pakistan 22k, Indonesia 19k, Tajikistan 17k; Uzbek and Tajik stress the last syllable (as Kazakh Azamat /ɑzɑˈmɑt/)

alternatives.context: Pakistan, Indonesia, Malaysia, Arabic (first-syllable stress; today's reading)

entries.notes: Uzbek and Tajik bearers (about 220k) far outnumber the first-syllable readings (about 60k). No IPA source covers the Uzbek name itself.

entries.name: Cosme
entries.source: Brazilian Portuguese: s before m is [z], final -e is [i] (Cosme Velho, Cosme e Damião). Forebears 2014: Brazil 55k, Mexico 17k, Benin 5k, Argentina 5k, Peru 5k, Philippines 5k

alternatives.context: Spanish-speaking bearers (Mexico, Argentina, Peru, US); about 45k together

entries.notes: Today's KOHZM drops the final vowel. Brazil is the largest single group (55k) against about 45k Spanish speakers; the Brazilian vowel quality is not sourced, hence low.

entries.name: Fidèle
entries.source: French Fidèle [fi.dɛl] (final stress in English). Forebears 2014: Burundi 10k, Rwanda 7k, Madagascar 6k (accented); unaccented Fidele: DR Congo 107k, Rwanda 38k
entries.notes: Today's fi-DEL-ay adds a final syllable; French final e is silent.

entries.name: Abdulrahman
entries.source: Arabic ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān: the l of al- assimilates to r, and the long final mān takes the stress (as Abd al-Rahman n0001, Abdurrahman n0020). Forebears 2014: Egypt 74k, Nigeria 72k, Sudan 22k, Qatar 12k

alternatives.context: as spelled, with the l (some Nigerian and diaspora bearers)

entries.notes: Today's ab-DUL-ruh-mun stresses the second syllable.

entries.name: Quazi
entries.source: Forebears 2014: Bangladesh 46k of 48k bearers; the Bangladeshi spelling of Kazi/Qazi (Arabic qāḍī), as Kazi (n0006)
entries.notes: Today's KWAH-zee reads the English qu. Same reading as Kazi.

entries.name: Ralf
entries.source: Wiktionary, German Ralf: /ralf/. Forebears 2014: Germany 354k of 388k bearers
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today says ROLF (ɹˈɒlf). German short a is the British 'a' (as Hans n0002). US already right.

entries.name: Gaël
entries.source: Wikipedia, Gaël Monfils: French [ɡaɛl]; the diaeresis makes two syllables. FR register 8,570 births
entries.notes: Today's GAYL is the English word Gael in one syllable. French names take final stress in English.

entries.name: Américo
entries.source: Wikipedia, Américo Tomás: Portuguese [ɐˈmɛɾiku]. Forebears 2014 (accented spelling): Mozambique 64k, Angola 16k, Portugal 10k, Brazil 1k
entries.notes: Today's uh-MUR-uh-koh has the 'her' vowel in the stressed syllable.

entries.name: Yuri
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Yuri: /ˈjʊɹi/; Russian Ю́рий, Japanese ゆり, Portuguese Iúri all stress yu-. Forebears 2014: Brazil 91k, Japan 54k, Angola 52k

entries.name: Made
entries.source: Balinese birth-order name Made (second child), two syllables with final [ɛ]. Forebears 2014: Indonesia 367k
entries.notes: Ordinary word 'made', very common, including capitalised at the start of a sentence ('Made in...'). The Balinese name is MAH-day (us/gb); shipping it would break the word.

entries.name: Egon
entries.source: Wikipedia, Egon Schiele: German [ˈeːɡɔn]; Wiktionary Danish Egon /eːɡɔn/. Forebears 2014: Germany 89k, Brazil 6k, Denmark 6k, Austria 5k
entries.notes: Today's EE-gun reads e as 'ee'.

entries.name: Milagros
entries.source: Wikipedia, Milagros Sequera: Spanish [miˈlaɣɾos]. Forebears 2014: Philippines 121k, Venezuela 64k, Peru 55k, Spain 44k
entries.notes: Today's mih-LAG-rohz has the 'cat' vowel and a final z.

entries.name: Mert
entries.source: Wiktionary, Turkish Mert: /mært/; Wikipedia, Mert Günok [mæɾt]. Forebears 2014: Turkey 50k of 54k
entries.notes: Today's MURT has the 'her' vowel; Turkish e before r is open 'air'.

entries.name: Bello
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hausa Bello: bellò (ha-IPA). Forebears 2014: Nigeria 571k, Cameroon 27k
entries.notes: Today's BEL-oh matches the Hausa reading.

entries.name: Alwi
entries.source: Indonesian orthography (penultimate stress), from Arabic ʿAlawī. Forebears 2014: Indonesia 28k of 31k
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today says OL-wee (ˈɒlwi). US already right.

entries.name: İsa
entries.source: Turkish personal names stress the last syllable (as Mehmet, Ahmet, İmran); the dotted İ marks Turkish or Azerbaijani spelling. Forebears 2014 (Isa): Turkey 106k, Azerbaijan 8k

alternatives.context: Arabic ʿĪsā, as the undotted Isa (n0028); today's reading

entries.notes: Wiktionary's Turkish İsa gives no IPA; the stress follows the Turkish precedent.

entries.name: Rowan
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Rowan: US /ɹoʊən/, RP /ɹəʊən/ (also /ˈɹaʊ.ən/ for the tree)
entries.notes: Treated as a name, not protect-word, as Colleen (n0023): the word 'rowan' (a tree) is uncommon and lowercase, and ROH-un is also its first dictionary reading, so the entry can't misread it. US today says ROW-un (as in 'cow'); the name (66k US births, Rowan Atkinson) is ROH-un. GB already right.
entries.word_check: gold has 'rowan'; kept: the tree is said both ROH-an and ROW-an (Merriam-Webster), so the name's reading suits it

entries.name: Rajab
entries.source: Forebears 2014: Pakistan 44k, Iran 25k, Afghanistan 18k, Tanzania 13k, India 13k, Kenya 9k, Uganda 9k, Egypt 7k, Libya 6k; Urdu short a is [ə]; Wiktionary Persian رجب raˈjab, Hausa rajàb

alternatives.context: Arabic and Swahili bearers (Egypt, Libya, Tanzania, Kenya)

entries.notes: First-syllable stress (Urdu, Hindi, Arabic, Swahili; about 100k) outnumbers Persian final stress (about 43k, today's ruh-JAHB). The Urdu stress follows the batch convention for CV.CVC names (Lalit, Madhur), which is still open; hence low.

entries.name: Collin
entries.source: English Collin, as Colin: /ˈkɒlɪn/ (CMUdict reading)

entries.name: Safa
entries.source: Arabic صفاء ṣafāʾ: the long final syllable takes the stress (as Saba n0011); Turkish Safa and Persian Safâ also stress the last. Forebears 2014: Iraq 108k, Sudan 88k, Egypt 29k, Jordan 22k, Syria 20k
entries.notes: Today's SAH-fuh stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Merlin
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Merlin: GA /ˈmɝlɪn/, RP /ˈmɜːlɪn/
entries.notes: Ordinary word 'merlin' (a falcon). The name is said like the word, as today. Forebears: US 15k is the largest group (Honduran Merlin is mer-LEEN).

entries.name: Harper
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Harper: GA /ˈhɑɹpɚ/
entries.notes: Ordinary word 'harper' (a harp player). The name is said like the word, as today.

entries.name: Fauzi
entries.source: Indonesian and Malay au is the diphthong [au] (Arabic fawzī). Forebears 2014: Indonesia 61k, Malaysia 7k, Libya 4k
entries.notes: Today's FAW-zee reads au as in 'caught'.

entries.name: Willi
entries.source: Wiktionary, German Willi: /ˈvɪli/. Forebears 2014: Germany 303k, Switzerland 12k
entries.notes: Today's WIL-ee reads German w as English w.

entries.name: Samy
entries.source: Arabic sāmī, as Sami (n0006). Forebears 2014: Egypt 72k, DR Congo 26k, Kuwait 7k, France 3.5k, Algeria 2.4k, Sudan 2.4k; FR register 18,800 births
entries.notes: Today's SAY-mee reads a as 'ay'. Arabic-speaking bearers outnumber the French ones.

entries.name: Gael
entries.region: US, France, Spain, Mexico, DR Congo
entries.source: Wikipedia, Gael García Bernal: Spanish [ɡaˈel]; French Gaël [ɡaɛl]. Registers: US 45,856, FR 28,325, ES 14,996 births; Forebears 2014: France 10k, DR Congo 8k, Spain 6k, Madagascar 5k

alternatives.context: English: a Gaelic speaker; some English-speaking bearers (today's reading)

entries.notes: The US births are mostly Hispanic (Gael has been a top Hispanic boys' name since 2005); Spanish, French and Portuguese bearers all say gah-EL. Also matches capitalised 'Gael' (a Gaelic person), which is rare in text.

entries.name: Ayoub
entries.source: Wiktionary, Arabic أيوب ʔayyūb (Moroccan ʔayyūb, ʔiyyūb); the long final syllable takes the stress, as Ayub (n0010). Forebears 2014: Morocco 168k, Tanzania 20k, Sudan 11k
entries.notes: Today's AY-owb reads it as one syllable.

entries.name: Hilmi
entries.source: Turkish final stress for personal names (as Hamdi n0013, Mehmet). Forebears 2014: Turkey 39k, Indonesia 7k, Malaysia 2k
entries.notes: Turkish bearers are the large majority.

entries.name: Risto
entries.source: Wikipedia, Risto Ryti: Finnish [ˈristo]. Forebears 2014: Finland 26k, North Macedonia 12k (also first-syllable stress)

entries.name: Mélanie
entries.source: Wikipedia, Mélanie Laurent: French [melani]. FR register 123,665 births
entries.notes: The accented spelling is French; today's MEL-uh-nee is English Melanie. French names take final stress in English (Valérie n0015, Stéphanie n0017).

entries.name: Abd al-Hussein
entries.source: Arabic ʿAbd al-Ḥusayn; as Abd al-Aziz (n0002) and Hussein (n0002, husˈAn). Wikidata: IR 12, IQ 5
entries.notes: Today's reading stresses al- and reads Hussein as HUSS-ayn. Iranian bearers usually write Abdolhossein.

entries.name: Erkan
entries.source: Wiktionary, Turkish Erkan: /æɾˈkɑn/. Forebears 2014: Turkey 144k of 152k
entries.notes: Today's UR-kun stresses the first syllable with the 'her' vowel.

entries.name: Gerd
entries.source: Wiktionary, German Gerd: /ɡɛʁt/; Wikipedia, Gerd Müller [ɡɛʁt]. Forebears 2014: Germany 262k, Norway 22k, Sweden 21k
entries.notes: Today's GURD has the 'her' vowel. German final d is t. Norwegian and Swedish Gerd (women) is not sourced here.
entries.word_check: gold has 'gerd'; kept: the illness is written GERD, in capitals

entries.name: Darrell
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Darrell: UK /ˈdæɹɪɫ/
entries.notes: GB-only fix, as Darryl, Larry and Carrie: British keeps the 'marry' vowel. US unchanged.

entries.name: Fabiana
entries.source: Portuguese orthography: Fabiana [fabiˈɐ̃nɐ] (penultimate stress); Italian [faˈbjaːna], Spanish [faˈβjana]. Forebears 2014: Brazil 299k, Argentina 44k, Italy 12k
entries.notes: Today's fah-bee-AN-uh has the 'cat' vowel in the stressed syllable; every group says 'ah'.

entries.name: Hassane
entries.source: French spelling of Ḥasan: the final -e keeps the n oral, it is not a syllable. Forebears 2014: Niger 85k, Morocco 52k, Chad 32k, Burkina Faso 23k, Algeria 10k
entries.notes: Today's hah-SAH-nee reads the silent e. French names take final stress in English; no source gives the Hausa, Zarma or Moroccan stress, hence low.

entries.name: Vesna
entries.source: Wikipedia, Vesna Vulović: [ʋêsna]; Wiktionary Serbo-Croatian Vȅsna, English /vɛsnə/. Forebears 2014: Serbia 67k, Croatia 33k

entries.name: Paulos
entries.source: Ge'ez ጳውሎስ Pawlos ends in s. Forebears 2014: Eritrea 27k, South Africa 16k, Ethiopia 11k
entries.notes: Today's POW-lohz differs only in the final z; the Eritrean and Ethiopian name ends in s.

entries.name: Kishor
entries.source: Hindustani weight rule: the extra-heavy final syllable shor (long o + r) takes the stress (as Hemant, Balwant). Forebears 2014: India 493k, Bangladesh 12k
entries.notes: Today's KISH-ur stresses the first syllable and reduces the long o.

entries.name: Tapan
entries.source: Bengali তপন [t̪ɔpon] (inherent vowel ɔ, second vowel o by Bengali vowel harmony). Forebears 2014: India 444k, Bangladesh 25k

alternatives.context: Hindi and Sanskritic reading (Indian English TUP-un)

entries.notes: Today's TAY-pun fits no group. Tapan is mostly a Bengali and Odia name, but the share in India is unknown, as for Satyajit; decision to review with the Bengali names (Santanu n0013).

entries.name: Therese
entries.region: DR Congo, Cameroon, France, Ivory Coast, Benin
entries.source: Forebears 2014: DR Congo 607k, Cameroon 106k, US 48k, Germany 47k, France 46k, Ivory Coast 20k, Benin 19k, Burkina Faso 17k; French Thérèse /te.ʁɛz/, as Thérèse (n0011)
entries.notes: Today's THERR-eess fits no group. Francophone bearers (about 850k, mostly Central Africa) dominate this unaccented spelling. Decision to review with Leopold, Emilie and Angelique (n0023): whether an unaccented spelling counts the francophone bearers whose records drop the accent.

entries.name: Patric
entries.source: Forebears 2014: DR Congo 15.6k (French pa-TREEK) against US 12.6k, South Africa 7k, Nigeria 5k, Uganda 4k, Tanzania 3k (English PAT-rik); Sweden 1.8k (PAH-trik)
entries.notes: English-speaking bearers together (about 36k) are the largest group.

entries.name: Estela
entries.source: Spanish orthography /esˈtela/ (penultimate stress; e in an open syllable is 'ay' per the guide). Forebears 2014: Mexico 152k, Argentina 107k, Philippines 38k, US 29k
entries.notes: Today's es-TEL-uh uses the closed-syllable vowel.

entries.name: Kostas
entries.source: Wiktionary, Greek Κώστας: /ˈko.stas/; Wikipedia, Kostas Karamanlis: [ˈkostas]. Forebears 2014: Greece 12k, US 2k, Lithuania 2k (Kòstas, also first-syllable)
entries.notes: Today's KOH-stuz ends in z; Greek has s.

entries.name: Suzana
entries.source: Penultimate stress in Swahili and Portuguese (Suzana). Forebears 2014: Tanzania 111k, Angola 85k, Brazil 76k, Mozambique 24k, DR Congo 23k

alternatives.context: Croatia, Serbia, North Macedonia (Wiktionary Serbo-Croatian Sùzana, first-syllable stress)

entries.notes: Today's soo-ZAN-uh has the 'cat' vowel in the stressed syllable.

entries.name: Béla
entries.source: Wikipedia, Béla Bartók: English /ˈbeɪlɒ/, Hungarian [ˈbeːlɒ]. Forebears 2014: Hungary 82k of 83k
entries.notes: Today's BEL-uh reads é as short e.

entries.name: Azzedine
entries.source: Wikipedia, Azzedine Alaïa: French [azedin], Arabic ʕizz adˈdiːn; Wiktionary French Azzedine (ze = zé). Forebears 2014: Algeria 37k, Morocco 5k
entries.notes: Today's aht-say-DEE-nee reads zz as ts and adds a syllable.

entries.name: Witold
entries.source: Wikipedia, Witold Pilecki: Polish [ˈvitɔlt]. Forebears 2014: Poland 83k of 88k
entries.notes: Today's WIT-ohld reads Polish w as English w; final d is devoiced.

entries.name: Enver
entries.source: Wikipedia, Enver Hoxha: Albanian [ɛnˈvɛɾ]; Wiktionary Albanian Enver /ɛnˈvɛr/; Turkish final stress. Forebears 2014: Turkey 62k, Kosovo 6k, Russia 5k, Bosnia 5k
entries.notes: Today's EN-vur stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Italo
entries.source: Wiktionary, Italian Ìtalo; Wikipedia, Italo Calvino: Italian [ˈiːtalo]; Brazilian Ítalo [ˈitalu]. Forebears 2014: Brazil 81k, Italy 38k, Chile 6k, Ecuador 6k, Argentina 6k, Peru 5k

alternatives.context: Italy and Spanish-speaking countries (about 66k); Italo Calvino

entries.notes: Today's it-AH-loh stresses the second syllable; every group stresses the first. Brazil (81k) is the largest single group; the Italian and Spanish -loh differs only in the final unstressed vowel. Decision to review: Italo Calvino in English text would end in -loo.

entries.name: Brooklyn
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Brooklyn: /ˈbɹʊk.lən/
entries.notes: Same as the New York borough.

entries.name: Kabelo
entries.source: Sotho-Tswana stress the penultimate syllable. Forebears 2014: South Africa 27k, Botswana 11k, Lesotho 4k
entries.notes: Today's kəbˈɛlO has the penultimate stress; no IPA source for the name.

entries.name: Hilario
entries.source: Spanish h is silent: /iˈlaɾjo/; Wiktionary Tagalog Hilario (also Ilario). Forebears 2014: Mexico 89k, Mozambique 40k (Portuguese Hilário, h also silent), Philippines 30k
entries.notes: Today's hee-LAH-ree-oh says the h.

entries.name: Yeong-cheol
entries.source: Korean 영철: Revised Romanization eo is [ʌ], ch is [tɕʰ]; stress by the guide's two-syllable convention (as Chun-hui n0022)
entries.notes: Today's yong-KEE-ul misreads ch and eo. Korean has no lexical stress; final primary is the convention.

entries.name: Will
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Will: /wɪl/
entries.notes: Ordinary word 'will'. The name sounds like the word, but in a sentence the app de-stresses it like the auxiliary verb (I met Will yesterday: wˌɪl).

entries.name: Yoshinori
entries.source: Japanese よしのり yo-shi-no-ri; English convention stresses the penultimate (as Noriko, Hiroyuki). Forebears 2014: Japan 195k
entries.notes: Today's jOʃinˈɔɹi follows the convention; ɔɹ and Oɹ are the same before r in English.

entries.name: Rocky
entries.source: English Rocky, as the word
entries.notes: Ordinary word 'rocky'. The name is said like the word, as today.

entries.name: Saima
entries.source: Urdu صائمہ Sāʾima, said with the 'ai' diphthong; Finnish Saima [ˈsɑimɑ] also SY-mah. Forebears 2014: Pakistan 531k, Bangladesh 103k, India 22k, Finland 0.7k
entries.notes: Today's SAY-muh reads ai as 'ay'. No IPA source for the Urdu name.

entries.name: Teófilo
entries.source: Wikipedia, Teófilo Stevenson: Spanish [teˈofilo]. Wikidata: PE 27, PT 10, BR 9, AR 8; Forebears 2014 (unaccented): Peru 47k, Mexico 24k, Bolivia 12k
entries.notes: Today's tee-oh-FEE-loh stresses -fi-; the accent marks -ó-.

entries.name: Rian
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Rian: /ˈriː.ən/ (Irish name), /ˈraɪən/ (variant of Ryan). Forebears 2014: Indonesia 82k, Brazil 25k, Thailand 14k, Netherlands 3.5k, US 3k; registers: US 8,928, IE 3,118, GB-EAW 2,064 births

alternatives.context: US and UK bearers using it as a spelling of Ryan (Rian Johnson); today's reading

entries.notes: Indonesian (82k), Irish (Rían) and Dutch bearers say REE-un; US Rians (about 9k births) say RY-un. Decision to review: changes Rian Johnson in English text.

entries.name: Keyvan
entries.source: Wiktionary, Persian کیوان (keyvân): Iran formal [kʰʲej.vɒ́ːn]
entries.notes: ey → 'ay'. Today's KEE-vun reads ey as 'ee' and stresses the first syllable. Middle Persian kēwān (Saturn).

entries.name: Moustafa
entries.source: Egyptian Arabic stresses the penultimate -ṭa- (Moṣṭafa); as Moustapha (n0013). Forebears 2014: Egypt 103k, Saudi Arabia 36k, Sudan 6k
entries.notes: Today's MUS-tuh-fuh stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Basile
entries.source: French Basile [ba.zil] (s between vowels is z; final stress in English). Forebears 2014: DR Congo 15k, Benin 11k, Cameroon 10k; FR register 18,075 births
entries.notes: Today's BAH-sul is the English Basil with the French spelling.

entries.name: Diya
entries.source: Hindi दिया (lamp); as Riya and Priya (n0026, n0002). Forebears 2014: India 12k, Saudi Arabia 3k (Arabic Ḍiyāʾ, men), Sudan 2k
entries.notes: Today's DEE-uh matches the Indian reading, as for Riya.

entries.name: Zaynab
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Zaynab (alt. of Zainab, from Arabic زَيْنَب); as Zainab (n0007). Forebears 2014: Russia 24k, Tajikistan 9k, Uzbekistan 5k, Somalia 4k, Morocco 3k; registers GB-EAW 3,871, US 2,364, FR 2,115

alternatives.context: Iran, Tajikistan, possibly Russia (final stress; unsourced for Russian)

entries.notes: Kept as today's ZAY-nab. Russian (Dagestan, Chechnya) and Tajik bearers may stress the last syllable, but no source gives the Russian stress of Зайнаб.

entries.name: Kelsey
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Kelsey: /ˈkɛlsi/

entries.name: Fereydun
entries.source: Wiktionary, Persian فریدون (Iranian firēdūn/firaydūn, modern [feɾejˈduːn]; final stress)
entries.notes: Today's FERR-ih-dun stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Jadwiga
entries.source: Wikipedia, Jadwiga of Poland: Polish [jadˈviɡa]. Forebears 2014: Poland 39k of 49k
entries.notes: Today's JAD-wig-uh reads j and w as English.

entries.name: Cosmas
entries.source: Forebears 2014: Tanzania 34k, Kenya 22k, Nigeria 21k, Zambia 15k, Malawi 15k, Zimbabwe 14k, Uganda 12k; Swahili spelling is phonemic (s is [s])
entries.notes: Today's KAWZ-muz voices both s sounds. East African bearers are the large majority.

entries.name: Anaïs
entries.source: Wikipedia, Anaïs Nin: French [ana.is], English /ˌænaɪˈiːs/; Wiktionary French Anaïs. FR register 130,160 births
entries.notes: Today's uh-NAY drops the final syllable. French bearers say ah-nah-EES.

entries.name: Júlia
entries.source: Portuguese Júlia /ˈʒu.li.ɐ/ (Wiktionary Portuguese Jú-li-a). Forebears 2014 (accented spelling): Angola 53k, Mozambique 35k, Slovakia 26k, Hungary 12k, Portugal 10k, Brazil 8k
entries.notes: Portuguese-speaking bearers (about 106k) outnumber Slovak and Hungarian ones (about 38k). Today's JOOL-yuh reads j as English j.

entries.name: Christie
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Christie: /ˈkɹɪsti/

entries.name: Soha
entries.source: Egyptian Soha (Arabic Suhā). Forebears 2014: Egypt 88k, Iraq 32k, Jordan 11k
entries.notes: Today's SOH-huh matches the Egyptian reading (and Soha Ali Khan's).

entries.name: Mohsin
entries.source: Wiktionary, Urdu محسن (mohsin). Forebears 2014: Pakistan 136k, Saudi Arabia 63k, Bangladesh 49k, India 40k
entries.notes: Today's MOH-sin is the South Asian reading; the h after the vowel is weak in Urdu.

entries.name: Édgar
entries.source: Spanish Édgar /ˈeðɡaɾ/ (the accent marks first-syllable stress); Wiktionary Portuguese Édgar
entries.notes: Today's ED-gur differs only in the unstressed vowel.

entries.name: Daniella
entries.source: English Daniella (CMUdict reading); Wiktionary Portuguese Daniella

entries.name: Yeong-ho
entries.source: Korean 영호: Revised Romanization eo is [ʌ]; stress by the guide's two-syllable convention (as Chun-hui n0022)
entries.notes: Today's YAWNG-hoh reads eo as 'aw' and stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Hamidou
entries.source: French spelling (ou = oo) of Fula and Mande Hamidou. Forebears 2014: Burkina Faso 135k, Mali 55k, Niger 53k, Guinea 16k
entries.notes: Today's HAM-ih-doo stresses the first syllable. Final stress follows the French-spelling convention (Abdoulaye n0004); no source gives the Fula or Mooré stress.

entries.name: Afia
entries.source: Bengali আফিয়া and Akan Afia (Friday-born girl) both stress a- with 'ah'. Forebears 2014: Bangladesh 77k, Ghana 14k
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today says OFF-ee-uh (ˈɒfiə). US already right.

entries.name: Helmi
entries.source: Indonesian and Finnish stress the first syllable. Forebears 2014: Indonesia 53k, Saudi Arabia 7k, Egypt 6k, Finland 5k

entries.name: Pepe
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Pepe: /ˈpɛpeɪ/; Spanish /ˈpepe/, Italian Pépe
entries.notes: Today's PEP-ee reads the final e as 'ee'.

entries.name: Marshall

entries.name: Helene
entries.region: DR Congo, France, Cameroon, Benin, Burkina Faso

entries.name: Srđan

entries.name: Ayaan

entries.name: Randolph
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Randolph: /ˈɹændɒlf/

entries.name: Qazi

entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today says KOZ-ee (kˈɒzi). US already right.

entries.name: Othman

entries.name: Genaro
entries.source: Spanish /xeˈnaɾo/: g before e is [x], English h (as Jesús); Wiktionary Cebuano Genaro: Henaro. Forebears 2014: Mexico 98k, Peru 22k, Philippines 22k, US 16k

entries.name: Saša

entries.name: Rifat
entries.source: Wiktionary, Egyptian Arabic رفعت: [ˈɾɪfʕæt] (first-syllable stress). Forebears 2014: Pakistan 155k, Bangladesh 133k, Turkey 39k, Russia 10k

entries.name: Ata

entries.name: Freya
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Freya: /ˈfɹeɪə/

entries.name: Doan

entries.notes: Unaccented spelling, most likely of Đoàn (đ = d, oa = [wa]). The plain-d spelling could also be Doãn, so confidence is low. Today's DOHN reads it as English. Tone dropped.

entries.name: Djamila

entries.name: Bình

entries.name: Enes
entries.source: Turkish Enes (from Arabic Anas): regular orthography; Turkish names take final stress (as Erol, Kenan, n0023)
entries.notes: Today's EENZ reads it as an English word. Bearers are mostly Turkish (wd TR 114; FR 3.9k Turkish families).

entries.source: Wiktionary, Hungarian András: [ˈɒndraːʃ]; Hungarian stresses the first syllable

entries.name: Hein
entries.source: Forebears 2014: Myanmar 852,129, Cambodia 11,154, Netherlands 8,770, South Africa 3,605, Germany 900; Wiktionary, Burmese ဟိန်း: /héɪɴ/ (BGN/PCGN hein:); Wikipedia, Kyaw Hein: Burmese [tɕɔ́ hɛ́ɪɰ̃]

entries.notes: Burmese Hein (ဟိန်း, 'great, grand') is a very common name element in Myanmar, about 60 times the Dutch, German and Afrikaans bearers together; Wikidata's given-name links only cover the Dutch and German ones. Burmese ei [eɪ] with a nasal coda is English 'ayn' (as Thein Sein); tone dropped. Review: capitalised Hein in English text is also a German and American surname (Mel Hein, Christoph Hein) and Piet Hein, which this changes to HAYN.

entries.name: Rodrigue

entries.name: Cemal

entries.name: Margot
entries.source: Wiktionary, Margot: English /ˈmɑɹ.ɡoʊ/, French /maʁ.ɡo/, German /ˈmaʁ.ɡɔt/; Forebears 2014: Germany 162,214, US 17,664, Netherlands 12,303, Peru 10,445, France 8,637
