The German reading would change Margot Robbie and Margot Fonteyn in English text. Today's English reading stays until someone decides.

entries.name: Justus
entries.source: Forebears 2014: Uganda 42,337, Kenya 40,394, Tanzania 5,796, Nigeria 4,698 against Germany 2,154, Netherlands 725: East African bearers use the English reading, as today's

entries.name: Nobuyuki
entries.source: Japanese のぶゆき No-bu-yu-ki; penultimate stress in English (guide, as Haruki); today's nˌObujˈuki matches

entries.name: Daya
entries.source: Hindi दया dayā [dəjaː]; Forebears 2014: India 199,492, Nepal 9,515, Sri Lanka 9,157; Hindi schwa before y is heard as English 'dye', as Jaya (n0009)
entries.notes: Today's DYE-uh is the usual English rendering, as for Jaya and Maya; only the unstressed final vowel differs.

entries.name: Salimata
entries.source: West African (Mali, Côte d'Ivoire, Senegal, Burkina Faso) name, French spelling; a is 'ah'; penultimate stress as today and as Aminata (n0006)
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today says the 'lot' vowel in the stressed syllable. The stress is unsourced; kept today's.

entries.name: Cirilo
entries.source: Spanish Cirilo [siˈɾilo] (Latin America): regular orthography; today's səɹˈilO matches apart from the unstressed first vowel

entries.name: Evie
entries.source: English Evie /ˈiːvi/ (pet form of Eve, Evelyn); today's reading matches

entries.name: Vito
entries.source: Wiktionary, Italian Vito: /ˈvi.to/; today's vˈitO matches

entries.name: Deon
entries.source: English and Afrikaans Deon, stressed on the first syllable (DEE-on); today's dˈiɑn matches
entries.notes: US bearers also say dee-AHN; the first-syllable reading is shared by South African bearers.

entries.name: Filomena
entries.source: Forebears 2014: Italy 149,970; Angola 91,504, Brazil 26,246, Mozambique 20,160, Portugal 19,186 (Portuguese [filuˈmenɐ]); Peru, Mexico, Argentina, Bolivia (Spanish [filoˈmena])
entries.notes: Population call: Portuguese and Spanish bearers together (about 250k) say a closed e (open syllable → 'ay', guide table); Italians (150k) the open 'eh'. Today's fil-uh-MEE-nuh is the English spelling reading either way.

entries.name: Erhan
entries.source: Turkish Erhan: regular orthography; Turkish names take final stress (as Erol, Kenan, n0023)
entries.notes: Today's UR-hun stresses the first syllable with the 'her' vowel.

entries.name: Tomislav
entries.source: Wikipedia, Tomislav of Croatia: Croatian [tǒmislaʋ]
entries.notes: First-syllable stress with o and a long 'ah' (GB as Miroslav, n0016). Today's TAH-mih-slahv uses the 'lot'/'ah' vowel for o.

entries.name: Williams
entries.language: English (Latin American and West African use)
entries.source: Forebears 2014: Nigeria 45,664, Venezuela 25,573, Ghana 14,384, US 13,688, Brazil 8,668, Peru 8,559: English-speaking bearers are the largest group
entries.notes: Also a very common surname in English text, so today's English reading should stay in any case.

entries.name: Zane
entries.source: English Zane /zeɪn/; US register 55.7k
entries.notes: anglo_share 0.37, but the English bearers (US 55.7k, GB, CA) far outnumber the Latvian ones (wd LV 25).

entries.name: Kirk
entries.notes: Also the Scots word 'kirk' (church). Name and word are read the same today (kˈɜɹk), the name's established reading, so nothing needs to ship.

entries.name: Hatem
entries.source: Arabic حاتم Ḥātim [ˈħaːtim]; Maghrebi/Egyptian spelling with e; ḥ → h, ā → 'ah'
entries.notes: Today's HAT-im uses the 'cat' vowel for the long ā.

entries.name: Kris
entries.source: Pet form of Kristopher, Kristian, Kristin, said like Chris /kɹɪs/ (Wiktionary Chris); today's GB already kɹˈɪs
entries.notes: Today's US gold reading KREES is the dagger 'kris'. Matching is case-sensitive, so lowercase 'kris' keeps its reading. Flemish Kris is also KRIS.
entries.word_check: gold has 'kris'; kept: 'kris' (a dagger) is rare

entries.name: Cajetan
entries.source: de.wiktionary, Kajetan (variant spellings Cajetan, Kayetan): [ˈkaːjetaːn], [ˈkajetaːn], [ˌkajeˈtaːn]; Wikipedia, Cajetan: English /ˈkædʒətən/ KAJ-ə-tən

alternatives.context: English name of St Cajetan and Cardinal Cajetan, also used by Nigerian Catholic bearers, KAJ-uh-tun (today's reading)

entries.notes: Capitalised 'Cajetan' in English text is mostly St Cajetan (Gaetano of Thiene: feast, churches, parishes) and Cardinal Cajetan (Thomas de Vio, Luther's examiner), both KAJ-ə-tən as today. The given name's bearers are few (wd DE 9, AT 2, CH 2, NG 2). As with Saul, the English reading is protected and the German name reading, first-syllable stress per de.wiktionary, is recorded here. Polish Kajetan is ka-YEH-tahn.

entries.name: Firmin
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Firmin: /fiʁ.mɛ̃/; nasal ɛ̃ → 'an' (as Augustin, n0007); French names take final stress in English
entries.notes: Today's FUR-min reads it as English.

entries.name: Andries
entries.source: Dutch Andries (Andreas): stress on -dries, final s voiceless; Wiktionary Andries
entries.notes: Today's un-DREEZ voices the final s; Dutch and Afrikaans final s is [s].

entries.name: Baptist
entries.source: de.wiktionary, Baptist (Vorname): [bapˈtɪst]
entries.notes: Capitalised 'Baptist' in English text is the denomination (Baptist church, Southern Baptist) and John the Baptist, said BAP-tist. A name entry would change all of them, so it is protected; the German name reading (Johann Baptist) is recorded here.

entries.name: Robi
entries.source: Forebears 2014: Indonesia 50,356, Pakistan 31,905, Ethiopia 18,841, Bangladesh 15,397, India 11,847; Indonesian Robi and Bengali রবি Robi [robi] say ROH-bee, as today's ɹˈObi
entries.notes: Slovene and Hungarian Robi (pet form of Robert) has a similar o.

entries.name: Romy
entries.source: Wikipedia, Romy Schneider: German [ˈʁoːmi]; Forebears 2014: Philippines 29,515, Germany 7,468, Indonesia 6,370, Madagascar 5,744, Netherlands 4,808, US 3,251; today's ɹˈOmi matches
entries.notes: Filipino, German, Dutch and English bearers say ROH-mee; French bearers are fewer than those together.

entries.name: Nahed
entries.source: Arabic ناهد nāhid [ˈnaːhid]; Egyptian spelling with e
entries.notes: Today's gold NAD drops the h and the second syllable.

entries.name: Bohdan
entries.source: Wikipedia, Bohdan Khmelnytsky: Ukrainian Богдан [boɦˈdɑn]; Forebears 2014: Ukraine 133,981, Poland 6,597, Czechia 1,482
entries.notes: Ukrainian г [ɦ] → h. Ukrainian bearers far outnumber Polish and Czech ones; today's BOH-dun follows the Polish stress and drops the h.

entries.name: Javid
entries.source: Wiktionary, Persian جاوید jâvid: Iranian [d͡ʒɒː.ʋíːd]; Azerbaijani Cavid [dʒɑˈvid]
entries.notes: Today's JAV-id stresses the first syllable and shortens the ī.

entries.name: Cornelio
entries.source: Spanish Cornelio [koɾˈneljo]: regular orthography; stressed e in an open syllable → 'ay' (guide table, as Valeria)
entries.notes: Today's kor-NEL-ee-oh has the open 'eh' and an extra syllable.

entries.name: Imre
entries.source: Wikipedia, Imre Kertész: Hungarian [ˈimrɛ ˈkɛrteːs]; Hungarian stresses the first syllable
entries.notes: Today's IM-ruh uses the English 'bit' vowel and reduces the final e. Estonian Imre also says EEM-reh.

entries.name: Mayumi
entries.source: Japanese まゆみ Ma-yu-mi [majɯmi]; penultimate stress in English (guide, as Haruki)
entries.notes: Today's my-OO-mee merges ma and y into the 'eye' diphthong and leaves the stressed syllable without its y.

entries.name: Levent
entries.source: Turkish Levent: regular orthography; Turkish names take final stress (as Erol, Kenan, n0023)
entries.notes: Today's LEV-unt stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Hichem
entries.source: Maghrebi form of Hishām هشام [hiˈʃaːm], with ā fronted to e (as Djamel, n0017); ch = sh in French spelling (as Hicham, n0015)
entries.notes: Today's HITCH-im reads ch as English ch and stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Sharmin
entries.source: Bengali শারমিন Sharmin, first-syllable stress; today's ʃˈɑɹmɪn matches apart from the unstressed i

entries.name: Fatimata
entries.source: West African form of Fāṭima in French spelling (Burkina Faso, Niger, Mali, Senegal); a is 'ah'; penultimate stress as today and as Aminata (n0006)
entries.notes: Today's US gives the first syllable the 'cat' vowel and GB the stressed one the 'lot' vowel. The stress is unsourced (Fatoumata, n0005, stayed unresolved on it); kept today's.

entries.name: Ștefan
entries.source: Wikipedia, Stephen the Great: Romanian Ștefan cel Mare [ˈʃtefan tʃel ˈmare]
entries.notes: Ș is sh; today's STEF-ahn drops it.

entries.name: Shelby
entries.source: English Shelby /ˈʃɛlbi/; today's CMUdict reading matches

entries.name: Gyula
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hungarian Gyula: [ˈɟulɒ]; gy → English j (as György, n0024); Hungarian stresses the first syllable
entries.notes: Hungarian gy [ɟ] has no English match; English speakers use j. Today's JYOO-luh adds a y.

entries.name: Cyprien
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Cyprien: /si.pʁi.jɛ̃/; -ien as Adrien (n0017); French names take final stress in English
entries.notes: Today's SIP-ree-un is an English reading. FR register 8.6k.

entries.name: Abass
entries.source: West African spelling of Abbas عباس [ʕab.baːs]; same reading as Abbas (n0002)
entries.notes: Stress on the long final syllable; today's uh-BASS has the 'cat' vowel.

entries.name: Sabiha
entries.source: Forebears 2014: Bangladesh 92,563, Turkey 44,545, India 43,443, Pakistan 23,072, Algeria 13,141, Iran 4,891, Bosnia 2,286; Wikipedia, Sabiha Gökçen: Turkish [sabiˈha]; Arabic صبيحة ṣabīḥa stresses the long ī

alternatives.context: Arabic and Urdu bearers (Algeria, Pakistan, North Indian Muslims; about 65-80k), suh-BEE-huh (today's reading)

entries.notes: Conflicting evidence. Bangladesh is the largest group (about 93k, over 100k with Indian Bengalis), and this project stresses Bengali names on the first syllable (Abul, n0007; Sharmin in this batch), which would give SAH-bee-hah, possibly with Bengali sh for s; no source gives a Bengali or Bangladeshi-English pronunciation of this name. The earlier claim that Bangladeshi usage follows the Arabic sa-BEE-ha was unsourced. Today's suh-BEE-huh (Arabic/Urdu) stays until a Bengali source settles it.

entries.name: Mame
entries.source: French spelling of Wolof maam ('grandparent', honorific): Mame Diarra Bousso is Maam Jaara Buso in Wolof (Boston University Wolof materials); Forebears 2014: Senegal 191,650, Ethiopia 12,137, Mauritania 5,593, US 788

alternatives.context: English pet form of Mary (Auntie Mame, the musical Mame), MAYM (today's reading)

entries.notes: One syllable with a long 'ah'; the final e is French spelling only. Today's MAYM reads it as English. Senegalese bearers far outnumber any other group. Review: the entry also changes Auntie Mame and the musical Mame in English text to MAHM.

entries.name: Vasilis
entries.source: Wiktionary, Greek Βασίλης: /vaˈsilis/
entries.notes: Greek final s is s; today's ends in z.

entries.name: Robinson
entries.source: An English name borrowed into Spanish and Portuguese (Colombia, Brazil, Peru, Venezuela); bearers keep the English stress (Robinson Canó)

alternatives.context: Spanish-speaking bearers with Spanish vowels, ROH-been-sohn

entries.notes: Also a very common English surname, so the English reading has to stay.

entries.name: Cristiane
entries.source: Brazilian Portuguese Cristiane: ti → chi, nasal [ɐ̃] → 'uh', final e [i] (as Viviane and Cristiano, n0019)
entries.notes: Bearers are Brazilian (wd BR 71). Today's kris-tee-ANN drops the final syllable.

entries.name: Gilda
entries.source: Forebears 2014: Brazil 33,387, Mozambique 27,839, Angola 9,042 (Portuguese [ˈʒiɫdɐ]/[ˈʒiwdɐ]); Philippines 21,053; US 16,868; Italy 10,862; Spanish-speaking countries about 50k

alternatives.context: English-speaking and Filipino bearers (Gilda Radner), GIL-duh
Spanish-speaking bearers (Mexico, Argentina, Guatemala, Chile), HEEL-dah

entries.notes: Population call to review: Portuguese speakers (about 70k) are the largest group, then Spanish (about 50k) and English plus Filipino (about 38k). Brazil vocalises the l (ZHEEW-duh); Mozambique and Angola keep it, so l is kept.

entries.name: Urmi
entries.source: Bengali উর্মি Urmi ('wave', Sanskrit ūrmi): u is 'oo', first-syllable stress
entries.notes: Today's UR-mee uses the English 'her' vowel. ur before m as Özgür (n0023).

entries.name: Bikash
entries.source: Eastern spelling of Vikās (Nepali बिकाश, Bengali বিকাশ): b for v, long ā stressed as Vikas (n0004) and Prakash (n0001)
entries.notes: Today's BIK-ush reduces the long ā.

entries.name: Ramy
entries.source: Arabic رامي Rāmī [ˈraːmi]; as Rami (n0019); Ramy Youssef
entries.notes: Today's RAY-mee gives the long ā the English 'ay'.

entries.name: Pramila
entries.source: Wikipedia, Pramila Jayapal: /prəˈmɪlə/ prə-MIL-ə (her own English)
entries.notes: Today's PRAM-uh-luh stresses the first syllable with the 'cat' vowel.

entries.name: Saroja
entries.source: Sanskrit-derived Sarojā (lotus): j is English j, the long ō takes the stress
entries.notes: Today's sar-OH-yuh reads j as y.

entries.name: Tibor
entries.source: Wiktionary, Hungarian Tibor: [ˈtibor]; Hungarian stresses the first syllable
entries.notes: Today's TY-bur reads i as 'eye'. Slovak and Czech Tibor is also TEE-bor.

entries.name: Kwaku
entries.source: Wikipedia, Kwaku: Akan name for Wednesday-born boys; Akan a is 'ah' (as Kwame, n0017)
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today says the 'lot' vowel (KWOK-oo). US already right.

entries.name: Adán
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Adán: /aˈdan/; the accent marks final stress
entries.notes: Today's AY-dun is the English Aden. Spanish intervocalic d [ð] is said d by English speakers.

entries.name: Rosana
entries.source: Forebears 2014: Brazil 185,279, Argentina 81,218, Philippines 25,952, Venezuela 11,458, Colombia 10,473, Peru 6,982, Spain 6,969; Brazilian nasal [ɐ̃] → 'uh' (as Viviane, n0019)
entries.notes: Population call to review: Brazil (about 188k with Angola) and the Spanish-speaking countries plus the Philippines (about 175-190k) are close to even. Today's roh-ZAN-uh has the 'cat' vowel, wrong for both.

entries.name: Clotilde
entries.source: Wiktionary, Clotilde: Spanish /kloˈtilde/, French /klɔ.tild/; Forebears 2014: Peru 13,597, Brazil 12,473, DR Congo 10,148, Argentina 9,740, Mexico 8,220, France 7,911, Cameroon 7,904

alternatives.context: French-speaking bearers (France, Belgium, DR Congo, Cameroon), kloh-TEELD

entries.notes: Population call to review: Spanish speakers (about 45k+) narrowly outnumber French speakers (about 37k); all agree on the stressed 'TEEL'. Final unstressed e → 'ay' (guide table). Today's kluh-TILD has the 'bit' vowel.

entries.name: Erna
entries.source: German Erna [ˈɛʁna] (as Ernst, n0006); Forebears 2014: Germany 163,525, Austria 24,518, Netherlands 11,455, Belgium 6,728, Switzerland 5,908, Norway 4,072; Indonesia 206,639

alternatives.context: Indonesian bearers if the e is the schwa (pepet); unverified

entries.notes: Population call to review: German-speaking, Dutch and Norwegian bearers (about 216k) say AIR-na; Forebears also lists 206k Indonesian bearers whose vowel I could not source. Today's UR-nuh is the English reading.

entries.name: Ofelia
entries.source: Spanish Ofelia [oˈfelja]: stressed e in an open syllable is 'ay' (guide table); today's OfˈAliə matches

entries.name: Yasmina
entries.source: Arabic ياسمينة yāsmīna, stress on the long ī; Forebears 2014: Algeria 76,343, Egypt 20,105, Morocco 14,849, India 11,344, Spain 8,320, France 7,394
entries.notes: Arabic, Spanish and Russian/Tajik bearers stress MEE; today's YAZ-mi-nuh stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Nilufar
entries.source: Persian نیلوفر nilufar [niː.luː.ˈfæɾ]; Uzbek and Bengali Nilufar also stress -far with an 'ah'

alternatives.context: Iranian Persian, with the 'cat'-like æ in the last syllable

entries.notes: Final stress in every bearer group; today's NIL-uh-far stresses the first syllable. Uzbek, Tajik and Bengali bearers have 'ah' in -far.

entries.name: Adrienne
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Adrienne: /eɪdɹiˈɛn/, /ædɹiˈɛn/; French /a.dʁi.jɛn/
entries.notes: US register 67k makes English the main group. Today's ah-dree-EN (US) and od-ree-EN (GB, 'lot' vowel) miss the English 'ay'.

entries.name: Asghar
entries.source: Forebears 2014: Pakistan 232,962, Iran 189,266; Wiktionary اصغر: Urdu /əs.ɣəɾ/, Iranian Persian [ʔæs.ɢǽɹ]

alternatives.context: Iranian bearers (Asghar Farhadi: [æsˈɢæɾ]), as-GHAR with final stress

entries.notes: Population call to review: Pakistani bearers outnumber Iranian ones by about a fifth. Urdu ə is the 'cup' vowel (as Nandini, n0021); gh [ɣ] → g. Today's ASS-gur has the 'cat' vowel. Akbar (n0004) was left unresolved on a similar split.

entries.name: Saturnino
entries.source: Spanish Saturnino [satuɾˈnino]; today's sɑtʊɹnˈinO matches

entries.name: Odile
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Odile: /ɔ.dil/; French names take final stress in English (as Odette, n0012)
entries.notes: Today's oh-DEE-lee sounds the silent final e. FR register 85.8k.

entries.name: Yukiko
entries.source: Japanese ゆきこ Yu-ki-ko; penultimate stress in English (guide, as Haruki); today's jukˈikO matches

entries.name: Floyd
entries.source: English Floyd /flɔɪd/; today's CMUdict reading matches

entries.name: Eberhard
entries.source: de.wiktionary, Eberhard: [ˈeːbɐhaʁt]
entries.notes: German long e in an open syllable is 'ay'; today's EB-er-hart shortens it.

entries.name: Nuria
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Nuria: /ˈnuɾja/
entries.notes: ES register 118.9k. Today's NOOR-ee-uh uses the 'book' vowel and adds a syllable.

entries.name: Gleb
entries.source: Wiktionary, Russian Глеб: [ɡlʲep]; English renders it Gleb, as today's ɡlˈɛb
entries.notes: Russian devoices the final b and palatalises l; English renderings mark neither (as Miroslav, n0016).

entries.name: Alexandr
entries.source: Wiktionary, Russian Александр: [ɐlʲɪkˈsandr]; same reading as Aleksandr (n0026)

alternatives.context: Czech bearers (Czech spelling Alexandr), first-syllable stress

entries.notes: Population call: wd CZ 33 against RU 23, KZ 13, MD 9, and the US/ES births are mostly Russian-speaking families. Today's al-ig-ZAN-der is the English Alexander.

entries.name: Kwesi
entries.source: Fante spelling of Kwasi (Sunday-born boys); English renderings give KWEH-see or KWAY-see (pronounce.tv /ˈkwɛ.si/ UK); today's kwˈɛsi is the first
entries.notes: No Fante IPA found. Akan writes e (not ɛ), which may point to KWAY-see; today's KWEH-see is a common English rendering.

entries.name: Karam
entries.source: Forebears 2014: Pakistan 103,977, India 85,631, Egypt 39,690, Iran 23,169, Syria 14,255; Urdu/Punjabi کرم karam [ˈkəɾəm]
entries.notes: Population call: South Asian bearers (about 190k) outnumber Arabic-speaking ones (about 85k). Urdu ə is the 'cup' vowel (as Nandini, n0021). Today's KARE-um fits none of them.

entries.name: Comfort
entries.notes: Ordinary word 'comfort'. Ghanaian and Nigerian bearers use the English word as the name, read the same; nothing needs to ship.

entries.name: Esmeralda
entries.source: Wiktionary, Spanish Esmeralda: /esmeˈɾalda/
entries.notes: GB-only fix: British today says the 'lot' vowel in RAHL. US already right.

entries.name: Ema
entries.source: Wiktionary, Czech Ema: [ˈɛma]; Slovene, Croatian, Romanian and Portuguese Ema and the English variant of Emma agree
entries.notes: Today's EE-muh reads the e as 'ee'; every bearer group says EM-ah.

entries.name: Mini
entries.notes: Ordinary word 'mini' and the car brand Mini, usually capitalised in English text. The Indian name Mini (Kerala) is said the same, MIN-ee; nothing needs to ship.

entries.name: Wendell
entries.source: English Wendell /ˈwɛndəl/; today's CMUdict reading matches

entries.name: Norah
entries.source: English Norah /ˈnɔːrə/ (variant of Nora); today's CMUdict reading matches

entries.name: Elliott
entries.source: English Elliott /ˈɛliət/; today's CMUdict reading matches

entries.name: Saddam
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Saddam: /səˈdɑːm/ (also /ˈsɑ.dəm/ US); Arabic صدام Ṣaddām stresses the long ā
entries.notes: Today's SAH-dum is an American English variant; bearers and most English sources stress DAHM.

entries.name: Akira
entries.source: Wikipedia, Akira (1988 film): Japanese アキラ [aꜜkiɾa]; Japanese ki has a plain [i] ('ee'); penultimate stress in English (guide, as Haruki); Forebears 2014: Japan 752k

alternatives.context: common English uh-KEER-uh (today's reading), with the 'near' vowel before r

entries.notes: Today's uh-KEER-uh uses the 'near' vowel (US ɪɹ, GB ɪə) for the plain Japanese i, the same miss corrected for Samira (n0007), Mira (n0010), Amira (n0012) and Hira (n0027). Only the stressed vowel changes.

entries.name: Lúcio
entries.source: Wiktionary, Portuguese Lúcio: /ˈlu.si.u/; final unstressed -io is 'yoo' (as Márcio, n0011)
entries.notes: The accented spelling is Portuguese only (Lucio, n0019, stays Spanish). Today's LOO-see-oh.

entries.name: Arda
entries.source: Turkish Arda (Arda Turan): regular orthography; Turkish names take final stress (as Erol, Kenan, n0023)
entries.notes: Today's AR-duh stresses the first syllable. Bearers are Turkish (wd TR 136; GB 694 and FR 1.5k Turkish families). Review: also Tolkien's name for the world (Arda, AR-duh in English), which this changes to ar-DAH; the footballers Arda Turan and Arda Güler are the common English-text uses.

entries.name: Stevan
entries.source: Serbian Стеван Stȅvan, first-syllable stress; Forebears 2014: Serbia 20,712, North Macedonia 2,426, Bosnia 2,373, Croatia 1,834, US 3,972
entries.notes: Serbian bearers outnumber English ones about six to one. Today's STEE-vun is the English Steven.

entries.name: Kanta
entries.source: Japanese かんた Kan-ta [kanta]; Hindi कांता Kāntā [kaːn̪t̪aː]: both 'ah'
entries.notes: Japanese (wd JP 33) and Indian bearers both say 'ah'; today's KAN-tuh uses the 'cat' vowel.

entries.name: Badri
entries.source: Hindi बद्री badrī (Badrinath); Forebears 2014: India 168,038, Nepal 23,799, Indonesia 19,797, Georgia 9,368, Iran 8,284
entries.notes: Indian and Nepali bearers are the large majority; Hindi ə is the 'cup' vowel (as Nandini, n0021). Today's BAD-ree has the 'cat' vowel.

entries.name: Benson
entries.source: English Benson /ˈbɛnsən/; Kenyan, Nigerian and Ugandan bearers use the English name

entries.name: Lynette
entries.source: Wiktionary, English Lynette: /lɪˈnɛt/
entries.notes: Today's CMUdict lye-NET gives the first syllable the 'eye' vowel.

entries.name: Mohand
entries.source: Wikipedia, Si Mohand: Kabyle Si Muḥend U Mḥend
entries.notes: Kabyle and Riffian form of Muhammad (Kabyle Muḥend, e.g. Si Muḥend U Mḥend; wd DZ 19, MA 2; FR 1.5k, ES 353). The vowels (u and a schwa) and the stress are not given by any source I found; French speakers say moh-AND. Today's MOH-hand (with secondary stress on the 'cat' vowel) may be close. Needs a Kabyle source.

entries.name: Mubarak
entries.source: Arabic مبارك mubārak [muˈbaːrak]; today's mubˈɑɹɪk matches apart from the unstressed final vowel

entries.name: Łukasz
entries.source: Wiktionary, Polish Łukasz: /ˈwu.kaʃ/
entries.notes: Ł is w and sz is sh (as Tomasz, n0015). Today's YOO-kush reads Ł as y.

entries.name: Narcisse
entries.source: Wiktionary, French Narcisse: /naʁ.sis/; French names take final stress in English
entries.notes: Today's NAR-sis is the English 'narcissus' stem.

entries.name: Valter
entries.source: Forebears 2014: Brazil 116,336, Italy 22,936, Angola 8,907, Mozambique 6,240; Brazilian Portuguese l before a consonant is [w] (as Osvaldo, n0009: oz-VOW-doo)

alternatives.context: Italian, Swedish, Estonian and Slovene bearers, VAHL-ter

entries.notes: Population call to review: Brazilian bearers are the large majority. Today's VAWL-ter is the English Walter vowel.

entries.name: Franziska
entries.source: de.wiktionary, Franziska: [fʁanˈt͡sɪska]

entries.name: Firouzeh
entries.source: Behind the Name, Firouzeh: /fiː.ɾuː.ˈze/; Wiktionary فیروزه Iran formal [fiː.ɹuː.ze]
entries.notes: Final -eh is Persian [e]; written 'ay' (A), the nearest full English vowel, as Fatemeh and Afsaneh in earlier batches (Iranians' own vowel has no glide). Today's FY-row-zuh reads i as 'eye' and ou as 'ow'.

entries.name: Golnar
entries.source: Wiktionary, Persian گلنار (golnâr): Iran formal [ɡ̥ol.nɒ́ːɹ]
entries.notes: Today's GOHL-ner stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Golnaz
entries.source: Wiktionary, Persian گلناز (golnâz): Iran [ɡolˈnɒːz]; Behind the Name /ɡol.ˈnɒːz/
entries.notes: Today's GOHL-naz stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Khosrow
entries.source: Behind the Name, Khosrow: /xos.ˈɹow/ (Persian); Wiktionary خسرو Iran formal [xos.ɹow]
entries.notes: kh [x] has no English sound: k is the nearest sound English speakers use. Today's KAHS-roh stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Koorosh
entries.source: Wikipedia, Kourosh (also spelled Koorosh): Persian [kuːˈɾoʃ]; Behind the Name Kourosh /kuː.ˈɾoʃ/
entries.notes: Spelling variant of Kourosh; same reading.

entries.name: Minoo
entries.source: Behind the Name, Minoo: /miː.ˈnuː/; Wiktionary مینو Iran formal [miː.núː]
entries.notes: Today's mənˈu / mənˈuː (muh-NOO) has the right stress, consonants and stressed vowel; only the unstressed first vowel is reduced (Persian long ī). Kept per the guide; mee-NOO (minˈu / miːnˈuː) would be slightly closer.

entries.name: Mojdeh
entries.source: Behind the Name, Mojdeh: /moʒ.ˈde/; Wiktionary مژده (možde) Iran formal [moʒ.d̪e]
entries.notes: The j is the French-style spelling of zh [ʒ] (as in Bijan, Jaleh). Final -eh is Persian [e]; written 'ay' (A), the nearest full English vowel, as Fatemeh and Afsaneh in earlier batches (Iranians' own vowel has no glide). Today's mOjdˈɛ has a y sound for the zh.

entries.name: Mojgan
entries.source: Behind the Name, Mozhgan (Mojgan is its variant): /moʒ.ˈɡɒːn/; Wiktionary مژگان (možgân), romanised Mojgan, Mozhgan
entries.notes: The j is the French-style spelling of zh [ʒ] (as in Bijan, Jaleh). Today's guessed reading has no stress.

entries.name: Nooshin
entries.source: Behind the Name, Nooshin: /nuː.ˈʃiːn/; Wiktionary نوشین Iran formal [nuː.ʃíːn]
entries.notes: Today's NOO-shin stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Payman
entries.source: Wiktionary, Persian پیمان (peymân): Iran formal [pʰej.mɒ́ːn], romanised Payman, Peyman, Paymon; Wikipedia Peyman: English /ˌpeɪˈmɑːn/
entries.notes: Same name as Peyman (پیمان); Iranian bearers who spell it Payman still say pay-MAHN. Today's PAY-mun stresses the first syllable.

entries.name: Pouya
entries.source: Wiktionary, Persian پویا (puyâ, 'dynamic'): Iran formal [pʰuː.jɒ́ː]
entries.notes: Today's POY-uh reads ou as 'oy'.

entries.name: Ziba
entries.source: Behind the Name, Ziba (1): /ziː.ˈbɒː/ (Persian, 'beautiful'); Wiktionary زیبا Iran formal [ziː.bɒː]
entries.notes: Today's ZEE-buh stresses the first syllable.
